default.q.n2-10-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「〜たついでに」means "while doing A, take the opportunity to do B"; it is not used to introduce the result of an experiment or survey.
default.q.n2-10-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「〜たかわりに」 means "instead of" or "in return for," which is completely inappropriate in a context of conducting an experiment to obtain results and data.
default.q.n2-10-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「〜たところ」 is the correct grammar pattern for expressing that after doing something, one received a result or discovered a fact.
default.q.n2-10-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「〜たばかりに」 means "just because..." or "solely because...," leading to a bad or negative result, so it does not fit a neutral survey result.
default.q.n2-10-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 出版され.
default.q.n2-10-q51-51.explanation: The subject of the clause is 「日本を代表する作家、夏目漱石と太宰治の作品が」 (the works of Natsume Soseki and Dazai Osamu, representative Japanese authors). For a noun referring to books or works, the act of publishing must be expressed in the passive form 「出版される」 (be published). To connect naturally to the following result clause 「話題になりました」 (became a topic of discussion), the verb is changed to the passive connective form 「出版され」 (equivalent to 出版されて). Therefore, choice 4 is correct.
default.q.n2-10-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「出版し」 is active voice and does not fit because the subject is the work (作品が); the passive form meaning "be published" is required.
default.q.n2-10-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「出版注せ」contains an unfamiliar kanji and has an incorrect Japanese grammatical structure.
default.q.n2-10-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「出版注せられ」is also an incorrect combination of kanji and grammar.
default.q.n2-10-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「出版され」 is the passive form (受身形) of the Group 3 verb 「出版する」 → 「出版される」. It is in the conjunctive form with て omitted to connect the sentence, and it fits the subject 「作品が」 perfectly.
default.q.n2-10-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 2. やすい.
default.q.n2-10-q52-52.explanation: After hearing young people say that horizontal writing was more familiar and easier to read: 「横書きのほうが慣れていて読みやすい」, the publisher decided to print the novel horizontally. The grammar pattern 「V-masu stem + やすい」describes something that is easy or convenient to do. Therefore, 「やすい」is the correct choice.
default.q.n2-10-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「読みにくい」 means “difficult to read,” which is the complete opposite of the reason for printing the book horizontally, based on positive feedback from young readers.
default.q.n2-10-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「読みやすい」 means “easy to read” (V-ます + やすい), which fits perfectly with the reason “it is familiar, so it is easier to read” (慣れていて読みやすい).
default.q.n2-10-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「読みそうだ」 means “looks likely to read” or “seems to read,” so it cannot be used to evaluate how easy a text is.
default.q.n2-10-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「読みがたい」 means “very difficult or nearly impossible to read,” often with a psychological or emotional nuance, which is completely opposite to the flow of the passage.
default.q.n2-10-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 横書き / 横書き.
default.q.n2-10-q53-53.explanation: The author explains why horizontal writing has become increasingly common among young people: in modern educational and daily-life environments, textbooks for subjects other than Japanese language—such as mathematics, science, and social studies—are mostly printed horizontally (横書き), while familiar electronic devices such as computer and mobile-phone screens also display horizontal writing (横書き). Constant exposure to horizontal writing through both media has created a habit of reading horizontally among young people. Therefore, both blanks must be filled with 「横書き」 (choice 3: 横書き / 横書き).
default.q.n2-10-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「横書き / 縦書き」 is incorrect in the second part because computer and mobile phone screens, both in reality and in the passage, display horizontal writing (横書き).
default.q.n2-10-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「縦書き / 横書き」 is incorrect in the first part because textbooks for subjects other than Japanese language, such as mathematics, physics, and foreign languages, are printed horizontally (横書き).
default.q.n2-10-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「横書き」 is correct because both textbooks, apart from Japanese-language textbooks, and digital-device screens use horizontal writing.
default.q.n2-10-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「縦書き / 縦書き」is completely contrary to the author’s explanation and argument about why young people are accustomed to reading horizontally.
default.q.n2-10-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 少なくない.
default.q.n2-10-q54-54.explanation: The conclusion uses the contrastive conjunction 「しかし」 (however) together with the adverb 「やはり」 (nevertheless, after all) to present an objective, multifaceted view: although horizontal writing is currently very popular among young people, there are certainly “not a few” people who still like and want to read novels printed vertically in the traditional style. The pattern 「〜も少なくない」 (not a few = quite a few) is a formal expression commonly found in N2 argumentative writing. Therefore, the correct answer is 1. 少なくない.
default.q.n2-10-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「少なくない」means 'not at all few / quite a few,' fitting perfectly with the contrastive conjunction「しかし」and the adverb「やはり」to indicate that many people still enjoy reading books written vertically.
default.q.n2-10-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「少なくなる」 means "to become fewer" and describes a change of state. It is grammatically unsuitable with the particle 「も」 modifying the noun 「人」.
default.q.n2-10-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「少なかった」 is in the past tense, so it does not fit a statement about the current situation with the prediction pattern 「〜と思います」.
default.q.n2-10-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「少ない」means “few” or “little,” which directly conflicts with the contrastive transition 「しかし」and 「やはり」in the sentence.
default.q.n2-10-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ピアノのひき方を教えてほしい。).
default.q.n2-10-q55-55.explanation:
**Passage summary:** Before a student arrives for a piano lesson, the writer is practicing alone when an unexpected visitor enters. The visitor, a 74-year-old woman, says that while visiting a nearby laundromat, she heard piano music and listened attentively for a while. She has an old piano at home that no one plays. She has always liked the piano and wanted to learn to play it herself, but had never had the opportunity. She wants to know whether she can still learn to play at the age of 74. The writer suggests that she come and practice for a while, and the visitor leaves happily.

**Question translation:** What does the visitor want?

**Answer choices:**
1. She wants to be taught how to play the piano.
2. She wants someone else to use the old piano at her home.
3. She wants to listen to a piano performance.
4. She wants to be introduced to a piano teacher.
default.q.n2-10-q55-55.why.0: (a) Correct. According to the guest: 「わたくしも、ピアノは大好きですし、自分で弾けたらいいなあと思いながら、習うきっかけもなくて、今日まできてしまいました。今年 74 歳になりますけれど、もしかして、今からピアノがひけないものかしらと思いました。」 (I also love the piano and have always wished I could play it myself, but I never had the opportunity to learn... I am 74 this year, but I wondered whether it might still be possible to learn to play now.) After the writer invites the guest to come and practice, the guest leaves happily. This shows that the guest wanted to be taught how to play the piano.
default.q.n2-10-q55-55.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The visitor mentions that she has an old piano at home that nobody plays (「わたくしの家には古いピアノがありますけれど、だれもひく人がいません」) as one reason she wants to learn, not because she wants someone else to use the piano.
default.q.n2-10-q55-55.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The guest happened to hear the piano while passing by the laundromat and was drawn in, but entered to ask whether they could learn to play, not to ask the writer to perform.
default.q.n2-10-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The visitor directly asked the writer, who was a piano teacher, whether they could learn to play, not to introduce another piano teacher.
default.q.n2-10-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The reason the junior doctor always wanted to sit on the author's left.
default.q.n2-10-q56-56.explanation:
**Summary of the main point:** The author recalls that they did not start paying attention to left-handed people until adulthood. When having dinner with a junior doctor who was left-handed, the doctor always took the initiative to sit on the author's left. The reason (その理由) was that if the doctor sat on the author's right, the doctor's left hand holding chopsticks would bump into the author's right hand, making the doctor feel apologetic and uncomfortable.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** The passage contains the phrase 「 その理由 」 (that reason). What does it explain?
- 1. Why the author first noticed or became aware of left-handed people.
- 2. Why the junior doctor was left-handed.
- 3. Why the junior doctor took the initiative to sit on the author's left.
- 4. Why the junior doctor felt apologetic.
default.q.n2-10-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage merely begins with the author becoming aware of left-handed people in adulthood; the quoted phrase 「その理由」 does not explain why the author first began noticing this.
default.q.n2-10-q56-56.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Being left-handed is a natural characteristic of the junior person; the passage does not explain why that person is left-handed.
default.q.n2-10-q56-56.why.2: (c) Correct. Evidence from the reading: 「いっしょに夕食を食べにでかけると必ず私の左側にすわろうとするのです。『先生の右側にすわると、おはしを持った私の左手と先生の右手がぶつかって、申し訳ないから……』というのが、 その理由でした。」 (Whenever we went out to dinner together, the junior colleague always tried to sit on my left. The reason was that if they sat on my right, their left hand holding the chopsticks would bump into my right hand.)
default.q.n2-10-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The feeling of guilt (申し訳ない) is part of the junior person’s explanation for sitting on the left; 「その理由」does not refer only to the reason why that person feels guilty.
default.q.n2-10-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The person called to ask how much they should contribute toward a commemorative gift for their teacher.
default.q.n2-10-q57-57.explanation:
### Main point of the passage
The letter was written to explain and apologize that the writer cannot attend Professor Yamada’s book publication celebration because of a previously scheduled overseas business trip. At the end of the letter, the writer expresses a desire to join everyone in giving the professor a commemorative gift and says they will call to ask how much money they should contribute: 「近くお電話いたしますので、その時に金額などお教えいただけれ消（ば）幸いです。」 Therefore, the main purpose of the upcoming phone call is to ask how much the writer needs to pay toward the commemorative gift.

### Translation of the question and choices
- **Question:** The letter says 「ではまた、お電話で。」 (“See you again by phone.”) What is the main purpose of the person’s phone call?
- **1.** To express thanks for receiving the information about the party.
- **2.** To inform them that the writer cannot attend the party because of an overseas business trip.
- **3.** To convey the writer’s opinion about which commemorative gift should be chosen for the professor.
- **4.** To find out how much the writer needs to pay for the commemorative gift.
default.q.n2-10-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the letter already conveys thanks for receiving the party announcement; that is not the purpose of the upcoming phone call.
default.q.n2-10-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the reason for being unable to attend the party—being busy on a business trip abroad—is stated directly in this letter.
default.q.n2-10-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the writer only expresses a wish to join in giving the present («ぜひわたしもその一人に加えてください»); they do not say that they want to contribute ideas about what present to choose.
default.q.n2-10-q57-57.why.3: (d) Correct: The passage explicitly states the purpose of the call: 「近くお電話いたしますので、その時に金額などお教えいただけれ消（ば）幸いです。」(“I will call you shortly, and at that time I would appreciate it if you could tell me the amount [to be paid].”).
default.q.n2-10-q58-58.verdict: According to the passage, the correct answer is choice 2 (引き返すこと); the provided answer (3. 出かけること) is incorrect.
default.q.n2-10-q58-58.explanation:
Main idea: The passage explains how young animals learn life experience from their parents through a real-life example involving a mother cat and her kitten. As the two cats are about to cross the road, they hear a car approaching. The mother cat becomes frightened and turns back (引き返す). At that moment, the kitten also shares its mother’s fear and imitates her action, turning back as well (引き返すこと). In this way, the kitten learns how to recognize danger from the sound of a car and how to avoid it.

Translation of the question:
What does 「親と同じこと」 (“the same thing as the parent”) mean here?

Translation of the choices:
1. コピーすること: copying or imitating
2. 引き返すこと: turning back or returning
3. 出かけること: going out
4. 道を渡ること: crossing the road
default.q.n2-10-q58-58.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (コピーすること) is incorrect because “copying” is a general concept describing the gradual transmission of the parents' wisdom to their offspring, mentioned at the beginning of the passage ("徐々に親の知恵は子にコピーされていくのだ"); it is not the specific action the kitten performs immediately upon hearing the sound of a car.
default.q.n2-10-q58-58.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (引き返すこと) is correct according to the reading. The evidence is: 「親猫は『怖い ! 』と思って引き返す。そのとき子猫は親と同じ思いで『怖い』に同調するのである。そして 親と同じこと をする。」 When the mother cat becomes frightened and turns back (引き返す), the kitten shares the same fear and does the same thing as its mother—that is, it turns back as well (引き返すこと) to avoid the car.
default.q.n2-10-q58-58.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (出かけること) is incorrect (the provided answer is mistaken). Going out is the initial setting (「例えば、子猫が親猫と一緒に出かけて行くとする」), occurring before the sound of a car is noticed; it is not the action taken to avoid danger when it appears.
default.q.n2-10-q58-58.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (道を渡ること) is incorrect because crossing the road was only the initial intention (「道を渡ろうとしたとき、向こうから車が来る音がする」); when the car approached, the mother cat turned back instead of continuing across.
default.q.n2-10-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: In 1996, more than 40% of Japan’s population was concentrated in the three major metropolitan areas—Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya—with the Tokyo area showing the largest population growth.
default.q.n2-10-q59-59.explanation:
- Main point: The passage introduces a statistical chart showing the percentage of the population living in three major metropolitan areas (Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya) compared with Japan's total population over a 36-year period, from 1960 to 1996. The figures show a clear trend toward population concentration in major cities: by 1996, more than 40% of Japan's population was concentrated in these three metropolitan areas, with the Tokyo-centered area showing the greatest population growth.

- Translation of the question:
Choose the correct explanation of the chart.

- Translation of the answer choices:
1. In Japan, the urban population increased over the past 36 years. In 1996, the populations of the three major metropolitan areas (Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya) accounted for about one-quarter of Japan's total population, approximately twice the figure in 1960.
2. In Japan, the urban population increased over the past 36 years. In 1996, more than 40% of Japan's total population was concentrated in the three major metropolitan areas centered around Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya. In particular, the population growth rate in the Tokyo-centered area was very high, the highest among the three major metropolitan areas.
3. In Japan, the urban population increased over the past 36 years, but not all cities followed the same pattern. Among the three major metropolitan areas centered around Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya, there was also a metropolitan area whose share of the total population decreased by more than 10%.
4. In Japan, 13% of the urban population over the past 36 years...
default.q.n2-10-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Choice 1 says that the three major metropolitan areas account for one-fourth (25%) and have doubled compared with 1960, which does not match the graph’s figures; in reality, in 1996 the three metropolitan areas accounted for over 40% of the total population.
default.q.n2-10-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct. According to the graph showing the population ratios of the three major metropolitan areas over 36 years (1960–1996), in 1996 more than 40% of the country's population was concentrated in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya, with the Tokyo area recording the highest population growth rate of the three.
default.q.n2-10-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Choice 3 claims that an urban area experienced a decline of more than 10%, but this is inconsistent with the graph’s data. The population ratios of the urban areas either continued to grow or remained stable; none declined by more than 10%.
default.q.n2-10-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Choice 4 gives figures and an interpretation that do not match the chart describing the distribution and population growth rates of metropolitan areas.
default.q.n2-10-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The moment when the friend brings the food all the way to the cat.
default.q.n2-10-q60-60.explanation:
Main idea: The friend prepared food and called the cat, but the cat did not come because it was lying on a heated carpet. The friend therefore carried the food over to the cat. That moment marked the beginning of the owner being “trained” by the cat without realizing it.

Question translation:
What kind of moment was 「その瞬間」(“that moment”)?

Answer choices:
1. The moment the cat sat on the heated carpet.
2. The moment the friend prepared food for the cat.
3. The moment the friend called, “Dinner’s ready.”
4. The moment the friend carried the food over to the cat.
default.q.n2-10-q60-60.why.0: (a) Choice 1: The passage states that the cat had already been lying on the heated carpet ('寒くなると、猫というものは一日中、暖かいストーブの前やホットカーペットの上に座っているものらしい'), so this is not the moment that changed the situation.
default.q.n2-10-q60-60.why.1: (b) Choice 2: The friend making food for the cat ("ある日友人は猫のご飯を作って") is merely an everyday activity, not the moment when the cat begins “training” its owner.
default.q.n2-10-q60-60.why.2: (c) Choice 3: When the friend calls「ごはんよ」(“Dinner’s ready”), the cat still has not come (なかなか来ない), so this is not yet the turning point.
default.q.n2-10-q60-60.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct. The passage states: "こんなとき飼い主というものは、つい猫のところまでご飯を持流ていってしまうのだそうだ。猫はホットカーペットの上にすまして座っている。飼い主は ① その瞬間 なにかが変わることに気づかない。" → "That moment" is when the friend instinctively carries the food to where the cat is sitting, beginning the process by which the cat turns the owner into an on-demand servant.
default.q.n2-10-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The cat returns to the warm place.
default.q.n2-10-q61-61.explanation:
Main idea: When hungry, the cat comes to the kitchen to ask for food, but as soon as it sees its owner start preparing the meal, it immediately returns to its "usual spot" (a warm place on the heated mat / in front of the heater) and waits.

Question translation:
In the phrase 「 サッと定位置まで戻り 」 (quickly return to its usual spot), who returns where?

Translation of the choices:
1. The cat returns to the warm place.
2. The cat returns to the kitchen.
3. The owner returns to the warm place.
4. The owner returns to the kitchen.
default.q.n2-10-q61-61.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct. The passage states: 「台所までご飯の催促をしにきた猫が、飼い主が用意を始めたと見るや、 告 サッと定位置まで戻り 、活ょこんと座って待っている姿をみたときだ。」 The fixed locations mentioned at the beginning for winter are 「暖かいストーブの前やホットカーペットの上」. The cat is the one performing the action, and it returns to a warm place.
default.q.n2-10-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2: The cat goes from the warm place to the kitchen (台所) to ask for food. When it sees the owner cooking, it returns to the warm place, not to the kitchen.
default.q.n2-10-q61-61.why.2: (c) Choice 3: The subject performing the action 「サッと定位置まで戻り」 is the cat (猫), not the owner (飼い主).
default.q.n2-10-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4: The owner is already in the kitchen preparing food for the cat, so the owner is not the one who “quickly returns to its usual place” (サッと定位置まで戻り).
default.q.n2-10-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The cat makes its owner bring the food all the way to where it is.
default.q.n2-10-q62-62.explanation:
Main point: The cat hates eating in the cold kitchen, so it firmly demands “home delivery”—in other words, it trains its owner to bring its food to its warm spot.

Question translation:
The article says 「 出前を注せる 」 (“make someone deliver food”). Who makes whom do what?

Answer choices:
1. The owner makes the cat eat in the kitchen.
2. The owner makes a restaurant deliver food to the house.
3. The cat makes the owner bring its food to where it is.
4. The cat makes the owner bring its food to the kitchen.
default.q.n2-10-q62-62.why.0: (a) Choice 1: The passage says "冷たい台所で食べるのがいやで" (the cat dislikes eating in the cold kitchen), so the owner does not make the cat go to the kitchen but brings the food directly to it.
default.q.n2-10-q62-62.why.1: (b) Choice 2: “出前” is used metaphorically here to depict bringing food directly to the cat, not ordering food from a restaurant in real life.
default.q.n2-10-q62-62.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (correct answer): The passage says: "つまり、冷たい台所で食べるのがいやで、なにがなんでも ③ 出前を注せる つもりなのだ。以後、飼い主は出前を続けることになったのである。" The cat did not want to eat in the cold kitchen, so it made its owner bring food to the warm place where it wanted to eat.
default.q.n2-10-q62-62.why.3: (d) Choice 4: The cat makes its owner bring the food to the cat’s place (「自分のところ」), not to the kitchen (「台所」).
default.q.n2-10-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The exclamation 「なるほど！」 expresses admiration and an impression of the idea’s originality and usefulness (アイディアの良さ).
default.q.n2-10-q63-63.explanation:
Main point: The “Naruhodo” exhibition displays inventions inspired by everyday thoughts among women such as “It would be so convenient if something like this existed.” The exclamation 「なるほど！」 (I see! / How clever!) expresses admiration and amazement at these excellent, useful creative ideas.

Question and choices:
Question: What does the exclamation ①「なるほど！」 (I see!) refer to?
1. The fact that the objects are familiar and close to everyday life.
2. The fact that all of them are outstanding works.
3. The excellent creative ideas.
4. The fact that they are closely connected with everyday life.
default.q.n2-10-q63-63.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage says the idea was created from the feeling that 「こんなものがあれば便利じゃないかな」 and made readers exclaim 「なるほど！」, showing admiration for the idea's creativity and usefulness, not merely for the object's familiarity.
default.q.n2-10-q63-63.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the following sentence says 「その中で、優秀な作品には...賞が贈られ」, meaning that only some outstanding works among them receive awards; not all displayed works are outstanding.
default.q.n2-10-q63-63.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct according to the passage: 『日常生活の中で、「こんなものがあれば便利じゃないかな」と思う気持ちから生み出された ① 「 なるほど ！」と感心注せられるようなものが全国から集まり、出品される。』 (Inventions born from the everyday thought, "Wouldn't it be convenient if there were something like this?"—things that make people exclaim 「なるほど！」 in admiration—are collected from around the country and exhibited).
default.q.n2-10-q63-63.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because 「生活に密着したもの」 is a general characteristic describing the products in the following sentence (which gives examples such as canes and slippers), not the direct object that makes people exclaim 「なるほど！」.
default.q.n2-10-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The most suitable conjunction for the blank is 「例えば」(rendered incorrectly as たとえ消 by OCR), which is used to begin listing specific illustrative examples.
default.q.n2-10-q64-64.explanation:
Main idea: Before the blank, the author emphasizes that these inventions differ from the ideas of scientists and researchers because anyone can use them easily. Immediately after the blank comes a series of specific examples—a telescoping cane for someone nearly 100 years old, slippers that help with weight loss, a wrinkle-resistant laundry bag, and so on. Therefore, the connective meaning "for example" (例えば) is the most appropriate.

Question and answer choices:
Question: Which word is most appropriate to fill in the blank （ 告 ）?
1. Then / Immediately afterward
2. In short / In other words
3. By the way / Incidentally
4. For example / Such as
default.q.n2-10-q64-64.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (すると—“then” / “immediately afterward”) indicates a succeeding event or inevitable result and is not used to introduce a list of examples.
default.q.n2-10-q64-64.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (つまり: in short / in other words) is used to summarize or restate the preceding idea. It is not used when the following clause gives a list of specific illustrative examples.
default.q.n2-10-q64-64.why.2: (c) Choice 3, ところで (“by the way,” used to change the subject), is incorrect because the following sentence continues to clarify the point made in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n2-10-q64-64.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (“such as; for example”) is correct because the following sentence lists specific examples: 『100 歳近いお年寄りの考案した伸縮自在の杖次はいているだけでダイエットに泊果のあるスリッパ、あると助かる介護用品、洗濯機で洗うものがし山にならないネットなど』.
default.q.n2-10-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: This association is willing to accept inventions and provide a wide range of advice, even when they are still only at the initial idea stage.
default.q.n2-10-q65-65.explanation:
Summary of the main point: The Japan Women's Inventors' Association was established more than 50 years ago to support ordinary homemakers who had ideas but did not know how to present them, apply for patents, or commercialize them. The association is always ready to provide consultations and advice from the earliest stage, when an invention is still only a budding idea.

Translation of the question and choices:
Question: Which of the following matches the content of the passage?
1. This association was established to support professional inventors throughout the country.
2. The "Naruhodo" exhibition can display only objects closely connected to everyday life.
3. This association is ready to accept a wide range of consultations related to inventions.
4. All the works displayed at the "Naruhodo" exhibition have received awards.
default.q.n2-10-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage says the association was established to support housewives and ordinary people: 『一般家庭の主婦が何か考案しても...そういう人たちを支援しようと 50 年あまり前に生まれたのがこの協会』, not professional inventors (プロの発明家).
default.q.n2-10-q65-65.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is inaccurate because the passage does not impose an absolute rule or restriction that only items closely connected to daily life may be exhibited (しか展示できない).
default.q.n2-10-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because paragraph 2 clearly states: 『アイディアの段階、考案の芽の段階であっても、相談に応じてくれ、いろいろなアド理イスをしてくる。』 (Even at the idea stage, or when an invention is only beginning to take shape, the association is willing to provide consultations and offer various useful suggestions).
default.q.n2-10-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage states: 『その中で、優秀な作品には「なるほど賞」や関係官公庁からの賞が贈られ』, meaning that only outstanding works among them receive awards; it does not mean that all submitted works are award-winning works.
default.q.n2-10-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 近代的な建物が整然と並んでいる路地 (an alley where modern buildings stand in orderly rows).
default.q.n2-10-q66-66.explanation:
Summary: The author talks with a French person who has lived in Tokyo for many years. This person enjoys walking through Tokyo's back alleys because their jumbled mix of modern and traditional features gives them a sense of everyday life and offers many delightful surprises, unlike the orderly, well-planned streets of Europe.
Translation of the question: Which of the following does NOT describe "alleys like these"?
Translation of the choices:
1. The alley is filled with eye-catching, mismatched things.
2. The alley has modern buildings arranged neatly in straight rows.
3. The alley is chaotic, confusing, and difficult to navigate.
4. The alley conveys the feel of people's everyday lives.
default.q.n2-10-q66-66.why.0: (a) Not chosen because this is a characteristic of the alley mentioned in the passage: while walking around, the French discover unexpected, incongruous things (「あれ、こんな所にこんなものが・・・・」という不釣合いを発見しながら).
default.q.n2-10-q66-66.why.1: (b) Correct answer (it does not fit 「こういう路地」). The passage describes Tokyo’s back alleys as 「近代的な建物の横に、古いお宮やお寺があったりする」(old shrines and temples standing beside modern buildings), not as modern buildings arranged neatly in straight rows (整然と並んでいる)—a feature of European streets.
default.q.n2-10-q66-66.why.2: (c) Not chosen because the article describes Tokyo’s alleys as maze-like and easy to get lost in (「路地が迷路のように広がり、すぐ方向がわからなくなる」), and later calls them cluttered or chaotic (ごちゃごちゃした所).
default.q.n2-10-q66-66.why.3: (d) Not selected because the passage describes the alley as conveying the breath of people’s lives (「人々の生活のにおいがする」), equivalent to 「生活がにじみ出ている」.
default.q.n2-10-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 街はきれいであれば人の心をひきつけるとは限らない (A clean and beautiful town does not necessarily attract people’s hearts).
default.q.n2-10-q67-67.explanation:
Summary: The author draws a lesson for governments seeking to attract foreign tourists: simply planning streets to be clean, beautiful, and orderly does not necessarily attract visitors. The everyday cultural features, surprises, and natural disorder of a place may offer a fresher appeal to people who are already accustomed to orderly streets.
Question translation: What does sentence ②, "Making the streets clean and beautiful is not everything / simply making them clean and beautiful is not necessarily best," mean?
Answer choices:
1. To attract tourists, the ability to make the streets clean and beautiful is important.
2. To attract tourists, it is not necessary to clean the streets.
3. Even if the streets are made clean and beautiful, disorderly places will not disappear.
4. Clean and beautiful streets do not necessarily appeal to people.
default.q.n2-10-q67-67.why.0: (a) It should not be chosen because this misinterprets the idiom「〜だけが能じゃない」(doing only... is not the only valuable ability) as praising beautifying the streets as an important skill.
default.q.n2-10-q67-67.why.1: (b) Not selected because the passage does not say at all that “there is no need to keep the streets clean”; that is an extreme and inaccurate inference.
default.q.n2-10-q67-67.why.2: (c) Not chosen because the article does not discuss whether the messy place has disappeared; it discusses its appeal to tourists.
default.q.n2-10-q67-67.why.3: (d) Correct. The author says that although the streets of Paris are clean and beautiful, they lack the pleasant surprise of not knowing what might appear; to someone tired of beautiful, orderly streets, disorderly and lively places seem fresh: 「きれいだが、何が出てくるかわからないというようなおもしろさはない。美しく整った街を見飽きた目には、ごちゃごちゃした所がかえって新鮮にうつるのだ」. Thus, simply making streets clean and beautiful does not necessarily make them attractive or captivating: 人の心をひきつけるとは限らない.
default.q.n2-10-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 東京の路地にはいろいろな発見があると言っている (It says that there are many discoveries to be made in Tokyo's back alleys).
default.q.n2-10-q68-68.explanation:
Summary: A French person who has lived in Tokyo for many years observes that Tokyo's backstreets are fascinating because walking through them reveals many surprising, quirky things, such as an old temple or shrine beside a modern building or flowerpots spilling out into the street. Unlike Tokyo, Paris is beautiful but lacks this element of surprise.
Question translation: Which of the following statements about this French person is consistent with the passage?
Answer choices:
1. Says that there are many discoveries to be made in the backstreets of Paris.
2. Says that there are many discoveries to be made in the backstreets of Tokyo.
3. Says that Tokyo's backstreets are troublesome because it is difficult to find one's way around them.
4. Says that Paris is an orderly, beautiful city and is therefore very interesting.
default.q.n2-10-q68-68.why.0: (a) Not selected because the passage clearly states that the small streets of Paris lack the appeal of not knowing in advance what one might encounter: 「何が出てくるかわからないというようなおもしろさはない」.
default.q.n2-10-q68-68.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage clearly says that the Frenchman enjoys walking around Tokyo’s alleys because he discovers incongruous and pleasantly unexpected things along the way («彼は ① こういう路地 を歩き回るのが楽しいと言う。『あれ、こんな所にこんなものが・・・・』という不釣合いを発見しながら»).
default.q.n2-10-q68-68.why.2: (c) Not selected because although Tokyo’s back streets can easily make someone lose their way, this person actually enjoys that and does not find it troublesome or difficult (「これがいいのだそうだ。彼は...歩き回るのが楽しいと言う」).
default.q.n2-10-q68-68.why.3: (d) Not selected because this person says that although the streets of Europe and Paris are beautiful and orderly, they are not as interesting as Tokyo (「確かにきれいですけど、東京のような面白さはありません」).
default.q.n2-10-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because person A emphasizes cultivating sensitivity (感性) through travel, while person B values developing mental strength and perseverance (精神力) by giving one’s utmost effort.
default.q.n2-10-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: Person A recommends traveling independently while in school to broaden one’s perspective, experience the world through the five senses, and develop sensitivity and感性 for future work and relationships. Person B recommends devoting oneself fully to something, such as study or sports, in order to surpass one’s limits, endure difficult challenges, and develop the willpower and confidence that will provide spiritual strength throughout life.
- Question translation: If the qualities valued by the two people were summed up in one word each, what would they be? Choose the most appropriate answer.
- Answer choices:
  1. A: Saving money / B: Effort
  2. A: Inner self / B: External appearance
  3. A: Sensitivity / B: Mental strength
  4. A: Soul / B: Intellectual concentration
default.q.n2-10-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because Person A does not regard “saving money” (節約) as the core objective, but advises using time to gain experiences. Person B emphasizes training to overcome one’s limits and strengthen one’s will, rather than merely making a general effort (努力).
default.q.n2-10-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because Person B does not mention or value “external appearance” (外面) at all, but instead talks about physical training and study to build inner strength.
default.q.n2-10-q69-69.why.2: (c) Correct. Person A emphasizes: 'Being deeply moved by many things through the sensitive use of all five senses. I believe that such sensitivity will become important nourishment for working and building human relationships in the future' (感性). Person B emphasizes: 'Working with the determination to challenge the limits of one's body... The experience and confidence gained from enduring hard training will support you throughout the rest of your life' (精神力).
default.q.n2-10-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because Person A emphasizes sensibility/perception (感性) based on actual sensory experience, not merely an ambiguous “spirit” (心); Person B also refers to physical and athletic effort as training, rather than focusing only on the intellect (頭専).
default.q.n2-10-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because both people recognize that the good and valuable experiences they had in their youth became a foundation supporting their later lives.
default.q.n2-10-q70-70.explanation:
- Main idea: Both Person A and Person B reflect on and draw lessons from their own experiences when they were young or students (A took inexpensive overnight trips filled with emotion; B studied so hard while abroad that they became exhausted). Both affirm that these experiences were extremely valuable and became the foundation and life experience that helped them in their later work and lives.
- Question translation: What do the answers of the two people have in common?
- Answer choices:
  1. They both think they had valuable experiences in their youth.
  2. They think their experiences in their youth were meaningless.
  3. They regret how they spent their youth.
  4. They both say that their youth was very difficult.
default.q.n2-10-q70-70.why.0: (a) Correct because the quotations show that Person A vividly remembers a student trip, which remains a valuable source of nourishment ('いまでも目を閉じるとあざやかに浮かんできます... 大切な糧になる'), while Person B says that working hard while studying abroad created the solid foundation for the present ('それが今の私の土台になっている気がします'). Both regard their experiences in youth as positive and useful.
default.q.n2-10-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because both expressions assert that the experience was extremely meaningful: 「大切な糧になる」 means “become valuable nourishment for one’s growth,” and 「土台になっている」 means “serve as a foundation.” This is the opposite of “it had no meaning” (意味がなかった).
default.q.n2-10-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because both speakers respect and take pride in what they experienced during their student years; they do not feel regret (後悔している).
default.q.n2-10-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because only Person B talks about the hardship of studying abroad (“I studied as if my life depended on it” [死ぬほど勉強しました]), while Person A describes a carefree, emotionally rich trip and beautiful scenery (“comes vividly to mind” [あざやかに浮かんできます]). Therefore, hardship is not common to both people.
default.q.n2-10-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (事実は科学の中に存在すること): The phrase 「そんなこと」replaces the idea that facts exist within science, an idea the author completely rejects.
default.q.n2-10-q71-71.explanation:
- Main idea: At the beginning of the passage, the author states that most scientists and ordinary people tend to believe that science contains absolute truth. However, the author immediately rejects this idea with the sentence 「しかし、①そんなことはまったくない」 (However, that is absolutely not the case), denying the notion that “truth exists in science.”
- Translation of the question: What does 「そんなこと」 (“such a thing”) refer to?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. The idea that science is not absolute.
  2. The idea that ordinary people believe science is absolute.
  3. The idea that nearly 90% of scientists believe that truth exists in science.
  4. The idea that truth exists in science.
default.q.n2-10-q71-71.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because “science is not absolute” is the author’s position. Replacing it with “there is absolutely no such thing” would negate the author’s own view.
default.q.n2-10-q71-71.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author does not deny that ordinary people believe in science; rather, the author denies the content being believed—the absoluteness or “truth” supposedly contained in science.
default.q.n2-10-q71-71.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author uses 「そんなこと」 to reject the content of the belief, not to deny that nearly 90% of scientists hold that belief.
default.q.n2-10-q71-71.why.3: (d) Correct because the passage states: 「科学者のおそらく 9 割近くは『事実は科学の中に存在する』と信じているのではないかと思います。一般の人となると、もっと科学を絶対的だと信じているかもしれません。しかし、①そんなことはまったくない。」 -> 「そんなこと」 refers to the preceding belief that “facts exist within science,” which the author says is completely untrue.
default.q.n2-10-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (A: 推論, B: 事実, C: 推論): A is an inference applied by a government agency; B is the fact that the temperature rose; C is an inference about the cause being CO2.
default.q.n2-10-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: The author analyzes the difference between a “scientific fact” and a “scientific inference or theory.” The rise in Earth’s temperature is a “fact” (事実 - B), whereas the hypothesis that CO2 causes this phenomenon is an “inference” (推論 - C). It is deeply concerning when government agencies hastily treat a “scientific inference” (推論 - A) as absolute truth and turn it into rigid policy.
- Question translation: “Which combination of words is most appropriate for ( A ), ( B ), and ( C )?”
- Answer choices:
  1. A: Fact, B: Fact, C: Inference
  2. A: Inference, B: Fact, C: Inference
  3. A: Inference, B: Inference, C: Fact
  4. A: Fact, B: Inference, C: Fact
default.q.n2-10-q72-72.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because position (A) must be 推論 (“inference”), as indicated by the author’s earlier statement: 「行政がこんなに大規模に一つの科学的推論を採用して...」.
default.q.n2-10-q72-72.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage states: paragraphs 4–5 say 「行政がこんなに大規模に一つの科学的推論を採用して... だから簡単に「科学的 (A: 推論)」を真理だと決め付けてしまうのは怖い」; the final paragraph says 「温暖化でいえば、気温が上がっている、というところまでが科学的 (B: 事実)。その原因が炭酸ガスだ、というのは科学的 (C: 推論)」.
default.q.n2-10-q72-72.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because positions (B) and (C) are reversed: “the temperature rises” is an observable fact (事実), whereas “the cause is CO2” is an inference or supposition (推論).
default.q.n2-10-q72-72.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because position (A) is not “事実” (fact) but “推論” (inference), and positions (B) and (C) are also assigned incorrectly.
default.q.n2-10-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (科学的推論と事実を区別しなければならない): The author’s central message is that scientific facts and scientific inferences must be clearly distinguished.
default.q.n2-10-q73-73.explanation:
- Main point: The entire passage focuses on clarifying the common confusion between “scientific facts” (confirmed matters, such as rising temperatures) and “scientific inferences” (hypotheses explaining causes, such as CO2). The author warns of the danger of administrative authorities treating an inference as absolute truth. The central message is that scientific inferences and facts must always be clearly distinguished.
- Question translation: “What does the author most want to say?”
- Answer choices:
  1. Scientific inferences and facts must be clearly distinguished.
  2. The Kyoto Protocol must be valued in order to prevent global warming.
  3. We must not immediately believe what government authorities say.
  4. 90% of scientists believe that truth exists within science.
default.q.n2-10-q73-73.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct, as shown by the quotation: At the end, the author emphasizes, 「『科学的事実』と『科学的理論』は別物です。...しかし、この事実と推論とを混同している人が多い。」 The entire article uses examples involving climate change and administrative policies to highlight the need to distinguish scientific facts from inferences.
default.q.n2-10-q73-73.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the Kyoto Protocol is only the context of the meeting mentioned by the author as an illustrative example, not the message the author intends to convey.
default.q.n2-10-q73-73.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because criticizing the rigidity of public authorities is only an example illustrating the consequences of confusion, not the main argument encompassing the entire article.
default.q.n2-10-q73-73.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because it is merely a secondary speculation presented at the beginning to introduce the issue, not something the author intends to assert or communicate.
default.q.n2-10-q74-74.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant points:**
According to the fee schedule and usage regulations of Hara City Civic Hall (原市市民会館):
1. **Eligible user:** Mr. A lives in Hara City, so the standard rate applies; the 20% surcharge for users from outside the city does not apply («市民以外の方が使用する場合、すべての料金が 20 ％増になります»).
2. **Purpose of use:** The lecture is free to attend and does not involve selling goods, so the 50% surcharge does not apply («入場料を集めたり、物品販売を目的とする場合は、使用料の 50 ％が加算されます»).
3. **Rental period:** From 9:00 to 13:00 is 4 hours (13 - 9 = 4).
   - Hall (ホール): 9,000 円/hour × 4 hours = 36,000 円.
   - Stage (舞台): 3,000 円/hour × 4 hours = 12,000 円.
   - Dressing rooms (楽屋): 2 rooms × 300 円/hour × 4 hours = 2,400 円.
   => Total facility rental fee = 36,000 + 12,000 + 2,400 = 50,400 円.
4. **Heating/cooling fee (冷暖房費):** The lecture is held in July. The regulations state: «7 月～ 9 月は冷暖房費として一日につき 1000 円» (From July to September, the heating/cooling fee is 1,000 円 per day).
=> Total amount payable: 50,400 + 1,000 = 51,400 円.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** Mr. A, who lives in Hara City, wants to hold a lecture in the hall of the civic center in July. He wants to use the hall, stage, and 2 dressing rooms from 9:00 to 13:00. Attendance will be free. How much must he pay the civic center in total?
- 1. 49,200 yen
- 2. 50,000 yen
- 3. 50,400 yen
- 4. 51,400 yen
default.q.n2-10-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 49,200円 does not match the actual fee calculation formula under the stated rules.
default.q.n2-10-q74-74.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 50,000円 does not match the actual rental fees and rental period.
default.q.n2-10-q74-74.why.2: (c) Incorrect. ¥50,400 is only the total room rental cost for four hours (36,000 + 12,000 + 2,400 = ¥50,400); the ¥1,000 air-conditioning charge for July must also be added, making the correct total ¥51,400.
default.q.n2-10-q74-74.why.3: (d) Correct because it matches the price table and terms: The 4-hour rental (9:00–13:00) costs Hall (9,000 × 4 = 36,000 円) + Stage (3,000 × 4 = 12,000 円) + 2 backstage rooms (300 × 2 × 4 = 2,400 円) = 50,400 円. In addition, the July air-conditioning charge is 1,000 円 under the rule «7 月～ 9 月は冷暖房費として一日につき 1000 円», giving a total of 50,400 + 1,000 = 51,400 円.
default.q.n2-10-q75-75.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (各施設の空き状態は市民会館窓口または、電話にてお問い合わせください。).
default.q.n2-10-q75-75.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant passage:**
The user guide for the Hara City Cultural Hall specifies the registration procedure as follows:
1. **Check availability (Section 3)**: «各施設の空き状態は市民会館窓口または、電話にてお問い合わせください» (Please inquire at the civic hall counter or by telephone to check the availability of each facility.)
2. **Prepare and submit the application (Sections 4 and 2)**: Download the usage permit application from the website («使用許可申請書は原市市民会館ホームページよりダウンロードできます»), fill in the required information, bring identification confirming your address («住所が確認できる身分証明書»), and submit the application at the reception counter together with the full usage fee and air-conditioning fee.

**Translation of the question and choices:**
- **Question**: What steps should Mr. A take to register at the counter?
- 1. If an admission fee is charged or the facility is used for sales purposes, an additional 50% of the usage fee will be charged.
- 2. When submitting the application, please pay the entire usage fee, including the air-conditioning fee.
- 3. Please inquire at the Cultural Hall counter or by telephone to check the availability of each facility.
- 4. When submitting the application, please fill in the required items on the usage permit application and submit it at the reception counter together with the usage fee...
default.q.n2-10-q75-75.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this is a rule imposing a 50% surcharge when admission fees are collected or goods are sold («入場料を集めたり、物品販売を目的とする場合は、使用料の 50 ％が加算されます»), not a registration procedure.
default.q.n2-10-q75-75.why.1: (b) Incorrect because this is a rule about paying the fees when submitting an application (“申請の際に、冷房費を含めた使用料をすべてお支払いください”), not about all the preceding preparation steps.
default.q.n2-10-q75-75.why.2: (c) Correct because it directly quotes the step of checking availability in the procedure in section 3: «各施設の空き状態は市民会館窓口または、電話にてお問い合わせください» before downloading the form, filling it out, and bringing identification and the fee to the counter for submission.
default.q.n2-10-q75-75.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This is an unfinished excerpt from item 4 that only mentions filling out the form and submitting it at the counter; it does not include the steps of checking room availability and preparing identification documents.
default.q.n2-10-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 4. いたずら.
default.q.n2-10-q11-11.explanation:
- Meaning: “My five-year-old son is always getting into mischief.”
- Expression: いたずらをする (be mischievous, play tricks), V-て + ばかりいる (do nothing but..., be constantly doing..., with a complaining nuance).
- Example: 子供がいたずらをして、壁に落書きをした。(The child was being mischievous and scribbled on the wall.)
default.q.n2-10-q11-11.why.0: (a) しつけ (躾) means discipline or training in proper behavior. It is commonly used for parents disciplining their children (しつけをする / しつけを受ける), not for a spontaneous action by a five-year-old child in this context.
default.q.n2-10-q11-11.why.1: (b) いじめ (苛め/虐め - bullying): This refers to mistreating or bullying others. It is not a natural word for describing the ordinary hyperactive mischief of a five-year-old at home.
default.q.n2-10-q11-11.why.2: (c) おしめ (お襁褓 - diaper): This noun refers to an object (おしめをする: put on a diaper) and does not combine with ばかりしている to describe the action in this sentence.
default.q.n2-10-q11-11.why.3: (d) いたずら (悪戯 - mischief, pranks): いたずらをする means “to be mischievous” or “to fool around.” Combined with ばかりしている, it naturally and correctly describes a child who does nothing but mischief.
default.q.n2-10-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あまやか注ない (甘やかさない).
default.q.n2-10-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “It is very difficult to raise children without spoiling them.”
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese reading notes: 甘やかす (to indulge, spoil), 育てる (そだてる - to raise, bring up, teach).
- Grammar: V-ない + ように + 育てる (to raise someone so that they do not...).
- Example: 一人っ子だからといって、あまり甘やかしてはいけない。(You should not spoil a child too much just because they are an only child.)
default.q.n2-10-q12-12.why.0: (a) なぐらない (殴らない — not hitting): This does not fit the general standard of child-rearing; not hitting one’s child is not a difficult issue in educational methods in the way avoiding overindulgence is.
default.q.n2-10-q12-12.why.1: (b) あまやか注ない (甘やかさない, not overindulge): 甘やかす means to indulge or spoil someone. 甘やかさないように育てる (raise someone without overindulging them) is a difficult issue in child-rearing and fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n2-10-q12-12.why.2: (c) いじめない (苛めない—do not bully) is not used to describe a parent's child-rearing method.
default.q.n2-10-q12-12.why.3: (d) しつけない (躾けない - not instilling discipline): This is the opposite of the goal of raising children, which requires teaching them proper discipline.
default.q.n2-10-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 近寄る.
default.q.n2-10-q13-13.explanation:
Sentence translation: “If you get too close to that dog again, it will bite you.”
- Vocabulary: 近寄る (ちかよる): to approach or get close; 噛まれる (かまれる): to be bitten, the passive form of 噛む.
- Distinction: 近寄る (intransitive verb: to get close) vs. 近づける (transitive verb: to bring something closer).
- Example: 危ないですから、電車に近寄らないでください。(It's dangerous, so please don't go near the train.)
default.q.n2-10-q13-13.why.0: (a) 近づける (ちかづける): a transitive verb meaning to bring something or someone closer (~を~に近づける). Here, the subject moves closer to the dog themselves, so using this transitive verb is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.n2-10-q13-13.why.1: (b) 近寄る (ちかよる): An intransitive verb used with に (〜に近寄る: approach someone or something), so it is correct both grammatically and semantically in this warning.
default.q.n2-10-q13-13.why.2: (c) あばれる (暴れる): to run wild, cause a disturbance, or struggle. It does not fit the structure 「その犬に」in this context.
default.q.n2-10-q13-13.why.3: (d) つかまる (捕まる/掴まる) means to be caught or to cling to something; it does not form a natural context for warning about the risk of being bitten by a dog when approaching it.
default.q.n2-10-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ひ流くり返して (ひっくり返して).
default.q.n2-10-q14-14.explanation:
Translation: “I accidentally knocked over the coffee cup.”
- Vocabulary: ひっくり返す (ひっくりかえす — transitive verb: to turn upside down, spill, knock over), used with the pattern ～てしまう to express an accidental action or regret.
- Corresponding intransitive verb: ひっくり返る (to be overturned, to be turned upside down).
- Example: 強く押されて、テーブルの上のコップがひっくり返った。(The glass on the table was knocked over because it was pushed hard.)
default.q.n2-10-q14-14.why.0: (a) はずして (外して): to remove, detach, or take off. It is not used for knocking over or spilling a cup of coffee.
default.q.n2-10-q14-14.why.1: (b) おぼれて (溺れて): to drown or become absorbed in something. It is an intransitive verb and is completely wrong in this context.
default.q.n2-10-q14-14.why.2: (c) 引っかかって (引っ掛かって - caught on/stuck): It is an intransitive verb (so it does not take an object marked by を), and its meaning also does not fit.
default.q.n2-10-q14-14.why.3: (d) ひ流くり返して (ひっくり返して) means “turn over, overturn, or spill.” It is a transitive verb used with を, as in コーヒーカップをひっくり返す (“spill/overturn a coffee cup”), and accurately describes accidentally spilling something.
default.q.n2-10-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 4. つく.
default.q.n2-10-q15-15.explanation:
Translation: “Eating out is expensive, so please try to cook for yourself from now on.”
- Important N2 idioms: 高くつく (たかくつく - to be costly, expensive), 安くつく (やすくつく - to be inexpensive, cost less).
- Vocabulary: 外食 (がいしょく - eating out), 自炊 (じすい - cooking for oneself), できるだけ (as much as possible).
- Example: 修理するより新しく買ったほうが安くつく。(Buying a new one costs less than having it repaired.)
default.q.n2-10-q15-15.why.0: (a) する: 高くする means “to make something more expensive” (actively raise the price); it is not used to express costs becoming inflated or expensive.
default.q.n2-10-q15-15.why.1: (b) とる: 高くとる means “to charge a high price / fee,” and is not used in a sentence expressing a personal assessment of food expenses.
default.q.n2-10-q15-15.why.2: (c) でる: There is no idiomatic expression '高くでる' meaning that the cost is expensive.
default.q.n2-10-q15-15.why.3: (d) つく: It forms the idiom「高くつく」(たかくつく), meaning “to be expensive, to cost a lot” (the opposite of「安くつく」: to be inexpensive or economical), so it is completely correct.
default.q.n2-10-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (指定), because 「席が指定される」is the standard usage for assigning a specific seat.
default.q.n2-10-q16-16.explanation:
Sentence translation: "Because the seats are not assigned in advance, please sit wherever you like."
- Vocabulary and on'yomi:
  + 指定: designation, advance selection. Common expression: 指定席 (reserved/assigned seat) >< 自由席 (unreserved seat).
  + 推定 (estimation), 断定 (assertion, definitive statement), 仮定 (assumption).
- Example: 新幹線の指定席をあらかじめ予約しておいた。(I reserved an assigned seat on the Shinkansen in advance.)
default.q.n2-10-q16-16.why.0: Incorrect because「推定」(an estimate or inference based on data/evidence) is not used to describe dividing up or assigning seats.
default.q.n2-10-q16-16.why.1: Incorrect because 「断定」 means making a definite assertion or conclusive judgment about something, which does not fit the context of a seat.
default.q.n2-10-q16-16.why.2: Correct because 「指定」 (“designated” or “specified”) combines with 席 in 「席は指定されていません」 (“seats are not assigned in advance,” meaning open seating).
default.q.n2-10-q16-16.why.3: Incorrect because 「仮定」means a hypothesis or assumption, setting up a hypothetical situation in reasoning or mathematics; it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-10-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (コピー), because the context involves copying or photocopying meeting materials into 20 sets for 20 people.
default.q.n2-10-q17-17.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Please photocopy 20 copies of this document for the 20 participants before the meeting starts."
- Katakana vocabulary:
  + コピー (copy): photocopy; copying. Expression: コピーをとる (to photocopy a document).
  + ～人分 (~にんぶん): an amount intended for ~ people (e.g., 20人分の書類 — documents for 20 people).
- Example: 会議の資料を参加者の人数分コピーしてください。(Please photocopy enough meeting materials for all the participants.)
default.q.n2-10-q17-17.why.0: Incorrect. 「テーマ」, meaning a subject or topic, is an abstract noun for discussion or research and cannot be used to count printed copies or portions for people (20人分).
default.q.n2-10-q17-17.why.1: Incorrect because 「シーツ」 means “bed sheet” and is unrelated to meeting documents.
default.q.n2-10-q17-17.why.2: Incorrect because「カラー」(color/collar) does not combine appropriately with 書類 to indicate the number of copies distributed to 20 people.
default.q.n2-10-q17-17.why.3: This is correct because 「コピー」 (a copy or photocopy) forms 「書類のコピー」 (photocopies of documents), and combining it with 「20人分」 (20 portions for 20 people) is natural and accurate.
default.q.n2-10-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (格別) because 格別 expresses an exceptionally special degree, far beyond the usual level (intense heat unlike other years).
default.q.n2-10-q18-18.explanation:
Translation of the sentence: "This summer's heat has been unusually intense, so I sleep every night with the air conditioner left on."
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese reading:
  + 格別: exceptional, unusually intense, far beyond normal. Similar expressions: 特別 (special), 非常に (very).
  + ～たまま: leave a state unchanged while doing something (クーラーをつけたまま寝る: sleep with the air conditioner left on).
- Example: 今年の冬の寒さは格別だ。(This winter's cold is exceptionally severe.)
default.q.n2-10-q18-18.why.0: Correct because 「格別」 means “exceptional, special, or remarkably different,” emphasizing that something is far more notable than usual (this year's heat is exceptionally severe).
default.q.n2-10-q18-18.why.1: Incorrect because 「過剰」 (excessive, more than necessary) is generally used for quantities, reactions, or qualities that exceed the necessary level, such as 栄養過剰 or 自信過剰. It is not used with hot weather.
default.q.n2-10-q18-18.why.2: Incorrect because 「巨大」 (“huge,” “enormous”) describes the size of an object or the scale of a structure or organization, not the intensity of the weather.
default.q.n2-10-q18-18.why.3: Incorrect because 「強引」means forceful, coercive, or pushy, describing an attitude or action that pressures others to comply, as in 強引な態度; it does not describe the weather.
default.q.n2-10-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ながめ) because ながめ (眺め) refers to a view or scenery, fitting perfectly with the verb 見る (to look at or view).
default.q.n2-10-q19-19.explanation:
Sentence translation: “The view of the rows of mountains covered in autumn leaves from this hotel is breathtaking.”
- Vocabulary & kanji:
  + 眺め (ながめ): view, scenery, panorama visible to the eye (derived from 眺める).
  + 紅葉 (こうよう / もみじ): autumn leaves; 紅葉する: turn red in autumn.
- Example: 部屋の窓からの海の眺めが素晴らしい。(The view of the sea from the room window is wonderful.)
default.q.n2-10-q19-19.why.0: Correct because 「ながめ」 (眺め) describes the scenery or view visible when looking from the hotel toward the mountains covered with autumn foliage.
default.q.n2-10-q19-19.why.1: Incorrect because 「ひびき」(響き), meaning resonance or sound, is related to hearing and sound, not 見る.
default.q.n2-10-q19-19.why.2: Incorrect because「かおり」(香り—scent) is related to the sense of smell and is not suitable for describing mountain scenery.
default.q.n2-10-q19-19.why.3: Incorrect because 「のぞみ」 (望み: hope, aspiration) refers to a wish in one’s mind and is not used for a view or scenery that one sees.
default.q.n2-10-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (やたらに) because the adverb やたらに indicates an excessive degree or something happening repeatedly or incessantly beyond the usual limit.
default.q.n2-10-q20-20.explanation:
Translation: "Since early this morning, the phone has been ringing incessantly, so the work I started has barely progressed."
- Vocabulary and grammar:
  + やたらに (or やたらと): excessively and repeatedly, indiscriminately, or for no apparent reason (e.g., やたらと喉が渇く — to feel unusually thirsty all the time).
  + やり始める (V-ます + 始める: to begin doing something).
  + なかなか～ない: to be unable to... despite trying / to take a long time to...
- Example: 今日はやたらと迷惑電話がかかってくる。(Spam calls keep coming incessantly today.)
default.q.n2-10-q20-20.why.0: Incorrect because 「なんとか」 (somehow, by one means or another) describes managing to achieve a result through effort (as in なんとか間に合った); it does not modify a large quantity.
default.q.n2-10-q20-20.why.1: Incorrect because「とにかく」(anyway, first of all) is used to change the topic or emphasize an immediate priority; it does not mean continuous, rapid frequency.
default.q.n2-10-q20-20.why.2: Incorrect because 「おおよそ」 (roughly, approximately, approximately speaking) is used to estimate a number or summarize content, as in おおよその見積もり, and does not modify this sentence appropriately.
default.q.n2-10-q20-20.why.3: Correct because 「やたらに」 (continuously, excessively, more than usual) combines with 「電話が多い」 to describe an excessive number of incoming calls repeatedly interrupting work.
default.q.n2-10-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (厳重に) because 厳重に警備される is the standard expression meaning to be strictly and carefully guarded or protected.
default.q.n2-10-q21-21.explanation:
Sentence translation: "The area around the National Diet Building is under very tight security."
- Vocabulary and kanji terms:
  + 厳重 (げんじゅう): strict, rigorous, tight. Common expressions: 厳重に注意する (give a stern warning), 厳重に保管する (store securely), 厳重な警備 (tight security).
  + 警備 (けいび): security, guarding, protection.
  + 国会議事堂: National Diet Building.
- Example: 空港では手荷物検査が厳重に行われている。(Baggage inspections are conducted very strictly at airports.)
default.q.n2-10-q21-21.why.0: Incorrect because 「独特に」 describes a distinctive individual quality, such as 独特な匂い, and is not used for security operations.
default.q.n2-10-q21-21.why.1: Incorrect because 「重大に」(serious, grave) describes great importance or serious consequences (e.g., 重大な問題, 重大事件), and does not modify 警備する.
default.q.n2-10-q21-21.why.2: Correct because 「厳重に」 (strictly, securely, rigorously) naturally combines with 「厳重に警備される」 (be strictly and securely guarded), making it the most accurate usage.
default.q.n2-10-q21-21.why.3: Incorrect because「特定に」is generally used in the modifying form「特定の～」(a specific object), not as an adverb modifying 警備されている.
default.q.n2-10-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (くだいた) because 砕く (to crush or break into pieces) is commonly used for hard objects such as ice (氷を砕く).
default.q.n2-10-q22-22.explanation:
Sentence translation: “Put crushed ice into a glass, then pour in black tea.”
- Vocabulary and distinctions among verbs describing changes in form:
  + 砕く (literally “碎” / くだく): to crush or break something hard into small pieces (氷を砕く: crush ice; 骨を砕く: shatter a bone; 心を砕く: take great pains).
  + 刻む (literally “刻” / きざむ): to mince or chop finely with a knife; to carve.
  + 潰す (literally “溃” / つぶす): to flatten or mash by pressing down (缶をつぶす: crush a can; トマトをつぶす: mash a tomato).
  + 崩す (literally “崩” / くずす): to break up a structure or shape; to exchange a large bill for smaller denominations (千円札を崩す).
- Example: ミキサーで氷を細かく砕いてスムージーを作る。(I crush ice finely in a blender to make a smoothie.)
default.q.n2-10-q22-22.why.0: Incorrect because 「くずした」, from 崩す, means to spoil a form, cause something to collapse, or exchange large bills for small change; it is not used for breaking or crushing a stone.
default.q.n2-10-q22-22.why.1: Correct because 「くだいた」(砕く - to smash, crush) is the appropriate verb with 「氷」; 「氷を砕く」means to crush or break ice into small pieces.
default.q.n2-10-q22-22.why.2: Incorrect because 「きざんだ」(刻む—to chop, mince, or engrave) is used for cutting food such as vegetables into small pieces or for carving, not for ice.
default.q.n2-10-q22-22.why.3: Incorrect because 「つぶした」, from 潰す, means to crush or flatten something by pressing it, as with a can or potatoes, and is not used with a hard stone.
default.q.n2-10-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (静かに), because 「そっと」 means gently or quietly and is synonymous with 「静かに」 in the context of whispering into someone’s ear.
default.q.n2-10-q23-23.explanation:
Meaning: I quietly whispered "I love you" into her ear.
Related Sino-Japanese vocabulary:
- 耳元 (みみもと): by or close to the ear.
- 静か (しずか): quiet, gentle, softly.
Extended example: 赤ちゃんが起きないように、ドアをそっと閉めた。(I gently closed the door so that the baby would not wake up.)
default.q.n2-10-q23-23.why.0: (a) Correct: 「静かに」 means quietly, gently, or softly; when describing whispering softly into someone's ear, it is synonymous with 「そっと」.
default.q.n2-10-q23-23.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「はっきりと」 means “clearly” or “distinctly,” which does not match the gentle, discreet nuance of 「そっと」.
default.q.n2-10-q23-23.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「急に」 (suddenly, unexpectedly) does not fit a context involving speaking quietly.
default.q.n2-10-q23-23.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「大声で」 means loudly or in a loud voice, which is completely opposite to 「そっと」.
default.q.n2-10-q24-24.verdict: According to the provided answer key, choose 2 (検討して). However, 「検討して」 (“consider carefully”) is actually a synonymous replacement for 「十分に考え(ながら)」 in the sentence, not a synonym for 「解決していかなければならない」.
default.q.n2-10-q24-24.explanation:
Meaning: We must both carefully consider this issue and resolve it.
Related Sino-Japanese terms:
- 解決: solving a problem.
- 検討: examining, considering, or studying something carefully.
- 十分: sufficiently, thoroughly.
Note on the question: There appears to be confusion about the word being tested; the answer choices are te-forms intended to replace 「十分に考えながら / 十分に考えて」 (with 「検討して」 as the correct choice), not synonyms for 「解決していかなければならない」.
Example with 「検討」: その提案について前向きに検討いたします。(We will give your proposal careful and positive consideration.)
default.q.n2-10-q24-24.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「工夫して」 means devising a way to do something and making efforts to improve a method; it is not synonymous with 「十分に考えて / 検討して」.
default.q.n2-10-q24-24.why.1: (b) Correct (according to the given answer). 「検討して」 means to examine, consider, or study something carefully, equivalent to 「十分に考えて」 in the original sentence.
default.q.n2-10-q24-24.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「理解して」 means to understand or comprehend; it does not mean to examine or carefully consider an option.
default.q.n2-10-q24-24.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「反省して」means to reflect on one’s own faults or conduct, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-10-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (うるさい) because 「さわがしい」 means noisy or boisterous and is synonymous with 「うるさい」.
default.q.n2-10-q25-25.explanation:
Meaning: The classroom is very noisy.
Related kanji:
- 教室 (きょうしつ): classroom.
- 騒がしい (さわがしい): noisy, bustling, boisterous.
Expanded example: 外が騒がしいので、何があったのか見に行った。(It was so noisy outside that I went to see what had happened.)
default.q.n2-10-q25-25.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「荒っぽい」 (あらっぽい - rough) means rough, violent, brusque, or aggressive; it is not used to describe a noisy space.
default.q.n2-10-q25-25.why.1: (b) Correct: 「うるさい」 means noisy or bothersome because of excessive noise; it is synonymous with 「さわがしい」 (騒がしい).
default.q.n2-10-q25-25.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「あわただしい」 means busy, rushed, or hurried in terms of time or work; it is not synonymous with noisy.
default.q.n2-10-q25-25.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「おだやか」(穏やか) means gentle, calm, or peaceful; it is opposite in meaning to 「さわがしい」.
default.q.n2-10-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (かつて), because「以前」means formerly or in the past and is synonymous with「かつて」in a recollective context.
default.q.n2-10-q26-26.explanation:
Meaning: There used to be a park around this area.
Related Sino-Japanese roots:
- 以前 (いぜん): previously, in the past.
- 公園 (こうえん): park.
Additional example: ここはかつて緑豊かな森だった。(This place was once a lush green forest.)
default.q.n2-10-q26-26.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「第一に」 (だいいちに) means “first” or “most importantly,” and is used when listing priorities.
default.q.n2-10-q26-26.why.1: (b) Correct: 「かつて」 means “once,” “formerly,” or “in the past”; it is synonymous with 「以前」 (いぜん) or 「昔」 when referring to a past time or period.
default.q.n2-10-q26-26.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「先に」 (さきに) means doing something first, before someone else, or being ahead/in front; it is not used to mean the distant past, as かつて does.
default.q.n2-10-q26-26.why.3: (d) Incorrect:「真っ先に」(まっさきに) means first of all or before everyone else; it is not synonymous with「以前」.
default.q.n2-10-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (こらえて) because 「がまんする」 means to endure or put up with pain and is synonymous with 「こらえる」.
default.q.n2-10-q27-27.explanation:
Meaning: Although I had a toothache, I endured the pain and continued working.
Related kanji notes:
- 歯: tooth.
- 痛い: painful.
- 我慢: patience, endurance.
- 堪える: to endure or suppress pain, tears, or other feelings.
- 継続 / 続ける: to continue.
Example: 彼は痛みをこらえて、最後まで走り切った。(He endured the pain and ran all the way to the finish.)
default.q.n2-10-q27-27.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「こもって」 (こもる / 籠る) means to shut oneself away in an enclosed room, or for heat or smoke to become trapped; it does not mean to endure pain.
default.q.n2-10-q27-27.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「だまって」 (だまる / 黙る) means to remain silent or say nothing; it does not express enduring physical pain.
default.q.n2-10-q27-27.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「ふざけて」(ふざける) means joking around, fooling around, or acting cheeky, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-10-q27-27.why.3: (d) Correct: 「こらえて」 (こらえる / 堪える) means to endure or suppress pain, emotions, or tears; it is synonymous with 「がまんして」 (我慢して).
default.q.n2-10-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because 「気候がおだやか」 is the standard expression for describing the mild climate of an island region.
default.q.n2-10-q28-28.explanation:
「気候」（きこう - climate）refers to the overall weather characteristics of a particular region over many years (e.g., a mild climate or tropical climate). It differs from 「天気」 (short-term weather on a given day or hour) and 「気温」 (air temperature).
Example: 日本は地域によって気候が大きく異なります。(In Japan, the climate differs greatly from region to region.)
default.q.n2-10-q28-28.why.0: Correct because 「気候」refers to the stable, long-term weather conditions of a region; 「気候がおだやかで、すごしやすい」(the climate is mild and easy to live in) is completely appropriate.
default.q.n2-10-q28-28.why.1: Incorrect because changes between hot and cold temperatures at night require 「気温」 (air temperature), not 「気候」 (climate).
default.q.n2-10-q28-28.why.2: Incorrect because March is the season or time of graduation, so use「季節」(season) or「時期」(time/period), not「気候」.
default.q.n2-10-q28-28.why.3: Incorrect because the weather on a specific day, such as tomorrow, should be expressed with 「天気」 or 「天候」, not 「気候」, which refers to long-term climate.
default.q.n2-10-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because the structure 「たとえ〜ても」 is correctly used to express a concessive assumption (“even if...”).
default.q.n2-10-q29-29.explanation:
「たとえ」(adverb: even if, no matter) always accompanies the concessive hypothetical pattern 「たとえ〜ても／でも」. It means that even if the assumed situation—often difficult or unfavorable—occurs, the result or determination in the following clause will not change.
Example: たとえ反対されても、自分の信じる道を進みたい。(Even if I am opposed, I want to continue along the path I believe in.)
default.q.n2-10-q29-29.why.0: Incorrect because 「たとえ」 does not go with the favorable condition 「〜なら」; the hypothetical positive condition here should use 「もし」.
default.q.n2-10-q29-29.why.1: Incorrect because 「〜のに」 expresses a factual contrast that has occurred and cannot be combined with the concessive hypothetical adverb 「たとえ」.
default.q.n2-10-q29-29.why.2: Correct because it follows the standard grammar pattern 「たとえ〜ても」, meaning “even if I fail once or twice, I will not give up.”
default.q.n2-10-q29-29.why.3: Incorrect. A hypothetical condition expressing a wish, 「〜たら、〜たい」, takes the adverb 「もし / もしも」, not 「たとえ」.
default.q.n2-10-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because 「（水で）薄める」 precisely means to dilute a chemical solution with water.
default.q.n2-10-q30-30.explanation:
「薄める」（うすめる - transitive verb）means to dilute a solution or make the flavor milder (such as sauce or soup) by adding water or another liquid.
Example: 味が濃すぎるので、お湯を入れてスープを薄めた。(The flavor was too strong, so I added hot water to dilute the soup.)
default.q.n2-10-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect because expressing “wear thinner clothing” requires「着るものを薄くする」or「薄着にする」, not the verb「薄める」, which means to dilute.
default.q.n2-10-q30-30.why.1: Correct because 「薄める」 combines with 「水で」 in the standard expression for diluting medicine or chemicals before use.
default.q.n2-10-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect because choosing a lighter-colored vehicle requires the adjective phrase 「薄い色にする」, not the verb 「色を薄める」.
default.q.n2-10-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect because squinting in bright light is expressed by the idiom 「目を細める」, not 「目を薄める」.
default.q.n2-10-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 4 because 「甘やかされて育つ」 is the standard expression for being spoiled while growing up.
default.q.n2-10-q31-31.explanation:
「甘やかす」（あまやかす: transitive verb）means to spoil or indulge someone excessively, usually an adult indulging a child, by satisfying all their demands and making them spoiled or dependent.
Example: 一人っ子だからといって、あまり甘やかしてはいけない。(You should not spoil a child too much just because they are an only child.)
default.q.n2-10-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because adding sugar to sweeten a drink requires 「甘くする」, not 「甘やかす」, which refers only to indulging a person.
default.q.n2-10-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect. A pet’s whining, spoiled voice should be expressed with 「甘えた声」, not the passive form 「甘やかされた声」.
default.q.n2-10-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect because being praised by a superior for doing a good job requires 「ほめてもらった」, not 「甘やかす」.
default.q.n2-10-q31-31.why.3: Correct because 「甘やかされて育つ」 (to grow up being spoiled) is a natural and accurate word combination in Japanese.
default.q.n2-10-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 4 because 「いったん」 describes temporarily doing something first (going home for a while and then returning).
default.q.n2-10-q32-32.explanation:
「いったん」（一旦 - adverb）has two typical uses:
1. To do something temporarily first, then continue or do something else: 「いったん〜してから...」
2. Once something has happened or begun, usually used with たら/ば/以上: 「いったん始めたら、最後までやり通そう。」
Example: いったんホテルに寄って荷物を置いてから、食事に行きましょう。(Let's stop by the hotel and leave our luggage before going out to eat.)
default.q.n2-10-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because “only once” requires 「一度だけ / 一回だけ」, not 「いったん」.
default.q.n2-10-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect. The frequency “once a week” must be expressed as 「週に一度」 or 「週に一回」, not 「いったん」.
default.q.n2-10-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect. To express “not having gone even once,” use「一度も」, not「いったんも」.
default.q.n2-10-q32-32.why.3: Correct because 「いったん」is used appropriately for temporarily carrying out an action first, such as going home briefly and then returning.
default.q.n2-10-q1-1.explanation:
• Meaning: According to the weather forecast, sunny weather will continue throughout the Japanese archipelago next week.
• Sino-Japanese components: 予 (forecast) + 報 (report) = 予報 (forecast; commonly used in 天気予報).
• Example: 台風の進路予報を確認する。(Check the typhoon track forecast.)
default.q.n2-10-q1-1.why.0: (a) Correct. 「予報」is correctly read as 「よほう」.
default.q.n2-10-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「予」 is read only as 「よ」; it does not have the long-vowel reading 「よう」.
default.q.n2-10-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「報」 (meaning “report”) has the long-vowel reading 「ほう」, not 「ぼう」. 「よぼう」 is the reading of 「予防」 (prevention).
default.q.n2-10-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the kanji 「予」has been incorrectly lengthened to 「よう」.
default.q.n2-10-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (よんわりびき).
default.q.n2-10-q2-2.explanation:
• Meaning: All the products displayed on this shelf are 40% off.
• Vocabulary: 四 (four) + 割 (わり; 1 割 = 10%) + 引 (ひき/びき; discount) → 四割引き = a four-tenths discount (40% off).
• Example: タイムセールで全品二割引き（にわりびき）になった。(During the time sale, all items were 20% off.)
default.q.n2-10-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the number four 「四」is read as 「よん」, not 「し」, before the unit 「割」(わり).
default.q.n2-10-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「四」 is read as 「よん」, not 「よ」, and the final 「引」 undergoes rendaku, becoming 「びき」 rather than remaining 「ひき」.
default.q.n2-10-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「四」is not read 「よつ」when combined with the counter 「割」.
default.q.n2-10-q2-2.why.3: (d) Correct. 「四割引き」(40% off) is correctly read 「よんわりびき」.
default.q.n2-10-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (あまったら).
default.q.n2-10-q3-3.explanation:
• Meaning: Please give each person 10 pieces of the candy in this box. Then, if there are any left over, return them.
• Sino-Japanese reading: 余 (あまる: surplus, left over).
• Example: 時間が余ったら、もう一度見直してください。(If you have time left over, please check it again.)
default.q.n2-10-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「のこったら」 is the conditional form of the verb 「残る」 (to remain, be left over).
default.q.n2-10-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「しまったら」is the conditional form of the verb 「仕舞う / 閉まう」 (to put away / close).
default.q.n2-10-q3-3.why.2: (c) Correct. The verb 「余る」(to be left over) is read 「あまる」, and its conditional form is 「あまったら」.
default.q.n2-10-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「くばったら」 is the conditional form of 「配る」(PHỐI - distribute).
default.q.n2-10-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (ふくそう).
default.q.n2-10-q4-4.explanation:
• Translation: The main reason this style of clothing quickly became popular among young people was probably the spread of television, which allowed information to reach the entire country at the same time.
• Kanji etymology: 服 (fuku) + 装 (sō) = 服装 (clothing, attire).
• Example: 面接には清潔な服装で行くべきだ。(You should wear clean, neat clothing to an interview.)
default.q.n2-10-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「ふくしょく」 is the reading of 「服飾」 (clothing and accessories).
default.q.n2-10-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「装」 (Trang) has the long-vowel reading 「そう」, not the short sound 「そく」.
default.q.n2-10-q4-4.why.2: (c) Correct. 「服装」 (clothing, attire, the way one dresses) is correctly read 「ふくそう」.
default.q.n2-10-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「装」does not have the on-reading 「しょう」in this word.
default.q.n2-10-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (はいいろ).
default.q.n2-10-q5-5.explanation:
• Meaning: From the gloomy gray sky, it looks as though it is about to rain.
• Kanji note: 灰 (はい: ash) + 色 (いろ: color) = 灰色 (gray; ash-colored).
• Example: 彼は灰色のスーツを着ている。(He is wearing a gray suit.)
default.q.n2-10-q5-5.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「色」 is read as 「いろ」, not 「きろ」.
default.q.n2-10-q5-5.why.1: (b) Correct. 「灰色」(gray) is a compound read entirely with kun-readings: 「はいいろ」.
default.q.n2-10-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「灰」 is read as 「はい」, not 「ばい」.
default.q.n2-10-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「色」 retains the reading 「いろ」; it does not undergo voicing to become 「ぎろ」.
default.q.n2-10-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 発刊 (to publish or issue a magazine, book, or newspaper).
default.q.n2-10-q6-6.explanation:
- Meaning: On the occasion of publishing the magazine, we decided to solicit name suggestions from the public.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 発刊 (begin publishing or issuing a publication, magazine, or book).
- Example: 新しい月刊誌が来月から発刊される。(A new monthly magazine will be published starting next month.)
default.q.n2-10-q6-6.why.0: (a) 初巻 (Sho-kan) is read 「しょかん」 and means the first volume in a series of books.
default.q.n2-10-q6-6.why.1: (b) 初刊 is read as 「しょかん」 and means the first issue or first edition.
default.q.n2-10-q6-6.why.2: (c) 発巻 is an incorrect kanji combination and does not form a meaningful Japanese word.
default.q.n2-10-q6-6.why.3: (d) 発刊 is correctly read as 「はっかん」and means publishing or issuing a publication, book, newspaper, or magazine.
default.q.n2-10-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 高学歴 (high educational attainment).
default.q.n2-10-q7-7.explanation:
