default.q.n2-18-q38-38.why.2: (c) Correct because 「N に向かって（むかって）」 means 'toward N,' and combined with 「まっすぐ進む」 (rendered as ま流すぐ due to an OCR error), it forms the complete phrase 'move straight toward the goal.'
default.q.n2-18-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「～にあって」 means “in a particular circumstance or position” and is used in formal written language, not simply to indicate the direction of an action.
default.q.n2-18-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ぬきで.
default.q.n2-18-q39-39.explanation: Meaning: “Putting jokes aside, please think seriously.” Grammar: 「N 抜きで / 抜きにして（ぬきで）」 means leaving N out, putting N aside, or disregarding N. Common expression: 「冗談抜きで」 (no more joking / seriously). Kanji note: 冗談 (a joke), 抜く (to pull out / leave out), 考える (to think). Example: 冗談抜きで、これからの進路について話し合おう (Seriously, let's discuss our future plans).
default.q.n2-18-q39-39.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「ぬいて」 is the te-form of the verb 「抜く」 and cannot directly follow a noun to form an adverbial expression meaning exclusion, as in 「抜きで」.
default.q.n2-18-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect. If the verb 「する」 is used, the particle 「は」 is required: 「冗談はしないで」. It also does not form the standard N2 expression 「冗談抜きで」.
default.q.n2-18-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「しても」 (even if one jokes) is completely inconsistent both grammatically and logically with the clause requiring seriousness.
default.q.n2-18-q39-39.why.3: (d) Correct because 「N 抜きで（ぬきで）」 means "leaving N out / putting N aside," forming the fixed expression 「冗談抜きで」 (seriously / no kidding).
default.q.n2-18-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 3. じゃないか.
default.q.n2-18-q40-40.explanation: Sentence meaning: “Don’t stay cooped up at home all the time anymore—let’s go see a movie or do something!” Grammar: 「V-よう ＋ じゃないか」is an enthusiastic pattern used to invite, urge, or encourage the listener to do something together. Kanji readings: 家 (home), 映画 (movie), 見る (to watch), 行く (to go). Example: みんなで力を合わせて、この困難を乗り越えようじゃないか (Let’s join forces and overcome this difficulty together!).
default.q.n2-18-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「～まいか」 expresses negative volition or appears in the hesitant-choice pattern 「～ようか～まいか」 (“whether to do it or not”), and is not used to make an invitation after 「行こう」.
default.q.n2-18-q40-40.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「～ようともしない」 means "not even bother to / have no intention of doing something"; it is not used to invite someone.
default.q.n2-18-q40-40.why.2: (c) Correct because the pattern 「V-ようじゃないか」 (here, 「行こうじゃないか」) is used to enthusiastically invite or call on someone to do something together.
default.q.n2-18-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「～ようともする」 describes an action one is attempting or preparing to carry out; it is not used at the end of a sentence as an invitation.
default.q.n2-18-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. くれた.
default.q.n2-18-q41-41.explanation: Meaning of the sentence: "Today is the graduation ceremony, so I will wear the scarf my younger sister bought for me when I go out." The grammar expresses giving and receiving: 「[Someone else] が 私に V-てくれる」 describes someone else performing an action that benefits the speaker. くれる is used because the subject is the speaker’s younger sister, a family member who is younger than the speaker. Kanji-related terms: 卒業式 (graduation ceremony), 妹 (younger sister), 私 (I), 買う (buy). Example: 誕生日に友達がプレゼントしてくれた時計を大切にしている (I treasure the watch my friend gave me for my birthday).
default.q.n2-18-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「いただいた」 is the humble form of 「もらった」, so the subject must be the recipient (「私が」); it cannot be used with 「妹が私に」.
default.q.n2-18-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「くださった」 (with さ misread as 注 in the scan) is the honorific form of 「くれた」. It is used when the giver is a superior or respected partner, not for a younger sister in the family.
default.q.n2-18-q41-41.why.2: (c) Correct because with 「もらった」, the subject must be the person who received the action (「私が」), whereas in this sentence the person who bought the item is the younger sister (「妹が」).
default.q.n2-18-q41-41.why.3: (d) Correct because the structure 「A が私に V-てくれた」expresses another person, such as a peer, younger person, or family member, doing something for the speaker (“the towel that my younger sister bought for me”).
default.q.n2-18-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 1. になって.
default.q.n2-18-q42-42.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Please wait here."
Honorific language (敬語): 「お＋V(stem without masu)＋になる」 is the respectful form used to show respect for the other person's action. The complete polite request pattern is 「お～になってください」 (equivalent to 「お～ください」).
Sino-Japanese character meaning: 待つ (to wait).
Example: こちらのお席にお掛けになってお待ちください (Please take this seat and wait a moment.)
default.q.n2-18-q42-42.why.0: (a) Correct. The respectful form「お＋V (masu-stem)＋になる」becomes「お＋V (masu-stem)＋になってください」in a polite request; here, it is「お待ちになってください」.
default.q.n2-18-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「お＋V (masu-stem)＋して」 is the humble form 「お～する」, used for the speaker’s own actions. It cannot be combined with 「ください」 to ask the other person to wait.
default.q.n2-18-q42-42.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「にな注った」 contains a character-recognition error and is also in the past form (-た), so it cannot directly precede 「ください」.
default.q.n2-18-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「注せて」 (a misrecognition of させて) is the causative form and does not form a standard honorific expression in a request.
default.q.n2-18-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. からには.
default.q.n2-18-q43-43.explanation: Meaning: "Once you have accepted this job, you should give it everything you have." The grammar pattern 「V (plain form) ＋ からには」 means "once... then naturally one must..." The following clause commonly expresses intention, duty, determination, or an appeal (～よう / ～つもりだ / ～べきだ). Sino-Vietnamese readings: 仕事 (SĨ SỰ - work), 引き受ける (DẪN THỦ - to undertake), 全力 (TOÀN LỰC - all one’s strength). Example: 約束したからには、どんなことがあっても守らなければならない (Once you have made a promise, you must keep it no matter what happens).
default.q.n2-18-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「からに」is not a complete structure for connecting a dictionary-form verb to an expression of volition; only idiomatic expressions such as「見るからに」exist.
default.q.n2-18-q43-43.why.1: (b) Correct because the pattern 「V-る / V-た ＋ からには」 means “once one has..., one must...” The following clause expresses determination: 「全力でやろう」 (“Once I have accepted the job, I will give it my all”).
default.q.n2-18-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「～を限りに」 means "from" or "until the end of" a time limit; it does not follow the dictionary form to express a volitional condition.
default.q.n2-18-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「かぎりで」 (“within the scope of”) is grammatically and semantically unsuitable before a clause expressing determination.
default.q.n2-18-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1. つき.
default.q.n2-18-q44-44.explanation: Meaning: "The water bill costs about 3,000 yen per month." Grammar: 「Number / unit ＋ につき」means "per each / for every unit" and indicates a rate, allowance, or corresponding unit price. Kanji readings: 水道代 (water bill; in the scanned question, 代 was mistakenly printed as 答), 一か月 (one month), 円 (yen). Example: この駐車場は、1時間につき500円かかります (This parking lot charges 500 yen per hour).
default.q.n2-18-q44-44.why.0: (a) Correct because the pattern 「Number/Unit ＋ につき」 means “per...” or “for each...,” and is used to express a recurring unit price (“The water bill is 3,000 yen per month”).
default.q.n2-18-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「～にとって」means “for” or “from the standpoint of,” and is not used for a billing cycle unit.
default.q.n2-18-q44-44.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「～にわたり（にわたって）」means “throughout” an extended continuous period or broad range; it does not indicate a periodic cost unit.
default.q.n2-18-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「～にかけて」 is generally used in the pattern 「A から B にかけて」 (“from A to B”), not with 「一か月に」 to indicate a unit price.
default.q.n2-18-q45-45.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 3 → 4; the choice in the ★ position is 3 (ものすごい).
default.q.n2-18-q45-45.explanation:
Complete sentence: ちょっと信じられないことだが、もしそれが事実としたらものすごい発見だ。
Translation: It may be a little hard to believe, but if it is true, it would be an incredible discovery.
default.q.n2-18-q45-45.why.0: (a) 「としたら」 follows the noun or clause 「中実（事実）」 to form the hypothetical structure 「もし～としたら」, meaning “supposing that...” or “if it were...”.
default.q.n2-18-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「中実」(or 事実) comes immediately after 「もしそれが」to form the hypothetical structure 「もしそれが中実（事実）としたら」.
default.q.n2-18-q45-45.why.2: (c) 「ものすごい」 is an i-adjective that directly modifies the noun 「発見」 immediately after it, so it belongs in the star-marked position (★).
default.q.n2-18-q45-45.why.3: (d) 「発見」 is a noun combined with 「だ」 at the end of the sentence and modified by 「ものすごい」 to form 「ものすごい発見だ」.
default.q.n2-18-q46-46.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1; the starred position (★) is answer choice 3 (として).
default.q.n2-18-q46-46.explanation:
Complete sentence: これは平和をテーマとして作られた作品です。
Meaning: This is a work created around the theme of peace.
default.q.n2-18-q46-46.why.0: (a) 「作られた」is a passive verb modifying the noun 「作品」at the end of the sentence, forming the phrase 「作られた作品です」(“it is a work that was created”).
default.q.n2-18-q46-46.why.1: (b) 「平和を」 comes first and connects to form the grammar pattern 「～をテーマとして」, meaning “taking peace as the theme.”
default.q.n2-18-q46-46.why.2: (c) 「として」 combines with 「平和をテーマ」 to form 「平和をテーマとして」 (“with peace as the theme”), and goes in the starred position (★).
default.q.n2-18-q46-46.why.3: (d) 「テーマ」 is a noun placed after 「平和を」 and before 「として」 in the pattern 「～をテーマとして」.
default.q.n2-18-q47-47.verdict: The correct order is 4 → 1 → 2 → 3; the starred ★ position is choice 2 (成長).
default.q.n2-18-q47-47.explanation:
Complete sentence: 学生とともに教師も成長していくべきだ。
Meaning: Teachers should also grow and develop together with their students.
default.q.n2-18-q47-47.why.0: (a) 「教師も」 serves as the subject of the following clause and comes immediately after 「学生とともに」 to express “the teacher also... together with the students.”
default.q.n2-18-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「成長」 is a noun that combines with 「していく」 to form the verb 「成長していく」, so it belongs in the starred position (★).
default.q.n2-18-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「していく」follows「成長」and combines with「べきだ」at the end to form the predicate「成長していくべきだ」(should continue to grow/develop).
default.q.n2-18-q47-47.why.3: (d) 「とともに」 follows the noun 「学生」 to form the grammar pattern 「～とともに」 (together with the students).
default.q.n2-18-q48-48.verdict: The correct order is 2 → 3 → 1 → 4; the starred ★ position is choice 1 (車を).
default.q.n2-18-q48-48.explanation:
Complete sentence: 係員の指示にしたがって車を止めてください。
Meaning: Please stop or park the car according to the staff member’s instructions.
default.q.n2-18-q48-48.why.0: (a) 「車を」is the object of the verb「止めて」that follows, so it belongs in the position marked ★.
default.q.n2-18-q48-48.why.1: (b) 「指示に」 follows 「係員の」 and combines with 「したがって」 to form 「係員の指示にしたがって」 (according to the staff member's instructions).
default.q.n2-18-q48-48.why.2: (c) 「したがって」 follows 「指示に」 in the grammar pattern 「～にしたがって」, meaning “in accordance with” or “following.”
default.q.n2-18-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「止めて」is the te-form of the verb and comes before「ください」to form the polite request「止めてください」(please stop or park).
default.q.n2-18-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1; the starred position (★) is answer choice 3 (作った).
default.q.n2-18-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 料理の本に書いてあるとおりに作ったのに失敗した。
Meaning: Although I followed the recipe exactly as written in the cookbook, I still failed.
default.q.n2-18-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「のに」is a conjunction expressing contrast or an unexpected result (“although...”), following「作った」and connecting to「失敗した」.
default.q.n2-18-q49-49.why.1: (b) 「書いてある」 follows 「料理の本に」 and modifies 「とおりに」, forming 「料理の本に書いてあるとおりに」 (“exactly as written in the cookbook”).
default.q.n2-18-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「作った」 is the past form of the verb in the conditional clause. It comes before 「のに」, takes the complement from 「とおりに」, and occupies the starred position (★).
default.q.n2-18-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「とおりに」follows the plain form「書いてある」in the grammar pattern「～とおりに」(exactly as / just as...).
default.q.n2-18-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 知っておきたい.
default.q.n2-18-q50-50.explanation: After posing the question “Then, how much could it be sold for?” about pricing a product, the author leads into an economics lesson and introduces a basic term: “In a case like this, there is a word we should know in advance (知っておきたい言葉があります). It is ‘demand and supply’ (需要と供給).” The structure 「〜ておきたい」combines 「〜ておく」(prepare or learn something in advance) with 「〜たい」and expresses the idea that one should learn or understand important knowledge beforehand.
default.q.n2-18-q50-50.why.0: (a) “知っている” means “to know/be aware of” and describes an established state of knowledge. It is unsuitable when the author is about to introduce and explain a new economic concept to the reader.
default.q.n2-18-q50-50.why.1: (b) “知らない” (“not know”) is negative, so it does not fit the logic of introducing a term that readers need to know.
default.q.n2-18-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「知っておきたい」 (“should/need to know in advance”) combines the grammar pattern 「〜ておく」 (“do or prepare in advance”) with 「〜たい」 (“want to/should”), modifying 「言葉」 to indicate an important term that readers should know beforehand.
default.q.n2-18-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「知ってみる」(“try knowing”) uses the grammar「〜てみる」(to try doing something), but it does not combine naturally with the cognition verb「知る」in this context.
default.q.n2-18-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 売ることができる.
default.q.n2-18-q51-51.explanation: The passage presents two contrasting definitions in parallel: “Demand” (需要) is the amount people want to buy (みんなが買いたがっている量), while “supply” (供給) is the amount of goods that can actually be sold on the market (実際に売ることができる量). Therefore, the structure「V-ることができる」expressing ability is the only correct choice for completing the definition.
default.q.n2-18-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「売ることができる」 (“can be sold”) uses the potential pattern 「〜ことができる」 to modify 「量」 and accurately expresses the definition of supply: the quantity of goods that can actually be sold on the market.
default.q.n2-18-q51-51.why.1: (b) "売れるはずがない" (“there is no way it can sell”) is a strongly negative prediction, completely contrary to the economic definition of the quantity of goods supplied.
default.q.n2-18-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「売れるわけにはいかない」 (“cannot be sold” because of ethical or situational constraints) expresses prohibition or an objective or psychological reason something cannot be done. It is not suitable for defining the concept.
default.q.n2-18-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「売れたかもしれません」 (“may have sold”) expresses a past conjecture, so it cannot be used to state a general definition or universal rule.
default.q.n2-18-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 一方.
default.q.n2-18-q52-52.explanation: The previous sentence analyzes the case where “many people want to buy → prices rise” (だから、商品の値段は上がります). The next sentence analyzes the opposite case: “few people want to buy while many want to sell → prices fall” (ですから、商品の値段は下がります). The conjunction 「一方」(on the other hand, conversely) is used to connect and contrast these two cases in the law of supply and demand.
default.q.n2-18-q52-52.why.0: (a) "つまり" (in other words / in short) is used to restate or summarize what came before, not to introduce a contrasting case.
default.q.n2-18-q52-52.why.1: (b) “一方” (“on the other hand” or “in contrast”) is a conjunction used to contrast two aspects or two opposing situations within the same topic (first, Demand > Supply causes prices to rise; then, Supply > Demand causes prices to fall).
default.q.n2-18-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「だから」 (therefore, so) expresses a straightforward cause-and-effect relationship, so it does not fit when the two sentences describe opposite price trends.
default.q.n2-18-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「ただし」(however / with the exception that) adds a limiting condition or exception to the preceding sentence; it is not used to present a parallel hypothetical contrast.
default.q.n2-18-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 3. その結果.
default.q.n2-18-q53-53.explanation: The previous sentence describes the action: Because prices were high, the producer thought that producing a large quantity would be profitable and made a great deal of merchandise (沢山商品を作ります). The following sentence describes the resulting development: When the market became flooded with goods, prices fell (今度は値段が下がります). The relationship between the two clauses is a direct cause-and-effect relationship, so the conjunction「その結果」(as a result) is the correct choice.
default.q.n2-18-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「活なみに」(a printing error for ちなみに: by the way/incidentially) adds supplementary information and does not express a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n2-18-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「それはそうと」(“by the way / speaking of something else”) is used in everyday conversation to change the subject. It is unsuitable in an explanatory text discussing a general principle.
default.q.n2-18-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「その結果」 (as a result / consequently) is a conjunction expressing an inevitable result arising from the preceding event: producers mass-produced the goods because they seemed profitable, and as a result, the supply on the market increased and prices were pushed down.
default.q.n2-18-q53-53.why.3: (d) "しかも"(moreover; in addition) adds information in the same direction with an intensifying effect; it does not indicate the result of a sequence of actions.
default.q.n2-18-q54-54.explanation: In Japanese, 「長い目で見る」(often used in the conditional forms 「長い目で見ると」or「長い目で見れば」) is a fixed expression meaning "to take a long-term view / in the long run." The particle 「で」indicates the viewpoint or manner of observation. The author concludes that although prices may fluctuate in the short term, in the long run (長い目で見ると), commodity prices will always settle at a reasonable level (ふさわしい値段に落ち着く).
default.q.n2-18-q54-54.why.0: (a) で forms the fixed expression「長い目で見る／長い目で見ると」, meaning “to take a long-term view / in the long run.” Here, the particle「で」indicates the standpoint or perspective of evaluation.
default.q.n2-18-q54-54.why.1: (b) "が" marks the subject or the object of an i-adjective or potential expression, and it does not work with「長い目...見る」in this way.
default.q.n2-18-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「を」 is the particle marking the direct object. Using 「長い目を」 would literally mean “look at long eyes,” which is completely grammatically incorrect for this idiom.
default.q.n2-18-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「に」indicates a direction, location, or definite point in time; it is not used to indicate the viewpoint in this set expression.
default.q.n2-18-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (大きすぎて).
default.q.n2-18-q55-55.explanation:
Main point: Everyone knows that Japan is an island country, but in daily life most people forget this fact. The four main islands (Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku) account for 95% of Japan’s total land area, and because these islands are so large, the feeling of being surrounded by the sea is barely noticeable. To truly experience what it feels like to be on an island, one must visit smaller, more remote islands.

Question:
Which of the following should be inserted in the brackets [ ] in the passage?

Answer choices:
1. 多すぎて: too many
2. 小注すぎて: too small
3. 大きすぎて: too large
4. 少なすぎて: too few
default.q.n2-18-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage discusses the scale or area of the four main islands, which makes the sense of the sea less noticeable; it is not saying that there are too many islands.
default.q.n2-18-q55-55.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The next sentence clearly says that to truly experience the feeling of being on an island, one must visit smaller islands (もっと小注な), showing that these four large islands are too large, not too small.
default.q.n2-18-q55-55.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage states: "日本全体の画積の 95 パーセントは本州 · 北海道 · 九州 · 四国の四 つの島が占めている。この四島では [ 大きすぎて ] 、周囲を海に囲まれているという実感は薄い。本当に島という感じを味山うにはもっと小注な、い山ゆる離島に 行流てみなければならない。" (Because these four islands account for 95% of Japan's area and are too large, the feeling of being surrounded by the sea is weak.)
default.q.n2-18-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that the small number of islands leads to a lack of feeling surrounded by the sea.
default.q.n2-18-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is answer choice 2: 湯と水の区別がはっきりとあって、それぞれに名前があるとい う見方.
default.q.n2-18-q56-56.explanation:
- **Main point of the passage**: The passage discusses how people often assume that “hot water” (湯) and “water/ordinary or cold water” (水) are clearly distinct beforehand, and that the corresponding names were then assigned to them. However, the author points out that this view is not entirely satisfactory: we can only vaguely say that hot water is warm and water is cold, but cannot precisely determine at what temperature water becomes hot or below what temperature it is simply water. In nature, there is no such clear boundary.

- **Question translation**: The passage says, “If we take this view,” so what kind of view does “this view” refer to?

- **Answer choices:**
1. The view that Japanese has the words “yu” and “mizu” to represent H2O in its liquid state.
2. The view that hot water and water are clearly distinct, with each having a corresponding name.
3. The view that it is self-evident that hot water is warm and water is cold.
4. The view that nature inherently contains no clear temperature-based division between water and hot water.
default.q.n2-18-q56-56.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inaccurate because this is merely a linguistic fact presented in the opening sentence to introduce the issue—the fact that Japanese has two words, “yu” and “mizu,” for liquid H2O—not the content of the cognitive viewpoint discussed.
default.q.n2-18-q56-56.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct. The preceding sentence states: 「湯というもの、水というものの区別がまずはっきりとあって、それに対してそれぞれ「湯」および「水」という名前がつけられているというふうに普通考えられる。これは、ごく当たり前の見方であり…」 (People generally think that there is first a clear distinction between what is called “hot water” and “water,” and that the names 「湯」 and 「水」 are assigned to them accordingly. This is a very natural way of seeing things...). The demonstrative expression 「この見方」 directly replaces this viewpoint.
default.q.n2-18-q56-56.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the text states: 「湯は温かいもの、そして水は冷たいものという程度の漠然としたことは言えても…」 (At most, one can vaguely say that hot water is warm and water is cold...). This is only a vague result inferred when applying the viewpoint, not the viewpoint itself.
default.q.n2-18-q56-56.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because it is the author's counterargument at the end of the passage (「つまり、自然界には、水と湯の明確な区分というものは本来存在しないのである」), which is completely contrary to the initial conventional view ('この見方').
default.q.n2-18-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (a: テープ式コーダー, b: テレビ, c: ビデオテープ式コーダー, d: 自動車).
default.q.n2-18-q57-57.explanation:
Main point and translation:
- Main point: Based on a graph, the passage analyzes changes since 1980 in the purchase prices of household electronic devices and automobiles in Japan:
  + (a) テープ式コーダー (cassette player/tape recorder): The price rose rapidly after 1987 because a CD player was added around 1988 («1988年頃、CDプレーヤーがついて価格が上がったため»).
  + (b) テレビ (television): The price rose sharply from 1987, peaked in 1991, and then gradually declined because the trend toward larger televisions first raised prices, after which consumers moved away from large-size models («大型化による価格の上昇とその後の消費者の大型離れが影響している»).
  + (c) ビデオテープ式コーダー (video tape recorder/VCR): Statistics began to be collected in 1985 («1985年から統計をとり始めた»); the price gradually increased and then declined slightly after 1992.
  + (d) 自動車 (automobile): The price gradually increased from 1983 and rose sharply in 1993 because imports increased («1993年には大きく購入価格が伸びている。その理由は、輸入が増加したからである»).
- Translation of the question: Based on the graph, choose the correct combination for the items at positions (a), (b), (c), and (d) in the passage.
- Translation of the choices:
  1. a: Television, b: Video recorder, c: Automobile, d: Cassette player
  2. a: Television, b: Cassette player, c: Video recorder, d: Automobile
  3. a: Cassette player, b: Television, c: Automobile, d: Video recorder
  4. a: Cassette player, b: Television, c: Video recorder, d: Automobile
default.q.n2-18-q57-57.why.0: Choice 1 is incorrect because it assigns (a) to テレビ and (b) to ビデオテープ式コーダー. According to the passage, (a) became more expensive because it was equipped with a CD player («1988年頃、CDプレーヤーがついて価格が上がったため»), so it must be a cassette player (テープ式コーダー); (b) became more expensive because of the trend toward larger screens («大型化による価格の上昇とその後の消費者の大型離れが影響している»), so it must be a television (テレビ).
default.q.n2-18-q57-57.why.1: Choice 2 is incorrect because (a) and (b) have been assigned to テレビ and テーブ式コーダー in reverse. The device in (a) with a built-in CD player must be テープ式コーダー, while (b), which concerns the trend of enlarging screen sizes followed by consumers abandoning large appliances, must be テレビ.
default.q.n2-18-q57-57.why.2: Choice 3 is incorrect because it reverses (c) 自動車 and (d) ビデオテープ式コーダー. According to the passage, (c), which began being statistically recorded in 1985 («1985年から統計をとり始めた»), is ビデオテープ式コーダー; (d), which increased sharply in 1993 because imports rose («その理由は、輸入が増加したからである»), is 自動車.
default.q.n2-18-q57-57.why.3: Choice 4 is correct because it completely matches the facts in the passage: (a) is a cassette player because a CD player was added: «1988 年頃、 CD プレーヤーがついて価格が上がったため»; (b) is a television because prices rose as screens became larger and then consumers moved away from large-screen models: «大型化による価格の上昇とその後の消費者の大型離れが影響している»; (c) is a videotape recorder because statistics began to be collected in 1985: «1985 年から統計をとり始めた»; (d) is a car because the purchase price rose sharply in 1993 as imports increased: «1993 年には大きく購入価格が伸びている。その理由は、輸入が増加したからである».
default.q.n2-18-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (苦しい思いをして).
default.q.n2-18-q58-58.explanation:
* Main idea: The passage says that looking at the lighting fixtures can reveal whether the builder constructed the house calmly and comfortably or with great difficulty. Since installing the lighting is the final stage of construction, if the funds gradually run out (資金につまる), this last stage will be handled very poorly.

* Translation of the question: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [ ].
* Translation of the choices:
1. 時間が不足して: because of a lack of time
2. 体力がなくなって: because of physical exhaustion
3. 楽しみにして: looking forward to it
4. 苦しい思いをして: with great difficulty / after going through hardship
default.q.n2-18-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage discusses a shortage of funds when building a house (「資金につまってくると」), not a lack of time.
default.q.n2-18-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage discusses difficulties caused by running out of money (「だんだんに資金につまってくると」), not physical exhaustion.
default.q.n2-18-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect because in the contrastive structure 「楽にその家を建てたか、それとも、かなり [ ] 建てたか」, the missing expression must contrast with 「楽に」 (easily, comfortably). 「楽しみにして」 does not fit the context of running out of money and finishing the construction poorly.
default.q.n2-18-q58-58.why.3: (d) Correct because it provides a contrast with「楽に」in the sentence「家を建てた人が、楽にその家を建てたか、それとも、かなり [ ] 建てたかということは照明器具を見ればわかるという」. It is also supported by the later example of funding shortages: 「建築でいえば、照明の取りつけが最後になる。従って、だんだんに資金につまってくると、最後のところでお粗末になる」.
default.q.n2-18-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ア： B イ： D ウ： C エ： A).
default.q.n2-18-q59-59.explanation:
・ Main point: The passage tells how six-year-old Susumu-kun often made noise at the library even though he did not like reading. Instead of scolding him, the narrator read manga to him. From then on, whenever he came, he asked to have books read to him, but careful observation showed that he was not truly interested in the content; he was simply happy to receive attention and care from an adult.
・ Question translation: Choose the correct combination.
・ Answer choices:
1. ア: B, イ: D, ウ: C, エ: A
2. ア: D, イ: B, ウ: C, エ: A
3. ア: D, イ: B, ウ: A, エ: C
4. ア: B, イ: D, ウ: A, エ: C
default.q.n2-18-q59-59.why.0: (a) Correct. Position [ア] takes B because the noisy behavior and running around (「奇声を発したり、机の間を走ったり、騒ぎはじめます」) is what 「それをしかるかわりに」 (instead of scolding him for it) refers to; position [イ] takes D, describing the change after he was read to (「それからは、来るたんぴに、読め読めとせがむようになりました」); position [ウ] takes C, following 「でも、見ていますと」 and showing that the boy was not very interested in the content of the book (「肝心の読んでもらっている本には、それほど興味を持っていない」); and position [エ] takes A, summarizing his feelings after 「結局」 (「進くんにとっては、読んでもらうということが、かまってもらえるという意味でうれしかったのでしょう」).
default.q.n2-18-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because D and B have been switched, with D placed in [ア] and B in [イ]. If D is placed in [ア], the clause “それをしかるかわりに” (“instead of scolding them for it”) loses the preceding misbehavior that serves as its premise.
default.q.n2-18-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it reverses all four positions (D in [ア], B in [イ], A in [ウ], C in [エ]), completely disrupting the narrative flow and the character’s psychological development.
default.q.n2-18-q59-59.why.3: (d) Insert A into [ウ] and C into [エ]. The clause after 'でも、見ていますと' needs a concrete observation (C: not being interested in books), while A is a conclusion about the underlying nature of the matter and therefore must come after '結局'.
default.q.n2-18-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: In countries where the number of cards is increasing, both the positive and negative aspects of credit cards have emerged.
default.q.n2-18-q60-60.explanation:
Summary of the relevant content: The opening paragraph states that in Asia, the number of credit cards issued has increased sharply, bringing both positive effects (strong sales, economic growth, and an improving economy) and negative effects (many people overspending and becoming unable to repay their debts).

Question and answer choices:
- Question: Which explanation correctly describes the situation regarding credit cards in Asia?
- Choice 1: In Asia, cards other than Visa and MasterCard have not increased.
- Choice 2: In countries where the number of cards has increased, both the positive and negative aspects of credit cards have emerged.
- Choice 3: The increase in credit cards in Asia has had more negative than positive effects.
- Choice 4: Across Asia, the number of people unable to repay their card debt is increasing.
default.q.n2-18-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage states only that the two companies Visa and MasterCard experienced strong growth (「ビザ、マスターの2社だけでも...」); it does not claim that other types of cards did not grow.
default.q.n2-18-q60-60.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage clearly presents both sides in countries where the number of cards has increased: the positive side is that goods sell well, the economy grows, and business conditions improve (「それらの国では物がよく売れ、経済成長率も上がり景気もよくなってきた」), while the negative side is that more people overspend and become unable to repay their debts (「しかしつい買いすぎて借金が払えなくなる人も増えてきた」).
default.q.n2-18-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage merely lists both positive and negative effects; it does not compare the negative aspects as greater than the positive ones.
default.q.n2-18-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage only says that the number of people unable to repay their debts increased in the countries mentioned above, where card issuance rose sharply (「それらの国では」). It does not generalize this to all of Asia (「アジア全体で」).
default.q.n2-18-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: If the court does not recognize it, the debt must still be repaid.
default.q.n2-18-q61-61.explanation:
**Relevant summary:** Paragraph 2 explains the procedure for personal bankruptcy (自己破産) in Japan: in most cases, the court approves the applicant’s discharge from debt, but debts such as gambling-related debts must still be repaid. Bankruptcy also involves restrictions, such as being unable to obtain a credit card for about seven years and restrictions related to residence, and it can affect social relationships, even though companies are legally prohibited from dismissing employees for this reason.

**Translation of the question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** Which statement is consistent with the explanation of personal bankruptcy?
- **Choice 1:** Personal bankruptcy can only be declared once.
- **Choice 2:** If the court does not recognize or approve the bankruptcy, the debts must still be repaid.
- **Choice 3:** When someone declares personal bankruptcy, they are required to leave their company.
- **Choice 4:** After declaring personal bankruptcy, it is permanently impossible to obtain a credit card.
default.q.n2-18-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention any rule stating that personal bankruptcy can be declared only once in a person’s lifetime.
default.q.n2-18-q61-61.why.1: (b) Correct. According to the passage, when an individual declares bankruptcy, most people are recognized by the court as not having to repay their debts, but debts may still have to be repaid if approval is not granted or if they resulted from gambling (as shown in: 「自己破産するとほとんどの人が、婚判所に借金を払山なくてもいいと認めてもらえる。だがギャンブル（注 2 ）な どの借金の場合は返注なければならない」).
default.q.n2-18-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that a company cannot force an employee to resign because of personal bankruptcy (「自己破産を理由にして社員を辞め注せることはできない」); some people resign only because they feel uncomfortable after the company learns about it.
default.q.n2-18-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage says that the person may be unable to obtain a credit card for approximately seven years (「だいたい 7 年ぐらいはク式ジットカードを作れなかったり」), not that it will be permanently impossible.
default.q.n2-18-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: The increase in credit cards also affects the economy.
default.q.n2-18-q62-62.explanation:
**Relevant summary:** The passage discusses the effects of the increasing use of credit cards on the economy (boosting sales, promoting economic growth, and encouraging consumption), as well as the consequences of poor spending management, which can lead to debt and bankruptcy.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** Which statement is consistent with the content of the passage?
- **Choice 1:** In Thailand in 2003, the number of cards issued increased by as much as 46% compared with the previous year.
- **Choice 2:** In Asian countries, the bankruptcy rate caused by credit cards increased in proportion to the rate at which cards were issued.
- **Choice 3:** The increase in credit cards also affects the economy.
- **Choice 4:** Anyone who owns a credit card will inevitably buy unnecessary things.
default.q.n2-18-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the 46% figure in the passage refers only to the increase for the two companies Visa and MasterCard (「ビザ、マスターの2社だけでも 2003 年はタイが前年に比べて 46 ％増」), not the total number of cards issued in Thailand.
default.q.n2-18-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not state that the bankruptcy rate increased by exactly the same percentage as card issuance.
default.q.n2-18-q62-62.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage clearly states that increased card issuance in Asian countries stimulated consumption and promoted economic growth: 「それらの国では物がよく売れ、経済成長率も上がり景気もよくなってきた」.
default.q.n2-18-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage only says that having a card caused people to accidentally overspend (「つい買いすぎて」); it does not claim that they bought unnecessary items.
default.q.n2-18-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (書いたにせよ).
default.q.n2-18-q63-63.explanation:
Summary: The author discusses how, no matter how beautiful a handwritten font created by an artist may be (even if it was written by a wonderful artist), it is still someone else's handwriting. Therefore, many people want a font of their own.
- Question translation: Which phrase has the same meaning as「書いたにしろ」in paragraph 2?
- Answer choices:
1. 書いたとしたら: If one assumes that it was written
2. 書いたにせよ: Even if it was written / Whether it was written
3. 書いたにもかかわらず: Although it was written
4. 書いたものなら: If one could write it / If one happened to write it
default.q.n2-18-q63-63.why.0: (a) 「〜としたら」 expresses a hypothetical condition, "if" or "supposing that..." It does not have the concessive meaning "even if" or "even though" expressed by 「〜にしろ」.
default.q.n2-18-q63-63.why.1: (b) QUOTATION: 「素晴らしい芸術家が 書いたにしろ 、それは他人の文字だ。」—Here, 「〜にしろ」expresses concession (“even if / even though...”) and is completely synonymous with and interchangeable with the pattern 「〜にせよ」.
default.q.n2-18-q63-63.why.2: (c)「〜にもかかわらず」means “although…; despite…,” describing an actual or unexpected result contrary to the preceding clause; it does not express the hypothetical concession of「〜にしろ」.
default.q.n2-18-q63-63.why.3: (d) 「〜ものなら」 means “if it were possible to...” or “if one were to...,” and is used for difficult conditions or warnings about consequences. It is not equivalent to 「〜にしろ」.
default.q.n2-18-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (子供が 1 人残されただけにかわいそうでならなかった。).
default.q.n2-18-q64-64.explanation:
Summary: The grammar pattern「〜だけに」indicates that precisely because of a particular cause or characteristic, the degree or result in the following clause is correspondingly greater. In the passage, because the alphabet or Hangul has fewer characters than Japanese, producing fonts for it is less expensive.
- Question: Which sentence uses「だけ」in the same way as「文字数が少ないだけに」?
- Answer choices:
1. Let’s just read today.
2. Let’s give only sweets to the children.
3. I tell secrets only to my close friend Akiko.
4. Precisely because the child was left all alone, I feel extremely sorry for them.
default.q.n2-18-q64-64.why.0: (a) 「だけ」 here expresses limitation, meaning “only” (Today, we will do nothing but read books), rather than the reason-related pattern 「〜だけに」.
default.q.n2-18-q64-64.why.1: (b)「だけ」here expresses limitation, meaning “only” (“Distribute the cake and sweets only to the children”), and does not correspond to the reason-related usage「〜だけに」.
default.q.n2-18-q64-64.why.2: (c) 「だけ」 here expresses limitation, meaning "only" (I told the secret only to my close friend Akiko); it does not correspond to the reason-related pattern 「〜だけに」.
default.q.n2-18-q64-64.why.3: (d) QUOTATION:「アルファベットやハングルの文字なら、日本語より 文字数が少ないだけに 、もっと安い料金でできると思う。」 Here, 「〜だけに」 means "precisely because / since ..., correspondingly ...," exactly as in sentence 4, 「子供が 1 人残されただけにかわいそうでならなかった」(Because the child had been left alone, I felt terribly sorry for them).
default.q.n2-18-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (筆者は自分の文字を作るつもりはない。).
default.q.n2-18-q65-65.explanation:
Summary: The article discusses how people favor digitized handwriting on computers because it feels warm and expresses individuality. As a result, a service that converts a user's own handwriting into a computer font has become very popular. However, in the concluding sentence, the author says that their handwriting is poor, so creating such a font has nothing to do with them personally (the author has no intention of doing it).
- Question: Which of the following is consistent with the content of the reading?
- Answer choices:
1. Receiving a handwritten letter is enjoyable, but receiving a computer-typed letter is not.
2. The author has no intention of creating their own font.
3. Because artists have beautiful handwriting, their fonts are more popular than fonts based on one's own handwriting.
4. Not only letters but also e-mails are more enjoyable when written in handwriting.
default.q.n2-18-q65-65.why.0: (a) In paragraph 1, the author only says that typed letters feel somehow administrative (なんとなく事務的な感じがして仕方がない), not that receiving a computer-written letter is "not enjoyable" (もらってもうれしくない).
default.q.n2-18-q65-65.why.1: (b) QUOTATION: 「とはいえ、字が下手な自分にはまったく関係のない話だ。」(However, as someone with poor handwriting, this has absolutely nothing to do with me.) This shows that the author has no intention of creating a font of their own.
default.q.n2-18-q65-65.why.2: (c) The passage states that both the artist's calligraphy (大変な人気を呼んだ) and the writer's calligraphy service (大変な人気商品になった) were very popular; it does not compare them by saying the artist's calligraphy was more popular.
default.q.n2-18-q65-65.why.3: (d) The passage mentions only letters and postcards (手紙やはがき); it does not mention e-mail at all.
default.q.n2-18-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (特別な): the most suitable word for the blank is "特別な" (special).
default.q.n2-18-q66-66.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage explains that ordinary public bathhouses are gradually changing to attract customers. For example, on special occasions such as Children's Day on May 5, they add fragrances or herbs to the bathwater. Therefore, people who want to experience this should visit on special days like these.
- Question translation: Fill in the appropriate word in the parentheses （ ）.
- Answer choices:
  1. 一般: ordinary / general
  2. 別の: another / different
  3. 特別な: special
  4. 並の: ordinary / usual
default.q.n2-18-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「一般」(ordinary or widespread) contrasts with the context, which gives examples of specific festivals and events such as May 5.
default.q.n2-18-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect because "別の" (another/different) does not express the quality of being a festival, holiday, or special event given as an example.
default.q.n2-18-q66-66.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「また 5 月 5 日の子供の日などにはお湯に何か入れる銭湯が多い。銭湯を経験してみたい人は、こういう（ 特別な ）日に行ったほうがさらにいい経験になるかもしれない。」 (On days such as Children's Day on May 5, many public baths add something to the bathwater. People who want to experience a sento may have an even better experience if they go on such a special day).
default.q.n2-18-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「並の」 means ordinary or average, which is inappropriate when describing a special holiday with its own distinctive activities.
default.q.n2-18-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (家の風呂が普及してきたからです。): The number of sento declined because bathtubs in private homes became widespread.
default.q.n2-18-q67-67.explanation:
- Main point: Paragraph 1 explains that the sharp decline in the number of public bathhouses and their users (in Tokyo, from a peak of 2,641 to only 1,077 today) is because most households now have bathtubs at home, so people no longer need to make the effort to go out to a public bath.
- Question translation: Why are public bathhouses (sento) becoming less common?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because people are no longer interested in ordinary bathtubs.
  2. Because bathtubs at home have become widespread.
  3. Because public bathhouses have become more expensive.
  4. Because the number of people who do not know proper bathing etiquette has increased.
default.q.n2-18-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the article does not mention that people have lost interest in ordinary bathtubs.
default.q.n2-18-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「今はほとんどの家に風呂があるから、わざわざ外出して銭湯に行くまでもないということだろう。」 (Since almost every house now has a bath, people probably no longer need to go out of their way to visit a public bathhouse.)
default.q.n2-18-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage says that ordinary sento baths cost around 400 yen, and even facilities that raised their prices slightly to invest in additional premium services remained very popular. Therefore, prices are not the reason sento baths are declining.
default.q.n2-18-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because some people’s lack of knowledge about bathing rules is merely a manners-related issue that causes an argument in paragraph 4; it is not the reason for the decline in the number of sento.
default.q.n2-18-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (風呂のマナーはみんなで使う物や場所を汚さないことだ。): Bathing etiquette means not making shared items or places dirty.
default.q.n2-18-q68-68.explanation:
- Main point: The passage explains the rules for bathing in a communal bath or hot spring: rinse your body before entering the tub, do not put your towel in the tub so that everyone can enjoy clean water, and dry your feet when leaving so that you do not wet the shared floor. All these rules are intended to keep shared items and spaces clean.
- Translation of the question: Which of the following is correct according to the explanation of bathing rules?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. You should be careful because failing to follow the rules will result in being warned and feeling uncomfortable.
  2. Since people from other countries do not know the rules, they should preferably ask a Japanese person.
  3. Whether at a hot spring or a communal bath, it is important to wash your body thoroughly before entering the tub.
  4. The rule for bathing is not to make the objects and spaces shared by everyone dirty.
default.q.n2-18-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage only says that failure to follow the rules is the source of arguments (けんかの種); it does not discuss being reminded of the rules and becoming upset.
default.q.n2-18-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the article only says that recently even some Japanese people do not know the rule; it does not say that foreigners are unaware of it or advise them to ask Japanese people.
default.q.n2-18-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage only instructs people to rinse themselves briefly to remove the initial dirt (ざっと汚れを取って); it does not say they must wash and scrub themselves thoroughly (十分洗う) before entering the bath.
default.q.n2-18-q68-68.why.3: (d) Correct. default.q.n2-18-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (敬語を過剰に使う必要はない).
default.q.n2-18-q69-69.explanation:
**Main points of the related passages:**
- Passage A criticizes excessive use of honorific language (過剰な敬語), such as 「おみえになられました」, because it sounds awkward and discourteous. It recommends using only the appropriate standard form, 「おみえになりました」.
- Passage B explains that double honorifics (二重敬語) are accepted in some cases, but generally there is no need to deliberately pile up honorific forms (あえて重ねる必要はない).
- Passage C warns that combining multiple layers of honorific language in an overly contrived way can result in incorrect honorific usage (間違った敬語使い). Using more honorifics is not always better.
-> The common point in all three passages is: excessive use of honorific language is unnecessary.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What common point is stated in all three passages, A–C?
- **Choice 1:** It is unnecessary to use excessive honorific language. (Correct)
- **Choice 2:** Honorific language is unnecessary in modern language.
- **Choice 3:** Polite honorific expressions are not commendable.
- **Choice 4:** The more polite the honorific language, the more accurate it is.
default.q.n2-18-q69-69.why.0: (a) Correct. All three passages indicate that there is no need to use honorific language excessively or pile on too many honorific expressions: Passage A says, "丁寧に話そうとして、敬語をたくさん使ってしまうのかもしれませんが、これでは、かえって聞きにくく失礼になります"; Passage B concludes, "二重敬語はすべてだめだというわけではない 敬語は重ねてもよいが、あえて重ねる必要はないのです"; Passage C emphasizes, "敬語は、いくつも重ねればよいというものではありません。使いすぎるとかえって間違った敬語使いになって しまうので気をつけましょう".
default.q.n2-18-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because no author says that honorific language is unnecessary in modern Japanese (「現代語に敬語表現は不要である」). Honorific language is still necessary when used appropriately.
default.q.n2-18-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The authors do not oppose polite expressions (「丁寧な敬語表現は好ましくない」); they oppose excessive use of honorific language (過剰な敬語 / 丁寧すぎる二重敬語), which can have the opposite effect.
default.q.n2-18-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because, according to all three passages, using more honorific language or trying to be increasingly polite does not mean being more accurate; instead, it can sound unpleasant, impolite, or grammatically incorrect (passage A: "かえって聞きにくく失礼になります", passage C: "使いすぎるとかえって間違った敬語使いになって しまう").
default.q.n2-18-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (A と C の筆者は使ってはいけないと考えているが、 B の筆者は使う必要のないも...).
default.q.n2-18-q70-70.explanation:
**Main points from the relevant passages:**
- Passage A: The author says that using too much honorific language (double honorifics) is a common mistake that sounds awkward and impolite, and gives the standard expressions: 「○○さんがおみえになりました」「召し上がりましたか」が正しい表現方法です.
- Passage B: The author says that double honorifics are not all unacceptable (二重敬語はすべてだめだというわけではない); some cases create an appropriately polite impression and are accepted (許容されている). They may be repeated, but there is no need to deliberately do so (あえて重ねる必要はない).
- Passage C: The author states that combining two honorific forms (such as おっしゃる + られる) is incorrect (間違いになります) and advises caution to avoid overuse.
-> Authors A and C regard double honorifics as incorrect / something that should not be used, whereas author B says that they are not necessarily prohibited, only unnecessary.

**Translation of the question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What position does each author take regarding “double honorifics”? 
- **Choice 1:** None of the authors regard them as correct usage, and because they are impolite to the other person, they must not be used...
- **Choice 2:** Authors A and C say that they must not be used, whereas author B says that they are unnecessary... (Correct)
- **Choice 3:** Authors B and C say that this is an honorific expression that should not be used, whereas author A says...
- **Choice 4:** Authors A and C say that this is correct usage, whereas author B says that it is incorrect usage...
default.q.n2-18-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because Author B does not regard double honorifics as entirely wrong or prohibited, but explains that some cases are accepted: "「お･召し上がり・になる」や「お・伺い・いたし・ます」等は、適度な丁寧さを感じて不快感がないので、許容されている表現だと言えます。二重敬語はすべてだめだというわけではない".
default.q.n2-18-q70-70.why.1: (b) Correct. Authors A and C regard double honorifics as incorrect or impolite and say they should not be used (A: "敬語をたくさん使ってしまう...これでは、かえって聞きにくく失礼になります。「○○さんがおみえになりました」「召し上がりましたか」が正しい表現方法です"; C: "「おっしゃる」プラス「られる」と、敬語表現を重ねているので、間違いになります...気をつけましょう"). Author B, however, says that some cases are acceptable and may be used, although there is no need to deliberately use them (B: "二重敬語はすべてだめだというわけではない 敬語は重ねてもよいが、あえて重ねる必要はないのです").
default.q.n2-18-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because author A clearly opposes double honorifics, pointing out that they are disrespectful and providing the correct way to speak; the author is not hesitant or saying that either form is acceptable. In addition, author B does not categorically state that it "should not be used."
default.q.n2-18-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because authors A and C both regard double honorifics as incorrect usage, not as “正しい用法” (correct usage).
default.q.n2-18-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: A method for solving the problem of judging personality by blood type (血液型性格判断問題の解決方ぐです).
default.q.n2-18-q71-71.explanation:
**Relevant part of the passage:**
Near the end of the article, the author points out that judging personality by blood type can lead to discrimination and negatively affect the standing of people with minority blood types (types B and AB), emphasizing 「こうなるとそのまま放っておくわけにもいきません」(At this point, we cannot simply leave things as they are). After explaining why this trend became popular and is not likely to disappear immediately, the most logical and natural next development would be to discuss ways to resolve or respond to the problem.

**Question and answer choices:**
- Question: Which of the following would be the most appropriate topic for the next part of the article?
- 1. An analysis of why judging personality by blood type became popular.
- 2. Ways to resolve the problem of judging personality by blood type.
- 3. An analysis of the psychology of people who like judging personality by blood type.
- 4. The scientific reasons behind judging personality by blood type.
default.q.n2-18-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author has already analyzed the popularity of judging personality by blood type in the final paragraph («なぜこんなに人気があるでしょうか。それは仲間意識です。同じ価値観で人を判断する安心感があります...»). Therefore, the following section would not repeat this analysis of its reasons.
default.q.n2-18-q71-71.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is correct because the author first presents the harm caused by discrimination and states that it cannot simply be left alone («こうなるとそのまま放っておくわけにもいきません»), then explains why the phenomenon is widespread and unlikely to disappear on its own («とするとこれは簡単にはなくならないでしょう»). The most logical continuation is therefore to propose solutions to the problem.
default.q.n2-18-q71-71.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the psychological reasons why people enjoy blood-type fortune-telling—belonging, the reassurance of sharing the same values, and playfulness—are fully explained at the end: «それは仲間意識です。同じ価値観で人を判断する安心感があります... 遊びの部分も多いから楽しいのです».
default.q.n2-18-q71-71.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the entire article focuses on social psychology and issues of prejudice and discrimination, rather than on scientific grounds. The author is also seeking ways to address this social issue.
default.q.n2-18-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: The idea that personality can be judged based on blood type (血液型で性格が判断できるということです).
default.q.n2-18-q72-72.explanation:
**Relevant passage summary:**
In the first paragraph, the author states that in countries where 90% of the population has the same blood type, people would never think of using blood type to predict personality. If someone said that («そんなこと» = the idea that personality can be predicted from blood type), people would laugh because if blood type determined personality, nearly everyone in that country would have exactly the same personality.

**Question and answer choices:**
- Question: In the first paragraph, what does «そんなこと» in the phrase «そんなことを言うと» (if you say something like that) refer to?
- 1. The fact that 90% of the people in that country have the same personality.
- 2. The fact that many different blood types exist in a reasonably balanced distribution.
- 3. The idea that personality can be judged from blood type.
- 4. The fact that people in Japan judge personality by blood type.
default.q.n2-18-q72-72.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the text only states «90 ％が同じ血液型という国もあります» (some countries have 90% of their population with the same blood type), not that 90% of the people in that country share the same personality.
default.q.n2-18-q72-72.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the balanced distribution of blood types is described as a characteristic of Japan («日本には A 型 40 ％、O 型 30 ％、 B 型 20 ％、 AB 型 10 ％の全部の血液型の人がほどよくいます»), not the subject of «そんなこと» that foreigners laugh at.
default.q.n2-18-q72-72.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the text directly shows that the preceding sentences are: «その国では血液型で性格を判断しようなどと誰も考えないでしょう。そんなことを言うと笑われてしまいます。» -> The demonstrative expression «そんなこと» directly replaces the idea or statement «血液型で性格を判断しよう（血液型で性格が判断できる）》.
default.q.n2-18-q72-72.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because «そんなこと» here refers to the idea of “guessing people’s personalities from their blood types” in general, not specifically to “people in Japan judging personalities by blood type.”
default.q.n2-18-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: Judging personality by blood type can lead to discrimination (血液型性格判断は差別を生むことがあるということです).
default.q.n2-18-q73-73.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant passage:**
The author analyzes the phenomenon of fortune-telling based on blood type in Japan and points out that this seemingly entertaining practice conceals discrimination («差別が隠れている»). Blood types that are more common are often associated with positive personality traits, while minority blood types such as B and AB are often assigned negative stereotypes and may even face discrimination in hiring and social life.

**Question and answer choices:**
- Question: What is the passage about?
- 1. Judging personality by blood type hurts others, so it should be banned.
- 2. Judging personality by blood type is the standard used by the majority of people.
- 3. Judging personality by blood type is useful depending on how it is used.
- 4. Judging personality by blood type can create discrimination.
default.q.n2-18-q73-73.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author points out the negative aspects and harm of discrimination but does not advocate completely banning it («禁止すべき»).
default.q.n2-18-q73-73.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the article only mentions the distribution of blood types in Japan and the reassurance people feel when they share the same values. It does not claim that blood-type fortune-telling is the standard used to evaluate most people.
default.q.n2-18-q73-73.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author does not discuss the usefulness of blood-type fortune-telling depending on how it is used; the focus is on warning against stereotypes imposed on minority groups.
default.q.n2-18-q73-73.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because throughout the article the author emphasizes: «実はここに差別が㞃れていることがあります», «多数派にいい性格判断が多いので、少数派で嫌な思いをしている人がいる», «そういう言葉はやはり差別だと思います。それが一般に広まって B 型や AB 型の人の立場を悪くすることがあるのです».

default.q.n2-18-q11-11.why.0: (a) 1. 連続 (“continuous”): Refers to events or actions continuing one after another without interruption, as in 連続勤務 (“continuous work”). It is not used to mean preserving or maintaining product quality.

default.q.n2-18-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence translation: "What you said feels selfish to me." (The original problem actually used わがまま, which was misread by OCR as 山がまま, and choice 4 was 感じられる.)
- Structure: 〜と感じられる (to naturally feel that something is so; the spontaneous form of 感じる).
- On'yomi: 感じる (KAN, 感), 信じる (SHIN, 信), 報じる (HŌ, 報), 生じる (SHŌ, 生).
- Example: 彼の態度には誠意が感じられない。(His attitude does not convey any sincerity.)
default.q.n2-18-q12-12.why.0: (a) 1. 生じられる: the passive/potential form of the verb 生じる (to arise, occur; used for problems or conflicts), and it does not combine with 「〜だと」 to express the speaker’s subjective impression.
default.q.n2-18-q12-12.why.1: (b) 2. 報じられる: The passive form of 報じる, meaning “to be reported” or “to be covered by the media.” It is used for news reports, not for a personal impression expressed with 私には.
default.q.n2-18-q12-12.why.2: (c) 3. 信じられる: This is the potential form of 信じる (can be trusted), and it sounds unnatural with '私には〜だと' when commenting on the selfish character or attitude (わがまま).
default.q.n2-18-q12-12.why.3: (d) 4. 感じられ: a form of the verb 感じる, specifically the spontaneous form 感じられる, creating the familiar pattern 「私には〜だと感じられる」 to express a feeling or thought that arises spontaneously in the speaker.
default.q.n2-18-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 属して (forming 〜に属している: to belong to or be affiliated with a department).
default.q.n2-18-q13-13.explanation:

default.q.n2-18-q13-13.why.2: (c) 3. 属して: From the verb 属する (to belong to, be affiliated with), it combines with the particle に to form 人事課に属している (to belong to the personnel department), which is correct in meaning and grammar.

  + 法: on-readings ほう/ぽう/はっ (as in 法律 - ほうりつ: law, 文法 - ぶんぽう: grammar, 法度 - はっと: rule/regulation). In 憲法, it is read as ぽう.
- Example: 国会で憲法改正についての議論が行われた。(The Diet held a discussion on constitutional revision.)
default.q.n2-18-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「けんぽい」: Incorrect. 法 does not have the reading ぽい; the given answer appears to have い instead of う at the end.
default.q.n2-18-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「けんぽう」: Correct. 憲 (HIẾN - けん) + 法 (PHÁP - ぽう) forms 憲法 (けんぽう: constitution).
default.q.n2-18-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect pronunciation. When attached after けん, 法 undergoes rendaku and becomes the semi-voiced sound ぽう, as in 文法 (ぶんぽう) and 憲法 (けんぽう).
default.q.n2-18-q1-1.why.3: (d)「けんほ」: Incorrect. 法 is read ほう/ぽう, with a long vowel う; ほ is incomplete.
default.q.n2-18-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (じんるいがく).
default.q.n2-18-q2-2.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: His major is social anthropology, and he is writing a thesis on a wide variety of everyday phenomena that occur in society.
- Kanji components: 人 + 類 + 学 -> 人類学 (anthropology).
- Expanded readings:
  + 人: On-readings じん (人類 - じんるい, 人口 - じんこう) or にん (人間 - にんげん, 人数 - にんずう).
  + 類: On-reading るい (書類 - しょるい: documents, 親類 - しんるい: relatives, 分類 - ぶんるい: classification).
  + 学: On-readings がく/がっ (学問 - がくもん, 学校 - がっこう).
- Example: 彼は大学で文化人類学を研究している。(He is researching cultural anthropology at a university.)
default.q.n2-18-q2-2.why.0: (a) 「じんるいがく」: Correct. 人 (じん) + 類 (るい) + 学 (がく) is read as じんるいがく.
default.q.n2-18-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「じんぬいがく」: Incorrect reading of the kanji 類; it is read as るい, not ぬい.
default.q.n2-18-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「にんぬいがく」: Both readings are incorrect. 人 is read as じん in this word, not にん, and 類 is read as るい, not ぬい.
default.q.n2-18-q2-2.why.3: (d) 「にんるいがく」 has an incorrect reading. In 人類, 人 is read with the Go-on reading じん, not にん.
default.q.n2-18-q3-3.explanation:
- Sentence translation: The face reflected in the mirror is reversed left to right.
- Kanji: 左 (left) + 右 (right) → 左右 (left and right; influence or control).
- Reading expansion:
  + 左: on-reading さ (左右 - さゆう, 左折 - させつ: turn left), kun-reading ひだり.
  + 右: on-readings ゆう / う (左右 - さゆう, 右折 - うせつ: turn right, 右翼 - うよく: right wing), kun-reading みぎ.
- Example: 左右をよく見てから道路を渡りましょう。 (Look carefully to the left and right before crossing the road.)
default.q.n2-18-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「さう」: Incorrect. 右 has the long-vowel reading ゆう; reading it as う omits a sound.
default.q.n2-18-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「さゆ」: Incorrect; the long vowel う is missing in the reading of 右. In addition, さゆ written as 白湯 means cooled boiled water.
default.q.n2-18-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「さよう」: Incorrect reading for 右, which is read ゆう; さよう is the reading of 作用 (effect) or 左様 (so/that is right).
default.q.n2-18-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「さゆう」: Correct. 左 (さ) + 右 (ゆう) is correctly read as さゆう.
default.q.n2-18-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (かこまれた).
default.q.n2-18-q4-4.explanation:
- Sentence translation: This small village, surrounded by mountains, is recruiting young people to help with farm work.
- Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 囲 (い).
- Related vocabulary:
  + Active verbs: 囲む (かこむ: to surround, encircle), 囲う (かこう: to fence in, enclose).
  + Passive form: 囲まれる (かこまれる: to be surrounded) → past form: 囲まれた (かこまれた).
  + On-reading: い (周囲 (しゅうい): surroundings, 範囲 (はんい): range, 雰囲気 (ふんいき): atmosphere).
- Example: その庭は美しい花に囲まれている。(That garden is surrounded by beautiful flowers.)
default.q.n2-18-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「つつまれた」: Incorrect. This is the past passive form of 包む (つつむ: to wrap or cover).
default.q.n2-18-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「はさまれた」: Incorrect. This is the past passive form of 挟む (はさむ: to sandwich, insert, or trap between).
default.q.n2-18-q4-4.why.2: (c) 「かこまれた」: Correct. It is the past passive form of the verb 囲む (かこむ: to surround, enclose).
default.q.n2-18-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「つかまれた」: Incorrect. This is the past passive form of 掴む/捉む (つかむ: to seize or grasp).
default.q.n2-18-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (びょうどう).
default.q.n2-18-q5-5.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: A conference on gender equality was opened, and delegates from various countries attended and discussed issues occurring in families and workplaces.
- Kanji readings: 平 + 等 -> 平等 (gender equality).
- Additional readings:
  + 平: on-readings びょう (平等 - びょうどう) and へい (平和 - へいわ: peace, 平日 - へいじつ: weekday, 平均 - へいきん: average); kun-readings たいら / ひら.
  + 等: on-readings どう (平等 - びょうどう) and とう (同等 - どうとう: equal, equivalent, 高等 - こうとう: advanced, high-level); kun-reading ひとしい.
- Example: すべての国民は法の下に平等である。(All citizens are equal under the law.)
default.q.n2-18-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「へいとう」 is incorrect in both readings: 平 is read びょう in this word, and 等 is read どう, not とう.
default.q.n2-18-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「へいどう」: Incorrect reading of 平 (in 平等, 平 is pronounced びょう in the special Go-on reading, not へい).
default.q.n2-18-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「びょうとう」: Incorrect reading of 等 (in 平等, 等 undergoes voicing and is pronounced どう, not とう).
default.q.n2-18-q5-5.why.3: (d) Correct: 平 (びょう) + 等 (どう) in 平等 is correctly read びょうどう.
default.q.n2-18-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 破片 (はへん - fragment).
default.q.n2-18-q6-6.explanation:
Meaning: I injured my finger on a shard of glass and had it bandaged.
- Sino-Japanese roots: 破片 (shard, fragment).
- Example: 割れた皿の破片を片付ける。(Clean up the shards of the broken plate.)
default.q.n2-18-q6-6.why.0: (a) Correct. 破 means “to break or shatter,” and 片 means “fragment”; together they form 「破片」(はへん), meaning “fragment” or “shard.”
default.q.n2-18-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 歯 (tooth) is read 「は」 or 「し」 and does not combine with 片 to mean a shard of glass.
default.q.n2-18-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 葉 (leaf) has the kun-reading 「は」 and the on-reading 「よう」; it does not mean fragment.
default.q.n2-18-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 波 (wave) has the kun-reading 「なみ」 and the on-reading 「は」; it is not used to mean a fragment.

default.q.n2-18-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 粗 (coarse, rough, shoddy, as in 粗末 and 粗品) contains the 米 radical and is read 「そ」; the meaning is incorrect.
default.q.n2-18-q7-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 組 means “organize, combine, or group” (as in 組合 and 番組) and has the 糸 radical; it does not combine with 父 to indicate a relative.
default.q.n2-18-q8-8.verdict: The provided answer is 3 (贈加), but the correct kanji for「ぞうか」is 4. 増加 (INCREASE — to increase / rise).
default.q.n2-18-q8-8.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The capital’s population is increasing rapidly, and it is said that it may reach 10 million before the end of the 20th century.

- Antonym: 減少 (げんしょう: decrease, decline).
- Example: 観光客の数が大幅に増加した。(The number of tourists increased significantly.)
default.q.n2-18-q8-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 層 is read「そう」and does not form a word meaning an increase in quantity.
default.q.n2-18-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 憎 (meaning hatred) is read as 「ぞう」 or 「にく(む)」 and means to hate or detest, not to increase.
default.q.n2-18-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The kanji 贈 means “to give as a gift” (as in 贈り物 and 贈答) and is read「ぞう」or「おく(る)」; it does not mean to increase the quantity, so the provided answer choice 3 is inaccurate.
default.q.n2-18-q8-8.why.3: (d) The correct kanji is used. 増 (increase) combines with 加 (add) to form 「増加」(ぞうか), meaning an increase or rise.
default.q.n2-18-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 免許 (めんきょ: license, driver's license).

Meaning: If you violate traffic laws, your driver's license may also be confiscated.

default.q.n2-18-q10-10.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 昇 (to rise or be promoted) is read 「しょう」 or 「のぼ(る)」; both the reading and the kanji are wrong.
