default.q.n2-25-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「～としても」 expresses hypothetical concession: “even if” or “assuming that.” This contrasts with the praise described in the following clause.
default.q.n2-25-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「普通形 + だけあって」means “no wonder,” “as expected of,” or “true to the reputation of.” It praises the food as being delicious enough to justify everyone waiting in a long line.
default.q.n2-25-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ほしくなるものだ (one tends to want it even more, according to ordinary human psychology).
default.q.n2-25-q39-39.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Whenever people cannot buy something because they do not have enough money, they want it even more. This is a common aspect of human nature."
• Vocabulary / kanji reading: 余計（よけい）: even more, all the more; 欲しい: to want.
• Structure: V-る / V-たい + ものだ (expresses a natural human tendency, inherent nature, or self-evident truth).
• Example: 人は禁止されると、余計に見たくなるものだ。(When people are forbidden to see something, they naturally want to see it even more.)
default.q.n2-25-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「～ものだ」 expresses a natural law or an inherent psychological tendency of human beings. Combined with 「ほしくなる」, it fits perfectly with the adverb 「よけい」: the less one can have something, the more one naturally wants it.
default.q.n2-25-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「～ことだ」is used to give advice or a mild command (“you should...”); it is not used to describe an ordinary psychological state.
default.q.n2-25-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「ほしくなくなる」means “to come to no longer want something,” which is opposite to the psychological logic accompanying the adverb 「よけい」(even more).
default.q.n2-25-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「ほしくなくなることだ」is incorrect both in psychological meaning and in the advisory structure of the pattern ことだ.
default.q.n2-25-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 3. にしたがって (the more... the more..., in proportion to the progress of a change).
default.q.n2-25-q40-40.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "The farther upstream you go, the faster the water flows."
• Vocabulary: 川 (river), 上流 (upstream), 流れ (flow), 速い (fast).
• Structure: V-る / N + にしたがって (the more..., the more..., with B changing in parallel with A).
• Example: 標高が高くなるにしたがって、気温が下がる。(The higher the altitude, the lower the temperature.)
default.q.n2-25-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「～に沿って」means “along / in accordance with” and usually follows a noun directly (川に沿って); it does not follow the verb 行く to indicate a corresponding change.
default.q.n2-25-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「～に対して」 means “toward,” “with respect to,” or “in contrast to,” and is not used to express a parallel change over time.
default.q.n2-25-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「Vる + にしたがって」means “the more...the more...” or “as...,” describing a corresponding change, as in “the farther upstream one goes, the stronger the current becomes.”
default.q.n2-25-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「～に際して」 means “on the occasion of / when beginning” a formal event, and is not used for the natural changes of a phenomenon.
default.q.n2-25-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. わりに (relatively..., considering the degree; although...).
default.q.n2-25-q41-41.explanation:

default.q.n2-25-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「Naな + わりに（は）」means “compared with...” or “although...,” expressing that the salary is unexpectedly high compared with the easy nature of the work.

Meaning: "Just because I happened to mention that I majored in English at university, I was assigned a difficult translation job."

default.q.n2-25-q55-55.explanation:
- Main point: The author has a younger brother but has always wished for an older brother. Whenever snacks (おやつ) were handed out, the author would look at the younger brother and regretfully think, "If only this guy (こいつ) weren't here, it would all be mine." If the author had had an older brother, he might have willingly given his share to his younger sister when she asked. In addition, whenever they argued, the younger brother would cry and tell their mother, so the author felt disadvantaged. Therefore, 「こいつ」 here refers to the younger brother (弟).

- Question translation:
  「 こいつ 」(this guy/this person) refers to whom or what?

- Answer choices:
  1. 弟: younger brother
  2. お兄注ん (お兄ちゃん): older brother
  3. 妹: younger sister
  4. おやつ: snacks/sweets

The passage states: 「おやつをもらうときも、弟を横目で見ながら、『こいつさえいなければ、全部私のものになるのに』とが流かりした。」 When receiving a snack, the author glanced sideways at her younger brother and thought, “If only this guy weren’t here, it would all be mine.” 「こいつ」 refers to the younger brother (弟), whom she was looking at.

- **Choice 4:** The number of public telephones is steadily increasing.
default.q.n2-25-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not say that public telephones are "no longer needed at all" (全く必要ない); it explains the shift from vivid colors to subdued colors once attracting attention is no longer necessary as before.
default.q.n2-25-q58-58.why.1: (b) Correct because the author states: "かつては必要不可欠だったから、最も目立つ赤である必要があった。しかし現在では、ほとんどの人が携帯電話を持っているため..." and "人を引きつけようとするものは派手な色を好み、振りかえられなくて済むようになれば、だんだん地味な色に変わっていく...". In other words, the period when public telephones needed to be conspicuous and eye-catching to attract users has passed.
default.q.n2-25-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the change in color originated from whether there was a need to attract attention, not from “color preferences changing with the times” (色の好みが時代とともに変わってきた).
default.q.n2-25-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that public telephones are operating at a loss and continually disappearing from street corners ("街角からつぎつぎと消えていく"), which is the exact opposite of "their number has been steadily increasing" (数がだんだん増えてきた).
default.q.n2-25-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Earth’s surface temperature remains stable at an average of 15°C because water vapor and CO2 in the atmosphere absorb heat radiation from the ground, while the oceans moderate temperatures and prevent sudden fluctuations.
default.q.n2-25-q59-59.explanation:
Main point of the passage:
The passage explains the mechanism that keeps Earth's surface temperature at an average of 15°C. The author clearly states that water and CO2 in the atmosphere absorb heat radiation from the ground and retain warmth, while the oceans and atmosphere regulate temperature differences and prevent sudden changes in temperature.

Translation of the question:
According to the passage, which statement correctly expresses the author's view of why the temperature of areas near Earth's surface is maintained at an average of 15°C?

Translation of the answer choices:
1. Earth's atmosphere contains carbon dioxide (CO2) and water, which, together with the oceans, help maintain air temperature.
2. About 70% of Earth's surface is covered by oceans, and the oceans absorb heat from the Sun at a certain distance.
3. Earth has air and water, and living organisms are constantly active within them.
4. Earth's atmosphere contains carbon dioxide (CO2), which spreads across Earth's surface and absorbs heat.
default.q.n2-25-q59-59.why.0: (a) This matches the quoted passage exactly: 「これは、大気の中にある水と二酸化炭素などが、地表から放射される熱を吸収して、地表の気温を適温に保つはたらきがあるためである。また、海は大気とともに地表全体の温度差を少なくすると同時に、急激な温度の変化を防ぐはたらきをしている。」 (This is because water, carbon dioxide, and other substances in the atmosphere absorb heat radiated from the Earth's surface and keep its temperature within a suitable range. In addition, together with the atmosphere, the sea reduces temperature differences across the Earth's surface and prevents abrupt changes in temperature.)
default.q.n2-25-q59-59.why.1: (b) Does not fit: The article only states that the sea and atmosphere reduce temperature differences and prevent sudden temperature fluctuations. It does not say that the sea absorbs heat from the Sun at a certain distance.
default.q.n2-25-q59-59.why.2: (c) Does not match: the passage only mentions that air and water are necessary for living organisms to survive. It does not say that the organisms' activity is what maintains the temperature at 15°C.
default.q.n2-25-q59-59.why.3: (d) Does not match: the passage states that components including "water and CO2..." (水と二酸化炭素など) absorb radiant heat from the ground, not that CO2 alone "spreads across the entire ground and absorbs heat."
default.q.n2-25-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is answer choice 2: きれいに工夫してある手紙 (a letter skillfully made beautiful).
default.q.n2-25-q60-60.explanation:
- Main point: At the beginning, the author says that they often receive many letters from readers and cancer patients. These letters are always prepared with great care and are beautifully decorated (beautiful envelopes and stationery, pressed flowers, and fragrance). The letter received this time was very plain, completely unlike “letters like that.”
- Question translation: What kind of letters are “letters like that”?
- Answer choices:
  1. A simple letter with no decorations.
  2. A carefully and beautifully decorated letter.
  3. A letter asking for urgent advice or consultation.
  4. A letter without the sender’s name.
default.q.n2-25-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because “a simple, undecorated letter” (簡素) describes the letter the author received this time (“その封書は、「そうした手紙」と異なり簡素...”), contrasting with 「そうした手紙」.
default.q.n2-25-q60-60.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「たくさんの読者やがん患者仲間からの手紙は、いつも美しい封筒や便箋、押し花、香りの工夫が凝らしてあり慰められる。」 The letters from readers and fellow cancer patients were always carefully decorated with beautiful envelopes, stationery, pressed flowers, and fragrances. Therefore, 「そうした手紙」 refers to beautifully and carefully decorated letters.
default.q.n2-25-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect because an “urgent consultation” (緊急の相談) is merely the exception for which the author replies ("筆無精の私は緊急の相談以外にはめったに返事を書けない"), not what 「そうした手紙」 describes.
default.q.n2-25-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the letter without a sender's name (only the address of Hiroshima City) was the letter that arrived later with 6,000 yen ("差出人も広島市○○○としか記していなかった"), not 「そうした手紙」.
default.q.n2-25-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: 青年が困っているようだったから (Because the young man seemed to be in difficulty).
default.q.n2-25-q61-61.explanation:
- Main idea: The author recalls an incident from several months earlier at a ticket counter in Tokyo Station. Seeing a young man standing frozen and pale with confusion because he did not have enough money for a ticket to Hiroshima, despite having to leave urgently, the author could not bring himself to ignore him. He asked how much money was missing and gave the young man the rest.
- Question translation: Why did the author give the young man money?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because he was a young man the author had met before.
  2. Because the young man seemed apologetic or remorseful.
  3. Because the young man seemed to be in trouble or at a loss.
  4. Because the author had once had a similar experience.
default.q.n2-25-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author had never known the young man before. When the author received the letter, they even wondered, 「誰だろう．．．？」 (Who could it be?).
default.q.n2-25-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the apologetic reaction (申し訳なさそうに口ごもった) came from the young man after the author gave him money, not because of the author’s decision to help him.
default.q.n2-25-q61-61.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「広島まで、と駅員に告げた青年が途方に暮れていた。どうやら所持金では足りないらしい。青ざめ呆然と立ち尽くしている。いたたまれず、私は尋ねた。」 The author sees the young man helpless and standing there pale and stunned because he does not have enough money for the ticket, and decides to help by giving him money.
default.q.n2-25-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage only speculates about the young man’s emergency circumstances (“There are times in life when one must act despite having no money. A death in the family? Pursuing a lover who ran away?”). It does not say that the author experienced a similar situation.
default.q.n2-25-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: 青年のまじめな気持ちが伝わってきたから (Because the young man's sincere and earnest feelings came through).
default.q.n2-25-q62-62.explanation:
- Main point: Although the author had told the young man not to repay the money and instead to help others in need, the young man remembered the address and sent the money back with a heartfelt note of thanks. The author sensed his sincerity, integrity, and warmth, which made the author feel happy for several days.
- Translation of the question: Why did the author “feel happy for several days”?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Because the young man returned the 6,000 yen he had borrowed.
  2. Because the young man’s sincere and honest feelings reached the author.
  3. Because the author felt good about doing something kind by helping someone else.
  4. Because the young man gave the author something that could not be bought with 6,000 yen.
default.q.n2-25-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author was happy not simply because they received 6,000 yen, but because they felt they had received heartfelt warmth that money could not buy (“6千円で買えない温かい気持ちを贈られた気分で”).
default.q.n2-25-q62-62.why.1: (b) Correct. Although the author had told the young man not to repay him and instead to help someone else in the future, the young man kept his promise and sent a thank-you letter 【あのときはありがとうございました。ご恩は忘れません】 together with the repayment. The author felt: 「6千円で買えない温かい気持ちを贈られた気分で、数日うれしかった。」 He felt as if he had received warmth that could not be bought with 6,000 yen and was happy for several days.
default.q.n2-25-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this joy comes from receiving the letter and sensing the young man’s feelings after several months, not from feeling proud after doing a good deed at the station.
default.q.n2-25-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the young man returned the money rather than buying an object to give the author. “6千円で買えない” (“cannot be bought for 6,000 yen”) is a metaphor for his warm feelings (温かい気持ち).
default.q.n2-25-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The statement asks about everyone's schedule or plans for the day.
default.q.n2-25-q63-63.explanation:
Summary: One morning, while the family is hurriedly eating breakfast, the mother asks 「今日は？」 (What about today?). The family members (the father, older sister, and Chisa) take turns stating their plans for the day. The mother also announces that she will go out to attend a wine class and tells everyone to turn on the bathwater whoever gets home first.

- Question translation: What does the statement 「お母注んが「今日は？」と言った」 (The mother said, "What about today?") mean?
- Answer choices:
1. She was asking who would clean up after breakfast today.
2. She was asking about everyone’s schedule for today, including whether anyone would be home late.
3. She was asking whether anyone would stay home all day to clean and look after the house.
4. She was asking whether there was anything that needed to be done or anything to buy that she could be asked to take care of.
default.q.n2-25-q63-63.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage never says that the mother asked who would clean up after breakfast.
default.q.n2-25-q63-63.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because when the mother asks 「今日は？」, the family members take turns describing their schedules (Father: 「接待」, older sister: 「バイト」, Chisa: 「図書館」). The mother then gives her own schedule and asks who will come home first and heat the bathwater: 「カルチャーセンターの友達と、ワインの講習会に行くことになってるの。じゃあ、一番に帰ってきた人が、お風呂沸かしておいてくれる？」.
default.q.n2-25-q63-63.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the mother is only asking about the members’ schedules, not whether anyone will be home all day to clean and look after the house.
default.q.n2-25-q63-63.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the mother does not ask whether any family member wants her to buy or do anything for them.
default.q.n2-25-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Chisa wants to become a university student like her older sister soon so that she can enjoy the long summer vacation.
default.q.n2-25-q64-64.explanation:
Summary: On her way to school under the blazing sun, Chisa complains that high school is too restrictive because summer vacation still has not begun. She wishes she could enter university like her older sister and enjoy a long summer vacation, even though she knows that she must first go through the difficult university entrance examination.

- Question translation: Which phrase best fits the position ( ★ )?
- Answer choices:
1. Want to be able to enjoy a long summer vacation.
2. Want to study a specialized subject seriously and thoroughly.
3. Want to give her parents time to relax.
4. Want to do what she likes every day.
default.q.n2-25-q64-64.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because Chisa had complained that high school was restrictive and had still not given them summer vacation: 「こんなに暑くなる前に、さっさと夏休みにしてくれれば良いのに、学校というところは、いかにも窮屈な場所だ。早くお姉ちゃんのように大学生になって、（ ★ ）けれど...」. This shows that she wanted a long summer vacation like a university student.
default.q.n2-25-q64-64.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because in the passage, Chisa thinks only about the summer vacation and the comfort of entering university. She does not mention wanting to study her major seriously.
default.q.n2-25-q64-64.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention wanting to make one's parents comfortable and free from worry.
default.q.n2-25-q64-64.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the context continues the speaker's frustrated thoughts about the short summer vacation in high school. Thus, what she longs for when comparing herself with her university-student sister is a long summer vacation, not simply being able to do whatever one wants every day.
default.q.n2-25-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Around this time next year, Chisa will have to devote herself fully to studying for the university entrance examinations.
default.q.n2-25-q65-65.explanation:
Summary: Chisa realizes that at this time next year, she will have to work as hard as possible to prepare for the university entrance exam, just like Masa. Because she will face a demanding exam next year, she wants to enjoy this year’s summer vacation as fully and happily as possible.

- Question translation: Why does she say, “That is why I want to have as much fun as possible during this year’s summer vacation”?
- Answer choices:
1. Because next year she will have to devote herself completely to studying for the entrance exam.
2. Because she will do nothing but work part-time once she enters university, so she wants to enjoy her summer vacation.
3. Because she wants to experience many things while she is young and still able to be forgiven or given some leeway.
4. Because studying for the exam every day is so difficult that she wants to forget about it for a while.
default.q.n2-25-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because the reason is stated immediately beforehand: 「来年の今頃は、千紗だってマサくんみたいに、それなりに一生懸命に受験勉強をしなければならないだろう。だが、だからこそ今年は思い切り楽しい夏休みを過ごしたい。」
default.q.n2-25-q65-65.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage does not say that university consists entirely of part-time work; it implies that university offers a more relaxed summer vacation.
default.q.n2-25-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage contains no information about being forgiven or excused for enjoying one’s youth.
default.q.n2-25-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because Chisa is not yet under such pressure to prepare for an examination this year; she will have to prepare for the exam next year. Therefore, it is not because she wants to temporarily forget the hardship of studying for an exam every day.
default.q.n2-25-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The main character feels hesitant and apprehensive, unsure whether it is appropriate to enter a supermarket—“the domain of housewives.”
default.q.n2-25-q66-66.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant passage:** The protagonist enters a supermarket in front of the station and feels somewhat self-conscious and hesitant (「多少気がひけた」) because they regard it as a place exclusively for housewives (「主婦たちのテリトリー」), but the hesitation lasts only briefly after entering.

**Question translation:**
The passage says 「多少気がひけた」(felt somewhat hesitant). What was the protagonist feeling at the supermarket?

**Answer choices:**
1. Because the store was crowded, they felt that taking their time choosing items would inconvenience others.
2. Because housewives shop there, they became flustered and could not remain calm.
3. Because the supermarket was frequented by housewives, they hesitated, wondering whether it was all right for them to enter.
4. Although they had not visited shopping areas recently, they realized that they had actually liked them all along.
default.q.n2-25-q66-66.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage never says that the main character feared leisurely choosing items would obstruct or inconvenience others when the supermarket was crowded.
default.q.n2-25-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The main character only felt hesitant and embarrassed upon entering; it was not because they were rushed or flustered and unable to remain calm (あわててしまって落ち着かなかった).
default.q.n2-25-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct. Direct evidence from the passage: 「主婦た活のテリトリー である...こういう場所に縮 入 する のは多少気がひけたが、それも初めのう活だった。」 (I felt somewhat hesitant about entering a place that was the territory of housewives, but that was only at first.) The expression 「気がひける」 conveys a feeling of hesitation, reluctance, or uneasiness about whether it is acceptable to enter.
default.q.n2-25-q66-66.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the sentence 「もともと、こういう場所は嫌いじゃない」 shows that the character had not disliked these places from the beginning. It does not mean that the character had recently stopped going and only then realized that they had liked them all along; nor does it explain the feeling 「気がひけた」.
default.q.n2-25-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The phrase depicts many products of varied contents and types neatly and orderly arranged on shelves.
default.q.n2-25-q67-67.explanation:
**Summary of the main point:** The author feels fascinated and excited by the abundance of products in a supermarket, comparing the neatly arranged, tightly packed rows of seasonings and canned goods to the books lined up on shelves in a bookstore, with each book spine visible.

**Question translation:**
What does the phrase 「本屋で本の背表紙を見るよう」(like looking at book spines in a bookstore) mean?

**Answer choices:**
1. A scene in which items of various sizes, shapes, and contents are scattered everywhere.
2. A scene in which the contents are noted on the outside and everything is attractively arranged and decorated.
3. A scene in which countless items with a wide variety of contents are neatly and orderly arranged on shelves.
4. A scene in which many types of products are sorted by manufacturer.
default.q.n2-25-q67-67.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because 「あちこちに置かれている」(placed here and there) contradicts the image of book spines in a bookstore, which are neatly arranged in rows on shelves.
default.q.n2-25-q67-67.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because books in a bookstore are arranged neatly along the shelves, not beautifully decorated or displayed (美しく飾りつけられている).
default.q.n2-25-q67-67.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it directly quotes the passage: 「スパイスや缶詰の棚など、本屋で本の背表紙を見るよう で、ちょっとした興奮さえおぼえる。」 The spice and canned-food shelves resemble the rows of book spines in a bookstore, creating a slight sense of excitement. In a bookstore, countless books with diverse contents are neatly arranged on shelves; similarly, many kinds of spices and canned goods are lined up in an orderly fashion.
default.q.n2-25-q67-67.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage never mentions that the goods are classified by producer (生産者ごとに分類されている).
default.q.n2-25-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The protagonist feels as though it were 30 years ago because the dairy shop sells a yogurt container identical to the one their college sweetheart used to like, with the same design and paper lid as before.
default.q.n2-25-q68-68.explanation:
**Main point:** As the protagonist is about to head to the checkout, their attention is drawn to the dairy section by a glass yogurt jar—the favorite item of their first romantic partner during university. Among the modern paper cartons, the short, rounded yogurt jar with its paper lid still has the design it had 30 years ago, bringing back a rush of nostalgia and making the protagonist feel as though that particular corner had remained frozen 30 years in the past.

**Question translation:**
Why did the protagonist think that 「そこだけ三十年前のようだった」(it was as though only that spot were 30 years ago)?

**Answer choices:**
1. Because they remembered the yogurt shop where they used to buy yogurt for their romantic partner 30 years ago.
2. Because that place sold exactly the same type of yogurt that their romantic partner had loved as a university student.
3. Because the dairy section looked very much like the store display in their memory.
4. Because the dairy section displayed its products in the same way as stores had 30 years ago.
default.q.n2-25-q68-68.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is incorrect because the passage never mentions that the main character often bought yogurt for their partner or recalled a specific yogurt shop from 30 years earlier.
default.q.n2-25-q68-68.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because it is directly supported by the passage: 「学生時答、初めてつきあった恋人の、好物だったびん入りヨー子ルト。ずんぐりした小型のびんといい紙のフタといい、なんとなくくすんだ ガラスの表面といい、昔のままだ。整然と 並んだ清潔な紙パック入り乳製品の中で、 そこだけ三十年前のようだった。」 (The bottled yogurt had been the favorite food of the author’s first partner when they were students. The short, stout bottle, the paper lid, and the slightly cloudy glass surface were all just as they had been in the past. Among the neatly arranged, clean paper cartons of dairy products, that spot alone seemed to belong to thirty years earlier.)
default.q.n2-25-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect. It is not that the entire dairy counter resembles the scene in the writer's memory; only the position of the traditional yogurt jars remains unchanged among the modern paper milk cartons.
default.q.n2-25-q68-68.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not mention that the milk counter was decorated or arranged in the style of a shop from 30 years ago.
default.q.n2-25-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 4. The idiomatic expression 「開いた口がふさがらない」 describes being speechless and astonished at the outrageous, disgraceful behavior of the groom’s friends as they fought over the microphone.
default.q.n2-25-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: Passage B records the impressions of a colleague of the bride. At first, the party is warm and enjoyable, but after drinking too much, the groom's friends begin to go too far (やりすぎ) and even fight over the microphone to sing karaoke, leaving writer B speechless in shock (開いた口がふさがりませんでした).
- Question translation: What feeling is expressed by 「開いた口がふ注がりませんでした」 (being left speechless in shock)?
- Answer choices:
1. Being astonished by an exceptionally joyful scene and unable to speak.
2. Being moved by an exceptionally beautiful singing voice and unable to speak.
3. Being jealous of the overwhelming congratulations and unable to speak.
4. Being astonished by behavior so outrageous and terrible that one is unable to speak.
default.q.n2-25-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the idiom 「開いた口がふさがらない」describes being stunned or dismayed by another person's negative or excessive behavior. It is not used for surprise at an "extremely cheerful scene."
default.q.n2-25-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage only says that the groom’s friends fought over the microphone like participants at a karaoke contest (カラオケ大会のようにマイクを奪いあった). It does not mention singing ability (歌のうまさ) or being moved by the song.
default.q.n2-25-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this idiom does not mean feeling jealous of or admiring someone (うらやましい) after receiving congratulations.
default.q.n2-25-q69-69.why.3: (d) Correct. The evidence is the author B’s comment about the groom’s friends going too far: 「新郎のお友達が元気なのはとてもいいんですが、ちょっとやりすぎだなと思うところもありました。最後のほうで、カラオケ大会のようにマイクを奪いあったときは、 開いた口がふ注がりませんでした」. The idiom 「開いた口がふさがらない」 means being astonished, stunned, or speechless at how excessive or appalling (ひどさ) something is.
default.q.n2-25-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3. Both A and B view it as a warm and pleasant wedding reception, but B is somewhat put off by A’s friends drinking too much and taking over the microphone.
default.q.n2-25-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point: Both A (the groom’s friend) and B (the bride’s coworker) think the wedding reception was wonderful, warm, and a happy celebration for the couple. However, A admits that his group drank so much that they almost forgot they were at a wedding, while B also felt that the groom’s friends were overly rowdy (やりすぎ) and fought over the microphone, leaving B somewhat annoyed or dissatisfied with their behavior.
- Question translation: Which of the following is correct about A’s and B’s impressions?
- Answer choices:
1. Both A and B thought it was a wonderful party, but B thought it would have been better without karaoke.
2. A thought it was a wonderful party, but B thought it would have been better without A’s group.
3. Both A and B thought it was a wonderful party, but B was somewhat annoyed or dissatisfied with A’s group’s behavior.
4. A thought it was a wonderful party, but B thought it was a terrible party.
default.q.n2-25-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because B does not claim that “there should be no karaoke.” B merely uses the comparison “like a karaoke contest” (カラオケ大会のようにマイクを奪いあった) to describe A’s friends excessively fighting over the microphone.
default.q.n2-25-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because B never wishes that A's group did not exist. B even praises the lively groom's friends (新郎のお友達が元気なのはとてもいいんですが) and concludes that it is "not something worth getting angry about" (怒るほどのことではありませんね).
default.q.n2-25-q70-70.why.2: (c) Correct. Both A and B praise the wedding party (A: 「とてもいい結婚パーティーでした」; B: 「考え方によっては友達のお祝いを受けたということですから、怒るほどのことではありませんね」「きっと幸せになれるでしょう」), but B feels that A's group went too far by getting drunk and taking the microphone (「ちょっとやりすぎだなと思うところもありました」「開いた口がふさがりませんでした」).
default.q.n2-25-q70-70.why.3: (d) This is incorrect because B does not regard it as a terrible party (ひどいパーティー). B still thinks the bride is beautiful, the cake is delicious, and sincerely wishes the couple happiness.
default.q.n2-25-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: They think that studying or thinking at night would be more effective.
default.q.n2-25-q71-71.explanation:
- Main point: The opening of the article discusses how people are increasingly becoming nocturnal (夜行性). Although they continue to work normally during the day, people firmly assume and absolutely believe that intellectual activities and studying should be done at night ("夜の信仰" - an absolute faith in nighttime).
- Translation of the question: The article says, "They have created something that could be called a nighttime religion." What does "nighttime religion" mean?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Working at night and sleeping during the day or in the morning.
  2. Living a life like young people do.
  3. Living a life like elderly people do.
  4. Believing that studying or thinking is better done at night.
default.q.n2-25-q71-71.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage clearly states that working during the day is normal (「昼間働くのが常態」). The "religion of the night" refers only to intellectual activities (知的活動), not to completely reversing one's schedule to work at night and sleep during the day.
default.q.n2-25-q71-71.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because young people are only an example of people who habitually stay up late and sleep late (「現在の若ものも当然のように宵っ張りの朝寝坊になって」); the expression itself does not mean living like young people.
default.q.n2-25-q71-71.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because in the passage, getting up early is what young people mock as old-fashioned (「老人くさい、と笑われる始末である」), which is the complete opposite of a “nighttime belief.”
default.q.n2-25-q71-71.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the context is made clear: 「こと、知的活動になると、夜ときめてしまう」 and 「勉強は夜でなくてはできないものと、思いこんでいる」 (They decide that intellectual activities must be done at night and assume that studying cannot be done unless it is nighttime).
default.q.n2-25-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: It has happened many times that things one could not manage to do in the evening could be completed easily the next morning.
default.q.n2-25-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: The author recounts a personal experience: sometimes they struggle with a problem at night and cannot solve it, so they go to bed and work on it the next morning. When they begin again in the morning, the problem is solved smoothly and easily. At first, they thought this was coincidental, but it happened so many times that they found it strange (“これはおかしい”) and realized that their mind was clearer in the morning than at night.
- Question translation: There is a statement saying, “This is strange.” What does “this” (これ) refer to here?
- Answer choices:
  1. The content of a book about the experience of having letters published overseas.
  2. The proverb “Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today.”
  3. The fact that things they could not manage at night were repeatedly completed easily the next morning.
  4. The fact that better ideas occur at night than in the morning.
default.q.n2-25-q72-72.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inaccurate because the foreign book about letter-writing experience is merely an example mentioned in the previous paragraph to demonstrate the difference between bright and dark ways of thinking; it is not the unusual thing referred to by "これ."
default.q.n2-25-q72-72.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because the proverb "Do not put off until tomorrow what you can do today" is merely a passing thought that occurred to the author before going to bed; it is not what 「これ」 refers to.
default.q.n2-25-q72-72.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it directly connects to the preceding text: 「ゆうべはあんなに手におえなかった問題が、するすると片づいてしまうではないか」 and 「偶然にしては同じことがあまりにも多すぎる」 (The problem that had been impossible to handle the previous night was solved smoothly by morning, and this had happened too many times to be mere coincidence.)
default.q.n2-25-q72-72.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is inaccurate because the author says that the mind is apparently sharper in the morning than at night (「朝の頭の方が、夜の頭よりも、優秀であるらしい」), which is the opposite of what the choice states.
default.q.n2-25-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: The author used to do intellectually demanding activities at night but realized that doing them in the morning made it easier to complete tasks efficiently.
default.q.n2-25-q73-73.explanation:
- Main point summary: The passage describes a change in the author's understanding. The author used to have a habit and belief that intellectual work should be done at night, but through experiences such as writing letters and handling practical tasks, came to realize that intellectual work in the morning is much more efficient and allows tasks to be completed much more smoothly than in the evening.
- Question translation: What is the author's main point in this passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. The number of night owls is increasing, but even if people say they are becoming like old people, working in the morning is more efficient...
  2. The author used to do intellectual work at night but realized that tasks can be handled more efficiently in the morning.
  3. After reading a foreign book about the experience of writing letters, the author felt that letters should be left overnight and reread the next day before being sent...
  4. Intellectual work in the morning is not at all a sign of old age, so young people should also change their lifestyles...
default.q.n2-25-q73-73.why.0: (a) Option 1 is inaccurate because the author focuses on the efficiency of intellectual activity (知的活動), not on the general recommendation to work during the day (昼間働くのが常態). The detail about being told that one resembles an old person is merely a minor point at the beginning.
default.q.n2-25-q73-73.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage’s concluding message is summarized in the quotations: from the habit of 「こと、知的活動になると、夜ときめてしまう」, the author realized that 「朝の頭の方が、夜の頭よりも、優秀であるらしい」 and that 「ゆうべはあんなに手におえなかった問題が、するすると片づいてしまう」, concluding 「朝と夜とでは、同じ人間でありながら、人が違うことを思い知らされた」.
default.q.n2-25-q73-73.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the foreign book about letter writing is merely an example supporting the observation that bright and dark ways of thinking differ; it is not the core message of the passage.
default.q.n2-25-q73-73.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage shares the author's awareness and reflections on how she thinks; it does not focus on advising or urging young people to change their lifestyles.
default.q.n2-25-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 3: For the fourth class (△× February), students need to bring basic supplies—a small sketchbook, pencils, an eraser, and drawing colors—along with a frame at least A4 size and glass materials.

For the fourth session, the additional supplies specified are an A4-size-or-larger frame「A4サイズ以上の額」and glassware「ガラス」, while an apple「リンゴ」is the subject for a different session and should not be brought to session 4.

default.q.n2-25-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 大 (forming the prefix 「大歓迎」 - だいかんげい: a very warm welcome or enthusiastic reception).
default.q.n2-25-q11-11.explanation:
Meaning: Because he was the first international student from Japan, he was given an extremely warm welcome.
Sino-Japanese reading: 大歓迎 (a very warm welcome).
Example: 新入社員を大歓迎する。(To give new employees a very warm welcome.)
default.q.n2-25-q11-11.why.0: (a) 1. 超: The prefix 「超〜」 (super-, ultra-, extremely) commonly combines with adjectives or nouns indicating scale or state, such as 超満員 and 超小型. It does not form the standard word *超歓迎 in this context.
default.q.n2-25-q11-11.why.1: (b) 2. 熱: Japanese has no word *熱歓迎. To express a warm welcome, the four-character expression 熱烈歓迎 (ねつれつかんげい) is used rather than attaching the single syllable 熱 directly to 歓迎.
default.q.n2-25-q11-11.why.2: (c) 3. 高: The prefix 「高〜」 commonly indicates a high level, value, or status, as in 高収入, 高性能, and 高学歴; it does not combine with 歓迎.
default.q.n2-25-q11-11.why.3: (d) 4. 大: The prefix 「大〜」 indicates a large degree or great importance. Combined with 歓迎, it forms the noun/verb 大歓迎 (だいかんげい), meaning a very warm welcome.
default.q.n2-25-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 1. かけた (combining to form the compound verb 「やりかけた」: started but left unfinished).
default.q.n2-25-q12-12.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Just as I was in the middle of doing my homework, a friend came over.
Grammar pattern: 「V (ます-stem) + かける / かけた」indicates an action that has been started but is unfinished when it is interrupted or stopped.
Example: テーブルの上に食べかけのケーキが置いてある。(There is a half-eaten cake on the table.)
default.q.n2-25-q12-12.why.0: (a) 1. かけた: The suffix「〜かける」(past form「〜かけた」) follows the verb stem after removing ます and expresses an action that has been started but remains unfinished (やりかける: to leave something half-done).
default.q.n2-25-q12-12.why.1: (b) 2. かかった: 「かかる」is an intransitive verb and cannot be attached after the ます-stem of another verb to mean “leave something unfinished” (*やりかかった is incorrect).
default.q.n2-25-q12-12.why.2: (c) 3. 続いた: 「続く」is an intransitive verb and does not directly follow a verb in the ます-stem form as a compound suffix (*やりつづいた is incorrect).
default.q.n2-25-q12-12.why.3: (d) 4. 続けた: The pattern 「Vます + 続ける」 means to continue doing something without stopping. However, the context contains 「〜ところへ」 (“just as...”), indicating that another event interrupts the action. Therefore, 「やりかけた」 (started but left unfinished) is the most accurate and natural choice.
default.q.n2-25-q13-13.verdict: The answer key gives 4. 採; however, this is incorrect, probably due to a printing/OCR error involving 青 in 青白い or 薄 in 薄白い. 採 cannot be combined with 白い.
default.q.n2-25-q13-13.explanation:
Sentence meaning: A bright white moon is appearing in the night sky.
Analysis: Standard Japanese commonly uses compound words describing moonlight, such as 「青白い」(あおじろい - bluish-white, pale), 「薄白い」(うすじろい - faintly white), or 「真白い」(ましろい - pure white). The kanji 「採」 does not add any meaning related to color.
Correct example: 青白い月の光が夜道を照らしている。(Bluish-white moonlight is illuminating the night road.)
default.q.n2-25-q13-13.why.0: (a) 1. 黄: The form 「黄白い」 (きじろい, “yellowish white”) is very rare in modern Japanese and is not used to describe the moon at night.
default.q.n2-25-q13-13.why.1: (b) 2. 赤: 「赤白い」(あかじろい: whitish-red) usually describes a person’s complexion and is not used to describe moonlight.
default.q.n2-25-q13-13.why.2: (c) 3. 黒: The compound *黒白い does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n2-25-q13-13.why.3: (d) 4. 採: The provided answer is 4, but 採 (to pick, select) cannot function as a color-related prefix when combined with 「白い」. This may be a question or OCR error involving 青, forming 青白い (あおじろい, bluish-white), or 薄, forming 薄白い.
default.q.n2-25-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 的 (forms the na-adjective 「消極的」 — しょうきょくてき: passive, negative).
default.q.n2-25-q14-14.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Her passive personality is due to the way her parents raised her.
Kanji compound: 消極的 (passive, negative), the antonym of 積極的 (active, positive).
Example: 彼は何事に対しても消極的な態度をとる。(He always takes a passive attitude toward everything.)
default.q.n2-25-q14-14.why.0: (a) 1. 風: The suffix 「〜風」 means style or in the manner of, as in 現代風 and 西洋風; it does not combine with 消極.
default.q.n2-25-q14-14.why.1: (b) 2. 的: The suffix「〜的」(having the nature of...) attaches to a noun to form a na-adjective, as in 消極的な (しょうきょくてきな: passive, negative).
default.q.n2-25-q14-14.why.2: (c) 3. 級: The suffix 「〜級」 indicates rank or level (as in 上級 and プロ級) and does not combine with 消極.
default.q.n2-25-q14-14.why.3: (d) 4. 界: The suffix 「〜界」means a field or sphere, as in 芸能界 and 医学界, and does not follow 消極.
default.q.n2-25-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 出す, which forms the compound verb 「言い出す」—いいだす—meaning “to bring up,” “to say,” or “to put forward an idea.”
default.q.n2-25-q15-15.explanation:
Meaning: It is very difficult to speak up and voice an opposing opinion.
Kanji: 言い出す (say something, speak up, put forward an opinion).
Example: 最初にその計画を言い出したのは田中さんだ。(Tanaka was the first person to suggest that plan.)
default.q.n2-25-q15-15.why.0: (a) 1. 上げる: The suffix 「〜上げる」 indicates completing something or directing an action upward, as in 読み上げる and 仕上げる; it does not combine with 言う in the context of proposing or expressing an opposing opinion.
default.q.n2-25-q15-15.why.1: (b) 2. 上がる: 「上がる」is an intransitive verb and cannot be attached after the V-masu stem to form *言い上がる.
default.q.n2-25-q15-15.why.2: (c) 3. 出す: The suffix 「〜出す」is attached to the verb stem after removing ます and means “to begin” or “to bring something out.” 「言い出す」means to start saying something or put forward an opinion.
default.q.n2-25-q15-15.why.3: (d) 4. 出る: 「出る」 is an intransitive verb and cannot follow the V-masu stem to form *言い出る.
default.q.n2-25-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 展開 (development, progression in a certain direction).
default.q.n2-25-q16-16.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The discussion developed in an unexpected direction.
Kanji vocabulary: 展開 (development, progression, unfolding).

default.q.n2-25-q16-16.why.1: (b) 展望: a long-range view, future outlook (e.g., 展望台, observation deck; 将来を展望する, look toward the future). It is not used to mean the course or development of a discussion.
default.q.n2-25-q16-16.why.2: (c) 拡張 means expanding the scale, scope, or size, such as 道路を拡張する (expand a road) or 機能を拡張する (expand functionality); it is not used for the direction of a discussion.
default.q.n2-25-q16-16.why.3: (d) 拡大 means “to expand” or “enlarge,” as in 被害が拡大する (the damage spreads) and 地図を拡大する (enlarge a map). It does not combine with 「方向へ～する」in this context.
default.q.n2-25-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 成功 (combining with を収めた to form 成功を収める: to achieve success).
default.q.n2-25-q17-17.explanation:
Meaning: After starting his own business independently, he achieved great success.

default.q.n2-25-q17-17.why.0: (a) 泊果 is not a Japanese vocabulary word with a meaning; 泊 has been confused with 結 in 結果 or 成 in 成果.
default.q.n2-25-q17-17.why.1: (b) 結果: result; it commonly takes expressions such as「結果を出す / 結果を得る / 結果が残る」, not「～をおさめる」.
default.q.n2-25-q17-17.why.2: (c) 成功 (SUCCESS): success; combined with the verb 収める（おさめる）to form the fixed expression 「成功を収める」, meaning to achieve great success.
default.q.n2-25-q17-17.why.3: (d) 効率 (efficiency): work efficiency, commonly used with 「効率を上げる」 or 「効率がいい」; it does not combine with 「～をおさめる」.
default.q.n2-25-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 名物 (a specialty or famous product of a particular locality).
default.q.n2-25-q18-18.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I bought a local specialty apple confection as a souvenir from the trip.

Meaning: The food at that restaurant tastes exactly the way I like it.

default.q.n2-25-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 手間 (combined with がかかる to form 手間がかかる: require a great deal of effort and time).
default.q.n2-25-q20-20.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Although it is only a small garden, taking care of the plants requires quite a lot of effort.

default.q.n2-25-q20-20.why.0: (a) 手間 (SHU-KAN): the time and effort required to complete a task; combined with 「かかる」, it forms the fixed expression 「手間がかかる」, meaning “to take a lot of time and effort.”
default.q.n2-25-q20-20.why.1: (b) 手入れ (THỦ NHẬP): care, trimming, maintenance; this word combines with 「をする」 (e.g., 庭の手入れをする, tend the garden), not 「がかかる」.
default.q.n2-25-q20-20.why.2: (c) 手ぬぐい: a traditional Japanese cloth hand towel or face towel; it is a noun referring to an object and does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-25-q20-20.why.3: (d) 手前 (on-reading: しゅぜん): in front, directly before someone, or one's pride/face; it cannot combine with 「がかかる」 in this sentence.
default.q.n2-25-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 言いわけ (an excuse, justification, or explanation for a mistake).
default.q.n2-25-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning: If you refuse to admit your own fault and keep making excuses, it will only sound like a justification.
On-reading: 言い訳 means an excuse, justification, or rationalization.
Common expressions: 「言い訳をする」 = make excuses; 「言い訳に聞こえる」 = sound like an excuse.
Another example: 失敗したときは、言い訳をせずに素直に謝るべきだ (When you fail, you should apologize honestly instead of making excuses.)
default.q.n2-25-q21-21.why.0: (a) 言いつけ (INSTRUCTION): an instruction or order from a superior, or tattling (e.g., 先生の言いつけ, “the teacher’s instruction”); it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-25-q21-21.why.1: (b) 言い分: an argument, justification, or explanation put forward by one side in a dispute (e.g., お互いの言い分, “both sides’ arguments”); here, it refers to an excuse for avoiding responsibility for a mistake.
default.q.n2-25-q21-21.why.2: (c) 言い伝え: A legend or folk tale orally passed down from ancient times (e.g., 古い言い伝え — an old legend). It does not fit the intended meaning.
default.q.n2-25-q21-21.why.3: (d) 言いわけ (usually written 言い訳): an excuse, justification, rationalization; 「言いわけに聞こえる」 describes the listener feeling that the explanation is merely intended to avoid responsibility.
default.q.n2-25-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 1. くせ (a habit, an individual's characteristic tendency).
default.q.n2-25-q22-22.explanation:
Meaning: He has a habit of folding down the corners of pages where he finds something interesting.
Vocabulary: 癖 (personal habit, quirk).
Grammar/expression: 「動詞辞書形 ＋ くせ（癖）がある」 = have a habit of doing something.
Additional example: 彼は緊張すると爪をかむくせがある (He has a habit of biting his nails when he gets nervous).
default.q.n2-25-q22-22.why.0: (a) くせ (癖): A person’s habit or personal quirk; in 「～するくせがある」, it means “to have a habit of doing something.”
default.q.n2-25-q22-22.why.1: (b) けが (怪我): injury, physical wound (e.g., 足にけがをする, injure one’s leg); it is completely inappropriate in this context.
default.q.n2-25-q22-22.why.2: (c) きまり (決まり): a rule or regulation shared by a group (e.g., 学校の決まり: school rules); it is not used for an individual's personal habit.
default.q.n2-25-q22-22.why.3: (d) かた (方 / 型): Means a way of doing something, as in 読み方 and 作り方, or a model/type; it does not combine with 「～するかたがある」 to express a habit.
default.q.n2-25-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 不安だ because 「心細い」means anxious, uneasy, or lacking a sense of support.
default.q.n2-25-q23-23.explanation:
- Meaning: Living alone for the first time feels very unsettling and anxiety-provoking.
- Vocabulary: 「心細い」（こころぼそい - literally, “heart + thin”）means feeling anxious, insecure, or lonely because one lacks support or reassurance.
- Example: 一人で外国へ行くのは心細い。(Going abroad alone feels very unsettling.)
default.q.n2-25-q23-23.why.0: (a) 「不安だ」means “anxious, worried, or uneasy,” making it the closest synonym for「心細い」when describing anxiety about living alone for the first time.
default.q.n2-25-q23-23.why.1: (b) 「さびしい」 means "lonely" or "sad" because someone is absent; it does not emphasize anxiety or a lack of emotional support as 「心細い」 does.
default.q.n2-25-q23-23.why.2: (c) 「つらい」 means physically or emotionally painful, bitter, or difficult; it is not synonymous with 「心細い」.
default.q.n2-25-q23-23.why.3: (d) 「不要心だ」: 「不要心」(usually written 不用心 - ふようじん) means “careless, negligent, insufficiently cautious,” and is not used to describe a feeling of anxiety.
default.q.n2-25-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 静かに, because 「そっと」 means gently, quietly, or without making a sound.
default.q.n2-25-q24-24.explanation:
- Meaning: I gently closed the door.
- Vocabulary: 「そっと」is an adverb describing a gentle, quiet action performed without making a sound or drawing attention.
- Example: 赤ちゃんを起こさないように、そっと部屋を出た。(I quietly left the room so as not to wake the baby.)
default.q.n2-25-q24-24.why.0: (a) 「きちんと」 means “neatly, properly, carefully”; it does not express being gentle or making no noise.
default.q.n2-25-q24-24.why.1: (b) 「しっかりと」 means “firmly, securely, steadily,” and is not synonymous with 「そっと」.
default.q.n2-25-q24-24.why.2: (c) 「静かに」 means “quietly, gently, softly,” making it an exact synonym of 「そっと」 when closing a door quietly.
default.q.n2-25-q24-24.why.3: (d) 「素早く」 means “quickly, swiftly” (すばやく); it does not describe something quiet or gentle.
default.q.n2-25-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 2. つめたい because 「そっけない」 means cold, curt, or aloof.
default.q.n2-25-q25-25.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: I received a cold, curt reply from him.
- Vocabulary: 「素っ気ない」（そっけない—cold, curt, unfriendly, showing little concern）describes a cold or indifferent attitude.
- Example: 相談に乗ってほしいと頼んだが、そっけない態度を取られた。(I asked him for advice, but he responded with a very cold attitude.)
default.q.n2-25-q25-25.why.0: (a) 「あじけない」: 「味気ない」 means “insipid, dull, or dreary,” often describing life or a succession of days. It is not used to describe a curt manner of responding.
default.q.n2-25-q25-25.why.1: (b) 「つめたい」: 「冷たい」 can mean cold-hearted, distant, or insensitive, making it the closest synonym to 「そっけない」 when describing a reply or manner toward someone.
default.q.n2-25-q25-25.why.2: (c) 「やるせない」: “sorrowful, helpless, unbearably frustrated,” describing a gloomy feeling that cannot be relieved; it does not fit the context of the answer.
default.q.n2-25-q25-25.why.3: (d) 「きどらない」: 「気取らない」means “natural,” “unpretentious,” or “not putting on airs,” with a positive nuance.
default.q.n2-25-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 4. まじめに, because 「真剣に」 means seriously, earnestly, or in a sincere manner.
default.q.n2-25-q26-26.explanation:
- Meaning: I am thinking seriously about the future.
- Kanji and vocabulary: 「真剣」（しんけん）literally means “real sword,” and figuratively means serious, earnest, and fully committed.
- Example: 彼は真剣な表情で先生の話を聞いていた。(He listened to the teacher with a very serious expression.)
default.q.n2-25-q26-26.why.0: (a) 「熱心に」: means “enthusiastically, eagerly, passionately” (devoting oneself to study or work), and does not mean thinking seriously or earnestly like「真剣に」.
default.q.n2-25-q26-26.why.1: (b) 「重要に」: 「重要」 is a na-adjective meaning “important”; it does not combine as 「重要に考える」 to express thinking seriously.
default.q.n2-25-q26-26.why.2: (c) 「ていねいに」: 「丁寧に」 means politely, carefully, attentively, or meticulously; it is not synonymous with 「真剣に」 in this context.
default.q.n2-25-q26-26.why.3: (d) 「まじめに」means “seriously, earnestly, sincerely” and is the most accurate synonym for「真剣に」when thinking about the future.
default.q.n2-25-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 意図的に because 「わざと」 means intentionally, deliberately, or on purpose.
default.q.n2-25-q27-27.explanation:
- Meaning: I deliberately threw the ball at someone, so I was scolded.
- Vocabulary: 「わざと」 is an adverb meaning deliberately or intentionally; 「意図的」（いとてき）means intentional or deliberate. Distinguish 「わざと」(deliberately doing something bad or inappropriate) from 「わざわざ」(taking the trouble to do something despite the effort involved).
- Example: 彼はわざと聞こえないふりをした。(He deliberately pretended not to hear.)
default.q.n2-25-q27-27.why.0: (a) 「わざわざ」 means going out of one’s way to do something despite the time or effort involved. It does not describe intentionally doing something wrong.
default.q.n2-25-q27-27.why.1: (b) 「意図的に」 means “deliberately,” “intentionally,” or “purposely,” and is an exact synonym of 「わざと」.
default.q.n2-25-q27-27.why.2: (c) 「素早く」 means “quickly, swiftly” and is unrelated to whether an action is intentional or accidental.
default.q.n2-25-q27-27.why.3: (d) 「積極的に」means “actively / positively.” Its positive nuance does not fit the context of throwing a ball at someone and causing trouble.
default.q.n2-25-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 私の大学は最近、図書館の設備を 拡 充 した。
default.q.n2-25-q28-28.explanation:
「拡充」（かくじゅう）means expanding the scale while improving quality and strengthening or enhancing the content, facilities, or system. It is commonly used with 設備・施設・制度・人員・サービスなどを拡充する.

default.q.n2-25-q28-28.why.0: Correct because 「設備を拡充する」 is a proper collocation meaning to expand and enhance library facilities in both quantity and quality.
default.q.n2-25-q28-28.why.1: Incorrect: To expand a road in terms of width or space, use 「拡張」（かくちょう）or 「拡幅」, not 「拡充」.
default.q.n2-25-q28-28.why.2: Incorrect. The term for an additional software or computer feature is 「拡張機能」 (extension/add-on), not 「拡充機能」.
default.q.n2-25-q28-28.why.3: Incorrect: To make life richer and more fulfilling, use「充実させる」（人生を充実させる）, not「拡充させる」.
default.q.n2-25-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 塩分を 過剰 に取ると心臓の病気を引き起こすことがある。
default.q.n2-25-q29-29.explanation:
「過剰」（かじょう）is a noun/na-adjective indicating a state that exceeds the normal or necessary level, usually with a negative connotation (excessive, superfluous). Common expressions: 過剰摂取、過剰反応、過剰包装、過剰な期待。
Example: 自信過剰になると、思わぬミスをしてしまう。
default.q.n2-25-q29-29.why.0: Incorrect: 「過剰」is not used as the verb 「過剰する」; for exceeding a budget, use 「予算をオーバーする／超過する」.
default.q.n2-25-q29-29.why.1: Incorrect: 「過剰に」 is not used for studying and working harder than usual. 「懸命に／猛烈に／いつも以上に」 would be appropriate here.
default.q.n2-25-q29-29.why.2: Incorrect: For unnecessary or excess belongings in a room, use 「余分な（もの）」, 「不要な（もの）」, or 「余計な（もの）」.
default.q.n2-25-q29-29.why.3: Correct: 「塩分を過剰に取る（過剰摂取）」 is the standard expression for taking in more salt than necessary.
default.q.n2-25-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 2: この町はたくさんの若い人が集まり、いつ来ても 活気 がある。
default.q.n2-25-q30-30.explanation:
「活気」（かっき）refers to the lively, energetic atmosphere of a place (such as a neighborhood, market, or event) or a group. It is commonly used with: 活気がある・ない, 活気に満ちている, 活気を帯びる.
Example: 商店街は買い物客で活気にあふれていた。
default.q.n2-25-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect: To encourage and cheer up a sick person, use 「元気づける／励ます」. 「活気づける」 is generally used to invigorate a market, economy, neighborhood, and so on.
default.q.n2-25-q30-30.why.1: Correct: 「町に活気がある」 is a standard collocation describing a neighborhood or town as lively, bustling, and full of vitality.
default.q.n2-25-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect: for fresh fish or shrimp that are alive and moving vigorously, use「生きがいい／活きがいい」, not「活気がある」, which is not used for animals or fish.
default.q.n2-25-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect: To describe the confidence, vitality, or energy conveyed by an individual who works effectively, expressions such as 「バイタリティ／覇気／頼もしさ」 are commonly used. 「活気」 describes the atmosphere of a group or place.
default.q.n2-25-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 慣れないので、 苦心 してパソコンで書類を作成した。
default.q.n2-25-q31-31.explanation:
「苦心」（くしん）means to devote considerable effort, rack one’s brains, and try every possible way to overcome difficulties in order to complete something (to labor over something, take great pains).
Common expressions: 苦心して〜する, 苦心の作 (a work produced with great effort).
Example: 彼は苦心して新しいプログラムを完成させた。
default.q.n2-25-q31-31.why.0: Correct: 「苦心して〜する」describes putting in considerable effort and struggling to find a way to complete the document while inexperienced.
default.q.n2-25-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect. To express gratitude, embarrassment, or humility when receiving excessively kind treatment from someone, use 「恐縮（です）」 or 「恐れ入ります」.
default.q.n2-25-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect: The hardship and struggle parents experience in raising children is expressed with the noun 「苦労」（親の苦労）, not 「苦心」.
default.q.n2-25-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect: feeling uncomfortable or being poor at interacting with someone should use 「苦手（だ）」, not 「苦心」.
default.q.n2-25-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 何もしないであとで くやむ くらいなら今すぐ行動すべきだ。
default.q.n2-25-q32-32.explanation:
「悔やむ」（くやむ）means to regret or feel sorry about a past action or decision that led to a bad result. It can also mean to express condolences or mourn someone’s death (悔やみを述べる). Common expressions: 後で悔やむ、過去を悔やむ、悔やんでも悔やみきれない。
Example: どんなに悔やんでも、過ぎた時間は戻らない。
default.q.n2-25-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect: feeling jealous or envious of someone else's promotion is expressed with 「ねたむ／うらやむ」, not 「くやむ」.
default.q.n2-25-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect: After having an accident but fortunately avoiding serious injury, one would feel relieved or reassured, expressed with 「ほっとした／安心した」.
default.q.n2-25-q32-32.why.2: Correct: 「あとで悔やむ」 is a natural and accurate expression meaning that one will regret later not having taken action.
default.q.n2-25-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect: To describe blaming oneself or lamenting one’s abilities, use 「嘆く（なげく）」 or 「責める」. 「悔やむ」 generally takes a specific past action or event.
default.q.n2-25-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 2. うら: The kanji 「裏」 has the kun-reading 「うら」, meaning the back or reverse side.
default.q.n2-25-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: There is a field behind my house.

- Example: コインの裏と表 (The reverse and obverse sides of a coin).
default.q.n2-25-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「おもて」(表) means the front or outward surface, the opposite of「裏」.
default.q.n2-25-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「うら」(裏) is the correct kunyomi reading of 「裏」, meaning the back or the rear side of a house.
default.q.n2-25-q1-1.why.2: (c) 「わき」 (脇) refers to the armpit, side, or vicinity; it is not the reading of 「裏」.
default.q.n2-25-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「そば」(側/傍) indicates a position beside or near something; it is not the reading of 「裏」.
default.q.n2-25-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2. さいふ: the kanji 「財布」 is correctly read as 「さいふ」.
default.q.n2-25-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: There are only 50 yen left in my wallet.

default.q.n2-25-q2-2.why.0: (a) 「ざいふ」is incorrect because the「財」in「財布」has the unvoiced reading「さい」, not「ざい」.
default.q.n2-25-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「さいふ」is the correct on-reading of 「財布」(財 - さい + 布 - ふ), meaning wallet.
default.q.n2-25-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「さいふう」is incorrect because 「布」(ふ) does not have a long vowel.
default.q.n2-25-q2-2.why.3: (d) 「さいほう」 (裁縫) means sewing and mending, and is not the reading of 「財布」.
default.q.n2-25-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 4. つかまった: the verb 「捕まる」 is read 「つかまる」, and its past form is 「つかまった」.
default.q.n2-25-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: The pickpocket was arrested.

- Example: 犯人が警察に捕まった。(The criminal was arrested by the police.)
default.q.n2-25-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「とまった」is the past form of「止まる」(to stop) or「泊まる」(to stay overnight), not the reading of「捕まった」.
default.q.n2-25-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「かまった」 is the past form of 「構う」 (to care about, to mind) and is unrelated to 「捕」.
default.q.n2-25-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「あやまった」 is the past form of 「謝る」 (to apologize) or 「誤る」 (to be mistaken or make a mistake).
default.q.n2-25-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「つかまった」 is the past form of the intransitive verb 「捕まる」 (“be arrested” or “be caught”), which fits the context of the pickpocket being caught.
default.q.n2-25-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ていりゅうじょ: 「停留所」is correctly read as「ていりゅうじょ」.
default.q.n2-25-q4-4.explanation:

default.q.n2-25-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「ていはくじょ」 is incorrect because 「留」(りゅう) was confused with 「泊」(はく in 停泊 - ていはく - a ship or boat being moored).
default.q.n2-25-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「ているじょ」is incorrect because「留」is read with its on-reading「りゅう」here, not「る」(as in 留守 - るす).

default.q.n2-25-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「ていりゅうじょ」 is the standard on-reading of 「停留所」 (停 - てい + 留 - りゅう + 所 - じょ), meaning a bus stop.
default.q.n2-25-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ていど: The kanji 「程度」 is correctly read as 「ていど」.
default.q.n2-25-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: It is impossible to be satisfied at this level.

default.q.n2-25-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「ていど」 is the correct on-reading of 「程度」 (程 - てい + 度 - ど), meaning degree or level.
default.q.n2-25-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「おんど」(温度) means temperature; the first kanji is 「温」, not 「程」.
default.q.n2-25-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「いど」 (緯度: latitude, or 井戸: well) is not the reading of 「程度」.
default.q.n2-25-q5-5.why.3: (d) 「かんど」(感度) means sensitivity; the first kanji is 「感」, not 「程」.
default.q.n2-25-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 夢 (MŌNG), corresponding to 「ゆめ」, meaning a dream or aspiration.
default.q.n2-25-q6-6.explanation:
- Meaning: My dream is to become an elementary school teacher.

default.q.n2-25-q6-6.why.1: (b) 「希」 is commonly used with the on-reading キ, as in 希望 (きぼう, hope); it does not have the kun-reading ゆめ.
default.q.n2-25-q6-6.why.2: (c) 「夢」 has the kunyomi reading ゆめ (yume - dream, aspiration), which is the correct kanji being sought.
default.q.n2-25-q6-6.why.3: (d) 「優」 is read as やさ・しい (yasashii: gentle), すぐ・れる (sugureru: excellent), or with the on-reading ユウ (as in 優秀); it is not read as ゆめ.
default.q.n2-25-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 巻 (volume), a counter for books and manga volumes (かん).
default.q.n2-25-q7-7.explanation:
- Meaning: This manga series has as many as 30 volumes, so there is no way to finish reading it in one day.

default.q.n2-25-q7-7.why.0: (a) 「完」(COMPLETE) means completion or wholeness, as in 完結 (kanketsu - conclusion); it is not the counter for book volumes, 「～かん」.
default.q.n2-25-q7-7.why.1: (b) 「巻」 is read with the on-reading かん (kan) and is a counter for volumes of books, manga, or documents (30巻 = 30 volumes), so it is completely correct.
default.q.n2-25-q7-7.why.2: (c) 「集」 is read しゅう (shuu) in 全集 and 作品集, or あつ・まる; it is not used as a counter for volumes in this way.
default.q.n2-25-q7-7.why.3: (d) 「港」 (PORT) is read as みなと (minato), or with its on-reading コウ (kou) in 空港 (airport), and means “harbor/port”; it is unrelated to counting volumes of a series.
default.q.n2-25-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 税金 (THUẾ KIM), corresponding to 「ぜいきん」, meaning taxes.
default.q.n2-25-q8-8.explanation:
- Meaning: It is said that taxes will increase starting next month.

- Example: 国民には税金を納める義務がある。 (Citizens have an obligation to pay taxes.)
default.q.n2-25-q8-8.why.0: (a) 「秘金」is an incorrect word; 「秘」(as in 秘密) has the 禾 radical like 税, but its right component is 必, so it does not form a word meaning tax money.
default.q.n2-25-q8-8.why.1: (b) 「悦金」is an incorrect word; 「悦」(as in 喜悦) has the right component 兌 like 税, but its left component is the heart radical (忄), not the 禾 radical.
default.q.n2-25-q8-8.why.2: (c) 「役金」 is not the vocabulary for tax money; 「役」 (as in 役所 and 役割) is not read as ぜい.
default.q.n2-25-q8-8.why.3: (d) 「税金」 is formed from 税 (ぜい) and 金 (きん), creating the noun 「ぜいきん」 (“tax money”), so this is completely correct.
default.q.n2-25-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 帽子 (MẠO TỬ), corresponding to 「ぼうし」, meaning a hat or cap.
default.q.n2-25-q9-9.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: I took off my hat and greeted them.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 帽子 (hat).
- Example: 日差しが強いので帽子をかぶって出かけた。 (The sunlight was strong, so I put on a hat before going out.)
default.q.n2-25-q9-9.why.0: (a) The first kanji in「温子」is incorrect;「温」(温: as in 気温 and 温かい) is not read ぼう and does not mean “hat.”
default.q.n2-25-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「冒子」 uses the wrong kanji. 「冒」 (as in 冒険) lacks the 巾 component below, so it is not 「帽」 (“hat”).
default.q.n2-25-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「昌子」 uses the wrong kanji; 「昌」 is commonly used in personal names or in 繁昌 and does not mean “hat.”
default.q.n2-25-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「帽子」 consists of 帽, which contains the 巾 radical associated with cloth headwear, and 子. It is correctly read ぼうし and means hat or cap.
default.q.n2-25-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 迷って, from the verb 迷う, used in 「道に迷う」 to mean “get lost.”
default.q.n2-25-q10-10.explanation:
- Meaning: I seem to have gotten lost.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 迷 (MEI: to lose one's way, to be uncertain). Fixed expression: 道に迷う (get lost).
- Example: どちらの道を行くべきか迷っている。 (I'm unsure which road I should take.)
default.q.n2-25-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「惑って」 has the wrong reading. The kanji 「惑」 (as in 迷惑) is read まど・う (madou, to be confused) or まど・わす, not まよう in the context of getting lost.
default.q.n2-25-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「迷って」 comes from the verb 「迷う」 (まよう), used in the expression 「道に迷う」 (“to get lost”), and its te-form 迷って is completely correct.
default.q.n2-25-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「留って」comes from「留」(留), read とまる / とどまる (to stop, remain), not まよって.
default.q.n2-25-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「寄って」 comes from the verb 「寄る」 (よる, to stop by or drop in). Its te-form is よって, not まよって.
default.q.n2-26-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2. まい because the pattern 「〜のではあるまいか」 expresses speculation or a mild question meaning “might it be...?” or “could it be that...?”
default.q.n2-26-q33-33.explanation:
Meaning: “Could it be that he has already returned to his home country?”
Pattern: V / A / N (plain form) + のではあるまいか (Could it be that...? / Might it not be that...?), used to express a cautious, polite supposition or doubt. It is often used with 「もしかして」(perhaps, possibly).
Example: この計画は失敗するのではあるまいか。(Could this plan fail?)
default.q.n2-26-q33-33.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the structure「〜のではあるだろうか」does not exist; when using「だろう」, it should be「〜のではないだろうか」.
default.q.n2-26-q33-33.why.1: (b) Correct because the grammar 「〜のではあるまいか」 (=「〜のではないだろうか」) expresses a tentative supposition and often appears with the adverb 「もしかして」.
default.q.n2-26-q33-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ものか / もんか」expresses strong negation (“absolutely not...”), which does not fit the conjectural adverb 「もしかして」.
default.q.n2-26-q33-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「こと」does not form the grammar pattern「〜のではあることか」in this context.
default.q.n2-26-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 4. につき because the pattern「N + につき」is used in notices and formal documents to state a reason or cause (“because of / due to …”).
default.q.n2-26-q34-34.explanation:
Meaning: "This road is under construction, so it cannot be used."
Kanji-based terms: 工事中 (under construction), 通る (pass through, travel along).
Structure: N + につき (due to / because of...), a formal expression commonly used in public notices and signs.
Example: 清掃中につき足元にご注意ください。(Cleaning in progress; please watch your step.)
default.q.n2-26-q34-34.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜について」 means “about” a topic or subject; it is not used to indicate a cause or reason.
default.q.n2-26-q34-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect because「〜をめぐって」means “concerning” or “over” a dispute or issue, so it does not fit.
default.q.n2-26-q34-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect because after the noun it should be 「工事中のせいで」rather than being used directly. In addition, 「〜のせいで」usually carries a blaming nuance and is unsuitable for a formal notice.
default.q.n2-26-q34-34.why.3: (d) Correct because 「N + につき」 is a formal grammar pattern used in notices to state a reason (“Due to construction, passage is prohibited”).
default.q.n2-26-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 1. に際して, because the pattern「V-る / N + に際して」means “when / on the occasion of / before undertaking something” in a formal context.
default.q.n2-26-q35-35.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “Before using this sports center, I would like to explain a few points to keep in mind.”
Kanji-related vocabulary: 活用 (effective use, utilization), 注意点 (points to note).
- Pattern: V-る / N + に際して (when / on the occasion of / before undertaking an event or activity), with a formal tone.
- Example: お申し込みに際しては、身分証明書をご提示ください。(When applying, please present your identification.)
default.q.n2-26-q35-35.why.0: (a) Correct. 「V-る + に際して」 indicates the time when a formal action or event begins, meaning “before or when using...”.
default.q.n2-26-q35-35.why.1: (b) is incorrect because 「〜を問わず」 means “regardless of, irrespective of” (age, gender, nationality, etc.), which does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-26-q35-35.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜をはじめ」means “representative examples include” or “first and foremost,” and is used to list typical examples.
default.q.n2-26-q35-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜あまり」means “because something is excessive, resulting in a bad or unusual outcome,” which is not appropriate here.
default.q.n2-26-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 【なせて (死なせて) because the object-marking particle 「猫を」requires the causative form (使役形)「死なせる」to express that one’s carelessness caused the cat to die.
default.q.n2-26-q36-36.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “My beloved cat died because of my carelessness.”
Kanji reading: 不注意 (carelessness, lack of caution).
Structure: [Object] を + V-させる (causative form: make or cause someone/something to...). Here, 「死ぬ」is an intransitive verb; when changed into the causative form, it becomes 「死なせる」(make or let something die), taking the object 「猫を」.
Example: 不注意で植物を枯らして（死なせて）しまった。(Because of my carelessness, I ended up killing the plant.)
default.q.n2-26-q36-36.why.0: (a) Incorrect because【なれて (死なれて) is the passive form expressing adversity (迷惑の受身), so it must be used with the particle「猫に」, not「猫を」.
default.q.n2-26-q36-36.why.1: (b) Incorrect because【んで (死んで) is the te-form of an intransitive verb and takes the particle「猫が」, not the object particle「猫を」.
default.q.n2-26-q36-36.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 【なせられて (死なせられて) is the causative-passive form (being forced to cause someone to die), so its meaning is completely inappropriate.
default.q.n2-26-q36-36.why.3: (d) Correct because【なせて (死なせて) is the causative form of the verb 死ぬ. Combined with「猫を」, it forms「猫を死なせてしまった」(I accidentally caused my pet cat to die through my carelessness).
default.q.n2-26-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 2. に反して, because the structure「N + に反して」means “contrary to” or “against” a wish, expectation, or prediction.
default.q.n2-26-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: "Although I felt guilty, contrary to my parents' wishes, I chose to start working instead of going to university."
- 希望: hope, wish, aspiration.
- 反する: to go against, contradict.
- Pattern: N + に反して (contrary to, against someone's wishes, expectations, or predictions).
- Example: 親の期待に反して、彼は進学しなかった。(Contrary to his parents' expectations, he did not continue his education.)
default.q.n2-26-q37-37.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜に対して」 means “toward...” or “in contrast to...” when comparing two objects; it does not express acting contrary to expectations or wishes.
default.q.n2-26-q37-37.why.1: (b) Correct because「〜に反して」means “contrary to,” as in “contrary to the parents’ wishes.”
default.q.n2-26-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect because「〜にともなって」means “along with” or “in conjunction with” a change, indicating parallel changes.
default.q.n2-26-q37-37.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the standard pattern is「〜を問わず」(not に問わず), meaning “regardless of.”
default.q.n2-26-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2. どころか because the structure 「〜どころか」 means “far from...; on the contrary...” and describes a reality that is completely opposite to, or worse than, what is stated in the preceding clause.
default.q.n2-26-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: "Far from improving, this country's economy has become much worse than before."
Vocabulary: 経済 (economy), 以前 (before, previously).
Grammar: A どころか B (far from A; rather, B / not only is A untrue, but B is even worse).
Example: 貯金ができるどころか、借金が増える一方だ。(Far from saving money, my debts just keep increasing.)
default.q.n2-26-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「〜あまり(に)」means “because something is too...,” leading to a negative result; it is not used in a contrasting comparison like this.
default.q.n2-26-q38-38.why.1: (b) Correct because 「V-る + どころか」expresses the idea that the economy not only failed to improve but instead became much worse than before.
default.q.n2-26-q38-38.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜としたら」 means "if we assume that..." and is used for a hypothetical condition.
default.q.n2-26-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect because「〜にもかかわらず (にもかか山らず)」means “although...,” whereas it does not express the strong negation and contrast with reality conveyed by どころか.
default.q.n2-26-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4. かのように, because the structure 「〜であるかのように」means “as if...” and modifies the action described in the following clause.
default.q.n2-26-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: "He told everyone a made-up story as if it were a true story."
On'yomi: 作り話 (a fabricated story, made-up story).
Structure: Plain form / N + である + かのように (as if..., as though...), used to compare an unreal situation to another state as though it were real.
Example: 彼は何でも知っているかのように話す。(He talks as if he knows everything.)
default.q.n2-26-q39-39.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「ようで」is the te-form of「ようだ」and cannot modify the following verb「話した」in this way.
default.q.n2-26-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect because「そうに」must combine with the stem form (the V-masu stem or an adjective stem without i), not「であるそうに」.
default.q.n2-26-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「り」does not form any meaningful grammar pattern when it follows 「である」.
default.q.n2-26-q39-39.why.3: (d) Correct, because 「N + であるかのように」 means “as if it were true” and modifies the verb 「話した」.
default.q.n2-26-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ばかりか, because the pattern 「N + ばかりか 〜 も」 means “not only ... but even ... .”
default.q.n2-26-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: “I hear that this cat doll is very popular not only with children but also with adults.”
Kanji: 人形: doll, puppet; 人気: popularity.
Pattern: N / plain form + ばかりか 〜 も (not only... but even... also).
Example: 彼は英語ばかりか、フランス語も流暢に話せる。(He can speak not only English but also French fluently.)
default.q.n2-26-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「〜ばかりに」means “just because...,” leading to an unintended negative result.
default.q.n2-26-q40-40.why.1: (b) Correct because the pattern 「N + ばかりか ... にも」 means “not only children, but even adults...”.
default.q.n2-26-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜はともかく」 means “setting A aside” or “without considering A for the moment.” It does not fit a statement about something being liked simultaneously by both groups.
default.q.n2-26-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜にはんして」(に反して) means “contrary to...”; it does not combine with 「〜にも」 in the following clause.
default.q.n2-26-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ことには, because the pattern 「V-ないことには〜ない / しようがない」 means “unless...; otherwise, it is impossible / there is no way to...”.
default.q.n2-26-q41-41.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “If you do not know the phone number, there is no way to contact them.”
Kanji readings: 連絡 (contact), 電話番号 (telephone number).
Pattern: V-ないことには 〜 ない / しようがない (unless..., there is no way to... / until..., it is impossible to...).
Example: 実際に使ってみないことには、良さがわからない。(Unless you actually try using it, you cannot understand its merits.)
default.q.n2-26-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect because there is no grammatical form 「〜ものには」 expressing a negative condition leading to impossibility.
default.q.n2-26-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜としては」means “as / considering that...,” and does not express a conditional relationship.
default.q.n2-26-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ながらも」means “although...,” expressing concession and contrast, which does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-26-q41-41.why.3: (d) Correct because the pattern 「V-ないことには + negative clause (しようがない)」 expresses “unless one knows the phone number, there is no way to contact them.”
default.q.n2-26-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 1. にわたって because the structure 「period of time + にわたって」means “throughout” or “over the entire period.”
default.q.n2-26-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: "That lecturer's lecture lasted for three full hours."
Kanji-based vocabulary: 講義 (lecture), 行われる (to be held, take place).
Pattern: A period of time / range + にわたって (throughout, over the entire period or range), emphasizing duration or spatial extent.
Example: 台風の影響で、雨は一週間にわたって降り続いた。(Due to the typhoon, the rain continued for an entire week.)
default.q.n2-26-q42-42.why.0: (a) Correct. 「〜にわたって」 is used with a duration such as 3時間 to emphasize that something continues throughout the entire three hours.
default.q.n2-26-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜にかけて」normally appears in the pair 「A から B にかけて」(from around A to around B); it does not directly follow a single duration.
default.q.n2-26-q42-42.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ばかりか」 means “not only... but also,” and is not used to indicate a period of time.
default.q.n2-26-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜ばかりで」 means “nothing but...” or “only...” and is not used to express the duration of an event.
default.q.n2-26-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. すえの (末の), because the structure「V-た + すえの + N」means “the result after a long period of thought or struggle.”
default.q.n2-26-q43-43.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “Dropping out of university was a decision I made after careful consideration, so I have no doubts about it at all.”
Sino-Japanese readings: 十分 (sufficient, thorough), 迷い (doubt, hesitation).
Pattern: V-た / N-の + 末(に / のN) (after a long period of struggle or deliberation, resulting in...).
Example: 悩んだ末の決断だから、後悔はしていない。(It was a decision I made after much deliberation, so I do not regret it.)
default.q.n2-26-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「〜はずの」means “supposedly certain to be...,” based on logical deduction, and does not simply indicate the result after a process of deep deliberation.
default.q.n2-26-q43-43.why.1: (b) Correct because 「V-た + すえ(末)の + N」expresses an answer or result reached after a thorough process of consideration (“the result after thinking it over carefully”).
default.q.n2-26-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜ものの」 means “although...,” and connects two contrasting clauses. It does not modify a noun in this way.
default.q.n2-26-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「このの」 is not a Japanese grammar pattern and is completely meaningless.
default.q.n2-26-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 4. みせる because the structure 「V-てみせる」 expresses a strong determination to do something and show others that it can be done.
default.q.n2-26-q44-44.explanation:
