default.q.n2-26-q1-1.why.2: (c) Correct because 巨大 is formed from 巨 (きょ) and 大 (だい), is read as きょだい, and means “huge, enormous.”
default.q.n2-26-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 大 is read だい in this compound, not たい.
default.q.n2-26-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (せいしん).
default.q.n2-26-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: “Sports not only help the body but also strengthen the mind.”
- Kanji note: 精神 (spirit, mind).
- Example: 強い精神力を持つ。(To have strong mental strength.)
default.q.n2-26-q2-2.why.0: (a) Correct because 精神 consists of 精 (せい) and 神 (しん), is read せいしん, and means “spirit” or “mentality.”
default.q.n2-26-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the on-reading of 神 in this word is しん, not the voiced reading じん. せいじん is written as 成人 (adult) or 聖人 (saint).
default.q.n2-26-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect because ぜんしん is the reading of 全身 (the whole body) or 前進 (moving forward).
default.q.n2-26-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect because しんけい is the reading of 神経 (nerves).
default.q.n2-26-q3-3.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “The desk is here.”
- Kanji-based meaning: 机 (つくえ) means “desk” or “table.”
- Example: 机の上をきれいに片付ける。(Clean up the surface of the desk.)
default.q.n2-26-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect because かびん is the reading of 花瓶 (flower vase).
default.q.n2-26-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because ひきだし is the reading of 引き出し (drawer).
default.q.n2-26-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect because かがみ is the reading of 鏡 (mirror).
default.q.n2-26-q3-3.why.3: (d) Correct because 机, when used independently, is read with the kun-reading つくえ and means “desk” or “table.”
default.q.n2-26-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (かんそく).
default.q.n2-26-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: "I like observing the stars."
- Sino-Japanese roots: 観測 (QUAN TRẮC) = to observe, measure, or monitor a natural phenomenon.
- Example: 天気を観測する。(Observe the weather.)
default.q.n2-26-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect because かんそう is the reading of 感想 (impression) or 乾燥 (dryness, drying).
default.q.n2-26-q4-4.why.1: (b) Correct because 観測 is formed from 観 (かん) and 測 (そく), is read かんそく, and means “observation, measurement.”
default.q.n2-26-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect because かんしゃ is the reading of 感謝 (gratitude, thanks).
default.q.n2-26-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect because かんさつ is the reading of 観察 (observation) or 監察 (inspection).
default.q.n2-26-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (きゅうしゅう).
default.q.n2-26-q5-5.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Children absorb everything very quickly."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 吸収 (absorb, take in).
- Example: 知識を素早く吸収する。(Absorb knowledge quickly.)
default.q.n2-26-q5-5.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 吸 has the on-reading きゅう, not きょう; きょうしゅう is the reading of 教習 or 強襲.
default.q.n2-26-q5-5.why.1: (b) Correct because 吸収 is formed from 吸 (きゅう) and 収 (しゅう), is read きゅうしゅう, and means “absorption, assimilation.”
default.q.n2-26-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect because かんしゅう is the reading of 慣習 (custom) or 観衆 (audience).
default.q.n2-26-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect because こしゅう is the reading of 固執 (stubbornly clinging to something) or 呼気/呼集.
default.q.n2-26-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 危険 (きけん).
default.q.n2-26-q6-6.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: It is dangerous here, so please do not enter.
• Kanji vocabulary: 危険 (dangerous, danger).
• Related vocabulary and kanji:
  - 危 (danger): 危ない (あぶない - dangerous), 危機 (きき - crisis).
  - 険 (peril): 保険 (ほけん - insurance), 険しい (けわしい - steep, rugged).
• Example: 危険な場所に近づいてはいけません。 (Do not go near dangerous places.)
default.q.n2-26-q6-6.why.0: (a) Correct. 危険 (DANGER) means danger or risk, pronounced 「きけん」.
default.q.n2-26-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The first kanji in 「機」 (きかい) is wrong; it should be 「危」.
default.q.n2-26-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The second kanji is wrong: 「験」(EXPERIENCE - as in jikken/taiken, with the 馬 radical) is incorrect; the correct kanji is「険」(DANGER, with the 阝 radical).
default.q.n2-26-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「剣」 (sword) is the wrong second kanji; the correct kanji is 「険」 (dangerous, steep).
default.q.n2-26-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 捨てる (すてる).
default.q.n2-26-q7-7.explanation:
• Translation: Don’t throw trash on the street!
• On’yomi: 捨てる (to discard, throw away).
• Kanji with the hand radical (扌):
  - 捨 (捨てる (すてる — to throw away, give up), 四捨五入 (ししゃごにゅう — rounding numbers).
  - 拾 (拾う (ひろう — to pick up), 拾得物 (しゅうとくぶつ — found property).
  - 投 (投げる (なげる — to throw), 投票 (とうひょう — voting).
• Example: 使わなくなった服を思い切って捨てた。 (I finally decided to throw away the clothes I no longer wore.)
default.q.n2-26-q7-7.why.0: (a) Correct. 捨てる means to throw away, dispose of (trash), or give up.
default.q.n2-26-q7-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「拾」 (ひろう) is used in the verb 拾う (“to pick up”), the opposite of 捨てる, and does not take the okurigana てる to form すてる.
default.q.n2-26-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The kanji 「投」 is used in the verb 投げる (なげる, to throw); it does not form 投てる, pronounced すてる.
default.q.n2-26-q7-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「打」 (on-reading: だ) is used in the verb 打つ (うつ: to hit or strike); 打てる is its potential form, meaning “can hit,” not すてる.
default.q.n2-26-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 報告 (ほうこく).
default.q.n2-26-q8-8.explanation:
• Meaning: I listened to the sales department’s report at the meeting.
• Kanji compound: 報告 (report).
• Related vocabulary and kanji:
  - 報: 予報 (よほう, forecast), 情報 (じょうほう, information), 報道 (ほうどう, news reporting).
  - 告: 広告 (こうこく, advertisement), 警告 (けいこく, warning), 告白 (こくはく, confession, disclosure).
• Example: 上司に進捗状況を報告した。 (I reported the progress to my supervisor.)
default.q.n2-26-q8-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「酷」 (cruel, harsh, as in 残酷/ざんこく and 過酷/かこく) is the wrong kanji.
default.q.n2-26-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The kanji 「治」 (associated with “rule” or “treatment,” as in 政治/せいじ and 治療/ちりょう) is the wrong kanji combination.
default.q.n2-26-q8-8.why.2: (c) Correct. 報告 means a report or an announcement about the state of affairs or a work-related matter.
default.q.n2-26-q8-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「浩」 is a kanji commonly used in personal names and is incorrectly combined here.
default.q.n2-26-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 犯人 (はんにん).
default.q.n2-26-q9-9.explanation:
• Meaning: That person is the culprit!
• Kanji: 犯人 means culprit.
• Similar and related kanji:
  - 犯 (with the 犭radical): 犯人 (はんにん - culprit), 犯罪 (はんざい - crime), 犯す (おかす - to commit).
  - 氾 (with the 氵radical): 氾濫 (はんらん - overflowing, flooding).
  - 罪: 罪人 (ざいにん / つみびと - sinner, criminal), 罪 (つみ - sin, crime).
• Example: 警察は防犯カメラの映像から犯人を特定した。 (The police identified the culprit from security camera footage.)
default.q.n2-26-q9-9.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「氾」 (on-reading: はん; with the water radical 氵, as in 氾濫/はんらん) uses the wrong kanji radical; the correct character is 「犯」, which has the 犭 radical.
default.q.n2-26-q9-9.why.1: (b) Correct. 犯人 means the culprit or perpetrator and is pronounced 「はんにん」.
default.q.n2-26-q9-9.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The kanji「疑」, as in 疑う/うたがう and 容疑者/ようぎしゃ, cannot form the word 疑人 read as はんにん.
default.q.n2-26-q9-9.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「罪人」is read 「ざいにん」or 「つみびと」, not 「はんにん」.
default.q.n2-26-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 暮れた (くれた).
default.q.n2-26-q10-10.explanation:
• Meaning: It is already getting dark, so let's go home.
• Kanji meaning: 暮れる (to grow dark, for the day or year to end).
• Related expressions and kanji:
  - 日が暮れる (ひがくれる): the sun sets, it gets dark.
  - 年が暮れる (としがくれる): the year comes to an end.
  - 途方に暮れる (とほうにくれる): to be at a loss, lose one's way.
  - 暮らす (くらす): to live.
  - 夕暮れ (ゆうぐれ): dusk, late afternoon.
• Example: 日が暮れる前に山を下りよう。 (Let's come down the mountain before it gets dark.)
default.q.n2-26-q10-10.why.0: (a) Correct. 暮れる (MỘ) is used in 「日が暮れる」 to indicate that the sun sets and it gets dark; the past form is 暮れた.
default.q.n2-26-q10-10.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The kanji 「落」 is used in 落ちる (おちる, “to fall”) or 落とす (おとす, “to drop”), not conjugated as 「落れた」.
default.q.n2-26-q10-10.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「沈」(as in 沈む, しずむ, sink) is used for the sun setting:「日が沈んだ」. The form「沈れた」does not exist.
default.q.n2-26-q10-10.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The kanji 「下」 is used in 下がる (さがる) and 下りる (おりる); it does not combine with this kanji to form a verb read as くれる.
default.q.n2-3-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ように.
default.q.n2-3-q33-33.explanation:
Meaning: Please write the characters larger so they can be seen clearly from a distance.
• Structure: 「V (dictionary form/potential form/nai-form) + ように」: so that, in order to (the preceding clause usually describes a state or ability that is not directly controlled by the speaker's will). Distinguish this from 「V (volitional form) + ために」.
• Example: 忘れないように、メモを取っておきます。(I will take notes so that I do not forget.)
default.q.n2-3-q33-33.why.0: (a) Correct. 「V (potential/non-volitional) + ように」 expresses the purpose 'so that one can...'; the following clause describes an action taken to achieve that state. Here, 「見える」 is a potential verb, so it takes 「ように」.
default.q.n2-3-q33-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜ために」can also mean 'in order to,' but it is used with volitional verbs. 「見える」is a potential/spontaneous verb, not a volitional one, so it does not combine with 「ために」.
default.q.n2-3-q33-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜だけに」 means “precisely because..., all the more...” or “in proportion to...,” expressing an inevitable cause-and-effect relationship. It is not used to state a purpose.
default.q.n2-3-q33-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜ばかりに」means “just because...,” leading to a bad or regrettable result; it is not suitable for expressing purpose or for use with a request or imperative.
default.q.n2-3-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 4. こと.
default.q.n2-3-q34-34.explanation:
Meaning: It is not that I do not want to go, but I do not have time today.
• Pattern: 「V-ない + ことはない / こともない」: It is not that... / It is not entirely true that... (a mild affirmation expressed through double negation).
• Example: 納豆は食べられないことはないが、あまり好きではない。(It is not that I cannot eat natto, but I do not like it very much.)
default.q.n2-3-q34-34.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜ないほうではない」does not form a standard grammar pattern for partially negating a state or desire.
default.q.n2-3-q34-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜もの」is used to explain a reason (〜ものだから) or express a natural rule; it does not form the grammar 「〜ないものはない」with the meaning “it is not that there is nothing…”.
default.q.n2-3-q34-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜ようではない」 is not used in the double-negative pattern meaning “it is not that one does not want to ...”.
default.q.n2-3-q34-34.why.3: (d) Correct. The pattern 「〜ないことはない / 〜ないこともない」 means “it is not that... is impossible” or “it is possible, although...,” expressing a mild affirmation or conditional acceptance.
default.q.n2-3-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2. くだ注った (くださった).
default.q.n2-3-q35-35.explanation:
Meaning: Because the teacher explained it carefully to me, I understood it clearly as well.
• Honorific language: 「ご/お + noun/verb stem + くださる」is a respectful form indicating that someone of higher status does something for the speaker (with 先生が as the subject).
• Note: The character "注" in the question is an OCR error for "さ" (くだ注った = くださった, 注しあげた = さしあげた).
default.q.n2-3-q35-35.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「ご〜いただく」is humble language and is used with に (先生にご説明いただいた - I had the teacher explain it to me). Here, the subject is marked by が (先生が), so respectful language must be used for the teacher's action.
default.q.n2-3-q35-35.why.1: (b) Correct. 「ご〜くださる」 (the OCR error is くだ注った) is a respectful expression indicating that the other person does something for the speaker, and correctly agrees with the subject 「先生が」.
default.q.n2-3-q35-35.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「ご〜いたす」 is humble language used for the speaker's own actions and is not used for a teacher's actions.
default.q.n2-3-q35-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「ご〜さしあげる」 (with 注しあげた as an OCR error) is humble language meaning that one does something for or offers something to a superior; it is not used for an action performed by a teacher for oneself.
default.q.n2-3-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ため.
default.q.n2-3-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: Since I had already lent my umbrella to someone else, I had no choice but to get wet on the way home.
• Pattern: 「Plain form + ため（に）」: because, due to... (indicates an objective cause or reason leading to a result).
• Example: 台風が近づいているため、電車が遅れている。(The train is delayed because a typhoon is approaching.)
default.q.n2-3-q36-36.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜だけあって」 means “just as one would expect from...” or “no wonder...” and is usually followed by praise or a result worthy of the expectation. It is not used simply to state a cause leading to an unfortunate outcome.
default.q.n2-3-q36-36.why.1: (b) Correct. 「〜ため（に）」states an objective cause or reason leading to the event in the following clause (because the speaker accidentally lent out the umbrella, they had no choice but to walk home in the rain).
default.q.n2-3-q36-36.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜のだから」 states an obvious reason as the premise for a judgment, request, or responsibility in the following clause; it is not used to recount an objective event that has already occurred.
default.q.n2-3-q36-36.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「からし」is not a complete standard grammar pattern. It may be an error for からして or からには, but neither fits the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-3-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ことに.
default.q.n2-3-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: Strangely enough, after quitting my job, I started sleeping much better.
• Pattern: 「adjective / V-た + ことに」: “It is … that …,” placed at the beginning of a sentence to express the speaker’s subjective emotion or evaluation of what follows.
• Kanji-related note: 不思議 (strange, mysterious, difficult to understand).
• Example: 残念なことに、旅行は中止になった。(Unfortunately, the trip was canceled.)
default.q.n2-3-q37-37.why.0: (a) Correct. The grammar pattern 「A-な + ことに」 expresses the speaker's emotion or evaluation ('how...!' / 'strangely enough...'). 「不思議なことに」 means 'strangely enough' or 'it is strange that...'
default.q.n2-3-q37-37.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜せいで」 means “because of” and indicates a cause leading to a negative result. It does not form an opening phrase such as 「不思議なせいで」, and “sleeping better” is a positive result.
default.q.n2-3-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜ものから」 is used at the end of a clause to explain or justify one's action; it is not used in this position.
default.q.n2-3-q37-37.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜ばかり」 means “nothing but,” “only,” or “have just...”; it cannot combine with 「不思議な」 to create a suitable context.
default.q.n2-3-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2. たびに.
default.q.n2-3-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: Every time I read this book, I remember him.
• Pattern: 「V-る / N + の + たびに」: every time..., whenever... (whenever event A occurs, event B always follows).
• Example: この写真を見るたびに、楽しかった旅行を思い出す。(Every time I look at this photo, I remember the enjoyable trip.)
default.q.n2-3-q38-38.why.0: (a) is incorrect. 「〜とおりに」 means “exactly as / in accordance with...”; it does not express a repeated time-related or retrospective relationship.
default.q.n2-3-q38-38.why.1: (b) Correct. 「V-る + たびに」means “every time...,” expressing a repeated action or event that is followed by another recurring feeling or action.
default.q.n2-3-q38-38.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜からして」means “judging from the very...,” presenting a representative example for evaluation; it does not directly combine with 「V-る」.
default.q.n2-3-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜ように」means “so that” or “like,” and does not express habitual repetition or emotional association.
default.q.n2-3-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 1. いられない.
default.q.n2-3-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: Every year, whenever I hear frogs croaking, I cannot help but think of my hometown.
• Pattern: 「V-ずにはいられない」: cannot help but... / cannot restrain oneself from... (V-ない with ない removed + ずにはいられない; する becomes せずにはいられない).
• Note: ふる注と in the test is an OCR error for ふるさと (hometown).
• Example: その知らせを聞いて、泣かずにはいられなかった。(When I heard the news, I could not hold back my tears.)
default.q.n2-3-q39-39.why.0: (a) Correct. The grammar pattern 「V-ずにはいられない」 means “cannot help but...” or “cannot hold back one’s feelings,” describing a natural psychological reaction that cannot be restrained.
default.q.n2-3-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜えない/ありえない」 means “cannot happen” or “impossible,” and does not combine with 「〜ずには」 to form this expressive structure.

Meaning: Although I said that my younger brother cannot drink alcohol, that does not mean he cannot drink even a little.

Meaning: It is embarrassing that even a child knows this, yet an adult like me does not.

Meaning: "That person over there feels like the person who came to the office yesterday..."

default.q.n2-3-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (検査したところ).

default.q.n2-3-q50-50.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The structure 「〜一方で」 expresses two simultaneous actions or contrasting aspects (“on the one hand... on the other hand...”), so it is unsuitable for connecting an examination with the diagnosis received afterward.

default.q.n2-3-q50-50.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The structure 「〜らしく」 expresses an uncertain inference or reported information (“apparently, it was examined”), and does not fit the author’s direct experience of going to the doctor.
default.q.n2-3-q50-50.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The structure 「Nどころか」strongly negates the preceding idea, meaning “let alone / not only... but even...”; it does not form a grammatically and semantically appropriate expression in this sentence.
default.q.n2-3-q51-51.explanation: The author was genuinely experiencing a headache, so the moment the doctor said that nothing was wrong, the author suddenly became even more worried. default.q.n2-3-q51-51.why.0: (a) Correct. The grammar pattern 「Vたとたん（に）」describes something that happens immediately after another event: “just when I heard that there was nothing unusual, I suddenly became worried instead.”
default.q.n2-3-q51-51.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「Vたきり」 expresses a state that continues without any subsequent change after an action is performed (“ever since...”); it does not fit a context involving an immediate psychological change.
default.q.n2-3-q51-51.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The pattern 「Vたあげく」 describes reaching a bad outcome after a long, difficult process (“after much... in the end”), so it is not used for an immediate psychological reaction right after hearing something.
default.q.n2-3-q51-51.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜反面」is used to present two contrasting sides of the same thing or phenomenon (“on the other hand”), and does not combine with the Vた-form to indicate when a psychological change occurred, as in this sentence.

default.q.n2-3-q52-52.explanation: According to the context, the author clearly has a headache and therefore cannot believe that the result is normal: “With pain this severe, there is absolutely no way that nothing is wrong; there must definitely be some problem.” The structure 「A わけがない」 expresses an absolute negation based on logic: “there is absolutely no way that...”. default.q.n2-3-q52-52.why.1: (b) Correct. The pattern 「〜わけがない」strongly asserts, based on logic, that “there is absolutely no way that...” (“With pain this severe, there is no way nothing is wrong / it cannot possibly be fine”).
default.q.n2-3-q52-52.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The pattern 「〜わけにはいかない」 expresses that one cannot or must not do something for ethical, social, or psychological reasons, so it does not fit a statement about a medical condition.
default.q.n2-3-q52-52.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The pattern 「〜わけだ」expresses an obvious conclusion or explanation of a cause (“that explains why / so that is why”), which is completely contrary to the author's doubt and speculation.
default.q.n2-3-q53-53.explanation: Before this, the author was worried that they might have an unexplained serious illness and spent a long time thinking about it. The pattern 「V-た末（に）」indicates that, after a long process of thinking, deliberation, or going through various experiences, one ultimately reaches a decision or result. Here, the result was the decision to visit the neurology department at a large hospital. Therefore, answer choice 3 is correct.

default.q.n2-3-q53-53.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜わけで」means “because...” or “the reason is that...”; it does not express going through a period of hesitation before finally taking action.
default.q.n2-3-q53-53.why.2: (c) Correct. The pattern 「Vた末（に） / Nの末（に）」means "after a long period of worry and careful consideration, finally..." (after much hesitation and concern, the person finally decided to visit the neurology department of a major hospital).
default.q.n2-3-q53-53.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜とおり（に）」 means “exactly as...” or “in accordance with...”; it does not fit a structure expressing hesitation followed by a decision.

default.q.n2-3-q54-54.why.3: (d) Correct. The pattern 「V (ます-stem) + っぱなしだ」 describes a state or action that continues unchanged for a long time, such as “sitting facing the computer / staring at the computer from morning until night.”

default.q.n2-3-q57-57.why.1: (b) The quotation proves that the author is female: «近頃の中学生や高校生の女の子は自分のことを僕と呼ぶと言う記事が載っていた。実に、私も自分のことを僕と呼ぶひとりだ。», together with the detail that the author uses «あたし» in front of a superior.
default.q.n2-3-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author writes «もう高校生でもない» (“I am no longer even a high school student”), showing that the author has grown up and is no longer of middle-school age.
default.q.n2-3-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author states 「もう高校生でもないのにちょっと恥ずかしい」(although I am no longer a high school student, I feel a little embarrassed), showing that the author is not a high school student.
default.q.n2-3-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (筆者が妻と娘に): The author calls out to his family (his wife and daughter) to tell them that he will go open the door.
default.q.n2-3-q58-58.explanation:
Summary of the passage:
When the doorbell rings or someone calls at the door, the author says 「出るよ。」 (I'll get it) to let the people in the house know that he will answer the door. He then opens it and sees a postal worker standing outside (ドアの向こうに郵便配達員が立っていた). His wife, who is in the kitchen, hears him and calls out 「どなただったの。」 (Who was it?), and he replies that it is a package sent by his grandmother from the countryside (田舎のお消活ゃんからだ …).

Question translation:
Who did the author say 「出るよ。」 (I'll get the door) to?

Answer choices:
1. The postal worker
2. The author's wife
3. The author's wife and daughter
4. The grandmother in the countryside
default.q.n2-3-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「出るよ。」 (“I'll go out and answer the door”) is something a person inside the house says to another person before going to open the door, not something the author says to the postal worker standing outside.
default.q.n2-3-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the wife is in the kitchen and only afterward calls out 「どなただったの。」(Who was it?), showing that the person who opened the door was not the wife.
default.q.n2-3-q58-58.why.2: (c) Correct because the author calls out 「出るよ。」 to the family and goes to open the door, where 「ドアの向こうに郵便配達員が立っていた」. Only afterward does the wife ask who has arrived from the kitchen (台所から妻の声).
default.q.n2-3-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the grandmother in the countryside is only the person who sent the package (田舎のおばあちゃんからだ); she is not present there.
default.q.n2-3-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (しかしながら).
default.q.n2-3-q59-59.explanation:
**Main point:**
The passage discusses how cultural characteristics develop in people over time. When they are born, children of every nationality and skin color are alike, with no differences in behavior or culture. However, after growing up for several years in the environment of a particular culture, children begin to display distinct cultural characteristics in everything from eating, sleeping, and playing to their way of thinking. Since the first clause (a) describes "similarity / no difference" and the following clause describes "differences emerging according to each culture," a conjunction expressing contrast or a shift in direction ("However") is needed.

**Question translation:**
Which word is most appropriate to fill in blank (a)?

**Answer choices:**
1. しかしながら: However / Nevertheless
2. そういえば: Come to think of it / That reminds me
3. このように: In this way / Thus
4. したが: Therefore / For that reason (a shortened or incorrectly written form of したがって)
default.q.n2-3-q59-59.why.0: (a) Correct. "しかしながら" (however) connects two contrasting ideas: there are no differences among newborn babies based on culture or nationality: 「生まれたばかりの赤ちゃんには、文化の違いや国籍による違いは見られない... その行動様式に大きな違いは見られない。」 Later, after several years of growing up within their respective cultures, differences emerge: 「その後数年たつとそれぞれの文化のなかで育った子供達は、それぞれの文化に特徴的な様相を示すようになる。食事の仕方、睡眠のとり方、遊び方といったことから、考え方にも違いが現れる。」
default.q.n2-3-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「そういえば」(now that you mention it / that reminds me) is used to associate something and shift to a topic that suddenly comes to mind based on the conversation. It is not suitable for expressing a contrastive transition between two sentences.
default.q.n2-3-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「このように」(in this way / like this) is used to summarize or continue an explanation based on what was stated before. It is not used when the following sentence contrasts completely with the preceding sentence in nature.
default.q.n2-3-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. “したが” is an erroneous or incomplete form of したがって (therefore), which connects clauses with a straightforward cause-and-effect relationship. The passage, however, describes an opposing change: initially similar, but later different.
default.q.n2-3-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (はず), because it expresses a recollection or well-founded supposition about something in the past.
default.q.n2-3-q60-60.explanation:
- Main point: The author explains that when Japanese people say 「先日はどうも」, it is less awkward if a foreigner can recall a specific reason—such as remembering that they probably had a meal together last time—than if they cannot remember any reason at all.
- Question translation: Fill in the blank ( ) with the appropriate word or phrase.
- Answer choices:
1. らしい: seems, apparently
2. っぽい: seems, has the quality of
3. はず: should be, is expected to be
4. わけだ: no wonder, that explains why
default.q.n2-3-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「らしい」expresses an inference based on indirect information or hearsay; it is not used to express personally remembering a specific event from one’s own past.
default.q.n2-3-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「っぽい」means “having a tendency or quality like...” and generally follows a noun, adjective, or ます-stem. It does not combine with the past form 「した」in this context.
default.q.n2-3-q60-60.why.2: (c) Correct because「はず」expresses an inference or recollection based on reliable grounds. The passage states: 『そういえば食事をご活そうした 60（はず）と具体的に思い出せるときはまだいい』 (When you can specifically remember, "Come to think of it, I must have invited them to a meal / been invited to a meal," things are still manageable).
default.q.n2-3-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「わけだ」 explains a natural result or reason (“no wonder / so that is why”) after the situation has become clear. It does not fit the retrospective structure 『～と思い出せる』 here.
default.q.n2-3-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because「こんなとき」refers to a situation in which a Japanese person has helped someone, but the other person does not say thank you.
default.q.n2-3-q61-61.explanation:
- Main point: The passage explains that Japanese people often begin conversations by following up on their previous meeting, such as thanking someone for a gift or for helping them. Therefore, when Japanese people have helped someone and the other person says nothing, they feel somewhat disappointed or let down.
- Question translation: What does “at times like this” in paragraph 3 refer to?
- Translation of the choices:
1. When a foreigner does not say thank you.
2. When taking care of someone or receiving a gift.
3. When they have helped someone with something.
4. When starting a conversation.
default.q.n2-3-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because "foreigners do not say thank you" belongs to the following conditional clause, 『何も言われないと』, rather than being the content referred to by the demonstrative phrase 『こんなとき』.
default.q.n2-3-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect because this option confuses the subject and the action ('take care of someone or receive a gift') and does not correctly reflect that the Japanese person is the one who provided the help.
default.q.n2-3-q61-61.why.2: (c) Correct based on the preceding context: 『何かお世話になったりしていたら当然... 「先日はどうもありがとうございます。」... 日本人は 61 こんなとき 、何も言われないと活ょ流と残念な気持ちになるらしい』. When Japanese people have helped or done someone a favor (何か世話をしてあげたとき) and receive no thanks, they reportedly feel disappointed.
default.q.n2-3-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because “when starting a conversation” is only a general communication setting and does not specify the circumstances in which the Japanese person helped the other person.
default.q.n2-3-q62-62.verdict: The given answer is 1 (foreigners cannot use it because they lack this custom); however, based on the reading, choice 4 is the most accurate because the passage clearly states that foreigners have difficulty both using it and responding to it.
default.q.n2-3-q62-62.explanation:
- Main point: The greeting 「先日はどうも」 originated from the Japanese custom of continuing a previous conversation. Even foreigners who have lived in Japan for a long time may find both understanding how to respond to it and using it proactively at the beginning of a conversation difficult.
- Question translation: What does the author say about the expression "Thank you for the other day" (先日はどうも)?
- Answer choices:
1. The author says that because this custom does not exist elsewhere, it is an expression foreigners cannot use.
2. The author says that it is fine if foreigners cannot use this expression.
3. The author says that living in Japan for a long time will make foreigners able to use this expression.
4. The author says that both using and responding to this expression are difficult for foreigners.
default.q.n2-3-q62-62.why.0: (a) According to the provided answer: The sentences 『外国人がなかなか慣れない生活習慣』 and 『外国人にはこれがなかなか言えないようだ』 show that foreigners find this custom difficult to get used to and difficult to say. However, the passage does not conclude absolutely that it is "unusable" (使えない); it only says that it is difficult to get used to or say.
default.q.n2-3-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage states 『日本人は... 何も言われないと活ょ流と残念な気持ちになるらしい』 and 『外国人にと流てや流かいな問題であることには違いない』. In other words, not being able to say anything disappoints Japanese people and is certainly an inconvenient problem for foreigners, rather than being “no problem even if it cannot be used.”
default.q.n2-3-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the opening sentence states: 『日本で長く暮らしていても外国人がなかなか慣れない』 (even after living in Japan for a long time, foreigners still find it difficult to get used to it).
default.q.n2-3-q62-62.why.3: (d) Based on the text, this is the choice most consistent with the reading because the author identifies both difficulties: not knowing how to respond when someone greets you (『どう答えていいか分からなくなる... これが難しい』—the response stage) and finding it difficult to initiate a conversation when necessary (『外国人にはこれがなかなか言えないようだ』—the usage stage).
default.q.n2-3-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (昔から使われてきた物を包むための便利な布です).
default.q.n2-3-q63-63.explanation:
- Main point: Furoshiki is a traditional Japanese square cloth that has been used since long ago to wrap variously shaped objects conveniently.
- Question translation: Which is the correct explanation of "Furoshiki"?
- Answer choices:
  1. There are both square and round types.
  2. It is a cloth invented and made long ago for the purpose of creating no waste.
  3. It is a convenient cloth that has been used since long ago to wrap objects.
  4. Foreigners do not know how to use Furoshiki.
default.q.n2-3-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage clearly states that furoshiki is 「一枚の四角い布」 (“a single square piece of cloth”); it does not mention a round type (丸い).
default.q.n2-3-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage only says that reusable furoshiki help reduce waste; it does not claim that they were originally created in the past to prevent littering.
default.q.n2-3-q63-63.why.2: (c) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「一枚の四角い布で、細長い瓶や大きいすいかなど、どんな形のものでも包むことができる。使わないときは小さくたたんで簡単に持ち運びできる。それが日本で昔から使われてきた「風呂敷」だ。」 (With a single square piece of cloth, objects of any shape can be wrapped... This is furoshiki, which has been used in Japan since ancient times.)
default.q.n2-3-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage says that overseas, furoshiki are popularly used to decorate walls or cover tables (海外では壁に飾ったりテーブルの上に敷いたりして使用されているようだ); it does not say that foreigners do not know how to use them.
default.q.n2-3-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (because it can be used repeatedly, it reduces waste and can be reused).
default.q.n2-3-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point: The main advantage of Furoshiki over paper or plastic bags is that it can be reused many times, helping reduce waste.
- Question: What does the article say is good about “Furoshiki”?

  1. Backpacks are originally made from “Furoshiki.”
  2. “Furoshiki” is suitable as a souvenir for people abroad, for example as a wall hanging or tablecloth.

default.q.n2-3-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The fact that foreigners like using it as a gift or for decoration/table settings is merely how it is used abroad, not the main advantage 「～にぴったりの品物だ」that the author highlights.

default.q.n2-3-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (風呂敷リ画ックは風呂敷 2 枚を縫い合わせたものです).
default.q.n2-3-q65-65.explanation:
- Main point: A Furoshiki backpack can be made simply by folding two pieces of cloth and tying (結ぶ) their ends together; there is no need to sew them together (縫い合わせる).

- Answer choices:
  1. A Furoshiki backpack is one of the new ways to use Furoshiki.

default.q.n2-3-q65-65.why.0: (a) This matches the passage. The passage presents the Furoshiki backpack as an example of introducing a new use that did not previously exist: 「従来にない使用方法を紹介することで... 例えば風呂敷で作るリュックサック」.
default.q.n2-3-q65-65.why.1: (b) This does not match the passage and is the answer to be selected. The passage states: 「三角形の山の部分と先ほど作った紐の中心を結ぶ。紐の端を三角形のそれぞれの残りの端と結ぶとできあがる。」 The Furoshiki backpack is made by folding and tying (結ぶ), not by sewing the pieces together (縫い合わせる).

default.q.n2-3-q65-65.why.3: (d) Matches the passage. It states that wrapping workshops also introduce new ways of using wrapping materials: 「包み方を教える会がたびたび開かれている。その際、従来にない使用方法を紹介することで...」.
default.q.n2-3-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 4. The statement that “the method used for blue roses in the past was different from the method used this time” is incorrect according to the passage, because blue roses had never been successfully created before.
default.q.n2-3-q66-66.explanation:
• Main point: The passage explains the history of rose colors. Selective breeding (品種改良) has produced roses in many colors, but blue roses could not be created because natural roses do not have the gene for blue pigment. It was only after two companies collaborated using genetic engineering technology (遺伝子組み換え技術) that a blue rose was successfully created for the first time.
• Question translation: Which of the following is DIFFERENT (incorrect) from the explanation of rose colors?
• Answer choices:
1. As a result of selective breeding, many different rose colors have been created over the years.
2. Without genetic engineering technology, blue roses could not have been created.
3. The source of the color in this blue rose may be used to create many other blue flowers in the future.
4. The method used to create blue roses in the past differs from the method used to create this blue rose.
default.q.n2-3-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this statement is true according to the passage: thanks to selective breeding (品種改良), roses in many different colors have been created over the years.
default.q.n2-3-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect because this statement agrees with the passage: roses do not naturally have genes that produce blue pigment, so blue roses cannot be created without using genetic modification technology (遺伝子組み換え技術).
default.q.n2-3-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this statement is true according to the passage: this source of blue pigment holds promise for creating many other blue-flowered species in the future.
default.q.n2-3-q66-66.why.3: (d) Correct (and different from the passage) because blue roses were previously considered impossible to create, and there had never been a "blue rose before." A blue rose was achieved for the first time through genetic modification technology.
default.q.n2-3-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The blue rose was created through cooperation between two companies using genetic modification technology.
default.q.n2-3-q67-67.explanation:
・Main point: The reading explains that blue roses were successfully created through 14 years of cooperation between two companies, using genetic modification technology to introduce a blue-pigment gene into roses.
・Question: How were blue roses created?
・Answer choices:
1. The variety was continuously improved over 14 years.
2. Two companies worked together and used genetic modification technology to create them.
3. They were easily created because variety-improvement techniques and genetic modification technology had been developed.
4. The genetic modification technologies of several companies were combined to create them.
default.q.n2-3-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because simple variety improvement (品種改良) cannot produce blue roses; roses lack the gene for blue pigment.
default.q.n2-3-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage clearly states that the two companies collaborated and used genetic modification technology (遺伝子組み換え技術) for 14 years to create blue roses.
default.q.n2-3-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the research took 14 difficult years; it was not completed easily (簡単に作れました).
default.q.n2-3-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage says that two companies collaborated on the research, not that several companies combined multiple gene-transfer technologies.
default.q.n2-3-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 1: This rose is considered the most promising because it could lead to the creation of many other rose colors in the future.
default.q.n2-3-q68-68.explanation:

1. Because it may be possible to create roses in many different colors in the future.

3. Because it is an expensive type of rose.

default.q.n2-3-q68-68.why.0: (a) Correct because, according to the passage, discovering the source of this color creates the prospect of producing many more unusual rose colors in the future.
default.q.n2-3-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that the expectation comes from being able to produce roses in large quantities.
default.q.n2-3-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention high cost as the most expected reason at all.
default.q.n2-3-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because, although the rare flower has only recently been commercialized, the main reason it is expected to have technological value is its potential to produce many new flower colors in the future.
default.q.n2-3-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (採用試験の結果 — the result of the employment examination).

Summary: Text A is a company’s notice announcing the result of a recruitment examination (the applicant was not selected). Text B is a notice about the result of an earlier preliminary recruitment examination (the applicant passed), along with instructions for the next interview. Therefore, the common point mentioned in both texts is the result of the recruitment examination (採用試験の結果).

1. The result of the interview examination

default.q.n2-3-q69-69.why.3: (d) This is incorrect because both texts are announcements of results after taking an examination or applying for a position, not announcements of the recruitment examination schedule (採用試験の日程).
default.q.n2-3-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (森さんがこの会社に就職できるかどうかはわからない - It is not known whether the person receiving the message will be able to get a job at this company).
default.q.n2-3-q70-70.explanation:
Summary: Notice B was sent to an applicant to inform them that they had passed the first screening and to provide the schedule for the upcoming interview examination on May 20 in the first-floor meeting room of Midori City Hall. 1. Anyone who cannot attend the interview will fail.

default.q.n2-3-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The view that it is not interesting without a strong Japanese wrestler.
default.q.n2-3-q71-71.explanation:
- Main point: At the beginning of the passage, the author notes that many foreign wrestlers are performing brilliantly and providing exciting matches. However, many fans and celebrities say, "It isn't interesting without a strong Japanese wrestler." The author feels a sense of discomfort (違和感を覚える) whenever hearing this opinion (これ).

- Question translation: What does 「これ」 (this) refer to?
- Answer choices:
1. The opinion that it is not interesting if there are no strong Japanese wrestlers.
2. The opinion that it is very interesting because strong foreign wrestlers are competing actively.
3. The fact that the number of good sumo wrestlers, whether foreign or Japanese, has decreased.
4. The opinion that it is very interesting because there are many strong Japanese wrestlers.
default.q.n2-3-q71-71.why.0: (a) matches the sentence immediately before the demonstrative: 「相撲ファンの中から多く聞かれるのが、『日本人の強い力士がいないと面白くない』という意見だ。... 私は、①これを聞くたびに違和感を覚える。」
default.q.n2-3-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author acknowledges at the beginning that foreign wrestlers compete actively and make matches exciting. That is not what makes the author feel uneasy when listening.
default.q.n2-3-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not say that the number of sumo wrestlers or matches has decreased. On the contrary, many foreign wrestlers are contributing to excellent matches.
default.q.n2-3-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage states that there are fewer Japanese wrestlers in high-ranking positions, not that “there are many strong Japanese wrestlers.”
default.q.n2-3-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author believes that people should not be lumped together as “foreigners” or “Japanese,” but should be viewed as individuals.
default.q.n2-3-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: The author criticizes grouping all wrestlers together as “foreign wrestlers” and labeling them with stereotypes. Instead of lumping people together by nationality, we should recognize and evaluate each individual separately (such as Asashoryu and Baruto) and avoid hastily believing labels imposed by others.

- Question: “Which of the following is consistent with the author’s view?”
- Answer choices:
1. Foreign wrestlers and Japanese wrestlers are inherently different, so they should not be lumped together when considering them...
2. Rather than lumping people together as “foreigners” and “Japanese,” we should consider each individual separately...
3. It is not good to lump people together as “foreigners” and “Japanese,” but...
4. It is not good to distinguish between foreign and Japanese wrestlers, but when it comes to foreign wrestlers...
default.q.n2-3-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author says that Japanese and foreign martial artists are equally matched once they have trained hard on the same stage, not that their essential nature is different.
default.q.n2-3-q72-72.why.1: (b) This matches the concluding sentence: 「『外国人力士』と、一括りに考えるのではなく、『朝青龍』『把瑠都』と考えるようにしてみよう。人によってはられたラベルは簡単に信じないことだ。」
default.q.n2-3-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the wording is incomplete and fails to convey the author's intended message of recognizing each individual.
default.q.n2-3-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author completely opposes prejudice and does not reserve any discriminatory view toward foreign wrestlers.
default.q.n2-3-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 3: It is inappropriate to draw a boundary between “foreigners” and “Japanese” among wrestlers standing on the same ring.
default.q.n2-3-q73-73.explanation:
- Main point: The author argues that regardless of where they come from, once people enter the world of sumo and train hard to improve their standing, they are all equal “wrestlers” standing together on the same ring (土俵). Therefore, drawing a dividing line between “foreigners” and “Japanese” is unreasonable; what matters most is whether the wrestler gives the audience exciting matches.

- Question translation: “Which sentence below matches the author's way of thinking?”
- Answer choices:
1. Foreign wrestlers are stronger because sumo is a sport in which physical strength is the most important factor...
2. Clearly, they should all be grouped together and considered as “foreign wrestlers”...
3. It is wrong to draw a line between foreigners and Japanese when they are all “wrestlers” standing on the same ring...
4. Stereotyping and labeling people as “serious Japanese” or “gloomy/quiet Americans”...
default.q.n2-3-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author clearly points out that some wrestlers with small physiques can still create excellent matches through speed and flexibility; sumo is not based solely on physical strength.
default.q.n2-3-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it is completely opposite to the author's view. The author advises: 「『外国人力士』と、一括りに考えるのではなく...」
default.q.n2-3-q73-73.why.2: (c) This matches the point made in paragraph 2: 「文字通り、同じ土俵に立つ『力士』なのに、どうして、『外国人』『日本人』という線引きをするのかが、私にはわからないのだ。相撲を面白くしてくれる力士なら、出身なんてどうでもいいじゃないか。」
default.q.n2-3-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author gives examples of prejudice to warn about the danger of stereotyping, not to endorse that way of thinking.
default.q.n2-3-q74-74.explanation:
• Summary: A notice for a karate class (空手教室) states that elementary school students practice every Tuesday and Thursday (16:00 ～ 17:15) and may attend as many sessions as they wish (「稽古には何回でも参加できます」). Regarding fees, the enrollment fee is free (「入会金 無料」), and the monthly fee for elementary school students is 2,000 円 (「月会費 小学生 2,000 円」, including sports insurance). Therefore, even if a student attends twice a week, the monthly fee remains 2,000 円.
• Question translation: If an elementary school student attends karate practice twice a week, how much must they pay per month?
• Answer choices:
1. 1,000 yen
2. 2,000 yen
3. 3,000 yen
4. 4,000 yen
default.q.n2-3-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The 1,000-yen fee does not appear in the Karate class fee table.
default.q.n2-3-q74-74.why.1: (b) Correct. The text states: 「月会費 小学生 2,000 円」 and 「稽古には何回でも参加できます」, along with 「入会金 無料」. Therefore, the fee is a monthly flat rate with unlimited attendance, and elementary school students only need to pay 2,000 円 per month.
default.q.n2-3-q74-74.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The 3,000-yen fee is the monthly tuition for 「大学生・一般」 (university students and adults), not for elementary school students.
default.q.n2-3-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The amount of 4,000 yen is an invalid inference obtained by multiplying 2,000 yen by 2. In fact, 2,000 yen is the monthly fee (月会費), allowing unlimited participation.
default.q.n2-3-q75-75.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (空手とヨガ).
default.q.n2-3-q75-75.explanation:
• Summary:
1. Karate class: Open to participants from elementary school age and up (「参加資格 … 小学生以上」). The text also emphasizes that it is suitable for older people seeking to maintain their health and for women learning self-defense (「お年寄りの健康維持や女性の護身術としてもお勧めします」). Therefore, the 62-year-old woman is eligible for the class for junior high school students and older (「中学生以上」).
2. Yoga class: Participants must be at least 18 years old and live or work in Midori City (「参加資格 みどり市にお住まい・またはお勤めの 18 歳以上の方」). This woman is 62 and works at a supermarket in Midori City (「みどり市のスーパーで働いている」), so she is fully eligible.
Therefore, she can take both Karate and Yoga.
• Question: Which of the following classes can the 62-year-old woman who works at a supermarket in Midori City attend?
• Answer choices:
1. Karate only
2. Yoga only
3. Both Karate and Yoga
4. Neither class
default.q.n2-3-q75-75.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The person is eligible not only to study Karate but also to study Yoga.
default.q.n2-3-q75-75.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The person is eligible not only to study Yoga but also to study Karate.
default.q.n2-3-q75-75.why.2:
(c) Correct. The passage provides the following evidence:
- Karate: 「参加資格 … 小学生以上」 and 「お年寄りの健康維持や女性の護身術としてもお勧めします」—a 62-year-old woman is fully eligible to participate in the class for 「中学生以上」.
- Yoga: 「参加資格 みどり市にお住まい・またはお勤めの 18 歳以上の方」—a 62-year-old woman who works at a supermarket in Midori City (みどり市のスーパーで働いている) meets both the age requirement (≥ 18) and the employment requirement (お勤め).
Therefore, she can take both classes (空手とヨガ).
default.q.n2-3-q75-75.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Both classes have participation requirements appropriate for this woman's age and workplace.
default.q.n2-3-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 3. かけられ, from the compound verb 追いかける, meaning to chase or pursue.
default.q.n2-3-q11-11.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Yesterday, while I was walking home, I was chased by a strange man. It was really frightening.
- Vocabulary: 追いかける (to chase) → passive: 追いかけられる (to be chased).
- Example: 警察が逃げる犯人を追いかけた。(The police chased the fleeing criminal.)
default.q.n2-3-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「追いはらう」 means “to drive away” or “to chase away,” which does not fit the context of being followed by a stranger.
default.q.n2-3-q11-11.why.1: (b) There is no compound verb 「追いおそう」; 「襲われる」(to be attacked) is an independent verb and does not combine with 追い-.
default.q.n2-3-q11-11.why.2: (c) Correct. The compound verb 「追いかける」means “chase” or “pursue.” In the passive form 「追いかけられる」, it means being chased by a stranger.
default.q.n2-3-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「注山がれ」 is a meaningless combination of kanji and is entirely incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 真流 (the prefix 真- combines with 暗 to form 真暗/真っ暗, meaning pitch-dark, as dark as ink).
default.q.n2-3-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence meaning: At this time of year, it gets pitch-dark outside shortly after 5 p.m.
- Vocabulary: 真っ暗 / 真暗 (pitch-dark, completely dark).
- Prefix 「真-」 (ま/しん): indicates something complete, pure, or extreme (for example: 真夜中 - midnight, 真っ白 - pure white, 真っ赤 - bright red).
default.q.n2-3-q12-12.why.0: (a) Correct. The prefix 「真-」 means completely/extremely, and combined with 「暗」 forms 「真暗 / 真っ暗」 (pitch-dark, completely dark).
default.q.n2-3-q12-12.why.1: (b) The prefix 「全-」 (entire/all) does not combine with 「暗」 to describe how dark the sky and earth are.
default.q.n2-3-q12-12.why.2: (c) The prefix 「大-」 (big) cannot be combined directly with 「暗」 in this structure.
default.q.n2-3-q12-12.why.3: (d) The prefix 「深-」 means “deep” and is used in 深夜 (“late at night”); it is not combined to express pitch darkness.
default.q.n2-3-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 品 (combines to form the noun 日用品, meaning daily necessities, household goods).
default.q.n2-3-q13-13.explanation:
Meaning: I bought daily necessities at the supermarket near my home.
- Vocabulary: 日用品 (daily necessities, household goods).
- Example: 毎日の生活に必要な日用品を買い出しに行く。(I go shopping for the daily necessities needed for everyday life.)
default.q.n2-3-q13-13.why.0: (a) 「日用物」is not a standard Japanese compound noun.
default.q.n2-3-q13-13.why.1: (b) Correct. The suffix「品」(ひん - goods, articles) combines to form「日用品」(にちようひん - everyday goods, daily necessities).
default.q.n2-3-q13-13.why.2: (c) 「貨」(currency, goods) is used in 雑貨 and 百貨店; it does not combine to form 「日用貨」.
default.q.n2-3-q13-13.why.3: (d) 「荷」(luggage, package) is used in 荷物 and 出荷; it does not combine to form 「日用荷」.
default.q.n2-3-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 3. らしく (the suffix 〜らしい indicates being strongly characteristic of or typical of spring).
default.q.n2-3-q14-14.explanation:
Meaning: As the temperature rises and the flowers begin to bloom, it is finally starting to feel much more like spring.
- Grammar: N + らしい (characteristically N; truly like N) → N + らしく + verb.
- Example: 暖かくなって、ようやく春らしい季節になった。(The weather warmed up, and it finally became a truly springlike season.)
default.q.n2-3-q14-14.why.0: (a) When 「ように」 follows a noun, it requires the particle の (春のようになった) and means “like,” without necessarily indicating that it is actually spring. This does not fit the context in which spring is truly arriving.
default.q.n2-3-q14-14.why.1: (b) 「こんで」comes from the verb 込む and cannot be attached directly after the noun「春」.
default.q.n2-3-q14-14.why.2: (c) Correct. Noun + 「らしく」 means “distinctively,” “in the manner of,” or “typical of.” 「春らしくなりました」 describes the weather and scenery becoming distinctly spring-like.
default.q.n2-3-q14-14.why.3: (d) 「そうに」 cannot directly follow the noun 「春」 to form an adverb; 春そうに is not a valid expression.
default.q.n2-3-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 戻注 (the compound verb 払い戻す means to refund or return money; its passive form is 払い戻された).
default.q.n2-3-q15-15.explanation:
Meaning: Because the concert was canceled, the ticket money was refunded.
- Vocabulary: 払い戻す (to refund, return ticket costs/expenses) → passive: 払い戻される (to be refunded).
- Example: 悪天候で飛行機が欠航になり、航空券代が払い戻された。(Because the flight was canceled due to bad weather, the airfare was refunded.)
default.q.n2-3-q15-15.why.0: (a) 「返」 is commonly used in the noun 「返金」 (refund), but it does not form the standard combination required here.
default.q.n2-3-q15-15.why.1: (b) 「過ごす」(to spend time, go beyond) does not combine with 払い in the context of a ticket refund.
default.q.n2-3-q15-15.why.2: (c) 「元」does not combine with 払い to form a verb meaning “to refund.”
default.q.n2-3-q15-15.why.3: (d) Correct. The compound verb 「払い戻す」 (はらいもどす) means to refund or return money; its passive forms are 「払い戻される / 払い戻された」.
default.q.n2-3-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 影響.
default.q.n2-3-q16-16.explanation:
Meaning: That painting had a major influence on artists of later periods.
- Key expression: 「～に影響をおよぼす/及ぼす」(to have an influence on ~).
- Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 影響 (influence), 反映 (reflection), 貢献 (contribution), 関連 (connection).
- Example: 彼の研究は後世の学者に大きな影響を及ぼした。(His research had a major influence on scholars of later generations.)
default.q.n2-3-q16-16.why.0: (a) 影響 (えいきょう — influence): It forms the fixed expression 「影響をおよぼす」 (影響を及ぼす: to have a major influence on...), which is natural and accurate in the context of an artwork deeply affecting later generations of artists.
default.q.n2-3-q16-16.why.1: (b) 反映 (はんえい): Usually used with the verbs 「反映する / 反映させる」, meaning to reflect an image or reflect opinions or actual conditions. It does not combine with 「をおよぼす」.
default.q.n2-3-q16-16.why.2: (c) 貢献 (こうけん - contribution): commonly combines with 「～に貢献する」or 「貢献を果たす」(to contribute to development/society), and does not combine with 「をおよぼす」.
default.q.n2-3-q16-16.why.3: (d) 関連 (かんれん): Usually used with 「関連する / 関連がある」 (to be related to); it does not form an appropriate meaning with 「をおよぼす」.
default.q.n2-3-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 1. あわただしい.
default.q.n2-3-q17-17.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Since moving day is approaching, every day is extremely busy with packing belongings and handling all kinds of procedures.
- Common expression: 「慌ただしい毎日を送る」(to spend hectic days).
- Related vocabulary: 慌ただしい (hectic, rushed), 羨ましい (envious, admiring), 悔しい (frustrating, regrettable), 激しい (intense, fierce).
- Example: 年末は仕事が重なって慌ただしい日々が続いている。(At the end of the year, work piles up and the hectic days continue.)
default.q.n2-3-q17-17.why.0: (a) あわただしい (慌ただしい — busy, hectic, bustling): describes a state in which many things happen continuously, forcing people to work constantly without time to rest (「慌ただしい毎日」: hectic days). This fits the context of preparing to move house perfectly.
default.q.n2-3-q17-17.why.1: (b) うらやましい (羨ましい - envious, wishing for, longing for): Expresses admiration or a desire for something good that another person has; it is not used to describe days overwhelmed by moving-related paperwork.
default.q.n2-3-q17-17.why.2: (c) くやしい (悔しい – frustrated, bitter, regretful): describes the frustration or regret felt after failure or defeat; it does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-3-q17-17.why.3: (d) はげし, from 激しい, means 'intense, violent, fierce.' It describes wind or rain, severe pain, or fierce competition, not busy days spent cleaning and organizing.
default.q.n2-3-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 通信.
default.q.n2-3-q18-18.explanation:
Sentence meaning: By using computers, exchanging information and communicating not only domestically but also internationally has become possible.
- Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 通信 (つうしん — communication, telecommunications, exchange of information), 通知 (つうち — notification, informing), 通行 (つうこう — passage, traffic), 通用 (つうよう — circulation, validity).
- Example: 衛星を使った通信技術の発展により、世界中どこでも瞬時に連絡が取れる。(Thanks to the development of satellite communication technology, it is possible to contact anyone instantly from anywhere in the world.)
default.q.n2-3-q18-18.why.0: (a) 通知 (つうち - notice; notification): This means sending an official notice or announcement unilaterally to someone, such as 合格通知 or 採用通知. It does not mean exchanging information or communicating interactively via computer.
default.q.n2-3-q18-18.why.1: (b) 通信 (つうしん — telecommunications, communication, data transmission): Often used with computers or networks (コンピューター通信, データ通信), referring to the exchange of information and data between parties domestically and internationally.
default.q.n2-3-q18-18.why.2: (c) 通行 (つうこう - passage, movement, traffic): Used for people or vehicles moving along roads or through transport networks, as in 通行止め and 通行料. It does not apply to computer networks.
default.q.n2-3-q18-18.why.3: (d) 通用 (つうよう — commonly accepted/in circulation, valid for use): It means being recognized or widely valid for use within a certain scope, as in この規則は世界で通用する. It does not fit the context of the sentence.
default.q.n2-3-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あずける.
default.q.n2-3-q19-19.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Because something urgent came up, I decided to leave my child with a friend to look after.
- Distinguish these easily confused words:
  + 預ける (あずける — transitive verb): to leave someone or something in another person's care (「子供・荷物を～に預ける」).
  + 預かる (あずかる — transitive verb): to take care of or hold something for someone else (「子供・荷物を預かる」).
- Sino-Japanese readings: 預 (entrust), 受取 (receive, take), 与 (give).
- Example: 旅行に行く間、ペットを友達に預けることにした。(I decided to leave my pet with a friend while I went on a trip.)
default.q.n2-3-q19-19.why.0: (a) あずかる (預かる - look after, keep, take care of): This is the action performed by the person who accepts someone or something into their care (for example: 友人が私の子供を預かる). In the sentence, the subject 「私は」 is leaving a child in someone else's care, so 「預かる」 cannot be used.
default.q.n2-3-q19-19.why.1: (b) あずける (預ける—entrust, leave in someone’s care): According to the pattern 「[Place/recipient] に [person/thing entrusted] を預ける」 (to leave someone or something in another person’s care), the subject 「私」 leaves the child at a friend’s house, so using 「預ける」 is completely correct.
default.q.n2-3-q19-19.why.2: (c) うけとる (受け取る - to receive, accept): Refers to receiving a package, message, or letter sent to oneself. It is not used in the context of sending one's child somewhere to be looked after.
default.q.n2-3-q19-19.why.3: (d) あたえ (from 与える: to grant, provide, or bring about): used for providing opportunities, causing effects or damage, or giving rewards; it is not used for sending one's child to someone else to be looked after.
default.q.n2-3-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 緊張.
default.q.n2-3-q20-20.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I have to give a speech at my friend’s wedding today, so I feel very nervous and tense.
- Common expressions: 「緊張する」(to feel nervous or tense), 「緊張がほぐれる」(to relax, have one’s tension ease).
- Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 緊張 (tension, nervousness), 拡張 (expansion), 出張 (business trip), 主張 (assertion, expressing an opinion).
- Example: 大勢の人の前で発表するときは、誰でも緊張するものだ。(Anyone gets nervous when speaking in front of a large crowd.)
default.q.n2-3-q20-20.why.0: (a) 拡張 (かくちょう – expansion, enlargement): Commonly used for roads, the scale of a business, or memory capacity (such as 道路の拡張 and 勢力拡張), but not to describe a person's psychology.
default.q.n2-3-q20-20.why.1: (b) 出張 (しゅっちょう): a business trip, meaning traveling away from one's workplace for work at the company's direction. It is not used to describe how one feels when standing up to give a speech.
default.q.n2-3-q20-20.why.2: (c) 緊張 (きんちょう — nervousness, tension, anxiety): 「緊張する / 緊張している」 describes a tense or anxious mental state before an important event or when standing in front of a crowd, so it is exactly correct.
default.q.n2-3-q20-20.why.3: (d) 主張 (しゅちょう, assertion, insistence, claim): to emphasize and firmly defend one’s opinion or make a demand. It does not mean a state of anxiety or nervousness.
default.q.n2-3-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ぎっしり.
default.q.n2-3-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: In the package sent by her mother, all kinds of canned foods are packed tightly inside.
- Common expression: 「ぎっしり詰まる / ぎっしり入っている」(be packed tightly/full to the brim).
- Related mimetic adverbs:
  + ぎっしり: tightly packed, full with no space left (a packed schedule, a suitcase full of belongings).
  + びっしり: densely packed, closely spaced (writing covering a page).
  + がっかり: disappointed, crestfallen.
  + ぐっすり: soundly, deeply (sleep).
- Example: スーツケースにお土産がぎっしり詰まっている。(The suitcase is packed full of souvenirs.)
default.q.n2-3-q21-21.why.0: (a) が流かり is a font error for がっかり, meaning disappointed or dejected. It describes a psychological state when expectations are not met and does not modify the verb「詰まる」(to become clogged or packed).
default.q.n2-3-q21-21.why.1: (b) ぎっしり (packed tightly, filled to the brim, crammed): An adverb describing objects packed so tightly that no space remains. It is often used in the fixed expression 「ぎっしり詰まる / ぎっしり詰まっている」 and is completely appropriate for describing a package filled with canned goods.
default.q.n2-3-q21-21.why.2: (c) ぐ流すり (a font error for ぐっすり, meaning “soundly” or “deeply asleep”): This adverb is used with sleep-related verbs such as 「ぐっすり眠る / 寝る」, not with 「詰まる」.
default.q.n2-3-q21-21.why.3: (d) 消った is an incorrect spelling/answer choice; it is not a Japanese adverb expressing how tightly a package is packed with belongings.
default.q.n2-3-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 2. くどい.
default.q.n2-3-q22-22.explanation:
Sentence meaning: His explanations are always long-winded, repetitive, and drawn out, which makes me extremely irritated.
- Important meanings of 「くどい」:
  1. Speech or explanations that are overly long and repetitive: 「話・説明がくどい」(The talk/explanation is long-winded and tedious.)
  2. Food that is excessively rich, greasy, or strongly flavored: 「くどい味」(an overly rich flavor).
  3. Colors or makeup that are too flashy or gaudy: 「くどい化粧」(overly heavy makeup).
- Example: 同じことを何度もくどくど言うのはやめてください。(Please stop going on and on about the same thing repeatedly.)
default.q.n2-3-q22-22.why.0: (a) えらい (偉い - capable, excellent, great / 偉い目に遭う: to go through serious trouble): An adjective praising ability, social status, or the seriousness of a situation; it is not used for a long-winded explanation that causes irritation.
default.q.n2-3-q22-22.why.1: (b) くどい (wordy, tedious, repetitive): When used with speech or explanations (「説明がくどい」), it means going around in circles and repeating oneself unnecessarily, making the listener annoyed and impatient (「いらいらする」). This is a perfect fit.
default.q.n2-3-q22-22.why.2: (c) かゆい (痒い - itchy): describes an itchy sensation on the surface of the skin (from an insect bite or allergy) and is unrelated to the explanation.

default.q.n2-3-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 静かに, because the adverb「そっと」means gently, quietly, or without making a sound, and is synonymous with「静かに」.
default.q.n2-3-q23-23.explanation:

default.q.n2-3-q23-23.why.0: (a) 静かに (しずかに - TĨNH): quietly, softly, gently; synonymous with 「そっと」 when describing whispering softly into someone’s ear. -> Correct.
default.q.n2-3-q23-23.why.1: (b) はっきりと means “clearly” or “distinctly,” which does not match the soft, whispering nuance of「そっと」. → Incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q23-23.why.2: (c) 急に (きゅうに): suddenly, unexpectedly; it describes how quickly an event occurs, not the quality of a soft, quiet sound. → Incorrect.

default.q.n2-3-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 気持ちのいい, because the na-adjective 「さわやか（な）」means refreshing, fresh, or pleasant, and is synonymous with 「気持ちのいい」.
default.q.n2-3-q24-24.explanation:

default.q.n2-3-q24-24.why.0: (a) 気持ちのいい (きもちのいい): pleasant, refreshing, comfortable; synonymous with 「さわやかな」when describing pleasant weather or a fresh morning that creates a爽快 feeling. → Correct.
default.q.n2-3-q24-24.why.1: (b) 晴れた (はれた): sunny, clear; it describes sunny weather and is not synonymous with the adjective「さわやか」, meaning refreshed or invigorating. -> Incorrect.

default.q.n2-3-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 基準 because the noun 「目安」means a reference point or standard used as a basis for taking action, and is synonymous with 「基準」.
default.q.n2-3-q25-25.explanation:

default.q.n2-3-q25-25.why.1: (b) 基準 (きじゅん - standard): a standard or criterion used as a basis; synonymous with 「目安」in the context of a criterion for taking medicine. -> Correct.

default.q.n2-3-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 2. かつて, because the adverb 「以前」 means “before” or “in the past,” and is synonymous with 「かつて」 (“once,” “formerly”).
default.q.n2-3-q26-26.explanation:
- Translation: There used to be a park in this area.
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese readings:
  + 以前 (いぜん): formerly, previously.
  + かつて: once, formerly, in the past.
  + 辺り (あたり): the surrounding area, nearby.

default.q.n2-3-q26-26.why.0: (a) 第一に (だいいちに) means “first of all,” “first,” or “most importantly”; it is not used to indicate a time in the past. → Incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q26-26.why.1: (b) かつて: formerly, once, at one time in the past; synonymous with 「以前」. -> Correct.
default.q.n2-3-q26-26.why.2: (c) 先に (さきに): “Beforehand” or “ahead,” referring to the order of actions or physical position. It is not used to indicate a distant time in the past, such as 「以前」. → Incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q26-26.why.3: (d) 真っ先に (まっさきに): first of all, before anything else, with top priority; it does not indicate a time in the past. → Incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2. うるさい because the i-adjective 「さわがしい」 means noisy or boisterous and is synonymous with 「うるさい」.
default.q.n2-3-q27-27.explanation:
- Meaning: The classroom is very noisy.
- Vocabulary and kanji:

default.q.n2-3-q27-27.why.0: (a) 荒っぽい (あらっぽい - HOANG): Rough, violent, coarse, or forceful, describing actions, behavior, or driving; it is not used for loud, boisterous noise. → Incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q27-27.why.1: (b) うるさい: noisy, boisterous, unpleasant because of sound; it is synonymous with「さわがしい」when describing a noisy classroom. → Correct.
default.q.n2-3-q27-27.why.2: (c) あわただしい (慌ただしい): busy, hurried, hectic, describing work or the rapid passage of time, not merely noise. → Incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q27-27.why.3: (d) おだやか (穏やか): calm, peaceful, gentle; it has the opposite meaning of noise and disorder. -> Incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because 「上達が早い」 (make rapid progress / improve quickly) is the completely correct collocation for learning and practicing a skill.
default.q.n2-3-q28-28.explanation:
「上達」(じょうたつ): improvement or advancement in a skill, technique, or ability, such as learning a foreign language, playing an instrument, or playing sports.
- Common expressions: 上達が早い (to improve quickly), 腕前が上達する (to improve one's skill), 日本語が上達する (to improve in Japanese).
- Example: 毎日コツコツ練習すれば、必ずピアノが上達します。(If you practice steadily every day, your piano playing will definitely improve.)
default.q.n2-3-q28-28.why.0: Incorrect because 「上達」 is used only for personal skills or abilities. When referring to a country's development, use 「発展」 (development) or 「成長」 (growth).
default.q.n2-3-q28-28.why.1: Incorrect because 「上達」is a noun or a Group 3 verb, not a na-adjective that can be conjugated as 「上達に」. To praise someone's cooking as skillful or delicious, use the adverb 「上手に」('skillfully, well').
default.q.n2-3-q28-28.why.2: Correct because 「上達が早い」 (“to improve quickly” or “to become skilled quickly”) is a natural and accurate expression for rapid improvement in a skill or ability.
default.q.n2-3-q28-28.why.3: The employee is reporting the work situation to the company president, so the verb 「報告する」 (“to report”) is required, not 「上達する」.
default.q.n2-3-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because 「戸締りを確認する」 (check that the doors and windows are closed and locked) is the correct expression for checking something again before going out.
default.q.n2-3-q29-29.explanation:
「確認」(かくにん): confirmation; carefully checking whether something, a condition, or a fact is correct or safe.
- Common expressions: 安全を確認する (check safety), 日程を確認する (confirm the schedule), 再確認する (check again).
- Example: 予約内容に間違いがないか、メールで確認してください。(Please check by email that there are no errors in the reservation details.)
default.q.n2-3-q29-29.why.0: Correct because 「確認する」 (check, confirm) combines with 「戸締り」 (locking the doors) to express carefully checking that the doors have been securely locked before going out.
default.q.n2-3-q29-29.why.1: Incorrect because when confidently predicting that a team will win or become champion, the adjective/noun 「確実」(certain, assured) is required, not 「確認」.
default.q.n2-3-q29-29.why.2: Incorrect because entering the room requires permission or approval from the secretariat or office, so 「許可」(permission) or 「承認」(approval) must be used, not 「確認」.
default.q.n2-3-q29-29.why.3: Incorrect because there was only one candidate, who was therefore elected or decided without an election. 「当選した」(was elected) or 「決定された」(was decided) should be used, not 「確認された」.
default.q.n2-3-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because 「やけどをする」(suffer a burn) is exactly the correct expression for an injury caused by a fire or flames.
default.q.n2-3-q30-30.explanation:
「やけど」(火傷) means a burn or burn injury: damage to the skin or body tissue caused by high temperatures, fire, boiling water, hot oil, and so on.
- Common phrases: やけどをする (get burned), やけどを負う (sustain a burn injury), ひどいやけど (a severe burn).
- Example: 熱湯をこぼして、手にやけどをしてしまった。(I accidentally spilled boiling water and burned my hand.)
default.q.n2-3-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect because the feeling of giving up or becoming careless and depressed after a breakup is expressed by 「やけになっている」 (from やけ - 自棄: giving up), not 「やけど」.
default.q.n2-3-q30-30.why.1: Correct because「やけどをする」(to get burned) accurately describes bodily injury caused by the high temperature or flames of the fire.
default.q.n2-3-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect. The heartburn or uncomfortable burning sensation in the chest caused by eating too many sweets should be expressed as「胸やけ（むねやけ）がする」, not「胸がやけどしている」.
default.q.n2-3-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect because the beautiful night view of Tokyo from above requires the noun「夜景（やけい）」(night view), not「やけど」.
default.q.n2-3-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because 「すらすらと解く」(solve smoothly and without difficulty) is a completely appropriate use of the adverb 「すらすら」.
default.q.n2-3-q31-31.explanation:
「すらすら」(adverbial mimetic word): smoothly, fluently, effortlessly, without stumbling or hesitation. It is often used for reading, writing, speaking, solving exercises, and similar activities.
- Common expressions: すらすら解く (solve effortlessly), すらすら読む (read fluently), すらすら話す (speak fluently).
- Example: 彼女は難しい日本語の文章をすらすらと読み上げた。(She read aloud a difficult Japanese passage very fluently.)
default.q.n2-3-q31-31.why.0: Correct because 「すらすら（と）」describes an action—such as solving a problem, reading text, or answering questions—being performed smoothly and fluently without any difficulty.
default.q.n2-3-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect. A slippery road should be described with words such as 「滑りやすい」(easy to slip on) or 「つるつるした」(smooth and slippery), not 「すらすらな」.
default.q.n2-3-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect. Feeling refreshed and relieved after bathing is expressed with「さっぱりした」or「すっきりした」. Smooth, dry skin is described with「さらさら」, not「すらすら」.
default.q.n2-3-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect because spending the whole day aimlessly fooling around and dragging things out is expressed with 「だらだら（遊ぶ）」, not 「すらすら」.
default.q.n2-3-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because 「緊張して眠れなかった」 (I was too nervous to sleep) accurately expresses the anxious psychological state before an important exam.
default.q.n2-3-q32-32.explanation:
「緊張」(きんちょう): nervousness, tension, or psychological stress; it can also refer to tension or confrontation in diplomatic relations or political situations.
- Common expressions: 緊張してあがる (become flustered from nervousness), 緊張がほぐれる (relax and release tension), 緊張感を持つ (maintain a sense of focus or tension).
- Example: 面接の前は誰でも緊張するものだ。(Everyone gets nervous before an interview.)
default.q.n2-3-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect usage: 「緊張」 is not used as a na-adjective to describe a person's character. To describe someone as strict or stern, use 「厳格な人」 (a strict person) or 「真面目な人」.
default.q.n2-3-q32-32.why.1: Correct because 「緊張する」 (to feel tense or nervous) accurately describes the anxious, restless mental state before an exam that makes it difficult to sleep.
default.q.n2-3-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because the adjective form 「緊張な」does not exist. In formal or ceremonial situations, use 「改まった場面」; to describe a tense atmosphere, use 「緊張した場面」.
default.q.n2-3-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect because 「緊張」does not become the adverb 「緊張に」. To apologize seriously and sincerely, use 「真剣に」(seriously), 「必死に」(desperately), or 「丁寧に」(politely).

default.q.n2-3-q1-1.why.3: (d) ひたい: Correct. 「額」has the kun-reading「ひたい」and means forehead.

default.q.n2-3-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 2. むずかしい.
