- Example: 事故の影響で、駅前は一時混乱した。(Because of the accident, the area in front of the station was in confusion for a while.)
default.q.n2-3-q9-9.why.0: (a) 1.「混乱」: Correct kanji (confusion, disorder); read こんらん.
default.q.n2-3-q9-9.why.1: (b) 2.「困惑」: Read as こんわく (confusion, bewilderment); the reading is incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q9-9.why.2: (c) 3. 「混浴」 is read as こんよく and means mixed bathing by men and women; the word and meaning are incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q9-9.why.3: (d) 4.「困難」: Pronounced こんなん (KON NAN – difficulty, obstacle), so the reading is incorrect.
default.q.n2-3-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 勤勉 (diligence).
default.q.n2-3-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: Japanese people are often considered very diligent and hardworking.
- Sino-Japanese note: 勤勉 (きんべん) = diligence, industriousness, hard work.
- Example: 彼は勤勉な働き手として、上司から高く評価されている。(He is highly regarded by his supervisors as a diligent worker.)
default.q.n2-3-q10-10.why.0: (a) 1.「勤便」: The character 便 was used incorrectly instead of 勉, as in 勉強.
default.q.n2-3-q10-10.why.1: (b) 2.「緊勉」: The kanji 緊 is incorrect (as in 緊急 and 緊張); it should be 勤 (as in 勤務 and 勤勉).
default.q.n2-3-q10-10.why.2: (c) 3.「金便」: Both 金 (KIM) and 便 (TIỆN) are combined incorrectly.
default.q.n2-3-q10-10.why.3: (d) 4.「勤勉」: Correct kanji (CẦN MIỄN - きんべん), meaning diligent, hardworking, or industrious.
default.q.n2-30-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (わけにはいかない).
default.q.n2-30-q33-33.explanation:
- Meaning: Even if one says that one is busy, one cannot postpone the deadline for the work.
- Grammar: V-る + わけにはいかない: cannot do something because of moral reasons, rules, social responsibility, or psychological constraints.
- Linking pattern: 「〜からといって、〜わけにはいかない」(Even if one says that..., one cannot...).
- Example: 大事な会議があるから、熱があっても休むわけにはいかない。(I have an important meeting, so I cannot take the day off even if I have a fever.)
default.q.n2-30-q33-33.why.0: (a)「〜わけだ」expresses an obvious conclusion or gives an explanation (“no wonder,” “that is why,” “it means that”), so it does not fit after「からといって...」.
default.q.n2-30-q33-33.why.1: (b) 「〜わけもない」 expresses absolute, logically based negation (“there is no way that...,” “it is absolutely impossible”). It is not used to express one's personal responsibility or principles.
default.q.n2-30-q33-33.why.2: (c) 「〜わけがある」 means “there is a reason to...,” and does not form a suitable grammar pattern for expressing that a deadline cannot be postponed.
default.q.n2-30-q33-33.why.3: (d) 「〜わけにはいかない」 expresses "cannot do something" for moral, responsibility-based, or principled reasons. Combined with 「〜からといって」, it forms a complete and accurate sentence.
default.q.n2-30-q34-34.explanation:
- Meaning: Since I am going for a walk anyway, I will return the books to the library while I am out.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 散歩 (walk), 図書館 (library), 本 (book).
- Grammar: N / V-masu stem + がてら: while doing A, especially an activity involving going somewhere, take the opportunity to do B as well.
- Example: 買い物がてら、郵便局に行って手紙を出してきた。(While I was out shopping, I stopped by the post office and mailed a letter.)
default.q.n2-30-q34-34.why.0: (a)「ついで」: To use it, the pattern must be 「〜のついでに」. Here, the noun 「散歩」 is not followed by the particles 「の」 and 「に」, so the grammar is incorrect.
default.q.n2-30-q34-34.why.1: (b) 「つれて」 appears in the structure 「〜につれて」 (“as...,” “along with a change in...”); it requires the particle 「に」 and does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-30-q34-34.why.2: (c)「ながら」: The grammar pattern 「〜ながら」(while doing...) follows the V-masu stem and does not directly follow the noun 「散歩」.
default.q.n2-30-q34-34.why.3: (d) 「がてら」directly follows a noun denoting an action or movement (N + がてら) and means “while taking the opportunity to do something,” forming 「散歩がてら」(“while taking a walk”).
default.q.n2-30-q35-35.verdict: The given answer is 3 (足りることはない); however, according to N2 grammar, the correct answer is 2 (越したことはない).
default.q.n2-30-q35-35.explanation:
- Translation: Preparing thoroughly in advance is the best option.
- Kanji etymology: 前もって (in advance), 十分 (sufficiently, thoroughly), 準備 (preparation).
- Grammar: V-る / A-い / Na-である / N-である + に越したことはない: there is nothing better than..., it is best to....
- Example: 風邪の予防には、手洗いうがいをするに越したことはない。(For preventing colds, nothing is better than washing your hands and gargling.)
default.q.n2-30-q35-35.why.0: (a) 「〜に過ぎたことはない」is not a standard grammar pattern; only「〜にすぎない」, meaning “it is merely...,” is used.
default.q.n2-30-q35-35.why.1: (b) 「〜に越したことはない」: This standard N2 grammar pattern means “nothing is better than ... / ... is best,” and fits the idea that being fully prepared in advance is best.
default.q.n2-30-q35-35.why.2: (c)「〜に足りることはない」 does not form a grammatical pattern with the intended meaning. The valid forms are 「〜に足る」 or 「〜に足りない」, meaning “worthy of” or “not worthy of.”
default.q.n2-30-q35-35.why.3: (d)「〜に負けることはない」is not a fixed grammar structure expressing advice or the optimal course of action.
default.q.n2-30-q36-36.explanation:
- Meaning: Judging from the way he speaks, he is not from this area.
- Grammar: N + からすると / からすれば: judging from, based on... Used to make an inference or judgment based on a specific clue or sign.
- Example: あの足音からすると、帰ってきたのは父のようだ。(Judging from those footsteps, it seems that my father has come home.)
default.q.n2-30-q36-36.why.0: (a)「聞くと」:「〜から聞くと」is not a grammar pattern for making a judgment; 「〜から聞く」only means to hear information from someone.
default.q.n2-30-q36-36.why.1: (b)「言うと」:「〜から言うと」is generally used to judge something from a standpoint, aspect, or perspective (e.g., 専門家から言うと, 結論から言うと), not to infer something from outward clues.
default.q.n2-30-q36-36.why.2: (c)「見ると」:「〜から見ると」is generally used to express the viewpoint or perspective of an observer (e.g., 親から見ると = from a parent's perspective). When making a judgment based on specific clues such as someone's voice or gestures,「からすると」is more accurate.
default.q.n2-30-q36-36.why.3: (d)「すると」: The pattern「〜からすると」is used to make a judgment or inference based on specific evidence, here 話し方 (the way someone speaks).
default.q.n2-30-q37-37.explanation:
- Meaning: Stop joking around and speak seriously.
- Kanji readings: 冗談 (joke), 話 (conversation / speech).
- Grammar: N + ぬきで / ぬきにして: leaving N aside / without taking N into consideration. The idiomatic expression 「冗談ぬきで」is very common and means "seriously; no kidding."
- Example: お世辞ぬきで、あなたの日本語は本当に自然で上手です。(No flattery—you speak Japanese very naturally and well.)
default.q.n2-30-q37-37.why.0: (a)「なしで」usually indicates being without something (e.g., 砂糖なしで, “without sugar”); it does not form the fixed expression for a serious attitude, 「冗談ぬきで」.
default.q.n2-30-q37-37.why.1: (b)「ぬきで」: The pattern 「N + ぬきで」 means “leaving N out / setting N aside,” forming the phrase 「冗談ぬきで」, “seriously, no kidding.”
default.q.n2-30-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「せずに」 is the negative form of する (without doing); it does not directly follow the noun 「冗談」 in this way.
default.q.n2-30-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「べからず」 is a formal, archaic prohibition pattern, 「V-る + べからず」 (must not do), and does not follow a noun. It is also completely unsuitable for the context.
default.q.n2-30-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: Kyoto offers new discoveries every time I visit.
- Vocabulary: 京都 (Kyoto), 行く (to go), 発見 (discovery).
- Grammar: V-る / Nの + たびに: every time..., whenever... (a repeated event produces the same reaction or result).
- Example: この写真を見るたびに、楽しかった旅行を思い出す。(Every time I look at this photo, I remember the enjoyable trip.)
default.q.n2-30-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「うえに」 means “moreover” or “in addition to” (“not only... but also...”), so it is unsuitable for expressing a regularly repeated event.
default.q.n2-30-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「たびに」: The pattern 「V-る + たびに」 means “every time...,” expressing that each visit to Kyoto brings a new discovery.
default.q.n2-30-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「み活に」 is not a grammatical structure with a meaning; it is a misspelling or meaningless expression.
default.q.n2-30-q38-38.why.3: (d)「なかに」: cannot directly follow the dictionary-form V-る to express this meaning.
default.q.n2-30-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (どころではなかった).
default.q.n2-30-q39-39.explanation:
- Translation: During a long holiday, it is not as if I have the time or energy to travel. I have to go to work at the company every day.
- Kanji-based explanation: 連休 (long consecutive holiday), 旅行 (travel), 毎日 (every day), 会社 (company).
- Grammar: N / V-る + どころではない / どころではなかった: not in a situation to do something because difficult or busy circumstances take priority.
- Example: 試験の前で、遊ぶどころではない。(With an exam coming up, I am in no position to play.)
default.q.n2-30-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「すべきではなかった」 means "should not have done it," but the following clause shows that the speaker did not travel at all, so this regret pattern cannot be used.
default.q.n2-30-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「しかなかった」 means “there was no choice but to...”; it does not directly follow the noun 「旅行」 and contradicts the idea of working every day.
default.q.n2-30-q39-39.why.2: (c)「とてなかった」: This grammar structure does not exist.
default.q.n2-30-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「どころではなかった」: The structure 「N + どころではなかった」means “it was absolutely no time to do N” or “doing N was out of the question,” which fits the context of being busy working perfectly.
default.q.n2-30-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (お目にかかった).
default.q.n2-30-q40-40.explanation:
- Translation: I do not know your name, but I have had the opportunity to meet you before.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 存じます (to know [humble]), 以前 (previously).
- Honorific language: 「お目にかかる」is the humble form (kenjōgo) of「会う」(to meet).
- Distinctions:
  + お目にかかる = 会う (to meet)
  + お目にかける = 見せる (to show)
  + 目を通す = 読む・見る (to look through, read)
- Example: 先生にお目にかかることができて、光栄です。(It is an honor to have been able to meet you, Professor.)
default.q.n2-30-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「お目にかけた」 is the humble form of 「見せる」 (to show something), not an expression for meeting someone.
default.q.n2-30-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「お目に入れた」 also carries the sense of showing something to someone or bringing it to their attention; it does not mean meeting someone.
default.q.n2-30-q40-40.why.2: (c)「お目を通した」means “looked over” or “skimmed a document,” and is not used for meeting someone.
default.q.n2-30-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「お目にかかった」is the past form of 「お目にかかる」, the humble form of 会う (to meet). It politely describes the speaker having met the other person before.
default.q.n2-30-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (せざるを得ない).
default.q.n2-30-q41-41.explanation:
- Meaning: Because it is an important meeting, I have no choice but to attend.
- Kanji meanings: 重要 (important), 会議 (meeting), 出席 (attendance).
- Grammar: V-ない + ざるを得ない (remove ない; する changes to せざるを得ない): to have no choice but to do something, even though one does not necessarily want to.
- Example: 理由はどうであれ、規則を破った以上は罰を受けざるを得ない。(Whatever the reason, once you have broken the rules, you have no choice but to accept the punishment.)
default.q.n2-30-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「しざるを得ない」: This is an incorrect classical conjugation of the group-3 verb 「する」; before 「〜ざるを得ない」, 「する」 must change to 「せざるを得ない」, not 「し」.
default.q.n2-30-q41-41.why.1: (b)「せざるを得ない」: the structure「V-nai (remove ない) + ざるを得ない」means “have no choice but to / be forced to”; the irregular form of「する」is correctly「せざるを得ない」.
default.q.n2-30-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「しかねない」: 「V-masu」 stem + 「かねない」 means “may” or “be at risk of causing a bad result,” which does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-30-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「すべからずだ」 is grammatically and morphologically incorrect; in Japanese, only 「〜べからず」 is used as a prohibition, not 「すべからずだ」.
default.q.n2-30-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: The management fee is 4000 yen per month.
- 管理費: management fee.
- Grammar: Quantity/unit + につき means “per each” or “for every,” expressing a unit price or allocation rate.
- Example: 入場料は、大人1人につき1000円です。(Admission is 1000 yen per adult.)
default.q.n2-30-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「つき」: the structure 「数量詞 + につき」 expresses a unit rate (“per”), so 「1か月につき」 (“per month”) is exactly correct.
default.q.n2-30-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「ごと」 usually follows a noun or time expression directly (e.g., 1か月ごと); it does not combine with 「に」 as in 「1か月にごと」.
default.q.n2-30-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「より」 is used in comparisons or in 「〜により」 (because of, depending on); it does not express a unit price ratio.
default.q.n2-30-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「まい」: 「〜まい」 follows a verb expressing negative volition or negative conjecture; it does not follow 「1か月に」.
default.q.n2-30-q43-43.explanation:
- Meaning: When I contacted them to ask about tickets for the concert, they had already sold out.
- Vocabulary: 問合せ means an inquiry or contact, and 売り切れ means sold out.
- Grammar: V-た + ところ indicates that after doing something, one discovered an unexpected result or actual situation.
- Example: 病院で検査を受けたところ、特に異常はなかった。(After being examined at the hospital, it turned out that there were no particular abnormalities.)
default.q.n2-30-q43-43.why.0: (a)「ので」: indicates a direct cause-and-effect relationship (“because...therefore...”) and does not express the nuance of discovering only after asking that the tickets had sold out.
default.q.n2-30-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「ところ」: The structure「V-た + ところ」means “after doing something, [someone] obtained a result/discovered that…” and is exactly appropriate in this context.
default.q.n2-30-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「ことで」indicates a cause or method (“by doing,” “because of doing”). It is not used to express realizing a result after a specific action.
default.q.n2-30-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「はずみ」: The pattern 「V-た + はずみに」means “in the momentum of doing something” or “accidentally while doing something,” which does not fit contacting someone to ask about tickets.
default.q.n2-30-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ほかならない).
default.q.n2-30-q44-44.explanation:
- Meaning: Abnormal weather phenomena around the world are none other than a warning from nature.
- Kanji terms: 異常気象 (abnormal weather), 自然 (nature), 警告 (warning).
- Grammar: N + にほかならない: "is precisely" / "is nothing other than..." Used at the end of a sentence to strongly assert the sole cause, reason, or nature of something.
- Example: 彼が成功したのは、日頃の努力の結果にほかならない。(His success is precisely the result of his everyday efforts.)
default.q.n2-30-q44-44.why.0: (a)「かえられない」: It appears in the structure 「〜にはかえられない」, meaning “cannot be exchanged for / nothing can replace,” which does not fit the meaning here.
default.q.n2-30-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「なりやまない」: 「鳴りやまない」 means “to continue ringing” or “not stop sounding,” used for bells, applause, and similar sounds; it does not follow the noun 「警告に」.
default.q.n2-30-q44-44.why.2: (c)「ほかでもない」: This phrase introduces a topic, as in「ほかでもないが」(there is no other matter except...); it does not come after「〜に」at the end of a sentence to draw a conclusion.
default.q.n2-30-q44-44.why.3: (d)「ほかならない」: The structure 「N + にほかならない」 strongly asserts “is precisely / is nothing other than...,” forming 「警告にほかならない」 (“is nothing other than a warning”).
default.q.n2-30-q45-45.verdict: The correct order is 4 → 1 → 2 → 3. The starred ★ position is choice 2 (ので).
default.q.n2-30-q45-45.explanation:
Complete sentence: 会期末は大変込み合いますのでお早めにお越しください。
Meaning: The exhibition will be very crowded toward the end, so please come early.
default.q.n2-30-q45-45.why.0: (a) 込み合います: The predicate verb combines with the degree adverb 「大変」 (4) to form 「大変込み合います」 (very crowded), occupying position 2.
default.q.n2-30-q45-45.why.1: (b) ので: A conjunction expressing cause or reason, placed after the polite form 「込み合います」 (1) to form the causal clause 「大変込み合いますので」 (“because it will be very crowded”), in position 3 (★).
default.q.n2-30-q45-45.why.2: (c) お早めに: An adverb expressing manner, placed before 「お越しください」 to modify the action of coming early; it occupies position 4.
default.q.n2-30-q45-45.why.3: (d) 大変: This degree adverb occupies position 1 after 「会期末は」and modifies the predicate 「込み合います」(1).
default.q.n2-30-q46-46.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The ★ position is choice 1 (先生方は).
default.q.n2-30-q46-46.explanation:
Complete sentence: 学長はじめ先生方は全員参加されたと伺いました。
Meaning: I heard that all the teachers, including the university president, took part.
default.q.n2-30-q46-46.why.0: (a) 先生方は: A noun phrase functioning as the subject with the particle 「は」. Together with the preceding phrase 「学長はじめ」(2–4), it forms an expanded subject and occupies position 3 (the ★ position).
default.q.n2-30-q46-46.why.1: (b) 学長: This representative noun comes first, in position 1, and combines with 「はじめ」 (4) in the pattern 「N + はじめ」.
default.q.n2-30-q46-46.why.2: (c) 全員: An adverbial noun expressing “everyone / the whole group,” appearing in the fourth position immediately before the honorific predicate 「参加された」.
default.q.n2-30-q46-46.why.3: (d) はじめ: It follows the noun 「学長」 (2) in the pattern 「～をはじめ（として）」 (“beginning with,” “first and foremost”), and occupies the second position.
default.q.n2-30-q47-47.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The fragment placed in the starred position (★) is 4 (エサを).
default.q.n2-30-q47-47.explanation:
Complete sentence: 朝、花に水をやり小鳥にエサをやってから出かけます。
Meaning: In the morning, I water the flowers and feed the birds before going out.
default.q.n2-30-q47-47.why.0: (a) 小鳥に: The noun marks the recipient of the action, feeding the birds, and comes second after the connecting clause 「水をやり」 (2).
default.q.n2-30-q47-47.why.1: (b) 水をやり: Immediately following 「花に」, it forms the phrase 「花に水をやり」. This is the conjunctive form formed by removing ます to connect successive actions, and it occupies position 1.
default.q.n2-30-q47-47.why.2: (c) やってから: The 「Vてから」 form (after doing V) of the verb 「やる」, placed fourth, immediately before the main verb 「出かけます」.
default.q.n2-30-q47-47.why.3: (d) エサを: The object meaning “food” combines with 「小鳥に」 (1) and 「やってから」 (3) to form 「小鳥にエサをやってから」, occupying the third position (the ★ slot).
default.q.n2-30-q48-48.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The ★ position is choice 4 (あったら).
default.q.n2-30-q48-48.explanation:
Complete sentence: コピー機に何か不具合あったら次の番号にご連絡ください。
Meaning: If there is any problem with the photocopier, please contact us at the following number.
default.q.n2-30-q48-48.why.0: (a) 不具合 is a noun meaning “malfunction” or “problem.” It follows the pronoun 「何か」(2) as the subject of 「あったら」(4), with the particle が omitted in casual speech, and occupies position 2.
default.q.n2-30-q48-48.why.1: (b) 何か is an indefinite pronoun in position 1 after 「コピー機に」, modifying the noun 「不具合」 (1): “some kind of malfunction.”
default.q.n2-30-q48-48.why.2: (c) 次の番号: the noun phrase referring to the contact telephone number, placed in position 4 to combine with the particle 「に」 in 「次の番号にご連絡ください」.
default.q.n2-30-q48-48.why.3: (d) あったら: The conditional 「たら」 form of 「ある」 (“if there is/are”), ending the hypothetical conditional clause and occupying the third position (the ★ slot).
default.q.n2-30-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1. The starred position (★) is answer choice 3 (うちに).
default.q.n2-30-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 台風が近づいているので電車が止まらないうちに帰宅するよう言われた。
Meaning: Because a typhoon is approaching, I was told to go home before the trains stop running.
default.q.n2-30-q49-49.why.0: (a) 帰宅するよう stands fourth, before「言われた」, in the indirect-request pattern「Vる + よう（に）言われる」(to be told to...).
default.q.n2-30-q49-49.why.1: (b) 電車が: It stands at the beginning of the subordinate clause in position 1, serving as the subject marked by「が」for the predicate「止まらない」(4).
default.q.n2-30-q49-49.why.2: (c) うちに: It follows the negative form 「止まらない」 (4) according to the grammar pattern 「Vない + うちに」 (before or while something has not yet happened), occupying the third position (★).
default.q.n2-30-q49-49.why.3: (d) 止まらない: the negative verb is in the second position, serving as the predicate for 「電車が」 (2) and modifying the noun 「うちに」 (3).
default.q.n2-30-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 本音 (the consumer's true thoughts or genuine opinion).
default.q.n2-30-q50-50.explanation: In the context of a passage about researching and analyzing public opinion online (Social Listening / Text Mining), companies are very interested in understanding consumers' "true feelings" or "actual thoughts" (本音) behind their posts and comments, rather than merely their polite remarks. Therefore, 「本音」in answer choice 2 is the most accurate choice.
default.q.n2-30-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「うそ」(a lie, falsehood) has a negative meaning and does not reflect the purpose of tools for analyzing customer opinions.
default.q.n2-30-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「本音」(one's true feelings, genuine thoughts/emotions) is completely accurate and fits the context of analyzing consumers' true opinions on social media.
default.q.n2-30-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「式ポート」is an incorrect or meaningless expression in this context.
default.q.n2-30-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「ひょうろん」(評論: an academic commentary or critique) is unsuitable for referring to the actual thoughts and opinions of the majority of consumers.
default.q.n2-30-q51-51.explanation: Blank 51 serves as a link between the sentence introducing the problem's context and the following sentence analyzing the data-processing mechanism. Choice 4 provides the most logical and cohesive transition in this context.
default.q.n2-30-q51-51.why.0: (a) Choice 1 does not fit the context connecting the sentences in the passage.
default.q.n2-30-q51-51.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect in terms of grammatical structure and logical flow.
default.q.n2-30-q51-51.why.2: (c) Choice 3 does not correctly express the connection between the clauses.
default.q.n2-30-q51-51.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is the correct answer because it connects the preceding and following sentences most coherently and naturally.
default.q.n2-30-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 辞書に従ってシステムが判断していく (the system makes judgments automatically based on the dictionary).
default.q.n2-30-q52-52.explanation: The passage explains how opinions are automatically classified: the computer uses a labeled vocabulary database (辞書 - a dictionary for classifying items as positive or negative). The entity reviewing and evaluating large numbers of texts here is the technology system (システム), so only choice 2, “辞書に従ってシステムが判断していく,” accurately reflects this technical context.
default.q.n2-30-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「読み手が判断していく」 (the reader makes judgments) is incorrect in terms of the agent performing the action, because the passage is describing an automated process handled by a software system.
default.q.n2-30-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「辞書に従ってシステムが判断していく」 (“the system makes judgments according to the dictionary”) is completely correct both in terms of the subject (the system: システム) and the basis used for judgment (the dictionary specifying words of praise and criticism: 辞書).
default.q.n2-30-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「書き手に従って読み手が判断していく」is completely incorrect both in its basis (following the author) and its subject (the reader), and does not express the nature of automatic processing.
default.q.n2-30-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「書き手に従ってシステムが判断していく」 (the system makes judgments by following the writer) is illogical because a mechanical system must rely on rules or a dictionary (辞書) established in advance; it cannot independently “follow” the writer’s consciousness.
default.q.n2-30-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 中立 (neutral, in an intermediate position).
default.q.n2-30-q53-53.explanation: In sentiment analysis, feedback data is divided into 3 standard categories: positive (プラス), negative (マイナス), and neutral (中立). When a sentence or expression is not clearly favorable or unfavorable, the system classifies it as “neutral” (中立), so answer 3 is correct.
default.q.n2-30-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「すばらしい」 (wonderful) is a specific adjective with a positive meaning; it is not the name of an evaluative category parallel to プラス/マイナス.
default.q.n2-30-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「プラス」(positive/additive) is an evaluative term expressing praise. Since it has already been mentioned, it cannot represent a neutral state.
default.q.n2-30-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「中立」(neutral) is a noun describing an intermediate, in-between state. It fits perfectly and completes the three-part classification: プラス (positive) - マイナス (negative) - 中立 (neutral).
default.q.n2-30-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「マイナス」 (“negative,” “minus”) expresses a critical evaluation, not a neutral state between two sides.
default.q.n2-30-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 余地があるという (it is said that there is still room/potential for improvement).
default.q.n2-30-q54-54.explanation: In the final sentence, the author summarizes the current limitation of technology (it cannot yet perfectly process sarcasm and complex implied meanings) while also asserting that there is still considerable room for improvement in the future. The phrase 『改善の余地がある』 (there is room for improvement) is the most common and accurate expression in academic and journalistic Japanese, combined with 『という』 to quote a general opinion or assessment.
default.q.n2-30-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「〜ことは不可能である」(be completely impossible...) expresses an absolute negative assertion, so it does not fit a context evaluating the potential for technological development.
default.q.n2-30-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「余地があるという」naturally combines with the established expression 『〜の余地がある』 (there is still room or potential for improvement), presenting an objective assessment of the system's potential for development.
default.q.n2-30-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「はずである」(should certainly be, is expected to be) is used for an inference based on common sense and does not naturally accompany a phrase expressing potential for improvement.
default.q.n2-30-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「はずはない」 (there is absolutely no way) is an absolute negative, completely contrary to the passage’s spirit of opening up a possible solution for the future.
default.q.n2-30-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 衛生管理やすし文化の知識を身につけてもらうため (To equip foreign chefs and staff with knowledge of hygiene management and sushi culture).
default.q.n2-30-q55-55.explanation:
- Main point: As sushi has become increasingly popular overseas, Japan's National Federation of Sushi Sanitation Associations introduced an international certification program called "すし知識海外認定制度" (Overseas Sushi Knowledge Certification Program). Its main purpose is to equip and educate foreign chefs and staff with accurate knowledge of sushi culture and strict sanitation practices, such as how to store fish, washing the cutting board after each use, and the antibacterial effects of vinegar and wasabi.

- Question translation: Why was the "Overseas Sushi Knowledge Certification Program" started?
- Answer choices:
  1. To test and confirm foreign chefs' knowledge related to sushi.
  2. To help them acquire knowledge of sanitation management and sushi culture.
  3. To increase the number of foreign sushi chefs overseas.
  4. To promote sushi culture even more widely overseas.
default.q.n2-30-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the purpose of the examination is not to "check or confirm" (確認するため) the foreign chefs' existing knowledge, but to equip them with accurate knowledge and disseminate it to them (身につけてもらう / 普及させる).
default.q.n2-30-q55-55.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage directly states the objective: 「外国人の職人や店員らに正しい知識を身につけてもらおうと...国際検定『すし知識海外認定制度』をスタートさせる」 and 「衛生管理の方法や『すし文化』など正しい知識を普及させるのが狙い」 The aim is to spread accurate knowledge, including hygiene-management methods and sushi culture.
default.q.n2-30-q55-55.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage never mentions “increasing the number of foreign sushi chefs” (外国人のすし職人を増やすため); it emphasizes improving quality and knowledge of food hygiene and safety.
default.q.n2-30-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect because sushi is already highly popular overseas (海外ですしの人気が高まる中). The purpose of the certification system is not simply to promote Japanese culture (広めるため); its central aim is to provide people with accurate knowledge and ensure hygiene and safety (正しい知識を身につけてもらう).
default.q.n2-30-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3: When speaking, one should focus on the main points and speak concisely.
default.q.n2-30-q56-56.explanation:
- Main point of the passage: The author points out that a mistake in giving a speech is trying to use up all the allotted time. Just as eating until you are eight-tenths full is considered healthy, a speech should also stop at about eight-tenths, ending while the audience is still eager to hear more. The speaker should omit lengthy greetings and preliminaries, get straight to the main subject, and finish at the most engaging moment.

- Question translation: What is the author mainly trying to say in this passage?

- Answer choices:
1. When giving a speech, you must adhere exactly to the allotted time.
2. Before giving a speech, you must not eat until your stomach is full.
3. When giving a speech, you should focus on the main points and keep it concise.
4. When giving a speech, you do not need to worry about seniority.
default.q.n2-30-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage advises against trying to use all the allotted time (「その十五分を目いっぱい使おうと思うからだ」is the reason for failure); instead, one should finish earlier, at about 80% completion.
default.q.n2-30-q56-56.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The statement “eating until you are 80% full is good for the body” (腹八分目が体にいい) is only a metaphor advising the speaker to end the speech at an appropriate point, not advice about eating before giving a speech.
default.q.n2-30-q56-56.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「「高い所から」「先輩をさしおいて」などの修辞は省いていきなり本論に入り、スピーチのいちばん盛り上がったところでサンキュー・ベリー・マッチとやめてしまえばよいのだ」 (Omit rhetorical introductions such as “from a high position” and “setting aside one's seniors,” get straight to the main point, and stop with “Thank you very much” at the most exciting part of the speech) and 「スピーチも八割でやめておけばよい」 (A speech should also end at about 80%, because it works well when the audience still wants to hear more).
default.q.n2-30-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author only says to omit introductory rhetorical phrases such as “with your permission, senior...,” so as to get straight to the point; the author does not say that one need not consider the status of seniors and juniors.
default.q.n2-30-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 3: A souvenir that shows an understanding of the recipient’s preferences, such as a gift of stationery, brings the greatest joy and meaning.
default.q.n2-30-q57-57.explanation:
Main point:
The author emphasizes that the true meaning of a souvenir (お土産) lies in understanding and caring about the recipient's interests. When people receive a gift that matches their tastes, such as stationery exchanged among people who share a passion for paper, they not only have something enjoyable to talk about but also experience multiplied joy as they excitedly imagine how to use the gift.

Translation of the question:
What does the author most want to say?

Translation of the answer choices:
1. Because of the nature of their profession, when giving a gift to someone who likes paper, one should always choose paper with a classic design...
2. As for souvenirs, when returning from Hawaii, it is best to buy a whole box of macadamia nuts at Narita Airport...
3. Like the paper received after a trip to France, a souvenir is best when it demonstrates an understanding of the recipient...
4. Since you never know when you will give a souvenir to someone, you should buy plenty in advance during your everyday life...
default.q.n2-30-q57-57.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage only discusses the joy of people who share an interest in paper; it does not advise always choosing paper with a classic design (クラシックなデザイン).
default.q.n2-30-q57-57.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because buying an entire bulk box of macadamia nuts at the airport is merely an example of buying souvenirs casually. It does not demonstrate the thoughtfulness or understanding of the recipient that the author values.
default.q.n2-30-q57-57.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage states: 「紙好き同士、お土産話に花が咲いた。注て、これをどう使おうと想像を巡らす楽しみも加えて、幾重にも喜びが増す。」 This shows that a gift matching the recipient’s interests and chosen with that person in mind brings the fullest and deepest joy.
default.q.n2-30-q57-57.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage contains no information advising readers to buy and stock up on large quantities of souvenirs every day.
default.q.n2-30-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Broaden one's perspective and use the information obtained to form one's own thoughts.
default.q.n2-30-q58-58.explanation:
Summary: The author believes that if you keep reading only one newspaper, your thinking will unconsciously become fixed. You should read different newspapers to take in multiple perspectives, broaden your outlook, and use the information you gather to form your own independent opinions. That is what “information literacy in the true sense” means.

Question: What does “information literacy in the true sense” mean?
Answer choices:
1. Broadening your outlook and forming your own opinions based on the information you obtain.
2. Reading different newspapers and selecting useful information.
3. Being able to accept differing opinions.
4. Reading many newspapers and learning about many different kinds of information.
default.q.n2-30-q58-58.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「広い視野を形成するには複眼的思考が大切です。違った角度からものを見る習慣をつけ、ときには問題意識を持ち、得た情報から自分なりの考えを持つ。こうした本当の意味での情報力を身につけることが...」 “True information literacy” means developing a multifaceted perspective, broadening one’s outlook, and forming one’s own ideas from the information one obtains.
default.q.n2-30-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not mention “selecting and filtering information” (取捨選択 / 取捨選抜).
default.q.n2-30-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Absorbing different opinions (異なった意見を吸収する) is only one part of developing multifaceted thinking; it is not the complete definition of “information literacy in the true sense.”
default.q.n2-30-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Simply knowing a lot of information is not enough; the author emphasizes that the key is to use that information to form one's own ideas (自分なりの考えを持つ).
default.q.n2-30-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 1: a 警備犬 that searches for survivors at a disaster site (a service dog that searches for survivors at the scene of a disaster).
default.q.n2-30-q59-59.explanation:
• Summary: The passage distinguishes two groups of police dogs by how they use their sense of smell. Dogs from the Forensic Investigation Division (鑑識課の犬) use 「地鼻」, a method of tracking scents close to the ground, to pursue suspects at crime scenes. Security dogs (警備犬), on the other hand, use 「高流鼻」, a method of detecting scents carried through the air, to search for survivors at disaster sites or detect explosives at airports.
• Translation of the question: What does «高流鼻» refer to?
• Translation of the answer choices:
1. Security dogs searching for survivors at a disaster site.
2. Security dogs tracking a suspect at a crime scene.
3. Security dogs of a high-nosed breed searching for explosives at an airport...
4. Security dogs of a high-nosed breed tracking a suspect at a crime scene.
default.q.n2-30-q59-59.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage says: 「災害現場で生存者を探したり、空港などで爆発物を見つけたりする『警備犬』」 and 「一方、空気中に漂う人や爆発物のにおいをかぎ取る警備犬は『高流鼻』だ」. Thus, «高流鼻» refers to the ability of working security dogs to detect scents in the air while searching for survivors or explosives.
default.q.n2-30-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Tracking a suspect at a crime scene (「事件現場で犯人を追う」) is the duty of dogs from the identification unit (「鑑識課の犬」), which use ground-level scent tracking (「地鼻」), not police guard dogs.
default.q.n2-30-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. «高流鼻» is a technical term for the way the nose is used to detect airflow, not a physical feature or a dog breed with a high nasal bridge (「鼻が高い犬種」).
default.q.n2-30-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice gets both elements wrong: it misinterprets «高流鼻» as a dog breed with a high nose (「鼻が高い犬種」) and wrongly assigns it the task of chasing criminals, which belongs to police dogs («地鼻»).
default.q.n2-30-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 2. さまざまな商品を売っている。
default.q.n2-30-q60-60.explanation:
- Translation of the question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate reason for calling a vending machine a robot?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. It can work like a human.
  2. It sells many different kinds of products.
  3. It can calculate money.
  4. It can talk.
- Summary of the relevant passage: The passage defines a robot as a machine that autonomously takes over human labor («人の労働を自律的に肩代わりする機械»). A vending machine accepts money, dispenses products, calculates change, and even calls out to customers like a salesperson; in other words, it replaces human labor. Selling many different kinds of products merely describes the variety of products and is not the reason it is defined as a robot.
default.q.n2-30-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage describes a robot as a machine that autonomously takes over human labor («人の労働を自律的に肩代わりする機械»), and vending machines are performing the work of selling in place of people («まさに販売という労働を、人に代わって行っているわけだ»).
default.q.n2-30-q60-60.why.1: (b) This choice was selected because selling a wide variety of items—water, tickets, rice, eggs, and so on—is merely evidence of the variety of goods sold automatically. It is not the criterion or reason for calling the machine a robot. The passage states: «「人の労働を自律的に肩代わりする機械」という一般的なロボットの定義に従えば、自動販売機も立派なロボットなのだ».
default.q.n2-30-q60-60.why.2: (c) Not chosen because the passage clearly states that the vending machine can calculate the amount and even return change when necessary («必要であればきちんと計算してお釣りまで返す»).
default.q.n2-30-q60-60.why.3: (d) Not selected because the passage gives the example that DyDo's machine can even sell drinks in a merchant-like Osaka accent, mixing in sales talk such as 「冷たーい飲み物どうですか」「お釣り忘れんといてや～」.
default.q.n2-30-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ロボットコンビニには、店員はいない。
default.q.n2-30-q61-61.explanation:
- Question translation: Which of the following is true about the “robot convenience store”?
- Answer choices:
  1. There are no sales staff at the robot convenience store.
  2. Humanoid robots sell merchandise at the robot convenience store.
  3. Visitors can also enter a hot spring bath at the robot convenience store.
  4. There is nothing that cannot be purchased at the robot convenience store.
- Summary of the relevant passage: The author explains that a “robot convenience store” is a store without staff that gathers every kind of vending machine in one place («あらゆる種類の自販機を無人の店舗内に集めた»), so there are no sales staff at all.
default.q.n2-30-q61-61.why.0: (a) Correct because the passage clearly states that a robot convenience store is a place where all kinds of vending machines are gathered inside an unmanned store (Quote: «最近はそうしたあらゆる種類の自販機を無人の店舗内に集めた、いわば「 ロボットコンビニ 」まで現れた»).
default.q.n2-30-q61-61.why.1: (b) Not chosen because this is a store bringing together 「あらゆる種類の自販機」 (all kinds of vending machines), not a place where humanoid robots sell things.
default.q.n2-30-q61-61.why.2: (c) Not selected because the passage only says that some places even sell hot-spring water through vending machines («場所によっては温泉の湯までもが自販機で買えてしまう»); it does not say that people can bathe in a hot spring at a robot-run convenience store.
default.q.n2-30-q61-61.why.3: (d) It is not selected because the passage only says that all kinds of products can be purchased through vending machines; it does not absolutely claim that there is nothing that cannot be purchased.
default.q.n2-30-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 2. The existence of convenience stores consisting only of various vending machines.
default.q.n2-30-q62-62.explanation:
- Question translation: Which is the most appropriate interpretation of "a story that would make people marvel"?
- Answer choices:
  1. Robots taking over human work is becoming widespread.
  2. Convenience stores exist that consist entirely of vending machines.
  3. Vending machines exist that sell a wide variety of drinks.
  4. Vending machines capable of speaking many dialects are being developed.
- Summary of the relevant passage: The phrase "a story that would make people marvel" appears immediately after a sentence describing the appearance of a "robot convenience store"—an unmanned store containing all kinds of vending machines. If people 100 years ago were told that such a convenience store made up entirely of automated machines existed, they would marvel at the progress of the 21st century.
default.q.n2-30-q62-62.why.0: (a) Not chosen because this is general information at the beginning of the passage, not a specific story directly connected immediately before 「感心しそうな話」.
default.q.n2-30-q62-62.why.1: (b) is correct because the phrase «感心しそうな話» directly refers to the appearance, in the immediately preceding sentence, of an unmanned convenience store made up entirely of vending machines (Excerpt: «最近はそうしたあらゆる種類の自販機を無人の店舗内に集めた、いわば「 ロボットコンビニ 」まで現れた。 100 年ぐらい前の人々に聞かせたら、「さすがは 21 世紀！」と 感心しそうな話 である»).
default.q.n2-30-q62-62.why.2: (c) Not selected because selling many kinds of beverages is merely an ordinary example, not a remarkable story of the times that would amaze and impress someone from 100 years ago.
default.q.n2-30-q62-62.why.3: (d) Not selected because the passage only mentions DyDo's machine joking in an Osaka accent as a minor example; it does not mention researching or developing a machine that speaks in various dialects.
default.q.n2-30-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「体の声」 refers to fatigue (疲れ)—an SOS signal from the body warning of illness before it develops.
default.q.n2-30-q63-63.explanation:
- Main point: The author explains that fatigue is an SOS warning signal sent by the body before illness develops—in other words, it is the "voice of the body" (体の声). If it is taken lightly or ignored, abnormalities gradually appear in the body and may eventually develop into illness.
- Translation of the question: What is the "voice of the body"?
- Translations of the choices:
1. Saying, "Ah, I'm so tired."
2. Fatigue
3. Illness
4. A feeling
default.q.n2-30-q63-63.why.0: (a) Not accurate. 「あー、疲れた」 is merely an unconscious utterance introduced by the author at the beginning to raise the issue; it is not the definition of 「体の声」.
default.q.n2-30-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「疲れとは、病気の手前で、体が発する SOS アラーム、つまり、「 体の声 」です。」 (Fatigue is an SOS alarm emitted by the body before illness, in other words, “the voice of the body.”)
default.q.n2-30-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage states: 「それがひどくなった状態が「病気」です」, meaning that illness is the condition that results when the body’s voice is ignored and the problem worsens, not the body’s voice itself.
default.q.n2-30-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「感覚」 is mentioned only later, when referring to a vague feeling people have when tired (漠然とした感覚); it is not the core definition of 「体の声」.
default.q.n2-30-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 1: This phrase refers to the body beginning to lose physical strength, accumulate fatigue more easily, and become more prone to illness or physical weakness.
default.q.n2-30-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point: The author contrasts healthy men in their 20s through early 30s with the period from their late 30s onward, when their bodies begin to "stop obeying them"—their health declines, fatigue builds up more easily, and they become more prone to illness. At that point, they are forced to pay attention to their bodies.
- Translation of the question: What condition is described by "the body begins to stop obeying you"?
- Translation of the choices:
1. The body accumulates fatigue more easily, and periods of poor health become more frequent.
2. Physical strength increases compared with one's 20s, and the body becomes less prone to fatigue.
3. One can no longer control one's emotions.
4. One can no longer hear voices or sounds clearly.
default.q.n2-30-q64-64.why.0: (a) Correct. 「体が言うことをきかなくなり始める」 describes the age-related decline in physical strength: after the latter half of one's thirties, the body no longer maintains the flexibility and vitality of one's twenties, becomes tired more easily, and is more prone to illness (「体に疲れがたまりやすくなり、体調を崩すことが増える」).
default.q.n2-30-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This choice says that physical strength increases and one becomes less prone to fatigue than at age 20, which is completely contrary to the passage.
default.q.n2-30-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect. This expression concerns the physical body and health (体), not the control of emotions or feelings (気持ち).
default.q.n2-30-q64-64.why.3: (d) Inaccurate. This is a mistaken literal interpretation of 「言うことをきく / 声」 as meaning that sounds cannot be heard clearly. In the context of the passage, it is an idiomatic expression referring to the body or physical condition no longer functioning as intended.
default.q.n2-30-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 「その数」refers to the number of ways men relieve fatigue (疲れを解消する方法の数).
default.q.n2-30-q65-65.explanation:
- Main point: The passage points out that men’s ways of relieving fatigue are usually monotonous—they simply lie down and rest or try to sleep—and that there are so few such methods that they can be counted on one hand (「片手で数えられるほど」).
- Question translation: What does “that number” refer to?
- Answer choices:
1. The number of men who develop illnesses after their late thirties
2. The number of people who pay attention to their bodies only after becoming ill
3. The number of ways men relieve fatigue
4. The number of people who develop diseases characteristic of modern civilization
default.q.n2-30-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage only says that men in the latter half of their thirties often begin paying attention to their bodies after developing an illness; 「その数」does not refer to the number of men who became ill.
default.q.n2-30-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This content is not the noun referred to earlier by the demonstrative expression「その数」.
default.q.n2-30-q65-65.why.2: (c) Correct. The preceding sentence states: 「疲れを解消する方法も、男性は、「じっと休む」とか、「とにかく寝る」など単純になりがちです。 その数は片手で数えられるほどではないでしょうか。」 The demonstrative 「その数」 directly refers to 「疲れを解消する方法」, meaning that men have very few ways of relieving fatigue—only a handful.
default.q.n2-30-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「現代文明特有の病気にかかる人の数」 appears in the concluding sentence to explain why few people know how to listen to their bodies; it is not what 「その数」 refers to.
default.q.n2-30-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The item is not 100% satisfactory, but it is heavily discounted.
default.q.n2-30-q66-66.explanation:
- Main idea: When shoppers see an item marked down substantially from its original listed price, they often feel that they are getting a bargain. As a result, they are more likely to compromise and buy items they do not actually like 100%.
- Translation of the question: What kind of items are people "likely to compromise on and buy"?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Everyday goods that are both reasonably priced and high-quality.
  2. Expensive brand-name goods discounted to less than half price.
  3. High-quality goods being sold for less than half their original listed price.
  4. Goods they are not 100% satisfied with but that are heavily discounted.
default.q.n2-30-q66-66.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not mention having to compromise when buying everyday goods that offer both a reasonable price and good quality.
default.q.n2-30-q66-66.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage does not mention expensive brand-name goods (「高価なブランド品」) at all.
default.q.n2-30-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because it only mentions a price reduction and does not express the essential meaning of “compromise”: accepting a purchase despite not being fully satisfied.
default.q.n2-30-q66-66.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because it matches the quotation: 「はじめの値段より大幅に値引きされていると、何か得した気分になって、少し気に入らないところがあっても妥協して買ってしまいがちです。」 When an item is heavily discounted from its original price, people feel they are getting a bargain and tend to compromise and buy it despite minor dislikes.
default.q.n2-30-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Because one would end up buying unnecessary things with no intended use.
default.q.n2-30-q67-67.explanation:
- Main idea: What seems like a bargain can actually become wasteful because, even if an item is inexpensive for its quality, you will ultimately never wear or use it if you do not genuinely like it. You end up spending money on unnecessary items with no practical purpose.
- Translation of the question: Why would it "instead become wasteful"?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Because buying things based only on their price will exceed your budget.
  2. Because you will buy unnecessary items that you never use.
  3. Because buying things that are not consumables is pointless and wasteful.
  4. Because even if you buy high-quality items at a low price, their quality may sometimes still be poor.
default.q.n2-30-q67-67.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not mention exceeding the spending budget (予算額を上回る).
default.q.n2-30-q67-67.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because it matches the quotation: 「品質のわりに値段が安くても、あまり気に入らないものだと着ないことになりがちです。賢く買ったつもりで、かえって浪費したことになります。」 (Even if something is inexpensive for its quality, if you do not really like it, you tend not to wear or use it, so what you thought was a smart purchase becomes wasteful instead.)
default.q.n2-30-q67-67.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author does not say that buying anything other than consumables is wasteful, but recommends carefully considering whether something is really needed before buying it.
default.q.n2-30-q67-67.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author clearly says that the goods are high quality for their price (品質のわりに値段が安い). The waste occurs because buyers do not like them and therefore do not use them, not because the quality is poor.
default.q.n2-30-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3: When buying something, one should not choose based on its price, but on whether one truly needs or wants it.
default.q.n2-30-q68-68.explanation:
- Main point: The author emphasizes that, to live neatly and avoid waste, consumable items may be purchased based on low price, but for other goods, one should not look only at the price. Before buying, one should carefully consider whether one genuinely likes or truly needs the item.
- Question translation: What does the author mainly want to say in this passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. Buying inexpensive items during a sale is a smart way to shop.
  2. Owning expensive, high-quality items can improve one’s character.
  3. When buying something, one should choose based on whether one needs it rather than on its price.
  4. End-of-season sale items are of poor quality, so one must be careful.
default.q.n2-30-q68-68.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author points out that buying discounted items just because they are cheap, without actually liking them, only leads to waste and is not smart at all.
default.q.n2-30-q68-68.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage never mentions buying expensive items to improve one’s character.
default.q.n2-30-q68-68.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the concluding sentence expresses the author's main idea: 「値段で買ってもいいのは消耗品だけ、そうでないものは厳しくチェックして本当に好きか必要か、吟味してから買いましょう。」 (Only consumable goods should be bought based on price; for everything else, carefully consider whether you truly like or need it before buying.)
default.q.n2-30-q68-68.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author does not say that end-of-season sale items are poor in quality; even good-quality items may go unused if the buyer does not like them.
default.q.n2-30-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: The boy has few friends and only goes out to have fun occasionally.
default.q.n2-30-q69-69.explanation:
- Relevant summary: The mother talks about her second-year university student son, who is very quiet and spends all his time in his room outside school hours. Even during summer vacation, he only leaves his room for the three meals. Although he does have friends, someone invites him out only about once a month. She thinks he is old enough to have freedom, but she cannot help worrying.
- Question translation: It says, "I feel worried." What is the mother worried about?
- Answer choices:
  1. Her son does not listen to his parents and only comes home at mealtimes.
  2. Her son never leaves his room, so she does not know what he is doing.
  3. Her son has few friends and rarely goes out for fun.
  4. His parents keep nagging him about various things.
default.q.n2-30-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the son does not stay away from home; rather, he spends almost all his time in his room at home («学校へ行く以外はほとんど自分の部屋で過ごしています»), not merely returning home at mealtimes.
default.q.n2-30-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage only says that the son leaves his room when it is time to eat; it does not mention that the mother “does not know what he is doing in his room.”
default.q.n2-30-q69-69.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: «学校へ行く以外はほとんど自分の部屋で過ごしています... 友達がゼロというわけでもないらしく、月に一度くらいは誘いが来て、出かけることもあります。» The mother is worried because her son is very withdrawn, spends almost all his time in his room, and has few friends; only occasionally—about once a month—does someone invite him out.
default.q.n2-30-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the mother thinks that her child has grown up and therefore says little («もう大人なのだから、親はよけいなことは言わず»), not that the parents constantly nag the child.
default.q.n2-30-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: A states an opinion from the advice seeker's standpoint, while B shows an understanding of the son's psychology and emotions.
default.q.n2-30-q70-70.explanation:
- Relevant summary:
  + Passage A: From the parents' concern that their child gets little exercise and has little interaction with others («親子の関係は難しいですね...»), it offers the practical advice that the parents should tactfully suggest that the child get a part-time job and interact with people.
  + Passage B: It shows an understanding of the son's feelings at this age («本当は親から独立したいと考えているのだと思われます。この年ごろにはだれもが経験することです»), explaining that he wants to become independent and advising the parents not to interfere but to wait patiently for him to open up.
- Translation of the question: Which of the following is correct about A and B's responses to the advice seeker's concern?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Both A and B say that the son is already an adult, so it is better to let him do as he wishes.
  2. Both A and B say that communication is important, so the parents should actively talk with him.
  3. A understands the son's feelings, whereas B gives an opinion from the advice seeker's point of view.
  4. A gives an opinion from the advice seeker's point of view, whereas B shows an understanding of the son's feelings.
default.q.n2-30-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because A does not recommend giving the child complete freedom; it suggests that parents tactfully introduce the idea of part-time work («それとなく、アルバイトをすすめるのがいいんじゃないでしょうか»), whereas only B recommends letting the child become independent without interference.
default.q.n2-30-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because B advises the parents not to interfere or pressure the child, but to wait until the child comes to them to discuss their worries («本人から悩みを相談して来るまで待つことをおすすめします»). B does not advise both sides to take the initiative and talk actively.
default.q.n2-30-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the roles are reversed: A is the parent viewing the situation from a worried perspective, while B is the one who understands the son’s desire for independence.
default.q.n2-30-q70-70.why.3: (d) Correct, as shown by the quotations: A speaks from the parents' standpoint, concerned about their child's health and communication, and suggests gentle intervention («親子の関係は難しいですね... それとなく、アルバイトをすすめるのがいいんじゃないでしょうか»); B, meanwhile, understands that a boy of this age wants to separate from or become independent of his parents («本当は親から独立したいと考えているのだと思われます。この年ごろにはだれもが経験することです»).
default.q.n2-30-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 努力は、かけた時間によって測定できる (Effort can be measured by the amount of time spent).
default.q.n2-30-q71-71.explanation:
- Question translation: At ( ★ ) is the statement that had a major impact on the author's life. Which statement is it?
- Answer choices:
  1. The value of effort lies in hiding it.
  2. If you make an effort, other people's evaluations will change.
  3. Effort can be measured by the amount of time spent.
  4. If you make an effort, you will also become better at managing your time.
- Main idea: At the beginning, the author mentions a statement they came up with themselves that changed their way of thinking, helping them stop feeling embarrassed about making an effort and live more easily. Throughout the essay, the author explains that the measure for objectifying effort is "time" (努力を客観視するための測定方法が「時間」なのです). Therefore, the key statement at (★) is "Effort can be measured by the amount of time spent."
default.q.n2-30-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author says that hiding one's efforts (努力を隠す) is very dangerous (とても危険), not something valuable.
default.q.n2-30-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author advises readers not to be swayed by other people's judgments; the purpose is not to make an effort to change those judgments.
default.q.n2-30-q71-71.why.2: (c) Correct, as shown by the sentences in the passage: 「そして、努力を客観視するための測定方法が「時間」なのです」「努力を時間で測定すれば...魔法の言葉なのです」, which state that effort is measured by converting it into time.
default.q.n2-30-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage discusses using time to measure and manage effort; it does not say that effort helps improve time-management skills.
default.q.n2-30-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 自分の努力の結果に対し、他人にいろいろ言われたり思われたりしたくないか (Because the person does not want others to comment on or judge the results of their efforts).
default.q.n2-30-q72-72.explanation:
- Question translation: According to the author, why do people "deliberately deny their own efforts"?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because they feel that effort is subjective and cannot be understood by others.
  2. Because they do not want others to make comments about or judge the results of their efforts.
  3. Because they think their efforts are insufficient compared with those of others and that they need to work harder.
  4. Because, by revealing that they made an effort, they want others to see them as humble.
- Main point: The author points out people's fear of others' attention and judgment: if they fail to achieve results, they fear being mocked as having "tried so hard and still failed," while if they succeed, they fear being told that success was inevitable after preparing so thoroughly. People therefore tend to conceal and deny their efforts because they fear comments and judgment about the results.
default.q.n2-30-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage gives the reason as beginning to worry about other people’s evaluations (他者の評価を気にし始めると), not because other people cannot understand one’s subjectivity.
default.q.n2-30-q72-72.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage directly states the reason: 「まず結果が出なかったとき「あいつ、あれだけやってダメだった」とバカにされるのを恐れます。結果が出ても「あれだけ準備すれば当然だ」と評価が下がるのを恐れます。他者の評価を気にし始めると、いずれにせよ努力を隠すに越したことはないわけです」.
default.q.n2-30-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention feeling that one's own efforts are insufficient compared with those of others.
default.q.n2-30-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the effort was downplayed out of fear of other people’s judgment, not in order to be praised by others as a modest person.
default.q.n2-30-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 何をどれだけ努力したかを確認しながら、努力自体を楽しむことが大切だ (What matters is to check what and how much we have worked on while enjoying the effort itself).
default.q.n2-30-q73-73.explanation:
- Translation of the question: What does the author say about “effort”?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Effort is subjective, so each person should decide for themselves how much effort is enough.
  2. Once people start working, it is better not to let others see them making an effort.
  3. To achieve good results, it is important to let others see that one is making an effort.
  4. It is important both to confirm what one has worked on and how much effort one has made, and to enjoy the process of making that effort.
- Main point: The author emphasizes the importance of creating a system that allows one to enjoy the process of making an effort (そのプロセスを楽しむ仕組み). At the same time, measuring effort in terms of time makes it easier to manage what one has worked on and for how long (自分がどこまで努力をしたのか、わかりやすく管理できるようになり), enabling one to make deliberate choices and give one’s best effort.
default.q.n2-30-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author recommends converting effort into time in order to make it objective and manage it clearly, not simply making a rough personal decision because effort is subjective.
default.q.n2-30-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The author criticizes hiding one’s efforts (努力を隠す対応はとても危険) and encourages people to speak confidently about the process of their efforts.
default.q.n2-30-q73-73.why.2: (c) is incorrect because the author never says that the key to achieving good results is displaying one’s efforts for others to see.
default.q.n2-30-q73-73.why.3: (d) Correct because it cites the following sentences from the passage: 「そのプロセスを楽しむ仕組みをつくらなければなりません」「自分がどこまで努力をしたのか、わかりやすく管理できるようになり」「何を努力するのか自分で考え、決めなければいけません」.
default.q.n2-30-q74-74.explanation:
Summary and meaning:
- Sato’s requirements:
  + The monthly payment should be as low as possible (毎月払う金額は安いほうがいい).
  + Since Sato regularly takes the train, the apartment should be as close to a station as possible; Sato does not own a car (いつも電車を使うので、駅から近いほうがいい。車は持っていない).
  + Since Sato lives alone, a small apartment is acceptable (一人で住むので、狭くてもいい).
- Comparing the apartments in the table:
  + Apartment C: ¥65,000 rent + ¥0 management fee = ¥65,000 per month; a 3-minute walk from the station (徒歩 3 分); 30 ㎡ (1DK).
  + Apartment F: ¥65,000 rent + ¥5,000 management fee = ¥70,000 per month; a 3-minute walk from the station.
  + Apartments B and E are large (60–65 ㎡), farther from the station, and cost more than ¥115,000 per month.
=> Therefore, apartment C is the best match for Sato’s requirements because it has the lowest monthly cost and is closest to the station.

Question translation: Which apartment best meets Sato’s requirements?
1. B
2. C
3. E
4. F
default.q.n2-30-q74-74.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 (B) is incorrect: Apartment B has a total monthly cost of 115,000 yen (115,000 yen in rent with no management fee) and is a 7-minute walk from the station, making it much more expensive and farther from the station than apartment C.
default.q.n2-30-q74-74.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 (C) is correct. According to the table, Apartment C has a rent of 65,000 yen and no management fee (管理費: なし), so its total monthly cost is only 65,000 yen—the lowest of all the apartments. It is a 3-minute walk from the station (徒歩 3 分), has an area of 30 ㎡ suitable for one person, and has no parking cost because the resident does not own a car.
default.q.n2-30-q74-74.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (E) is incorrect: Apartment E has total monthly costs of 128,000 yen (118,000 yen rent plus a 10,000-yen management fee) and is a 20-minute walk from the station, so it does not meet Sato's conditions at all.
default.q.n2-30-q74-74.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (F) is incorrect: Apartment F is also a 3-minute walk from the station, but its 5,000-yen management fee brings the total monthly cost to 70,000 yen (65,000 + 5,000), making it more expensive than Apartment C (65,000 yen).
default.q.n2-30-q75-75.explanation:
Summary & translation:
- Based on the regulations below the table:
  1. The security deposit (敷金) is expressed as a number of months' rent (賃料の「○か月」分).
  2. When moving in (入居ときには), you must pay one month's expenses—rent, management fee, and parking fee (1か月分の諸費用：賃料、管理費、駐車場料金)—together with the security deposit (敷金).
- Calculation of the move-in costs for apartment F with a parking space:
  + One month's rent (賃料): 65,000 yen.
  + One month's management fee (管理費): 5,000 yen.
  + One month's parking fee (駐車場料金): 18,000 yen.
  + Security deposit (敷金 = two months' rent): 65,000 × 2 = 130,000 yen.
  => Total amount due when moving in = (65,000 + 5,000 + 18,000) + 130,000 = 218,000 yen.

Translation of the question: If you rent room F and a parking space, how much must you pay when moving in?
1. 70,000 yen
2. 88,000 yen
3. 200,000 yen
4. 218,000 yen
default.q.n2-30-q75-75.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (70,000 円) is incorrect: this is only the one-month total of rent (65,000 yen) and the management fee (5,000 yen), excluding the parking fee and security deposit.
default.q.n2-30-q75-75.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (88,000 円) is incorrect: This is only the total of the first month’s expenses—rent, management fee, and parking fee (65,000 + 5,000 + 18,000 = 88,000 yen)—and does not include the deposit (敷金).
default.q.n2-30-q75-75.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (200,000 yen) is incorrect. This total combines the deposit (130,000 yen) with one month's rent and management fee (70,000 yen), but omits the parking fee of 18,000 yen.
default.q.n2-30-q75-75.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (218,000 円) is correct: Under rules 1 and 2, moving in requires one month’s initial costs (65,000 rent + 5,000 management fee + 18,000 parking fee = 88,000 yen) and a security deposit equal to two months’ rent (65,000 × 2 = 130,000 yen). Total: 88,000 + 130,000 = 218,000 yen.
default.q.n2-30-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 層 (富裕層: the wealthy class, affluent people).
default.q.n2-30-q11-11.explanation:
Meaning: People known as the upper class (the wealthy) make up 3% of the population.
- Sino-Japanese note: 富裕層 (ふゆうそう: the wealthy, affluent class).
- Example: この商品は富裕層をターゲットに開発された。(This product was developed for affluent customers.)
default.q.n2-30-q11-11.why.0: (a) 帯: a suffix indicating a zone or belt, as in 火山帯 (volcanic belt), or a range or period, as in 時間帯 (time slot) and 年齢帯 (age range). It does not combine with 富裕.
default.q.n2-30-q11-11.why.1: (b) 答: Means “answer” or “reply”; it is not used as a suffix forming a noun for a group of people.
default.q.n2-30-q11-11.why.2: (c) 人 means a person (e.g., 現代人 - modern person), but Japanese does not use 富裕人; it uses 富裕層 or 富裕な人.
default.q.n2-30-q11-11.why.3: (d) 層 (layer, stratum): A suffix referring to a social class or group of people (such as 富裕層 - the wealthy class, 貧困層 - the poor, 中間層 - the middle class, 若者層 - young people).
default.q.n2-30-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 並み (〜並み: at a comparable level, as usual/as in previous years).
default.q.n2-30-q12-12.explanation:
Meaning: This winter’s cold is about the same as in an ordinary year. Note: The question contains a typo, 紙年/寒注 instead of 例年/平年の寒さ.
- Sino-Japanese term: 並 (equal, comparable, on the same level).
- Example: 今年の冬のボーナスは例年並みの支給額だった。(This winter’s bonus was about the same amount as usual.)
default.q.n2-30-q12-12.why.0: (a) 同じ: this adjective means “same” and cannot directly follow a noun marking a point in time; the structure と同じ is required.
default.q.n2-30-q12-12.why.1: (b) 並み: a suffix attached to nouns meaning “at the same level as, at the ordinary level,” as in 例年並み/平年並み (as usual), 人並み (like an ordinary person), and プロ並み (at a professional level).
default.q.n2-30-q12-12.why.2: (c) 位い means “approximately” or “about,” but it is not used as a suffix indicating a weather level comparable to that of previous years.
default.q.n2-30-q12-12.why.3: (d) 通り: Means “exactly as” or “according to,” as in 予定通り (“as scheduled”) and 予想通り (“as expected”). It does not indicate a temperature’s degree relative to the annual standard.
default.q.n2-30-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 制 (全寮制: a system in which all students live in dormitories; a fully residential school).
default.q.n2-30-q13-13.explanation:
Meaning: This school operates under a full boarding-school system, with all students living in dormitories.
- Vocabulary: 全寮制 (a system in which all students live in dormitories).
- Example: その高校は全寮制で、生徒全員が寮生活を送っている。(That high school is a full boarding school, and all the students live in dormitories.)
default.q.n2-30-q13-13.why.0: (a) 型 (type, model): A suffix indicating a model, mold, or design, as in 新型 (new model), 大型 (large-sized), and 血液型 (blood type). It is not used for an organizational system or structure.
default.q.n2-30-q13-13.why.1: (b) 制 (せい): a suffix indicating a “system or regulated scheme” (such as 全寮制, an all-residential system; 会員制, a membership system; and 予約制, a reservation system).
default.q.n2-30-q13-13.why.2: (c) 系: a suffix indicating a system, field, or academic stream, as in 理系 and 文系; it does not combine to form 全寮系.
default.q.n2-30-q13-13.why.3: (d) 統: It indicates continuity or a system in vocabulary such as 系統 and 伝統, and is not used as a suffix after 全寮.
default.q.n2-30-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 高 (売上高: sales revenue, total sales amount).
default.q.n2-30-q14-14.explanation:
Meaning: Approximately how much is the company's sales revenue (the prompt says 社会/当社)?
- Sino-Japanese reading: 売上高 (total sales, sales revenue).
- Example: 今年度の売上高は前年比で 10 ％増加した。(This fiscal year's sales revenue increased by 10% compared with last year.)

default.q.n2-30-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is question 2: 実際の生活は、想像していたのとは違った。

• Common expressions: 想像がつく (to be able to imagine), 想像を超える (to exceed one's imagination), 想像を絶する (to be beyond imagination).

default.q.n2-30-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect usage: To create a new game oneself, use 「考案した」 (to devise), 「開発した」 (to develop), or 「創作した」 (to create), not 「想像した」 (to imagine).
default.q.n2-30-q30-30.why.1: Correct usage: 「想像する」 means to picture or imagine something in one’s mind. This sentence describes reality turning out differently from what the speaker had imagined beforehand.
default.q.n2-30-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect usage: To describe a creative or original painting, use the adjectives「独創的な」or「創造的な」; Japanese does not use「想像的な絵」.
default.q.n2-30-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect usage: To make a plan for living, use 「計画を立てて」 or 「見通しを立てて」; the combination 「想像を立てる」 does not exist.
default.q.n2-30-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 3: もっと高齢者を いたわって ほしい。

default.q.n2-30-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect usage: 「いたわる」 is a transitive verb meaning to care for or show consideration to another person. To describe a dog sleeping peacefully, curled up, use 「丸くなって」 or 「気持ちよさそうに」.
default.q.n2-30-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect usage. For caring for flowers and plants in a garden, use「かわいがって」,「大切にして」, or「心を込めて」. 「いたわる」is mainly used for people or tired body parts.
default.q.n2-30-q31-31.why.2: Correct: 「いたわる（労る）」 means to treat someone with care, look after them, and show thoughtful concern, especially toward vulnerable people such as the elderly, sick people, or subordinates.
default.q.n2-30-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect. Injuring one’s leg while kicking a ball is expressed with 「痛めて（いためて）」(injure or hurt), not 「労る」.

default.q.n2-30-q32-32.explanation:
「ひりひり」 is an adverb / mimetic word describing a localized burning or stinging sensation on the skin or mucous membranes (from burns, sunburn, or abrasions), or a tongue-searing spicy sensation (from chili peppers, mustard, or pepper).
• Common phrases: 傷口がひりひり痛む (a wound stings), 辛いものを食べて舌がひりひりする (your tongue burns after eating spicy food).
• Another example: 熱湯がかかって、手がひりひりと痛む。(Hot water splashed on my hand, making it sting.)
default.q.n2-30-q32-32.why.0: Correct usage: 「ひりひり」 describes a stinging, burning sensation on the skin caused by sunburn (日に焼けて), a burn, or salt rubbed into it.
default.q.n2-30-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect usage: The impatient, irritated feeling caused by a train that never arrives should be expressed with 「いらいらした」 or 「やきもきした」, not 「ひりひり」.
default.q.n2-30-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect usage: The startled, frightened feeling when one nearly gets hit by a car should be expressed with 「ひやりとした」, 「はっとした」, or 「ぞっとした」, not 「ひりひり」.
default.q.n2-30-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect. 「ひりひり」describes a tongue-searing spicy sensation, such as from chili peppers or pepper, or a stinging, burning pain. It is not used for eating sweet candy; for sensitive or aching teeth, use 「ズキズキ」or 「しみる」.
default.q.n2-30-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 4. いとなんで.
default.q.n2-30-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: The traditional Japanese confectionery shop has been in business / operating for 300 years.
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 営 (business, management, operation).
- Example: 彼は父の後を継いで、貿易会社を営んでいる。(He took over from his father and runs a trading company.)
default.q.n2-30-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「やんで」: Incorrect. It is the te-form of「病む／止む」(to become ill / to stop or let up), not the reading of「営む」.
default.q.n2-30-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「はぐくんで」: Incorrect; this is the te-form of the verb 「育む」 (to nurture, foster).
default.q.n2-30-q1-1.why.2: (c) 「えいんで」: Incorrect. 「営」 has the on-reading 「えい」, as in 経営 (けいえい), but the native Japanese verb form is not read 「えいむ」.
default.q.n2-30-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「いとなんで」: Correct. The verb「営む」(いとなむ: to conduct or run a business) becomes「営んで」in the te-form.
default.q.n2-30-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2. やとって.
default.q.n2-30-q2-2.explanation:
Sentence meaning: That store is hiring 30 part-time employees.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 雇 (KO - to hire, employ).
- Example: 新しいプロジェクトのために優秀なプログラマーを雇った。(We hired an excellent programmer for the new project.)
default.q.n2-30-q2-2.why.0: (a) 「かこって」: Incorrect; it is the te-form of the verb 「囲う」, meaning “to surround; enclose.”
default.q.n2-30-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「やとって」: Correct. The verb 「雇う」(やとう - CỐ: to hire or employ someone) takes the te-form 「雇って」.
default.q.n2-30-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「とって」: Incorrect; it is the te-form of 「取る／採る／撮る」, meaning “to take; pick; photograph,” and so on.
default.q.n2-30-q2-2.why.3: (d) 「こって」: Incorrect. 「こる」 is usually written 「凝る」 (to be absorbed in something, congeal, or have stiff shoulders); it is not the reading of 「雇う」.
default.q.n2-30-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ねらって.
default.q.n2-30-q3-3.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The team is training hard with the aim of winning the championship.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 狙 (そ: aim at, target).
- Example: 彼は次の大会で金メダルを狙っている。(He is aiming for a gold medal at the next competition.)
default.q.n2-30-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「したくって」: Incorrect. The noun「支度」(preparation) combines with「する」as「支度して」; there is no verb「したく・る」.
default.q.n2-30-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「になって」: Incorrect. It is the te-form of the verb 「担う」(になう: to take on, shoulder responsibility).
default.q.n2-30-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「ねらって」: Correct. The verb 「狙う」 (ねらう, to aim at or target something) becomes 「狙って」 in the te-form.
default.q.n2-30-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「きまって」: Incorrect; this is the te-form of 「決まる」 (to be decided, be fixed).
default.q.n2-30-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 4. こうち.
default.q.n2-30-q4-4.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Japan also uses mountainous areas as farmland.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 耕地 (KŌCHI - cultivated land, farmland).
- Example: 耕地面積を増やすために森林を開拓する。(Forests are cleared to expand the area of farmland.)
default.q.n2-30-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「はたち」: Incorrect. 「はたち」 means 20 years old (二十歳), while a field for growing crops is 「はたけ」(畑).
default.q.n2-30-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「ていち」: Incorrect.「ていち」is the reading of「低地」(lowland) or「定地」, not「耕地」.
default.q.n2-30-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Agricultural land is「農地」(のうち - 農地); the kanji「耕」does not have the reading「の」.
default.q.n2-30-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「こうち」: Correct. 「耕」(on-reading こう) combines with「地」(on-reading ち) to form「耕地」(こうち: farmland).
default.q.n2-30-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. とる.
default.q.n2-30-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: Picking or collecting plants here is prohibited.
- Kanji reading and meaning: 採 (THẢI - to pick, collect, select).
- Distinguishing the homophones とる:
  + 採る: pick vegetables or fruit, catch insects, select personnel.
  + 取る: take or pick up ordinary objects.
  + 撮る: take photographs or shoot video.
  + 捕る: catch animals or fish.
- Example: 山で山菜を採る。(Pick edible wild plants in the mountains.)
default.q.n2-30-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「とる」: Correct. The verb「採る」(とる) is used with plants or insects to mean “pick,” “gather,” or “catch.”
default.q.n2-30-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「おる」: Incorrect. It is the reading of「折る」(to break, fold) or「織る」(to weave fabric).
default.q.n2-30-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「きる」: Incorrect; this is the reading of 「切る／斬る」(to cut, to slash).
default.q.n2-30-q5-5.why.3: (d) 「かる」: Incorrect; it is the reading of「刈る」(to reap rice, to trim grass or plants).
default.q.n2-30-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 保つ (たもつ: to maintain, to preserve).
default.q.n2-30-q6-6.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: "Maintaining good health is difficult."
- Kanji meaning: 保 means to maintain, preserve, or keep.
- Example: 平和を保つために努力する。(Make an effort to maintain peace.)
default.q.n2-30-q6-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「持つ」 is read as もつ (to hold, carry, have), not たもつ.
default.q.n2-30-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「補」 is commonly used in the verb 補う (おぎなう: to supplement, make up for); there is no conjugated form 「補つ」.
default.q.n2-30-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「留」 is commonly read as とめる (留める) or とまる (留まる); there is no word 「留つ」.
default.q.n2-30-q6-6.why.3: (d) Correct. 「保つ」 (ほつ) has the kun-reading たもつ and means to maintain or preserve a state, such as one's health, distance, or condition.
default.q.n2-30-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 慎重 (しんちょう: cautious, careful).
default.q.n2-30-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: “Since it is an important document, please handle it carefully.”
- Sino-Japanese components: 慎 (careful, cautious) + 重 (important, careful).
- Example: 慎重に検討した上で決定します。(We will make a decision after careful consideration.)
default.q.n2-30-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「真長」 uses the wrong kanji combination and does not form a vocabulary word meaning “cautious.”
default.q.n2-30-q7-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「慎長」 mistakenly replaces 「重」 (じゅう / ちょう) with 「長」 (ちょう) because they share the same on-reading.
default.q.n2-30-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「信重」 confuses 「慎」 (しん) with 「信」 (しん); they have the same on-reading.
default.q.n2-30-q7-7.why.3: (d) Correct. 「慎重」 (THẬN TRỌNG) is read しんちょう and means acting or thinking carefully and cautiously, without rushing.
default.q.n2-30-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 慣習 (かんしゅう: customs, conventions).
default.q.n2-30-q8-8.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “According to the village’s customs, the festival is held every year.”
- Kanji note: 慣習 combines 慣 (familiarity or custom) and 習 (habit or practice).
- Example: 古くからの慣習に従う。(Follow long-standing customs.)
default.q.n2-30-q8-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「観衆」(かんしゅう) is a homophone, but it means spectators or an audience.
default.q.n2-30-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「監修」 (on-reading: カンシュウ) is a homophone but means supervision or responsibility for specialist direction and editing.
default.q.n2-30-q8-8.why.2: (c) Correct. 「慣習」 (かんしゅう) means a custom, convention, or established practice that has developed over a long period in a society or community.
default.q.n2-30-q8-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「慣衆」 is an incorrectly formed compound and does not exist as a Japanese word.
default.q.n2-30-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 経ちました (たちました: time passed, a period of time elapsed).
default.q.n2-30-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: "It has been three years since I came to Japan."
- Sino-Japanese reading: 経 (KEI — to pass, elapse).
- Example: あれからもう10年が経った。(Ten years have already passed since then.)
