default.q.n2-30-q9-9.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「立ちました」means to stand up or erect something, and is not used for time passing.
default.q.n2-30-q9-9.why.1: (b) Correct. 「経ちました」 (read たちました; dictionary form 経つ) is specifically used to express the passage of time.
default.q.n2-30-q9-9.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「建ちました」 (the dictionary form of 建つ) is used for buildings and other structures being built.
default.q.n2-30-q9-9.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「発ちました」 (read たちました; dictionary form 発つ) means to depart or leave a place.
default.q.n2-30-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 素直 (すなお: obedient, docile, willing to listen).
default.q.n2-30-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: “Bright and obedient/easygoing in personality.”
- Kanji components: 素 (plain, pure) + 直 (straightforward, honest).
- Example: 自分の非を素直に認める。(Honestly admit one’s own fault.)
default.q.n2-30-q10-10.why.0: (a) Correct. 「素直」 is read すなお and describes someone gentle, obedient, honest, and not stubborn.
default.q.n2-30-q10-10.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「正直」 is read しょうじき and means honest or truthful; it is not read すなお.
default.q.n2-30-q10-10.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「実直」(実直) is read じっちょく and means honest, upright, and serious; it is not read すなお.
default.q.n2-30-q10-10.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「奏直」 mistakenly replaces 「素」 with 「奏」 (そう) because the kanji look similar; this word does not exist.
default.q.n2-31-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1. だけ, because the pattern 「好きなだけ」 means “as much as one likes.”
default.q.n2-31-q33-33.explanation:
Translation: "Please don't be shy—eat as much as you like."
遠慮 means hesitation, reserve, or holding back.
Example: 食べたいだけ食べてもいいですよ。(You may eat as much as you like.)
default.q.n2-31-q33-33.why.0: (a) Correct: The structure「好きなだけ」(or V-たいだけ) expresses the maximum extent one desires, meaning “as much as one likes” or “to one’s heart’s content.”
default.q.n2-31-q33-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「ほど」expresses a comparative degree or the “the more..., the more...” structure (〜ば〜ほど); 「好きなほど」cannot mean “as much as one likes.”
default.q.n2-31-q33-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「ぐらい」indicates an approximate degree or extent, and does not combine with「好き」to express freedom of choice regarding quantity.
default.q.n2-31-q33-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「ばかり」 means all or only, or indicates that something has just been done; it does not mean “to one's heart's content.”
default.q.n2-31-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 先立って, because the grammar pattern 「N に先立って」means “before carrying out” an event or major or important project.
default.q.n2-31-q34-34.explanation:
Translation: Before the waste-processing facility was built, an information session for residents was held.
Vocabulary and kanji-based meanings: 処理場 (processing facility), 建設 (construction), 住民 (residents), 説明会 (information session).
Example: 新商品の発売に先立って、展示会が開催された。(An exhibition was held before the launch of the new product.)
default.q.n2-31-q34-34.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜にしたがって」 means “as,” “in accordance with,” or “the more..., the more...” and does not indicate a time point before an event.
default.q.n2-31-q34-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜にかけて」 means “from...to...” for a range of space or time, so it does not fit.
default.q.n2-31-q34-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜において」 means “at,” “in,” or “within” a place or context; it does not mean doing something in advance as preparation.
default.q.n2-31-q34-34.why.3: (d) Correct: 「〜に先立って」 means “before” or “prior to,” and is used when doing something in preparation for an important event or plan.
default.q.n2-31-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2. つき, because the pattern 「N につき」 is used in formal notices and written language to state a reason (“due to” / “because of…”).
default.q.n2-31-q35-35.explanation:
Translation: Because the elevator has broken down, we are temporarily suspending its use.
Vocabulary & Sino-Japanese readings: 故障 (KOSHŌ: malfunction, breakdown), 中止 (CHŪSHI: suspension, cancellation).
Example: 工事中につき、立ち入り禁止。(No entry due to construction.)
default.q.n2-31-q35-35.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜につけ」 means “whenever...” or “whether... or...”; it is not used to state a reason in an announcement.
default.q.n2-31-q35-35.why.1: (b) Correct: 「〜につき」 is a formal expression used in notices and posted announcements to indicate a reason (“due to/because of...” ).
default.q.n2-31-q35-35.why.2: (c) Incorrect:「〜について」means “about” or “concerning” a topic or subject; it is not used to indicate the cause or reason for the elevator stopping.
default.q.n2-31-q35-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜にとって」 means "for" from a particular standpoint or perspective, which does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-31-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 3. のもとで because the pattern 「N のもとで」means “under the direction, guidance, or protection of N.”
default.q.n2-31-q36-36.explanation:
Translation: If you want to become a pianist, you should receive instruction under the guidance of a top-class performing artist.
Vocabulary and kanji-based meanings: 一流 (top-class), 演奏家 (performing artist), 指導 (instruction, guidance).
Example: 厳しい指導者のもとで、練習を重ねた。(I practiced repeatedly under the guidance of a strict instructor.)
default.q.n2-31-q36-36.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜とともに」means “together with / at the same time,” and does not combine with 「指導を受ける」to mean receiving guidance under someone’s supervision.
default.q.n2-31-q36-36.why.1: (b) Incorrect:「〜をもとに（して）」means “based on” or “using as a basis” (for materials or information), and is not used for an instructor.
default.q.n2-31-q36-36.why.2: (c) Correct: 「〜のもとで」 (UNDER: 下で) indicates being influenced by, studying under, receiving guidance from, or living under the protection of someone.
default.q.n2-31-q36-36.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜として」 means “as” or “in the capacity of,” which does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-31-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 4. きっかけに, because the pattern 「N をきっかけに（して）」 means “on the occasion of,” “thanks to,” or “using N as a turning point or opportunity.”
default.q.n2-31-q37-37.explanation:
Translation: Team A had been held scoreless in the first half, but thanks to a goal by a teammate, they regained their momentum in the second half.
Vocabulary and kanji: 前半 (first half), 後半 (second half), 味方 (one’s side, teammate), 勢いがつく (gain momentum, regain one’s drive).
Example: 留学をきっかけに、自分の視野が広がった。(Studying abroad became a turning point that broadened my perspective.)
default.q.n2-31-q37-37.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜を通じて」means “through / throughout a period,” and does not describe an event that acts as a trigger or turning point for changing the atmosphere.
default.q.n2-31-q37-37.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜をはじめ（として）」 means “starting with” or “representatively,” and is used to introduce a typical example.
default.q.n2-31-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜をもって」 means “by means of” or “as of a certain time (when something ends),” not “a turning point.”
default.q.n2-31-q37-37.why.3: (d) Correct: 「〜をきっかけに」means “taking ... as the turning point / thanks to ... as a catalyst,” which fits scoring a goal and giving the team momentum.
default.q.n2-31-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2. あげく, because the pattern「V-た + あげく」means that after a long time or repeated attempts, something ultimately leads to a negative result.
default.q.n2-31-q38-38.explanation:
Sentence translation: After causing trouble at work repeatedly, he was eventually forced to leave the company.
Vocabulary: 問題を起こす (cause trouble), やめさせられる (be forced to quit, be dismissed).
Example: 色々悩んだあげく、転職することにした。(After agonizing over it, I eventually decided to change jobs.)
default.q.n2-31-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜あまり（に）」 usually follows words expressing emotion or an excessive degree (“because of being too...”), and does not combine with 「何度も問題を起こした」 to describe a prolonged series of actions.
default.q.n2-31-q38-38.why.1: (b) Correct: 「〜あげくに / あげく」(挙句) indicates that after a long process or repeated attempts, an unfavorable result ultimately occurs, such as being dismissed from one’s job.
default.q.n2-31-q38-38.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜たとたん（に）」 describes something unexpected happening immediately after an action takes place. It does not combine with a repeated process such as 何度も.
default.q.n2-31-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect:「〜うえに」means “moreover, not only... but also...” and does not express a cause-and-eventual-result relationship.
default.q.n2-31-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ことなく, because the pattern 「V-る + ことなく」means “without doing V (doing something else without carrying out action V at all).”
default.q.n2-31-q39-39.explanation:
Sentence translation: That student returned to his home country without saying goodbye to the teacher who had supported him wholeheartedly.
Vocabulary: お世話になった (to have been cared for or helped by someone), 帰国 (return to one's home country).
Example: 彼は一度も諦めることなく、走り続けた。(He kept running without giving up even once.)
default.q.n2-31-q39-39.why.0: (a) Correct:「V-る + ことなく」is the formal equivalent of「〜ないで」, meaning “without…” or “without doing V.”
default.q.n2-31-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜わけはなく / わけがない」 means “there is no way...” or “certainly not,” and is not used to connect actions in a sentence.
default.q.n2-31-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜ばかりでなく」 means “not only... but also...,” which does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n2-31-q39-39.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜までもなく」 means “without needing to” or “not to the extent of having to...”; it does not fit the context of regretting returning home without saying goodbye.
default.q.n2-31-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 思いながらも because the pattern 「V-masu stem + ながらも」 means 'although / even though..., still...'.
default.q.n2-31-q40-40.explanation:
Translation: When my phone rings while I am on a train, I know I should not answer it, but sometimes I still end up picking up.
Key vocabulary and kanji compounds: 携帯電話 (mobile phone), 鳴る (to ring, sound).
Example: 体に悪いと知りながらも、夜遅くにラーメンを食べてしまう。(Although I know it is bad for my health, I still end up eating ramen late at night.)
default.q.n2-31-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜たところ」 means “after trying something” or “just after doing something,” and does not express a contrast between one’s thoughts and actions.
default.q.n2-31-q40-40.why.1: (b) Correct: 「〜ながらも」combines with the verb stem to express “although one knows...” or “despite...,” followed by an action contrary to that thought.
default.q.n2-31-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜ものなら」 means “if it were possible...” (an unlikely supposition) or “if someone were to...,” implying a bad result. It does not fit this context.
default.q.n2-31-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜わりには」 means “considering...” or “compared with..., contrary to the usual expectation.” It does not sound natural with 「〜とは思う」 in this context.
default.q.n2-31-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 1. といっても, because the pattern 「〜といっても」 means “although one says…” or “even though it is called…, in reality it is only to a modest degree.”
default.q.n2-31-q41-41.explanation:
Sentence translation: Although I say I can play the piano, I only play it as a hobby.
Vocabulary and kanji: 弾く (play an instrument), 趣味 (hobby), 程度 (degree, level).
Example: 料理ができるといっても、簡単なものしか作れません。(Although I say I can cook, I can only make simple dishes.)
default.q.n2-31-q41-41.why.0: (a) Correct: 「〜といっても」 means “although one says ..., in reality it is not as much as that,” and is appropriate for lowering the degree in the following clause (“only at the level of a hobby”).
default.q.n2-31-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜というより」 means “rather than saying...” or “more accurately...,” and is used to compare two descriptions or terms, not to clarify degree.
default.q.n2-31-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜としたら」 introduces a hypothetical condition (“if we suppose that…”), which does not fit the known fact that the person plays an instrument.
default.q.n2-31-q41-41.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜ものなら」 is used for a hypothetical event that is difficult to happen, so it does not fit here.
default.q.n2-31-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 1. にかかわらず because the pattern「N にかかわらず」means “regardless of / irrespective of N,” where N is a criterion or variable quantity.
default.q.n2-31-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: Products bearing a famous brand name sell very well regardless of their price.
Vocabulary: 商品 (goods, products), 値段 (price).
Example: 参加者の年齢にかかわらず、誰でも楽しめます。(Anyone can enjoy it regardless of the participants’ age.)
default.q.n2-31-q42-42.why.0: (a) Correct. 「N にかかわらず」 directly combines with a noun expressing a variable range or criterion, such as 値段, 年齢, or 天候, and means “regardless of the price.”
default.q.n2-31-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜にもかかわらず」 means “although…,” and normally accompanies a specific fact, such as 値段が高いにもかかわらず (“although the price is high”). It does not follow a noun representing a criterion alone, such as 「値段」.
default.q.n2-31-q42-42.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜にかぎって」 means “only ~” or “just when ~, something unfortunate happens,” so it does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n2-31-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜にかぎらず」means “not limited to...; not only... but also...,” expanding the range of applicable subjects.
default.q.n2-31-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 出席するにしろ欠席にしろ, because the pattern 「A にしろ B にしろ」 means “whether A or B, (the same action must be taken / the same judgment applies).”
default.q.n2-31-q43-43.explanation:
Sentence translation: If you do not reply to an invitation, whether you attend or not, it is very rude.
Vocabulary and kanji: 招待状 (invitation card), 返事 (reply, response), 失礼 (rude, impolite).
Example: 行くにしろ行かないにしろ、早めに連絡してください。(Whether you go or not, please contact them early.)
default.q.n2-31-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「A につけ B につけ」 means “whether A or B,” but the following clause generally describes a naturally occurring psychological state or emotion. It is not used for requests or obligations.
default.q.n2-31-q43-43.why.1: (b) Correct: 「A にしろ B にしろ」 means “whether A or B,” and the following clause presents a judgment, obligation, or advice to be followed.
default.q.n2-31-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「A やら B やら」 lists multiple things or activities, often suggesting busyness, disorder, or uncertainty.
default.q.n2-31-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「A とか B とか」 is used to list ordinary examples in spoken language, not to mean “regardless of the situation.”
default.q.n2-31-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 買わないことには, because the pattern「V-ないことには〜ない」means “unless one does V, it is completely impossible to do what follows.”
default.q.n2-31-q44-44.explanation:
Translation: Winning the lottery is very difficult, but if you do not buy a ticket, you have absolutely no chance of winning.
Vocabulary and kanji: 宝くじ: lottery ticket, 当てる/当たる: to win a prize.
Example: 実際に使ってみないことには、良さがわからない。(Unless you actually try using it, you cannot know what is good about it.)
default.q.n2-31-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜からといって」 means “just because...” or “even if one says it is because...”; the following clause usually takes a partial negation such as 〜わけではない, not an absolute negation expressing a prerequisite condition.
default.q.n2-31-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜わりには」means “relatively, considering...,” and does not fit a conditional relationship.
default.q.n2-31-q44-44.why.2: (c) Correct: 「V-ないことには〜ない」 expresses a necessary condition: “unless A is done, B cannot happen.”
default.q.n2-31-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜どころか」 means “not only... but rather...,” and is not used to express a prerequisite condition.
default.q.n2-31-q45-45.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1. The ★ position is choice 4 (かけて).
default.q.n2-31-q45-45.explanation:
Complete sentence: 彼は何か言いかけてやめてしまった。
Meaning: He started to say something, but then stopped.
default.q.n2-31-q45-45.why.0: (a) 1.やめて: It is in the fourth position, immediately before 「しまった」, forming 「やめてしまった」 (ended up quitting or stopping).
default.q.n2-31-q45-45.why.1: (b) 2.言い: In the second position, it is the continuative form (V-stem) of the verb 「言う」, combining with 「かけて」 to form 「言いかけて」.
default.q.n2-31-q45-45.why.2: (c) 3.何か: It occupies position 1 immediately after「彼は」and functions as the object of the following action phrase, meaning “something.”
default.q.n2-31-q45-45.why.3: (d) 4. かけて: It occupies the third position (★), follows the V-stem 「言い」 in the grammar pattern 「～かける」 (be in the middle of doing something / be about to do something), and comes before 「やめて」.
default.q.n2-31-q46-46.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 4 → 2. The ★ position is answer choice 4 (店).
default.q.n2-31-q46-46.explanation:
Complete sentence: ひとくちにカレーライスといっても店によって材料はさまざまだ。
Meaning: Even though they are all called curry rice, the ingredients vary greatly from one restaurant to another.
default.q.n2-31-q46-46.why.0: (a) 1.といっても: In the second position, following the noun 「カ式ーライス」, it forms 「～といっても」 (even though one says...), completing the first part 「ひとく活に～といっても」.
default.q.n2-31-q46-46.why.1: (b) 2. によって: In fourth position, it follows the noun「店」to form「～によって」(depending on...), modifying the following clause「材料はさまざまだ」.
default.q.n2-31-q46-46.why.2: (c) 3.カ式ーライス: It comes immediately after 「ひとく活に」 in position 1 and serves as the noun being introduced as the topic.
default.q.n2-31-q46-46.why.3: (d) 4. 店: It occupies the third position (the ★ position) and is the noun before 「によって」, forming 「店によって」 (“depending on the shop”).
default.q.n2-31-q47-47.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 3 → 4. The choice at ★ is 3 (引っ越し).
default.q.n2-31-q47-47.explanation:
Complete sentence: お金がなくて旅行もできないのだから引っ越しどころではない。
Meaning: I cannot even afford to travel, so moving is completely out of the question.
default.q.n2-31-q47-47.why.0: (a) 1.もできないのだから: Occupies the second position after the noun 「旅行」, forming the causal clause 「～もできないのだから」(if one cannot even do...).
default.q.n2-31-q47-47.why.1: (b) 2.旅行: It appears in the first position after 「お金がなくて」 and is the noun describing the simpler activity that could not be done either.
default.q.n2-31-q47-47.why.2: (c) 3.引っ越し: It is in third place (the ★ position), a noun describing a larger matter that comes before the structure 「～どころではない」.
default.q.n2-31-q47-47.why.3: (d) 4.どころでは: It follows the noun 「引っ越し」in the fourth position and combines with 「ない」at the end of the sentence to form 「～どころではない」(this is no time for..., it is impossible to...).
default.q.n2-31-q48-48.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 3 → 4 → 1. The ★ position is choice 4 (一人で).
default.q.n2-31-q48-48.explanation:
Complete sentence: あんなに大きい荷物、私一人で運べと言うんですか。
Meaning: Are you telling me to carry such a large piece of luggage all by myself?
default.q.n2-31-q48-48.why.0: (a) 1. 運べ: It appears in the fourth position, immediately before the particle 「と」, and is the imperative form of the verb 「運ぶ」used in a quoted clause before 「と言うんですか」(are you saying, “Carry it over”?).
default.q.n2-31-q48-48.why.1: (b) 2.大きい荷物: It is in the first position immediately after 「あんなに」, forming the object phrase 「あんなに大きい荷物」 (such a large piece of luggage).
default.q.n2-31-q48-48.why.2: (c) 3. 私: It occupies position 2 and combines with 「一人で」 to form 「私一人で」, meaning "I alone" or "by myself."
default.q.n2-31-q48-48.why.3: (d) 4.一人で: It occupies the third position (the ★ slot), immediately follows 「私」 to form 「私一人で」 before the verb 「運べ」.
default.q.n2-31-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The ★ position is choice 4 (長い間).
default.q.n2-31-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 子供のころ別れたきり彼女とは長い間会っていない。
Meaning: I have not seen her for a long time since we parted when we were children.
default.q.n2-31-q49-49.why.0: (a) 1.彼女とは: It occupies position 2 and functions as the topic or object highlighted by the particle 「とは」in the predicate 「長い間会っていない」.
default.q.n2-31-q49-49.why.1: (b) 2.別れたきり: Placed first, immediately after 「子供のころ」, it forms the phrase 「子供のころ別れたきり」 using the pattern 「V-た + きり」 (ever since..., with no change up to the present).
default.q.n2-31-q49-49.why.2: (c) 3.会って: Placed fourth, directly before 「いない」 at the end of the sentence, it forms the state or ongoing negative pattern 「会っていない」 (have not met again).
default.q.n2-31-q49-49.why.3: (d) 4. 長い間: It occupies the third position (★) and is a time adverb placed before 「会って」to modify 「会っていない」(have not met for a long time).
default.q.n2-31-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 3. につれて (as ...; along with changes in ...).
default.q.n2-31-q50-50.explanation: This describes a natural pattern when climbing a mountain: as the altitude changes and rises, the temperature changes accordingly and falls, while the weather becomes more changeable. The N2 pattern 「V-る / N ＋ につれて」 expresses that as A progresses or changes, B changes along with it. Therefore, 「につれて」 is the most accurate choice.
default.q.n2-31-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「ので」 expresses an ordinary cause-and-effect relationship (“because ... therefore ...”); it does not express the corresponding parallel change over time required by the context.
default.q.n2-31-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「というより」means “rather than saying” or “more accurately,” and is used to correct or adjust an assessment; it does not fit a connection between two clauses describing simultaneous changes.
default.q.n2-31-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「につれて」 is an N2 grammar pattern (V-る/N + につれて) expressing a corresponding change in the second clause as the degree or progress of the first clause changes (“as the altitude rises, the temperature falls...”). It is completely accurate.
default.q.n2-31-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「ほど」 is commonly used in degree comparisons or the structure 「〜ば〜ほど」. It cannot stand alone after a verb in the dictionary form to express simultaneous change in this sentence.
default.q.n2-31-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 十分な準備をせずに (without making adequate preparations...).
default.q.n2-31-q51-51.explanation: The passage is giving a warning: even when climbing a beginner-friendly mountain that is easy to ascend, going mountain climbing without carefully preparing the necessary equipment, physical fitness, and knowledge is still extremely dangerous. The structure 「〜ずに」 (equivalent to 「〜ないで」, “without doing ...”) combines with 「十分な準備」 to form 「十分な準備をせずに」 (“without making adequate preparations and then ...”), expressing careless overconfidence and fitting perfectly with the warning of danger in the following clause.
default.q.n2-31-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「グループと一緒に」(together with a group) is an action that improves safety while mountain climbing, so it is logically inconsistent with the following warning that it is “very dangerous.”
default.q.n2-31-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「グループと離れて」 (separated from the group) may describe a risky action, but it does not capture the broader idea of a careless attitude toward preparation before a trip that the article emphasizes.
default.q.n2-31-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「十分な準備をして」 (having made sufficient preparations) is completely contrary in logic and meaning to the danger warning that follows.
default.q.n2-31-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「十分な準備をせずに」uses the structure「〜ずに」to express the careless action of 'going mountain climbing without making sufficient preparations,' which fits the author's warning about danger.
default.q.n2-31-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 弱まることになりかねない (there is a risk that it may weaken).
default.q.n2-31-q52-52.explanation: The sentence analyzes the consequences of physical exhaustion: when one’s strength is worn down, a mountain climber can easily experience a decline in sound judgment. The JLPT N2 pattern 「V-ます (remove ます) / V-る + かねない」 (or 「〜ことになりかねない」) means “there is a risk that... / it could possibly lead to a bad result,” making it well suited to warning that judgment (判断力) may weaken (弱まる).
default.q.n2-31-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「弱まることになりかねない」 uses the N2 grammar pattern 「〜かねない」 (there is a risk of leading to a negative consequence), accurately expressing the idea that one's judgment may weaken or deteriorate.
default.q.n2-31-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「失われるどころではない」means 'it is not merely a matter of being lost / this is no time for something to be lost.' It is not used to predict a danger or negative consequence resulting from loss of physical strength.
default.q.n2-31-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「増えるおそれもある」means "there is a risk of increasing." It cannot modify judgment ability, because under exhaustion one's judgment declines rather than improves.
default.q.n2-31-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「変わらないこともある」 means “there are also times when it does not change,” which is neutral and removes the warning about the serious negative effects of exhaustion.
default.q.n2-31-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 命にかかわる事態 (a life-threatening situation).
default.q.n2-31-q53-53.explanation: The phrase 「最悪の場合」 (in the worst-case scenario) signals an extremely serious consequence, possibly even one that threatens life. The JLPT N2 expression 「〜にかかわる」 (to seriously affect / directly threaten) forms the familiar phrase 「命にかかわる事態」 (a life-threatening situation) with the noun 「命」, which fits the context of a serious mountaineering accident perfectly.
default.q.n2-31-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「命にかかわる事態」 uses the N2 grammar pattern 「〜にかかわる」 (having a serious effect on one's life), accurately expressing the worst possible consequence: "in the worst case, it could develop into a life-threatening situation."
default.q.n2-31-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「体力が奪われる事態」 (a situation in which one’s physical strength is depleted) is only an intermediate cause mentioned in the preceding sentence. It is not an appropriate final consequence for “in the worst case” (最悪の場合).
default.q.n2-31-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「登山客が減る事態」(a situation in which the number of mountain climbers decreases) is completely off topic because the context concerns the lives and safety of mountain climbers, not the number of tourists.
default.q.n2-31-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「気軽に登れない事態」 (“a situation in which one cannot climb casually”) is far too mild to fit the serious danger expressed by 「〜に発展することもある」.
default.q.n2-31-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 2. なによりも (more than anything, above all).
default.q.n2-31-q54-54.explanation: This is the author’s concluding summary and central advice: to enjoy mountain climbing safely, nothing is more important than not pushing yourself beyond your limits. The adverb 「なによりも」means “more than anything / above all” and is often used with adjectives emphasizing importance, such as 「大切だ / 重要だ」.
default.q.n2-31-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「なんとなく」 means “somehow,” “vaguely,” or “for no particular reason,” expressing an unclear feeling. It is completely unsuitable for advice stating a definite safety principle.
default.q.n2-31-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「なによりも」means “above all” or “more than anything else,” and combines naturally with 「大切である」to emphasize the core and most important factor in the conclusion.
default.q.n2-31-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「どうしても」means “no matter what” or “by all means,” and commonly occurs with an unavoidable negative sentence or a strongly expressed intention. It does not combine with the predicate indicating a degree of importance, 「大切である」, here.
default.q.n2-31-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「どうにかして」 means “somehow / by any means possible” and indicates an effort to find a way to solve a problem. It does not modify the evaluative adjective 「大切である」.
default.q.n2-31-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Forgetting to take care of the tadpoles (オタマジャクシの世話をすること).
default.q.n2-31-q55-55.explanation:
- Main point: The author recalls that in third grade, the class had a science project studying tadpoles. They had to feed them, change their water, and deal with dead tadpoles, which was troublesome. When Golden Week arrived and school was closed for three or four days, the author, despite being responsible for caring for the animals, did not think about what would happen to the tadpoles during the holiday and completely forgot to take care of them.
- Question translation: The sentence 「私はすっかり忘れていた」(I had completely forgotten) appears. What had the author forgotten?
- Answer choices:
  1. That it was Golden Week.
  2. Catching tadpoles.
  3. That the eggs had hatched into tadpoles.
  4. Taking care of the tadpoles.
default.q.n2-31-q55-55.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author clearly knew that Golden Week had arrived and that there would be 3 or 4 days off from school (「そんなある日、ゴールデンウィークがやってきて、学校が 3 日だか 4 日だか休みになった」), rather than forgetting that it was a holiday.
default.q.n2-31-q55-55.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because being ordered to catch tadpoles (「オタマジャクシを採ってくるように命じられた」) was a task completed earlier, not something the author forgot during the vacation.
default.q.n2-31-q55-55.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage only mentions that some of them were still in the egg stage (「中にはまだ卵の状態のものもあったりして」), making them troublesome to care for. It does not mention forgetting that the eggs had hatched into tadpoles.
default.q.n2-31-q55-55.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the author is responsible for caring for the tadpoles—feeding them, changing their water, and dealing with those that die: 「エサをやったり水をかえたり、死んだオタマの始末をしたり...」 However, during the holiday: 「生き物係といえども、ゴールデンウィーク中までオタマジャクシがどうのこうの等と考えてはいない。私はす流かり忘れていた。」 Even though I was in charge of the class animals, I did not think about what was happening with the tadpoles during Golden Week. I had completely forgotten. Therefore, what the author forgot was to pay attention to and care for the tadpoles.
default.q.n2-31-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2: A person whose mental map is well organized and clear.
default.q.n2-31-q56-56.explanation:
- Question translation: What kind of person does the author say can think about or explain a route logically and clearly?
- Answer choices:
  1. Someone who is currently holding a map.
  2. Someone whose mental map is neatly and clearly organized.
  3. Someone who knows the name of the shopping district.
  4. Someone whose thinking is vague and unclear.
- Main point: The passage uses the example of giving directions from the station to one’s home by phone to show that a person with a clearly formed and well-organized mental map (「頭のなかに地図がちゃんとおさまっている人」) also thinks clearly and effectively (「考え方も上手」). Conversely, someone with a disorganized mental map will have vague thoughts. Therefore, choice 2 is correct.
default.q.n2-31-q56-56.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage refers to a map imagined in the mind (「頭のなかに地図が...」), not to physically holding a paper or actual map.
default.q.n2-31-q56-56.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage states: 「頭のなかに地図がちゃんとおさまっている人は、考え方も上手です。」 (“People who have a properly organized map in their heads are also good at thinking.”)
default.q.n2-31-q56-56.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the shopping district's name (「南口の商店街の名前」) is merely an example of a detail people often forget; the passage does not claim that knowing the district's name indicates strong thinking or navigation skills.
default.q.n2-31-q56-56.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because 「あいまいな考え方をする」 (“think vaguely”) is described as a characteristic of people with a poor sense of direction, whose mental maps are disorganized (「方向感覚の悪い人は、頭のなかの地図がぐちゃぐちゃになっています。だからあいまいな考え方をします。」), which is the complete opposite of being good at it.
default.q.n2-31-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Compared with adults, children have weaker resistance to stress and are more likely to accumulate it.
default.q.n2-31-q57-57.explanation:
- Main point: The passage explains that stress is the mind and body's response to stimuli from the environment, and includes both positive and negative stress. To prevent negative stress from building up and causing anxiety, irritation, or illness, people need to have a strong body and mind. Therefore, children—whose minds and bodies are still developing—have weaker resistance to stress than adults and are more likely to accumulate stress.

- Translation of the question:
What is the most appropriate word or phrase to fill in ( ★ )?

- Translation of the choices:
1. Compared with adults, they have weaker resistance to stress and are more likely to accumulate stress.
2. Compared with adults, they have weaker resistance to stress and are less likely to accumulate stress.
3. Like adults, they have weaker resistance to stress and are more likely to accumulate stress.
4. Like adults, they have weaker resistance to stress and are less likely to accumulate stress.
default.q.n2-31-q57-57.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「悪いストレスをためないためには、それに勝つための強い心と体が必要です。したがって、精神的にも体力的にもまだ成長過程にある子どもは、（ ★ ）。」. Since avoiding the accumulation of harmful stress requires a strong mind and body, and children are still developing both mentally and physically, they have weaker resistance to stress than adults (大人と比べて) and are more likely to accumulate stress (ストレスがたまりやすい).
default.q.n2-31-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This choice says「たまりにくい」(not easily accumulated), which is the opposite of the passage's logic: when physical and mental strength are not yet fully developed, stress is more likely to accumulate (たまりやすい).
default.q.n2-31-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect. This choice uses 「大人と同じように」 (“in the same way as adults”), which is unsuitable because adults have already matured while children are 「まだ成長過程にある」 (“still in the process of growing”). It should use 「大人と比べて」 (“compared with adults”).
default.q.n2-31-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice is wrong both in using 「大人と同じように」 (“like adults”) and in stating 「たまりにくい」 (“stress is less likely to accumulate”).
default.q.n2-31-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The writer broke a leg and therefore cannot attend this class reunion, but hopes to attend the next one in two years (the year after next).
default.q.n2-31-q58-58.explanation:
**Summary:**
The letter writer expresses regret at being unable to attend the recent class reunion and hot-spring trip because they fell and broke a leg («ちょっと転んだだけで骨折するなんて»). Their leg has now recovered considerably, and they look forward to seeing everyone at the next class reunion two years from now («出席できずとても残念に思います» and «二年後のその日を楽しみにしております», equivalent to 再来年).

**Question translation:**
Which of the following correctly describes the writer of this letter?

**Answer choices:**
1. They fell and broke a bone at the hot spring, could not attend the class reunion, and regretted it.
2. They fell and broke a bone but attended the class reunion because they were able to walk.
3. They talked with everyone about their junior high school memories at the class reunion and had a wonderful time.
4. They could not attend this time because they broke a bone, but hope to attend the class reunion the year after next (two years from now).
default.q.n2-31-q58-58.why.0: (a) This is incorrect because the writer did not go to the hot spring and ask how the other person’s trip was («温泉はいかがでしたか»); they did not fall at the hot spring.
default.q.n2-31-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the writer was completely unable to attend the class reunion («せっかくの同窓会に出席できずとても残念に思います»).
default.q.n2-31-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author did not attend the class reunion but only looked at photos («写真で拝見し»). Talking about memories from junior high school is something the author hopes to do at the next reunion («次回はぜひ皆さんと中学生のときの思い出話に花を咲かせたい»).
default.q.n2-31-q58-58.why.3: (d) Correct because the writer broke a bone and therefore cannot attend this time («出席できず», «骨折するなんて»), and looks forward to attending the next class reunion in two years («次回はぜひ... 二年後のその日を楽しみにしております» — 二年後 is equivalent to 再来年).
default.q.n2-31-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 3: a approximately 30% ／ b approximately 15%.
default.q.n2-31-q59-59.explanation:
**Main point of the passage:**
The passage presents survey data on internet use:
- The proportion of households with at least one person who has used the internet is 41.6% (about half).
- Purposes of use:
  + Gathering information (情報収集): the highest, at about 40%.
  + E-mail (電子メール): about 10 percentage points lower than gathering information → (a) = 40% - 10% = about 30%.
  + Buying and selling goods online (商品の売買): half the figure for e-mail → (b) = 30% / 2 = about 15%.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** Which combination of figures for (a) and (b) is correct?
- **1.** a: about 20% ／ b: about 15%
- **2.** a: about 50% ／ b: about 25%
- **3.** a: about 30% ／ b: about 15%
- **4.** a: about 30% ／ b: about 20%
default.q.n2-31-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect. According to the passage, information gathering accounts for about 40%, while email accounts for less than 10%, so (a) should be 30%, not 20%.
default.q.n2-31-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This choice miscalculates (a) as approximately 50% by adding 10% instead of subtracting it, and calculates (b) as approximately 25%, contrary to the passage.
default.q.n2-31-q59-59.why.2: (c) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「情報 収 集 が約 40 ％ と一番多い。 続いて電子メールが 10 ％少ない（ a ）である。次はインターネットによる商品の売買で、電子メールの半数の（ b ）である。」 → (a) = 40% − 10% = approximately 30%; (b) = 30% ÷ 2 = approximately 15%.
default.q.n2-31-q59-59.why.3: (d) is incorrect. The value in (a), approximately 30%, is correct, but (b) is half of the email value (30% / 2 = 15%), not approximately 20%.
default.q.n2-31-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 友人を得るためには、本人の努力が必要だ。
default.q.n2-31-q60-60.explanation:
- Main idea: The author uses the metaphor of growing plants (personally sowing seeds, watering them, and adding fertilizer) to compare with building friendships, emphasizing that making friends does not happen naturally like wild grass; it requires personal effort to nurture the relationship.
- Translation of the question: Choose the most appropriate answer to fill in ( ★ ).
- Translation of the choices:
  1. You should not rely on friends to grow plants.
  2. To make friends, you need to make your own effort.
  3. Friends should be as strong as wild grass.
  4. You can become friends with only a very small number of people.
default.q.n2-31-q60-60.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because planting trees is only a metaphor for making friends; the passage does not discuss actual planting techniques or say that one should not ask friends for help when planting trees.
default.q.n2-31-q60-60.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is correct because the preceding sentence says: "友人は雑草のように、何の手を加えなくても自然に生えてくるものではなく、自分で種をまいて、水をやり肥料 をやらね消育てられないものである" and the following sentence says: "「信頼できる友人がいない」と嘆く 人は、たいていの場合、この努力を怠り..." Together, they show that having friends requires personal effort to nurture and develop the relationship.
default.q.n2-31-q60-60.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author denies that friends grow on their own like weeds (「雑草のように、何の手を加えなくても自然に生えてくるものではなく」), rather than saying that friends must be strong like weeds.
default.q.n2-31-q60-60.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4 is incorrect because this is information describing the situation in paragraph 1, not a conclusion drawn (“つまり”) from the comparison of plant care in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n2-31-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1: そんなに簡単に友人ができるものではない。
default.q.n2-31-q61-61.explanation:
- Main point: The author criticizes people who simply sit secluded in one place, waiting for others to approach them and pat them on the shoulder, while hoping to make friends. The author insists that life cannot be so easy and convenient; to make friends, one must take the initiative to approach others.
- Question translation: What does the sentence "If you could make friends just by doing that, wouldn't it be convenient" mean?
- Answer choices:
  1. You cannot make friends that easily.
  2. Making friends that way is the best method.
  3. With that attitude, plants will become infested with insects.
  4. People like that are insignificant existences like insects on weeds.
default.q.n2-31-q61-61.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because the quotation: "自分から積極的に友人を得ようとするのではなく、自分の肩を優しくたたいてくれる人を待ち望んでいるだけだ。それで友人ができるのなら、そんな虫のいい話はない" shows that the author emphasizes that making friends cannot be so easy that one simply sits passively and waits for someone else to approach.
default.q.n2-31-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author criticizes this passive, lazy behavior (“この努力を怠り、自分の殻に閉じこもっている”) and does not consider it the best method at all.
default.q.n2-31-q61-61.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because "虫のいい話" is an idiomatic expression meaning "an overly favorable deal / an unreasonable demand / a self-serving proposition," not something literally related to insects that damage crops.
default.q.n2-31-q61-61.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not compare people to tiny insects on weeds.
default.q.n2-31-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 人の集まるところへ行き、多くの人とはなすこと。
default.q.n2-31-q62-62.explanation:
- Main idea: The author advises that the quickest way to make friends is to go deliberately to places where many people gather (such as social gatherings, clubs, and cultural classes) and actively start conversations and interact with many people.
- Translation of the question: What method does the author recommend for making a reliable friend?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Pat the other person lightly on the shoulder at parties.
  2. Be sure to attend the party even if you are sick.
  3. Go to places where many people gather and talk with many people.
  4. Water plants and grow them yourself.
default.q.n2-31-q62-62.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because "patting someone gently on the shoulder" is an image in the preceding passage describing passively waiting for someone else to come to you ("自分の肩を優しくたたいてくれる人を待ち望んでいるだけだ"), not a method recommended by the author.
default.q.n2-31-q62-62.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because going to a party despite being somewhat tired is only the author's personal example ("少々疲れていようが頑張って出席する"). The author also explicitly says they are not telling the reader to attend parties ("あなたも、何もパーティーに出席しろとは言わないが").
default.q.n2-31-q62-62.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct, as shown by the quotations: "では、どんな努力をすればいいかというと、やはり人が多く集まる場所に出かけて、多くの人と話をするのが 早道だ" and "いろいろな場所に何度も足を運んで人と話をすることが、真の友人を得るき流かけになる".
default.q.n2-31-q62-62.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because watering and caring for plants is only a metaphor in paragraph 2, not an actual method for making friends.
default.q.n2-31-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The “surprising fact” discovered was that, because flowers bloom year-round in Australia, the bees no longer go out to collect nectar.
default.q.n2-31-q63-63.explanation:
- **Main point**: The author tells the story of someone who brought honeybees from Europe to Australia to raise them because flowers bloom year-round in Australia. The first year was very successful, but from the second year onward, honey production declined sharply, and the bees almost stopped foraging. An investigation revealed something surprising: because flowers bloom year-round there, the bees lost their sense of urgency or scarcity (hunger) and no longer worked hard to store honey as they had in Europe, where flowers do not bloom during the harsh winter.
- **Translation of the question & answer choices**:
  - *Question*: What was the "unexpected thing" (「 意外なこと 」) here?
  - *1.* Because flowers bloom year-round in Australia, the bees stopped collecting nectar.
  - *2.* Even though Europe has long, harsh winters, the bees were able to collect a lot of honey.
  - *3.* Honeybees never have a sense of urgency or hunger.
  - *4.* Although excellent bees had been imported from Europe, the results did not meet expectations.
default.q.n2-31-q63-63.why.0: (a) QUOTATION: 「おかしいと思って調べてもらったら、いつも花があるからだという意外なことがわかった。ヨーロッパで働き蜂といわれるほどに勤勉であったのは、花のなくなる冬があるからだったのである。年中花のある恵まれたところに移って、蜂はハングリーでなくなってしまったらしい。」 (When someone thought it was strange and had it investigated, they discovered the surprising fact that it was because there were always flowers. The reason bees in Europe were so diligent that they were called worker bees was that Europe had winters when flowers disappeared. After moving to a fortunate place where flowers bloomed all year round, the bees apparently lost their hunger.) Choice 1 accurately paraphrases this content.
default.q.n2-31-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the fact that bees in Europe collect a large amount of honey despite severe winters was already known; it was not a new "surprise" discovered while investigating the cause in Australia.
default.q.n2-31-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage says that bees in Europe are originally hungry and hardworking (ハングリー) because flowers are scarce in winter. Only after moving to a warm environment with flowers year-round do they lose that drive; it does not say that bees cannot become hungry.
default.q.n2-31-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the failure to achieve the expected result—the sharp drop in production in the second year—was merely the initial phenomenon that puzzled the growers. The “unexpected fact” (意外なこと) was the cause revealed after investigation: the flowers bloomed throughout the year.
default.q.n2-31-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author argues that humans, like bees, make greater efforts when they are in difficult or deprived conditions (hungry), helping culture and society flourish.
default.q.n2-31-q64-64.explanation:
- **Main point**: Drawing on the story of bees becoming lazy when living in favorable conditions, the author relates this to human beings: “It cannot be said that this is only a matter concerning bees and that humans are different.” The reason is that when people live in difficult, harsh conditions—such as snowy or cold regions—they too are forced to develop a hunger to improve themselves (“ハングリー”), which makes them work harder and drives the development and prosperity of society, culture, and civilization.
- **Question and answer choice translations**:
  - *Question*: Why does the author think that “It cannot be said that this is only a matter concerning bees and that humans are different”?
  - *1.* Like bees, humans cannot prosper unless they live in a warm climate.
  - *2.* Like bees, humans make greater efforts when they are hungry and thereby help culture develop.
  - *3.* Neither bees nor humans can become hungry in either cold or warm places.
  - *4.* Bees cannot become hungry in favorable environments, but humans in cold places…
default.q.n2-31-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage says that people in cold or harsh environments make efforts and help society prosper, which is contrary to the claim that people must live in a warm climate in order to prosper.
default.q.n2-31-q64-64.why.1: (b) QUOTATION: 「人間も概して、きびしい環境におかれた方がよくはたらく。... 寒いところの人間は、温暖なところで生活する人に比べると、おしなべて勤勉で努力する。それがやがて社会の繁栄に結びつく、そう考えるのである。悪条件のもとではハングリーにならずにはいられない。ハングリーならよくはたらくというわけだ。」 (The same is generally true of human beings: they work better when placed in harsh environments... Compared with people living in warm regions, people in cold regions are generally more diligent and hardworking. They believe that this eventually leads to social prosperity. Under unfavorable conditions, people cannot help becoming hungry for success. And when they are hungry for success, they work better.) Answer choice 2 accurately reflects this argument.
default.q.n2-31-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage states that in a cold place or harsh environment, both bees and humans become “hungry” and work hard; it does not say that they cannot become hungry.
default.q.n2-31-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because this choice misrepresents the comparative argument. The article states that people in cold places or difficult conditions are forced to become “hungry” and work harder.
default.q.n2-31-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author’s main message is that both bees and humans make greater efforts in harsh environments and consequently produce better results.
default.q.n2-31-q65-65.explanation:
- **Main point:** The passage uses the story of honeybees (in Europe, harsh winters make them diligently collect honey, while in warm Australia, where flowers bloom year-round, they become lazy) to draw a general lesson for people: in a difficult, harsh environment ("きびしい環境 / 悪条件"), both bees and humans develop a desire to strive ("ハングリー") and work hard, and that effort produces good results (more honey / social progress and flourishing civilization).
- **Translation of the question and answer choices:**
  - *Question*: What does the author most want to say in this passage?
  - *1.* Compared with Europe, which has long, harsh winters, warm Australia is a better place.
  - *2.* Bees in harsh environments collect a lot of honey, but people in cold environments do not develop.
  - *3.* When both bees and humans are in a harsh environment, they work harder, and this is reflected in positive results.
  - *4.* To become hungry, one should move to a place with the worst possible conditions.
default.q.n2-31-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author is not comparing Australia and Europe to claim that Australia is better. The story about bees in Australia is used as a lesson about how the living environment affects diligence.
default.q.n2-31-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The final paragraph states that people in cold regions and harsh environments generally work harder and make greater efforts, helping their culture and society prosper and develop—not that they fail to develop.
default.q.n2-31-q65-65.why.2: (c) QUOTATION: Throughout the passage, from the example of European bees working diligently because of harsh winters to the argument about human beings, the author states: 「人間も概して、きびしい環境におかれた方がよくはたらく。... 寒いところの人間は、温暖なところで生活する人に比べると、おしなべて勤勉で努力する。それがやがて社会の繁栄に結びつく... 悪条件のもとではハングリーにならずにはいられない。ハングリーならよくはたらくというわけだ。」 The author emphasizes that difficult circumstances foster a hungry spirit of effort and lead to positive results. Choice 3 accurately summarizes this central idea.
default.q.n2-31-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author only analyzes the natural and social principle that adversity encourages effort; the author does not advise people to seek out the worst possible living conditions.
default.q.n2-31-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Because the person does not want to do things that would put them at a disadvantage.
default.q.n2-31-q66-66.explanation:
- Main point: The author explains that when refusing something they do not want to do, untrained people often begin by explaining the personal advantages and disadvantages because, fundamentally, everyone—including oneself—acts based on self-interest and does not want to do things that disadvantage them.
- Question translation: Why do people tend to begin by "explaining their own advantages and disadvantages"?
- Answer choices:
1. Because they do not want to do things that would disadvantage them.
2. Because they have not attended a seminar on refusing things they do not want to do.
3. Because they find it troublesome to explain the real reason.
4. Because they are dissatisfied when the other person benefits.
default.q.n2-31-q66-66.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「なぜなら、自分を含めて、すべての人は自分の利益中心に動きます。」 (Because everyone, including oneself, acts with their own interests at the center.) The preceding example also shows that when something does not benefit them, people tend to say 「自分はそれをしたくない」 (I do not want to do it).
default.q.n2-31-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The tendency of people without training (訓練を受けていない人) is merely a description of the phenomenon, not an explanation of the essence of human behavior.
default.q.n2-31-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not mention feeling 「面倒」 about explaining the real reason.
default.q.n2-31-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage does not mention being dissatisfied or annoyed when the other person benefits.
default.q.n2-31-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4: A society centered on self-interest is a natural state, not a “system” established to unify people's interests.
default.q.n2-31-q67-67.explanation:
- Main point: According to the author, a "system" is a method created by people to reconcile and unify the interests of many individuals so that they can work toward a common action or goal, such as capitalism, a parliamentary cabinet system, establishing rules, or appointing a leader. By contrast, people acting in their own self-interest is a naturally occurring, unrestrained state, not a system that has been created.
- Question translation: Which of the following is NOT a "system" in the author's sense?
- Choice translations:
1. Capitalism.
2. A parliamentary cabinet system.
3. An organization with a strong leader.
4. A society centered on self-interest.
default.q.n2-31-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect (this is the author’s system). Quotation: 「それを考えつづけ、システムとしてなんとか構築したのが、経済学では資本主義...」.
default.q.n2-31-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect (this system reflects the author’s viewpoint). Quotation: 「...社会学では議院内閣制です。」.
default.q.n2-31-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect (this is the system according to the author's view). Quotation: 「あるいはリーダー的な立場の人を作ることで、なんとか方向性を一致させ、同じ目的を達するようにします。」.
default.q.n2-31-q67-67.why.3: (d) Correct. Evidence: 「自分を含めて、すべての人は自分の利益中心に動きます」「自分と相手の利害は、野放しの状態では基本的にまったく一致しないのです。」 Society operating according to individual interests is a natural state (野放しの状態), not a “system” (システム) designed to unite interests.
default.q.n2-31-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Make your own interests and the other person's interests align.
default.q.n2-31-q68-68.explanation:
- Main idea: The author emphasizes that, in their natural state, one's interests and the other party's interests basically do not coincide at all. Therefore, an important issue in communication as well as in society and economics is finding a way to reconcile the parties' goals and interests so that they can achieve a common objective together.
- Question translation: Which of the following best reflects the author's view?
- Answer choices:
1. Think about the other party's advantages and disadvantages first.
2. Explain your own interests to the other party.
3. Make your own interests and the other party's interests align.
4. Build a system concerning advantages and disadvantages.
default.q.n2-31-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Although the author advises explaining the benefits to the other person when persuading them, the article’s broadest and most consistent message is how to align both sides’ interests and work toward a shared goal.
default.q.n2-31-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This is completely opposite to the author’s view; the author criticizes explaining only one’s own benefits as a lack of skill.
default.q.n2-31-q68-68.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「さまざまな人の利害を一致させ、同じ行動をとらせるようにすることは永遠の課題です。」 and 「なんとか方向性を一致させ、同じ目的を達するようにします。」 (Somehow aligning the direction so that everyone can achieve the same goal.)
default.q.n2-31-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Building systems such as capitalism and political institutions is merely a macro-level illustration of how people resolve conflicts between interests; it is not the author's core advice to readers.
default.q.n2-31-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Phone conversations are permitted in one designated private car (a “conversation car”).
default.q.n2-31-q69-69.explanation:
- Main idea: In the section titled "提案" (Proposal), the author observes that people have become aware that they should not talk on the phone on trains. However, this is inconvenient in emergencies because they have to get off the train before making or answering a call. The author therefore proposes creating a "phone-call car" (通話車両) where passengers can freely talk on the phone.

- Question translation: What is the content of the "Proposal"?
- Answer choices:
1. Allow passengers to send email or access the internet only in one designated car.
2. Allow passengers to talk on the phone only in one designated car.
3. Further promote proper phone etiquette on trains.
4. Stop talking on the phone on trains and require passengers to get off the train before making a call.
default.q.n2-31-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because everyone can still use email and the internet normally throughout the train, so the proposal is not to restrict these activities to a separate car.
default.q.n2-31-q69-69.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage clearly quotes the proposal: 「そこで、「通話車両」を作って、その車両では自由に携帯電話で話せることにしてはどうだろうか。」 (Therefore, why not create a "telephone car" where people can freely talk on their mobile phones?).
default.q.n2-31-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author says that cellphone etiquette rules have already become widespread (携帯マナーが浸透してきたようだ). The purpose of the proposal is not to promote those rules further.
default.q.n2-31-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because having to get off the train before making a phone call is the current inconvenience in an emergency (緊急の場合、わざわざ電車を降りなければならない), not the proposed content.
default.q.n2-31-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 4: B opposes establishing a “conversation car.”
default.q.n2-31-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point:
  + Paragraph A sympathizes with the need to make urgent calls and believes that people could speak quietly and briefly. However, A does not support establishing a “conversation car” because many people might speak loudly and cause even more inconvenience.
  + Paragraph B insists that trains and other public transportation are public spaces, so banning phone conversations is naturally a matter of common sense (常識) to avoid disturbing others. B opposes changing the rules to establish a conversation car and considers it selfish.

- Translation of the question: Which of the following correctly describes A and B’s opinions about the “Proposal”?
- Translation of the choices:
1. Both A and B think that talking on the phone on a train is absolutely unacceptable.
2. Both A and B think that talking on the phone on a train is acceptable in special circumstances.
3. A supports establishing a “conversation car.”
4. B opposes establishing a “conversation car.”
default.q.n2-31-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect because person A believes that, in an emergency, speaking quietly and briefly is still acceptable (小声で手短になら話してもかまわないと思います); it is not absolutely forbidden.
default.q.n2-31-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because Speaker B considers banning phone conversations on trains common sense in public places (禁止するのは、常識だと思います) and does not support allowing calls even in special circumstances.
default.q.n2-31-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because Person A is concerned that a conversation car would lead to people speaking loudly and causing more trouble (大声で話す人も出てきて、乗り合わせた人は、今以上に迷惑と感じるのではないでしょうか), so A does not agree with the idea.
default.q.n2-31-q70-70.why.3: (d) Correct because Person B considers banning conversation only natural and views the proposal to change the rules permitting conversation as: 「それを忘れ、わがままを通すためにルールを変えようとしているように思えてなりません」(an attempt to change the rules simply to satisfy one's own selfishness). This clearly shows opposition.
default.q.n2-31-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: The view that close friends will accept all of one's flaws does not accord with the ideas presented in the passage.
default.q.n2-31-q71-71.explanation:
The author discusses the proverb 「親しき仲にも礼儀あり」 (Even among close relationships, manners are necessary), emphasizing that even among friends, married couples, parents and children, or older people, one must not take others for granted, speak rudely, vent one's frustration, or hurt others.

Translation of the question:
Which of the following does NOT fit the spirit of "Even among close relationships, manners are necessary"?

Translation of the choices:
1. Believing that once one becomes old, anything one says to people around them will be forgiven is a misconception.
2. If they are a close friend, they will accept everything, including one's shortcomings.
3. Although family is a place where one can relax and let one's guard down, that does not mean one can say whatever one wants.
4. Parents must not take it for granted that their children will take care of them in the future.
default.q.n2-31-q71-71.why.0: (a) Choice 1 should not be selected because it agrees completely with the passage: 「周囲の人たちが我慢して聞いているのを、彼女は許されたと勘違いしていたのです」 (In reality, the people around her were patiently putting up with her, but the old woman mistakenly thought she had been forgiven). Therefore, 1 is not the inappropriate choice.
default.q.n2-31-q71-71.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because the passage states that even very close relationships require proper respect; one must not casually hurt the other person or vent one's frustration: 「『親しき仲にも礼儀あり』というのは、友達関係だけでなく... 相手を傷つけるようなことを平気で口にしたり、不愉快をのべつぶちまけてもいいというものでは決してありません」. The passage contains no claim that close friends will accept all of one's shortcomings.
default.q.n2-31-q71-71.why.2: (c) Choice 3 should not be selected because this idea completely matches the passage: 「家庭は気を許してもいいところですが、だからといって、相手を傷つけるようなことを平気で口にしたり、不愉快をのべつぶちまけてもいいというものでは決してありません」 (Although the family is a place where one can relax, that does not mean one may casually say hurtful things or constantly vent one's frustrations at others).
default.q.n2-31-q71-71.why.3: (d) Do not choose 4 because this idea fully matches the spirit of the article. The author argues that one should not interfere excessively with or impose on grown children, but should know when to withdraw: 「配偶者にも成人した子供にも立ち入りすぎた非礼はないと決心する」「親が子供にしてやれる大きな仕事の一つは、別れることを上手にやってのけることだ」.
default.q.n2-31-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4 (54 歳): The author’s son’s current age is closest to 54.
default.q.n2-31-q72-72.explanation:
Main point:
The passage discusses when the author's son became independent by entering university in Nagoya at the age of 18. More than 35 years have passed since then, and the son has been living an independent life of his own.

Question translation:
Which of the following is closest to the author's son's current age?

Answer choices:
1. 18 years old
2. 35 years old
3. 46 years old
4. 54 years old
default.q.n2-31-q72-72.why.0: (a) Do not choose 1 because 18 is the son’s age when he began attending university in Nagoya, according to the passage: 「彼は、自分の希望で十八歳のときに名古屋の大学へ進みました」. It is not his current age.
default.q.n2-31-q72-72.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is not selected because 35 years is the period that has elapsed since the child entered university: 「それからもう三十五年以上が経っています」. It is not the child’s age.
default.q.n2-31-q72-72.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is not possible because age 46 does not match the son’s calculated age: 18 plus more than 35 years equals more than 53.
default.q.n2-31-q72-72.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct. According to the passage, the author's son entered a university in Nagoya at age 18 (「十八歳のときに名古屋の大学へ進みました」), and more than 35 years have passed since then (「それからもう三十五年以上が経っています」). Therefore, he is now more than 53 years old: 18 + 35+. The closest answer is 54 (54 歳).
default.q.n2-31-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: The main point the author wants to convey is that courtesy and proper conduct must always be valued in all relationships between people.
default.q.n2-31-q73-73.explanation:
Main point:
The author asserts the importance of courtesy, restraint, and respect for personal boundaries in all human relationships—from friendships and marriage to parent-child relationships and relationships with elderly people. True love and lasting bonds require maintaining respect and knowing when to step back so that the other person can live an independent life.

Question:
What does the author most want to say in this passage?

Answer choices:
1. Courtesy and good manners should always be valued in human relationships.
2. To make children independent, parents should stop providing financial support before the children become adults.
3. Parents should not expect their children to take care of them in the future.
4. Friends who have known one another for a long time should be valued like family members.
default.q.n2-31-q73-73.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is the correct answer because the central idea throughout the passage is that the proverb “Even among close friends, manners are important” should be applied to every relationship: 「『親しき仲にも礼儀あり』というのは、友達関係だけでなく、夫婦や親子の間でも必要ですね」「だれにも甘えて不作法をしてはいけない。配偶者にも成人した子供にも立ち入りすぎた非礼はないと決心するほうが、かえって楽なのかもしれません」. The author emphasizes that everyone, whether family or friends, must maintain appropriate boundaries and respect one another.
default.q.n2-31-q73-73.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is not selected because the article never says that financial support must be cut off before the eldest child becomes an adult. In fact, the author continued providing financial support when the child entered university: 「経済的には私たちが面倒をみていましたが、そのときにいわゆる子育ては終わりました」.
default.q.n2-31-q73-73.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is not selected because the idea that parents should not depend on their children is merely an example supporting the importance of courtesy and moderation within the family, not the overall message of the entire passage.
default.q.n2-31-q73-73.why.3: (d) Do not choose 4 because the author never says that a longtime friend should be treated like a family member. Instead, the author maintains a measured distance from his biological son, treating him like someone he has known well for a long time: 「それは長くよく知っている人だから気がかりなのだと考えるようにしています」.
default.q.n2-31-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: A 35-year-old man working at a supermarket in Kawayama City.
default.q.n2-31-q74-74.explanation:
**1. Relevant information from the passage:**
- Workshop participants (対象): Working adults aged 18 or older who live or work in Kawayama City (「河山市在住・在勤の18歳以上の社会人」).
- Exclusion: Employees or civil servants of Kawayama City Hall are not included (「河山市職員を除く」).

**2. Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** Which of the following people can participate in this civic workshop?
- **Choice 1:** A 21-year-old female student from outside the city who is studying at a university in Kawayama City.
- **Choice 2:** A 35-year-old man working at a supermarket in Kawayama City.
- **Choice 3:** A 46-year-old woman who runs a tutoring class at her home outside Kawayama City.
- **Choice 4:** A 53-year-old man working in the Civic Affairs Department of Kawayama City Hall.
default.q.n2-31-q74-74.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because this person is a university student (通学—commuting to school) and lives outside the city (市外), so they are not a working adult (社会人) living or working in Kawayama City (河山市在住・在勤).
default.q.n2-31-q74-74.why.1: (b) Correct. The notice specifies that participants must be 「河山市在住・在勤の18歳以上の社会人（河山市職員を除く）」—working adults aged 18 or over who live or work in Kawayama City, excluding Kawayama City employees. The 35-year-old man working at a supermarket in Kawayama City meets all these conditions.
default.q.n2-31-q74-74.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this woman runs a tutoring class at home outside Kawayama City (河山市外); she does not live or work in Kawayama City.
default.q.n2-31-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect because this man is an employee of the Kawayama City Hall (河山市役所), while the notice clearly excludes such people: 「河山市職員を除く」 (excluding Kawayama city employees).
default.q.n2-31-q75-75.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: When registering through the website’s homepage, there is a time period during which registration is not possible.
default.q.n2-31-q75-75.explanation:
**1. Relevant information from the notice:**
- **Capacity (定員):** 20 people. If applications exceed capacity, a lottery will be held (「定員：20名（応募者多数の場合は抽選）」); applications are not accepted on a first-come, first-served basis.
- **Application methods (申し込み方法):**
  + At the 市役所市民課 counter: Applications are accepted from 9:00 to 17:00, except on Wednesdays (「水曜日を除く」).
  + By postcard (はがき): Each postcard can be used to apply for only one person (「はがき1枚につき1名のみ受付」).
  + Via the website (ホームページ): Online applications are accepted, except during the daily system-maintenance period from 2:00 to 5:00 a.m., when applications cannot be submitted (「毎日午前2:00～5:00はシステム点検のため申し込み不可」).

**2. Question and choices:**
- **Question:** Regarding applications to participate in this workshop, which of the following is correct?
- **Choice 1:** Because the capacity is limited to 20 people, applicants should apply early.
- **Choice 2:** Those applying at city hall must come during the designated hours on Wednesday.
- **Choice 3:** When applying by postcard, one postcard may be used to apply for any number of people.
- **Choice 4:** When applying through the website, there is a period during which applications cannot be submitted.
default.q.n2-31-q75-75.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the notice says 「定員：20名（応募者多数の場合は抽選）」 (Capacity: 20 people; if there are too many applicants, selection will be by lottery). Participants are chosen randomly by lottery, not on a first-come, first-served basis, so there is no need to apply early.
default.q.n2-31-q75-75.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the municipal office reception counter clearly states 「水曜日を除く」 (“excluding Wednesdays”), meaning applications are not accepted on Wednesdays.
default.q.n2-31-q75-75.why.2: (c) Incorrect because postal-card applications clearly state 「はがき1枚につき1名のみ受付」 (only one person may apply per postcard); multiple people may not apply on the same postcard.
default.q.n2-31-q75-75.why.3: (d) Correct because the website’s homepage registration instructions clearly state: 「毎日午前2:00～5:00はシステム点検のため申し込み不可」 (Applications cannot be submitted daily from 2:00 to 5:00 a.m. because of system maintenance). This means there is a time period during which applications are not accepted.
default.q.n2-31-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (続いて): 降り続く means that the rain keeps falling or continues without letup.
default.q.n2-31-q11-11.explanation:
Meaning: “The rain keeps falling continuously without letting up.”
- Grammar: The compound verb pattern 「Vます + 続く」 means to continue doing something over a period of time.
- Example: ここ数日、激しい雨が降り続いている。(Heavy rain has continued to fall for the past few days.)
default.q.n2-31-q11-11.why.0: (a) Correct: V-masu + 続く forms a compound verb meaning that an action continues without interruption; 降り続いている combines naturally with the adverb いつまでも (forever, without letting up).
default.q.n2-31-q11-11.why.1: (b) Incorrect: V-masu + かける means “to start doing,” “to leave unfinished,” or “to nearly do.” 降りかける (“start to fall” or “be in the process of falling”) does not fit with the adverb いつまでも (“forever,” “indefinitely”).
default.q.n2-31-q11-11.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 降り止む means “for the rain to stop.” With いつまでも, the negative form 降り止まない (it will not stop raining) is required; the affirmative form 降り止んでいる does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-31-q11-11.why.3: (d) Incorrect: V-masu + 始める means “to begin doing something.” 降り始める means “to begin raining” and indicates the starting point of an action, so it does not combine with the durative adverb いつまでも.
default.q.n2-31-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (一): forms the compound noun 日本一 (the best in Japan, number one in Japan).
default.q.n2-31-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence translation: "This restaurant's food really tastes like the best in Japan, doesn't it?"
- Sino-Japanese reading: 日本一 (NIHON'ICHI - number one in Japan, the best in Japan).
- Example: 富士山は日本一高い山です。(Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan.)
default.q.n2-31-q12-12.why.0: (a) Correct: The suffix 一 (ichi, “number one”) follows a noun indicating a scope, such as a place or period, to create a word meaning “the best or number one within that scope”; 日本一 means “number one in Japan.”
default.q.n2-31-q12-12.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 全 is generally used as a prefix before a noun (such as 全日本 — all-Japan, 全国 — nationwide), not after it to form 日本全.
default.q.n2-31-q12-12.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 半 (half) does not form a meaningful word when placed after 日本.
default.q.n2-31-q12-12.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 日本中 means “all over Japan” or “the whole of Japan,” referring to spatial scope. It is not used to evaluate the degree or quality of a food’s flavor (味).
default.q.n2-31-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (分け): it forms the noun 引き分け, meaning a tie or drawn result.
default.q.n2-31-q13-13.explanation:
Translation: “The match ended in a 1–1 draw.”
- Sino-Japanese roots & vocabulary: 引き分け (ひきわけ: draw, tie), 1対1 (いちたい いち: a score of one-all).
- Example: 昨日のサッカーの試合は0対0の引き分けに終わった。(Yesterday’s soccer match ended in a 0–0 draw.)
default.q.n2-31-q13-13.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 引き入れ, from 引き入れる, means “pull in,” “draw in,” or “lead water in,” and is not used for a game score.
default.q.n2-31-q13-13.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 引き出し (from the verb 引き出す) means “drawer” or “withdrawal of money” and is unrelated to sports or competitions.
default.q.n2-31-q13-13.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 引き算 (subtraction) is a mathematical term and is not used in the context of sports competition.
default.q.n2-31-q13-13.why.3: (d) Correct: 引き分け is a noun meaning “a draw” or “a tie” in a competition; 1対1で引き分けになる means “the match ends in a 1–1 draw.”
default.q.n2-31-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (塩): combined with からい, it forms the adjective 塩からい (塩辛い), meaning “salty.”
default.q.n2-31-q14-14.explanation:
Meaning: “This miso tastes too salty, doesn’t it?”
- Vocabulary: 塩辛い / 塩からい (salty), 味噌 (miso).
- Taste distinctions: 辛い (spicy), 塩辛い / しょっぱい (salty), 苦い (bitter), 酸っぱい (sour).
- Example: このスープは塩からくて飲めない。(This soup is too salty to drink.)
default.q.n2-31-q14-14.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 苦 has the i-adjective 苦い (bitter), so it cannot form 苦からい.
default.q.n2-31-q14-14.why.1: (b) Correct: 塩 (salt) combines with からい (辛い) to form 塩からい (しおからい - strongly salty), which is appropriate for describing the salty taste of miso.
default.q.n2-31-q14-14.why.2: (c) Incorrect: つよ (強) does not combine with からい to form a meaningful Japanese vocabulary word.
default.q.n2-31-q14-14.why.3: (d) Incorrect: うす (薄) appears in words such as 薄暗い, 薄味, and 薄い, but it does not combine with からい to form 薄からい.
default.q.n2-31-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (上げて), forming the compound verb 取り上げる, meaning “to discuss,” “to mention,” or “to deal with.”
default.q.n2-31-q15-15.explanation:
Sentence translation: "Let's bring this question up for discussion and consideration today."
- Vocabulary: 取り上げる: to bring up for discussion, address; also to seize or confiscate.
- Example: 次回の会議でその問題を取り上げる予定です。(We plan to bring up that issue at the next meeting.)
default.q.n2-31-q15-15.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 取り出すmeans “to take out” or “withdraw” a concrete object from inside a container (such as a bag or drawer), and is not used with “question” as its object.
default.q.n2-31-q15-15.why.1: (b) Correct: 取り上げる means “to bring up for discussion / address / deal with” a topic, question, or opinion; 質問を取り上げる means “to take up and answer a question.”
default.q.n2-31-q15-15.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 取り消す means “to cancel or withdraw” an order, decision, statement, or application, so it does not fit the context of examining and resolving the question.
default.q.n2-31-q15-15.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 取り替える/取り換える means “to exchange or replace one thing with another,” and is unnatural with 質問 in this context.
default.q.n2-31-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 接する (to come into contact with, communicate).
default.q.n2-31-q16-16.explanation:
Translation: Because I like interacting with people, I chose a job in sales.
• Kanji-based meaning: 接 (to come into contact with, interact with, adjoin).
• Related expressions: 人と接する (interact with people), 海に接する (border the sea).
• Example: 接客業はお客様と笑顔で接することが大切だ。(In customer service, it is important to interact with customers with a smile.)
default.q.n2-31-q16-16.why.0: (a) 「達する」(たっする) means “to reach” a level, number, or goal; it is not used for interpersonal relationships.
default.q.n2-31-q16-16.why.1: (b) 「接する」(せっする) in「人と接する」means to come into contact with, communicate with, or deal with people, making it highly appropriate as a reason for choosing a career in sales (営業).
default.q.n2-31-q16-16.why.2: (c) 「たがやす」(耕す) means “to plow, cultivate” (as in 田畑を耕す), which is completely inappropriate in this context.
default.q.n2-31-q16-16.why.3: (d) 「育てる」(そだてる) means to raise or cultivate someone, such as a child or subordinate. It takes を (人を育てる) and does not fit the context of choosing a business career.
default.q.n2-31-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 3. サイ式ン (the standard form is 「サイレン」—an alarm or siren, such as a fire-engine siren).
default.q.n2-31-q17-17.explanation:
Sentence meaning: At midnight, I heard a fire engine's siren near my house.
• Vocabulary: サイレン (siren, an alarm or the siren of a fire engine, ambulance, or police car).
• Common expressions: サイレンが鳴る (a siren sounds), 救急車のサイレン (an ambulance siren).
• Example: 遠くからパトカーのサイレンが聞こえてきた。(I could hear a police car's siren in the distance.)
default.q.n2-31-q17-17.why.0: (a) 「サイン」(sign) means a signature, sign, or signal; it is not used to refer to the sound of a car horn.
default.q.n2-31-q17-17.why.1: (b) 「サンプル」(sample) means a sample or test specimen; it has nothing to do with sound.
default.q.n2-31-q17-17.why.2: (c) 「サイ式ン」 is a display error derived from the original word 「サイレン」 (siren), meaning the siren or alarm of a fire engine (消防車のサイレン).
default.q.n2-31-q17-17.why.3: (d) 「サンダル」 means sandals; it has nothing to do with sound.
default.q.n2-31-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 工夫 (finding ways to arrange or improve something).
default.q.n2-31-q18-18.explanation:
Sentence translation: Because the room is small, I am experimenting and arranging things so that I can use the space as effectively as possible.
• Kanji meaning: 工夫 (devoting thought to finding an ingenious solution).
• Common expressions: 工夫を凝らす (devise improvements with great care), 色々工夫する (think of various ways to do something better).
• Example: 狭いキッチンスペースを有効に使えるように工夫した。(I devised a way to use the small kitchen space effectively.)
default.q.n2-31-q18-18.why.0: (a) 「工夫」(くふう) combines with する to mean devising and making an effort to find the best solution, here arranging the room so that its limited space can be used as effectively as possible.
default.q.n2-31-q18-18.why.1: (b) 「知恵」(ちえ) means wisdom or ingenuity. It commonly occurs in expressions such as「知恵を出す/知恵を絞る」, not directly as「知恵する」.
default.q.n2-31-q18-18.why.2: (c) 「見方」(みかた) means a way of seeing, viewpoint, or perspective (見方を変える); 「見方している」 is not grammatically appropriate in this context.
default.q.n2-31-q18-18.why.3: (d) 「小代」 is not vocabulary appropriate for the 「〜している」 structure in this context.
default.q.n2-31-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 1. すきとおって (transparent, allowing one to see through it).
default.q.n2-31-q19-19.explanation:
Sentence translation: Fish are transparent just after hatching from their eggs.
• Vocabulary: 透き通る (すきとおる): to be transparent, to be clear enough to see through.
• Kanji: 透: to pass through, be transparent; 通: to pass through.
• Common expressions: 透き通った青空 (a crystal-clear blue sky), 透き通るような声 (a clear, pure voice).
• Example: この湖の水は底まで透き通っている。(The water in this lake is clear enough to see all the way to the bottom.)
default.q.n2-31-q19-19.why.0: (a) 「すきとおる」(透き通る) means transparent or clear enough to see through, describing the body of a newly hatched fish.
default.q.n2-31-q19-19.why.1: (b) 「すく」(空く) means to be empty or uncrowded (as in お腹が空く, “to be hungry,” and 電車が空く, “for a train to be uncrowded”); it does not describe a transparent body.
default.q.n2-31-q19-19.why.2: (c) 「すれ活がって」 (from the base form 「すれ違う」) means to pass by each other or disagree, and is unrelated to physical characteristics.
default.q.n2-31-q19-19.why.3: (d) 「しずまる」(静まる/鎮まる) means “to die down” or “become quiet,” as with noise or a storm; it is not used to describe a fish's body.
default.q.n2-31-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 1. もったいない (wasteful, a shame to waste).
default.q.n2-31-q20-20.explanation:
- Translation: Throwing away food that is still edible is such a waste.
• Vocabulary: 勿体無い (もったいない: wasteful, a shame).
