• Common expressions: 時間を無駄にしてはもったいない (It would be a waste to spend time uselessly), もったいないお言葉 (That is too kind; I am not worthy of such praise).
• Example: まだ使えるノートを捨てるのはもったいない。(It is wasteful to throw away a notebook that can still be used.)
default.q.n2-31-q20-20.why.0: (a) 「もったいない」(勿体無い) means wasteful, especially when throwing away something that still has practical value, such as edible food.
default.q.n2-31-q20-20.why.1: (b) 「おもたい」(重たい) means heavy or burdensome, physically or emotionally, so it does not fit the sentence's meaning.
default.q.n2-31-q20-20.why.2: (c) 「馬鹿らしい」(ばからしい) means foolish, ridiculous, or absurd, especially when doing something pointless;「もったいない」is more natural when talking about wasting food.
default.q.n2-31-q20-20.why.3: (d) 「やむをえない」(止むを得ない) means unavoidable or having no other choice, which is completely opposite to criticizing the act of throwing away food.
default.q.n2-31-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 4. チャンス (opportunity).
default.q.n2-31-q21-21.explanation:
Translation: Everyone has an equal chance. (Note: 「誰にでも」in the question was misrecognized; it means “for anyone.”)
• Vocabulary: チャンス (chance, opportunity, good fortune).
• Common expressions: チャンスをつかむ (seize an opportunity), チャンスを逃す (miss an opportunity), チャンスを生かす (make use of an opportunity).
• Example: 誰にでも一度は大きなチャンスが巡ってくる。(Everyone gets a major opportunity at least once.)
default.q.n2-31-q21-21.why.0: (a) 「スケジ画ール」 is an error for 「スケジュール」, meaning “schedule” or “timetable”; it does not combine with 「平等にある」.
default.q.n2-31-q21-21.why.1: (b) 「コース」 means a course, route, or meal course, so it does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n2-31-q21-21.why.2: (c) 「式ジャー」 is an incorrectly formed character combination and has no suitable meaning in the sentence.
default.q.n2-31-q21-21.why.3: (d) 「チャンス」(chance) means “opportunity”; the sentence expresses the familiar truth 「チャンスは誰にでも平等にある」(Opportunities are equally available to everyone).
default.q.n2-31-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 短い (in the idiom「気が短い」: hot-tempered, impatient).
default.q.n2-31-q22-22.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Because the director has a short temper, the employees quickly finish their work so they will not be scolded.
• Idiomatic expressions with 気:
- 気が短い: short-tempered, impatient.
- 気が長い: calm, patient, unhurried.
- 気が小さい: timid, easily frightened.
- 気が大きい: generous, easygoing (or reckless when drunk).
• Example: 彼は気が短くて、少し待たされただけですぐ怒る。(He is very short-tempered and gets angry as soon as he has to wait even a little.)
default.q.n2-31-q22-22.why.0: (a) 「気が小さい」means timid or fainthearted; it is not the reason why someone would fear being scolded.
default.q.n2-31-q22-22.why.1: (b) 「気が大きい」 means generous or broad-minded (or overly emboldened by alcohol), not prone to losing one's temper.
default.q.n2-31-q22-22.why.2: (c) 「気が短い」is an idiom describing someone hot-tempered, impatient, and easily irritated, which fits the employees' fear of being scolded (怒られないように).
default.q.n2-31-q22-22.why.3: (d) 「気が長い」 means patient, calm, or tolerant, which is the opposite of the context requiring urgent action.
default.q.n2-31-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (よく話す).
default.q.n2-31-q23-23.explanation:
• Translation: Mr./Ms. Koizumi is a talkative person / likes to chat.
• Vocabulary:
  - 「おしゃべり」(noun / na-adjective): a talkative person, someone who enjoys chatting, casual conversation (synonyms: よく話す人, 口数が多い).
  - Example: 彼女はおしゃべりに夢中で、周りの声が聞こえなかった。(She was so absorbed in chatting that she couldn’t hear the voices around her.)
default.q.n2-31-q23-23.why.0: (a) (1) 「よく飲む」 means “drink often” (water/alcohol), so it does not correspond to 「おしゃべり」.
default.q.n2-31-q23-23.why.1: (b) (2) 「よく食べる」 means “eat often” or “eat a lot,” not “like talking.”
default.q.n2-31-q23-23.why.2: (c) (3) 「よく話す」 means “to talk a lot” or “be talkative,” synonymous with the noun/adjective 「おしゃべり」(a talkative person, someone who talks a lot).
default.q.n2-31-q23-23.why.3: (d) (4) 「よく怒る」means to get angry easily or often, so it is incorrect.
default.q.n2-31-q24-24.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: That person probably won't attend the party.
• Vocabulary and kanji explanation:
  - 「おそらく」(恐らく): probably, likely (an adverb expressing a high degree of probability, more formal/polite than たぶん, often used with endings such as 〜だろう and 〜のではないか).
  - Example: おそらく明日は雨が降るだろう。(It will probably rain tomorrow.)
default.q.n2-31-q24-24.why.0: (a) (1) 「たしかに」(certainly, indeed) is used to affirm a fact or express agreement; it is not an adverb expressing speculation.
default.q.n2-31-q24-24.why.1: (b) (2) 「もちろん」 (“of course,” “naturally”) indicates something obvious and beyond dispute, so it is not appropriate.
default.q.n2-31-q24-24.why.2: (c) (3) 「たとえ」(even if, supposing that) is an adverb commonly used with hypothetical patterns such as 「〜ても / 〜でも」, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-31-q24-24.why.3: (d) (4) 「たぶん」 (probably, perhaps) is an adverb of conjecture and is synonymous with 「おそらく」 when used with the ending 「〜だろう」.
default.q.n2-31-q25-25.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: The suitcase weighs approximately 3 kg.
• Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese reading notes:
  - 「約」(やく): approximately, about, roughly (synonyms: およそ, だいたい).
  - 「およそ」(凡そ): roughly, approximately, about.
  - Example: 会場にはおよそ100人の客が集まった。(Approximately 100 guests gathered at the venue.)
default.q.n2-31-q25-25.why.0: (a) (1) 「あと」 means “remaining” or “after,” indicating what is left or the following distance or period, as in あと3キロ. It does not mean “approximately.”
default.q.n2-31-q25-25.why.1: (b) (2) 「もう」 (“already / any more”) expresses completion or an additional amount; it is not synonymous with 「約」.
default.q.n2-31-q25-25.why.2: (c) (3) 「およそ」 (approximately, roughly) is an adverb indicating an estimated quantity and is completely synonymous with 「約」.
default.q.n2-31-q25-25.why.3: (d) (4) 「たった」(only, merely) emphasizes a very small quantity and is not equivalent to 「約」.
default.q.n2-31-q26-26.explanation:
• Sentence translation: I apologized to Mr./Ms. Ono about what happened the other day.
• Vocabulary:
  - 「おわびする」 (お詫びする): apologize, offer one's apologies; the formal, humble form of 詫びる (わびる), synonymous with 謝る (あやまる).
  - Note the distinction: 詫びる/謝る (apologize) is different from 感謝する (thank) and 怒鳴る (shout angrily).
  - Example: 迷惑をかけたことを心からお詫び申し上げます。 (I sincerely apologize for causing you trouble.)
default.q.n2-31-q26-26.why.0: (a) (1) 「怒鳴った」 (“shouted angrily” or “yelled”; kanji: 怒鳴る) means speaking loudly in anger, which is opposite to an apologetic attitude.
default.q.n2-31-q26-26.why.1: (b) (2) 「謝った」(apologized) is the past form of 謝る (あやまる), synonymous with「おわびした」(詫びる / お詫びする: to apologize).
default.q.n2-31-q26-26.why.2: (c) (3) 「感謝した」(感謝する: to thank) means to express gratitude or appreciation, not to apologize.
default.q.n2-31-q26-26.why.3: (d) (4) 「質問した」(asked a question - 質問する) means to ask or question someone and is unrelated.
default.q.n2-31-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (あちこち).
default.q.n2-31-q27-27.explanation:
• Meaning: Because the dog had gone missing, I ran all over the place looking for it.
• Vocabulary:
  - 「ほうぼう」(方々): everywhere, in all directions; synonymous with あちこち and 諸方 (しょほう).
  - 「探しまわる」(さがしまわる): search all around, look everywhere.
  - Example: ほうぼう手を尽くしたが、見つからなかった。(I tried everything and searched everywhere, but I could not find it.)
default.q.n2-31-q27-27.why.0: (a) (1) 「あちこち」(here and there, in various places) is the exact synonym of「ほうぼう」(方々: everywhere, in all directions).
default.q.n2-31-q27-27.why.1: (b) (2) 「あれこれ」(this and that) refers to various things or rambling thoughts; it is not used to indicate a direction or location.
default.q.n2-31-q27-27.why.2: (c) (3) 「うろうろ」(to wander around, loiter) is an onomatopoeic expression describing aimless movement; it does not mean searching in many different places.
default.q.n2-31-q27-27.why.3: (d) (4) 「まごまご」 describes being bewildered or confused and not knowing what to do, so it is unsuitable here.
default.q.n2-31-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is sentence 1 because 「きつい」can describe harsh or severe words that emotionally hurt the listener.
default.q.n2-31-q28-28.explanation: 「きつい」 has the following main meanings: (1) tight or constricting (for clothing or shoes: 靴がきつい); (2) demanding, strenuous, or harsh (for work, schedules, or words: きつい仕事, 一言がきつい); (3) strong or intense (for smells or alcohol: 匂いがきつい, お酒がきつい); (4) strong-willed or severe in personality (性格がきつい). Example:「今週は残業が多くてスケジュールがきつい。」(I have so much overtime this week that my schedule is extremely demanding.)
default.q.n2-31-q28-28.why.0: Correct: Here,「きつい」means harsh, severe, or biting words (辛辣・厳しい) that hurt the listener or are difficult to accept.
default.q.n2-31-q28-28.why.1: Incorrect: For an English sentence or grammatical explanation that is difficult to understand, use「難しい」(difficult) or「難解な」;「きつい」does not describe the difficulty of wording or grammar.
default.q.n2-31-q28-28.why.2: Incorrect. When overeating causes an uncomfortably full stomach, use「苦しい」or「お腹がいっぱい」. 「きつい」is used for tight clothing (ズボンがきつい), not directly for a stomach that feels full.
default.q.n2-31-q28-28.why.3: Incorrect: To describe a cramped, confining room, use 「狭い」 (narrow) or 「窮屈な」 (cramped or constricted). 「きつい部屋」 is not used to describe the physical space of a room.
default.q.n2-31-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is question 2 because 「味わう」 (mistakenly printed as 味山 in the test) correctly conveys the meaning of savoring or tasting again the familiar flavor of a dish after being away from home for a long time.
default.q.n2-31-q29-29.explanation:
「味わう」(which was incorrectly rendered as 味山 in the question due to a spelling or OCR error) has two main meanings: (1) to savor the flavor of food or drink carefully (料理・お酒を味わう); (2) to deeply experience or undergo an emotion or aspect of life (勝利の喜びを味わう, 人生の苦しみを味わう).
Example:「秋の味覚を心ゆくまで味わった。」(I savored the flavors of autumn to my heart’s content.)
default.q.n2-31-q29-29.why.0: Incorrect: When inviting everyone to start eating and drinking together during an ordinary meal, Japanese people use「いただきましょう」or「食べましょう」.「味わいましょう」does not sound natural as an invitation to eat.
default.q.n2-31-q29-29.why.1: Correct: 「味わう」(to savor, appreciate the flavor of) combines naturally with 「母の料理」when describing the experience of enjoying one’s mother’s cooking again after being away from home for a long time.
default.q.n2-31-q29-29.why.2: Incorrect: To taste seawater to find out what it tastes like, use 「なめてみたら」 (try licking it), 「飲んでみたら」 (try drinking it), or 「味をみたら」. 「味わう」 (to savor something delicious / experience something deeply) is not used for seawater.
default.q.n2-31-q29-29.why.3: Incorrect: For spending enjoyable time with friends, the standard collocations are 「楽しい時間を過ごした」 or 「楽しんだ」. 「時間を味わった」 is not used.
default.q.n2-31-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is sentence 4 because「工夫して使う」is the standard expression for figuring out how to arrange and use something skillfully to make the most of limited space.
default.q.n2-31-q30-30.explanation: 「工夫」(くふう) means putting thought and effort into finding a better method, developing a new idea, or arranging things skillfully to achieve better results. Common expressions include 「工夫を凝らす」(devise something creatively) and 「工夫して～する」(find a clever way to do something). Example:「限られた予算の中で工夫してイベントを成功させた。」(We used our ingenuity to make the event a success on a limited budget.)
default.q.n2-31-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect: To praise someone for sewing a dress themselves, praise their skill with expressions such as 「器用ですね」(You are really skillful) or 「上手ですね」. 「工夫していますね」alone does not praise sewing ability.
default.q.n2-31-q30-30.why.1: Incorrect. To express making an effort or studying hard to pass a university entrance exam, use 「努力すれば」 (“if one makes an effort”) or 「一生懸命勉強すれば」, not 「工夫すれば」.
default.q.n2-31-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect: In a friendship, to express getting along or being close, use「仲良く付き合う」(to associate closely) or「うまく付き合う」. 「工夫して付き合う」is not used in this sense.
default.q.n2-31-q30-30.why.3: Correct: 「工夫する」 means thinking of and finding an optimal solution. Its use in 「狭い部屋を工夫して使う」, meaning finding a smart way to make effective use of a small room, is precise and standard.
default.q.n2-31-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is sentence 3 because「費やす」(ついやす) is the verb conventionally used with quantifiable resources that are consumed, such as time (時間) and money (お金).
default.q.n2-31-q31-31.explanation: 「費やす」(ついやす) means to spend or devote a large amount of a limited resource—such as time, money, effort, years, or energy—on a particular purpose. Common collocations include:「時間／お金／労力／歳月／エネルギーを費やす」. Example:「彼は半生をその研究に費やした。」(He devoted half of his life to that research.)
default.q.n2-31-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect: With the noun 「努力」, use 「努力を重ねて」 (“continue making efforts”) or 「努力をして」; 「努力を費やす」 is not used.
default.q.n2-31-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect. When referring to personnel mobilized for a festival, use 「人手をかけて」(spend considerable manpower) or 「人手を割いて」, not 「人手をついやす」.
default.q.n2-31-q31-31.why.2: Correct: 「費やす」, meaning to spend a large amount of resources, commonly takes nouns referring to time and money, as in 「たくさんの時間とお金を費やした」.
default.q.n2-31-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect: When knitting a sweater as an expression of a mother’s love, the appropriate expressions are 「愛情を込めて」 (with love and affection) or 「愛を注いで」 (devoting love), not 「愛を費やす」.
default.q.n2-31-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is sentence 2 because「経験が乏しい」(to have little or limited experience) is a very common and accurate fixed expression in Japanese.
default.q.n2-31-q32-32.explanation: 「乏しい」(とぼしい) describes a state of lacking, scarcity, or poor quantity or quality in resources or abstract things. Common examples include: 「経験／知識／資源／資金／表情が乏しい」(lacking experience, poor in knowledge, scarce resources, insufficient funds, an expressionless face). Example: 「この地域は天然資源が乏しい。」(This region is poor in natural resources.)
default.q.n2-31-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect. When describing poor or weak physical strength, Japanese uses 「体力がない」 or 「体力が不足している」, not 「体力が乏しい」.
default.q.n2-31-q32-32.why.1: Correct: 「乏しい」 (“scarce, meager”) is used with abstract nouns; 「経験が乏しい」 (“to have little experience / lack experience”) is a very natural and accurate collocation.
default.q.n2-31-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect. To say that someone has few acquaintances or friends, use 「友達が少ない」, “have few friends,” not 「友達が乏しい」 to describe the number of people.
default.q.n2-31-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect: for a test score or exam performance below average, use 「点数が低くて」(the score is low) or 「悪くて」(poor), not 「とぼしい」.
default.q.n2-31-q1-1.explanation:
Translation: They bumped shoulders, which led to an argument or fight.
- Vocabulary & Sino-Japanese reading: 肩 (KEN) means shoulder.
- Example: 重い荷物を持って肩が凝った。(My shoulders became stiff from carrying heavy luggage.)
default.q.n2-31-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「そで」(袖) means “sleeve”; it is not the reading of 肩.
default.q.n2-31-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「けん」is the on-reading of 肩, as in「肩甲骨」(けんこうこつ) and「比肩」(ひけん). When used alone as a noun, it is read with its kun-reading, かた.
default.q.n2-31-q1-1.why.2: (c) 「わき」(脇) means armpit, side, or beside; it is not the reading of 肩.
default.q.n2-31-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「かた」(肩) is the correct kun-reading of 肩, meaning shoulder.
default.q.n2-31-q2-2.explanation:
Sentence meaning: My older brother is an X-ray technician.
- Vocabulary and kanji: 技師 means a technician or technical specialist (技 has the On-reading ぎ, and 師 has the On-reading し).
- Example: 彼女は臨床検査技師として病院で働いている。(She works at a hospital as a clinical laboratory technician.)
default.q.n2-31-q2-2.why.0: (a)「ぎし」is the correct on-reading of the compound「技師」(技: ぎ + 師: し).
default.q.n2-31-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「わざし」incorrectly combines the kun-reading「わざ」(技) with the on-reading「し」(師).
default.q.n2-31-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「きし」has the wrong reading for 技 (技 is read as ぎ, not き, in this word).
default.q.n2-31-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: I was misunderstood by my friends and was told, “I don’t want to see you anymore.”
- Vocabulary and kanji-based reading: 誤解 (misunderstanding; misinterpretation). The kanji 誤 is read ご, and 解 is read かい.
- Example: 私の言ったことが誤解を招いてしまった。(What I said caused a misunderstanding.)
default.q.n2-31-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「ごうかい」 (豪快) means big-hearted or generous; the 誤 in 誤解 has the short reading ご, not the long vowel ごう.
default.q.n2-31-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「ごがい」 has the wrong reading for 解; in this word, 解 retains the sound かい and does not become the voiced sound がい.
default.q.n2-31-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「ごっかい」is incorrect because 誤解 is pronounced ごかい, without the geminate consonant っ.
default.q.n2-31-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「ごかい」 is the correct on'yomi reading of 「誤解」 (誤: ご + 解: かい).
default.q.n2-31-q4-4.explanation:
Sentence meaning: This exercise seems to be effective for losing weight.
- Vocabulary: 効果 means effect, effectiveness (効 is read as こう, and 果 is read as か).
- Example: この薬は頭痛によく効果がある。(This medicine is very effective for headaches.)
default.q.n2-31-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「こうか」 is the correct on'yomi reading of 「効果」 (効: こう + 果: か).
default.q.n2-31-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「ごうか」(豪華) means luxurious or lavish; the character 効 has the reading こう, not the voiced reading ごう.
default.q.n2-31-q4-4.why.2: (c)「きか」is an incorrect reading of 効 (効 does not have the on-reading き).
default.q.n2-31-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「きが」(飢餓) means famine/starvation, and is completely incorrect as the reading of 効果.
default.q.n2-31-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: The exam will take place the week after next.
- Vocabulary: 再来週 (さらいしゅう) means the week after next.
- Time expressions: 先週 (せんしゅう — last week) / 今週 (こんしゅう — this week) / 来週 (らいしゅう — next week) / 再来週 (さらいしゅう — the week after next).
default.q.n2-31-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「週」(しゅう) means “week”; it is missing the prefix 「さらい」(再来).
default.q.n2-31-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「再来週」 (さらいしゅう) is the correct kanji expression for “the week after next.”
default.q.n2-31-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「再来月」(さらいげつ) means the month after next, not さらいしゅう.
default.q.n2-31-q5-5.why.3: (d) 「来週」 (らいしゅう) means next week, not さらいしゅう.
default.q.n2-31-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 訪問.
default.q.n2-31-q6-6.explanation:
Meaning: I visited my teacher's home.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 訪問 (HŌMON — visit, visiting).
- Example: 明日、取引先を訪問する予定です。(I plan to visit a business partner tomorrow.)
default.q.n2-31-q6-6.why.0: (a) Correct: 「訪問」(ほうもん) means to visit or call on someone.
default.q.n2-31-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect: The wrong kanji「門」(gate; on-reading モン) is used instead of「問」(to ask; question).
default.q.n2-31-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect: Both 「彷」(as in 彷徨) and 「門」(gate) are used incorrectly.
default.q.n2-31-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「彷」 (with the 彳 radical) is mistakenly used instead of 「訪」 (with the 言 radical).
default.q.n2-31-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 準備.
default.q.n2-31-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: The preparations for going out are finished.
- Sino-Japanese roots: 準備 (CHUẨN BỊ - to prepare, make preparations).
- Example: 旅行の準備はもう終わりましたか。(Have you finished preparing for the trip?)
default.q.n2-31-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect: It uses the wrong kanji 「順」(as in 順番 and 順調) instead of 「準」.
default.q.n2-31-q7-7.why.1: (b) Correct: 「準備」(じゅんび) means to prepare or make preparations.
default.q.n2-31-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect: Both 「順」 and 「捕」(as in “to catch”) are used incorrectly.
default.q.n2-31-q7-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「捕」 (to catch; on-reading ホ) is used incorrectly instead of 「備」.
default.q.n2-31-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 政治.
default.q.n2-31-q8-8.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I hear that he is not interested in politics.
- Kanji note: 政治 means politics or the affairs of government.
- Example: 彼は大学で政治学を専攻している。(He is majoring in political science at university.)
default.q.n2-31-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect: It uses the wrong kanji, 「路」(road, route; on-reading ロ), instead of 「治」.
default.q.n2-31-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect: The wrong kanji 「台」 is used (platform/stand; on-readings: ダイ, タイ).
default.q.n2-31-q8-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The kanji 「示」, as in 指示 and 表示, has the on-reading ジ but does not combine to form the word せいじ.
default.q.n2-31-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: For some reason, my chest feels tight and uncomfortable.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 胸 (kyō - chest, ribcage, or one's heart and feelings).
- Body-part kanji containing the flesh radical 月: 腕 (うで - arm), 腹 (はら - abdomen), 胸 (むね - chest).
- Example: 不安で胸がいっぱいになった。(My heart was filled with anxiety.)
default.q.n2-31-q9-9.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「脂」 is read as 「あぶら」 (fat, grease).
default.q.n2-31-q9-9.why.3: (d) Correct: 「胸」(むね) means chest, breast, or heart.
default.q.n2-31-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: My eyesight has gotten worse lately, so threading a needle is very difficult.
- Kanji etymology: 針 (needle).
- Common expression: 針に糸を通す (to thread a needle).
- Metal-related objects containing the radical 金: 針 (はり - needle), 釘 (くぎ - nail), 鋏 (はさみ - scissors), 鋲 (びょう - tack, thumbtack).

Translation: Athlete Yamada was selected to participate in the national tournament as the representative of the prefecture.

Meaning: It is precisely because he has gone through many experiences himself that he can offer suitable and well-considered advice.

default.q.n2-32-q36-36.why.2: Correct because 「plain form + からこそ」 means "precisely because..., that is why..." and emphasizes the fundamental reason leading to the result in the following clause. It often occurs with 〜のだ or 〜わけだ.
default.q.n2-32-q36-36.why.3: Incorrect because 「〜ものだから」 is used to explain a reason with an apologetic or defensive nuance, often for an inconvenience or an unintended personal outcome.

Meaning: Regarding this matter, we have also carried out everything we could possibly think of.

default.q.n2-32-q37-37.why.2: Incorrect because 「〜まで」 means “to the extent that / merely,” and does not form a natural modifying phrase in this context.

default.q.n2-32-q38-38.why.3: Correct because 「〜にすぎない」 (“merely ...” or “only ...”) emphasizes that something is limited or small in degree, as in returning only once every two or three years.

default.q.n2-32-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: You said you had read that book recently, but for someone who has only just finished reading it, you have already completely forgotten its contents.
・N2 grammar pattern: 『〜にしては』 (considering that... / for...): expresses a result that is contrary to the usual expectation based on the standard stated in the preceding clause.
・Distinction: 『V-たばかり』 (have just finished doing) differs from 『V-てばかり』 (do nothing but keep doing something).
・Example: 彼は日本に10年も住んでいるにしては、日本語があまり上手ではない。 (Considering that he has lived in Japan for 10 years, his Japanese is not very good.)

default.q.n2-32-q40-40.why.1: Incorrect because 「〜だけあって」 is used when the result in the following clause fully matches expectations. If that were the intended meaning, the person should remember it very clearly, whereas this sentence describes the unusual opposite—having forgotten the content.
default.q.n2-32-q40-40.why.2: The usage is incorrect because 「〜てばかり」 (“do nothing but…”) expresses frequency or a repeated habit; it does not describe an action that happened very recently, as 「読んだばかり」 does.
default.q.n2-32-q40-40.why.3: Correct because it properly combines 「V-たばかり」 (having just finished doing something) with 「〜にしては」 (even though / considering that...), meaning “You just finished reading it, yet you’ve already forgotten everything, haven’t you?” This expresses a contradiction with what would normally be expected.

default.q.n2-32-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning: Whenever people are told, "Don't tell anyone," they cannot help wanting to tell someone.

  1. 『V-ずにいられない / V-ずにはいられない』: cannot help ... / cannot suppress the feeling or urge to do something.

・Example: おもしろい映画を見ると、だれかに話さずにはいられないものだ。 (When people watch an interesting movie, they naturally cannot help wanting to tell someone about it.)

default.q.n2-32-q41-41.why.2: Correct because 「V-ずにはいられない / V-ずにいられない」 (cannot suppress the urge to / cannot help but...) combines with 「〜ものだ」 (a natural human tendency or psychological principle), expressing the idea that when people are forbidden to speak, they naturally cannot resist wanting to tell someone.

default.q.n2-32-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: Although this company's salary is not particularly high, no one quits because the working environment is very good.
・N2 grammar patterns:
  1. 『〜わけではない』: “it is not necessarily the case that...” or “it is not that...” (partial negation).
  2. 『〜ものの』: “although...,” “even though...” (a concessive contrast connecting two clauses).
・Example: 全問正解できたわけではないものの、合格点は取れたと思う。 (Although I did not necessarily get every question right, I think I got a passing score.)

default.q.n2-32-q42-42.why.2: Incorrect because 「〜わけがない」(there is absolutely no way...) expresses complete negation and is not suitable for describing a relative degree of evaluation ("not necessarily too high").

Meaning: Although the two people were meeting for the first time then, they looked as if they had known each other for a long time.

default.q.n2-32-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 溢れている.
default.q.n2-32-q50-50.explanation: The verb 「溢れる」(to overflow, be filled with, be abundant) is an intransitive verb describing a change of state. When describing information, documents, goods, and so on as overflowing or being widespread in society at the present time, the progressive/resultative form 「～ている」 must be used: 「溢れている」. The dictionary form (溢れる), past form (溢れた), and past progressive form (溢れていた) do not correctly express a state that currently exists and continues in the context of describing the present situation.
default.q.n2-32-q50-50.why.0: (a) 「溢れる」: The dictionary form of the verb describes a future action or a general truth/rule; it does not express an already existing state of overflowing at the present moment.
default.q.n2-32-q50-50.why.1: (b) 「溢れた」: The past/completed form describes an event that occurred and ended in the past, so it is unsuitable for describing a situation that is currently continuing.
default.q.n2-32-q50-50.why.2: (c) 「溢れている」: The 「～ている」form expresses a resulting state that continues in the present ("is overflowing / is abundant"), which accurately describes the situation in the passage.
default.q.n2-32-q50-50.why.3: (d) 「溢れていた」is the past progressive form, describing a state that existed in the past but no longer exists, or used when reminiscing about the past. It does not fit the present context.
default.q.n2-32-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ポイントとは.
default.q.n2-32-q51-51.explanation: The N2 grammar pattern 「～とは」(a shorter form of 「というのは」) introduces a topic, term, or concept, followed by a definition or explanation of its nature in the predicate. In this sentence, the writer wants to emphasize and explain the answer to the question “What exactly is the key point here?” Therefore, the particle 「とは」combined with 「ポイント」to form 「ポイントとは」is the most accurate choice.
default.q.n2-32-q51-51.why.0: (a) 「ポイントが」: The particle 「が」 simply marks the subject of the directly following predicate; it is not used to foreground a topic or concept that defines or explains the entire sentence.
default.q.n2-32-q51-51.why.1: (b) 「ポイントには」: It means “as for the key point,” indicating direction or the target of an action, and is not used to introduce a definition.
default.q.n2-32-q51-51.why.2: (c) 「ポイントでは」: Indicates a scope, location, or method (“as for the key point...”), so it is not suitable for introducing the topic to be clarified.
default.q.n2-32-q51-51.why.3: (d) 「ポイントとは」: The structure 「N + とは」 introduces a topic or concept to be defined or clarified, presenting its essential meaning ("The key point is..."), which fits the explanation that follows exactly.
default.q.n2-32-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 1. こういうふうに.
default.q.n2-32-q52-52.explanation: In Japanese argumentative writing, the demonstrative system (Ko-So-A-Do) follows clear usage rules. The 「こ」 group, specifically 「こういうふうに」 (in the following way; like this), is commonly used to direct the reader’s attention to specific content or a method that the writer is about to present. By contrast, the 「そ」 group (そういうふうに) refers back to content mentioned earlier, the 「あ」 group (ああいうふうに) refers to general knowledge shared by both parties, and the 「ど」 group (どんなふうに) is used in questions. Therefore, 「こういうふうに」 is the correct answer.
default.q.n2-32-q52-52.why.0: (a) 「こういうふうに」: This demonstrative expression in the Ko-series directs the reader to the manner or method that the writer is about to explain in detail immediately afterward (“as follows” or “in this way”), making it natural and accurate for introducing the text.
default.q.n2-32-q52-52.why.1: (b) 「そういうふうに」: This demonstrative expression from the “so” series refers back to something mentioned in the preceding sentence. It is not used to direct the reader toward content that will be introduced afterward.
default.q.n2-32-q52-52.why.2: (c) 「ああいうふうに」: The “A” demonstrative system refers to something that both the writer and reader clearly know from real-life experience; it is not used to introduce a new point.
default.q.n2-32-q52-52.why.3: (d) 「どんなふうに」: An interrogative expression meaning “in what way?” It does not fit the author’s affirmative, guiding statement.
default.q.n2-32-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 3. たとえば.
default.q.n2-32-q53-53.explanation: Looking at the logical connection between the sentences: the preceding sentence presents a general method or principle, while the sentence containing blank 53 begins giving a specific case to illustrate that principle more clearly. The most appropriate conjunction for introducing an example is 「たとえば」(for example). Other conjunctions such as 「つまり」(in other words), 「ところで」(by the way / changing the subject), and 「一方」(on the other hand) do not express an illustrative relationship.
default.q.n2-32-q53-53.why.0: (a) 「つまり」: A conjunction used to summarize or restate the preceding idea in another way (“in short/that is”), not to introduce a specific example.
default.q.n2-32-q53-53.why.1: (b) 「ところで」: A conjunction used to shift to a completely different topic (“by the way”), so it does not fit a sentence that continues analyzing the content.
default.q.n2-32-q53-53.why.2: (c) 「たとえば」: A conjunction used to give an illustrative example of the statement or method mentioned in the previous sentence (“for example / such as”), fitting the development of the passage perfectly.
default.q.n2-32-q53-53.why.3: (d) 「一方」is a conjunction indicating contrast or two parallel aspects of an issue (“on the other hand”/“in contrast”), so it does not fit a context that introduces an example.
default.q.n2-32-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 実践させてみることだ.
default.q.n2-32-q54-54.explanation: The N2 grammar pattern 「V-る / V-ない + ことだ」 means “You should V” or “The best thing to do is V.” It is used when the writer offers advice or summarizes the most effective method for someone else. In the concluding sentence, the author summarizes the solution and gives practical advice: let the people involved (students, employees, etc.) try practicing directly. Combined with the causative and experiential form 「実践させてみる」(let them try practicing), 「実践させてみることだ」 means “The important thing—or the best advice—is to let them try practicing in a real situation.”
default.q.n2-32-q54-54.why.0: (a) 「実践させてみるのだ」: The pattern「～のだ」is used for assertion, explanation, or a subjective authoritative tone. It is not the standard structure for presenting advice or a concluding solution.
default.q.n2-32-q54-54.why.1: (b) 「実践させてみることだ」: The N2 grammar pattern 「V-る + ことだ」 is used to give advice or state a lesson about the best solution (“the best thing to do is...”); it is therefore highly suitable as the article’s concluding, guidance-oriented sentence.
default.q.n2-32-q54-54.why.2: (c) 「実践させてみるのがよい」 is a general comment or evaluation and lacks the force and advisory, concluding nuance of the specialized structure 「～ことだ」.
default.q.n2-32-q54-54.why.3: (d) 「実践させてみてはどうか」: The pattern 「～てはどうか」 is a suggestion phrased as a question (“Why not try...?”), making it more conversational and direct than the argumentative/advisory style required here.
default.q.n2-32-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (文章理解より書き込みに力をさいではいけない。): You must not devote more effort to making notes or marking up the text than to understanding it.
default.q.n2-32-q55-55.explanation:
• Main point:
The author emphasizes that the fundamental and most important purpose of reading books and documents is to quickly and accurately understand the text (「あくまでも大事なのは、文章を素早く正しく理解することです」). Annotations are merely a supporting tool; it is enough to make quick, simple marks that will be understandable when reviewing them later. One should not spend too much effort making neat drawings or carefully ruled lines, because doing so causes distraction and wastes time.

• Question translation:
筆者の考えに合うものはどれか。
(Which statement agrees with the author’s view?)

• Answer choices:
1. 書き込みは雑にしてはいけない。 (Annotations must not be careless.)
2. 書き込みには集中力が必要だ。 (Concentration is necessary for making annotations.)
3. きれいな書き込みができる人は、文章もよく読める。 (People who can make neat annotations can also read texts well.)
4. 文章理解より書き込みに力をさいではいけない。 (One must not devote more effort to annotations than to understanding the text.)
default.q.n2-32-q55-55.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author says that notes only need to be written quickly by hand (「書き込みはフリーハンドでスピーディーにできればよいのです」) and be understandable when reread; careful, neat writing is unnecessary (「それ以上の丁寧さはムダ以外の何物でもありません」).
default.q.n2-32-q55-55.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author advises readers not to become distracted by drawing lines or adding beautiful symbols (「美しい線を引いたり、きれいに記号をつけたりすることに気を取られないでほしい」); their attention should be devoted to grasping the content.
default.q.n2-32-q55-55.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because it completely contradicts the passage; the author says that people who become absorbed in carefully drawing and coloring often retain nothing of the content in their minds (「こういう人に限って、内容は頭に入っていないものです」).
default.q.n2-32-q55-55.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the author emphasizes that the essential point is to understand the text quickly and accurately (「あくまでも大事なのは、文章を素早く正しく理解することです」). Therefore, readers should not place excessive importance or effort on careful note-taking and diagramming (「それ以上の丁寧さはムダ以外の何物でもありません」).
default.q.n2-32-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Although weeds may appear unnecessary, the author argues that they actually play a very important role for rice-field embankments and rice paddies.

- Main idea: The passage compares beautiful flowers in a flower shop with weeds by the roadside. Although weeds look plain and are not grown for people to admire, their firm roots help prevent soil erosion and maintain the soil's ability to retain water for rice fields. The author concludes that whether a plant is useful cannot be judged from its appearance alone.

  1. Like beautiful flowers, weeds can please people's eyes.
  2. Since weeds absorb water from rice fields, it is better to pull them out.
  3. It is wrong to pull out weeds for the sake of appearance.
  4. Although they may appear unnecessary, they actually play an important role.

default.q.n2-32-q56-56.why.3: (d) Correct because the author emphasizes that weeds, although they may look useless or plain, help hold the soil in place and maintain water retention: 「田んぼなどの土手に生えている雑草は、見た目は地味でも力強く根を張って土をつかみ、土手が崩れないようにしています。観賞用にもならないと言って、雑草を取り除いてしまったら、土手は、崩れやすくなり、田んぼの保水力も弱まってしまいます。つまり、植物が有用かどうかは、見た目からはわからないのではないでしょうか。」
default.q.n2-32-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: The sentence contains no excessive embellishment or decoration.
default.q.n2-32-q57-57.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage discusses the appeal of an excellent short story's opening, using "Rashomon" as an example. The author says that the beauty and appeal of the prose lie in removing anything superfluous, using concise wording, and carefully polishing it; it is precisely the lack of embellishment and showiness that creates the true beauty of the writing.
- Question translation: What kind of prose does the author say is appealing?
- Choice translations:
  1. Prose without unnecessary embellishment.
  2. Prose that makes the scenery appear before one's eyes.
  3. Prose that is easy to read aloud.
  4. Prose that is easy to understand and familiar.
default.q.n2-32-q57-57.why.0: (a) Correct because the author states: 「一切の無駄を排し、研ぎ澄まされた最小限の言葉だけで、鮮やかな情景を浮かび上がらせています」 and 「文章はキラキラと装飾されているから美しいのではなく、むしろ飾りがないから美しいのだということをあらためて感じます」 (Writing is beautiful not because it is covered in glittering decoration, but precisely because it has no ornamentation).
default.q.n2-32-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「鮮やかな情景を浮かび上がらせています」 describes the specific effect produced by the concise wording in \"Rashomon\", not the author’s general definition of what makes a sentence engaging.
default.q.n2-32-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「声に出して読んでみるとすんなり耳に入ってきます」 (when read aloud, it flows smoothly into the ear) is simply the reader's impression when reading the opening of "Rashomon", not the answer concerning the standard for engaging writing.
default.q.n2-32-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage mentions 「古めかしい用語が多くて一見堅苦しいようですが」 (there are many old-fashioned terms, so it may seem stiff at first glance). The author only says that the wording is not complicated and never claims that engaging sentences are "familiar" (親しみやすい).
default.q.n2-32-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Whether or not one lives a long life is related not only to lifestyle habits but also to physical constitution.
default.q.n2-32-q58-58.explanation:
**Main idea summary:**
The author rejects the belief that simply copying the habits of people who live past 100—such as drinking miso soup with every meal—will enable one to live a long life. According to the author, longevity may result from being born into a family with longevity genes (長寿の家系) or from having an exceptionally fortunate constitution that protects one from infectious diseases in an era when medical care was underdeveloped (運のよい体質). Therefore, believing that merely imitating their lifestyle will guarantee a long life is an oversimplification.

**Question and choice translations:**
- **Question:** What is the author mainly trying to say here?
- **Choice 1:** If you want to live a long life, you should follow the example of people who live past 100 and adopt their lifestyle.
- **Choice 2:** Living a long life does not necessarily mean having a rich or meaningful life.
- **Choice 3:** To live a long life, improving one’s diet alone is not enough; medical support is also necessary.
- **Choice 4:** Whether one can live a long life depends not only on lifestyle habits but also on one’s constitution.
default.q.n2-32-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author rejects this view in the final sentence: 「同じようにしていれ消自分も長生きできると考えるのは、単純すぎるのではないでしょうか」 (Thinking that you can live a long life simply by doing exactly the same thing is overly simplistic/naive).
default.q.n2-32-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not mention or discuss whether living a long life leads to a rich, meaningful life (豊かな人生).
default.q.n2-32-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author mentions the medical detail to emphasize that, before medicine had developed, those people may simply have been fortunate enough not to contract infectious diseases. The author does not claim that medical assistance is necessary for living a long life.
default.q.n2-32-q58-58.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「その人は、ただ長寿の家系に生まれただけかもしれません。現在のように医療の発達していない時答に、結核などの感染症にかからずに来られた、運のよい体質だったのかもしれませんが...」. The author points out that longevity may result not only from eating habits such as drinking miso, but also from family heredity and a fortunate constitution.
default.q.n2-32-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 若い人と同じ時答に生きていないように感じるから (Because they feel as if they are not living in the same era as young people).
default.q.n2-32-q59-59.explanation:
**Summary and basis:**
According to the author, when new words used by young people appear and older people cannot understand them, the shock they feel is not simply from realizing that there is a generation gap. More deeply, it comes from the fear that people can no longer understand one another through language, making them keenly aware of the difference between their eras. This is because mutual understanding through language serves as proof that they are people living in the same present age.

**Question translation:**
Why does the author think older people are shocked by the popularity of new words?

**Answer choices:**
1. Because they feel uneasy when they hear words whose meanings they do not understand.
2. Because they feel as if they are not living in the same era as young people.
3. Because they think it would be better if there were no generation gap.
4. Because they are afraid they cannot keep up with the trends of the times.
default.q.n2-32-q59-59.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is inaccurate because the passage does not mention feeling uneasy from hearing words whose meanings are unknown. Its focus is the fear of losing linguistic connection and being out of sync with the times.
default.q.n2-32-q59-59.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct. Evidence from the passage: 「言葉が通じなくなるかもしれないという恐怖があるからで、時答の違いを感じとってしまうからです。なぜなら、言葉が通じることこそ、現答という共通の時答を生きている同時答人のあかしだからです。」 (Older people are shocked because they fear that they may no longer be able to communicate through language and because they sense a difference between eras; this is because being able to communicate through language is proof that people are contemporaries living in the same era.)
default.q.n2-32-q59-59.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the reading only states the fact that people perceive a generation gap (世答のギャップ); it does not mention the desire or opinion that it would be better if there were no generation gap.
default.q.n2-32-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not discuss fear of failing to understand trends or the spirit of the times; it discusses the fear that difficulty communicating in the language makes one feel no longer connected to the same era as young people.
default.q.n2-32-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: Having visual acuity of about 1.2 does not cause problems in daily life.
default.q.n2-32-q60-60.explanation:
- Main point: The author explains that in modern human society, all systems of daily life are designed on the assumption that visual acuity of 1.0–1.2 is sufficient. Therefore, people with visual acuity of around 1.2 can live normally without difficulty.
- Question: Which statement about visual acuity is consistent with the passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. The better one's visual acuity, the more convenient modern life becomes.
  2. Visual acuity from 1.2 to 2.0 is considered normal.
  3. People with visual acuity of 1.5 sometimes have to wear corrective glasses.
  4. People with visual acuity of around 1.2 have no difficulty in their daily lives.

default.q.n2-32-q60-60.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage states that there is currently no suitable eyeglasses or medical method for correcting excessively sharp eyesight («視力のよすぎる人には、これといった眼鏡はありません。... 矯正する方法がないのです»).
default.q.n2-32-q60-60.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the passage provides the following evidence: 「一般に人類社会では、 1.0 から 1.2 くらいの視力で間に合うように、すべてのシステムが設計され、確立されています。」 In human society in general, all systems are designed and established to meet needs with visual acuity of approximately 1.0 to 1.2.
default.q.n2-32-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: No matter how beneficial something is considered to be, having too much of it or too many levels of it is not good.
default.q.n2-32-q61-61.explanation:
- **Main point:** The author cites the proverb «過ぎたるは及ばざるが如し» (Excess is as bad as insufficiency) to show that seeing too clearly or having excessively sharp eyesight can negatively affect one’s mental state and health; everything should be kept in moderation.
- **Question translation:** What does the proverb “Excess is as bad as insufficiency” mean?
- **Answer choices:**
  1. No matter how beneficial something is considered to be, having too much of it is still bad.
  2. No matter how good a method is, realizing its value after it is no longer needed is too late.
  3. No matter how good something is, repeatedly dwelling on the past is bad.
  4. No matter how valuable something is, its value decreases as it becomes old.
default.q.n2-32-q61-61.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because the idiom «過ぎたるは及ばざるが如し» means that anything beyond the proper limit or degree can have harmful consequences, just as something insufficient can. default.q.n2-32-q61-61.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because this idiom does not mean realizing a method only after it is too late.
default.q.n2-32-q61-61.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is incorrect because this idiom does not refer to bringing up events from the past.
default.q.n2-32-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because this idiom does not discuss an object's value declining over time.
default.q.n2-32-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: Conversely, there are objects that cannot be seen clearly.

default.q.n2-32-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: a is リサイクル (recycling), b is リサイクル (recycling), and c is リユース (reuse).
default.q.n2-32-q63-63.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage clearly distinguishes two concepts: “recycling” (recovering old items and processing them into materials for new products) and “reuse” (keeping an item intact and using it repeatedly). Specifically:
  + (a) Waste paper is recovered and made into new paper repeatedly → recycling (リサイクル).

  + (c) Bottles are kept in their original form and reused many times to hold beer → reuse (リユース).

  Which combination should be filled in for ( a ) ～ ( ｃ )?

- Answer choices:
  1. a: recycling, b: reuse, c: recycling
  2. a: recycling, b: recycling, c: reuse

  4. a: reuse, b: reuse, c: recycling

At (c), keeping the bottle intact and using it again is reuse (リユース), not recycling (リサイクル).
default.q.n2-32-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage clearly states: "紙は何度も（ a：リサイクル ）することができますが、リサイクルを重ねるにつれて繊維が細かくなり..." (Paper can be recycled many times) → a is リサイクル; "ガラスのびんは一度溶かしてから新しいびんに（ ｂ：リサイクル ）することもできますが..." (Melting old bottles down and casting them into new bottles is recycling) → b is リサイクル; "びんのまま何度も（ ｃ：リユース ）した方が使用するエネルギーが少なくてすみます" (Using the same bottle repeatedly requires less energy) → c is リユース.
default.q.n2-32-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because, in position (a), making recycled paper from collected waste paper is defined in the article as recycling (“古紙を回収してそれから再生紙を作ること... リサイクル”). Therefore, (a) must be リサイクル, not リユース.
default.q.n2-32-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because (a) should be リサイクル (paper recycling); melting bottles to make new bottles in (b) is also リサイクル; and keeping a bottle and using it again in (c) is リユース.
default.q.n2-32-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: Using the original material, natural wood pulp, to make disposable products is an unreasonable and wasteful use of resources.
default.q.n2-32-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point: The author explains that each time paper is recycled, its fibers become more fragmented and gradually lose quality. Since toilet paper is used once and then discarded and cannot be recycled again, it is most appropriate to use low-quality fibers that have already been recycled several times as its raw material. Using brand-new natural wood pulp, the original raw material, solely to produce a disposable product would be a waste of resources.

- Question:
What does the phrase “a waste of resources” mean in this case?

- Answer choices:
  1. Using the original raw material to produce a disposable product is an inappropriate use of resources.
  2. Any paper product that is made will quickly deteriorate.
  3. Natural wood pulp is very difficult to use to produce many different types of products.
  4. The production process is more likely to generate waste than materials such as aluminum.
default.q.n2-32-q64-64.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage clearly states: "トイ式ットパーパーは、もうそれ以上リサイクルすることができないので、質の悪くなった古紙を原料に作ることが合理的であり、天然パルプ で作ることは資源の由ダです。" (Since toilet paper cannot be recycled any further, it is rational to make it from lower-quality wastepaper, whereas making it from virgin natural pulp is a waste of resources.) Therefore, wasting resources means using newly extracted raw materials to make a disposable product that is then thrown away.
default.q.n2-32-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not say that all paper products quickly deteriorate. It says that paper fibers gradually become finer and lower in quality after repeated recycling ("リサイクルを重ねるにつれて繊維が細かくなり、質が悪くなっていきます").
default.q.n2-32-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage only explains that natural pulp (天然パルプ) consists of fibers obtained from natural wood and is used as a raw material for producing paper. It does not say that wood pulp is difficult to use to produce many kinds of products.
default.q.n2-32-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not compare paper production from natural wood pulp as producing more waste than aluminum production.
default.q.n2-32-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: Keeping the original form intact for repeated reuse does not require as much energy as recycling does.
default.q.n2-32-q65-65.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage compares two ways of handling used glass bottles: recycling them by melting them down to make new bottles, and reusing them by washing the old bottles and filling them with beer again. Reusing bottles in their original form consumes much less energy than remelting them, so reuse is always prioritized over recycling for environmental reasons.

- Translation of the question:
  Why is it said that “for the sake of the environment, reuse is prioritized over recycling”?

- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Because developing technology to recycle them into other products is very difficult.
  2. Because glass becomes very poor in quality once it has been melted and cannot be sold.
  3. Because washing large quantities of used bottles would cause wastewater to pollute the environment.
  4. Because keeping the bottles in their original shape and using them repeatedly does not require much energy.
default.q.n2-32-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention any difficulty in developing technology for manufacturing recycled products.
default.q.n2-32-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not say that melted glass would lose quality and become unsellable; on the contrary, it states that glass bottles can be melted and recycled into new bottles ("ガラスのびんは一度溶かしてから新しいびんにリサイクルすることもできますが").
default.q.n2-32-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not say that washing bottles causes environmental pollution through wastewater. On the contrary, washing beer bottles so they can be reused is presented as a positive example of reuse.
default.q.n2-32-q65-65.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: "ガラスのびんは一度溶かしてから新しいびんにリサイクルすることもできますが、びんのまま何度もリユースした方が使用するエネルギーが少なくてすみます。環境のためにはリサイクルよりもリユースが優先されます。" Although glass bottles can be melted down and recycled into new bottles, reusing them repeatedly requires less energy. For the environment, reuse takes priority over recycling.
default.q.n2-32-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Traditional boxed meals are sold on shelves kept at approximately 20°C.
default.q.n2-32-q66-66.explanation:
Main point: Paragraphs 2 and 3 contrast traditional boxed lunches (従来型) with chilled boxed lunches (チルド弁当). Traditional boxed lunches are usually displayed on shelves kept at around 20°C and have a shorter shelf life.

Question translation: Which characteristic matches the article’s description of traditional boxed lunches?
Answer choices:
1. At the store, the boxed lunches are displayed on shelves kept at around 20°C.
2. They have a shelf life twice as long as chilled boxed lunches.
3. The ingredients in the boxed lunches have a very enjoyable texture and freshness.
4. Their calorie content is calculated, and they are designed as health-oriented boxed lunches.
default.q.n2-32-q66-66.why.0: (a) Correct. Evidence from paragraph 2: 「コンビニで売っている従来型の弁当は通常、 20 度程度の棚に並べてある。」 (Traditional boxed lunches sold at convenience stores are usually displayed on shelves at around 20°C).
default.q.n2-32-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage states: 「保存性が良いため、消費期限は従来型の弁当より 2 倍以上長い。」 — a shelf life more than twice as long is a feature of chilled boxed meals (チルド弁当), not traditional boxed meals.
default.q.n2-32-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Preserving the fresh, crisp texture (食感) of ingredients such as green beans and lotus root is an advantage of chilled boxed meals because cooking is kept to a minimum: 「低温保存で食べ物が傷みにくいため、加熱調理は最小限で済み、インゲンやレンコンなどのシャキっとした食感が生かせる。」
default.q.n2-32-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The health-oriented feature (健康志向) belongs to the chilled boxed lunch, because it reduces additives as much as possible: 「食品添加物は最大で半分以上減らせるといい、エコで健康志向の弁当と言えそうだ。」 The passage does not mention calorie-counting for traditional boxed lunches.
default.q.n2-32-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The appropriate word for (★) is 「チルド弁当」 (a chilled boxed meal).
default.q.n2-32-q67-67.explanation:
Main point: After explaining the many advantages of chilled bento boxes (チルド弁当), the author uses the contrastive conjunction 「ただ」 (however) to point out that chilled bento currently accounts for only about 20% of all bento products because some people still prefer the fried foods and meat found in traditional bento.

Question translation: Which word is most appropriate for the blank ( ★ )?
Answer choices:
1. Traditional-style bento
2. Chilled bento
3. Convenience store
4. Store
default.q.n2-32-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The sentence that follows presents a contrasting opinion: 「『揚げ物や肉類は従来の弁当の方がおいしい』という意見もあるようだ」 (Some people apparently think that fried foods and meat taste better in traditional bento), showing that traditional bento are still selling well, while the bento whose sales have stalled at 20% are the chilled bento.
default.q.n2-32-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct. The preceding passage praises the advantages of chilled boxed lunches. Immediately afterward, the conjunction 「ただ」 signals a contrast: 「ただ、（チルド弁当）の売り上げは「弁当製品の 2 割程度」（セブンーイレブン・ジャパン）にとどまっている。」 (However, sales of chilled boxed lunches remain at only about 20% of total boxed-lunch products.)
default.q.n2-32-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「コンビニ」 (convenience store) does not fit the meaning here because this position requires a noun naming a specific type of boxed rice product to contrast with 「弁当製品の 2 割程度」.
default.q.n2-32-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「店舗」 (“store”) does not fit because one cannot say that a store's sales account for only 20% of boxed-meal products.
default.q.n2-32-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Chilled boxed meals are popular because, compared with traditional ones, their ingredients last longer and they contain fewer additives.
default.q.n2-32-q68-68.explanation:
Main point: Chilled bento boxes (チルド弁当) became popular because the food is less likely to spoil (so it keeps longer) and contains fewer additives than ordinary bento boxes.

Question translation: Why did chilled bento boxes become popular?
Answer choices:
1. Because the fried food and meat taste better than those in traditional bento boxes.
2. Because they can be eaten immediately without being heated in a microwave.
3. Because, compared with traditional bento boxes, the ingredients keep longer and fewer additives are used.
4. Because so many are displayed in convenience stores that they do not sell out.
default.q.n2-32-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly quotes the opinion that traditional boxed lunches have tastier fried foods and meat: 「『揚げ物や肉類は従来の弁当の方がおいしい』という意見もあるようだ。」
default.q.n2-32-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The chilled boxed meal must be heated in a microwave before eating: 「食べるときは電子レンジで加熱する。」 The type that does not require a microwave is the traditional boxed meal (「電子レンジ不要の従来型弁当」).
default.q.n2-32-q68-68.why.2: (c) Correct. Evidence from paragraph 1: 「食材が傷みにくく添加物が少ないことなどから、人気が出始めている。」 (Because the ingredients spoil less easily and contain few additives, this type of rice has begun to gain popularity.)
default.q.n2-32-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Being able to display the products for a long time reduces the store's concern about unsold items (「長く陳列できるため、店舗側は売れ残りの心配が少なくなる」); it is not the reason customers prefer the products.
default.q.n2-32-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Both passages follow the structure “Background information about the book ➝ Book content ➝ Evaluation of the work.”
default.q.n2-32-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point:
Both Passage A and Passage B introduce the novel 『R』 using the same clearly defined three-paragraph structure:
+ Paragraph 1: Background and publication information about the book (A: serialized in a monthly magazine and then published as a complete three-volume set of standalone books; B: a long-form work that became a bestseller and is soon to be adapted into a television drama).
+ Paragraph 2: A summary of the work's content and plot (A: beginning with a secret agreement to return Okinawa and the prosecution of a diplomat and a journalist; B: the secret agreement spreading through a reporter and gradually developing into a romantic relationship between the reporter and the source).
+ Paragraph 3: Comments and evaluation of the work (A: a masterpiece that recreates the backstage reality and characters' psychology and captivates readers; B: moving because of the author's commitment to pursuing the truth, with empathy for the professional setting but some regret about the return of Okinawa).

- Question and answer choice translations:
Question: How are both A and B structured?
1. Book content ➝ Evaluation of the work ➝ Other information
2. Book content ➝ Evaluation of the work ➝ Readers' opinions
3. Background information about the book ➝ Book content ➝ Evaluation of the work
4. Background information about the book ➝ Evaluation of the work ➝ Readers' opinions
default.q.n2-32-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect, because neither passage begins with "the contents of the book." Instead, each opens with background information about the book's publication or release: Passage A discusses how it was serialized before being published as a three-volume book, while Passage B discusses how the book became a bestseller and is about to be adapted into a television drama. In addition, the endings of both passages evaluate the works rather than providing "other information."
default.q.n2-32-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The openings of the two texts provide background information, not the content of the book. Also, the endings are the writer's comments/evaluation of the works, not a structure ending with “readers' opinions.”
default.q.n2-32-q69-69.why.2:
(c) Correct because both A and B follow the same clearly defined three-part sequence:
1. Background information about the book (本の背景情報): Passage A: "月刊「文芸いろは」連載中から読者に絶賛されていた『R』が、ついに全3巻の単行本となった。"; Passage B: "久々の長編である『R』もベストセラーとなって。来春にはドラマ化も決定している。"
2. The book's content (本の内容): Passage A: "物語はまず、沖縄返還の交渉のかげで、日本とアメリカの間で密約があったというところから始まる。その情報を漏らした外務省の職員と情報を得た新聞記者が次の年に罪を問われる。"; Passage B: "沖縄返還時に日米間で密約があったということが、主人公の新聞記者を通して世間に広がってしまう。外交問題から、徐々に新聞記者と情報源の人物との男女関係に移っていく。"
3. Evaluation of the work (作品の評価): Passage A: "...読者の真実を知りたいという願望を十二分に満たす傑作である。また、登場人物の心の動きや沖縄の様子が生き生きと描かれていて..."; Passage B: "徹底した取材と多くの資料をもとに書きあげられた本書を読み、著者の真実を追い求める姿勢に感動を覚えた...緊迫感が手に取るように伝わってきた。ただ、沖縄返還のシーンの描き方があまりにもありきたりだったことが、残念であった。"
default.q.n2-32-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the second paragraph of both A and B summarizes the book's content or plot; it does not immediately move to “evaluating the work” and then to “readers' opinions.”
default.q.n2-32-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 2: A writes with the readers in mind, whereas B focuses on the writer’s own feelings.
default.q.n2-32-q70-70.explanation:
- Main point:
- Passage A is an objective book review aimed at the general public, consistently placing the reader’s experience at the center through phrases such as 「読者に絶賛されていた」 (“was enthusiastically praised by readers”), 「読者の真実を知りたいという願望を十二分に満たす」 (“more than fully satisfies readers’ desire to know the truth”), and 「読者を小説の世界にぐんぐん引き込む」 (“draws readers rapidly into the world of the novel”).
- Passage B is strongly personal, drawing on the author’s own experiences and identity as a person from Okinawa and a journalist to express personal feelings: 「著者の真実を追い求める姿勢に感動を覚えた」 (“I was moved by the author’s pursuit of the truth”), 「沖縄は私の出身地でもあり」 (“Okinawa is also my birthplace”), 「ジャーナリストの私にとって」 (“for me as a journalist”), and 「残念であった」 (“I found it regrettable”).

- Translation of the question and choices:
Question: Which of the following statements about passages A and B is correct?
1. A praises the work, whereas B is generally critical.
2. A is written with the reader in mind, whereas B focuses on the writer’s own impressions.
3. A praises the work especially as a historical document, whereas B praises it especially as entertainment.
4. Both A and B state that the work’s greatest appeal lies in its characters’ diverse personalities.
default.q.n2-32-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect. B is not "generally critical" (全体的に批判的). The author of passage B is deeply moved by and highly praises the writer's determination to pursue the truth ("著者の真実を追い求める姿勢に感動を覚えた", "緊迫感が手に取るように伝わってきた"), with only one minor reservation at the end ("ただ...残念であった").
default.q.n2-32-q70-70.why.1:
(b) Correct because:
- Paragraph A repeatedly addresses the readers: "読者に絶賛されていた", "読者の真実を知りたいという願望を十二分に満たす傑作である", "読者を小説の世界にぐんぐん引き込む".
- Paragraph B mainly expresses personal impressions based on the writer’s background and profession: "著者の真実を追い求める姿勢に感動を覚えた", "沖縄は私の出身地でもあり", "ジャーナリストの私にとって非常に身近に感じられ", "残念であった".
default.q.n2-32-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because Passage A does not describe the book as "particularly valuable as a historical document" (A calls it a novel/masterpiece that recreates the behind-the-scenes reality to satisfy readers' curiosity), and Passage B does not describe it as "particularly valuable as entertainment" either (B emphasizes authenticity and the seriousness of pursuing the truth).
default.q.n2-32-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Neither passage A nor passage B states that “a highly distinctive character is the work's greatest appeal.” Both passages focus on the painstaking collection of source material and the effort to reconstruct the truth behind a secret agreement.
default.q.n2-32-q71-71.verdict: The given answer is 1 (米国); however, this answer is incorrect according to the passage.
default.q.n2-32-q71-71.explanation:
- **Main point:** At the beginning of the article, the author recounts arranging to meet again with a friend living in the United States (米国在住の友人) after more than ten years. When the author suggests exchanging phone numbers to make it easier to find each other, the friend says that, because the stay in Japan will be short, they do not have a phone. The passage does not specify an exact meeting place; it only refers to it generally as "待ち合わせ場所".
- **Question translation:** Where did the author and the "friend" arrange to meet in this passage?
- **Answer choices:**
  1. The United States (米国)
  2. Shizuoka (静岡)
  3. In front of the shop on the right side of the hall reception desk (ホール受付の右手にある売店の前)
  4. In front of a crowded station (混雑した駅前)
default.q.n2-32-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect, even though it is the provided answer. The passage only says 「米国在住の友人」, a friend living in the United States, and the friend says 「滞在期間が短いからケータイがないの」, meaning that they do not have a mobile phone because their stay is short. This indicates that the meeting took place in Japan when the friend came to visit, not in the United States 「米国」. The reading does not specify the exact location of the meeting; it only refers generally to the 「待ち合わせ場所」.
default.q.n2-32-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 静岡 is the place the author later went to meet an acquaintance (知人), not a place arranged for meeting a friend (友人). Quotation: 「それからしばらくして静岡に出かけた時も、ケータイなしの待ち合わせをすることになりました。土地勘がないので、知人に案内してもらうことに。」
default.q.n2-32-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect: "ホール受付の右手にある売店の前" is merely an example the author gives of a specific, clear meeting arrangement from the past, not the actual meeting place with a friend. Quotation: "待ち合わせの約束も、以前はもっと明確でした。たとえば「10時半、ホール受付の右手にある売店の前で」という具合。"
default.q.n2-32-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「混雑した駅前」is not mentioned as a place to meet a friend. The author only says generally that phones are really convenient in crowded places (「混雑したところでは本当に便利」).
default.q.n2-32-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 約束を守ればいいから.
default.q.n2-32-q72-72.explanation:
- **Main point**: When the author visited Shizuoka and asked an acquaintance for their mobile phone number, the acquaintance said they did not have one and laughed, saying: "You don't need a phone. When you make plans to meet, all you have to do is firmly decide on the time and place and keep your promise."
- **Question translation**: What reason is given in the passage for saying, "It is not troublesome even without a mobile phone"?
- **Answer choices**:
  1. Because there is a computer (パソコンがあるから)
  2. Because they can communicate by landline (固定の電話でも連絡できるから)
  3. Because they only need to keep their promise (約束を守ればいいから)
  4. Because there were no mobile phones in the past (昔はなかったから)
default.q.n2-32-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The article mentions that an acquaintance replies to computer email very quickly ("知人はパソコンのメールの返信は早いし"), but this detail merely shows that the person is not opposed to new technology. It is not the reason why the person does not need to use a mobile phone.
default.q.n2-32-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect. An acquaintance did say, "If anything happens, call the house phone" (「何かあったら家に電話を」), but the fundamental reason a mobile phone is unnecessary when meeting someone is simply to decide on a clear time and place and keep the appointment.
default.q.n2-32-q72-72.why.2: (c) Correct. The acquaintance says: "待ち合わせは場所と時間をしっかり決めて、約束を守ればいいだけだろう、とあっさり。" (You just need to decide the meeting place and time clearly and keep your promise.) This confirms that a phone is unnecessary as long as the agreed meeting time and place are observed.
default.q.n2-32-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author agrees that people used to live normally without mobile phones ("少し前まで、ケータイがなくても問題なく暮らしていたのですものね"), but this is the author's subsequent reflection, not the direct reason given by the acquaintance for saying that.
default.q.n2-32-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「ケータイ」ならいつでも連絡できるので、約束の変更を安易に行うようになること.
default.q.n2-32-q73-73.explanation:
- **Summary of the main point**: The author observes that the widespread use and convenience of mobile phones have made people dependent on them: they no longer arrange specific meeting places, become more casual about punctuality (ルーズ), and easily think that sending a message by phone is enough when they are late, eroding and neglecting the basic rules of courtesy and keeping promises between people.
- **Question translation**: What problem does the author say is arising because of the widespread use of “mobile phones”?
- **Answer choice translations**:
  1. Because all information is stored on the phone, losing it would be very troublesome.
  2. Because mobile phones make it possible to contact people at any time, people have become casual and careless about changing arrangements.
  3. Because the person who owns the mobile phone answers it personally, it is impossible to leave a clear message by phone.
  4. Using a mobile phone to contact someone regardless of the time whenever something suddenly comes to mind.
default.q.n2-32-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The passage does not mention that having all information on a phone would cause problems if the phone were lost.
default.q.n2-32-q73-73.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: "今はケータイで連絡がつくだけに、厳密に場所を決めないことが増えました。時間にもルーズになった気がします。遅れそうな時はケータイで「先に行って」などと伝えればいいや、と安易に考えているかも。便利な道具に頼って、いつの間にか人付き合いのルールをおろそかにしてしまったかなあ。" Because people can contact one another by mobile phone, they no longer set meeting places as precisely, and their attitude toward punctuality has become more relaxed. They may casually think that if they are late, they can simply message, “Go ahead,” and have consequently neglected the rules of social interaction by relying on a convenient tool.
default.q.n2-32-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect: The passage does not mention that “because the person in question answered the phone, it was impossible to leave a proper message.”
default.q.n2-32-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The passage does not discuss contacting someone whenever an idea suddenly occurs, regardless of the time. It focuses on people becoming careless and lax about keeping appointments and following social rules when meeting others.
default.q.n2-32-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (土曜日に、駅の ATM から振り込む。) because on Saturdays, the ATM at the station mainly operates only until 17:00, so the transfer may not be possible at 18:00 (午後 6 時).
default.q.n2-32-q74-74.explanation:
- Main point: The passage provides the operating hours of Midori Bank ATMs by day of the week and location. On Saturdays, ATMs located at stations and convenience stores (駅・コンビニ設置 ATM) are generally open only from 9:00 to 17:00 (9：00 ～ 17：00). Therefore, most of these ATMs are closed at 18:00 (午後 6 時).
- Question translation: If you want to make a bank transfer at 6:00 p.m. (18:00), which of the following cases is likely to be impossible?
- Answer choices:
1. Making a transfer on a weekday from an ATM inside a Midori Bank branch.
2. Making a transfer on Saturday from an ATM inside a Midori Bank branch.
3. Making a transfer on a weekday from an ATM at a train station.
4. Making a transfer on Saturday from an ATM at a train station.
