default.q.n2-32-q28-28.why.2: Incorrect because when describing hilly or mountainous terrain that is difficult to level, the word meaning physically flat must be「平ら」(or「平坦」), not「平等」.
default.q.n2-32-q28-28.why.3: Correct because 「平等に配る」 means to distribute something equally and fairly, without favoritism or discrimination among citizens, making it semantically and collocationally appropriate.
default.q.n2-32-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because 「省く」 (はぶく) means to omit or cut unnecessary parts to save time or effort, and is correctly used in 「要点だけ話して、あとは省いた」 (“I talked only about the main points and omitted the rest”).
default.q.n2-32-q29-29.explanation: 「省く」(はぶく): to omit or cut out unimportant or unnecessary parts in order to save time, effort, or expense. Common collocations include: 「手間を省く」「無駄を省く」「説明を省く」「手順を省く」. Example: 詳しい説明は省きますが、結論は以下の通りです。(I will omit the detailed explanation, but the conclusion is as follows.)
default.q.n2-32-q29-29.why.0: Correct because 「あとは省いた」 indicates omitting unnecessary details and mentioning only the key points due to limited time, which accurately reflects the meaning of 「省く」.
default.q.n2-32-q29-29.why.1: Incorrect because when you encounter a question you do not understand during an exam and skip it to answer another question, the natural expressions are 「飛ばして」 (or 「後回しにして」/「抜かして」), not 「省く」.
default.q.n2-32-q29-29.why.2: Incorrect because when surgically cutting out or removing a diseased organ part, the appropriate terms are「切除した」or「取り除いた」, not「省く」.
default.q.n2-32-q29-29.why.3: Incorrect because when an express train runs straight through and skips certain stations on the route, use「通過して」or「止まらずに」, not「省く」.
default.q.n2-32-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1 because 「ひとまず」 means "for now" or "temporarily" and describes a temporary action or decision in the present situation. It is very natural in the context of 「未完成だが、ひとまず目を通す」.
default.q.n2-32-q30-30.explanation: 「ひとまず」(for now, for the time being): used when taking temporary action to deal with an immediate situation, before reaching a final result (similar to とりあえず and 一応). Example: 手術が無事に終わって、ひとまず安心した。(The operation ended safely, so I feel relieved for the time being.)
default.q.n2-32-q30-30.why.0: Correct because 「ひとまず見てください」('for now, please take a look') describes showing something temporarily at the current stage even though it is not yet fully complete, which fits the context of 「ひとまず」.
default.q.n2-32-q30-30.why.1: Incorrect because to describe sleeping soundly/nonstop from the time one returns home from work until the next morning, use「ぐっすり」「一気に」「そのまま」, not「ひとまず」.
default.q.n2-32-q30-30.why.2: When politely asking someone to wait briefly, the appropriate word is「少々」(少々お待ちください) or「ちょっと」, not「ひとまず」.
default.q.n2-32-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect because you should call ahead before visiting someone’s home. Suitable expressions are 「あらかじめ」, 「事前に」, or 「まず」, not 「ひとまず」.
default.q.n2-32-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because 「ひとりでに」 (spontaneously, by itself) describes something that happens or is learned naturally without instruction or deliberate external influence, which fits the context of a child playing alone and eventually learning to play the piano naturally.
default.q.n2-32-q31-31.explanation: 「ひとりでに」(naturally, automatically, by itself): describes something happening or taking shape on its own, without outside human intervention, instruction, or deliberate mechanical action. It is often used for objects that move or operate by themselves, or for people who naturally learn or heal on their own. Example: ドアがひとりでに開いた。(The door opened by itself.) / 風邪は薬を飲まなくてもひとりでに治った。(The cold went away on its own without taking any medicine.)
default.q.n2-32-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because when children travel “alone” (without an accompanying adult), 「一人で」or「単独で」must be used, not「ひとりでに」.
default.q.n2-32-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because when asking whether someone cooked this dish alone, use「一人で」or「自分一人で」, not「ひとりでに」.
default.q.n2-32-q31-31.why.2: Correct because 「ひとりでに弾けるようになった」 indicates that the child played around with the instrument and naturally learned to play it without being taught or assisted by an adult, which is the proper use of 「ひとりでに」.
default.q.n2-32-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect. For natural phenomena such as cherry blossoms blooming and falling according to the seasons, use 「自然に」 rather than 「ひとりでに」.
default.q.n2-32-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because 「やたらに」 (recklessly, indiscriminately, or arbitrarily without thinking) is exactly appropriate in the context of advising someone not to use other people's belongings carelessly.
default.q.n2-32-q32-32.explanation: 「やたらに」(recklessly, indiscriminately, excessively): describes doing something without principles or consideration, carelessly, or to an excessive degree that leads to a bad result (usually with a negative nuance). Common combinations include:「やたらに買う」(to shop recklessly),「やたらに話す」(to speak carelessly),「やたらに人を疑う」(to suspect people without reason). Example: やたらにお金を使うと、すぐになくなってしまうよ。(If you spend money recklessly, you will run out of it very quickly.)
default.q.n2-32-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because the intended meaning is wanting to go to bed early since one has to go out early the next morning; the correct word is 「早く」, not 「やたらに」.
default.q.n2-32-q32-32.why.1: Correct because 「やたらに他人のものを使う」 means using other people's belongings carelessly and indiscriminately without asking permission or thinking about it, which accurately matches the negative meaning of 「やたらに」.
default.q.n2-32-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect. To emphasize that the party was very enjoyable, the natural choices are 「とても」, 「すごく」, or 「非常に」. 「やたらに」 usually has a negative or excessively indiscriminate nuance, so it does not fit the positive feeling expressed by 「楽しかった」.
default.q.n2-32-q32-32.why.3: Incorrect because planting many flowers in the garden makes it very beautiful. A word indicating a large or dense quantity, such as 「たくさん」 or 「いろいろな」, is needed; 「やたらに」 means “carelessly / indiscriminately.”
default.q.n2-32-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (ふれない).
default.q.n2-32-q1-1.explanation:
- Meaning: "Please do not touch this."
- Sino-Japanese roots: 触 (to touch, come into contact with).
- Example: 貴重な展示品には手を触れないでください。(Please do not touch the valuable exhibits.)
default.q.n2-32-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「かれない」 is the negative form of 枯れる/涸れる (“to wither” or “to dry up”), not the reading of the kanji 触.
default.q.n2-32-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「されない」 is the passive form of する, not a conjugated form of 触.
default.q.n2-32-q1-1.why.2: (c) 「ふれない」 is the correct reading of 触れない, the negative form of the verb 触れる (to touch, come into contact with).
default.q.n2-32-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「とれない」 is the negative potential form of 取る (to take) or 撮る (to photograph), not the character 触.
default.q.n2-32-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (こうすい).
default.q.n2-32-q2-2.explanation:
- Meaning: "There is a faint fragrance of perfume."
- Sino-Japanese roots: 香 (fragrance) + 水 (water) = perfume.
- Example: 彼女はいつもほのかに甘い香水をつけている。(She always wears a faintly sweet perfume.)
default.q.n2-32-q2-2.why.0: (a) 「こうずい」 is the reading of 洪水 (flood). The 水 in 香水 retains the reading 「すい」 and does not undergo voicing to become 「ずい」.
default.q.n2-32-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「こうすい」is the correct reading of 香水 (perfume).
default.q.n2-32-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「こうすう」 is an incorrect reading of 水; it is not read as すう.
default.q.n2-32-q2-2.why.3: (d) 「こずい」 is an incorrect reading: 香 is missing its long vowel, and 水 undergoes the wrong sound change.
default.q.n2-32-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ひょうか).
default.q.n2-32-q3-3.explanation:
- Meaning: “The evaluation of this report was rather low.”
- Kanji components: 評 (evaluation) + 価 (value) = evaluation, assessment.
- Example: 彼の新しい映画は専門家から高い評価を受けた。(His new film received high praise from experts.)
default.q.n2-32-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「ひょうか」is the correct reading of 評価 (evaluation, assessment).
default.q.n2-32-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「へいか」 is the reading of 陛下 or 平価, so it is the wrong on-reading for 評.
default.q.n2-32-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「ひか」is an incorrect reading caused by omitting the combined long-vowel sound「ょう」in 評.
default.q.n2-32-q3-3.why.3: (d)「かいか」is the reading of 開花 (flowering), not 評価.
default.q.n2-32-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (たんとう).
default.q.n2-32-q4-4.explanation:
- Translation: “I have become responsible for this work.”
- Kanji readings: 担 means to shoulder or undertake, and 当 means to be in charge of or be assigned to.
- Example: 営業部の担当者に連絡を取ってください。(Please contact the person in charge in the sales department.)
default.q.n2-32-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「たんとう」is the correct reading of 担当 (to be in charge of, responsibility).
default.q.n2-32-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「とう」 is an incomplete reading of 担 (たん).
default.q.n2-32-q4-4.why.2: (c) 「たとう」 is the reading of 妥当 (appropriate, valid) or 多当; it is an incorrect reading of 担, which includes the final ん sound.
default.q.n2-32-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「だんとう」 is an incorrect reading caused by voicing the initial consonant of 担; it is read たん, not だん.
default.q.n2-32-q5-5.explanation:
- Meaning: "I am a homemaker."
- Kanji components: 主 (chief) + 婦 (woman) = homemaker, housewife.
- Example: 彼女は専業主婦として家庭を支えている。(She supports her family as a full-time homemaker.)
default.q.n2-32-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「しゅうふ」is an incorrect reading because the 主 in 主婦 has the short reading「しゅ」, not the long vowel「しゅう」.
default.q.n2-32-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「しゅうふ」 is an incorrect reading, similar to Choice 1, because 主 has an extra long vowel.
default.q.n2-32-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「しゅふう」 is an incorrect reading because 婦 is pronounced briefly as 「ふ」 and does not have the long vowel 「う」; it is easily confused with the 風 in “ozu/phong cách.”
default.q.n2-32-q5-5.why.3: (d) 「しゅふ」 is the correct reading of 主婦; both kanji have short vowels, with no long-vowel sound.
default.q.n2-32-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 倒れた (たおれた: fell over, collapsed).
default.q.n2-32-q6-6.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: The tree fell because of the strong wind.
- Kanji: 倒 (to fall, collapse).
- Commonly confused verbs:
  + 倒れる (たおれる): to fall or topple (trees, utility poles, or people who collapse or fall ill).
  + 壊れる (こわれる): to break or malfunction (objects, machines, or relationships).
  + 折れる (おれる): to snap or break (tree branches, bones, pencils).
  + 割れる (われる): to shatter, crack, or break into pieces (glass, dishes, flower vases).
- Example: 台風で道路の街灯が倒れた。(The streetlight fell because of the typhoon.)
default.q.n2-32-q6-6.why.0: (a) 壊れた is read「こわれた」(broken, damaged), so the kanji reading is incorrect.
default.q.n2-32-q6-6.why.1: (b) 倒れた: The correct reading is 「たおれた」 (倒: to fall, collapse); the kanji 倒 describes a tree being blown down by strong wind.
default.q.n2-32-q6-6.why.2: (c) 折れた is read「おれた」(broken, snapped), so the required kanji reading is incorrect.
default.q.n2-32-q6-6.why.3: (d) 割れた is read 「われた」(to crack, to break), so the kanji reading is incorrect.
default.q.n2-32-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 爆発 (ばくはつ: explode, explosion).
default.q.n2-32-q7-7.explanation:
- Meaning: There was a loud explosion nearby.
- Kanji reading: 爆発 (ばくはつ: explosion, detonation).
- Kanji tip: 爆 (ばく) contains the fire radical 火, associated with fire and explosions. Do not confuse it with 曝 (as in 暴露 - ばくろ: expose, reveal) or 暴 (as in 暴風, 乱暴).
- Example: 工場でガス爆発事故が起きた。(A gas explosion accident occurred at the factory.)
default.q.n2-32-q7-7.why.0: (a) 暴発 is read 「ぼうはつ」 and means accidental firing or an unexpected explosion; the kanji reading is incorrect.
default.q.n2-32-q7-7.why.1: (b) 爆発: The correct reading is 「ばくはつ」 (爆発: explosion); the kanji 爆, which contains the fire radical 火, represents exploding or bursting.
default.q.n2-32-q7-7.why.2: (c) 曝発: The kanji 曝 (the 日 radical in 暴露 - ばくろ) is an incorrect spelling and does not form the word ばくはつ.
default.q.n2-32-q7-7.why.3: (d) 摸発: The character 摸 (the 手 radical) is incorrect; this vocabulary does not exist.
default.q.n2-32-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 想像 (そうぞう: imagination, visualization).
default.q.n2-32-q8-8.explanation:
- Translation: I tried to imagine myself 20 years from now.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 想像 (そうぞう: to visualize or imagine mentally).
- Distinguish these homophones and related words:
  + 想像 (そうぞう): imagining or conjecturing something that has not happened or is not visible.
  + 創造 (そうぞう): creating something new that has never existed before (e.g., 新しい世界を創造する).
  + 空想 (くうそう): a fanciful or unrealistic daydream.
  + 理想 (りそう): an ideal model or perfect state.
- Example: 想像以上の素晴らしい結果になった。(The result was more wonderful than I could have imagined.)
default.q.n2-32-q8-8.why.0: (a) 空想 is read 「くうそう」 and means a far-fetched or unrealistic fantasy; both the reading and the kanji are incorrect.
default.q.n2-32-q8-8.why.1: (b) 想像 is read 「そうぞう」 (sōzō). The kanji 想像 expresses imagining or picturing oneself in the future.
default.q.n2-32-q8-8.why.2: (c) 理想: read as 「りそう」, with an incorrect reading and incorrect kanji.
default.q.n2-32-q8-8.why.3: (d) 創造: Also read 「そうぞう」, but it means “creation” (producing new products or values), which does not fit the context of imagining the future.
default.q.n2-32-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 溶ける (とける: to melt).
default.q.n2-32-q9-9.explanation:
- Meaning: Because the weather is hot, the ice cream melts rapidly.
- Kanji note: 溶 (YŌ—melt, dissolve).
- Distinguishing the Japanese words pronounced 「とける」:
  + 溶ける (with the water radical 氵): a solid melts from heat (ice cream, butter, molten metal), or a substance dissolves into a liquid (salt or sugar dissolving in water).
  + 融ける (with 虫): snow or ice melts naturally as the weather warms (雪が融ける).
  + 解ける: something is untangled or resolved (問題が解ける—solve a problem, 誤解が解ける—clear up a misunderstanding, 緊張が解ける—relax).
- Example: チョコレートが手の温もりで溶けてしまった。(The chocolate melted from the warmth of my hand.)
default.q.n2-32-q9-9.why.0: (a) 解ける: read as 「とける」 (to untie, solve a problem, clear up a misunderstanding); it is not used for ice cream melting from heat.
default.q.n2-32-q9-9.why.1: (b) 説ける: The kanji 説 relates to explaining or persuading; it does not mean melting.
default.q.n2-32-q9-9.why.2: (c) 溶ける is correctly read 「とける」 (melt, dissolve). The 溶 character contains the water radical (氵), which is appropriate for ice cream melting from heat.
default.q.n2-32-q9-9.why.3: (d) 得ける: The kanji 得 (receive, obtain) is read 「える/うる」, not 「とける」.
default.q.n2-32-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 階段 (かいだん: stairs).
default.q.n2-32-q10-10.explanation:
- Meaning: As you get older, going up and down stairs becomes really difficult.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 階段 (stairs, steps).
- Kanji details:
  + 階: consists of the 阜 radical (阝 — indicating height or sloping ground) on the left combined with 皆 on the right.
  + 段: contains the 殳 radical on the right; be careful not to confuse it with 椴, which contains the 木 radical.
- Example: 階段を使うようにして運動不足を解消する。(I try to use the stairs to make up for my lack of exercise.)
default.q.n2-32-q10-10.why.0: (a) 階段: The correct reading is「かいだん」(stairs), and both 階 and 段 are written correctly.
default.q.n2-32-q10-10.why.1: (b) 階椴: the second character, 椴 (with the 木 radical), is an incorrect kanji, visually confusing it with 段.
default.q.n2-32-q10-10.why.2: (c) 皆椴: Both kanji are incorrect; 皆 is missing the 阝 radical on the left, and 椴 has been substituted with the 木 radical.
default.q.n2-32-q10-10.why.3: (d) 皆段: 皆 is missing the 阝 radical; 階 is the kanji with 阝, which indicates a step or floor.
default.q.n2-34-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (をめぐって).
default.q.n2-34-q33-33.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "The two major political parties are in fierce opposition over the budget for the new fiscal year."
- Kanji readings: 新年度 ( — new fiscal year), 予算 ( — budget), 政党 ( — political party), 対立 ( — opposition), 激しい ( — fierce/intense).
- Grammar: 「N をめぐって / をめぐる N」(over N / concerning an issue related to N), often used with words describing disputes, discussions, or opposition, such as 対立する, 議論する, and 争う.
- Example: 遺産の配分をめぐって、兄弟の間で激しい争いが起こった。(A fierce dispute arose among the siblings over the distribution of the inheritance.)
default.q.n2-34-q33-33.why.0: (a) を見て means “looking at...” and is not used to express the topic of an argument or a contrast.
default.q.n2-34-q33-33.why.1: (b) をめぐって: Grammatically correct in 「Nをめぐって」 (“concerning / surrounding N”), used for differing opinions, arguments, or opposing views about a topic or issue — here, the budget.
default.q.n2-34-q33-33.why.2: (c) を通して: Means “through” a means or intermediary, or “throughout” a period of time; it does not fit the contrasting context of an argument.
default.q.n2-34-q33-33.why.3: (d) をこめて: means “to put into” or “to imbue with” feelings or intentions, such as love, gratitude, or a prayer; it is not used with the noun 予算 (budget).
default.q.n2-34-q34-34.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "Even an expert cannot understand this issue, so how could amateurs like us possibly understand it?"
- Kanji-related terms: 専門家 (specialist, expert), 素人 (amateur, nonprofessional).
- Pattern: 「N でさえ」 (even N), presenting an extreme example to imply that ordinary cases naturally apply as well.
- Example: この漢字は日本人でさえ読めないのだから、外国人の私には読めないのも当然だ。(Even Japanese people cannot read this kanji, so it is only natural that I, as a foreigner, cannot read it.)
default.q.n2-34-q34-34.why.0: (a) だけ: Means “only.” Saying “only experts do not understand” is illogical when compared with amateurs in the following clause.
default.q.n2-34-q34-34.why.1: (b) こそ is used to emphasize “precisely” or “indeed,” not to present an extreme example as a point of comparison.
default.q.n2-34-q34-34.why.2: (c) のみ means “only” and is the formal equivalent of だけ, so it does not fit the logic of the sentence.
default.q.n2-34-q34-34.why.3: (d) でさえ: Grammatically correct 「Nでさえ」 (“even N”) presents an exemplary or highly capable case, such as an expert, to infer that a less capable person, such as an ordinary person or amateur, naturally cannot know either.
default.q.n2-34-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (にこたえて).
default.q.n2-34-q35-35.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "In response to our customers' requests for more inexpensive yet delicious dishes, our restaurant has added a new menu."
- Sino-Japanese readings: 当店 (this shop, our restaurant), 料理 (cuisine, dishes), 期待・要望・声に応える (to respond to, meet).
- Grammar:「N にこたえて / にこたえ」(in response to / to meet N), commonly used with nouns such as 期待 (expectations), 要望 (requests), 声 (voices or wishes), and 応援 (support or encouragement).
- Example: ファンの熱い声援に応えて、歌手はアンコール曲を歌った。(In response to the fans' enthusiastic support, the singer performed an encore song.)
default.q.n2-34-q35-35.why.0: (a) にあたって: Means “on the occasion of / when preparing to do something important,” and does not follow a noun referring to opinions or wishes, such as お客様の声.
default.q.n2-34-q35-35.why.1: (b) にこたえて: Grammatically correct in 「Nにこたえて」(in response to, in accordance with N), commonly used with nouns such as 声 (voice), 期待 (expectations), and 要望 (requests).
default.q.n2-34-q35-35.why.2: (c) につれて: Means “along with / as ... changes,” so the following clause must describe a corresponding change over time or during a process; it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-34-q35-35.why.3: (d) にしても means "even if it is..." or "even so" and is used in a concessive sentence, so it does not fit an action taken to fulfill someone's wishes.
default.q.n2-34-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (ばかりか).
default.q.n2-34-q36-36.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "Because of the economic downturn, not only small and medium-sized businesses but also large companies are finding it difficult to operate."
- Sino-Japanese readings: 景気 (economic conditions), 悪化 (deterioration), 中小企業 (small and medium-sized enterprises), 大企業 (large enterprises), 経営 (business management).
- Structure:「N / plain form + ばかりか…（も）」(not only... but even...), used to add information of an even greater degree.
- Example: 彼は英語ばかりか、フランス語やドイツ語も話せる。(He can speak not only English but also French and German.)
default.q.n2-34-q36-36.why.0: (a) に反して: Means “contrary to…” (a prediction or expectation), and cannot be used with the linking structure「...も」in the following clause.
default.q.n2-34-q36-36.why.1: (b) ばかりに: It means “just because ...,” identifying a cause that leads to a negative or regrettable result. It does not form the paired structure “A, and B as well.”
default.q.n2-34-q36-36.why.2: (c) ばかりか: Grammatically correct: 「Nばかりか…も」means “not only N but also...,” adding another person, thing, or degree beyond the initial one.
default.q.n2-34-q36-36.why.3: (d) の一方 means “on the other hand” or, after a verb, indicates that something is “increasingly...” It is not used to connect two nouns in an increasing relationship.
default.q.n2-34-q37-37.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “Today, I have not eaten anything since drinking coffee in the morning.”
- Pattern: 「Vたきり（だ／で）」 (ever since doing V, the same state has continued / nothing further has been done).
- Example: 息子は朝「行ってきます」と言って出かけたきり、夜になっても帰ってこない。(My son said “I’m off” and left in the morning, but he still has not come home, even though it is now night.)
default.q.n2-34-q37-37.why.0: (a) ばかり: The structure 「Vたばかり」 means "have just done something," so it is unsuitable for expressing that an action took place and was not followed by any further action.
default.q.n2-34-q37-37.why.1: (b) かぎり: The structure「Vたかぎり」means “within the scope of” or “as far as...,” and does not indicate an interruption of an action from that point onward.
default.q.n2-34-q37-37.why.2: (c) きりで: The grammar 「Vたきり（で）」 is correct (after doing something, nothing else has been done since then / the state has remained unchanged).
default.q.n2-34-q37-37.why.3: (d) 末: The structure「Vた末（に）」means “after a long time” or “after much effort,” indicating a result following a lengthy process. It does not fit the context of drinking coffee.

default.q.n2-34-q38-38.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "The international soccer tournament held in this town for the past week has come to an end today."
- Grammar:
  +「N にわたって + V」(over/throughout N, extending across a period of time or space), functioning adverbially to modify the following verb.
  +「N にわたる + N」: used when directly modifying the noun that follows.
- Example: 会議は3日間にわたって行われ、多くの重要な決定が下された。(The meeting was held over three days, and many important decisions were made.)
default.q.n2-34-q38-38.why.0: (a) わたって: Correct grammar「Nにわたって + V」(throughout / over the entire N); here it functions adverbially to modify「行われた」(was held).
default.q.n2-34-q38-38.why.1: (b) わたる: The pattern「Nにわたる + N」is used only when it directly modifies a noun immediately following it. Here, the following word is the verb「行われた」, so this form cannot be used.
default.q.n2-34-q38-38.why.2: (c) わたっての: Incorrect combination;「〜にわたっての + V」is not used.
default.q.n2-34-q38-38.why.3: (d) わたった: The past form modifies a noun in the pattern 「Nにわたった + N」; it is not used to modify a following verb.
default.q.n2-34-q39-39.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “You’re only a beginner at skiing, yet you’re saying you want to ski on the advanced course. How presumptuous.”
- Kanji meanings: 初心者 (a beginner), 上級者 (an advanced-level person), 生意気 (presumptuous, conceited, insolent).
- Pattern:「N の / plain form + くせに」(even though..., despite...), expressing sarcasm, criticism, or contempt toward the person mentioned.
- Example: 自分で何もできないくせに、人の悪口ばかり言っている。(Even though he cannot do anything himself, he does nothing but bad-mouth other people.)
default.q.n2-34-q39-39.why.0: (a) ものを: Often placed at the end of a sentence or clause with a regretful nuance, such as "if only..." or "even though...". With a noun, it requires 「であるものを」 and does not imply rude criticism or reproach.
default.q.n2-34-q39-39.why.1: (b) ものの: It means 'although...,' or 'though...,' and when combined with a noun it requires 「であるものの」. It expresses an objective fact rather than sarcasm or criticism.
default.q.n2-34-q39-39.why.2: (c) くせに: Grammatically correct in 「Nのくせに」 (even though one is only... / and yet...), expressing sarcasm, criticism, and contempt, which fits 「生意気だ」 (cheeky, conceited).
default.q.n2-34-q39-39.why.3: (d) かか山らず (かかわらず): The correct structure is 「Nに（も）かかわらず」 (regardless of, despite), not 「Nのかかわらず」.
default.q.n2-34-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (からといって).
default.q.n2-34-q40-40.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “Doing the right thing does not necessarily mean that you will receive cooperation from the people around you.”
- Kanji readings and meanings: 正しい (正 - correct), 協力 (協 - cooperation, assistance), 得る (得 - obtain), 限る (限 - limit).
- Structure: 「Plain form + からといって … とは限らない / わけではない」(Just because... does not necessarily mean...).
- Example: お金がたくさんあるからといって、必ずしも幸せになれるとは限らない。(Just because you have a lot of money does not necessarily mean you will be happy.)
default.q.n2-34-q40-40.why.0: (a) ににもかか山らず (にもかかわらず): Means “although ...,” “despite ...,” or “even though ...”. It is generally followed by a specific factual event, not by a speculative or broadly negative expression such as 「〜とは限らない」.
default.q.n2-34-q40-40.why.1: (b) くせに means “even though” or “despite,” expressing sarcasm or criticism toward a specific person or thing; the following clause states an actual fact.
default.q.n2-34-q40-40.why.2: (c) からには means “once... then one must...” or “now that...,” and the following clause usually expresses determination, obligation, or a command. This contrasts with 「とは限らない」.
default.q.n2-34-q40-40.why.3: (d) からといって: Grammatically correct in 「〜からといって…とは限らない」 (“just because… does not necessarily mean…”), which rejects the idea that a single reason inevitably determines the result.

default.q.n2-34-q41-41.explanation:
- Translation: Unless the company president agrees, the new project cannot be started.
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 社長 (company president), 賛成 (agreement, approval), 始める (begin, start).
- Structure:「Vないかぎり、…ない」(Unless V happens, the following action cannot be carried out).

default.q.n2-34-q41-41.why.0: (a) 新しいプロジェクトを始めるだろう: Means “will probably start a new project,” which is completely illogical after the condition “as long as the director has not approved it.”
default.q.n2-34-q41-41.why.1: (b) 新しいプロジェクトは始められない: Correct. The grammar pattern 「Vないかぎり、〜ない」means “unless V is done, ... cannot happen.” Logically, the project cannot start until the director gives approval.
default.q.n2-34-q41-41.why.2: (c) 新しいプロジェクトを始めるしかない means “there is no choice but to start a new project,” which is logically incorrect.
default.q.n2-34-q41-41.why.3: (d) 新しいプロジェクトは始められる: Means “the new project can be started,” directly contradicting the condition that the director has not approved it.

default.q.n2-34-q42-42.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "For Department Head Tanaka, English goes without saying; he is also good at both French and Chinese."
- Sino-Japanese readings: 部長 (department head), 英語 (English), フランス語 (French), 中国語 (Chinese).
- Structure:「N1 はもとより N2 も」(N1 goes without saying, and even N2...), used to emphasize that N1 is obvious and then add N2 in the same direction.
- Example: この病院では、内科はもとより外科や小児科も充実している。(At this hospital, internal medicine goes without saying; surgery and pediatrics are also well provided for.)
default.q.n2-34-q42-42.why.0: (a) フランス語、中国語しかできない: The structure 「しか〜ない」 means “only...,” which conflicts with 「はもとより」 (“English goes without saying, and in addition...” ).
default.q.n2-34-q42-42.why.1: (b) フランス語、中国語ならできる: This means “if it is French or Chinese,” an if-condition, and does not form the progressive listing structure with 「はもとより」.
default.q.n2-34-q42-42.why.2: (c) フランス語、中国語はできない: This means "cannot speak French or Chinese," whereas 「〜はもとより…も」 requires the latter clause to be affirmative and parallel with the obvious fact in the former clause.
default.q.n2-34-q42-42.why.3: (d) フランス語、中国語もできる: Grammatically correct with 「N1はもとよりN2も」 (“N1 goes without saying, and even N2...”); the first item is obvious, and the second is added.
default.q.n2-34-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ことから).
default.q.n2-34-q43-43.explanation:
- Meaning: “Because he is very knowledgeable about computers, people call him the ‘Computer Doctor.’”
- Kanji notes: 詳しい (knowledgeable, familiar with), 博士 (doctor, PhD), 呼ぶ (to call).
- Grammar: 「Plain form + ことから」(because / from the fact that...), often used with endings such as 〜と呼ばれている, 〜と言われている, and 〜と名付けられた.
- Example: 富士山が見えることから、この町は「富士見町」と名付けられた。(Because Mount Fuji can be seen from here, this town was named “Fujimi-cho.”)
default.q.n2-34-q43-43.why.0: (a) ことから: Grammatically correct. 「Plain form + ことから」 means 'because / originating from the fact that...' and is often used to explain the origin of a name or nickname (〜と呼ばれている) or the reason for a conclusion.
default.q.n2-34-q43-43.why.1: (b) ことにあたり: This grammar pattern does not exist; only 「〜にあたり」, meaning “on the occasion of/at the time of...,” is used.
default.q.n2-34-q43-43.why.2: (c) ことに: The structure 「A/Vた + ことに」 means “it is remarkable that...” or “to one’s...,” as in 驚いたことに, expressing the speaker’s emotion. It is not used to state a cause.
default.q.n2-34-q43-43.why.3: (d) ことだから: The pattern 「Nのことだから」is used with nouns referring to people (for example, 彼のことだから) to infer habits or personality, and does not follow the adjective 「詳しい」.
default.q.n2-34-q44-44.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "When she heard the news that she had passed, she burst into tears from overwhelming joy."
- Sino-Japanese readings: 合格 (passing an exam), 知らせ (news, notice), 泣き出す (to burst into tears).
- Pattern:「N（a noun expressing an emotion） / V-ru + のあまり（に）」(because of being overly..., resulting in an unusual or involuntary action or outcome).
- Example: 彼は緊張のあまり、スピーチの途中で言葉が出なくなってしまった。(He was so nervous that he became unable to speak halfway through his speech.)
default.q.n2-34-q44-44.why.0: (a) 末に: The pattern 「Nの末に」means “after a long period of...” and indicates the final result after a process of thought or struggle; it does not indicate a sudden emotional intensity.
default.q.n2-34-q44-44.why.1: (b) あまり: This is grammatically correct in 「N（emotion）のあまり（に）」(because of being overly...), which describes an emotion exceeding the normal level and leading to a sudden or impulsive action, such as bursting into tears from excessive happiness.
default.q.n2-34-q44-44.why.2: (c) かぎり: The structure 「〜かぎりだ」 at the end of a sentence expresses an extreme degree of emotion (“extremely / immensely”); it does not combine as 「Nのかぎり + V」 to indicate the cause of the following action.
default.q.n2-34-q44-44.why.3: (d) 上に: The pattern 「Nの上に」 means "not only... but also..." and adds information in the same direction; it is not used to indicate an emotional cause overflowing.
