default.q.n2-34-q6-6.why.0: (a) 「刑式」 is incorrect because 「刑」 is used in words related to punishment and crime; this word requires 「形」, meaning form or shape.
default.q.n2-34-q6-6.why.1: (b)「刑武」is incorrect in both kanji. 刑 means “punishment,” and 武 means “arms” or “martial arts”; together they do not form a meaningful word in this context.
default.q.n2-34-q6-6.why.2: (c) 「形式」 uses the correct kanji and means form, format, or the prescribed format of a document or text.
default.q.n2-34-q6-6.why.3: (d) 「形武」 is incorrect because 「武」 is the wrong kanji; the correct word ends with 「式」.
default.q.n2-34-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: Everyone, please take an active part in the discussion.
• Kanji meaning: 積極的 (literally, “active + inclined” - positive, proactive).
• Antonym: 消極的 (しょうきょくてき - negative, passive).
• Example: 彼女は仕事に積極的な態度で取り組んでいる。(She approaches her work with a very positive attitude.)
default.q.n2-34-q7-7.why.0: (a) 「責局的」 has both kanji wrong; 「責」 (as in 責任) and 「局」 (as in 局面) are not the correct characters.
default.q.n2-34-q7-7.why.1: (b) 「責極的」 uses the wrong kanji 「責」; the correct kanji is 「積」, as in “to accumulate” and “positive.”
default.q.n2-34-q7-7.why.2: (c) 「積局的」 uses the wrong kanji, 「局」. The correct kanji is 「極」, as in 積極的 and 極点.
default.q.n2-34-q7-7.why.3: (d)「積極的」has the correct kanji and means positive, proactive, or actively involved.
default.q.n2-34-q8-8.explanation:
Meaning: The mineral discovered at the bottom of the valley appears to be extremely rare.
• Related kanji: 底 (bottom, lowest part).
• Common expressions: 谷の底 (bottom of a valley), 海の底 (bottom of the sea), 心の底 (the bottom of one’s heart).
• Example: 彼は川の底に沈んだ時計を見つけ出した。(He found a watch that had sunk to the bottom of the river.)
default.q.n2-34-q8-8.why.0: (a) 「底」 uses the correct kanji, has the kun-reading 「そこ」, and means bottom or depths, such as the bottom of a valley, river, or one’s heart.
default.q.n2-34-q8-8.why.1: (b) 「低」 is incorrect: it means low or inferior, has the kun-reading 「ひく・い」, and is not read as 「そこ」.
default.q.n2-34-q8-8.why.2: (c)「抵」is incorrect because it is the kanji for tei (as in 抵抗 and 大抵), with the on-reading「てい」; it has no kun-reading「そこ」.
default.q.n2-34-q8-8.why.3: (d) 「邸」 is incorrect because it is the character in 邸宅, read 「てい」, and does not mean the bottom of a ravine or valley.
default.q.n2-34-q9-9.explanation:
Sentence meaning: I pray that war will never happen again.
• Kanji: 永久: eternal, permanent, forever.
• Distinctions: 永久 (えいきゅう: eternal, long-lasting), 永遠 (えいえん: forever, infinite), 恒久 (こうきゅう: lasting, permanent, as in 恒久平和).
• Example: 永久脱毛の手術を受けた。(I underwent permanent hair-removal treatment.)
default.q.n2-34-q9-9.why.0: (a) 「永久」has the correct kanji and the on-reading「えいきゅう」, meaning “permanent,” “eternal,” or “forever.”
default.q.n2-34-q9-9.why.1: (b)「永遠」has an incorrect reading; although the kanji mean eternity, it is read「えいえん」(eien), not「えいきゅう」.
default.q.n2-34-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「恒久」 has the wrong reading; although the kanji mean “permanent,” they are read as 「こうきゅう」(koukyuu), not 「えいきゅう」.
default.q.n2-34-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「恒遠」 is incorrect because it is not a commonly used Japanese vocabulary item and is not read as 「えいきゅう」.
default.q.n2-34-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: No matter how confident you are in your health, if you let your guard down, you may still catch a cold or the flu.
• Vocabulary: 油断 (carelessness, letting one's guard down, lack of vigilance).
• Related expression: 油断大敵 (ゆだんたいてき - carelessness is one's greatest enemy).
• Example: 油断している隙に財布を盗まれた。(While I was off guard, my wallet was stolen.)
default.q.n2-34-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「由断」 uses the wrong 「由」 (as in 理由); the correct kanji is 「油」 (oil, grease).
default.q.n2-34-q10-10.why.1: (b)「由談」uses two incorrect kanji;「由」and「談」do not combine to form this word.
default.q.n2-34-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「油断」uses the correct kanji and means carelessness, complacency, or letting one’s guard down.
default.q.n2-34-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「油談」uses the wrong kanji「談」; the correct second kanji is「断」.
default.q.n2-35-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 3. おける.
default.q.n2-35-q33-33.explanation:
- Meaning: At a conference in Japan, people discussed women’s status in the company.
- Kanji: 会議 (conference), 会社 (company), 女性 (women), 地位 (status).
- Example: 国際社会における日本の役割。(Japan’s role in the international community.)
default.q.n2-35-q33-33.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「～において」modifies a following verb or clause; it does not directly precede a noun as a modifier.
default.q.n2-35-q33-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「～においては」 contains the particle 「は」, which marks or emphasizes the topic of the following clause; it does not directly modify the noun immediately after it.
default.q.n2-35-q33-33.why.2: (c) Correct because the pattern 「N1 ＋ における ＋ N2」means “N2 in/at N1.” The attributive form 「における」directly modifies the noun 「女性の地位」.
default.q.n2-35-q33-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「～においても」 means "also in / even in..." and modifies the predicate or following clause, not a noun directly.
default.q.n2-35-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 対して.
default.q.n2-35-q34-34.explanation:
- Meaning: Using honorific language toward one’s seniors is not a cultural practice unique to Japan.
- Kanji meaning: 目上 (literally, “above the eyes” - a senior or superior), 敬語 (honorific language), 文化 (culture).
- Example: お客様に対して失礼な態度をとってはいけない。(You must not behave rudely toward customers.)
default.q.n2-35-q34-34.why.0: (a) Correct because the structure 「N ＋ に対して」 means “toward N” or “with respect to N,” indicating the recipient or target of an action (and is used with honorific language when referring to a superior).
default.q.n2-35-q34-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「N ＋ にとって」 means “for N” or “from N’s point of view,” expressing an evaluation or judgment based on N’s standpoint.
default.q.n2-35-q34-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「N ＋ について」 means “about N” and indicates the subject or topic of discussion or thought.
default.q.n2-35-q34-34.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「N ＋ によって」means 'by N,' 'depending on N,' or 'by means of N.'
default.q.n2-35-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2. よる.
default.q.n2-35-q35-35.explanation:
- Meaning: Traffic accidents caused by drivers falling asleep at the wheel are not decreasing at all.
- Sino-Japanese note: 運転 (うんてん: driving), 交通事故 (こうつうじこ: traffic accident), 減る (へる: to decrease).
- Example: 台風による被害が各地で報告されている。(Damage caused by the typhoon has been reported in various areas.)
default.q.n2-35-q35-35.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「～によって」 is used to connect clauses or modify a following verb or predicate; it does not appear directly before a noun.
default.q.n2-35-q35-35.why.1: (b) Correct because the structure 「N1 ＋ による ＋ N2」means 'N2 caused by or resulting from N1.' The attributive form 「による」directly modifies the following noun 「交通事故」.
default.q.n2-35-q35-35.why.2: (c) 「N ＋ によれば」 means “according to N” and is used to cite a source of information.
default.q.n2-35-q35-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect because「～により」is the formal form of「～によって」and modifies a clause, not a noun directly.
default.q.n2-35-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 4. せいで.
default.q.n2-35-q36-36.explanation:
- Meaning: I drank too much, so I had to miss university the next day.
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 酒 (alcohol), 次 (next), 大学 (university), 休む (rest, take time off).
- Example: 寝坊したせいで、電車に乗り遅れてしまった。(Because I overslept, I missed the train.)
default.q.n2-35-q36-36.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「～おかげで」 means “thanks to...” and is used when the cause produces a good or positive result.
default.q.n2-35-q36-36.why.1: (b) Incorrect, because「～うちに」means “while” or “during,” expressing taking advantage of a period or a change that occurs within that period.
default.q.n2-35-q36-36.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「～ところへ」 means “just as...” and describes another event unexpectedly occurring at that exact moment.
default.q.n2-35-q36-36.why.3: (d) Correct because the structure「V-た ＋ せいで」means “because of/due to” and indicates a cause leading to a bad or unwanted result (being absent from school).
default.q.n2-35-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 生まれて.
default.q.n2-35-q37-37.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: Ever since our child was born, my husband has come home earlier every evening.
- 子供: child, children; 以来: ever since; 主人: husband; 毎晩: every evening; 帰宅: returning home.
- Example: 日本に来て以来、ずっと東京に住んでいます。(I have lived in Tokyo ever since I came to Japan.)
default.q.n2-35-q37-37.why.0: (a) Correct. The structure「V-て ＋ 以来」means “ever since doing V,” indicating a state that has continued from that point until now.
default.q.n2-35-q37-37.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「以来」does not combine directly with the past form 「V-た」.
default.q.n2-35-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「以来」does not combine with the dictionary form 「V-る」.
default.q.n2-35-q37-37.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 以来 does not combine with the progressive form 「V-ている」.
default.q.n2-35-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 自分で掃除しなさい.
default.q.n2-35-q38-38.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: You are not a child anymore, so at least clean your own room.
- Kanji: 部屋 (へや, room), 掃除 (そうじ, cleaning).
- Example: 自分の靴くらい自分で履きなさい。(At least put on your own shoes yourself.)
default.q.n2-35-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「～たくない」 (not want to do) expresses a personal desire, which conflicts with the reminder in the preceding clause: “You’re not a child anymore.”
default.q.n2-35-q38-38.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「～なくてもいい」 (“it is okay not to do...”) contradicts the logic that the person is responsible for doing it.
default.q.n2-35-q38-38.why.2: (c) Correct because the structure 「V-しなさい」 gives a request or command, while the particle 「～くらい」 emphasizes the obvious minimum that must be done: “At least clean your own room.”
default.q.n2-35-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「～かもしれない」 (“may” or “might”) expresses uncertain conjecture and is unsuitable for advice or a request.
default.q.n2-35-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 戻り.
default.q.n2-35-q39-39.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: Mr. Tanaka is currently away from his seat, so I will ask him to call you back as soon as he returns.
- Kanji vocabulary: 席 (seat), 次第 (as soon as), 電話 (telephone).
- Example: 詳しい日程が決まり次第、ご連絡いたします。(I will contact you as soon as the detailed schedule has been decided.)
default.q.n2-35-q39-39.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the pattern 「～次第」 (as soon as...) does not combine with the dictionary form 「V-る」.
default.q.n2-35-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect because「～次第」does not combine with the past form「V-た」.
default.q.n2-35-q39-39.why.2: (c) Correct because the structure 「V-ます (ます removed) ＋ 次第」means “immediately after doing V, ...”; therefore, 「戻ります」becomes 「戻り次第」.
default.q.n2-35-q39-39.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「～次第」 cannot be combined with the V-て form.
default.q.n2-35-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 慣れることができた.
default.q.n2-35-q40-40.explanation:
- Meaning: Thanks to my senior colleague, even as a new employee, I was able to adapt to the company quickly.
- Vocabulary and kanji readings: 先輩 (senior colleague), 新入社員 (new employee), 慣れる (to become accustomed to, adapt), 会社 (company).
- Example: 先生のおかげで、無事に試験に合格することができました。(Thanks to my teacher, I was able to pass the exam successfully.)
default.q.n2-35-q40-40.why.0: (a) Correct because the preceding clause contains 「～のおかげで」 (“thanks to ...”), so the following clause must express a positive result achieved: 「慣れることができた」 (was able to adapt).
default.q.n2-35-q40-40.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the grammatical structure is wrong (the standard form expressing intention is「V-ようとする」, not「V-るようとする」), and it does not fit after「おかげで」.
default.q.n2-35-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect because「～たいと思う」expresses a desire or wish, so it does not fit after「おかげで」, which introduces an actual result that has been achieved.
default.q.n2-35-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it has a negative meaning (“was unable to get used to it”), which completely conflicts with the positive meaning of 「おかげで」.
default.q.n2-35-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ならないうちに.
default.q.n2-35-q41-41.explanation:
- Meaning: It is already five o’clock. Let’s go home before it gets dark.
- Kanji note: 暗い (dark), 帰る (to return home).
- Example: 忘れないうちに、メモを取っておきましょう。(Let’s make a note of it before we forget.)
default.q.n2-35-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「～ばかりに」 means “just because...” and leads to an unintended bad or negative result; it is not used to invite or propose an action.
default.q.n2-35-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「～までに」(by/before a certain time) generally takes the affirmative 「V-る」form or a noun, and does not combine with 「V-ないまでに」in this context.
default.q.n2-35-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「～ないように」means “so as not to...” and indicates the purpose of a deliberate action. Before a natural change caused by time or the environment, 「～ないうちに」is the most natural choice.
default.q.n2-35-q41-41.why.3: (d) Correct because 「V-ない ＋ うちに」 means “while still not...” or “before...”; here, it means “Let’s go home before it gets dark.”
default.q.n2-35-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. もとに.
default.q.n2-35-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: Hiragana and katakana were created based on kanji.
- Kanji note: 漢字 means kanji; 作る means to make or create.
- Example: この小説は実話をもとにして書かれた。(This novel was written based on a true story.)
default.q.n2-35-q42-42.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「N ＋ を問わず」means “regardless of/irrespective of N” (such as age or gender), so it does not fit the idea of creating written characters.
default.q.n2-35-q42-42.why.1: (b) Correct because the structure 「N ＋ をもとに（して）」 means “using N as the basis, material, or foundation for creating something new.”
default.q.n2-35-q42-42.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the grammar is 「N ＋ によって」, which takes the particle に, not the particle 「を」.
default.q.n2-35-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the grammar pattern is 「N ＋ に応じて」, meaning “according to” or “depending on,” and uses the particle 「に」, not 「を」.
default.q.n2-35-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 3. つれて.
default.q.n2-35-q43-43.explanation:
- Meaning: As the town develops, its population increases, and consequently the growing amount of waste is becoming a difficult problem.
- Related terms: 町 (town), 発展 (development), 人口 (population), 増える (increase), 結果 (result), 問題 (problem).
- Example: 年を取るにつれて、体力が衰えてきた。(As I have gotten older, my physical strength has gradually declined.)
default.q.n2-35-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「～に比べて」 means “compared with...” and is used to compare two separate things.
default.q.n2-35-q43-43.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「～にとって」 means “for” or “from the standpoint of,” presenting an evaluation from the perspective of a particular person or group.
default.q.n2-35-q43-43.why.2: (c) Correct because the structure 「V-る / N ＋ につれて」 means that as A changes, B changes correspondingly as well (as the town develops, the population increases).
default.q.n2-35-q43-43.why.3: (d) Incorrect because「～に対して」means “toward/with respect to” or “in contrast to,” and does not express simultaneous change over time.
default.q.n2-35-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 2. はじめ.
default.q.n2-35-q44-44.explanation:
- Meaning: After coming to Japan, I ate most of the main Japanese dishes; sushi comes first among them.
- Kanji readings: 主 (SHU - main, principal), 和食 (WA-SHOKU - Japanese cuisine).
- Example: 日本には富士山をはじめ、多くの有名な山がある。(Japan has many famous mountains, including Mount Fuji.)
default.q.n2-35-q44-44.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the grammatical structure 「～をおわず」does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n2-35-q44-44.why.1: (b) Correct because the pattern 「N ＋ をはじめ（として）」 means "including N as a representative example / foremost among them N" and introduces the most typical example in a group.
default.q.n2-35-q44-44.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「N ＋ をめぐって」 means “concerning or revolving around N,” and is commonly used for disputes, discussions, or disagreements.
default.q.n2-35-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「N ＋ をこめて」means “putting all of one’s N into something” (often used with feelings, sincerity, or wishes, such as 「心をこめて」and 「愛をこめて」).
default.q.n2-35-q45-45.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The ★ position is answer choice 1 (を).
default.q.n2-35-q45-45.explanation:
Complete sentence: 私たちの会社は経験の有無を問わず、やる気のある人を求めている。
Meaning: Our company is looking for motivated people, regardless of whether they have experience.
default.q.n2-35-q45-45.why.0: (a) 「を」: It occupies the third position (★), follows the noun 「経験の有無」, and combines with 「問わず」 to form the grammar pattern 「〜を問わず」.
default.q.n2-35-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「経験の」is in the first position and modifies the noun 「有無」that follows, forming the phrase 「経験の有無」(whether or not one has experience).
default.q.n2-35-q45-45.why.2: (c) 「問わず」: It comes fourth, after 「〜を」, completing the grammar pattern 「〜を問わず」 (regardless of...).
default.q.n2-35-q45-45.why.3: (d) 「有無」: It occupies position 2 and is modified by 「経験の」 to form a complete noun phrase functioning as the object of 「〜を問わず」.
default.q.n2-35-q46-46.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1. The star ★ is in position 4 (咲いている).
default.q.n2-35-q46-46.explanation:
Complete sentence: この道は、一年を通して美しい花々が咲いていることから「フラワー通り」と呼ばれている。
Translation: This street is called "Flower Street" because beautiful flowers bloom here throughout the year.
default.q.n2-35-q46-46.why.0: (a) 「ことから」: It occupies the fourth position, following the plain-form clause 「咲いている」 to form 「〜ことから」, which gives the basis or reason (because..., it is called...).
default.q.n2-35-q46-46.why.1: (b) 「美しい花々が」: It stands in the second position and serves as the subject immediately before the predicate 「咲いている」.
default.q.n2-35-q46-46.why.2: (c) 「を通して」 occupies position 1 and combines with the time noun 「一年」 to form 「一年を通して」, meaning “throughout the year” or “year-round.”
default.q.n2-35-q46-46.why.3: (d) 「咲いている」: It occupies position 3 (the ★ position), functions as the verb predicate for 「美しい花々が」, and modifies 「ことから」 that follows.
default.q.n2-35-q47-47.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 3 → 2 → 4. The ★ position is 2 (ことに).
default.q.n2-35-q47-47.explanation:
Complete sentence: 交際範囲が広い中村君は、情報集めることにかけてはだれよりも優れている。
Meaning: Nakamura, who has a wide circle of acquaintances, is better than anyone else at gathering information.
default.q.n2-35-q47-47.why.0: (a) 「情報」: It occupies position 1 as the direct object of the verb 「集める」 that follows (to collect information).
default.q.n2-35-q47-47.why.1: (b) 「ことに」: It occupies the third position (★), following the verb in its dictionary form 「集める」 to nominalize the action and combine with 「かけては」 in the structure 「〜ことにかけては」.
default.q.n2-35-q47-47.why.2: (c) 「集める」 is in position 2; it is the verb that follows the object 「情報」 and precedes 「ことに」.
default.q.n2-35-q47-47.why.3: (d) 「かけては」occupies the fourth position and combines with 「ことに」to form the grammar pattern 「〜にかけては」(when it comes to..., in terms of...), before a clause expressing superiority.
default.q.n2-35-q48-48.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 1 → 4 → 3. The ★ position is 4 (からに).
default.q.n2-35-q48-48.explanation:
Complete sentence: 私たちがこうして無事に暮らしていけるのは、みなさんが支えてくださるからにほかなりません。
Meaning: The only reason we can live peacefully like this is because of everyone’s support and help.
default.q.n2-35-q48-48.why.0: (a) 「くださる」: It occupies the second position and combines with the preceding te-form verb 「支えて」 to form the honorific expression 「支えてくださる」 (help us).
default.q.n2-35-q48-48.why.1: (b) 「支えて」: In position 1, this is the te-form of the verb 「支える」. It follows the subject 「みなさんが」 and connects to 「くださる」.
default.q.n2-35-q48-48.why.2: (c) 「ほか」: It occupies the fourth position, combining with 「からに」 before it and 「なりません」 after it to form the grammar pattern 「〜からにほかならない」 (“is precisely because... / is nothing other than...” ).
default.q.n2-35-q48-48.why.3: (d) 「からに」: It occupies the third position (the ★ position), follows the clause expressing the reason 「支えてくださる」, and comes before 「ほか」 in the pattern 「〜からにほかならない」.
default.q.n2-35-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The position of the star ★ is 1 (謝る).
default.q.n2-35-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: あなたに責任はないのだから謝ることはないと思う。
Meaning: Since you are not responsible at all, I don't think you need to apologize.
default.q.n2-35-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「謝る」occupies position 3 (the ★ position). It is a dictionary-form verb placed before 「ことはない」to form 「〜ことはない」(there is no need to apologize).
default.q.n2-35-q49-49.why.1: (b) 「責任はない」: In first position, it combines with「あなたに」at the beginning of the sentence to form the complete clause「あなたに責任はない」(you are not responsible / it is not your fault).
default.q.n2-35-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「ことはない」occupies the fourth position, follows the verb「謝る」to form「〜ことはない」(there is no need to...), and combines with「と思う」at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n2-35-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「のだから」 occupies the second position and follows the clause 「責任はない」 to explain the reason, providing the basis for the advice in the following clause.
default.q.n2-35-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 燃やすほど.
default.q.n2-35-q50-50.explanation:
This question tests the N2 grammar pattern 「〜ば〜ほど」(the more..., the more...).
- The first clause has the conditional form「燃やせば」, which combines with「燃やすほど」in the blank to form the complete pattern:「燃やせば燃やすほど、...」(the more fuel is burned, the more CO2 is emitted).
- The following clause expresses a corresponding increase in emissions or global temperature.
- The other choices are: (1)「〜限り」(as long as / within the limits of), (2)「〜こそ」(grammatically incorrect connection), and (3)「〜以上」(now that... / once...), none of which fits this proportional increase pattern.
default.q.n2-35-q50-50.why.0: (a) 燃やす限り: Means “as long as it continues to burn” or “provided that it is still burning,” expressing the scope or condition for continuation. It cannot combine with 燃やせば in the preceding clause to form a correlative comparative structure.
default.q.n2-35-q50-50.why.1: (b) 燃やすこそ: Grammatically incorrect connection. A dictionary-form verb cannot be followed directly by the emphatic particle「こそ」; use「燃やしてこそ」or「燃やすことこそ」instead.
default.q.n2-35-q50-50.why.2: (c) 燃やす以上: Means “once you have burned it, naturally...” and expresses an inevitable responsibility or consequence; it does not create a proportional “the more..., the more...” relationship.
default.q.n2-35-q50-50.why.3: (d) 燃やすほど: Combined with the preceding 「燃やせば」, it forms the N2 grammar pattern 「〜ば〜ほど」 (“the more..., the more...”), perfectly expressing “the more we burn, the greater the CO2 emissions become.”
default.q.n2-35-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 2. よる.
default.q.n2-35-q51-51.explanation:
This question tests the use of a connective expression that modifies a noun: 「〜による＋noun」(due to, caused by...).
- In the sentence, 「二酸化炭素の増加に＿＿地球温暖化」requires an expression indicating the cause of global warming.
- 「〜による」follows a noun expressing the cause (二酸化炭素の増加) and modifies the noun that follows (地球温暖化), meaning “global warming caused by the increase in CO2.”
- The other choices—「〜に対する」(toward, concerning), 「〜につれて」(as, in accordance with a change over time), and 「〜にとって」(for, from the standpoint of)—do not express a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n2-35-q51-51.why.0: (a) 対する: In the phrase「〜に対する」, it means “toward/in relation to (a target),” and is not used to indicate a causal relationship that produces a phenomenon.
default.q.n2-35-q51-51.why.1: (b) よる: In the pattern “〜による＋noun,” it means “caused by” or “due to,” modifying the following noun and indicating the cause of a phenomenon or result.
default.q.n2-35-q51-51.why.2: (c) つれて: In the structure "〜につれて," it means "along with/as something changes." It does not directly modify a noun in this way or indicate a direct cause.
default.q.n2-35-q51-51.why.3: (d) とって: Used in the phrase “〜にとって,” meaning “for” or “from the standpoint of...,” to state a viewpoint or evaluation from the perspective of a particular person or group. It does not fit here.
default.q.n2-35-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 3. おそれがあります.
default.q.n2-35-q52-52.explanation:
This question tests the N2 grammar pattern 「〜おそれがある」(there is a risk that..., there is a fear that something bad or dangerous will happen).
- The passage predicts disasters and negative climate change impacts in the future if global warming continues.
- 「おそれがあります」is a formal, objective expression commonly used in written language, news reports, and argumentative writing to warn about the possibility of negative or dangerous consequences, such as natural disasters, crop failures, rising sea levels, and ecosystem decline.
- The other choices are: (1)「ことになっています」(a rule or scheduled arrangement), (2)「せいです」(blaming something that has already happened), and (4)「とおりです」(as is true or as planned). None expresses a prediction of future risk.
default.q.n2-35-q52-52.why.0: (a) ことになっています: means "it is مقررated that" or "it is scheduled that" and is used for rules, customs, or predetermined schedules. It is not used for predicting a harmful risk in nature.
default.q.n2-35-q52-52.why.1: (b) せいです: Meaning “because of,” it is generally used to assign responsibility for an unfavorable result that has already occurred; it cannot be used at the end of a sentence as the predicate for predicting a future risk.
default.q.n2-35-q52-52.why.2: (c) おそれがあります: This belongs to the N2 grammar pattern 「〜おそれがある」 (“there is a risk that...”), making it precise and completely appropriate for a warning about environmental risks.
default.q.n2-35-q52-52.why.3: (d) とおりです: Means “just as / according to...,” used to confirm that something happened as expected or instructed, so it does not fit a context involving a predicted hazard.
default.q.n2-35-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 4. すれば.
default.q.n2-35-q53-53.explanation:
This sentence tests the use of the conditional pattern 「〜ば」(“if...then...”) in logical argumentative writing.
- The sentence presents an action that individuals can take and the positive result that may be achieved: 「生活をすれば、地球温暖化の進行を遅らせることができる」(If we adopt an energy-saving lifestyle, we can slow the progress of global warming).
- The conditional form 「〜ば」(すれば) expresses a hypothetical condition based on a logical and objective relationship, and naturally combines with the ability expression 「〜ことができる」in the following clause.
- 「したら」is conversational, 「するなら」usually accompanies a personal intention or advice, and 「すると」indicates an immediate discovery or natural consequence, so it does not naturally combine with volition or ability in the following clause.
default.q.n2-35-q53-53.why.0: (a) したら: This is a conditional form with a conversational, everyday nuance, or it can emphasize an action that occurs after doing something; it is not appropriate for formal argumentative writing.
default.q.n2-35-q53-53.why.1: (b) するなら: means “if you intend to do it” or “if it is a matter of doing it.” It is commonly followed by advice or a request directed at someone based on their intention, so it does not fit a general logical hypothetical statement.
default.q.n2-35-q53-53.why.2: (c) すると: This expresses an immediate natural consequence or a sudden discovery (“as soon as...,” “when...,” or “then I found that...”); the following clause cannot express ability or volition such as "〜ことができる".
default.q.n2-35-q53-53.why.3: (d) すれば: the conditional 「〜ば」has a logical, objective, and standard written style, expressing a hypothetical condition–result relationship: “if one does ..., it may be possible to ...”.
default.q.n2-35-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3. できることから始めてみてください.
default.q.n2-35-q54-54.explanation:
This question tests the ability to understand the structure and message of an argumentative essay that calls for action.
- This is the concluding sentence after the essay has analyzed the current situation and solutions to an environmental issue. The author wants to offer readers gentle, practical encouragement and call on them to take action together.
- The pattern 「できることから始めてみてください」(Please try starting with what you can do) has an encouraging, positive tone, urging readers to take small steps within their abilities to protect the Earth.
- The other options have inappropriate tones: rigidly forceful, personally negative, or indifferent and defiant.
default.q.n2-35-q54-54.why.0: (a) ルールを守らなければならない: This sounds coercive, like a rigid legal command, and does not create empathy or a sense of voluntary responsibility for the conclusion of the essay.
default.q.n2-35-q54-54.why.1: (b) 何もしないではいられません: This expresses the author’s own inability to suppress an agitated feeling (“I cannot simply sit still and do nothing”), not an appeal to the reader.
default.q.n2-35-q54-54.why.2: (c) できることから始めてみてください means “Please try starting with what you can do.” It is a gentle, encouraging, and perfectly appropriate appeal in an essay about the environment.
default.q.n2-35-q54-54.why.3: (d) これから地球がどうなるか見ていてください: This has an indifferent or challenging tone (“watch and see what happens to the Earth”), which is completely contrary to the article’s call to protect the environment.
default.q.n2-35-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (体の痛みは心にもよくない影響があるから): The author hates pain because physical pain does not remain merely physical; it also has a negative impact on and distorts the human mind and spirit.
default.q.n2-35-q55-55.explanation:
- Main point of the passage:
The author expresses a dislike of pain because it does not merely cause physical harm; it also has a deeply negative effect on the mind, breaking down and distorting the human spirit. The author rejects the traditional medical view that pain accompanying treatment is simply something patients must grit their teeth and endure.

- Question translation:
Which is the most appropriate reason for the author's dislike of pain?

- Answer choices:
1. Because the author fears the pain accompanying medical treatment.
2. Because physical pain also has a harmful effect on the mind.
3. Because a patient's pain is sometimes ignored during medical treatment.
4. Because enduring pain is considered natural.
default.q.n2-35-q55-55.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage never mentions that the author is “afraid” of pain during treatment (痛みが怖い); it emphasizes the harmful effects of pain on the mind.
default.q.n2-35-q55-55.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because it is directly quoted from the passage: 「僕は痛みが嫌いです。それは痛みというものが、単に肉体的な痛みや苦痛であるだけでなく、人間の精神にまで大きな影響をおよぼすものだからです」 and 「痛みは肉体を蝕むだけでなく、人間の心や魂までも変形させるものなのです。だから、僕は痛みが嫌いです」.
default.q.n2-35-q55-55.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because “the patient’s pain itself was being ignored” (患者の痛みそのものが無視されていた) is merely an example of insensitivity in past medical treatment, not the fundamental reason the author hates pain.
default.q.n2-35-q55-55.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because “believing that pain is inevitable” (痛みがあるのはあたりまえだ) is an outdated medical view that the author seeks to refute, not the author’s reason.
default.q.n2-35-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author does not mention choosing rice that contains a high amount of amylase.
default.q.n2-35-q56-56.explanation:
- Main point: The author discusses how to store rice so that it remains delicious. The worst method is to leave it in the original shopping bag at room temperature with sunlight shining on it. The author recommends storing rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Even refrigerated rice loses its flavor after about three months as its amylase content gradually decreases, so rice should be treated like fresh food.
- Question: Which of the following did the author NOT mention as a way to enjoy better-tasting rice?
  1. Keeping it in a cool place.
  2. Storing it away from direct sunlight.
  3. Choosing rice that contains a large amount of amylase.
  4. Putting it in a completely airtight container.
default.q.n2-35-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author does mention storing rice in the refrigerator (「冷蔵庫で保存するのがおすすめ」), which is a cool place.
default.q.n2-35-q56-56.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author does mention this indirectly by warning that the worst way to store it is in a place exposed to sunlight (「いちばんよくないのは、... 日光の当たるところに常温で置いておく方法です」), meaning it should be kept away from direct sunlight.
default.q.n2-35-q56-56.why.2: (c) Correct because the author only states that the gradual decrease of amylase reduces the tastiness of rice (「これは、お米に含まれるアミラーゼという物質が減ってしまうことによります」), and does not recommend choosing rice varieties containing more amylase.
default.q.n2-35-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author does mention putting rice in a container that can be sealed (「お米は密閉できる入れ物に入れて」), which corresponds to 完全に閉められる容器.
default.q.n2-35-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 4: It cannot be said that evolution necessarily means progress.
default.q.n2-35-q57-57.explanation:
Main point:
The author defines «evolution» (進化) simply as living organisms «changing» (変化) over time, and such change does not necessarily mean «progress» (進歩). The concept of «progress» involves a subjective value judgment—from bad to good—which has led to the biased classification of animals as lower or higher and to the assumption that humans are a superior species. Therefore, it is incorrect to say that evolution automatically means progress.

Question:
What does the author think about "evolution" and "progress"?

Answer choices:
1. When living organisms change, it always means both evolution and progress.
2. Change over time is evolution, not progress.
3. Evolution is necessary in order to make progress.
4. It cannot be said that evolution automatically means progress.
default.q.n2-35-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author clearly states that changes in living things are not necessarily always progress (「必ずしも『進歩』であるとは限りません」), which directly contradicts 常に (“always”) in the answer choice.
default.q.n2-35-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author only says that change over time is not necessarily progress, not that change is absolutely "not progress" (進歩ではない).
default.q.n2-35-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention a conditional relationship in which progress requires evolution.
default.q.n2-35-q57-57.why.3: (d) Correct because it is directly quoted from the opening sentence of the passage: 「進化とは、生物が時間とともに「変化」していくことであって、その変化は必ずしも「進歩」であるとは限りません。」 (Evolution is the process by which living organisms “change” over time, and that change is not necessarily “progress.”)
default.q.n2-35-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 実際に被害が出て初めて、手入れをする。
default.q.n2-35-q58-58.explanation:
Main point of the passage: The author explains why buildings are vulnerable to natural disasters (災害にもろい). In Japan, after building a house, people generally do not proactively perform regular maintenance. They only begin repairs when visible damage has actually occurred, such as roof tiles being blown away by a typhoon or wall plaster peeling off after heavy rain and flooding.

Question translation:
What does the author think about Japanese people’s attitude toward housing?

Answer choices:
1. They carefully maintain their homes every day, down to the smallest details.
2. They do not maintain their homes because they give up, believing that natural disasters cannot be prevented.
3. They do not maintain their homes because they believe that homes sell for more if nonprofessionals do not interfere.
4. They only begin maintenance and repairs after actual damage has appeared.
default.q.n2-35-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that in Japan, people generally do not actively maintain their homes after building them (「わが国では、建てたが最後、家の手入れを積極的にやらないのが一般的です」), contrary to carrying out meticulous daily maintenance.
default.q.n2-35-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not say that Japanese people resign themselves or give up because disasters cannot be prevented (あきらめ). The reason is that people easily forget disasters when they do not occur frequently.
default.q.n2-35-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that property sells for a higher price when nonprofessionals do not intervene. The author only states that the older a house is, the more sharply its real-estate value declines.
default.q.n2-35-q58-58.why.3: (d) Correct, as the passage clearly states: 「台風で屋根瓦が飛んだり、大雨で浸水して壁土が落ちたりすれば修理します。つまり、雨漏りがしなかったり、目で見て被害がわからなければ、家は補修しないのです。」 (Repairs are made only when a typhoon blows roof tiles away or heavy rain causes flooding and wall plaster to fall. In other words, if there is no leak or no visible damage, the house is not repaired or renovated.)
default.q.n2-35-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 2: そのテーマについて詳しくない人 (a person who is not familiar with that topic).
default.q.n2-35-q59-59.explanation:
**Main idea:** The author uses the metaphor of a movie theater to illustrate explanations and presentations: the speaker is someone who has been inside the theater for a long time and whose eyes have adjusted to the darkness (someone deeply familiar with the topic), while a first-time listener is like a “person who has just entered the movie theater” (someone unfamiliar with the darkness, meaning unfamiliar with the topic).

**Question translation:** What kind of person is “someone who has just entered the movie theater”?

**Answer choices:**
1. Someone whose eyes have not adjusted to the darkness and who has tripped.
2. Someone who is not familiar with the topic.
3. Someone giving a presentation for the first time.
4. Someone who knows the content of the explanation very well.
default.q.n2-35-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this is merely a literal detail in the hypothetical example (and the passage only says he was even afraid that he might trip 「転ばないかと恐怖さえ感じている」, not that he actually fell), not the metaphorical meaning the author intended to convey.
default.q.n2-35-q59-59.why.1: (b) Correct because the author clearly explains that a first-time listener on the topic is "a person who has just entered the movie theater," meaning someone who is unfamiliar with it. The passage states: 「一方、今日初めて説明を聞く人は、あなたが伝えたいテーマに関しては「たった今、映画館に入ったばかりの人」なのです。」
default.q.n2-35-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the speaker (話し手) understands the topic well and is someone who entered the theater earlier, whose eyes have already adjusted to the darkness—not someone who has just entered.
default.q.n2-35-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the person familiar with the explanation corresponds to the speaker (話し手 - 「説明したいテーマを熟知しています」), in contrast to the person who has just entered the theater.
default.q.n2-35-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The elderly man thought that the author had opened the door automatically for him.

- Main idea: As the author was about to leave the store, the automatic door opened. The elderly man riding the electric tricycle in front thought that the author had opened the door for him on purpose, so he turned around and said, "Thank you."
- Question translation: Why did the elderly man say, "Thank you"?
- Answer choices:
1. Because he thought the author would push the electric tricycle, which could not move.
2. Because he thought the author would transport the electric tricycle for him.
3. Because he thought the author had slowed down to match his pace.
4. Because he thought the author had opened the automatic door for him.

default.q.n2-35-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage contains no detail about carrying or transporting the electric tricycle.
default.q.n2-35-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author was simply leaving the store and did not intentionally slow down to match the elderly man's pace.
default.q.n2-35-q60-60.why.3: (d) Correct because the old man thought the author had opened the door for him, based on the sentence: 「お礼を言われるまで、おじいさんにとって自動ドアを通ることが大変だなんて、少しも気付かなかった。結果として親切な行動となったが、それは偶然のことで…」 (Until he thanked me, I had not noticed at all that passing through the automatic door was difficult for him. It turned out to be a kind act, but that was merely a coincidence...).
default.q.n2-35-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The action was not motivated by kindness, yet the elderly man thanked the person.
default.q.n2-35-q61-61.explanation:
- Main idea: The author feels very guilty and apologetic because they did not realize how difficult things were for the elderly man and had no intention of kindly helping him. The door happened to open when the author went outside, yet the elderly man sincerely thanked them.
- Question translation: Why did the author “feel very guilty toward the elderly man”?
- Answer choices:
1. Because the elderly man mistook the author for someone else and thanked them.
2. Because the action was not motivated by kindness, yet the author was thanked for it.
3. Although the author was thanked, they did not help the elderly man through the automatic door.
4. Because the author failed to notice how difficult it was for the elderly man to pass through the automatic door and closed it.
default.q.n2-35-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the elderly man never mistook the author for someone else.
default.q.n2-35-q61-61.why.1: (b) Correct because the passage states directly: 「結果として親切な行動となったが、それは偶然のことで、親切な気持ちではなかったのだから。」 (Although the result was a kind act, it happened by chance and did not come from kind feelings).
default.q.n2-35-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the automatic door had actually opened as the author was leaving, which enabled the elderly man to pass through; it was not that the author failed to help him.
default.q.n2-35-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the automatic door opened by itself when someone exited; the author never closed it in front of the elderly man.
default.q.n2-35-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Thinking about others and taking the initiative to help them sincerely.
default.q.n2-35-q62-62.explanation:
- Main point: Through this experience, the author realized that things that seem ordinary to them can be very difficult for someone else. The author tells themselves that if they encounter a similar situation again, they will quickly recognize the other person's difficulty and take genuinely heartfelt action to help.
- Translation of the question: What does the author plan to do from now on?
- Translation of the choices:
1. Because they were thanked, they want to respond clearly next time.
2. Think about the other person and proactively take action to help others.
3. When they receive help during a difficult time, they will definitely say thank you.
4. Even if something seems insignificant to them, they will try not to do things that other people dislike.
default.q.n2-35-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author wants the action to come from the heart and be worthy of the words of thanks, rather than merely “clearly returning the thanks.”
default.q.n2-35-q62-62.why.1: (b) Correct. The final sentence of the passage states: 「その人の立場にならなければ、なかなか分からないことだけれど、今度こんな状態に出合ったら、すぐに気が付くようにしたい。そして、今度はお礼を言われても、それにこたえられるような、気持ちからの行動にしたい。」 (It is difficult to understand unless you put yourself in that person’s position, but if I encounter such a situation again, I want to notice it immediately. Next time, I want to act sincerely so that I can respond even when someone thanks me.)
default.q.n2-35-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this choice refers to “thanking someone for helping,” which is contrary to the author's intention of “helping others.”
default.q.n2-35-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage focuses on recognizing the hardships of people who are struggling and helping them (苦労する人), not on things that other people dislike (いやがること).
default.q.n2-35-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 4: It is meant to remind someone cutting in line to join the line and queue properly in the correct order.
default.q.n2-35-q63-63.explanation:
Main point: Someone cut in line at a ticket counter, and another person reminded them, “Everyone is waiting in order.” The other people who witnessed it also wanted to say the same thing to the person who cut in line, so they felt relieved when someone spoke up for them: “Thank goodness someone said it.”

Question translation: The sentence says, “I wanted to say something inside,” but what did the person want to say, and to whom?
Answer choices:
1. They wanted to thank the person who spoke up.
2. They wanted to complain to the person who cut in line and tell them to keep order.
3. They wanted to tell the person who spoke up that they had also intended to say something.
4. They wanted to tell the person who cut in line to join the queue and wait properly.
default.q.n2-35-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the people around them did not want to thank the person who reminded them; they felt relieved that someone had voiced their feelings to the person who cut in line.
default.q.n2-35-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the intended reminder is to ask people to line up in order, not to complain that people cutting in line should remain orderly or quiet (“静かにするように”).
default.q.n2-35-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because they did not intend to tell the person who had just reminded them that they themselves had also intended to give a reminder.
default.q.n2-35-q63-63.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「人々が列をつくって並んでいるのに割り込む人に、「みんな、順番で待っているのよ」などと注意する。内心、何か言いたい、と思っていた他の人々は、「代わりに言ってくれてよかった」とほっとする。」 The people around them also wanted to tell the person who cut in line to wait their turn, just as the other person had done on their behalf.
default.q.n2-35-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Doing something for another person’s benefit even if one may suffer a personal disadvantage.
default.q.n2-35-q64-64.explanation:
Main point: The author defines "altruistic behavior" (利他行動) as acting for the benefit of others even when it is uncertain whether the action will benefit oneself and may even cause personal disadvantage or loss.

Question translation: What does "altruistic behavior" mean here?
Answer choices:
1. Acting for others even though one may suffer a disadvantage or loss.
2. Acting for others so that one can also feel comfortable and fulfilled.
3. Acting for others with the belief that other people's benefits will ultimately benefit oneself.
4. Acting with concern only for others without realizing that one might suffer a disadvantage.
default.q.n2-35-q64-64.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「必ずしも自分の得にならない、むしろ損になるかもしれないのに、他人の利益のために敢えてする、というのが利他行動である。」— Altruistic behavior means deliberately acting for someone else’s benefit even when it may not benefit oneself and may even cause a disadvantage.
default.q.n2-35-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage never states that acting for others is intended to give oneself a comfortable or enriched feeling (“自分自身も豊かな気分になれるように”).
default.q.n2-35-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the definition does not say that acting for others' benefit will ultimately become one's own benefit ("他者の利益は結局自分の利益になると考えて"). Instead, it emphasizes accepting the risk of suffering a loss oneself.
default.q.n2-35-q64-64.why.3: (d) The incorrect part is “not realizing the possibility that they might suffer a loss” (「自分が損をする可能性に気付かず」). In fact, they recognize the risk but still dare to do it (「敢えてする」).
default.q.n2-35-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The person who gives the reminder may have to endure the discomfort or irritation caused by reminding someone.
default.q.n2-35-q65-65.explanation:
Main point: Reminding others requires energy and carries the risk of causing arguments, frustration, and discomfort for the person doing the reminding. Accepting these disadvantages in order to create order and benefit everyone is why reminding someone is considered an altruistic act.

Question translation: What can be considered a "disadvantage" of "reminding someone"?
Answer choices:
1. Both the person doing the reminding and the person being reminded feel uncomfortable.
2. Reminding someone makes the people around them feel uncomfortable.
3. The person doing the reminding feels uncomfortable because of their own action.
4. The person being reminded feels uncomfortable because they were reminded.
default.q.n2-35-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because “disadvantage” in the definition of altruistic behavior here emphasizes the risks and losses borne by the person who steps forward to admonish someone else ("自らがそのような不利益を被りつつ"), not the idea that both people feel uncomfortable.
default.q.n2-35-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the people around them were not annoyed; instead, they benefited at no cost (“ゼロのコストで利益を得た”) and felt relieved (“ほっとする”).
default.q.n2-35-q65-65.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「一方で、行動することにはエネルギーが必要であり、喧嘩になったり、不快な思いをしたりするリスクもある。自らがそのような不利益を被りつつ、他者には無償の利益を与えるという意味で、「注意すること」は利他行動なのである。」 The disadvantages mentioned are that the person who gives the warning must expend energy, face the risk of an argument, and endure discomfort personally.
default.q.n2-35-q65-65.why.3: (d) This is incorrect because the disadvantage here refers to the risks faced by the person who gives the reminder—the person performing the altruistic act—not the person being reminded.
default.q.n2-35-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 4. つまり.
default.q.n2-35-q66-66.explanation:
Main point: The passage explains that when a plane crosses the International Date Line while traveling from the United States to Japan, the date must be moved forward by one day, which means losing one day of the journey. The missing conjunction should restate or summarize the equivalent idea.

Question translation:
Which word is most appropriate for （ ★ ）?

Choice translations:
1. ただし: however / there is one exception (adds a condition or exception)
2. ついに: finally (a result after a long period)
3. けれど: but (expresses contrast)
4. つまり: in other words / in short (restates or explains an equivalent idea)
default.q.n2-35-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because「ただし」adds a condition, limitation, or exception to the preceding clause; it is not suitable for restating equivalent content.
default.q.n2-35-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「ついに」indicates a final result achieved after a long period of waiting or effort; it does not fit a context in which a concept is being explained.
default.q.n2-35-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「けれど」 is a conjunction expressing opposition or contrast, whereas “moving one day forward” and “losing one day” are two ways of describing the same event and are not contradictory.
default.q.n2-35-q66-66.why.3: (d) Correct, because 「つまり」 summarizes or restates the preceding idea: moving the date forward by one day means losing one day. The passage says: 「日付変更線を越えるときに、 日付を 1 日先に進めることになった。（つまり）、 1 日失われたのである。」
default.q.n2-35-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 1. シックラーさんは、乗船していた人たちに誕生日を祝ってもらった。
default.q.n2-35-q67-67.explanation:
Main point: Mrs. Sickler is traveling on the train with her son. Because her birthday happened to fall on the day that was skipped when they crossed the International Date Line, everyone on the train held a party to celebrate and cheer her up.

Question:
Which of the following is consistent with the passage?

Choices:
1. The people traveling with Mrs. Sickler wished her a happy birthday.
2. Mrs. Sickler's son held a party for his sad mother.
3. At the International Date Line, one day was added, giving the passengers a more enjoyable experience.
4. The captain had to set the clocks back one hour every day until they reached the International Date Line.
default.q.n2-35-q67-67.why.0: (a) Correct because Ms. Sickler's birthday happened to fall on the day lost when crossing the International Date Line, and everyone on board held a party to celebrate and encourage her. Quotation: 「そのシックラーさんの誕生日がたまたま日付変更線を越える日で、シックラーさんのためにパーティーを開くことにして、みんなでシックラーさんを励ました。おかげでみんな特別なパーティーを楽しむことができて...」
default.q.n2-35-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage clearly says that everyone on the ship organized a party for her (「シックラーさんのためにパーティーを開くことにして、みんなでシックラーさんを励ました」), not that the son alone held the party.
default.q.n2-35-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because when crossing the date line while traveling from the United States to Japan, the date is moved forward, so one day is lost (「1 日失われたのである」), not added.
default.q.n2-35-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the sailor told the passengers to set their clocks back before going to bed every night («毎日寝る前に 1 時間時計を遅れさせるように船員に言われた»); it was not the captain who had to adjust the clock.
default.q.n2-35-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 失われた誕生日.
default.q.n2-35-q68-68.explanation:
Main point: The passage recounts a memorable experience on a ship crossing the Pacific: the time-zone difference and the International Date Line caused exactly one day, which happened to be Ms. Sickler's birthday, to disappear, leading to a special and unforgettable party. Therefore, "The Lost Birthday" best captures the central point of the article.

Question translation:
Which title would be most appropriate for this passage?

Answer choices:
1. 貨客船と時間: The Passenger-and-Cargo Ship and Time
2. 失われた誕生日: The Lost Birthday
3. 交換留学先での思いで: Memories from an Exchange Study-Abroad Program
4. 定年退職のパーティー: A Retirement Party
default.q.n2-35-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the title “Cargo-and-Passenger Trains and Time” is too general and dryly descriptive. It does not convey the central story or the memorable experience of the special birthday party.
default.q.n2-35-q68-68.why.1: (b) Correct because the entire story focuses on the amusing event in which crossing the International Date Line caused one day to disappear, and that missing day happened to be Mrs. Sickler's birthday, leading to a special party to make up for it. The passage states: 「日付変更線を越えるときに、 日付を 1 日先に進めることになった。（つまり）、 1 日失われたのである。ところで、...そのシックラーさんの誕生日がたまたま日付変更線を越える日で、シックラーさんのためにパーティーを開くことにして...」
default.q.n2-35-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the event occurred on a train while returning home after completing the study-abroad program (「その留学を終えて帰国するとき」), not at the school or study-abroad site in the United States.
default.q.n2-35-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the party was held to celebrate the birthday that was lost when crossing the International Date Line, not a retirement party; the retirement was merely information introducing Ms. Sickler.
default.q.n2-35-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Passage A focuses on describing the author’s changes, while Passage B focuses on summarizing the plot and the author’s intended message.
default.q.n2-35-q69-69.explanation:
- Summary of the content:
  + Passage A: Focuses on the author's changes and experimentation (shifting from a familiar, everyday style to an archaic, formal style) while maintaining an engaging ability to guide the reader, and also expresses thoughts about the possibility of a sequel.
  + Passage B: Provides a general outline of the plot (the protagonist is an ordinary young man who faces a financial upheaval that shakes society, as well as challenges in his private life) and the author's message or intention (the human heart cannot be defeated by social pressure), while expressing hopes for the sequel in order to evaluate the work as a whole.

- Translation of the question: Which of the following statements about Passage A and Passage B is correct?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Passage A mainly discusses changes in the author, while Passage B mainly discusses the story's outline and the author's intention.
  2. Passage A criticizes the author for not finishing the story, while Passage B agrees with that criticism.
  3. Passage A introduces the novel's historical setting, while Passage B introduces the characters' feelings.
  4. Passage A explains the distance between the author and the readers, while Passage B explains the distance between the author and the characters.
default.q.n2-35-q69-69.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is correct. Passage A focuses on the author’s experimental change in writing style (「著者は、この小説でひとつの実験を行った。それは、文体を変えるということだ」「この変化に読者は驚くかもしれないが」). Passage B gives a general summary of the plot (a young man becomes involved in a financial crime and faces upheaval in his life) and highlights the author’s purpose and message (「人間の心は社会的圧力に支配されるものではないという力強いメッセージを発している」).
default.q.n2-35-q69-69.why.1: (b) Choice 2: Incorrect. Passage A does not criticize the story for remaining unfinished; it says that readers can appreciate the ending according to their own feelings (「続きが出なくてもかまわないとも思う」). Passage B also does not praise it outright; the author wants to wait until the final volume is published before evaluating it fully (「この小説をきちんと評価するのは、最後の物語が出版されてからのこととしたい」).
default.q.n2-35-q69-69.why.2: (c) Choice 3: Incorrect. Passage A concerns an old-fashioned, formal style of expression (「古くてかたい表現を多く用い」), not the historical setting of the novel. Passage B mentions the characters' psychological development, but that is only part of the plot summary, not its main focus.
default.q.n2-35-q69-69.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4: Incorrect. Neither passage A nor B mentions or analyzes the “distance between the author and the reader” or the “distance between the author and the characters” at all.
default.q.n2-35-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Both writers felt that, even after finishing the story, part of it had not truly come to an end.
default.q.n2-35-q70-70.explanation:
- Content summary:
  + Passage A: The work contains many details and phrases that foreshadow what comes next, making it difficult to end the story in just one book.
  + Passage B: It clearly points out that part of the story remains unresolved, so the writer believes that the author has written a sequel.

- Question translation: Why do both passages A and B say that this novel will have a sequel?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because the publisher gave an ambiguous explanation about the sequel.
  2. Because after finishing the novel, they felt that part of the story remained unresolved.
  3. Because at the end of the work, the author announced that the story would continue.
  4. Because this author had previously released a sequel without announcing it in advance.
default.q.n2-35-q70-70.why.0: (a) Choice 1: Incorrect. Passage B says that the publisher has not made an official announcement (「出版社は公式には発表していない」), not that the publisher gave an ambiguous explanation. Passage A does not mention the publisher at all.
default.q.n2-35-q70-70.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct. Both passages recognize that the story is not completely finished in this volume. Passage A says: 「この物語は、続きを予告しているかのような文章が多く、この一冊で終わるとは思えない」 (There are many sentences that seem to foreshadow a continuation, so I do not think the story will end in this one volume). Passage B says: 「気になるのは、一部の物語が明らかに終わっていないことだ」 (What concerns me is that some of the stories clearly have not ended).
default.q.n2-35-q70-70.why.2: (c) Choice 3: Incorrect. Nothing in the article says that the author directly announced at the end of the book that there would be a sequel. Passage B clearly states that the publisher had not officially announced one.
default.q.n2-35-q70-70.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect. The passage contains no information that this author previously released a sequel without giving prior notice.
default.q.n2-35-q71-71.explanation:
- Question: How many methods for creating a “book-report reflection” did the author find while searching online?
- Answer choices:
  1. 2 methods
  2. 3 methods
  3. 4 methods
  4. 5 methods
- Main point: Paragraphs 1 and 2 clearly list three methods for creating a book-report reflection: (1) copying a ready-made report exactly as it is (既製品をそのまま書き写す), (2) using a template with blanks to fill in one’s own thoughts (テンプレート), and (3) using a generator that automatically creates text after the user answers several questions (ジェネレーター). The “reflection statement” website (反省文) in paragraph 3 is for dealing with being caught, not for writing a book-report reflection.
default.q.n2-35-q71-71.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (2 つ): Incorrect because the author found 3 methods for writing an impression essay online, not 2.
default.q.n2-35-q71-71.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (3 つ): CORRECT. The passage presents three formats: (1) a completed work that can be copied exactly, 「そのまま書き写せば出来上がり」; (2) a fill-in-the-blank template completed using each person’s ideas, 「（ ）の空欄を各自の発想で埋めて完成させる「テンプレート」」; and (3) a generator that produces text after users answer questions such as the book title, 「書名などいくつかの質問に答えると文が出来上がる「ジェネレーター」」.
default.q.n2-35-q71-71.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (4 つ) is incorrect. The author mentions only three types of tools for writing an essay. The “reflection paper” (反省文) found on the website was used afterward as a cover-up when the teacher discovered the copying.
default.q.n2-35-q71-71.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (5 つ) is incorrect because the passage does not mention five types of methods at all.
default.q.n2-35-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (realizing that it is wrong and no longer wanting to do it).
default.q.n2-35-q72-72.explanation:
- Question translation: What does the phrase "気が引ける" mean?
- Answer choices:
  1. To feel uneasy and reluctant to do something because you know it is wrong or inappropriate
  2. To feel sad and discouraged because you cannot do something on your own
  3. To feel ashamed and humiliated
  4. To be unable to concentrate
- Main point: The idiom 「気が引ける」 expresses guilt, hesitation, or reluctance when you realize that what you are doing is wrong or inappropriate. In the passage, the author says that students feel guilty about copying an assignment word for word and submitting it to the school (学校に提出するのに丸写しでは気が引ける), so they turn to fill-in-the-blank templates or software that generates assignments.
default.q.n2-35-q72-72.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (悪いこととわかって、したくなくなる): CORRECT. 「気が引ける」 expresses feeling guilty or hesitant to do something because one knows it is wrong or inappropriate. Context: 「学校に提出するのに丸写しでは気が引けるという生徒向けには...」 (for students who feel guilty or hesitant about submitting a direct copy to their school).
default.q.n2-35-q72-72.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (自分でできなくて、気が沈む): Incorrect. 「気が引ける」 does not mean feeling sad or hopeless because one cannot do something oneself; that meaning is expressed by 気が滅入る or 落ち込む.
default.q.n2-35-q72-72.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (格好悪いと思う): Incorrect. This phrase does not mean feeling ashamed or embarrassed (格好悪い / 恥ずかしい).
default.q.n2-35-q72-72.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4 (集中できなくなる): Incorrect. This expression does not specifically describe losing concentration (気が散る).
default.q.n2-35-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (対策をしても、その効果がすぐなくなる).
default.q.n2-35-q73-73.explanation:
- Question translation: What does the phrase “A new endless cat-and-mouse game begins” (新たなイタチごっこが始まる) mean?
- Answer choices:
  1. Even if a countermeasure is introduced, its effectiveness will quickly disappear.
  2. No new countermeasures will emerge anymore.
  3. Teachers who also copy and paste content will appear.
  4. School rules banning copying will be enacted.
- Main idea: イタチごっこ is an idiom referring to an endless cycle of countermeasures: one side makes a move, and the other immediately finds a way to counter it. In the article, when teachers use plagiarism-detection software, students will find websites that circumvent the software, causing the teachers’ countermeasure to quickly lose its effectiveness.
default.q.n2-35-q73-73.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (対策をしても、その効果がすぐなくなる): CORRECT. The passage states: 「生徒たちの側で「コピペ発見ソフトを打ち破る」サイトが生まれ、新たなイタチごっこが始まるに違いない」. This shows that when teachers use copy-and-paste detection software as a countermeasure, students will create websites that defeat it, quickly nullifying the countermeasure and creating an endless cycle.
default.q.n2-35-q73-73.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (新しい対策が出てこなくなる): Incorrect. "イタチごっこ" refers to two sides repeatedly introducing countermeasures against each other, not to there being no new measures left.
default.q.n2-35-q73-73.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 (コピペをする教師が出てくる): Incorrect. The passage says that teachers use software to detect students' copying; it does not mention teachers copy-pasting.
default.q.n2-35-q73-73.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (コピペを禁止する校則ができる): Incorrect. The passage does not mention introducing any school rule or regulation.
default.q.n2-35-q74-74.explanation:
- Main-point summary: The notice about the use of parking space 4 (第4駐輪場) lists two fee categories: 一般 (general: 1,500円 for 1 month, 4,200円 for 3 months, 7,200円 for 6 months) and 学生 (student: 1,100円 for 1 month, 3,100円 for 3 months, 5,200円 for 6 months). It also includes the note 「※学生は24歳まで」 (the student rate applies only to people aged 24 or younger). Although A is a student, he is 26, so the general rate applies. To use the parking space for one year (12 months) at the lowest cost, A should buy two 6-month passes: 7,200円 × 2 = 14,400円.
- Question translation: If A, a 26-year-old student, uses parking space 4 for one year, what is the lowest possible fee?
- Answer choices:
1. 10,400 yen
2. 12,400 yen
3. 14,400 yen
4. 16,800 yen
default.q.n2-35-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 10,400 yen is the amount obtained by applying the student rate twice for a six-month plan (5,200 yen × 2 = 10,400 yen). default.q.n2-35-q26-26.why.0: (a) 「おかしくなって」 (from おかしい) means “to become strange, funny, or abnormal”; it does not mean to like something.
default.q.n2-35-q26-26.why.1: (b) 「やさしくなって」 (from やさしい) means “become gentle/kind” or “become easier,” so it does not fit here.
default.q.n2-35-q26-26.why.2: (c) 「すきになって」 (from 好きになる) means “come to like, become fond of,” which exactly corresponds to the idiom 「気に入る」 (like, be pleased with).
default.q.n2-35-q26-26.why.3: (d) 「いやになって」 (from 嫌になる) means “to become fed up with, to come to dislike,” which is the opposite of 「気に入る」.

default.q.n2-35-q27-27.why.0: (a) 「不満」(ふまん): means “dissatisfaction, discontent, complaint,” and is synonymous with 「苦情」when expressing frustration or a grievance.
default.q.n2-35-q27-27.why.1: (b) 「不運」（ふうん）means “bad luck, misfortune” and is unrelated to complaining or filing a complaint.

default.q.n2-35-q27-27.why.3: (d) 「不正」（ふせい） means “wrongdoing, misconduct, fraud,” and is not synonymous with 「苦情」.
default.q.n2-35-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 1: ぼんやりしていて、駅を 1 つ乗り越してしまった。
default.q.n2-35-q28-28.explanation:
「乗り越す」（のりこす）means to go past the station or stop where one intended to get off, usually because of inattention or falling asleep.
Distinctions between easily confused words:

- 乗り換える / 乗り継ぐ: to transfer to another train, bus, or route.

default.q.n2-35-q29-29.explanation:
「節約」（せつやく）is a noun and verb meaning to save money or resources and reduce waste involving money, electricity, water, living expenses, and so on (used as Nを節約する).

- 省略 / 略す: omit or shorten words or procedures.

default.q.n2-35-q29-29.why.2: Incorrect word choice. To express putting or accumulating savings in a bank every month, use 「貯金（している）」 or 「預金」, not 「節約」.
default.q.n2-35-q29-29.why.3: 「電気代を節約する」is a precise and natural collocation meaning “save on electricity bills” by turning off the air conditioner in an unused room.
default.q.n2-35-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 家族と海の近くを ドライブ するのが、休日の楽しみだ。
default.q.n2-35-q30-30.explanation:
In Japanese, 「ドライブ」(drive) specifically means going for a drive by car for leisure, sightseeing, or relaxation.
Distinctions:
- ドライブする: go for a leisurely drive or sightseeing trip, mainly by car.
- 運転する: operate or drive a vehicle in general, such as a car or motorcycle.
- 操縦する: pilot or control an aircraft or large vessel.
- （車で）送る: take or drive someone somewhere by car.
- ツーリングする: go touring or on a long recreational trip by motorcycle.
Example: 週末は天気が良かったので、山へドライブに行きました。(The weather was nice over the weekend, so I went for a drive to the mountains.)
default.q.n2-35-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect word choice. To express driving one’s child to the station, use 「（車で）送ってやった」, not 「ドライブしてやった」.
default.q.n2-35-q30-30.why.1: 「海の近くをドライブする」 is completely natural and correct, meaning to drive around near the coast for sightseeing and recreation with one’s family on a day off.
default.q.n2-35-q30-30.why.2: The word choice is incorrect. With a motorcycle (オートバイ), the action of operating or riding it is expressed with 「運転する」(or 「ツーリングする」for going on a motorcycle tour), not 「ドライブする」.
default.q.n2-35-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect word choice. Flying an airplane requires the specialized verb 「操縦（そうじゅう）する」, not 「ドライブする」.

default.q.n2-35-q32-32.explanation:
「どっと」is an adverb describing:

Common expressions:
- 疲れがどっと出る: pent-up fatigue suddenly catches up with someone.

Distinguishing similar onomatopoeic adverbs:
- じっと: to sit still or remain motionless (じっとする).
- ずっと: continuously, all the way (ずっと待つ).

default.q.n2-35-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect usage. To express continuously waiting without a break since yesterday, use the adverb「ずっと」, not「どっと」.
default.q.n2-35-q32-32.why.2: The word is incorrect. To describe gently wiping away tears, use「そっと」(or「さっと」for quickly); do not use「どっと」.
default.q.n2-35-q32-32.why.3: 「疲れがどっと出る」 is a classic idiom/collocation describing the feeling of accumulated fatigue suddenly hitting all at once after the exam is over.

default.q.n2-35-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「かたむいて」 is the te-form of 「傾く」 (かたむ・く: to tilt or lean), the correct kun-reading of 「傾」.
default.q.n2-35-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1. しゅくはく.
default.q.n2-35-q2-2.explanation:
- Meaning: The hotel where I stayed the other day had good facilities and was very convenient and comfortable.

default.q.n2-35-q3-3.explanation:
- Meaning: Reading this book will give you a comprehensive overview of politics.

default.q.n2-35-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「ぜんはい」 incorrectly reads the on-reading of 「般」 (般 is not read はい).

default.q.n2-35-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「ぜいはん」 incorrectly reads 全 as ぜい instead of ぜん and does not apply the correct semi-voicing to 般.
default.q.n2-35-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「ぜんぱい」 misreads 「般」 as ぱい; it is easily confused with 「全敗」, meaning “a complete defeat.”

default.q.n2-35-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 厚かましい.

default.q.n2-36-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2. かねない (may or could lead to a negative result).
default.q.n2-36-q33-33.explanation:
- Meaning: If you continue overworking like that, you may damage your health.
- Pattern: V (ます-stem) + かねない (there is a risk that..., it may result in something bad).
- Vocabulary: 無理 (overexertion), 体 (body, health).

default.q.n2-36-q33-33.why.0: (a) 「〜えない / 〜得ない」 means “cannot” or “be impossible”; it is not used to warn that a bad consequence may occur.
default.q.n2-36-q33-33.why.1: (b) 「〜かねない」: means “may” or “could result in something bad” (V-masu + かねない), making it exactly appropriate for warning that overworking could harm one’s health.
default.q.n2-36-q33-33.why.2: (c) 「〜気味（ぎみ）だ」: to seem somewhat..., to have slight symptoms of... (usually used for a current feeling or condition, such as 風邪気味 or 疲れ気味). It is not used to warn of a future risk after the condition 「〜と」.
default.q.n2-36-q33-33.why.3: (d) 「〜すぎる」: doing something excessively, as in 食べすぎる or 働きすぎる; the combination「体をこわしすぎる」is unnatural and does not fit the warning.
default.q.n2-36-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3. とたん (just as ...; immediately afterward, an unexpected event occurs).
default.q.n2-36-q34-34.explanation:
- Translation: The person had just stood up from the seat when he suddenly collapsed.
- Structure: V-ta + とたん（に） (Just after..., something unexpected happens immediately in the second clause).
- On-readings: 席 (seat), 倒れた (fell, collapsed).
- Example: 窓を開けたとたん、強い風が入ってきた。(The moment I opened the window, a strong wind blew in.)
default.q.n2-36-q34-34.why.0: (a) 「〜や否や（いなや）」means “as soon as...,” but this grammar must follow the dictionary form of a verb (Vる + や否や), not Vた.
default.q.n2-36-q34-34.why.1: (b) 「そ馬鹿ら」: A meaningless word/display error; it is not a Japanese grammar structure.
default.q.n2-36-q34-34.why.2: (c) 「〜とたん（に）」: Means “as soon as” or “just after” (Vた + とたんに), describing an unexpected or unintended event that occurs immediately afterward, such as falling just after standing up.
default.q.n2-36-q34-34.why.3: (d) 「すぐに」is an adverb meaning “immediately”; it cannot directly link to a past-tense verb Vた without a conjunction.
default.q.n2-36-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 4. っぽい (full of..., having the quality of..., dusty).
default.q.n2-36-q35-35.explanation:
