- Pattern: N + っぽい (having the qualities of..., full of..., giving the impression of...).
- Kanji vocabulary: 掃除 (cleaning), 部屋 (room).
- Example: 油っぽい料理ばかり食べていると太りますよ。(If you keep eating greasy food, you will gain weight.)
default.q.n2-36-q35-35.why.0: (a) 「〜がち」: tend to, be prone to. It indicates a repeated habit or state, as in 留守がち and 遅刻しがち; it does not combine with the noun 「ほこり」 to describe a room full of dust.
default.q.n2-36-q35-35.why.1: (b) 「〜みたいな」: “like...” or “similar to...”; 「ほこりみたいな部屋」 would mean “a room like a speck of dust,” which does not express the intended meaning.
default.q.n2-36-q35-35.why.2: (c) 「〜そう」does not directly follow the noun 「ほこり」in this structure.
default.q.n2-36-q35-35.why.3: (d) 「〜っぽい」: full of, seems, has many of the qualities of... (N + っぽい); 「ほこりっぽい」 is a natural compound meaning “dusty, full of dust.”
default.q.n2-36-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ところをみると (judging from the current state or situation...).
default.q.n2-36-q36-36.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: Ishida looks so gloomy and lacking in energy—could it be that he failed the exam?
- Pattern: Plain form + ところをみると: judging from the current state; based on the situation, one can infer that...
- Vocabulary: 試験 (exam), 元気 (healthy, energetic, cheerful).
- Example: 明かりがついているところをみると、彼はまだ起きているようだ。(Judging from the fact that the light is still on, he seems to be awake.)
default.q.n2-36-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「〜だけに」: precisely because...; especially because..., emphasizing a particular cause that leads inevitably to a result. It is not used as a basis for inference.
default.q.n2-36-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「〜ことだから」: It is used in the form 「N + のことだから」 (“since it is someone like N, surely...”), and does not directly follow the predicate clause 「元気がない」.
default.q.n2-36-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「〜うえに」 means “not only... but also...” and adds information in the same direction; it is not used to state the basis for a judgment.
default.q.n2-36-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「〜ところをみると」means “judging from...” or “based on the fact that...”. It is exactly appropriate for inferring from Ishida’s gloomy appearance that he failed the exam.
default.q.n2-36-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 2. かけては (when it comes specifically to; in the area of..., it is outstanding).
default.q.n2-36-q37-37.explanation:
- Meaning: “My younger brother is nothing special when it comes to studying, but when it comes to swimming, he is second to none.”
- Structure: N + にかけては (when it comes specifically to / in the area of…, be the best or second to none).
- Kanji vocabulary: 弟 (younger brother), 勉強 (studying), 水泳 (swimming), 負けない (not be defeated, not lose).
- Example: 足の速さにかけては、クラスで彼の右に出る者はいない。(When it comes to running speed, no one in the class is faster than him.)
default.q.n2-36-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「〜にしては」: “although…,” “considering…” (compared with the usual standard, e.g., an adult with poor handwriting); it does not pair with a following clause affirming outstanding ability, such as “not inferior to anyone.”
default.q.n2-36-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「〜にかけては」means "when it comes to... / as far as ... is concerned," and is usually followed by an expression such as 誰にも負けない or 一番だ to assert exceptional strength in that area.
default.q.n2-36-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「〜に対しては」means “toward” or “in contrast to”; it indicates an attitude or target of an action, not an area of expertise.
default.q.n2-36-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「〜によっては」 means “depending on”; it indicates variation from case to case and does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-36-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 4. だけあって (as expected of..., no wonder..., worthy of...).
default.q.n2-36-q38-38.explanation:
- Meaning: No wonder people are lining up; this restaurant's food really is delicious.
- Pattern: Plain form / N + だけあって (as one would expect from, no wonder…, worthy of its reputation or expectations).
- Vocabulary: 並ぶ (ならぶ: line up), 料理 (りょうり: dish, cuisine), 本当 (ほんとう: truly, really).
- Example: 高かっただけあって、このコートはとても軽くて暖かい。(As one would expect from its high price, this coat is very light and warm.)
default.q.n2-36-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「〜かぎり（に）」 means “as long as” or “within the scope of”; it does not express praise for quality matching expectations.
default.q.n2-36-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「〜わけで」 cannot be used in this connective form between sentences to express a corresponding evaluation of quality.
default.q.n2-36-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「〜としても」 means “even if...” or “even though...”; it expresses a hypothetical concession and does not fit the meaning of praising the dish.
default.q.n2-36-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「〜だけあって」: “as expected of / no wonder...”; it describes a result or outstanding quality that is appropriate for the situation mentioned in the preceding clause.
default.q.n2-36-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ほしくなるものだ (you naturally want it even more; a natural psychological tendency).
default.q.n2-36-q39-39.explanation:
- Meaning: When people cannot afford to buy something, they naturally want it even more.
- Structure: V / adjective + ものだ (expresses a natural law or an inevitable, self-evident aspect of human psychology).
- Kanji: 金 (money).
- Example: 人間は禁止されると、かえってやりたくなるものだ。(When people are forbidden to do something, they naturally want to do it even more.)
default.q.n2-36-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「〜ほしくなるものだ」: 「〜ものだ」 expresses a natural tendency or common psychological pattern (“when people cannot buy something, they tend to want it even more”).
default.q.n2-36-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「〜ほしくなることだ」: 「〜ことだ」 is used to give advice or a gentle instruction (“you should...” ), not to describe a natural psychological reaction.
default.q.n2-36-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「〜ほしくなくなるものだ」means “end up wanting it even less,” which is contrary to the psychological tendency and the meaning of the adverb 「よけい」(even more).
default.q.n2-36-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「〜ほしくなくなることだ」 is incorrect both in vocabulary meaning (not wanting something) and in the grammar of 「ことだ」.
default.q.n2-36-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 3. にしたがって (the more..., the more..., or as a change progresses, another change follows).
default.q.n2-36-q40-40.explanation:
- Sentence translation: The farther upstream one goes along the river, the faster and stronger the current becomes.
- Pattern: V (dictionary form) / N + にしたがって (as A changes, B changes accordingly; the more..., the more...).
- Sino-Japanese readings: 川 (river), 上流 (upstream), 速い (fast).
- Example: 台風が近づくにしたがって、風が強くなってきた。(As the typhoon drew closer, the wind grew stronger.)
default.q.n2-36-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「〜にそって / 〜に沿って」: Means “along” or “following,” as with a riverbank, road, or plan; it is not used to connect simultaneous changes in a “the more..., the more...” relationship.
default.q.n2-36-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「〜に対して」: toward, with regard to, or in contrast to; indicates the target of an action or a contrast.
default.q.n2-36-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「〜にしたがって / 〜に従って」: “along with / the more..., the more...”; with Vる + にしたがって, a change in A leads to a corresponding change in B.
default.q.n2-36-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「〜に際して」: on the occasion of / when beginning an important event or undertaking; it does not fit a context involving continuous change.
default.q.n2-36-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. わりに (although; rather, considering the degree or expectation).
default.q.n2-36-q41-41.explanation:
- Translation: My current part-time job is easy, but the hourly wage is fairly high.
- Structure: Adj-na + な / Adj-i / V / N + の + わりに（は） (compared with... / although... — expresses an unexpected mismatch).
- Vocabulary: 楽 (easy, comfortable), 時給 (hourly wage).
- Example: この料理は簡単なわりに、とてもおいしい。(Although this dish is easy to make, it is very delicious.)
default.q.n2-36-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「〜おかげで」 means 'thanks to...' and expresses a cause leading to a positive result, but having plenty of free time is not the cause of earning a high salary; the two clauses are actually contrasting and unexpected.
default.q.n2-36-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「〜あまり」: Because something is excessive, it leads to a negative or abnormal result (e.g., 驚きのあまり); it does not fit this sentence.
default.q.n2-36-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「〜ようで」: seems to / appears to; it does not create a contrastive connection between how relaxed someone is and their salary.
default.q.n2-36-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「〜わりに（は）」: compared with..., although... (na-adjective + な + わりに). It describes a situation that does not match the usual expectation, such as having a high salary despite an easy job.
default.q.n2-36-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ばかりに (just because..., resulting in trouble or an undesirable outcome).
default.q.n2-36-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: Just because I happened to say that my university major was English, I was assigned the difficult task of translation.
- Structure: Plain form (especially V-ta) + ばかりに (Just because...; an action or cause leads to an undesirable, troublesome result).
- Kanji readings: 専門 (major, specialization), 翻訳 (translation of written text).
- Example: 本当のことを言ったばかりに、彼を怒らせてしまった。(Just because I told the truth, I ended up making him angry.)
default.q.n2-36-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「〜だけに」 means "precisely because... so all the more..." and expresses an inevitable, proportionate result; it does not emphasize regret or an unintended troublesome cause.
default.q.n2-36-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「〜わりに」 means “although / considering...”; it does not express a direct cause leading to being assigned a difficult task.
default.q.n2-36-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「〜ばかりに」means “just because... and consequently suffer a bad result or trouble” (V-ta + ばかりに). It accurately expresses the speaker’s regret at mentioning that he studied English and consequently being assigned difficult translation work.
default.q.n2-36-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「〜のもとで」 means “under the direction or guidance of...”; it does not form a conjunction expressing a cause.
default.q.n2-36-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. をめぐって (when centered around an issue, various debates and opinions arise).
default.q.n2-36-q43-43.explanation:
- Meaning: Various opinions are being expressed by residents regarding the construction of a public community center.
- Structure: N + をめぐって / をめぐる (around/concerning an issue; often used with discussion, debate, or differing opinions).
- Sino-Vietnamese readings: 公民館 (community center), 建設 (construction), 市民 (residents/citizens), 意見 (opinion).
- Example: 遺産の配分をめぐって、兄弟の間で激しい争いが起きた。(A fierce dispute broke out among the siblings over the division of the inheritance.)
default.q.n2-36-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「〜にとって」: “For / from the standpoint of” an entity; it does not directly follow a noun referring to an issue, such as “building a community cultural center,” to introduce a topic for discussion.
default.q.n2-36-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「〜をめぐって」: "concerning/around" a topic or controversial issue that gives rise to various opinions and discussions; this fits perfectly with the following clause, "many opinions emerged from local residents."
default.q.n2-36-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「〜にこたえて / 〜に応えて」means to respond to or meet expectations or wishes; it does not fit a context involving an argument or multiple opinions.
default.q.n2-36-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「〜につれて」 means “as... progresses”; the following clause must describe a gradual change, so it cannot be combined with a standalone noun in this way.
default.q.n2-36-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ぬきに (without, omitting, leaving out...).
default.q.n2-36-q44-44.explanation:
- Meaning: Since we do not have much time, let us skip the usual greetings and get straight to the main subject.
- Pattern: N + 抜きに（して） / 抜きで (to leave out N / proceed without N).
- Kanji compounds: 時間 (time), 挨拶 (greeting), 本題 (main subject).
- Example: お世辞ぬきで、あなたの企画案は本当に素晴らしいと思います。 (Without flattery, I truly think your proposal is excellent.)
default.q.n2-36-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「〜はもちろん」means “...of course, not to mention...” and adds an emphatic assertion, which is contrary to the intended meaning of omitting greetings.
default.q.n2-36-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「〜に加えて」 means “in addition to” or “besides”; it does not fit a context where procedures need to be reduced because of a lack of time.
default.q.n2-36-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「〜ことなく」 means “without doing...”. This pattern must follow a verb in dictionary form (Vる + ことなく, e.g., あいさつすることなく), and cannot directly follow the noun 「あいさつ」.
default.q.n2-36-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「〜ぬきに / 〜抜きに」means “without, leaving out, or setting aside...” (N + ぬきに), describing omitting social greetings and going straight to the main topic.

default.q.n2-36-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 住んでいなくても (even if one does not currently live there).
default.q.n2-36-q50-50.explanation: The passage gives examples of tangible property whose ownership is easy to determine: the money in one's wallet belongs to oneself, and a book one bought belongs to oneself. It then gives land as an example: even if one does not currently live on the property (今、住んでいなくても), it still belongs to oneself as long as one is legally registered as its owner. The negative concessive pattern 「〜なくても」("even if... not") highlights the legal value of property ownership regardless of whether one currently resides there.
default.q.n2-36-q50-50.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「住んでいれば」(if one is living there) expresses a hypothetical condition. It does not fit the passage’s assertion that ownership is independent of whether someone currently lives there.
default.q.n2-36-q50-50.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「住んでいなければ」means “if [someone] does not live there,” a straightforward negative condition; it does not create a natural concessive connection to the assertion of ownership in the following clause.
default.q.n2-36-q50-50.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「住んでいても」 means “even if one is living there,” which contradicts the intended emphasis on the exceptional case: “even if one does not live there, the land is still one’s own.”
default.q.n2-36-q50-50.why.3: (d) Correct. 「住んでいなくても」 (V-なくても: even if one does not...) expresses the appropriate concessive relationship: "Even if I do not currently live there, the land is still mine if I am registered as its owner."
default.q.n2-36-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 盗んだら (if you steal someone else's belongings, you will become a thief).
default.q.n2-36-q51-51.explanation: The author explains the clear and transparent nature of ownership of tangible property: ownership boundaries are clearly defined, and “if you steal someone else’s belongings, you become a thief / commit a crime.” The conditional structure 「〜たら」 is the most accurate and natural choice for expressing an action that leads to an inevitable consequence or a rule under the law.
default.q.n2-36-q51-51.why.0: (a) Correct. 「盗んだら」 (V-たら: a hypothetical condition, “if A, then B”) expresses the obvious cause-and-effect relationship: if you steal someone else’s belongings, you become a thief.
default.q.n2-36-q51-51.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「盗んでも」means "even if one steals something," expressing a concessive contrast, which does not fit the logic of the following clause, "become a thief."
default.q.n2-36-q51-51.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「盗まなかったら」 means “if someone does not steal it,” which completely contradicts the meaning and logic of the situation.
default.q.n2-36-q51-51.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「盗んだとしても」 means “even if someone were to steal something,” and expresses a concessive hypothetical contrast. It is unsuitable for stating an inevitable principle or consequence.
default.q.n2-36-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 2. できなくても (even if one cannot touch the object).
default.q.n2-36-q52-52.explanation: After giving examples of tangible assets that can be held or seen, such as money, books, and land, the author uses the contrastive conjunction 「しかし」to shift to intangible assets, such as literary works, music, designs, and inventions. These things have no physical form that can be touched, but they are still assets that need to be protected. Therefore, the concessive negative structure 「〜なくても」("even if one cannot touch the physical object") is accurate both grammatically and in the passage's contrasting line of thought.
default.q.n2-36-q52-52.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「できても」 means “even if it can be done,” which is completely contrary to the intangible nature of intellectual property, which cannot be touched or held.
default.q.n2-36-q52-52.why.1: (b) Correct. 「できなくても」 (V-なくても: “even if one cannot…”) expresses a concessive contrast: “However, even if people cannot touch the artifacts, there are still things that must be protected as property belonging to human beings.”
default.q.n2-36-q52-52.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「できる場合」 means “when it is possible” and cannot create a contrast after 「しかし」 when the following clause concerns protecting invisible things.
default.q.n2-36-q52-52.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「できない場合」 means “in cases where it is not possible”; it merely describes an ordinary condition and does not carry a concessive meaning (“even if one cannot... one must still protect...”) connecting it to the predicate 「守らなければならないものがある」.
default.q.n2-36-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 3. できないにしても (even if it is not possible to sell it immediately for cash).
default.q.n2-36-q53-53.explanation: The premise of the sentence clearly states 「実際に値段はついていないので」 (because it does not actually have a set price), so it cannot be immediately sold and converted into cash. The author uses the N2 grammar pattern 「〜にしても / 〜ないにしても」 to express concession (“even if / even though it cannot...”), emphasizing that although intellectual property cannot be sold for immediate cash like tangible assets, the author’s/creator’s ownership is still firmly asserted and fully protected (「持ち主はわたしです」 と主張することができる).
default.q.n2-36-q53-53.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「できるにしても」means “even if it is possible,” which directly contradicts the preceding reason that, in reality, no prices are attached.
default.q.n2-36-q53-53.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「できるとなったら」 means “if we assume that it is possible,” which contradicts the sentence’s negative premise.
default.q.n2-36-q53-53.why.2: (c) Correct. 「できないにしても」 (V-ないにしても: "even if one cannot..." / "even supposing that one cannot...") expresses strong concession. Although the creation cannot be immediately exchanged for cash because no price has been set, the creator can still assert ownership of it as one would of money or land.
default.q.n2-36-q53-53.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「できないとしたら」 means “if we assume that it is impossible.” It expresses an ordinary hypothetical condition, not a concessive contrast linking to the affirmative conclusion about ownership in the following clause.
default.q.n2-36-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 2. する場合は (in the case of carrying it out or using it, permission is required).
default.q.n2-36-q54-54.explanation: This sentence states a general legal rule concerning the use of intellectual property: when someone wants to use another person's intellectual property for economic activities, they must obtain the owner's permission in advance. The pattern 「〜場合は」 describes a situation or case in an objective, rule-based way in argumentative writing and appropriately accompanies the obligation pattern 「〜なければならない」.
default.q.n2-36-q54-54.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「したら」 (V-たら) indicates that an action has already been completed or that a specific condition has occurred, whereas legal regulations require permission to be obtained beforehand or when the situation arises.
default.q.n2-36-q54-54.why.1: (b) Correct. 「する場合は」 (V-る場合は: “in the case of doing / when carrying out...”) is a standard expression used in explanatory and legal writing: “When using another person's intellectual property for economic activities, permission must be obtained from the rights holder.”
default.q.n2-36-q54-54.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「するとしても」 means “even if one were to...” and expresses hypothetical concession, which does not fit a rule or mandatory obligation expressed by 「〜なければならない」.
default.q.n2-36-q54-54.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「しないとしても」means “even if one does not do...,” which is completely inconsistent with the sentence’s logic and meaning.
default.q.n2-36-q55-55.verdict: The provided answer is 4 (おやつ); however, in context and according to Japanese grammar, 「こいつ」 goes with 「いなければ」, an existence verb used for people or animals, and 「弟を横目で見ながら」 actually refers to the younger brother (choice 1).

default.q.n2-36-q55-55.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (おやつ): According to the provided answer, the passage states: 「おやつをもらうときも、弟を横目で見ながら、『こいつさえいなければ、全部私のものになるのに』とが流かりした」, in the context of sharing snacks. (Grammatically, 「こいつ」 refers to the younger brother as the reason the snacks must be divided.)
default.q.n2-36-q56-56.verdict: According to the passage, the accurate answer is 1; the given answer 2 is incorrect because the reading does not mention that traveling to Hokkaido is difficult.

Because its climate differs from that of Honshu, visitors can see cherry blossoms blooming late in May and autumn leaves appearing early in October. What does 「独特の楽しみ方」mean?

default.q.n2-36-q56-56.why.2: (c) Choice 3 does not match the content of the passage. Viewing cherry blossoms in May, which is later than in Honshu, or viewing autumn leaves in early October are examples of general climatic differences, not examples or definitions of a “unique way of enjoying” (独特の楽しみ方), which is mentioned in the following sentence in connection with viewing drift ice and attending snow festivals in winter.
default.q.n2-36-q56-56.why.3: (d) Choice 4 does not match the passage. The article does not say that people have different experiences depending on the individual (人によっていろいろな経験ができる); it focuses on Hokkaido's distinctive winter experiences.
default.q.n2-36-q57-57.verdict: The answer given in the question is 1 (however, based on the context, with 「これ」 preceding 「を金融政策といいます」, the accurate answer should be 4).
default.q.n2-36-q57-57.explanation:
**1. Summary of the passage:**
The passage discusses the independent legal status and roles and functions of the Bank of Japan (日本銀行):
- Issuing banknotes (as shown by the words 「日本銀行券」 on notes such as the 1,000-yen and 10,000-yen notes).
- Serving as the "Bank of the government" (「政府の銀行」): processing tax revenue and providing funds to the government.
- Serving as the "Bank of banks" (「銀行の銀行」): accepting deposits from and lending money to ordinary banks.
- Implementing "monetary policy" (金融政策): regulating the flow of money and stabilizing prices by raising or lowering the official discount rate (公定歩合) and open-market interest rates.

**2. Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** What does 「これ」 refer to?
- **Choice 1:** The Bank of Japan's issuance of banknotes such as the 1,000-yen and 10,000-yen notes.
- **Choice 2:** Processing tax revenue and providing funds to the government.
- **Choice 3:** Accepting deposits from and lending money to ordinary banks.
- **Choice 4:** Regulating the flow of money by raising or lowering open-market interest rates and the official discount rate.

**3. Answer evaluation:**
The 「これ」 tested at the end of the passage appears immediately before 「を金融政策といいます」 (is called monetary policy), so it directly replaces the preceding sentence about regulating interest rates (corresponding to Choice 4). The provided answer, Choice 1, may have been confused with the 「これ」 that appears at the beginning of the passage.
default.q.n2-36-q57-57.why.0: (a) This matches the beginning of the passage: 「ふだん私たちが使っている千円札や 1 万円札などの紙幣を見てみると、『日本銀行券』と書いてあります。これは、日本銀行が紙幣を発行しているということを意味しています。」 However, 「これ」 in this sentence refers to the fact that 「日本銀行券」 is printed on the banknotes, not to the entire act of issuing currency; furthermore, the question appears at the end of the passage.
default.q.n2-36-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「税金を扱ったり、資金を政府に支出したりする」 corresponds to the role of 「政府の銀行」, not to the content referred to by the pronoun 「これ」.
default.q.n2-36-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「一般の銀行から預金を受け入 れたり、貸し出しを行ったりする」corresponds to the role of「銀行の銀行」(the bank of banks), not to what the pronoun「これ」refers to.
default.q.n2-36-q57-57.why.3: (d) This is the accurate interpretation of the underlined 「これ」 at the end of the paragraph: 「日本銀行は公定歩合を上げ下げしたり、公開市場の金利を上げ下げする方などで、物価の安定をはかり、世の中のお金の流れを調整しています。これを金融政策といいます。」 The pronoun 「これ」 refers to the entire action of adjusting the flow of money through interest rates described in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n2-36-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The era when public telephones had to stand out prominently has come to an end.

What is the appropriate phrase to fill in ( ★ )?

default.q.n2-36-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage says: '当然、街角からつぎつぎと消えていく' (Naturally, they disappear one after another from the street corners), meaning that their number is gradually decreasing, not increasing (だんだん増えてきた).

1. Earth’s atmosphere contains carbon dioxide and water, and together with the oceans, they help maintain the temperature.

default.q.n2-36-q64-64.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage clearly states that the salesperson moved close to the customer at that moment («その瞬間、ぐっと近寄った販売員が間髪を入れずに...»), and the author concludes that the customer left because the salesperson approached too closely («距離の接近のいきすぎ»).
default.q.n2-36-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that customers would rather choose products themselves than receive advice from staff. It emphasizes that the fundamental cause was mishandling the contact distance.
default.q.n2-36-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: The sales clerk suddenly approached the man too closely.
default.q.n2-36-q65-65.explanation:
• Summary: The author concludes that the main reason sales staff miss sales opportunities («客追う動作») is failure to adjust interpersonal distance («対人距離のパフォーマンスの失敗»); specifically, the number-one reason is approaching customers too closely («距離の接近のいきすぎ»).
• Question translation: What was the main reason the sales clerk failed to sell a tie to the man?
• Answer choices:
1. Starting a conversation with the man too early.
2. Not having the pattern the man wanted to buy.
3. Ignoring the man.
4. Suddenly approaching the man too closely.
default.q.n2-36-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect because, although the staff member spoke immediately without delay («間髪を入れずに»), the passage identifies the primary reason as getting too close to the target («失敗の第一の理由は、『距離の接近のいきすぎ』にあります»).
default.q.n2-36-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not mention that the man wants to buy something without a pattern.
default.q.n2-36-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it was the customer who ignored the employee; the employee did not look down on or ignore the customer.
default.q.n2-36-q65-65.why.3: (d) Correct because the final sentence clearly states that the main reason for the failure was excessive proximity («その答えこそが、『販売員の対人距離のパフォーマンスの失敗』なのです。つまり、失敗の第一の理由は、『距離の接近のいきすぎ』にあります»).
default.q.n2-36-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 教育にも色々ある (There are many different kinds of education as well).
default.q.n2-36-q66-66.explanation:
**Relevant main point:**
The opening paragraph presents a logical progression: People are inherently diverse and come in many types → teachers are therefore also diverse → education consequently takes many different forms and approaches → for this reason, only the learner can choose what suits them best.

**Translation of the question and choices:**
- Question: Which of the following is appropriate for the position ( ★ )?
- Choices:
  1. Parents should conduct research.
  2. Education also comes in many diverse forms.
  3. The disadvantages of schools are easy to identify.
  4. Relationships among children are complicated and difficult.
default.q.n2-36-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention the role of parents or say that “parents should look into it” (両親が調べるべきだ).
default.q.n2-36-q66-66.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「人にはいろいろあるということである。だから、教師にもいろいろある。だから（教育にも色々ある）。どれが自分に彙（適）しているか、それは自分で選ぶしかない。」 (People are all different → teachers are all different → education is also varied → each person must choose what suits them.)
default.q.n2-36-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention “the shortcomings of schools” (学校の欠点).
default.q.n2-36-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not discuss “relationships among children” (子ども同士の関係).
default.q.n2-36-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 誰でも毎日一生懸命勉強するような、最も良い方法というものはない (There is no single best method that makes everyone study hard every day).
default.q.n2-36-q67-67.explanation:
**Relevant main idea:**
The author explains that people do not study all day, every day: sometimes they study and sometimes they do not; some people do not begin wanting to study until they are twenty; and sometimes they feel motivated while at other times they have no motivation at all. Therefore, there is no “one-size-fits-all remedy” (metaphorically, no universal method that can make everyone study diligently every day).

**Translation of the question and answer choices:**
- Question: What does the expression “There is no one-size-fits-all remedy for things like this” mean?
- Choices:
  1. Since teachers come in many types, it is difficult to choose the ideal teacher.
  2. In education, it is impossible to find a textbook that works for everyone.
  3. There is no single best method that can make everyone study hard every day.
  4. There is no medicine that can suddenly make a student who does not want to study start enjoying it.
default.q.n2-36-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this passage discusses learners’ timing and interest in studying, not the difficulty of choosing an ideal teacher.
default.q.n2-36-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage does not mention textbooks or coursebooks (テキスト).
default.q.n2-36-q67-67.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage states: 「人間は年がら年中、日がな一日、勉強しているわけではない。勉強することもあるし、しないこともある。... つまり時期にもよるのである。自分が気が向く時もあれば、まったく向かない時もある。そういうことに一般向けの薬なんかない。」("A general-purpose medicine" is a metaphor for a single optimal method that would make everyone study diligently at all times.)
default.q.n2-36-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「薬」('medicine') here is a metaphor for a measure or method, not actual medication that can instantly turn students who are lazy about studying into students who enjoy studying.
default.q.n2-36-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 学生には色々な人がいるし、勉強したい時期や時間もそれぞれ違うこと (Students are diverse, and the periods and times when they want to study also differ from person to person).
default.q.n2-36-q68-68.explanation:
**Relevant main point:**
The author explains that “the troublesome aspect of education” lies in the great variety among students: some want to study at present, while others want to play; those who are playing now may not play forever, and those who are studying now may not study forever. There is no single universal theory.

**Translation of the question and answer choices:**
- Question: What is “the troublesome aspect of education” (教育の面倒くさいところ)?
- Choices:
  1. Because education has many methods, it is impossible to choose just one suitable method.
  2. If all the teachers are permissive, it is impossible to know when the students will finally be willing to study.
  3. Students' moods easily change: sometimes they want to play, and sometimes they want to study.
  4. There are many different kinds of students, and the time and duration for which each person wants to study differ.
default.q.n2-36-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the explanation of this phrase focuses on students’ diversity and changing circumstances (学生にもいろいろいる), not on being unable to choose an educational method.
default.q.n2-36-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the idea of “if the teacher were permissive” (放任) is merely a hypothetical counterargument presented in the middle of the passage, not the explanation of “the troublesome aspect of education.”
default.q.n2-36-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author discusses stages of life—wanting to do something now does not mean one will do it for one's entire life, and Churchill only began studying at age 20—not students' brief, fluctuating moods.
default.q.n2-36-q68-68.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage says: 「教師にも色々な人がいるということは、学生にもいろいろいるということである。今学びたいと思っている人も、遊びたいと思っている人もある。... 今勉強している人が、一生勉強するとは限らない。教育の面倒くさいところは、そこにある。」 (The troublesome aspect of education is that students are diverse and each person wants to study at a different time).
default.q.n2-36-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2: A and B share the view that the questioner’s concern is perfectly normal.
default.q.n2-36-q69-69.explanation:
- **Main point**:
A high school student writes to share their worries because they are confused about what they want to do in the future and blame themselves for being immature or incapable.
+ Person A states that it is completely normal (普通) not to know what one wants to do at this age, and that one gradually realizes it after starting work.
+ Person B states that the writer is neither immature nor incapable, but perfectly ordinary (普通).
Thus, the common point in A’s and B’s responses is that both affirm that the writer’s worries are perfectly normal.

- **Translation of the question and choices**:
  - *Question*: What is the common point in A’s and B’s responses?
  - *1*: They both say that they do not understand the writer’s worries.
  - *2*: They both say that the writer’s worries are perfectly normal.
  - *3*: They both say that the writer should try doing something.
  - *4*: They both say that there is no need to do anything now and nothing to worry about.
default.q.n2-36-q69-69.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because both A and B clearly understand the questioner’s concerns and offer specific advice. Neither says that they do not understand the questioner’s worries.
default.q.n2-36-q69-69.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because both A and B directly state that the questioner’s situation is normal. A says: 「あなたの年齢で将来したいことがわからないのは、普通です。」 (It is normal not to know what you want to do in the future at your age.) B says: 「そんなあなたは、幼いのでもなく、だめなのでもなく、普通なのです。」 (Someone like you is neither immature nor inadequate; you are simply normal.)
default.q.n2-36-q69-69.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is incorrect because only B advises the person to try doing something (「スポーツとか、より自己表現的な何かをしてみたらどうでしょうか」), whereas A advises letting things develop naturally and says that the person will gradually realize it after starting work.
default.q.n2-36-q69-69.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because only A says there is no need to worry about anything (「何も心配いりません」), whereas B encourages actively making changes and trying new activities.
default.q.n2-36-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3: A thinks it is fine to leave things as they are, while B advises trying something.
default.q.n2-36-q70-70.explanation:
- **Main point**:
Regarding the questioner's concern:
+ Person A recommends leaving things as they are (そのままでいい): there is no need to worry because everyone is uncertain in this way, and the questioner will understand what they like after starting work (何も心配いりません).
+ Person B recommends taking action (何かしてみたほうがいい): because the questioner's current interests are somewhat passive, B suggests trying something involving self-expression, such as sports, in order to discover what they truly want to do.

- **Question and answer choices**:
  - *Question*: Which of the following correctly describes A's and B's responses to the questioner's concern?
  - *1*: A says that the questioner will come to like the job after joining a company, while B says that if the questioner plays sports, they will make an effort...
  - *2*: A recommends working, while B recommends having a hobby.
  - *3*: A says that it is fine to leave things as they are, while B says that the questioner should try doing something.
  - *4*: A says that being uncertain is bad, while B says that being passive is bad.
default.q.n2-36-q70-70.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because A does not assert that people will definitely enjoy their jobs simply by joining a company; A says that, through working, they will gradually discover what they like or are suited to. B is also not referring only to sports, but to activities involving self-expression.
default.q.n2-36-q70-70.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because A does not advise people to hurry out and get a job; it describes the natural path that people follow. B recommends trying activities that express oneself, not merely finding common interests.
default.q.n2-36-q70-70.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because A reassures the person that it is fine to leave things as they are and that there is nothing to worry about (A says: 「何も心配いりません。」 - There is nothing to worry about), while B recommends trying something proactive and self-expressive (B says: 「スポーツとか、より自己表現的な何かをしてみたらどうでしょうか。何かがん消ってやってみると、また違った気持活になって、したいことが出てくるかもしれませんよ。」 - Why not try sports or something more self-expressive? If you make an effort to try something, you may feel differently and discover something you want to do).
default.q.n2-36-q70-70.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because A says that uncertainty is normal at this age, not that it is bad. B merely observes that the person’s current interests are somewhat passive and suggests a change; it does not criticize them as bad.
default.q.n2-36-q71-71.verdict: The given answer is 4; however, according to the analysis of the passage, the correct view is choice 3: consumers tend to choose fresher food when all items are sold at the same price.
default.q.n2-36-q71-71.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant passage:**
Paragraph 1 describes the current waste of food approaching its use-by date and the Consumer Affairs Agency’s view that public awareness efforts should be strengthened. However, in paragraphs 2 and 3, the author points out that about 80% of people already correctly understand use-by dates. Food approaching its use-by date is left unsold and discarded because new products and near-expiry products are sold at the same price, naturally causing consumers to choose the fresher products.

**Question translation:**
According to the article, why is food returned or discarded because it is approaching its use-by date?

**Answer choices:**
1. Because consumers place too much importance on low food prices.
2. Because consumers do not understand the meaning of use-by dates.
3. Because consumers tend to buy food that is fresher.
4. Because the Consumer Affairs Agency’s public-relations efforts are insufficient.
default.q.n2-36-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not say that consumers’ preference for low prices caused near-expiry products to be discarded. On the contrary, they were willing to pay the regular price for fresher products.
default.q.n2-36-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Paragraph 2 refutes this with statistical data: 「いくつかの調査によれ消、描割前後の人が賞味期限の正しい意味や...知っている」 (surveys show that about 80% of consumers understand the correct meaning of the expiration period).
default.q.n2-36-q71-71.why.2: (c) The quotation supports the author’s view: 「値段が同じなら、少しでも鮮度の良い、つまり賞味期限に余裕のあるほうを選ぶのは、食品の鮮度を気にする消費者としては当然である」 (If the price is the same, it is natural for consumers concerned about freshness to choose the item with better freshness, in other words, more time before its expiration date).
default.q.n2-36-q71-71.why.3: (d) According to the provided answer (Choice 4): Passage 1 mentions the Consumer Affairs Agency’s initial intention to promote public relations and awareness activities (「日付を過ぎても食べられると PR することや消費者の意識を改革する啓発活動を行う」), although the author states in Passage 2 that PR alone is insufficient.
default.q.n2-36-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 多少古くても、安けれ消いいと思う人もいるから (Because some people think food is acceptable if it is cheaper, even if it is slightly less fresh).
default.q.n2-36-q72-72.explanation:
**Relevant passage summary:**
The author explains that if a store discounts products approaching their expiration dates, consumers have two options that suit their needs: they can either buy fresh food at the regular price or buy food that is slightly less fresh at a lower price. As a result, people who want to save money will buy food nearing its expiration date, helping reduce unsold inventory.

**Question translation:**
Why can we assume that 「植引き販売をすれば賞味期限の近付いた食品の売れ残りは減少する」 (if products are sold at a discount, the amount of unsold food nearing its expiration date will decrease)?

**Answer choices:**
1. Because consumers like inexpensive products.
2. Because an economic recession makes goods difficult to sell.
3. Because some people think that even if something is slightly old, it is still acceptable if it is inexpensive.
4. Because the store reduces the amount of food on display in order to maintain its profits.
default.q.n2-36-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author does not make the blanket claim that consumers only want cheap products, but analyzes how they diversify their choices between freshness and price.
default.q.n2-36-q72-72.why.1: (b) Not accurate. The passage does not mention an economic recession (不況) at all.
default.q.n2-36-q72-72.why.2: (c) Supporting evidence: 「期限切れが近付いたものの価格を下げれ消、消費者は新鮮で通常の価格のものと鮮度は少し落活るが低価格のもののどちらかを選抜できるようになる」 (If the prices of items nearing their expiration dates are lowered, consumers can choose between fresh items at the regular price and slightly less fresh items at a lower price).
default.q.n2-36-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage does not mention the store reducing the amount of food it sells in order to maintain profits.
default.q.n2-36-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 2: メーカーや店は、新しくない食品でも販売する工夫をすべきだ (Manufacturers and stores should devise ways to sell food that is no longer new instead of discarding it.)
default.q.n2-36-q73-73.explanation:
**Summary of the relevant passage:** The final part clearly states the author’s conclusion and message: manufacturers and retailers currently return or dispose of near-expiry products without making sufficient efforts to sell them. The author calls for measures—specifically, discount sales—to let consumers decide whether to buy the products before they are discarded, thereby reducing food waste.

**Question translation:**
What does the author most want to say in this passage?

**Answer choices:**
1. Manufacturers and retailers should think more seriously about food safety.
2. Manufacturers and retailers should adopt flexible measures to sell food that is no longer fresh.
3. Consumer affairs agencies should change the rules concerning expiration dates.
4. Consumers should stop being overly concerned about the freshness of food.
default.q.n2-36-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author states that food approaching its expiration date is still safe to eat and that storage is the buyer’s responsibility. The main point is not that companies should reconsider food safety.
default.q.n2-36-q73-73.why.1: (b) Evidence from the passage: 「現状ではメーカーや小売店は賞味期限切れの近付いた食品を売ろうという努力をせずに返品・廃棄しているが、それを購入するかどうかを消費者に委ねれ消、売れ残りは減小し、食品の廃棄も減らせるはずだ。それゆえ、消費者庁はメーカーや小売店が返品・廃棄の前に植引き販売を実施するように指導し...」 Currently, businesses make no effort to sell food nearing its expiration date; measures such as discount sales should be implemented before returning or discarding it.
default.q.n2-36-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author does not propose revising the rules or standards concerning expiration dates (賞味期限のルール).
default.q.n2-36-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author considers it natural for consumers to pay attention to freshness (「当然である」). The proposed solution is not to make consumers change, but for businesses to adjust their prices flexibly.
default.q.n2-36-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (B、D、E), because all three websites, B, D, and E, provide game and quiz sections where users can learn while playing.
default.q.n2-36-q74-74.explanation:
- Main point:
  + Taro wants to study while playing games and solving quizzes (ゲームやクイズをしながら学びたい).
  + Website B: It has a quiz corner (クイズコーナー) about statistical data and history, as well as a game for finding statistical terms (ゲーム).
  + Website D: Alongside lessons about meteorology, it has a game corner with quizzes and a shooting game (クイズや...ゲーム).
  + Website E: It teaches about taxes through games and quizzes (ゲームやクイズ), as well as an interactive game in which users act as a mayor and build a town.
  + Websites A, C, and F do not offer learning through games or quizzes (A only introduces Japanese anime and games; C only explains agricultural products; F introduces coin magic).

- Translation of the question:
  Taro wants to study while playing games and solving quizzes. Which websites allow him to do that?

- Translation of the choices:
  1. A, B, E
  2. B, C, D
  3. B, D, E
  4. A, B, F
default.q.n2-36-q74-74.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (A, B, E) is incorrect. Website A only introduces technology products, anime, and games originating in Japan; it does not offer learning through games or quiz-solving features.
default.q.n2-36-q74-74.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 (B 、 C 、 D) is incorrect: Website C only provides explanatory information about the production process and history of agricultural products; it has no games or quizzes for learning.
default.q.n2-36-q74-74.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (B, D, E) is correct. Page B has 「クイズコーナー、統計用語を探し出すゲームも楽しめる」, a quiz corner and a game for finding statistical terms. Page D has 「ゲームコーナーではクイズやシ画ーティン子ゲームも楽しめる」, a game corner with quizzes and shooting games. Page E says 「税に関係する内容をゲームやクイズ...楽しみながら学ぶことができる」, allowing visitors to learn about taxes through games and quizzes.
default.q.n2-36-q74-74.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (A, B, F) is incorrect: site A has no games or quizzes for learning, while site F only introduces a coin magic trick (手品), not a quiz or educational game.
default.q.n2-36-q75-75.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (B, C, D), because websites B, C, and D fully meet Hanako’s three research needs: learning how to create charts, researching agricultural products/crops, and learning about Earth’s environment.
default.q.n2-36-q75-75.explanation:
- Main idea:
  + Hanako's research topic is "Changes in the Earth's environment and their effects on crops" (地球環境の変化と作物への影響), and she also wants to "compile the information into a graph" (グラフにまとめよう).
  + Website D helps users learn about changes in the Earth's environment and climate ("気象観測、空、火山、台風、津波、地球環境などのの気象に関する学習").
  + Website C helps users learn about agricultural products and crops ("米や肉、魚、野菜... 農産物").
  + Website B teaches how to represent and create graphs ("グラフの表し方や作り方などを漫画やキャラクター同士の会話を通して、学べるコーナー").
  + Therefore, the three useful websites for Hanako are B, C, and D.

- Translation of the question:
  Hanako has decided to research "Changes in the Earth's environment and their effects on crops" as an independent-study project during the summer vacation. She plans to gather information and compile it into a graph. Which websites would be useful for her research?

- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. A, B, D
  2. A, C, D
  3. B, C, D
  4. B, D, F
default.q.n2-36-q75-75.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (A, B, D) is incorrect: Website A introduces only diplomatic work and Japanese culture; it contains no information about crops or agricultural products (作物).
default.q.n2-36-q75-75.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (A 、 C 、 D) is incorrect: Without website B, Hanako cannot learn how to present and create graphs (グラフの表し方や作り方); website A is also unrelated to the topic.
default.q.n2-36-q75-75.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (B, C, D) is correct: Page D provides information about Earth's environment through '地球環境などのの気象に関する学習'; page C provides knowledge about crops and agricultural products through '米や野菜...農産物'; and page B explains how to handle graphs through 'グラフの表し方や作り方などを...学べるコーナー'.
default.q.n2-36-q75-75.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (B, D, F) is incorrect: Website F only discusses the manufacturing process and the history of currency (貨幣), and has nothing to do with crops or agricultural products.
default.q.n2-36-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 築, forming 築20年, meaning it was built 20 years ago.
default.q.n2-36-q11-11.explanation:
Sentence translation: I live in a detached house that was built 20 years ago.
- Related kanji readings: 築: construction, building; 一軒家: detached house.
- Prefix 築: 築 + [number of years] (read as ちく + number of years) indicates the age of a building, counted from when construction was completed.
- Example: このアパートは築10年ですが、部屋の中はリフォームされてとても綺麗です。 (This apartment is 10 years old, but the interior has been renovated and is very beautiful.)
default.q.n2-36-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「経」 (in 経過 and 経年) cannot stand alone and be placed directly before a number of years to indicate the service life of a building.
default.q.n2-36-q11-11.why.1: (b) 「過」 (as in 過去 and 過半数) is not used as a prefix before the number of years indicating how long ago a house was built.
default.q.n2-36-q11-11.why.2: (c) 「建」, as in 建築 and 建物, means construction, but it cannot be used in the form「建20年」.
default.q.n2-36-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「築」 (CHIKU) is a prefix used before a number of years in 「築＋[number of years]」, for example 築20年 - ちくにじゅうねん, indicating the number of years since a house or building was constructed.
default.q.n2-36-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 資源ごみ (recyclable waste).
default.q.n2-36-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Let's dispose of the large cardboard boxes as recyclable waste.
- Kanji note: 資源 (recyclable resources), 生ごみ (food waste, kitchen waste), 分別 (sorting).
- Example: 古新聞や段ボールは資源ごみとしてリサイクルされます。 (Old newspapers and cardboard are collected as recyclable waste and recycled.)
default.q.n2-36-q12-12.why.0: (a) 「資源ごみ」 (recyclable or recoverable waste) refers to recyclable items such as cardboard (段ボール), newspapers, and plastic or glass bottles, so it fits the context perfectly.

Meaning: Because I was sweating from a fever, I changed my underwear.

default.q.n2-36-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 真後ろ (directly behind).

Sentence meaning: A train is running directly behind my house.

default.q.n2-36-q16-16.why.1: (b) 断定 (だんてい - assertion, definitive statement): used when stating something with certainty, not for a seat.

default.q.n2-36-q17-17.explanation:

default.q.n2-36-q18-18.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "Because this summer's heat is especially intense, I leave the air conditioner running all night whenever I sleep."

  + 巨大 (きょだい): huge, gigantic in physical size (e.g., 巨大な建物 — a gigantic building).
  + 強引 (ごういん): forceful, coercive, domineering (e.g., 強引なやり方 — a forceful approach).

default.q.n2-36-q18-18.why.0: (a) 格別 (かくべつ - exceptional, extraordinary): indicates a degree far beyond the ordinary and goes with 「暑さ」to mean exceptionally intense heat.
default.q.n2-36-q18-18.why.1: (b) 過剰 (かじょう - excessive, more than necessary): used for excessive amounts or degrees, such as excessive self-confidence or excessive nutrition. It is not used to describe the degree of the weather’s temperature.
default.q.n2-36-q18-18.why.2: (c) 巨大 (きょだい: enormous): Used to describe the large size or scale of an object, not a feeling or the weather.
default.q.n2-36-q18-18.why.3: (d) 強引 (ごういん: forceful or coercive) describes a forced or pushy attitude or action; it is not used for the weather.
default.q.n2-36-q19-19.explanation:
- Meaning: “The view of the autumn-colored mountains from this hotel is wonderful.”
- Related vocabulary:
  + 眺め (ながめ): view, scenery (verb: 眺める - to look at, gaze at).
  + 響き (ひびき): resonance, echo (verb: 響く).
  + 香り (かおり): fragrance, aroma (used for the sense of smell).
  + 望み (のぞみ): hope, wish (verb: 望む).
- Example:
  + 部屋の窓からの海の眺めが素晴らしい。(The view of the sea from the room window is wonderful.)
default.q.n2-36-q19-19.why.0: (a) ながめ (眺め - view, scenery): It combines with 「見る」 to refer to scenery viewed from a hotel, which fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n2-36-q19-19.why.1: (b) ひびき (響き: resonance, echo) relates to hearing and sound, so it cannot be used with「見る」to describe looking at mountains.
default.q.n2-36-q19-19.why.2: (c) かおり (香り: fragrance) belongs to the sense of smell and is not used to describe the view of red leaves seen from a distance.
default.q.n2-36-q19-19.why.3: (d) のぞみ (望み – hope, wish): refers to a psychological desire or aspiration and is not used for a natural landscape.
default.q.n2-36-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (やたらに).
default.q.n2-36-q20-20.explanation:
- Sentence translation: There have been an unusually large number of phone calls since this morning, so the work I started has barely made any progress.
- Related vocabulary:
  + やたらに / やたらと (矢鱈に): excessively, indiscriminately, unusually frequently (e.g., やたらにお腹が空く: to feel unusually hungry).
  + なんとか (何とか): somehow, by some means (e.g., 何とか間に合った: somehow, I made it on time).
  + おおよそ (凡そ): approximately, roughly (e.g., おおよその見積もり: a rough estimate).
- Example:

default.q.n2-36-q20-20.why.0: (a) なんとか (somehow, managing): Expresses making an effort to manage something; it does not modify an unusually high degree or frequency.

default.q.n2-36-q20-20.why.2: (c) おおよそ (roughly, approximately) estimates a general quantity and does not combine with 「電話が多い」to indicate the frequency of nuisance calls.
default.q.n2-36-q20-20.why.3: (d) やたらに (excessively, unusually often): 「やたらに電話が多い」(there are an unusually large number of phone calls) accurately expresses an excessive frequency that interferes with work.
default.q.n2-36-q21-21.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “The area around the National Diet Building is guarded extremely strictly.”
- Related vocabulary / kanji readings:
  + 厳重 (げんじゅう): strict, tight, stringent (e.g., 厳重に警備する - to guard strictly, 厳重注意 - severe warning).
  + 警備 (けいび): security, guarding, protection.
  + 独特 (どくとく): unique, distinctive.
  + 重大 (じゅうだい): major, significant, serious (e.g., 重大な問題 - a serious problem).
  + 特定 (とくてい): specific, identified clearly (a particular target or subject).

default.q.n2-36-q21-21.why.0: (a) 独特に (どくとくに): uniquely, distinctively; it is not used for protecting or guarding security.

default.q.n2-36-q21-21.why.2: (c) 厳重に (げんじゅうに - strictly, securely): 「厳重に警備される」(be strictly guarded) is the most accurate fixed collocation.
default.q.n2-36-q21-21.why.3: (d) 特定に (とくていに): specifically, in a targeted manner; it narrows down a particular subject and does not function as an adverb modifying the degree of 警備.
default.q.n2-36-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (くだいた).
default.q.n2-36-q22-22.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "Put crushed ice into a glass and pour black tea into it."
- Distinguishing verbs for deforming or breaking down objects:
  + 砕く (くだく): to crush or break into small pieces, especially hard objects such as ice or stones (e.g., 氷を砕く - crush ice, クラッシュアイス - crushed ice).
  + 刻む (きざむ): to finely chop or mince with a knife (e.g., ネギを刻む - chop green onions).
  + 潰す (つぶす): to crush or flatten soft or hollow objects (e.g., 缶をつぶす - crush a can, トマトをつぶす - crush tomatoes).
  + 崩す (くずす): to break apart a structure or cause it to collapse (e.g., 山を崩す - cause a mountain to collapse, お札を崩す - break a large bill into smaller denominations).
- Example:

default.q.n2-36-q22-22.why.0: (a) くずした (崩した): means “to collapse or break down” or “to exchange into smaller denominations.” It is used for breaking a structure or form, such as a posture or landslide, or for changing money, but not for smashing stones into pieces.
default.q.n2-36-q22-22.why.1: (b) くだいた (砕いた - crushed into small pieces):「氷を砕く」(to crush ice cubes) is the most accurate expression for a hard object such as ice.
default.q.n2-36-q22-22.why.2: (c) きざんだ (刻んだ — chopped finely, minced): used for cutting or mincing vegetables with a knife, or for carving; it is not used for ice.
default.q.n2-36-q22-22.why.3: (d) つぶした (潰した - crushed or flattened): Applying force to flatten a soft or hollow object, such as crushing fruit or flattening a can; it is not used for a lump of stone.
default.q.n2-36-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (おちついた) because 「冷静な」 and 「落ち着いた」 both mean calm and composed, without being controlled by emotion.

default.q.n2-36-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 3 because くれぐれも emphasizes sincere and earnest advice or a request to take care.

くれぐれも is an adverb meaning “earnestly,” “most sincerely,” or “please be sure to,” used to strongly emphasize a heartfelt request, reminder, or good wish addressed to someone. It often appears with patterns such as 「～てください」and 「～ようお願い申し上げます」.

default.q.n2-36-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 2 because あきらか (明らか) indicates that a fact or the truth is obvious and clear, beyond any doubt.
default.q.n2-36-q30-30.explanation:
あきらか (明らか) is a na-adjective expressing that a fact, truth, reason, or piece of evidence is very clear, evident, or beyond doubt. It is commonly used in the patterns 「～のは明らかだ」 and 「～を明らかにする」.

default.q.n2-36-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect: writing clearly and legibly requires はっきりと or わかりやすく, not あきらかに.
default.q.n2-36-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect because answering a question clearly and decisively requires はっきりと or てきぱきと, not あきらかに.
default.q.n2-36-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 4 because 該当 (corresponding to, applicable to) combines with the particle に to form 「～に該当する」, expressing correspondence or a match in meaning.
default.q.n2-36-q31-31.explanation:
該当 (gaitou) is a noun or Group 3 verb meaning “to correspond to, meet, or fall under” a condition, standard, category, or corresponding term. The most common structure is 「～に該当する」.
Example: 条件に該当する応募者を採用する。(We will hire applicants who meet the stated conditions.)
default.q.n2-36-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because 該当 cannot stand alone as an adverb meaning to answer vaguely or superficially. 適当に or 曖昧に should be used here.
default.q.n2-36-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because 該当的 is not a Japanese word. To modify a plan meaning practical or feasible, use 具体的, 現実的, or 画期的.
default.q.n2-36-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect because the noun 該当性 does not exist; to express the validity or soundness of a statement, use 妥当性 or 信憑性.
default.q.n2-36-q31-31.why.3: Correct because 該当する means “correspond to,” forming the phrase 「この単語に該当する外国語」 (“the foreign word corresponding to this word”).
default.q.n2-36-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 4 because 中断 refers to an ongoing process or activity being temporarily interrupted midway.
default.q.n2-36-q32-32.explanation:
中断 (chuudan) is a noun or Group 3 verb referring to an action, event, or match being temporarily stopped or interrupted midway, usually with the expectation that it will resume later. A very common expression is 「一時中断する」.
Example: 雨のため試合は一時中断された。(The match was temporarily interrupted because of the rain.)
default.q.n2-36-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because 中断 is used for an ongoing process that is interrupted, not for canceling a previously scheduled appointment (取り消した or キャンセルした would be appropriate here).
default.q.n2-36-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect because the field trip was completely canceled before it took place due to the storm, so 中止(cancellation) must be used, not 中断(a temporary interruption while something is in progress).
default.q.n2-36-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because trees broken or knocked down by lightning should be described with 折れた or 倒れた; 中断 is used for processes or activities, not physical objects.
default.q.n2-36-q32-32.why.3: Correct because the match was temporarily stopped halfway through due to rain, naturally combining with 「一時中断した」 (was temporarily interrupted).
default.q.n2-36-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (しずんだ).
default.q.n2-36-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: In the middle of the meeting, news came that the director had suddenly passed away, and all the employees were plunged into grief.
• Sino-Japanese reading: 沈 (chin).
• Fixed expression: 悲しみに沈む (to be immersed in grief).
• Example: 太陽が水平線に沈んだ。(The sun sank below the horizon.)
default.q.n2-36-q1-1.why.0: (a) いたんだ is the past form of 傷む/痛む (to hurt, deteriorate, feel pain), not the reading of 沈んだ.
default.q.n2-36-q1-1.why.1: (b) ゆるんだ is the past form of 緩む (to loosen, slow down, or relax), not the reading of 沈んだ.
default.q.n2-36-q1-1.why.2: (c) うかんだ is the past form of 浮かんだ (float up, appear, or come to mind), which is the opposite of 沈む and is not the reading of 沈んだ.
default.q.n2-36-q1-1.why.3: (d) しずんだis the past form of 沈む(to sink, go down, or be immersed in sadness), and is the correct reading of 沈んだin the phrase「悲しみに沈む」.
default.q.n2-36-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (やさしく).
default.q.n2-36-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: She is positively described as gentle, kind, humorous, and relatively free of flaws.
• On-reading: 優.
• Note: In the i-adjective「優しい」, 優 is read with the kun-reading やさしい; in the verb「優れる」, it is read すぐれる; its on-reading is ゆう, as in 優秀 (ゆうしゅう: excellent) and 俳優 (はいゆう: actor).
• Example: 彼女は誰に対しても優しく接してくれる。(She always treats everyone kindly and gently.)
default.q.n2-36-q2-2.why.0: (a) さびしい is written in kanji as 寂しい or 淋しい and means lonely or sad; it is unrelated to 優.
default.q.n2-36-q2-2.why.1: (b) はげしく is the adverbial form of 激しい (intense, fierce), not the reading of 優しく.
default.q.n2-36-q2-2.why.2: (c) したしく is the adverbial form of 親しい (close, familiar), not the reading of 優しく.
default.q.n2-36-q2-2.why.3: (d) やさしく is the adverbial form of 優しい (gentle, kind, or tender), and it is the correct reading of 優しく.
default.q.n2-36-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: Because of my work circumstances, my return time is not fixed; sometimes I get home early, while other times I do not get home until midnight.
• Kanji: 都 (capital) + 合 (fit) = 都合 (circumstances, convenience).
• Common expressions: 都合がいい (convenient, available), 都合が悪い (inconvenient, unavailable), 仕事の都合で (because of work circumstances).
• Example: 今週末は都合がつかないので、また次回にしましょう。(I can’t arrange my schedule this weekend, so let’s do it another time.)
default.q.n2-36-q3-3.why.0: (a) とごう is an incorrect on-reading of 都; in 都合, 都 is read つ, not と.
default.q.n2-36-q3-3.why.1: (b) とあい misreads both 都, which is と, and 合, which is read here with its kun-reading あい.
default.q.n2-36-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「つごう」 is the correct on-reading of both kanji: 都 (つ) + 合 (ごう). 都合 means conditions, circumstances, or convenience.
default.q.n2-36-q3-3.why.3: (d) つあい incorrectly reads 合 with the kun-reading あい instead of the on-reading ごう.
default.q.n2-36-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (えいようぶん).
default.q.n2-36-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Blood circulating through the body supplies oxygen and nutrients while also transporting and eliminating unnecessary substances.
• Kanji components: 栄 (glory) + 養 (nourishment) + 分 (portion).
• Related vocabulary: 栄養 (nutrition), 塩分 (salt content), 水分 (water content/moisture).
• Example: バランスよく栄養分を摂取することが健康の秘訣だ。(Taking in a balanced amount of nutrients is the secret to good health.)
default.q.n2-36-q4-4.why.0: (a) えようぶん is missing the long vowel い in 栄; the correct reading is えい.
default.q.n2-36-q4-4.why.1: (b) えいようぶん is the correct reading of 栄養分: 栄 (えい) + 養 (よう) + 分 (ぶん), meaning nutrients or nutritional components.
default.q.n2-36-q4-4.why.2: (c) えようふん is incorrect both because 栄 is missing its long vowel (え instead of えい) and because 分 has the wrong reading; it should be the voiced reading ぶん.
default.q.n2-36-q4-4.why.3: (d) えいようふん is an incorrect reading of 分. In nouns referring to components or amounts, 分 is read as ぶん, not ふん.
default.q.n2-36-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: After extensive experimentation, improvement, and continuous effort, the experiment finally succeeded.
• Kanji: 工 (effort) + 夫 (method) = 工夫 (ingenuity, creative effort).
• Common expressions: 工夫を凝らす (to devise creatively, think hard), 工夫を重ねる (to make repeated improvements and refinements).
• Example: 狭い部屋を広く見せるために、家具の配置を工夫した。(I creatively arranged the furniture to make the small room look larger.)
default.q.n2-36-q5-5.why.0: (a) こうふ is a reading of 工夫 when it refers to a miner or manual laborer (鉱夫, rarely used), so it does not have the meaning of ingenuity or creative problem-solving in this context.
default.q.n2-36-q5-5.why.1: (b) こうふう is the usual sound combination of 工 (こう) and 夫 (ふう), but the Japanese word meaning ingenuity or creative effort has the special reading くふう.
default.q.n2-36-q5-5.why.2: (c) くふう is the correct reading of 工夫, meaning to make an effort to devise, find solutions, or improve a method for solving a problem.
default.q.n2-36-q5-5.why.3: (d) くうふ incorrectly reverses the position of the long vowel in くふう.
default.q.n2-36-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 駐車場.
default.q.n2-36-q6-6.explanation:
Meaning: People going to the prefectural office are having trouble because the parking lot is too narrow.
- Sino-Japanese components: 駐 (park, stop) + 車 (vehicle) + 場 (place) = 駐車場 (parking lot).
- Related vocabulary: 駐車 (ちゅうしゃ: parking), 駐輪場 (ちゅうりんじょう: bicycle or motorcycle parking area).
- Example: このスーパーは広い駐車場がある。(This supermarket has a spacious parking lot.)
default.q.n2-36-q6-6.why.0: (a) 「駅車場」: Incorrect kanji. 「駅」 (station) is not used in this word, and this word does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n2-36-q6-6.why.1: (b) 「駐車場」: Correct. 「駐」(to stop or park) combines with「車」(vehicle) and「場」(place) to form「駐車場」(ちゅうしゃじょう: parking lot).
default.q.n2-36-q6-6.why.2: (c) 「馳車場」: The first kanji is incorrect. 「馳」(run fast, dash) resembles 「駐」, which uses the same horse radical 馬, but it does not form this word.
default.q.n2-36-q6-6.why.3: (d) 「騒車場」: Incorrect kanji. 「騒」 (Tao - noisy, tumultuous) looks similar to 「駐」 (which also contains the 馬 radical), but it is completely incorrect in meaning.
default.q.n2-36-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 偶然.
default.q.n2-36-q7-7.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: Yesterday, I happened to run into an old friend at the ticket gate.
- Kanji components: 偶 (GŪ — by chance, even number) + 然 (ZEN) = 偶然 (chance, coincidence).
- Antonyms: 必然 (ひつぜん — necessity, inevitability), 意図的 (いとてき — intentional).
- Example: 街で偶然、高校の同級生を見かけた。(I happened to see a high school classmate on the street.)
default.q.n2-36-q7-7.why.0: (a) 「寓然」: The kanji is incorrect. 寓 (グウ—parable, residence) uses the roof radical 宀 instead of the person radical 亻, and does not combine with 然 to be read ぐうぜん.
default.q.n2-36-q7-7.why.1: (b) 「偶然」: Correct. 「偶」(random, accidental) + 「然」 forms 偶然 (ぐうぜん: by chance, accidental).
default.q.n2-36-q7-7.why.2: (c) 「隅然」: Incorrect kanji. The kanji 「隅」 means a corner or nook and contains the 阝 radical; it is not used to form this word.
default.q.n2-36-q7-7.why.3: (d) 「伝然」: The kanji is incorrect. 「伝」 (to convey or spread) does not form this word.
default.q.n2-36-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 招待.
default.q.n2-36-q8-8.explanation:
Meaning: When I was invited to a celebration party, I was served alcohol.
- Kanji meanings: 招 (to invite, beckon) + 待 (to entertain, treat) = 招待 (to invite, entertain).
- Distinction: 招待 (しょうたい: invite someone to a party or event), 紹介 (しょうかい: introduce a person or thing to someone).
- Example: 友人の結婚式に招待された。(I was invited to my friend’s wedding.)
default.q.n2-36-q8-8.why.0: (a) 「紹待」: Incorrect kanji. 「紹」in 紹介 has been mistakenly combined with「待」.
default.q.n2-36-q8-8.why.1: (b) 「紹介」: Incorrect word/reading. 「紹介」 is read しょうかい (introduction), not しょうたい.
default.q.n2-36-q8-8.why.2: (c) 「招待」: Correct. 「招」(inviting) + 「待」(entertaining) forms 招待 (しょうたい: invitation, entertaining guests).
default.q.n2-36-q8-8.why.3: (d) 「招介」: Incorrect kanji. It is a mistaken combination of the kanji from 招待 and 紹介; this word does not exist.
default.q.n2-36-q9-9.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The smoke got into my eyes and made me cry.
- Related vocabulary: 喫煙 (きつえん: smoking), 禁煙 (きんえん: no smoking, smoking prohibition), 煙突 (えんとつ: chimney).
- Example: 焚き火から白い煙が上がっている。(White smoke is rising from the campfire.)
default.q.n2-36-q9-9.why.0: (a) 「煙」: Correct. The kanji 「煙」 means smoke, has the kun-reading けむり (or けむ), and the on-reading えん, as in 禁煙 (きんえん).
default.q.n2-36-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「燃」: Incorrect kanji. 「燃」 means burning or setting fire; its kun-readings are も(える)/も(やす), and its on-reading is ねん, as in 燃料 (ねんりょう).
default.q.n2-36-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「燥」: Incorrect kanji. 「燥」 means “dry” and has the on-reading そう, as in 乾燥 (かんそう); it is not read けむり.
default.q.n2-36-q9-9.why.3: (d) 「灯」: Incorrect kanji. 「灯」 means lamp or light; its kunyomi is ひ and its on-reading is とう (as in 電灯 - でんとう).
default.q.n2-36-q10-10.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The shore is covered with large rocks, and flowers are blooming there.
- Kanji note: 岩 means a large rock, crag, or cliff.
- Contrast: 「石」(いし: stone in general, small rock) vs. 「岩」(いわ: large rock, rocky outcrop, cliff).
- Example: 海岸には大きな岩がたくさん並んでいる。(Many large rocks are lined up along the coast.)
default.q.n2-36-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「石」: Incorrect reading and meaning. The kanji 「石」 means a stone or pebble, is read いし, and has the on-readings せき / こく.
default.q.n2-36-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「岩」: Correct. 「岩」 is read with the kun-reading いわ and the on-reading がん (as in 岩石 - がんせき).
default.q.n2-36-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「砂」: Incorrect kanji. 「砂」(sand) is read すな; its on-readings are さ / しゃ (as in 砂漠 - さばく).
default.q.n2-36-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「炭」: Incorrect kanji. 「炭」is read すみ, with the on-reading たん, as in 石炭 (せきたん).
default.q.n2-37-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (さえ): the pattern 「〜さえ〜ば」 expresses the minimum necessary condition, “as long as ...”.
default.q.n2-37-q33-33.explanation: Meaning: "I think the idea that you can do anything as long as you have money is mistaken." Kanji notes: 金 means money; 考 means thought or consideration; 間違 means mistake. In the test's OCR, it was incorrectly recognized as ま活. Pattern: 「N + さえ + Vば / Aければ / Na・Nなら」 (as long as...; if only...). Example: 体さえ健康なら、どんな困難も乗り越えられる。(As long as you are healthy, you can overcome any difficulty.)
default.q.n2-37-q33-33.why.0: (a) 「まで」 means “all the way to” or “even,” expressing the highest degree or an extreme limit. It does not combine with the conditional form 「〜あれば」 to mean “as long as” or “if only.”
default.q.n2-37-q33-33.why.1: (b) 「さえ」combines with the conditional form in「Nさえ〜ば」, meaning “as long as there is N...” and expressing the minimum necessary condition for what follows to occur.
default.q.n2-37-q33-33.why.2: (c) 「しか」normally combines with the negative form in「しか〜ない」to mean “only”; it does not directly combine with the affirmative auxiliary「あれば」as shown here.
default.q.n2-37-q33-33.why.3: (d) 「こそ」 is used for emphasis ("precisely" or "indeed"), often with 「〜からこそ」 (precisely because); in this context, it does not express a minimum condition.
default.q.n2-37-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (苦しくても): The adverb 「たとえ」combines with 「〜ても」to form a concessive pattern meaning “even if...” or “no matter how...”.
default.q.n2-37-q34-34.explanation: Sentence meaning: "No matter how difficult the training may be, I cannot give up my dream of winning a gold medal at the Olympics." Vocabulary: 練習 (training), 金 (gold; in the OCR, 金メダル was incorrectly recognized as 金申ダル), 夢 (dream), 苦 (painful, difficult). Grammar pattern: 「たとえ + Vても / Aくても / Na・Nでも」 (even if...; no matter how...). Example: たとえ両親に反対されても、留学する意志は変わらない。(Even if my parents oppose me, my intention to study abroad will not change.)
default.q.n2-37-q34-34.why.0: (a) 「苦しいので」means “because it is difficult/tough,” an ordinary expression of an objective reason, and does not combine with the hypothetical adverb「たとえ」.
default.q.n2-37-q34-34.why.1: (b) 「苦しかったら」 is the 「〜たら」 conditional form (if it is difficult), and is not used to form the hypothetical concessive pair with 「たとえ」.
default.q.n2-37-q34-34.why.2: (c) 「苦しくても」combines with 「たとえどんなに」to form the structure 「たとえ〜ても」, meaning “no matter how difficult it may be.” This is completely correct in both grammar and meaning.
default.q.n2-37-q34-34.why.3: (d) 「苦しけれ消」 is an OCR error for 「苦しければ」, the conditional 「〜ば」 form meaning “if it is difficult”; it does not pair with the correlative expression 「たとえ」.
default.q.n2-37-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (歩いて帰るしかない): the pattern 「Vる + しかない」 means “there is no choice but to…” or “have to….”
default.q.n2-37-q35-35.explanation: Meaning: "It’s late, so I want to take a taxi home, but I have no money, so I have no choice but to walk home." Kanji meanings: 遅 (late), 歩 (walk), 帰 (return home). Pattern 「Vる + しかない」 (have no choice but to do V). Example: 終電を逃してしまったので、始発まで漫画喫茶で過ごすしかない。(I missed the last train, so I have no choice but to spend the night at a manga café until the first train.)
default.q.n2-37-q35-35.why.0: (a) 「歩いて帰ることはない」 means “there is no need to walk home,” which is the opposite of a situation where having no money for a taxi makes walking home unavoidable.
default.q.n2-37-q35-35.why.1: (b) 「歩いて帰るまい」expresses the volitional idea “I will not walk home” or the negative conjecture “I probably will not walk home.” It does not fit a situation in which there is no other choice but to walk home.
default.q.n2-37-q35-35.why.2: (c) 「歩いて帰るわけがない」means “there is absolutely no way [someone] would walk home,” a logical inferential negation that does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-37-q35-35.why.3: (d) 「歩いて帰るしかない」means “have no choice but to walk home” or “can only walk home,” describing the lack of any other option because the person has run out of money.
default.q.n2-37-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (もので): The pattern 「〜もので / ものだから」 is used to give a reason or offer a mild, polite excuse.
default.q.n2-37-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: “I was a little busy, so I replied late. I am truly sorry.” Kanji: 忙: busy, 返事: reply, 申: say, 訳: reason.
Pattern: plain form (Naな/Nな) + もので / ものですから (“because...”; used when giving an explanation or polite apology).
Example: 道が混んでいたものですから、集合時間に遅れてしまいました。(The roads were so crowded that I arrived late for the meeting.)
default.q.n2-37-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「とたんに」 is typically used with 「Vた + とたんに」 to mean “just as soon as..., something unexpected happened,” and is not used to explain a delay.
default.q.n2-37-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「ところで」 means “even if ...” when used with Vた, or functions as a topic-changing conjunction (“by the way”). It is not used to give a reason or justification.
default.q.n2-37-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「もので」 (or 「ものだから」) follows the plain form and is used to give an objective reason, make an excuse, or apologize for one’s own behavior.
default.q.n2-37-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「ものなら」 is commonly used with the potential form 「V-れる + ものなら」 (“if it were possible to...”) or in the warning pattern 「Vよう + ものなら」 (“if one were to...”). It does not fit this sentence.
default.q.n2-37-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (にかけて): The pattern 「N1 から N2 にかけて」 means “from N1 to N2” and describes an uninterrupted span of time or space.
default.q.n2-37-q37-37.explanation: Sentence meaning: "Because there was very little rain from spring through autumn, water shortages are continuing nationwide this winter." Kanji readings: 春 (SHUN), 秋 (SHŪ), 冬 (TŌ), 非常 (HIJŌ — extremely/very), 全国 (ZENKOKU — nationwide), 水不足 (MIZUBUSOKU — water shortage), 状態 (JŌTAI — condition/state), 続 (ZOKU — continue). Distinction: 「〜から〜まで」indicates clearly defined starting and ending points, whereas 「〜から〜にかけて」indicates a continuous span of time or space with less clearly defined boundaries. Example: 明日の朝から昼にかけて強い雨が降るでしょう。(There will probably be heavy rain from tomorrow morning through around noon.)
default.q.n2-37-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「にかけて」 follows 「N1 から N2」 to form the pattern 「〜から〜にかけて」, meaning “from ... through ...” or “extending from ... to ...,” indicating an approximate period from spring to autumn.
default.q.n2-37-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「にἢって」 (an OCR error for 「に沿って」 or 「に伴って」) means “along/in accordance with” or “along with,” and does not follow 「から」 to indicate a period of time.
default.q.n2-37-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「に先立って」 means “before / prior to” a major event and is grammatically unsuitable with the double time span 「春から秋」.
default.q.n2-37-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「に 右 って」(an OCR error for「に当たって」or「に従って」) means “on the occasion of/when” or “according to,” and does not combine with the structure「AからB」indicating a time span.
default.q.n2-37-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (だらけ): The suffix 「N + だらけ」means “full of, covered with...,” and is used with nouns describing negative things that cover a surface.
default.q.n2-37-q38-38.explanation: Sentence meaning: "This room had not been used for a long time, so it became covered in dust." Sino-Japanese readings: 部屋 (— room), 長 (— long), 間 (— interval), 使 (— use). Vocabulary: ほこり (dust), ほこりだらけ (covered in dust). Structure: 「N + だらけ」(full of, covered with—used for dust, garbage, mistakes, blood, wounds, debts, etc.).
