Example: 書類の準備が整い次第、ご連絡いたします。(I will contact you as soon as the documents are ready.)
default.q.n2-38-q9-9.why.0: (a) 揃ったら: Incorrect. The verb 「揃う」(そろう), meaning to gather fully or become uniform, is written with 「揃」; it is not read ととのう.
default.q.n2-38-q9-9.why.1: (b) 終わったら: Incorrect. The verb 「終わる」(おわる - to end, be finished) uses the kanji 「終」, not ととのう.
default.q.n2-38-q9-9.why.2: (c) 補ったら: Incorrect. The verb 「補う」(おぎなう - to make up for, supplement) uses the kanji 「補」, not ととのう.
default.q.n2-38-q9-9.why.3: (d) 整ったら: Correct. The verb「整う」(ととのう: to be fully prepared, ready, or orderly) uses the kanji「整」, and its conditional past form is「整ったら」(ととのったら).
default.q.n2-38-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 強引 (forceful, coercive, overbearing, or stubbornly pushing ahead).
default.q.n2-38-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: "The former director failed because of his high-handed business methods."
Sino-Japanese reading: 強引 (gōin).
Related expressions: 無理やり (forcibly, by force), 独断的 (dictatorial, arbitrary).
Example: 彼の強引なやり方に反対する人が多い。(Many people oppose his high-handed approach.)
default.q.n2-38-q10-10.why.0: (a) 強因: Incorrect. 「因」is read as いん, but it does not combine with 「強」to form the word 「強因」.
default.q.n2-38-q10-10.why.1: (b) 強引: Correct. The kanji combines 「強」 (strong, forceful) with 「引」 (pull), forming the na-adjective 「強引」 (ごういん), meaning domineering, coercive, or forceful regardless of the opinions of others.
default.q.n2-38-q10-10.why.2: (c) 合因: Incorrect. Although 「合」 is read ごう, there is no word 「合因」 with this meaning.
default.q.n2-38-q10-10.why.3: (d) 合引: Incorrect. These two kanji do not form a meaningful word in this context.
default.q.n2-39-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (やめざるをえない).
default.q.n2-39-q33-33.explanation:
Meaning: Although I went to the trouble of finding a part-time job, my exam is approaching, so I have no choice but to quit.
- Pattern: V-ない (remove ない) + ざるを得ない (with する → せざるを得ない), expressing that circumstances force someone to do something even though they do not really want to.
- Example: 理由がどうであれ、規則を破った以上は処分を受けざるをえない。(Whatever the reason, once you have broken the rules, you have no choice but to accept disciplinary action.)
default.q.n2-39-q33-33.why.0: (a) 「〜ずにはいられない」 expresses an emotion or action that arises naturally and cannot be restrained (“cannot help but...”); it is not used for a deliberate decision made because circumstances require it.
default.q.n2-39-q33-33.why.1: (b) 「〜ざるをえない」means "have no choice but to" or "be forced to" do something because of circumstances, even unwillingly. It fits the situation of reluctantly giving up a job search because of exams.
default.q.n2-39-q33-33.why.2: (c) 「〜ないわけではない」 means “it is not that...,” expressing a cautious affirmation, so it does not fit the context of the sentence.
default.q.n2-39-q33-33.why.3: (d) 「〜にほかならない」 means “is precisely” or “is nothing other than ...” and is used to emphasize a sole reason or essential nature, so it is grammatically unsuitable in this sentence.
default.q.n2-39-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (にかけて).
default.q.n2-39-q34-34.explanation:
Meaning: From tonight until around tomorrow morning, there is a risk of heavy snowfall in the Kanto region.
- Vocabulary: 関東地方 (Kanto region), 大雪 (heavy snowfall), 恐れ (concern, risk).
- Pattern: N1 から N2 にかけて (“from around N1 to N2”) indicates an approximate, continuous span of space or time.
- Example: 明日は九州から四国にかけて大雨が降る見込みです。(Heavy rain is expected tomorrow from Kyushu to Shikoku.)
default.q.n2-39-q34-34.why.0: (a) 「〜につれて」 means “as...; in proportion to the change...,” and does not combine with the time-marker structure 「〜から〜」.
default.q.n2-39-q34-34.why.1: (b) 「〜から〜にかけて」 means “from... to...” and indicates a continuous range of time or space; it is commonly used in weather forecasts.
default.q.n2-39-q34-34.why.2: (c) 「〜にともなって」means “along with” or “accompanying,” indicating a change and its accompanying consequence; it is not used to connect points in time.
default.q.n2-39-q34-34.why.3: (d) 「〜に沿って / に従って」 means “along...” or “in accordance with...”; it is not used to express a period from A to B.
default.q.n2-39-q35-35.explanation:
Meaning: Recently, I feel that I have not been getting enough exercise, so I am trying to get up early and walk to the station.
- Kanji-based explanation: 運動不足 (lack of exercise), 気味 (a slight feeling or tendency toward something).
- Structure: N / V-ます stem + 気味 (ぎみ) expresses a slight tendency toward a negative condition, such as lack of exercise, cold symptoms, or fatigue.
- Example: 今日は朝から少し風邪気味なので、早く寝ることにします。(I have felt slightly feverish since this morning, so I have decided to go to bed early.)
default.q.n2-39-q35-35.why.0: (a) 「〜気味（ぎみ）」combines with a noun or verb stem to express a slightly noticeable state or tendency (“a little,” “somewhat”), often with negative conditions such as 運動不足気味 or 風邪気味. It fits the context very well.
default.q.n2-39-q35-35.why.1: (b) 「〜次第」 means “as soon as...” or “depending on...”; it does not combine with a noun to express this state of health.
default.q.n2-39-q35-35.why.2: (c)「〜反面」means “on the other hand, in contrast” and presents two opposing aspects of something; it does not form an appropriate meaning here.
default.q.n2-39-q35-35.why.3: (d) 「〜以来」means “since...,” indicating the starting point of a continuing state; it does not directly combine with 運動不足.
default.q.n2-39-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (ということだ).
default.q.n2-39-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: According to the doctor, my grandmother will probably be able to leave the hospital in two or three days.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 医者 (いしゃ: doctor), 祖母 (そぼ: grandmother), 退院 (たいいん: hospital discharge).
- Pattern: N + によると／によれば ... 〜ということだ／とのことだ (According to source N, I hear that...).
- Example: 天気予報によると、明日は午後から雨になるということだ。(According to the weather forecast, I hear that it will start raining tomorrow afternoon.)
default.q.n2-39-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「〜どころではない」 means “this is no time for…” or “it is impossible to…,” and is not used to cite an information source.
default.q.n2-39-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「〜にきまっている」means “must be...” and expresses the speaker’s absolute subjective judgment, so it is incompatible with the source-attribution structure 「〜によると」.
default.q.n2-39-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「〜ということだ」is used at the end of a sentence to report information (I hear that...), forming the standard pair with「〜によると」.
default.q.n2-39-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「〜というものだ」expresses a general judgment or assessment (“that is truly...”), and is not used to report information from someone else.
default.q.n2-39-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: Although my daughter is already 18, her personality is still very childish. I am worried about whether she will be able to become independent after entering society.
- Character-based readings: 娘 (むすめ: daughter), 社会人 (しゃかいじん: working adult, member of society), 一人立ち (ひとりだち: independence).
- Pattern: N + っぽい means "seems..., has the quality of..." It is often used critically for someone or something that does not behave according to its true nature. For example, an adult with a childish personality can be described as 子供っぽい.
- Example: 彼はもう大人なのに、子供っぽいことばかり言って周りを困らせている。(Although he is already an adult, he keeps saying childish things and causing trouble for those around him.)
default.q.n2-39-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「〜がちだ」 means “to tend to...” and commonly follows a V-ます stem or a noun describing a condition, as in 留守がち or 病気がち. It does not follow a noun referring to a person, such as 「子供」.
default.q.n2-39-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「〜だらけだ」means “full of” or “covered with,” and is used for an abundance of negative things such as garbage or mistakes. It is not used to describe a person’s personality.
default.q.n2-39-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「〜っぽい」attaches to a noun to express a personality trait or outward appearance resembling something. With its complaining nuance—someone is grown up but still childish—it fits the sentence expressing concern perfectly.
default.q.n2-39-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「〜らしい」 can mean 'characteristically' or 'just like...' as praise or an accurate description ('innocently childlike'), but here the daughter is 18 and the speaker is complaining.
default.q.n2-39-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (わけがない).
default.q.n2-39-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: How could such a young child possibly understand this novel?
- Kanji notes: 小説 means "novel"; 理解 means "understanding."
- Pattern: dictionary-form verb / adjective / noun + わけがない (there is no way that... / absolutely cannot...).
- Example: ちゃんと勉強もしないで、JLPT N2に合格できるわけがない。(There is no way you can pass JLPT N2 without studying properly!)
default.q.n2-39-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「〜わけだ」means “that explains it” or “so that means...,” and is used to confirm an obvious conclusion, which is contrary to the sentence's negative meaning of being unable to understand.
default.q.n2-39-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「〜わけがない」means “there is absolutely no way that... / it cannot possibly be...,” and is used to completely deny the possibility that a young child could understand a complex novel.
default.q.n2-39-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「〜しかない」 means “there is no choice but to...,” so it does not fit the potential form 「理解できる」 in this context.
default.q.n2-39-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「〜わけにはいかない」means “cannot do something” because of an ethical barrier, responsibility, or social rule; it is not used to deny natural ability.
default.q.n2-39-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: This room is designed so that people with disabilities or limited mobility can use it easily.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 不自由 (disability, inconvenience, restricted movement), 設計 (design).
- Structure: [V-potential / V-ない / i-adjective] + ように (so that, in order to achieve a desired state).
- Example: 後ろの人にもよく見えるように、大きな文字で書いてください。(Please write in large letters so that the people in the back can see clearly too.)
default.q.n2-39-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「〜ように」 indicates a goal directed toward achieving a certain state. Combined with an adjective or a potential form such as 「使いやすい」, it means “so that” or “in order to.” It is completely correct.
default.q.n2-39-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「〜ために」indicates the purpose of a volitional action and is generally used directly with a V-る form expressing an intentional action. It is not used with the adjective 「使いやすい」to express a purpose involving a state.
default.q.n2-39-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「〜ばかりに」 means “simply because..., resulting in a bad outcome,” so it does not fit the purpose of the design.
default.q.n2-39-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「〜とおりに」 means “exactly as...” and does not express the purpose of designing the room's functions.
default.q.n2-39-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (からこそ).
default.q.n2-39-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: It was precisely because of everyone's warm encouragement that I was able to keep trying until the very end.
- Vocabulary: 皆様 (everyone, ladies and gentlemen), 応援 (encouragement, support).
- Structure: [Plain form / V-た] + からこそ (precisely because...; it is exactly because... that...) emphasizes the fundamental reason leading to a positive result.
- Example: 家族の支えがあったからこそ、苦しい時期を乗り越えることができた。(It was precisely because I had my family's support that I was able to overcome that difficult period.)
default.q.n2-39-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「〜から見ると」means “from the perspective/standpoint of...”; it is not used to indicate the cause leading to an effort.
default.q.n2-39-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「〜からいうと」means “from the standpoint of / judging from...,” and is used to give an objective assessment, not to express a reason for gratitude.
default.q.n2-39-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「〜からこそ」means “precisely because...,” emphasizing the essential reason that produces the positive result that follows; it is exactly appropriate in an expression of gratitude.
default.q.n2-39-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「〜からといって」 means “just because ...,” usually followed by a negative or contrary clause. It is inconsistent with the affirmative result stated in the question.
default.q.n2-39-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (探しようがない).
default.q.n2-39-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning: I lost my wallet, but because I have absolutely no idea when or where I lost it, there is no way I can find it.
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 財布 (wallet), 探す (to search for, look for).
- Pattern: V-stem (remove ます) + ようがない (there is no way to do V; doing so is completely impossible because the necessary information or means is lacking).
- Example: 連絡先も住所も分からないので、連絡のしようがない。(I do not know either the contact information or the address, so there is no way to get in touch.)
default.q.n2-39-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「V-ます (remove ます) + ようがない」 means "there is no way to..." or "it is impossible to..." due to a lack of clues or conditions. It fits the situation of being unable to find a lost wallet because one does not remember where it was dropped.
default.q.n2-39-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「〜ざるをえない」 means “have no choice but to do something.” It is unsuitable because the preceding clause clearly says there is no information to look for.
default.q.n2-39-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「〜ずにはいられない」 means “cannot help doing something” due to an emotional urge; it does not express being unable to take action.
default.q.n2-39-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「〜にほかならない」 means “is precisely...” or “is nothing other than...,” so it does not form a meaningful sentence here.
default.q.n2-39-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ものがある).
default.q.n2-39-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: There is something moving in her singing voice that deeply touches the listener.
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 歌声 (singing voice), 感動 (being moved; emotion).
- Pattern: [V-る / i-adjective / na-adjective] + ものがある (there is something about it; it has a profound quality).
- Example: 彼の作品には、どこか人の心を引きつけるものがある。(There is something about his works that draws people in.)
default.q.n2-39-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「〜というものではない」means “it is not necessarily the case that...” or “it is not simply a matter of...”; it expresses partial negation and does not fit a context of praise.
default.q.n2-39-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「〜にほかならない」is used to assert that something is nothing other than a particular essence. Adding it after 「もの」creates an awkward expression that does not fit the context here.
default.q.n2-39-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「〜というものだ」 is used to state an obvious observation or general principle ("it is indeed the case that..."); it is not suitable for expressing a profound impression of a singing voice.
default.q.n2-39-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「V-る + ものがある」 expresses the speaker’s deep emotion or strong impression (“there is something that...,” or “it is deeply...”); 「感動させるものがある」 is therefore natural and correct.
default.q.n2-39-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (に限らず).
default.q.n2-39-q43-43.explanation:
Meaning: He is a tennis player, but apparently he is confident not only in tennis but also in ball sports in general.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 選手 (せんしゅ, player), 球技 (きゅうぎ, ball sport), 自信 (じしん, confidence).
- Structure: N + に限らず (not limited to N; not only N but also...).
- Example: この映画は子供に限らず、大人にも大人気だ。(This movie is extremely popular not only with children but also with adults.)
default.q.n2-39-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「〜にかかわらず」means “regardless of, irrespective of...” such as age or gender. It is not used to expand the scope from a specific sport, such as tennis, to a group of sports.
default.q.n2-39-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「〜に限らず」 means “not limited to ...; ... as well,” which is exactly right for expressing that he is confident not only in tennis but in ball sports in general.
default.q.n2-39-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「〜にしても」 means “even if / even though ...” and is used to present a concessive assumption, so it does not fit the connection of meaning here.
default.q.n2-39-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「〜にかけても」 means “even in terms of...” or “even if one stakes one’s honor...”; it does not form a logical clause with 「球技」.
default.q.n2-39-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (怒らないではいられない).
default.q.n2-39-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: After being subjected to such cruel and vicious words, who could possibly keep their anger under control?
- Sino-Japanese reading: 怒る (おこる: to get angry).
- Pattern: V-ない + ではいられない (equivalent to 〜ずにはいられない: cannot help doing something, cannot suppress an overwhelming emotion).
- Example: その感動的な結末を見て、涙を流さないではいられなかった。(After watching that moving ending, I could not hold back my tears.)
default.q.n2-39-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「〜ないこともない」means “it is not that ... is impossible” or “it is not that ... does not ...,” expressing cautious concession. It cannot express the intense, natural anger felt after being insulted.
default.q.n2-39-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「〜ことはない」means “there is no need to...” or “you do not have to...,” and is used as advice. This is completely contrary to the emotional state of someone who has been severely insulted.
default.q.n2-39-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「V-ない + ではいられない」 means “cannot help but...” or “cannot hold back from...,” expressing an emotion or natural reflex that bursts out. It is exactly appropriate for saying that anyone would become angry upon hearing cruel words.
default.q.n2-39-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「〜ものではない」is generally used for moral advice (“one should not...”) or absolute negation. Combining it in this form is grammatically incorrect and unnatural.
default.q.n2-39-q45-45.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 3 → 1 (The choice at ★ is 3: おそれが).
default.q.n2-39-q45-45.explanation:
Complete sentence: 雨の日は道路が渋滞するおそれがありますから、早く家を出たほうがいいでしょう。
Meaning: Because there is a risk of traffic congestion on rainy days, you should probably leave home early.
default.q.n2-39-q45-45.why.0: (a) あります: It occupies the fourth position, immediately before the conjunction indicating a reason, 「から」. Combined with the preceding noun 「おそれ」, it forms the complete pattern 「〜おそれがありますから」 (“because there is a fear/risk that…”).
default.q.n2-39-q45-45.why.1: (b) 道路が appears in the first position and serves as the subject of the subordinate clause modifying the noun 「おそれ」that follows.
default.q.n2-39-q45-45.why.2: (c) おそれが: It appears in the third position (the ★ position), directly after the dictionary form of the verb 「渋滞する」to form the grammar pattern 「V-dictionary form + おそれがある」(there is a risk / concern that an undesirable event will occur).
default.q.n2-39-q45-45.why.3: (d) 渋 滞 する: It appears in the second position, serves as the predicate of 「道路が」, and directly modifies the noun 「おそれ」 in the third position: 道路が渋滞するおそれ.
default.q.n2-39-q46-46.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 4 → 3 → 2 (The choice at ★ is 3: めぐって).
default.q.n2-39-q46-46.explanation:
Complete sentence: 兄と弟は、亡くなった父親の財産をめぐって争いを続けている。
Meaning: The two brothers continue to fight over their deceased father's estate.
default.q.n2-39-q46-46.why.0: (a) 父親の: It occupies position 1 and follows the modifying verb 「亡くなった」to form 「亡くなった父親の」(of the deceased father), which modifies 「財産」below.
default.q.n2-39-q46-46.why.1: (b) 争いを: It appears in the fourth position and serves as the direct object of the verb 「続けている」 at the end of the sentence, forming 「争いを続けている」(continue the dispute or struggle).
default.q.n2-39-q46-46.why.2: (c) めぐって: It appears in the third position (★) and combines with the preceding noun phrase to form the grammatical structure 「N + をめぐって」, meaning “concerning” or “over the issue of.”
default.q.n2-39-q46-46.why.3: (d) 財産を: This occupies the second position, is modified by「父親の」before it, and uses the particle「を」to connect directly with「めぐって」at position ★.
default.q.n2-39-q47-47.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3 (the ★ is in position 1: 謝りようが).
default.q.n2-39-q47-47.explanation:
Complete sentence: 彼女にあんなにひどいことをしてしまってはどんなに謝りたくても謝りようがない。
Meaning: After having done something so terrible to her, there is no way to apologize, no matter how much I want to.
default.q.n2-39-q47-47.why.0: (a) 謝りようが: At position 3 (★), this is the form 「V-masu stem + ようが」, followed by 「ない」 to form 「〜ようがない」 (“there is no way to...,” “it is impossible to...” ).
default.q.n2-39-q47-47.why.1: (b) どんなに: It occupies the first position and is an adverb expressing a high degree, used together with the concessive conditional pattern 「〜ても」 in the next position.
default.q.n2-39-q47-47.why.2: (c) ない: It occupies the fourth position at the end of the sentence and combines with 「謝りようが」 to complete the negative structure 「謝りようがない」.
default.q.n2-39-q47-47.why.3: (d) 謝りたくても: This is the 「〜ても」 form of the desiderative 「謝りたい」 and follows 「どんなに」 to create the pattern 「どんなに〜ても」 (“no matter how much one wants to apologize”). It belongs in position 2.
default.q.n2-39-q48-48.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 3 → 4 → 1 (the ★ position is choice 4: 努力をしている).
default.q.n2-39-q48-48.explanation:
Complete sentence: 英語が上手になるようにできるかぎりの努力をしているつもりだが、なかなか目標のレベルまで達しない。
Meaning: I believe I am making every effort I can to improve my English, but I still cannot seem to reach my target level.
default.q.n2-39-q48-48.why.0: (a) つもりだ: it occupies the fourth position, following 「〜ている」to form 「〜ているつもりだ」(believe or assume that one is doing something), and connects to the contrastive conjunction 「が」immediately afterward.
default.q.n2-39-q48-48.why.1: (b) できる: It occupies position 1 and is a dictionary-form verb placed before 「かぎりの」to form the fixed expression 「できるかぎり」(as much as possible, to the fullest extent possible).
default.q.n2-39-q48-48.why.2: (c) かぎりの: It comes second and uses the particle 「の」to modify the following noun 「努力」as an attributive phrase (できるかぎりの努力).
default.q.n2-39-q48-48.why.3: (d) 努力をしている: It is in the third position (★), modified by 「できるかぎりの」 and followed by the 〜ている form, forming the preceding clause of 「〜つもりだ」.
default.q.n2-39-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3 (the ★ is in position 1: 改善しつつ).
default.q.n2-39-q49-49.explanation:
Complete sentence: 年々悪化していた都市の治安が、警備の強化によって改善しつつありということだ。
Meaning: I hear that the city’s public safety, which had been worsening year by year, is gradually improving thanks to strengthened security measures.
default.q.n2-39-q49-49.why.0: (a) 改善しつつ: It occupies the third position (★) and combines with「あり」in the fourth position to form the grammar structure「V-masu (remove masu) + つつある/つつあり」(gradually changing or tending to change).
default.q.n2-39-q49-49.why.1: (b) 警備の強化に: It is in the first position, a noun phrase with the particle 「に」, which combines with 「よって」 in the following position.
default.q.n2-39-q49-49.why.2: (c) あり: This is the continuative form of 「ある」, completing 「改善しつつあり」before the indirect-information expression 「ということだ」(it is said that...).
default.q.n2-39-q49-49.why.3: (d) よって: This is in the second position and combines with 「警備の強化に」to form the grammar structure 「〜によって」, indicating a cause or means (“through / due to...”).
default.q.n2-39-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 3. べきだ (should or must do something according to ordinary standards of conduct or morality).
default.q.n2-39-q50-50.explanation: The passage begins by mentioning the familiar proverb “When in Rome, do as the Romans do” (郷に入っては郷に従え), and then gives a principle of social conduct: when visiting another region or country, people should follow the rules and customs there. The structure 「V-る + べきだ」means that one should or ought to do something as a matter of common sense, proper conduct, or moral standard, so it fits the author's opinion perfectly.
default.q.n2-39-q50-50.why.0: (a) Inappropriate: 「〜しかない」 means “there is no choice but to...” and carries a negative or reluctant nuance. It is unsuitable for expressing general travel advice or a rule of conduct.
default.q.n2-39-q50-50.why.1: (b) Not appropriate: 「〜ことになっている」 expresses a rule, regulation, or established custom (“it is مقرر by rule that...”), and is generally used for specific regulations of an organization or place rather than the author’s opinion-based advice.
default.q.n2-39-q50-50.why.2: (c) Appropriate: 「〜べきだ」 (V-る + べきだ) expresses the opinion that one should or must do something according to moral principles or social standards. After introducing the proverb "When in Rome, do as the Romans do," the author states that following the customs and rules of the place one visits is naturally the right thing to do.
default.q.n2-39-q50-50.why.3: (d) Inappropriate: 「〜まい」 is a formal negative form meaning “probably not” (negative conjecture) or “will not; shall not” (negative volition), giving the sentence a meaning completely contrary to the flow of the passage.
default.q.n2-39-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 2. たとえ (combined with 〜であっても to form a concessive conditional pattern meaning “even if...” or “no matter how...”).
default.q.n2-39-q51-51.explanation: The structure in the following clause, 「〜であっても」(even if it is...), indicates that the paired adverb completing the pattern is 「たとえ〜ても / であっても」(even if..., no matter whether...). The sentence emphasizes that even if it is only a short trip, following the rules and cultural etiquette of the destination is still essential.
default.q.n2-39-q51-51.why.0: (a) Not appropriate: 「おもに」（主に）is an adverb meaning “mainly” or “for the most part,” referring to the core component. It does not combine with the concessive hypothetical ending 「〜であっても」.
default.q.n2-39-q51-51.why.1: (b) Appropriate: 「たとえ」 is an adverb used with the grammar pattern 「たとえ〜ても / であっても」, meaning “even if / no matter how.” It emphasizes that even for a short trip, maintaining proper manners is still important.
default.q.n2-39-q51-51.why.2: (c) Inappropriate: 「しきりに」 is an adverb meaning “repeatedly, incessantly, persistently” (for example, rain falling heavily or someone repeatedly inviting others). It does not fit the context or grammar at all.
default.q.n2-39-q51-51.why.3: (d) Inappropriate: 「いわば」is an adverb meaning “in other words,” “so to speak,” or “one might say,” used for analogy or rephrasing. It does not pair with the concessive clause 「〜であっても」.
default.q.n2-39-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 3. マナーを無視する (to ignore or disregard rules of etiquette).
default.q.n2-39-q52-52.explanation: The pattern 「〜からといって、〜（てはいけない／のはよくない）」 is used to criticize or warn against improper behavior based on a certain excuse (“You cannot say that just because..., it is acceptable to...” ). The author criticizes the careless attitude of some travelers, emphasizing that they cannot use the excuse “This is not my country” to ignore or disregard the rules and social etiquette of the country they are visiting.
default.q.n2-39-q52-52.why.0: (a) Not appropriate: 「文化を育てる」 means "to build or nurture a culture," a long-term action undertaken by an entire community. It does not fit the context of an individual tourist's behavior.
default.q.n2-39-q52-52.why.1: (b) Inappropriate: 「文化に慣れる」 means “to become accustomed to/adapt to a culture.” If inserted into the clause “because it is not one’s own country, becoming accustomed to the culture is not good,” it completely distorts the logic of the passage.
default.q.n2-39-q52-52.why.2: (c) Appropriate: 「マナーを無視する」 means 'to ignore or disregard proper etiquette.' Combined with 「〜からといって、〜のはよくない」 (It is not right to do X just because...), the complete sentence is: 'Just because it is not one's own country, one should not disregard that country's rules of etiquette.'
default.q.n2-39-q52-52.why.3: (d) Not appropriate: 「マナーを守る」means "follow proper etiquette." Combined with the critical ending 「〜のはよくない」, it would mean "following proper etiquette is bad," which contradicts the message of the passage.
default.q.n2-39-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 1. しかし (however / but—a conjunction indicating contrast and a shift in the argument).
default.q.n2-39-q53-53.explanation: The conjunction 「しかし」 serves as a contrastive transition in the argument. After mentioning that travelers may feel unfamiliar with the rules or find them bothersome, the author uses “However” to reaffirm the true nature of these rules: they are not intended to make things difficult, but are civilized and reasonable solutions that allow everyone to live together comfortably.
default.q.n2-39-q53-53.why.0: (a) Appropriate. 「しかし」 (“however”) connects two clauses with contrasting meanings. The passage first says that rules can feel restrictive; “however” then shifts to explain that the true nature of rules of conduct is highly reasonable and useful.
default.q.n2-39-q53-53.why.1: (b) Not appropriate. 「そのため」 expresses a cause-and-effect result (“for that reason...”), so it is not used when the following sentence presents an opposing point or examines the fundamental nature of the issue more deeply.
default.q.n2-39-q53-53.why.2: (c) Not suitable: 「また」 indicates addition or the listing of further information in the same direction (“also,” “moreover”); it does not express the contrastive transition needed here.
default.q.n2-39-q53-53.why.3: (d) Inappropriate: 「なぜなら」 is used to explain a reason (“because...”) and is usually followed by 「〜からだ」. It does not fit the shift in reasoning required at this position.
default.q.n2-39-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 快く感じられる (to feel pleasant, comfortable, or naturally satisfying).
default.q.n2-39-q54-54.explanation: The phrase 「むしろ〜ようになる」 (“instead, gradually come to...”) signals a positive and somewhat unexpected result. At first, following new rules may feel restrictive, but once travelers understand and become accustomed to them, they come to feel that living or traveling abroad is extremely comfortable and pleasant (快く感じられる), thanks to the order and civility those rules create.
default.q.n2-39-q54-54.why.0: (a) Inappropriate: 「嫌な気分にさせられる」means "to be made uncomfortable / irritated," which contradicts the positive result the author predicts after adapting to the culture.
default.q.n2-39-q54-54.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「ダメと言われる」 means “to be refused” or “to be told that something is forbidden,” which does not fit the context of having come to understand and adapt to the place.
default.q.n2-39-q54-54.why.2: (c) Inappropriate: 「嬉しくさせられる」 (the causative-passive form of 嬉しい) carries the forced nuance of “being made to feel happy,” which is unnatural for describing an inner sense of comfort while adapting to an environment.
default.q.n2-39-q54-54.why.3: (d) Appropriate: 「快く感じられる」 consists of the -i adjective 快い changing into the adverb 快く, followed by the spontaneous-potential expression 感じられる, meaning "to naturally feel comfortable or pleasant." Together with the adverb 「むしろ」 (rather, on the contrary), the sentence means that once you become accustomed to those rules, being abroad may actually feel more comfortable and pleasant.
default.q.n2-39-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: 「禁止されていることを、人がするから自分も」という言い訳は通らない。
default.q.n2-39-q55-55.explanation:
- Main idea and basis: The passage criticizes the fact that many people ignore prohibitory signs in public places (no littering, no smoking, no parking, no photography) and strongly condemns the excuse of following the crowd: “If other people do it, I can do it too.”

- Question translation:
What does the author most want to say?

- Answer choices:
1. For Japanese people, public places are places where they can do anything freely without worrying about others.
2. The Japanese expression “Do not do it (suruna)” means “Everyone except oneself must not do it.”
3. For prohibited actions, the excuse “I did it because other people were doing it” is unacceptable.
4. Japanese expressions have meanings beyond their literal meanings, so they are easily misunderstood by foreigners.
default.q.n2-39-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author mentions violations in public places in order to criticize them; the author does not claim that public places are places where people may do anything freely without considering others.
default.q.n2-39-q55-55.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the question 「『するな』ということは…『自分だけならしてもいい』という意味なのだろうか」 is merely a rhetorical, sarcastic question, not the actual definition of the word.
default.q.n2-39-q55-55.why.2: (c) Correct, because the author uses a rhetorical question at the end to reject the fallacy of following the crowd: 「あるいは、『人がするから、自分もする』という言い訳をする人たちは、人が死ぬと言えば自分も死ぬのだろうか。」 (Would they also die just because someone else dies? This shows that the excuse “Others are doing it, so I will too” is completely illogical.)
default.q.n2-39-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the reference to foreigners (「外国人に日本語を教える際には、そういう意味があると注釈をつけなければいけない」) is merely a sarcastic comment on how Japanese people ignore prohibition signs; it is not about Japanese being misunderstood.
default.q.n2-39-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 子供に対して期待しすぎず、縛りつけないようにすること (Not expecting too much from one's children and not restricting or binding them).
default.q.n2-39-q56-56.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage discusses the increasing number of students who do not want to attend school or who stop attending. The author emphasizes that what these students truly need is "a change in their parents' attitudes" (親の意識の改革)—specifically, for parents to stop placing excessive expectations on them and release them from pressure and restraint (過度の期待をやめ、束縛から解いてやる). Then the students will naturally return to school.

- Question translation:
  「親の意識の改革」 (a change in the parents' attitudes) means what here?

- Answer choices:
  1. Encourage educators and psychologists to develop solutions as soon as possible.
  2. Not place excessive expectations on one's children or pressure and restrain them.
  3. Urge teachers working in schools even more strongly to develop measures.
  4. Become even stricter with one's children.
default.q.n2-39-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage only states that education and psychology researchers have not yet presented a specific solution (教育学者や心理者も具体的な解決策を明示するに至っていない). It does not mention parents needing to influence or urge them to find one.
default.q.n2-39-q56-56.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because immediately after raising the issue of changing parents' attitudes, the author explains: 「過度の期待をやめ、束縛から解いてやると、彼らは自然と学校に戻っていくのである」 (If excessive expectations are abandoned and the children are released from restrictions, they will naturally return to school.) This directly corresponds to “not expecting too much from one's child and not restraining them.”
default.q.n2-39-q56-56.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage only states that few teachers directly handling classes are addressing this issue (現場ではまだまだ少ない); it does not say that parents believe teachers should be urged to develop countermeasures.
default.q.n2-39-q56-56.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author recommends reducing expectations and letting go of restrictions, which is the complete opposite of treating one’s child more strictly (子供に対してもっと厳しくすること).
default.q.n2-39-q57-57.verdict: The provided answer is 3 (はたして); however, the grammatically and semantically correct answer in connection with the negative ending「〜とは思わない」is 2 (一概に).
default.q.n2-39-q57-57.explanation:
■ Summary of the passage's main point:
The passage discusses curiosity and attitudes toward acknowledging what one does not know. The author argues that clearly suppressing one's curiosity, being unable to honestly say “I don't know,” and feeling ashamed of it are evidence that a sense of self has developed. Therefore, it cannot simply be dismissed as something bad (一概にそれをわるいことだとは思わない). However, suppressing the desire to learn in order to pretend to know (知ったかぶり) is a major drawback in life, because the brain still has plenty of room to absorb information, and suppressing curiosity is by no means wise (決して賢明なことではない).

■ Translation of the question and answer choices:
Question: Which word best fits in position ( ★ )?
1. 多かれ少なかれ: to some extent / whether more or less
2. 一概に: categorically / without qualification (with a negative expression: not necessarily / cannot be dismissed outright)
3. はたして: I wonder whether / indeed (often used with a rhetorical question: はたして〜だろうか)
4. 必ず: certainly / without fail
default.q.n2-39-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「多かれ少なかれ」(to some extent, whether a little or a lot) is an adverb expressing a relative degree in an affirmative sentence, such as 多かれ少なかれ影響がある. It does not combine with the partial negative ending 「〜とは思わない」.
default.q.n2-39-q57-57.why.1: (b) Correct in terms of grammar and context. The pattern 「一概に〜とは思わない / 一概に〜とは言えない」 (not necessarily / cannot categorically say that...) fits the preceding explanation of the reason: 「それだけ自我意識が確立したということにほかならないのだから、（一概に）、それをわるいことだ、とは思わない」 (Since it simply means that one's sense of self has become established, I do not think it can categorically be considered a bad thing).
default.q.n2-39-q57-57.why.2: (c) According to the provided answer key, the answer is 3 (はたして - I wonder whether / indeed). However,「はたして」usually accompanies an interrogative or speculative ending such as「〜だろうか / 〜か」, rather than directly preceding the negative declarative expression「〜とは思わない」to state an opinion.
default.q.n2-39-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「必ず」 means “definitely” and expresses absolute certainty. To express “not necessarily,” use 「必ずしも〜ない / 必ずしも〜とは思わない」.
default.q.n2-39-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4 (世の中には特別な記᠈力を持つ人がいて驚かされる), rather than the provided answer 1.
default.q.n2-39-q58-58.explanation:
- Main point: The passage introduces people with extraordinary memories, such as remembering long strings of numbers for their entire lives and reading and memorizing a book written in a foreign language they have never studied, even backward from the final word. The author states that one in every 5,000 people has a photographic memory and expresses amazement and admiration at this exceptional ability. Therefore, the main point is that there are people in the world with extraordinary memories that amaze us (choice 4).

- Translation of the question:
What is the main point this passage is trying to make?

- Translation of the choices:
1. Remembering something forever means having a good memory.
2. The ability to instantly remember everything one has seen is unbelievable.
3. One in every 5,000 people can remember strings of numbers or books.
4. There are people in the world who possess extraordinary memories that amaze us.
default.q.n2-39-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not define what constitutes “good memory” (記᠈力がいい); it only gives examples of people with extraordinary memories.
default.q.n2-39-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author uses the phrase "信じられないような話だが" (although it sounds unbelievable) and then confirms that this ability actually exists in 1 out of 5,000 people. The author is not saying that the ability is impossible or unreal.
default.q.n2-39-q58-58.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the figure 「5,000 人に 1 人」is merely a supporting detail, not the main message or theme the author wants to convey (一番言いたいこと).
default.q.n2-39-q58-58.why.3: (d) Correct. The concluding sentence states: 「彼らは物を見てそれを永久に覚えていられる、い山ゆる写真のような記᠈力を持っているのである。驚くばかりである。」 The entire article introduces extraordinary cases of memory and ends by expressing amazement at people with such exceptional memories.
default.q.n2-39-q59-59.verdict: The given answer is 4; however, based on the passage, the correct and most accurate answer is 3 (寝そべってテレビなどを見ること), because the author explains it as lying sprawled out on a tatami mat and watching television.
default.q.n2-39-q59-59.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage explains the term 「ゴロ寝」 (sprawling or lying around) and the newly derived term 「テ式寝」 (a television-watching posture). The author describes an office worker lying stretched out on a tatami mat on Sunday, propping himself up on one elbow to watch television—a symbol of ordinary Japanese leisure. Propping up one elbow is merely the minimum effort required to adopt a posture oriented toward society (watching television), rather than simply lying on one's back and staring at the ceiling.
- Question translation: What does 「ゴロ寝」 mean?
- Answer choices:
  1. A new term derived from Te-shiki-ne.
  2. Something an office worker does on Sunday.
  3. Lying sprawled out while watching television,...
  4. Propping oneself up on one elbow.
default.q.n2-39-q59-59.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is incorrect because the text says 「そこから来たテ式寝という新語もある」 (“there is also a new word, テ式寝, derived from that”). Thus, テ式寝 is the new word derived from ゴロ寝, not the other way around.
default.q.n2-39-q59-59.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage gives the image of 「サラリーマンが日曜日に、畳の上にごろりと寝そべり...」 as a typical example. ゴロ寝 does not mean everything that salaried workers do on Sundays.
default.q.n2-39-q59-59.why.2: (c) Choice 3 accurately reflects the explanation: 「要するに、サラリーマンが日曜日に、畳の上にごろりと寝そべり、片ひじついてテレビなどを見ている図である」 (In short, it depicts an office worker lying sprawled out on a tatami mat on Sunday, propping himself up on one elbow and watching television.)
default.q.n2-39-q59-59.why.3: (d) Choice 4, as given in the answer key, does not match the definition. The sentence 「テレビ視聴という最低限の対社会的姿勢のためには、せめて片ひじつくくらいの努力は要るのである」 indicates that propping oneself up on one elbow is merely the minimum effort required to watch television while lying down; the act itself is not 「ゴロ寝」.
default.q.n2-39-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The child considers people with large bodies to be adults, but does not consider small people to be adults.
default.q.n2-39-q60-60.explanation:
**Main point:**
When the six-year-old child says to his mother,「お母さん、もう少し大人になりな、お父さんくらいに」(Mom, become a little more grown-up—about as grown-up as Dad), she asks what he means. The child hugs her and explains:「ほら、お母さんこんなに小さいよ。もっと大人になってお父さんくらい大きくなって！」(Look, Mom, you're this small. Become more grown-up and get as big as Dad!). The mother realizes that the child was talking about body size (体の大きさのことだったんだ). In the child's innocent understanding, being an adult means having a large body like his father's, while someone small is not an adult.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** How does this child understand or define an "adult"?
- 1. Someone who has children is an adult; someone without children is not.
- 2. Someone who has grandchildren is an adult; someone without grandchildren is not.
- 3. Children will inevitably become adults, but some adults are small.
- 4. Someone with a large body is an adult; someone small is not.
default.q.n2-39-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not mention whether or not the child has children as a way to identify the adult.
default.q.n2-39-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the child does not define an adult based on whether or not the person has grandchildren.
default.q.n2-39-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the idea that “some adults are small too” was expressed by the mother (「大人だって小さい人はいるよ」), while the child thought that she had once been large but had now shrunk.
default.q.n2-39-q60-60.why.3: (d) Correct. When the child hugs the mother and says, 「ほら、お母注んこんなに小さいよ。もっと大人になってお父注ん くらい大きくなって！」, the mother realizes, 「なーんだ体の大きさのことだたんだ」. This shows that, to the child, an adult is someone with a large build like the father.
default.q.n2-39-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The author thinks that he needs to cherish and love his aging, physically frail grandmother.
default.q.n2-39-q61-61.explanation:
**Main point:**
When the mother objects that adults can also be small, like a grandmother (おばあちゃん), the innocent child explains:「あのね、おばあちゃんはぼくが生まれる前、大人だったんだよ。でもね、今はおばあちゃんになって縮んだの」(You know, Grandma was an adult before I was born. But now she has become a grandmother and shrunk.) After hearing this, the mother says「うーんなるほど」(Oh, I see) and realizes that from now on she should love and cherish her elderly grandmother (「次はお消あ活ゃんを大切にしなければと考え注せられた」).

**Translation of the question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** When the expression “Oh, I see” was used, what did the author think?
- 1. She thought she should cherish and care for her elderly grandmother, who had become small again.
- 2. She thought her son could now speak like an adult.
- 3. She thought she herself should become more mature and adult-like.
- 4. She thought her husband was older than she was.
default.q.n2-39-q61-61.why.0: (a) Correct because it directly quotes the author's thoughts immediately after the exclamation:「うーんなるほど。初めは『大人になりな』なんてと言われて反省し、次はお消あ活ゃんを大切にしなければと考え注せられた」.
default.q.n2-39-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the child merely gave a naïve, childish explanation; the author never thought that the child had learned to converse like an adult.
default.q.n2-39-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect because wanting to become a better adult through self-reflection (反省) was the initial thought that arose when the author first heard the child speak, not what the author reflected on when saying 「うーんなるほど」 after the story about the grandmother.
default.q.n2-39-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect, because seeing her husband as mature or more grown-up is the author’s thought at the beginning of the passage, not what the author thinks when saying「うーんなるほど」.
default.q.n2-39-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The child’s words made the mother reflect on many things.
default.q.n2-39-q62-62.explanation:
**Main point:**
On the way to taking her child to preschool, the mother's innocent remarks—“Mom, become a grown-up as big as Dad” and “Grandma has gotten smaller because she has grown old”—make the mother reflect on and examine herself (反省し) and think that she must value the grandmother (大切にしなければと考えさせられた). Because the child's words make the mother reflect on many profound matters, the child appears more mature and grown-up than usual as the mother watches the child walk through the school gate.

**Translation of the question and choices:**
- **Question:** Why does the sentence “The child's back looked more mature than usual” describe the child that way?
- 1. Because the child's words made the author reflect on many things.
- 2. Because the child walked alone while waving.
- 3. Because, although still a child, the child spoke like an adult.
- 4. Because the child was worried about the grandmother.
default.q.n2-39-q62-62.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage points to two things the author reflects on after hearing the child’s words: 「初めは『大人になりな』なんてと言われて反省し、次はお消あ活ゃんを大切にしなければと考え注せられた」. These reflections make the child’s back appear more mature.
default.q.n2-39-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect because waving goodbye while passing through the school gate is an everyday action when taking a child to kindergarten, not the reason the author feels that the child has become more mature.
default.q.n2-39-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the child speaks very naively, understanding body size in a preschooler’s way, rather than speaking like an adult.
default.q.n2-39-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the child is simply explaining things innocently according to their own way of thinking, not worrying about their grandmother.
default.q.n2-39-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「表さなければならない」.
default.q.n2-39-q63-63.explanation:
Summary: The author emphasizes that when speaking, using abstract words makes it difficult for the other person to understand; therefore, what one wants to say must always be expressed concretely (言いたいことは常に具体的に[表さなければならない]).
- Question: What is expected to follow 「言いたいことは常に具体的に」(What one wants to say must always be...)?
- Choices:
1. There is no need to say it.
2. It must be expressed (concretely).
3. One may remember it.
4. It may become understandable.
default.q.n2-39-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author advises expressing an opinion specifically, rather than saying that it does not need to be expressed (「話さなくてもいい」).
default.q.n2-39-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「抽象的な表現をしても、相手には何のことかピンと来ないことが多いはずです。言いたいことは常に具体的に。これが大切です。」 The preceding sentence says that abstract expressions often fail to convey the meaning, so what one wants to say must always be expressed concretely ("表さなければならない").
default.q.n2-39-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「思い出すかもしれない」 (“might remember”) does not fit the context, which concerns how to express the intended message.
default.q.n2-39-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「わかるようになるだろう」 does not express the speaker's action or obligation to communicate, as required by the context (「これが大切です」).
default.q.n2-39-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「その国の話題について自分は興味があるから」.
default.q.n2-39-q64-64.explanation:
Summary: When someone mentions a person you know or a place you have visited, you become drawn into the conversation because you are interested and want to ask questions or hear more.
- Question: Why do you 「聞き返したくなる」(want to ask again or hear more)?
- Choices:
1. Because the other person is not interested in what you are saying.
2. Because you are interested in the topic or place being discussed.
3. Because you yourself are not very interested in the story.
4. Because you are also uninterested in a topic that the other person is not interested in.
default.q.n2-39-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage assumes that someone is talking to the speaker, and the desire to ask a follow-up question comes from the speaker’s interest, not from the other person’s lack of interest in what the speaker said.
default.q.n2-39-q64-64.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「このとき、あなたが知っている人の名前や、行ったことがある土地の名前が出てくると、思わず話に引き込まれる（注：話に興味を感じて聞く）ことがあるはずです。聞き返したくなるかもしれません。」 When a story mentions a place one has visited, it naturally creates interest and makes one want to keep listening or ask further questions.
default.q.n2-39-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage explains that “being drawn into the story” means taking an interest in it (「話に興味を感じて聞く」), which is the complete opposite of not being interested (「あまり関心がない」).
default.q.n2-39-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the reason for asking a follow-up question is that the topic has sparked the speaker’s own interest, not because neither side is interested.
default.q.n2-39-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 「会話の相手が話したいと思わなければ、会話はできない。」.
default.q.n2-39-q65-65.explanation:
Summary: A conversation is only truly established when the listener interacts and participates. Therefore, the speaker needs to use specific examples or familiar proper nouns to draw the other person into the conversation.
- Question: What does the sentence 「会話は相手が参加してくれてこそ成立します」(A conversation is only possible when the other person participates) mean?
- Choices:
1. If the other person does not want to talk, the conversation cannot take place.
2. If the other person is someone close to you, they will be drawn into the topic and be able to converse.
3. If you keep changing the way you speak according to the other person, you cannot have a conversation.
4. The other person can participate in a conversation even without a specific example.
default.q.n2-39-q65-65.why.0: (a) Correct. The grammar 「〜てこそ」 means that a conversation can only be established when the other person also participates, corresponding to the idea that if the other person does not want to talk, a conversation cannot take place (「会話の相手が話したいと思わなければ、会話はできない」).
default.q.n2-39-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect because at the beginning of the passage, the author clearly states that even people close to you (身近な人) will not understand if you speak abstractly; being close does not automatically make them engaged.
default.q.n2-39-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage recommends choosing ways of speaking and materials that attract the other person; it does not say that changing one's speech to suit the other person makes conversation impossible.
default.q.n2-39-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author clearly states that a concrete example is necessary material for drawing the other person into the topic: 「相手を話題に引き込む材料が必要です。それが、具体例なのです。」 This is the opposite of “concrete examples are unnecessary.”
default.q.n2-39-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 3. さらに (furthermore, in addition).
default.q.n2-39-q66-66.explanation:
Summary of the passage: The previous passage gave the example that only 18% of young people independently decide which company to join, while most follow their parents' or friends' advice. The next passage adds an even more surprising fact: only 29% choose their romantic partner themselves.

Question translation: Which word is most appropriate for （ ★ ）?
Answer choices:
1. 実は: actually
2. では: then
3. さらに: furthermore / in addition
4. ただし: however / with one exception
default.q.n2-39-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「実は」 (actually, in fact) is used to reveal an unexpected truth or clarify the real nature of something mentioned earlier. It is not suitable for adding a higher degree of surprise to the survey results discussed in the previous paragraph.
default.q.n2-39-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「では」 (“then,” “in that case”) is a conjunction used to change the topic or draw a conclusion based on the preceding premise; it does not express an increasing degree of surprise.
default.q.n2-39-q66-66.why.2: (c) Correct, because the author first presents the survey result that only 18% of people independently chose the company they would work for, and then adds an even more surprising statistic: 「（さらに）驚きなのは「恋人」を「自分で選ぶ」若者が、山ずか 29 パーセントであること」 (What is even more surprising is that only 29% of young people "choose their romantic partner themselves"). The conjunction 「さらに」 combined with 「驚きなのは」 naturally introduces information with an increased level of surprise.
default.q.n2-39-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「ただし」 (however, with the exception that) adds a condition, limitation, or exception to the preceding statement. It does not fit the additive relationship between the information here.
default.q.n2-39-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 恋人も結婚相手も自分で決めない人が多い (Many people do not decide for themselves either who to date or whom to marry).
default.q.n2-39-q67-67.explanation:
Summary: According to the survey data, only 29% of young people choose their romantic partners themselves; the largest group, 40%, simply leave it to “whatever happens.” Even fewer decide for themselves whom to marry—only 22%, while the rest follow their mother’s or friends’ opinions. Thus, for both romantic partners and marriage partners, most people do not make the decision themselves.

Question: According to the survey in this passage, how do young people decide on their romantic partners and marriage partners?
Answer choices:
1. Many people decide for themselves both their romantic partners and their marriage partners.
2. Many people do not decide for themselves either their romantic partners or their marriage partners.
3. Many people decide on their romantic partners themselves, but many ask others for advice before deciding on their marriage partners.
4. Many people ask others for advice before deciding on their romantic partners, but many decide on their marriage partners themselves.
default.q.n2-39-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that only 29% decide for themselves whom to date and only 22% decide for themselves whom to marry. Therefore, most young people do not decide for themselves; it is not true that many do.
default.q.n2-39-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct. According to the survey results in the passage, only 29% chose their own romantic partner (「『恋人』を『自分で選ぶ』若者が、山ずか 29 パーセントであること。『なるようになる』が 4 割で一番多い」), while an even smaller percentage—only 22%—decided for themselves whether to marry their current partner (「『今つきあっている恋人と結婚するかどうか』を『自分で決める』若者は注らに少ない（ 22 パーセント）」). In other words, most young people do not decide entirely for themselves either whom to date or whom to marry.
default.q.n2-39-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect because only 29% of people choose their romantic partners themselves—a minority, not “many people”—while the majority choose “whatever happens, happens” (40%).
default.q.n2-39-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect because only 22% decide their marriage partner themselves, a very small proportion; about 20% follow their mother and about 20% follow their friends. It is not true that many people choose their marriage partner independently.
default.q.n2-39-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 人生で大切なことも人生で決定しないで、あまり悩みを持たないこと (Not making your own decisions even about important matters in life, and not having many worries or concerns).
default.q.n2-39-q68-68.explanation:
Summary: The author argues that people usually feel troubled when faced with important choices. However, young people today do not choose their own careers or marriages—two major events in life—so they experience neither serious 고민 nor inner conflict. The author wonders whether living this way means living one's own life, yet 「それ」—not deciding important matters for oneself and having no serious 고민—is taken for granted among young people today.

Question translation: What does 「それ」 refer to?

Answer choices:
1. Not deciding even important matters in one's life for oneself and not having much 고민 or distress.
2. When making decisions in life, carefully considering what happiness means to oneself.
3. Actually harboring doubts about having no 고민 or inner conflict in life.
4. Trying to decide the most important matters in life according to one's own will without asking others.
default.q.n2-39-q68-68.why.0: (a) Correct because the preceding paragraphs point out that young people do not choose major life events such as employment or marriage for themselves, so they do not experience much inner conflict: 「これでは、悩みが生じないのも当然である。就職と結婚は、人生の二大イ登ェント。よい配偶者に恵まれて、自分を生かせるなら、確かに大した悩みも葛藤も生まれてこないだろう。しかしそれで果たして、自分の人生を生きていると言えるだろうか。けれど、それが今の若者の『当たり前』なのである。」 Therefore, 「それ」 refers to the entire situation: not deciding important matters in one’s own life and living without much distress or uncertainty.
default.q.n2-39-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the article criticizes young people for refusing to think or choose for themselves (「選ぼうとしていない。選ぶ意志がない」), which is completely contrary to “carefully considering what brings happiness to oneself.”
default.q.n2-39-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the person questioning this way of life is the author (「しかしそれで果たして、自分の人生を生きていると言えるだろうか」). For young people, however, not worrying about it is "natural" (当たり前), and they do not question themselves.
default.q.n2-39-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage says that young people often follow their parents or friends, or leave matters to nature; it does not say that they “try to make decisions according to their own will without asking others.”
default.q.n2-39-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 小学生に英語を学ばせること (having elementary school students learn English).
default.q.n2-39-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: Both passages A and B focus on "having elementary school students learn English" (小学生に英語を学ばせること). The author of passage A opposes it, arguing that learning English in elementary school is ineffective and interferes with learning Japanese and mathematics. The author of passage B supports it, arguing that elementary school students’ psychological and developmental characteristics are highly suitable for developing English communication skills (CC).
- Question translation: What common topic do passages A and B address?
- Answer choices:
  1. Effective methods for teaching English to elementary school students.
  2. Having elementary school students learn English.
  3. Effective methods for teaching English to junior high school students.
  4. The importance of English education after entering junior high school.
default.q.n2-39-q69-69.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inaccurate because the author of Passage A completely opposes teaching English to elementary school students; the passage does not discuss an "effective method" (効果的な方法) for teaching English to them.
default.q.n2-39-q69-69.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is correct. The evidence is as follows: Passage A begins and continues by discussing the teaching of English in elementary schools: 「そもそも小学校で英語をニ、三時間勉強しても何の足しにもなりません」 (To begin with, studying English for two or three hours at elementary school is of no benefit). Passage B also focuses on teaching English to children of this age: 「実際のところは「恥ずかしい」「面倒くさい」という気持ちの少ない小学生の方が CC 育成に向いている面がたくさんあります」 (In fact, elementary school students, who are less likely to feel embarrassed or bothered, are well suited to developing communication skills in many ways). Both passages discuss the same topic: “having elementary school students study English.”
default.q.n2-39-q69-69.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the focus of both passages is elementary school (小学校/小学生), not teaching methods for middle school students (中学生).
default.q.n2-39-q69-69.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because neither passage discusses the importance of studying English after entering middle school (中学生になってから英語教育の重要性); both focus on elementary school.
default.q.n2-39-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 4: A は反対、 B は賛成 (A is opposed, B is in favor).
default.q.n2-39-q70-70.explanation:
- Main points:
  + Passage A argues against it (反対): The author says that studying for two or three hours in elementary school is useless, while studying for ten hours causes students to neglect Japanese and mathematics, weakening both their language and thinking abilities (both Japanese and English reach only 50%).
  + Passage B supports it (賛成): The author believes elementary school students are less self-conscious and enjoy pronunciation and physical movement, making them well suited to developing English communication skills (CC).
- Question translation: Regarding English classes in elementary schools, which statement about A and B is correct?
- Answer choices:
  1. Both A and B support it.
  2. Both A and B oppose it.
  3. A supports it, while B opposes it.
  4. A opposes it, while B supports it.
default.q.n2-39-q70-70.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inaccurate because Author A opposes teaching English in elementary schools out of concern that it would distract students from Japanese language and mathematics.
default.q.n2-39-q70-70.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because Author B supports teaching English in elementary school, as this age is particularly suitable for developing communication skills.
default.q.n2-39-q70-70.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the positions are reversed: A is opposed, while B is in agreement.
default.q.n2-39-q70-70.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct. Author A objects because 「そもそも小学校で英語をニ、三時間勉強しても何の足しにもなりません」「英語より遥かに重要な国語や算数がおろそかになります」(Studying English for two or three hours in elementary school is of no benefit; it would cause students to neglect Japanese and mathematics, which are far more important than English). Author B supports it because 「小学生の方が CC 育成に向いている面がたくさんあります。例えば、声を出したり、身体を動かしたりするのはまさに小学生の得意とする活動です」(Elementary school students are well suited to developing CC in many ways. For example, speaking aloud and moving their bodies are activities at which they excel).
default.q.n2-39-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Temporarily refraining from using it when approaching the passage.
default.q.n2-39-q71-71.explanation:
• Relevant main point: The author argues that readers need to understand various forms of knowledge and different perspectives on issues, but when approaching a text, they should "temporarily set that knowledge aside" (いったん脇に置いて) in order to eliminate personal preconceptions and understand the true substance of the text more deeply.
• Question translation: What does "temporarily set aside" mean?
• Answer choices:
1. To temporarily refrain from using it.
2. To forget it so that it does not interfere.
3. To remember it thoroughly so that it can be used immediately.
4. To write it down on paper and leave it on the desk.
default.q.n2-39-q71-71.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「そのことを具体的な知識として把握したうえで、その知識を いったん脇に置いて 、 先入観を排除して問題文に接する。」 The figurative expression 「脇に置く」 means to temporarily set something aside, or 「とりあえずは使わない」, so that it does not create bias while reading the passage.
default.q.n2-39-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This choice says 「忘れる」 (“forget”), whereas the author recommends mastering the knowledge and then temporarily setting it aside, not forgetting it completely.
default.q.n2-39-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect. This choice uses 「よく覚えておく」 (memorize carefully for immediate use), which is the opposite of “temporarily set aside.”
default.q.n2-39-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice interprets the expression literally and physically as 「紙に書いて机の上に出しておく」(write it on paper and leave it on the desk), whereas the passage uses a metaphor related to thinking.
default.q.n2-39-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 4: A deep understanding of the essence of the issue, rather than something formal or superficial.
default.q.n2-39-q72-72.explanation:
• Key point: According to the author, relying solely on formal logical thinking cannot lead to a substantive understanding of the content. A solid foundation of background knowledge is needed as a context for achieving deep understanding (表面的ではない、深い理解).
• Question translation: What kind of understanding is meant by “substantive understanding” (実のある理解)?
• Answer choices:
1. A more accurate and honest understanding.
2. An original understanding that differs from other people’s.
3. An understanding that matches one’s own thoughts.
4. A deep understanding that is not merely superficial.
default.q.n2-39-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The text does not discuss understanding something more accurately in a straightforward or literal sense; it emphasizes a deep understanding of the substance of the content, in contrast to purely formal logical thinking.
default.q.n2-39-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The text does not mention the need for a unique or unconventional interpretation (ユニークな理解).
default.q.n2-39-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not say that “understanding the essence” means an understanding that coincides with one’s personal view (自分の考えと一致した理解).
default.q.n2-39-q72-72.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「それによって、たんに形式的な論理的な思考力に頼るだけでは得られない、内容についての 実のある理解 ができるのではないか次ということです。」 The phrase 「実のある理解」 (substantial understanding) is contrasted with 「たんに形式的な論理的な思考力に頼るだけ」 (relying only on superficial formal logical thinking), making it equivalent to 「表面的ではない、深い理解」 (deep, non-superficial understanding).
default.q.n2-39-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Deepening one's comprehensive knowledge of society is important for improving reading comprehension.
default.q.n2-39-q73-73.explanation:
• Relevant main idea: The author emphasizes that the third factor in reading comprehension ability is background knowledge of a wide range of topics (politics, economics, society, science, art, contemporary society, and so on). Broadening one's general knowledge is essential for substantially improving reading comprehension.
• Question translation: Which opinion agrees with what the author wants to say about improving reading comprehension?
• Answer choices:
1. Logical thinking ability alone is sufficient.
2. Reading editorials and commentaries is good practice.
3. One should study using reference books for the Japanese language subject.
4. Deepening one's knowledge of society as a whole is important.
default.q.n2-39-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage states: 「現代国語の参考書の中には、論理的思考力さえあれば文章の内容についての知識は必要ないと言い切っているものもあります」, and the author rejects this view by asserting that background knowledge (背景知識) is indispensable. Therefore, the claim that "logical thinking alone is sufficient" directly contradicts the author.
default.q.n2-39-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage mentions 「新聞や雑誌の論説・評論」 only as examples of practical reading materials in social life that require reading comprehension; it does not say that reading them is a good practice method.
default.q.n2-39-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author mentions a Japanese-language reference book only to challenge the view that foundational knowledge can be disregarded; the author does not recommend using reference books for studying.
default.q.n2-39-q73-73.why.3: (d) Correct. The text states: 「読解力の第三のポイントは、文章の内容についての背景知識です。政治、経済、社会、科学、スポーツ、芸術など、文章のテーマそのものに関わる知識です。」 and 「現答社会を生きる私たちにとって『読解力』が問題になる場面で問われている背景知識は、一言で言ってしまうと、『近答』というものに対する理解につきます」. The author asserts that acquiring and broadening comprehensive social knowledge is a key factor in improving reading comprehension.
default.q.n2-39-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3 (3. F and G) because this person already has the necessary clothing and only needs to register for the yukata-wearing service (F) and hairstyling service (G).
default.q.n2-39-q74-74.explanation:
• Summary: The information table lists kimono/yukata rental packages (A through E) and additional services (F through H, including dressing, hairstyling and makeup, and photography). The customer already has a yukata, obi, and geta but cannot put them on alone, so they needs the dressing service (F: 着付けサービス). They also want a hairstyle that matches the outfit, so they need hairstyling (G: ヘア＆メイク). Therefore, the customer only needs packages F and G.
• Translation of the question: Which packages should the person who says, "I already have a yukata, obi, and geta, but I cannot put them on myself. I would also like to have my hair styled to match the outfit," register for?
• Translation of the answer choices:
1. Package F (Dressing service)
2. Packages E and F (Yukata rental + dressing)
3. Packages F and G (Dressing + hairstyling and makeup)
4. Packages E, F, and G (Yukata rental + dressing + hairstyling and makeup)
default.q.n2-39-q74-74.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because registering only for package F (着付けサービス) does not include hairstyling service G (ヘア＆メイク), so it does not satisfy the customer’s request: 「髪型も、着物にあうようにしてもらいたい」.
default.q.n2-39-q74-74.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because Plan E is for renting the full set of a yukata, obi, and geta ('浴衣、帯次はき物'), whereas the customer already owns these items ('浴衣、帯次げたは持っている'). It also omits hair styling service G.
default.q.n2-39-q74-74.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct. The customer already has a yukata, obi, and geta but cannot put them on unaided ('自分で着られない'), so she needs service F ('F 着付けサービス / 浴衣着付け 4,000 円'). She also wants her hair styled to match ('髪型も、着物にあうようにしてもらいたい'), so she needs service G ('G ヘア＆申イク'). Therefore, combining F and G is the most accurate choice.
default.q.n2-39-q74-74.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because package E is a costume-rental service ('浴衣、帯次はき物'), while the customer already has these items and therefore does not need to rent package E.
default.q.n2-39-q75-75.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2 (2.2,000円) because the yukata rental service fee, discounted by 50% under the shop’s special offer, is 2,000 yen.
default.q.n2-39-q75-75.explanation:
• Content summary: According to the supplementary service price list, the listed price for yukata dressing (浴衣着付け) is 4,000円. However, the shop offers a 50% discount (半額) on dressing fees for customers who rent a kimono or yukata there ('当店で着物を式ンタルした方は半額となります'). Therefore, Tanaka has to pay 4,000円 × 50% = 2,000円.
• Question translation: How much is the total cost in Tanaka's case?
• Answer choices:
1. 1,500 yen
2. 2,000 yen
3. 2,500 yen
4. 3,000 yen
default.q.n2-39-q75-75.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the price of 1,500円 does not correspond to any price or discount formula in the passage.
default.q.n2-39-q75-75.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct. In section F (“F 着付けサービス”), yukata dressing costs 4,000 yen (「浴衣着付け 4,000 円」), and the store offers half-price service under the stated condition (「当店で着物を式ンタルした方は半額となります。」). With a 50% discount, the amount due is 4,000 ÷ 2 = 2,000 円.
default.q.n2-39-q75-75.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because 2,500円 does not match the service-fee calculation after the charge for dressing has been reduced by half.
default.q.n2-39-q75-75.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because 3,000円 is the price after halving the cost of G’s hair and makeup service (6,000 ÷ 2 = 3,000円), or the renewal fee for Plan E. It is not the cost of Tanaka’s yukata.
default.q.n2-39-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 消した (forming the compound verb 「打ち消した」, meaning to deny or dismiss an idea).
default.q.n2-39-q11-11.explanation:

default.q.n2-4-q37-37.explanation:
Translation: That sport was originally created for the purpose of self-defense.

default.q.n2-4-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「〜とともに」 means “together with...” or “at the same time as...”; it does not combine with 「〜を目的」 to form a pattern expressing purpose.
default.q.n2-4-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「〜につれて」 means “as...” or “along with a change in A, B changes,” so it does not follow 「〜を目的」.
default.q.n2-4-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「〜にとって」 means “for” or “from the standpoint of N,” which does not fit the intended meaning.
default.q.n2-4-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「N1 を N2 として」(here, 「〜を目的として」) is a standard structure meaning “take N1 as N2” or “with N1 as the purpose”; 「身を守ることを目的として」 means “with the purpose of protecting oneself.”

Meaning: It is precisely because I care about your health that I will not let you drink alcohol.

• Vocabulary: 健康 (health), 酒 (alcohol, sake).

default.q.n2-4-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「〜くらい / ぐらい」 indicates a slight or minimum degree (“about / to the extent that ...”), so it is unsuitable for expressing a justified reason.
default.q.n2-4-q38-38.why.2: (c) “Plain form + からこそ” means “it is precisely because...” and emphasizes the fundamental reason behind the action of preventing someone from drinking alcohol.
default.q.n2-4-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「〜にかぎって」 means “only in the case of / just when ...,” often when something bad happens, so it does not fit the grammar or meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-4-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 3. えない.
default.q.n2-4-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: It is impossible for someone as kind as that to do something bad.
• Pattern: Vます (remove ます) + 得る (える/うる): can, be possible / Vます (remove ます) + 得ない (えない): cannot possibly (describes whether something can occur).
• Kanji: 悪: bad, evil.
• Example: 今回の事故は、人為的なミスとは考え得ない。(This accident cannot possibly be considered a human error.)

default.q.n2-4-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「Vます (remove ます) + 得ない (えない)」is a negative form meaning “it is impossible that...”; 「ありえない」means “that is impossible” or “there is no way that could happen.”
default.q.n2-4-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「うない」 is completely ungrammatical. When the verb 「得る (える/うる)」 is changed to the negative form, the only form is 「得ない (えない)」; 「うない」 does not exist.
default.q.n2-4-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 4. うれし注 (a display error for うれしさ).
default.q.n2-4-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: I shouted out because I was so extremely happy.
• Pattern: N の / V (dictionary form or past form) + あまり. With i-adjectives and na-adjectives, use a noun form such as 嬉しさ, 悲しさ, 緊張, or 驚き + のあまり: “because of being so...,” resulting in an unusual outcome or impulsive action.

• Sino-Japanese reading: 叫ぶ (shout, cry out).

default.q.n2-4-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「うれし」 is only the stem of an adjective and cannot stand alone with the particle 「の」 to form 「うれしの」.
default.q.n2-4-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「うれしい」is an i-adjective, so in its dictionary form it must directly precede あまり, as in「うれしいあまり」, and cannot be followed by「の」.
default.q.n2-4-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「うれしくて」 is the te-form of an i-adjective and cannot be combined with 「のあまり」.
default.q.n2-4-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「うれし注」 is a display/OCR error for 「うれしさ」, the noun form of うれしい. The structure 「N のあまり」 requires a noun expressing an emotion, so 「うれしさのあまり」 means “because of being so overjoyed.”
default.q.n2-4-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. あげく.
default.q.n2-4-q41-41.explanation:
Complete sentence meaning: After making us wait for hours, he finally said that he wanted to cancel today's meeting.
• Original sentence: 彼は何時間も私達を待たせた（あげく）、今日の打ち合わせは中止したいと言った。(The question contains an OCR line-break error, causing part of the sentence to appear among the answer choices.)
• Pattern: Vた / Nの + あげく(に): after a long period of...; eventually, resulting in an unfavorable outcome.
• Example: 散々迷ったあげく、何も買わずに店を出た。(After agonizing over it for a long time, I eventually left the store without buying anything.)
default.q.n2-4-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「〜きり」 means that after doing something, the state has remained unchanged ever since, or “only.” It is not used to indicate an unfortunate outcome after a process.
default.q.n2-4-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「〜一方で」means “on the one hand..., while on the other hand...,” describing two aspects occurring in parallel. It does not fit a connection expressing a negative result.
default.q.n2-4-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「〜反面」means “on the other hand” or “conversely,” and is used to present two contrasting characteristics of the same subject.
default.q.n2-4-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「Vた / Nの + あげく（に）」means "after a long period / after much... it ultimately leads to a bad or regrettable result." Here, after making everyone wait for hours, they ultimately ask to cancel the meeting.
default.q.n2-4-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. まい.
default.q.n2-4-q42-42.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “Someone as rude as that—I will never invite them again.”
• Structure: Vる (Group 1) / Vる・Vます-stem (Groups 2 and 3) + まい: “I definitely will not...” (negative volition in the first person) or “probably will not...” (negative conjecture). Often used with 「二度と〜まい」.
• Kanji readings and meanings: 失礼 (失 - rude, discourteous), 誘う (誘 - invite, ask someone to join).
• Example: こんなひどい対応をされたら、二度とこのホテルには泊まるまい。(After being treated this badly, I will never stay at this hotel again.)
default.q.n2-4-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「〜もんか / ものか」expresses strong negation in everyday spoken language (“absolutely not / as if...”), but when used with the adverb「二度と」to express a firm resolve to deny something at the N2 level, the standard structure is「二度と〜まい」.
default.q.n2-4-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「V(る) + まい」 (for Group 1 verbs: 誘う → 誘うまい) expresses the speaker's firm negative intention ("I will never do it again"). Combined with 「二度と」, it forms the classic pattern 「二度と〜まい」 (I will never invite someone again).
default.q.n2-4-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「〜こそ」is an emphatic particle (“precisely...,” “it is ... that...”), and is not used to create a volitional negative form at the end of a sentence.
default.q.n2-4-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「〜ことか」 combines with exclamatory words such as どんなに and どれほど to express an exclamation (“how...!”). It does not express a negative intention.
default.q.n2-4-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 向け.
default.q.n2-4-q43-43.explanation:
Meaning: 80% of the agricultural products exported from Country B to the Japanese market are fruit.
• Pattern: N + 向けに / 向けの N: intended for; targeted at (a deliberately selected audience, market, or purpose).
• Distinction: 向け indicates deliberate targeting of an audience or market, while 向き indicates that something is naturally suitable for a particular quality or preference.
• Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 輸出 (export), 農産物 (agricultural products), 果物 (fruit).
• Example: このアニメは大人向けに作られている。(This anime was made for adults.)
default.q.n2-4-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「〜向き」 means "suitable or appropriate for..." based on natural characteristics or preferences, as in 子供向き or 初心者向き; it is not used to indicate a market or export destination deliberately targeted by people.
default.q.n2-4-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「N + 向け（に/の）」means “intended for or targeted at N,” referring to a deliberately designed, produced, or exported product. 「日本向けに輸出される」means “exported for the Japanese market.”
default.q.n2-4-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「向かい」 is a noun indicating an opposite or facing location, as in 学校の向かい; it is not used after a country name to indicate an export destination.
default.q.n2-4-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「向こう」 is a noun meaning “the other side” or “over there,” and cannot directly follow a country name to form 「日本向こう」.

default.q.n2-4-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: I think it is not good for adults to keep telling children to study while not studying themselves.

• Vocabulary: 勉強 (study), 大人 (adult).
• Example: ダイエット中と言いつつ、甘いものをたくさん食べてしまった。(Although I said I was dieting, I ended up eating a lot of sweets.)
