default.q.n2-4-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「謝」is used in the verb 謝る（あやまる - to apologize, admit fault）, not as a noun meaning a mistake; writing the okurigana as「謝まり」is also incorrect.
default.q.n2-4-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「過」 has the noun 過ち（あやまち）, meaning “mistake” or “fault”; there is no word or spelling 「過まり」.
default.q.n2-4-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「誤り」（NGỘ）is read あやまり and is a noun meaning an error, mistake, or inaccuracy in a text, calculation, or information.
default.q.n2-4-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「間違」 is used in 間違い（まちがい, mistake）or 間違える（まちがえる, to make a mistake or confuse something）, not written as 「間違り」.
default.q.n2-40-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1: でき流こない (the correct form is できっこない - absolutely impossible to do).
default.q.n2-40-q33-33.explanation:
Meaning: “Lose as much as 5 kg in one week? There’s absolutely no way that can be done!”
• Grammar: Vます + っこない means “absolutely impossible” or “there’s no way...,” expressing the speaker’s strong subjective certainty that something will not happen.
• Example: こんな難しい問題、私には解けっこない。(There’s no way I could solve such a difficult problem.)
default.q.n2-40-q33-33.why.0: (a) Correct: The structure 「Vます + っこない」strongly asserts that something is absolutely impossible or could never happen (the question contains a printing error in which っ is printed as 流: できっこない).
default.q.n2-40-q33-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜に限る」 means “it is best to...” or “be limited to...”. It does not combine with the dictionary-form verb できる in this way and does not fit the context of an absolute negative statement.
default.q.n2-40-q33-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect: This is the wrong grammatical form. 「できかねる」 is used for a polite refusal in formal language; it is not used with the strongly rejecting tone of 「そんなこと...よ」 in casual conversation.
default.q.n2-40-q33-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「〜がたい」(difficult to...) commonly follows verbs of emotion, cognition, or psychology, such as 信じがたい, 許しがたい, and 想像しがたい; it does not combine with the potential form できる.
default.q.n2-40-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 努力することだ (you should make an effort).
default.q.n2-40-q34-34.explanation:
Meaning: “If you really want to succeed, you should work several times harder than other people.”
• Grammar: 「〜たいなら、〜ことだ」(If you want to..., you should...). It is often used when an experienced person gives direct advice to someone in a specific situation.
• Vocabulary: 努力 (どりょく): effort, endeavor.
• Example: 日本語が上手になりたいなら、毎日声を出して練習することだ。(If you want to become good at Japanese, you should practice speaking aloud every day.)
default.q.n2-40-q34-34.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「Vる + ものか / もんですか」expresses absolute negation—“absolutely not / as if I would...” It does not fit a context involving advice.
default.q.n2-40-q34-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「Vる + ことか」 usually occurs with どんなに or どれほど to express “how much/how very...,” and is not used to give advice.
default.q.n2-40-q34-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「Vる + ものだ」expresses an obvious truth, a moral principle, or a natural characteristic. It is not used to give specific, direct advice to someone in the pattern “〜したいなら.”
default.q.n2-40-q34-34.why.3: (d) Correct: 「Vる / Vない + ことだ」is used to give advice or a reminder about what someone should or must do in a specific situation (“If you want to succeed, you should make an effort ...”).
default.q.n2-40-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 予測しえなかった (something that no one could have predicted).
default.q.n2-40-q35-35.explanation:
Meaning: 'No one could have predicted that our country's economic situation would become this bad.' (The question contains an OCR error, '山が国' instead of '我が国' - わがくに: our country).
• Grammar: V-stem + えない (or うる/えない) expresses the possibility of something happening. The past negative form is えなかった (could not possibly...).
• Vocabulary: 予測 (よそく): prediction, anticipation.
• Example: 当時は、そんな大事故が起きるなどだれも予想しえなかった。(At the time, no one could have imagined that such a serious accident would occur.)
default.q.n2-40-q35-35.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜ざるをえない」means “have no choice but to” or “be forced to.” The resulting phrase would mean “have no choice but to predict,” which does not fit the preceding clause expressing surprise at the worsening economic situation.
default.q.n2-40-q35-35.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜わけではない」means “it is not necessarily the case that...” or “it is not that...”; it does not combine with だれも to express that no one is capable of doing something.
default.q.n2-40-q35-35.why.2: (c) Correct: The structure 「Vます + えない (past: えなかった)」means "cannot...". Combined with だれも, it forms 「だれも予測しえなかった」(no one could have foreseen or predicted it).
default.q.n2-40-q35-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜かねない」means “there is a risk that something bad may happen”; it is not used in a negative past form to mean “cannot.”
default.q.n2-40-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 耐えかねて (being unable to endure it any longer, and therefore...).
default.q.n2-40-q36-36.explanation:
Meaning: "Apparently, many athletes could not endure the harsh training sessions and left the club."
• Grammar: V-ます stem + かねる expresses an inability to endure or cope with a feeling or situation (mainly used with words describing psychological states or sensations, such as 耐えかねる, 見かねる, and 待ちかねる).
• Vocabulary: 耐える (たえる): to endure, bear, tolerate.
• Example: あまりの痛さに耐えかねて、大声を上げてしまった。(The pain was so severe that I could not bear it and cried out.)
default.q.n2-40-q36-36.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜ぬく」 means “to do something to the end” or “to overcome all difficulties.” If one 「耐えぬいて」—endured to the end—the following clause could not be quitting the club (やめてしまう).
default.q.n2-40-q36-36.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜たところ」describes obtaining a result after trying something, so it does not fit as a cause leading to the decision to give up.
default.q.n2-40-q36-36.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜一方で」 expresses two aspects occurring at the same time or a one-directional trend such as “on the other hand / increasingly”; it does not express a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n2-40-q36-36.why.3: (d) Correct: The structure 「Vます + かねる」 (in the te-form: 耐えかねて) means “to be unable to endure or hold back any longer.” It explains that the pressure of training became unbearable, forcing the person to quit.
default.q.n2-40-q37-37.verdict: The correct answer is 2: かねません (there is a risk of becoming ill).
default.q.n2-40-q37-37.explanation:
Meaning: “If you do not take a break, you may become ill from overwork.”
• Grammar: Vます + かねない (polite form: かねません) means “may possibly... / there is a risk that...,” and is used for negative or undesirable outcomes.
• Example: このまま温暖化が進めば、海面が上昇しかねない。(If global warming continues at this rate, sea levels may rise.)
default.q.n2-40-q37-37.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「〜つつある」describes an action or change that is gradually unfolding over time; it is not used for a warning about a risk that will occur in the future if one does not rest.
default.q.n2-40-q37-37.why.1: (b) Correct: The structure 「Vます + かねない (polite: かねません)」 expresses the possibility of a bad or negative outcome occurring ('there is a risk of becoming ill').
default.q.n2-40-q37-37.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「Vます + かねる」(polite: かねます) means “to find it difficult or impossible to do,” and is used for a tactful refusal; it is not used with 病気になる to warn of a possible risk.
default.q.n2-40-q37-37.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「かけません」is not a standard grammar form. 「〜かける」means “nearly...” or “leave something unfinished,” and its negative form 「かけません」is not used in this context.
default.q.n2-40-q38-38.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 次第です (that is precisely the reason / that is how the situation came about).
default.q.n2-40-q38-38.explanation:
Meaning: “I have decided to resign from the company, which is why I have come here today to greet you.”
• Grammar: 〜次第です is commonly placed at the end of a sentence in formal letters and business communication to explain the process or reason leading to the current action or situation (= というわけです).
• Example: 事情が変わりましたので、日程を変更していただきたくご連絡を差し上げた次第です。 (Since circumstances have changed, I am contacting you to ask that the schedule be changed.)
default.q.n2-40-q38-38.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜以上は」 means “now that…” or “once…,” whereas 「以上です」 is used to announce the end of a speech or report (“That is all”). It is not used to present the cause of an event at the end of a sentence in this way.
default.q.n2-40-q38-38.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜限りだ」 follows an adjective expressing emotion and means “extremely...”; it does not follow the past-tense verb 伺った to explain a reason.
default.q.n2-40-q38-38.why.2: (c) Correct: The pattern 「〜次第です」 appears at the end of a sentence in formal or business language to explain the background and reason why the speaker is taking this action.
default.q.n2-40-q38-38.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜向きだ」 means “suitable for” or “intended for” a particular group, such as older people or children, so it does not fit this context at all.
default.q.n2-40-q39-39.verdict: The correct answer is 1: に限って (just when..., of all times...).
default.q.n2-40-q39-39.explanation:
Meaning: 'Just when you have no money, your friends invite you out more often.'
• Grammar: N + に限って expresses an ironic or frustrating coincidence in which something happens precisely under inconvenient or regrettable circumstances.
• Example: 傘を持っていない日に限って、雨が降る。(It always rains on the very days when I do not bring an umbrella.)
default.q.n2-40-q39-39.why.0: (a) Correct: The pattern 「N + に限って」 describes an ironically unfortunate situation: something troublesome or undesirable happens precisely at a particular time or on a particular day.
default.q.n2-40-q39-39.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜くせに」(despite..., even though...) is used to criticize or sarcastically reproach someone. The preceding clause generally has a person as its subject and does not combine with a noun indicating a time, such as とき.
default.q.n2-40-q39-39.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜ばかりか」means “not only... but also...,” and cannot express the ironic or unfortunate timing involved here.
default.q.n2-40-q39-39.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜もかまわず」means “without caring about / regardless of...,” describing a subject’s disregard for something, so it does not fit here.
default.q.n2-40-q40-40.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 子供じゃないもん (because I’m not a child anymore).
default.q.n2-40-q40-40.explanation:
Meaning: "— Can you stay home and look after the house by yourself? — Yes, I can. I'm not a little child anymore!" (The test contains a typographical error, '留守番次' instead of '留守番').
• Grammar: だって〜んだもん / だって〜もん expresses an explanation or excuse, often with a childish, whiny, or informal tone.
• Vocabulary: 留守番 (るすばん): looking after the house while someone else is away.
• Example: 「どうして食べないの？」「だって、嫌いなんだもん。」('Why aren't you eating?' 'Because I don't like it!')
default.q.n2-40-q40-40.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜っぽい」 means “having the appearance or quality of...,” but this sentence contains the typing error “子供流ぽくない” and does not fit the character ぼく’s explanatory connector 「だって」.
default.q.n2-40-q40-40.why.1: (b) Correct: placing 「〜もん / もの」at the end of a sentence gives a reason or excuse in casual conversation, often used by children or women, and frequently accompanied by the connective expression 「だって...もん」.
default.q.n2-40-q40-40.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「流け」 is a typing error for 「っけ」, which is used to confirm something one is unsure about or has forgotten; it is not used to make a definite statement.
default.q.n2-40-q40-40.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜にきまっている」 expresses the speaker’s certainty about another situation. It sounds unnatural with the child’s innocent, explanatory tone accompanied by “だって.”
default.q.n2-40-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4: にほかならない (is precisely; is nothing other than the criminal).
default.q.n2-40-q41-41.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "Because it involved deceiving someone to take their money, this is nothing other than a criminal act."
• Grammar: N + にほかならない (or からにほかならない when stating a reason) expresses an absolute assertion about the essential nature or fundamental cause of something, typically in written or formal language.
• Vocabulary: 犯罪 (はんざい): crime, criminal act.
• Example: 今回の成功は、チーム全員の努力の結果にほかならない。(This success is nothing other than the result of the entire team's efforts.)
default.q.n2-40-q41-41.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「〜というものだ」 is used to give a general comment or exclamation (“that is what...; indeed...”); to firmly assert that something is nothing other than A, にほかならない is more precise and emphatic.
default.q.n2-40-q41-41.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜に限る」 means “nothing is better than...” or “it is best to...”; it is not used to define the nature of a criminal act.
default.q.n2-40-q41-41.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜次第だ」 indicates the reason, circumstances, or “depending on...”; it is not used to affirm the nature of something.
default.q.n2-40-q41-41.why.3: (d) Correct: The structure 「N + にほかならない」 means “is precisely...” or “is nothing other than...,” and strongly and confidently asserts the nature of an action.
default.q.n2-40-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 3: わりに (although...; considering that it was not prepared carefully, the result was surprisingly good).
default.q.n2-40-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: Although I was not fully prepared for this exam, I still got a high score.
• Grammar: 〜わりに（は） indicates a discrepancy or mismatch between the actual result and what would normally be expected.
• Example: 彼はあまり勉強しなかったわりに、いい大学に合格した。(Although he did not study very much, he was accepted into a good university.)
default.q.n2-40-q42-42.why.0: (a) is incorrect: 「〜からすると / からすれば」 means “from the perspective of / judging from...”; it does not connect two clauses expressing an unexpected contrast.
default.q.n2-40-q42-42.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「〜というより」 means “rather than...” and is used to compare two different ways of expressing or evaluating something.
default.q.n2-40-q42-42.why.2: (c) Correct: The structure 「V・A・Naな・Nの + わりに（は）」 means that, compared with something, the degree or result is unexpectedly different (a contrast between the level of preparation and the test result).
default.q.n2-40-q42-42.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜ほど」 indicates degree (“to the extent that ...”) or comparison (“not as ... as ...”). It cannot be used as a conjunction expressing contrast or opposition in this sentence.
default.q.n2-40-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 4: ものの (although I managed to get into the company, I still have not been able to do the work I want).
default.q.n2-40-q43-43.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “Although I managed to get into the company I had always hoped to join, I still have not been assigned the work I want to do.”
• Grammar: 〜ものの (= けれども) connects two contrasting clauses. It acknowledges that the first clause is true, while the second describes an opposing reality. It is often used in written language.
• Vocabulary: 希望 (きぼう): hope, aspiration, desire.
• Example: 車を買ったものの、運転する機会がほとんどない。(Although I bought a car, I hardly ever have a chance to drive it.)
default.q.n2-40-q43-43.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「Vた + あげく（に）」 describes a bad outcome after a long period of worry or effort, and usually combines with verbs describing prolonged processes, such as 悩む, 迷う, and 議論する.
default.q.n2-40-q43-43.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「V + 以上（は）」 means “once one has..., one must...”; the following clause usually expresses responsibility, obligation, or determination, not a statement of dissatisfaction.
default.q.n2-40-q43-43.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「〜反面」 describes two contrasting aspects that coexist in the same thing or phenomenon (both advantageous and disadvantageous, for example). It does not connect events in chronological order as this sentence does.
default.q.n2-40-q43-43.why.3: (d) Correct: The structure 「Vた + ものの」 means “although…, …,” with the latter clause describing a reality that did not occur as expected or naturally follow from the former clause.
default.q.n2-40-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1: ものなら (if it were possible to do...).
default.q.n2-40-q44-44.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “If possible, I would like to become the president of the largest company in the world.”
• Grammar: The potential form + ものなら is used to hypothesize something impossible or very difficult to achieve; the following clause often expresses a desire (〜たい, 〜てみたい).
• Vocabulary: 社長 (Sino-Japanese reading: company president, CEO. - しゃちょう): company president, CEO.
• Example: 戻れるものなら、子供のころに戻りたい。(If I could go back, I would like to return to my childhood.)
default.q.n2-40-q44-44.why.0: (a) Correct. The structure「V potential form + ものなら」means “if it were possible to do...” and expresses a wish for something extremely difficult or nearly impossible in reality.
default.q.n2-40-q44-44.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「〜ものの」 means “although…,” and is not used to set up a hypothetical meaning “if…, then I would like to become a company director.”
default.q.n2-40-q44-44.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「〜あまり」 means “because something is too..., resulting in a negative outcome.” It is not used after the potential form to indicate a condition.
default.q.n2-40-q44-44.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「〜かぎりでは」means “as far as/within the scope of...” (for example, 私が見た限りでは - as far as I saw), and does not form a conditional structure expressing a wish.
default.q.n2-40-q45-45.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The correct answer at the star ★ is choice 1 (風も).
default.q.n2-40-q45-45.explanation: Complete sentence: この地方の冬は気温も低ければ風も強いので、寒さが厳しい。Meaning: Winters in this region are extremely cold because temperatures are low and the winds are strong.
default.q.n2-40-q45-45.why.0: (a) It follows the conditional「低ければ」to form the parallel listing pattern「〜も〜ば〜も…」(both... and...), occupying the third position (the ★ slot).
default.q.n2-40-q45-45.why.1: (b) It serves as the subject of the predicate 「低ければ」 in the first clause and comes first to introduce the reason clause.
default.q.n2-40-q45-45.why.2: (c) Ends the cause clause 「〜ので」, modifies the main clause 「寒さが厳しい」, and occupies the fourth position.
default.q.n2-40-q45-45.why.3: (d) The conditional 「〜ば」 form of the adjective 「低い」 follows 「気温も」 in position 2 of the structure 「Aも〜ばBも〜」.
default.q.n2-40-q46-46.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 3 → 2 → 1. The correct answer at the ★ position is choice 2 (子供たちが).
default.q.n2-40-q46-46.explanation: Complete sentence: 3 3 3 人の子の母親として毎日忙しいが、最近はありがたいことに子供たちが手伝ってくれるようになった。Meaning: As the mother of 3 children, I am busy every day, but fortunately, the children have recently started helping me.）
default.q.n2-40-q46-46.why.0: (a) The te-form of 「手伝う」 combines with 「〜てくれるようになった」 at the end of the sentence, so it occupies the fourth position.
default.q.n2-40-q46-46.why.1: (b) It functions as the subject performing the action 「手伝ってくれる」 and occupies the third position (the ★ slot).
default.q.n2-40-q46-46.why.2: (c) follows the emotion adjective 「ありがたい」 to form the connective phrase 「〜ことに」 (“fortunately / to one’s gratitude”), and belongs in position 2.
default.q.n2-40-q46-46.why.3: (d) It appears in position 1 and modifies 「ことに」 to express the speaker's emotion or evaluation.
default.q.n2-40-q47-47.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 3 → 1 → 4. The correct answer at the star ★ is choice 1 (のが).
default.q.n2-40-q47-47.explanation: Complete sentence: 辛いときに助け合えるのが真の友達というものだ。（Meaning: Being able to help each other in difficult times is what true friendship is all about.）
default.q.n2-40-q47-47.why.0: (a) The clause「辛いときに助け合える」is nominalized to serve as the subject of the sentence, occupying position 3 (the ★ slot).
default.q.n2-40-q47-47.why.1: (b) Following the adjective 「辛い」, it forms the adverbial time phrase 「辛いときに」(when things are difficult), which belongs in position 1.
default.q.n2-40-q47-47.why.2: (c) The potential form of the verb means mutual assistance, modifies the nominalizing particle 「のが」, and occupies the second position.
default.q.n2-40-q47-47.why.3: (d) A noun must come directly before the judgment pattern 「〜というものだ」, so the correct position is number 4.
default.q.n2-40-q48-48.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1. The correct answer at the ★ position is choice 4 (変化する).
default.q.n2-40-q48-48.explanation: Complete sentence: 時代の流れとともに人の考え方が変化するのは当然のことだ。（Meaning: It is only natural that people's ways of thinking change with the times.）
default.q.n2-40-q48-48.why.0: (a) The nominalizing particle turns the clause 「人の考え方が変化する」 into the subject of the predicate 「当然のことだ」 and is in the fourth position.
default.q.n2-40-q48-48.why.1: (b) The subject of the predicate「変化する」is in the second position.
default.q.n2-40-q48-48.why.2: (c) It follows the noun 「時代の流れ」 to form the grammar pattern 「N + とともに」 (along with...), and comes first.
default.q.n2-40-q48-48.why.3: (d) The main predicate verb in the subordinate clause occupies position 3 (the ★ blank), before the nominalizing particle 「のは」.
default.q.n2-40-q49-49.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The correct answer at the ★ position is choice 1 (どんな会社).
default.q.n2-40-q49-49.explanation: Complete sentence: 就職について、私は、自分の能力が発揮できるならどんな会社だってかまわないと考えている。（Meaning: Regarding employment, I think any company is fine as long as I can make full use of my abilities.）
default.q.n2-40-q49-49.why.0: (a) It occupies the third position (the ★ blank) and combines with 「〜だって」 to form the phrase “any company...”.
default.q.n2-40-q49-49.why.1: (b) It follows the potential form 「発揮できる」to create the conditional clause 「〜なら」(if/as long as), and occupies the second position.
default.q.n2-40-q49-49.why.2: (c) It follows 「どんな会社」 to form an emphatic structure with 「かまわない」 (“any company is fine”), and occupies the fourth position.
default.q.n2-40-q49-49.why.3: (d) It follows 「自分の能力が」 to form the phrase “be able to make use of one’s abilities,” so it goes in position 1.
default.q.n2-40-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ものはありません.
default.q.n2-40-q50-50.explanation: The sentence uses the superlative comparison pattern: 『N ＋ ほど ＋ [adjective] ＋ ものはない／ものはありません』, meaning "Nothing is as ... as N." Here, the author begins the passage by stating that among methods for treating insomnia, no method is as famous and familiar as counting sheep (「羊を数えることほど有名なものはありません」). Therefore, choice 3 is the only correct answer, both grammatically and in terms of the passage's meaning.
default.q.n2-40-q50-50.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「ものです」 expresses a truth, natural characteristic, exclamation, or past habit. It does not combine with the superlative comparison structure 「これほど／～ほど」.
default.q.n2-40-q50-50.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ものはあります」means “there is something...,” which disrupts the superlative comparison and makes the sentence illogical as an introduction.
default.q.n2-40-q50-50.why.2: (c) Correct. The structure 「～ほど...ものはない / ものはありません」 means “there is nothing as...as...,” emphasizing that counting sheep is the best-known method when having trouble sleeping.
default.q.n2-40-q50-50.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「ものではない」is used to advise someone not to do something or to strongly deny the nature of something; it does not combine with the comparative pattern「～ほど」.
default.q.n2-40-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 数えれば数えるほど.
default.q.n2-40-q51-51.explanation: The N2 grammar pattern 『V-れば V-るほど』 expresses the idea that “the more one does V, the more the degree or result in the following clause increases.” In this context, the author points out the ironic fact that the more people count sheep (数えれば数えるほど), the more focused and alert they become (目が冴えて), making it even harder to fall asleep. Therefore, choice 2 is the most accurate answer.
default.q.n2-40-q51-51.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The pattern 「～か～ないかのうちに」means "just as soon as...", describing one action being immediately followed by another; it does not express a gradual increase.
default.q.n2-40-q51-51.why.1: (b) Correct. The pattern 「V-れば V-るほど」 means "the more..., the more..." and combines perfectly with "目が冴えて" to express the paradox: the more one counts, the more awake one becomes.
default.q.n2-40-q51-51.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The pattern 「～にしろ～にしろ」 means "whether... or..." and does not express a directly or inversely proportional relationship between counting actions and the degree of alertness.
default.q.n2-40-q51-51.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The pattern 「～としても～としても」 means “whether it is assumed that... or that...,” which does not fit the semantic structure of the sentence.
default.q.n2-40-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 1. だからこそ.
default.q.n2-40-q52-52.explanation: Before blank 52, the author explains the phonetic basis of this method in English: the pronunciation of "sheep" is similar to that of "sleep," creating a self-suggestive effect that promotes sleep and relaxed breathing. The following clause concludes that this method is genuinely effective in English-speaking countries. 『だからこそ』 (precisely because of that...) emphasizes the fundamental reason leading to the conclusion in the following clause. Therefore, choice 1 is correct.
default.q.n2-40-q52-52.why.0: (a) Correct. The conjunction 「だからこそ」 means “that is precisely why,” emphasizing a direct cause-and-effect relationship between similar pronunciation and the method’s practical effectiveness.
default.q.n2-40-q52-52.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「だからといって」 means “even so” or “that does not mean that...,” and is usually followed by a partial negative such as ～わけではない. It is not used to assert a causal conclusion.
default.q.n2-40-q52-52.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「からすると」 means “from the perspective of...” or “judging from...”. It introduces a judgment based on a standpoint or grounds, and is not a conjunction connecting two cause-and-effect sentences.
default.q.n2-40-q52-52.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「からして」 means “starting with” or “even,” introducing a representative and often extreme example. It does not fit as a conjunction in this position.
default.q.n2-40-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 3. なぜ日本語だとうまく機能しないのでしょうか.
default.q.n2-40-q53-53.explanation: After explaining why counting sheep is effective in English in the preceding passage, the author shifts to analyzing why Japanese people may count sheep but still be unable to fall asleep. The sentence immediately after the blank is: “The reason lies in the sound of the word 「ひつじ」 in Japanese.” Therefore, question 53 should introduce the issue: 『なぜ日本語だとうまく機能しないのでしょうか』 (Why does it not work effectively in Japanese?). Thus, answer choice 3 fits the logic of the entire passage perfectly.
default.q.n2-40-q53-53.why.0: (a) Incorrect. This choice asks how the meanings differ, whereas the passage discusses the effect or function of supporting sleep, not lexical meaning.
default.q.n2-40-q53-53.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Choice 2 asks about “how to count sheep in English,” which goes against the passage’s shift toward analyzing the Japanese case.
default.q.n2-40-q53-53.why.2: (c) Correct. The question “Why is this method ineffective in Japanese?” serves as a problem statement (問題提起), providing an appropriate opening for the explanatory paragraph that follows.
default.q.n2-40-q53-53.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice asks broadly, “What is a good way to sleep?” It is too general and does not connect with the explanation of Japanese phonetics in the following sentence.
default.q.n2-40-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 生まれません.
default.q.n2-40-q54-54.explanation: The passage concludes that in Japanese, the word “hitsuji” has no phonetic connection at all with “nemuri” (sleep), unlike the English pair “sheep” and “sleep.” Therefore, the sleep-suggestion effect and the resulting state of relaxation “will not be produced / will not occur” (効果は生まれません). For this reason, the emphatic negative predicate 『生まれません』 in answer choice 4 is the most accurate answer.
default.q.n2-40-q54-54.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「期待できるでしょう」(can be expected) expresses a positive assertion, which is completely contrary to the claim that counting sheep in Japanese is ineffective.
default.q.n2-40-q54-54.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 「ないとは言えません」, literally “cannot say that there is not,” is a double negative expressing a cautious affirmation. It does not fit the passage’s decisive argument.
default.q.n2-40-q54-54.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「出てくるはずです」 expresses a confident prediction (“is certain to appear”), which contradicts the situation being analyzed.
default.q.n2-40-q54-54.why.3: (d) Correct. 「生まれません」 (“will not arise” or “will not appear”) is a definite negative form, accurately expressing that the effects of autosuggestion or relaxation will not arise when counting in Japanese.
default.q.n2-40-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ずいぶん単純なんだなあ。).
default.q.n2-40-q55-55.explanation:
- Main point: The author eagerly reads a book about which part of the brain is involved in love, expecting the human brain to have some mysterious, miraculous mechanism. However, the book explains that when a person meets an attractive member of the opposite sex, the amygdala sends emotions to the hypothalamus, triggering an instinctive sexual desire. Thus, the author exclaims 「なんだ、そんなことなのか」(So that's all it is?) to express disappointment upon realizing that love is merely an extremely simple instinctive biological reaction, not something mysterious or profound.

- Question translation:
What does the author mean by 「なんだ、そんなことなのか」(So that's all it is?)?

- Answer choices:
1. So that's how it is—the human brain really is ingeniously designed.
2. So the thing called "love" is actually that complicated.
3. After all, what exactly is "love"?
4. So it's actually that simple?
default.q.n2-40-q55-55.why.0: (a) Choice 1 does not fit: The author is not praising or marveling at the sophistication and ingenuity of the human brain, but is disappointed that the mechanism of love is merely an ordinary sexual instinct.
default.q.n2-40-q55-55.why.1: (b) Choice 2 does not fit: The author realizes that, from a biological perspective, love is merely a simple instinctive command, not something as mysterious or complex as they had thought. Therefore, saying that love is “complex” contradicts the author’s view.
default.q.n2-40-q55-55.why.2: (c) Choice 3 does not fit. The author has already found an answer to this question in the book (love is an instinctive command that triggers sexual desire), so the exclamation does not imply uncertainty or a search for the definition of love.
default.q.n2-40-q55-55.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4 is correct: The passage states: 「これを読むかぎり、「恋」とは、本能の指令によって異性に対して性欲を起こすこと次ということになる。 なんだ、そんなことなのか 。人間の専だから、何か神秘的な作用があって、「恋」に落活注せるのかと思ったか。」 (According to this book, “love” ultimately means developing sexual desire toward the opposite sex at the command of instinct. So that is all it is? Since it involves the human brain, I thought some mysterious force must cause us to fall in love.) The exclamation expresses disappointment upon learning that the mechanism of love is surprisingly simple and direct rather than mysterious.
default.q.n2-40-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 働こうとしない若者がいること (the fact that there are young people who are unwilling to work).
default.q.n2-40-q56-56.explanation:
Main point: The passage analyzes the phenomenon of young people today refusing to work. The author points out that in the past, people who did not work had nothing to eat, so this phenomenon did not occur; today, it is partly because financially comfortable parents indulge their children.

Question translation:
「こういうこと」("Something like this") refers to what?

Answer choices:
1. Parents indulging their children.
2. Some young people refusing to work.
3. Not working meaning having nothing to eat.
4. Leaving young people to do as they please.
default.q.n2-40-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect because parents’ spoiling of their children is mentioned in the following sentence («豊かになった親た活の甘やかしも一因だろう») as one cause of the situation, not as what the demonstrative 「こういうこと」 refers to.
default.q.n2-40-q56-56.why.1: (b) Correct. The preceding sentence states: «しかし、今の働かない若者た活に関しては、自然に任せておくわけにはいかない。働かなければ食べられなかった時答には、 こういうこと はなか流た» (However, when it comes to young people today who do not work, we cannot simply leave them to nature. In an era when those who did not work could not eat, there was no such thing.) Thus, 「こういうこと」 directly refers to the phenomenon of “young people who do not work” (働かない若者たち / 働こうとしない若者).
default.q.n2-40-q56-56.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「働かなければ食べられないこと」 is a real-life condition from an earlier period (「働かなければ食べられなかった時答には」), used as comparative background rather than as the content of 「こういうこと」.
default.q.n2-40-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect because «自然に任せておく» (leave things to nature) is something the author says cannot be applied to today's young people who do not work («自然に任せておくわけにはいかない»); it is not the content of 「こういうこと」.
default.q.n2-40-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 2: This former female university professor was not evaluated in proportion to her actual abilities.
default.q.n2-40-q57-57.explanation:
- Main idea of the passage: Although people often say that one should not judge by appearances and that what is inside is more important, first impressions are in fact largely based on appearance. A former female university professor once shared that she used to think appearance did not matter as long as she had ability, so she paid little attention to her looks. However, because her profession required her to stand before the public, she should have taken better care of her appearance, and if she had done so, people's evaluation of her might have been different (more favorable).

- Translation of the question:
  文章の内容からわかることはどれか。
  (Which of the following can be understood from the content of the passage?)

- Translation of the choices:
  1. この元大学教授は実力があったので評価も高かった。
     (Because this former university professor had ability, she was also highly regarded.)
  2. この元大学教授は実力ほどは評価されていなかった。
     (This former university professor was not evaluated as highly as her ability warranted.)
  3. 大学教授という仕事は外見には左右されない。
     (The job of a university professor is not influenced by appearance.)
  4. この元大学教授は外見に気をつかってよかったと言っている。
     (This former university professor says it was good that she paid attention to her appearance.)
default.q.n2-40-q57-57.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the former professor says that if she had paid attention to her appearance in the past, “people’s evaluation of her might have been different,” implying that despite her ability, she did not receive as much recognition as she had hoped.
default.q.n2-40-q57-57.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct. The evidence is: 「実力さえあれば、見かけは関係ないと思って、外見にはあまり注意をはらってこなかった。でも、人前に立つ職業である以上、もっと気をつかうべきだった」と言っていた。そうすれば、自分に対する評価ももっと違ったものになっていたのではないかと。 She believes that if she had paid more attention to her appearance, people’s evaluation of her might have been different, showing that her actual evaluation did not match her true ability.
default.q.n2-40-q57-57.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the former professor realized that, since it was "a profession that involves standing before people" (人前に立つ職業である以上), he should have paid more attention to his appearance. In other words, the job is affected by outward appearance.
default.q.n2-40-q57-57.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because in the past she “did not pay much attention to her appearance” (外見にはあまり注意をはらってこなかった) and now regrets that she should have paid more attention (もっと気をつかうべきだった), not because she had paid attention and felt good about it.
default.q.n2-40-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 社風に合わない型破りな (unconventional and incompatible with the company culture).
default.q.n2-40-q58-58.explanation:
**Main idea of the passage:** The passage describes a trick used by fishermen: when transporting fish to the port, they deliberately place several "natural enemies" (predators) in the tank. Because the predators are present, the fish remain tense and afraid of being eaten, allowing them to stay fresh, healthy, and active as they would be in the sea. Inspired by this story, a company director applied the idea to recruitment: he deliberately hired several unconventional employees whose personalities differed from the company's usual culture (社風に合わない型破りな), creating positive stimulation and tension so that the workforce would remain energetic rather than stagnant.

**Question translation:** According to the passage, which expression is most appropriate for the blank ( ★ )?

**Answer choices:**
1. The director's thinking can be understood.
2. The employees can be coordinated and reconciled.
3. Unconventional and incompatible with the company's culture.
4. Strong-willed and compatible with the company's culture.
default.q.n2-40-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because understanding the director’s thinking as referring to obedient, compliant employees does not match the image of a “natural enemy” (天敵), which provides positive stimulation and tension in the company environment.
default.q.n2-40-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because someone who can coordinate or mediate between employees tends to maintain harmony, reducing conflict rather than creating the necessary tension (緊張感) to promote dynamism.
default.q.n2-40-q58-58.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage states: 'わざわざとった魚の天敵のような魚を数匹投げ込んでおく' and '敵意を感じる魚がまじっていると、いつ自分が食われてしまうと緊張するためか、港まで、海にいるときと同じような元気を保つのだそうだ'. The author compares adding a fish's natural predators to the tank to keep the fish fresh and healthy with a manager deliberately hiring unconventional employees who do not fit the company's usual mold (社風に合わない型破りな) in order to create pressure and motivation that maintain the vitality of the entire group.
default.q.n2-40-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect because people who “fit the company culture” (社風に合う) would create a group made up entirely of similar people (like “only the same kind of fish”), causing employees to lose the necessary sense of tension and easily become less dynamic.
default.q.n2-40-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: 雌のチンパンジーがボスの座をめぐる争いに参加したこと.
default.q.n2-40-q59-59.explanation:
- Translation of the question: The phrase "an unusual event" (異変) refers to which of the following?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Two male chimpanzees fighting over the position of leader.
  2. Although males normally become leaders, a female challenges the leader for the position.
  3. A female chimpanzee being attracted to the personality or qualities of the chimpanzee leader.
  4. Female chimpanzees joining the fight over the position of leader.
- Main point: The passage describes an unusual event (異変) observed in a troop of wild chimpanzees. When a young male named Fanana challenged the leader, Kalunde, for his position and Kalunde was about to lose, three female chimpanzees rushed in, shouted loudly, and attacked Fanana to save Kalunde. The author emphasizes that in the chimpanzee world, it is extremely rare for females to join a power struggle over the position of leader («チンパンジーの世界ではボスの座を争う政権抗争に雌が加わるのはきわめてまれだ»). Therefore, the unusual event was that the female chimpanzees intervened in the fight over the leadership position.
default.q.n2-40-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because two male chimpanzees fighting over leadership is a normal event within a chimpanzee troop («チンパンジーは群れにはボスがいる», «ボスの座を奪うために挑戦した»), not an «異変» (abnormal occurrence).
default.q.n2-40-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the offspring rushed in only to help the former leader, Kalunde, not because they stood up to challenge him for the position of leader (「ファナナがボスの座を奪うために挑戦した」, 「カルンデを助けようとしたのだ」).
default.q.n2-40-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the fact that the offspring were attracted to Kalunde's personality is merely the reason explaining their action («カルンデの人柄にひかれていた雌 3 頭が»). It is not itself the «異変»; the main abnormal event is their participation in the power struggle.
default.q.n2-40-q59-59.why.3: (d) Correct because the passage clearly states: «この時、カルンデが負けそうになると、カルンデの人柄にひかれていた雌 3 頭が立ち上がり、大声をあげながらファナナに突進しカルンデを助けようとしたのだ。チンパンジーの世界ではボスの座を争う政権抗争に雌が加わるのはきわめてまれだという。» (At that moment, when Karunde seemed about to lose, three females who had been attracted to his character stood up, charged at Fanana while shouting loudly, and tried to help Karunde. In the chimpanzee world, it is extremely rare for females to join a power struggle over the position of boss).
default.q.n2-40-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 3: If one keeps hesitating instead of directly getting to work, one cannot understand or experience the interesting aspects of the work.
default.q.n2-40-q60-60.explanation:
Main point: The author believes that the time spent hesitating among many choices is a great waste (惜しい), because unless you face the work in front of you and commit yourself to it, you cannot explore it deeply or discover what is truly interesting about it.

Translation of the question: There is a sentence 「 惜しいと思いますね 」(I think it is a shame); why is that?
Translation of the choices:
1. Because they will grow old while hesitating.
2. Because there may still be other good jobs.
3. Because they will never be able to discover what is interesting about the job.
4. Because if they cannot decide on a job, they will not earn any income.
default.q.n2-40-q60-60.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not mention aging or age-related issues while the person is undecided.
default.q.n2-40-q60-60.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author does not say that the hesitation is due to the possibility of another, better job elsewhere.
default.q.n2-40-q60-60.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage clearly explains why hesitation is regrettable: 「仕中に正面から向き合わずにいると、奥へ踏み込んでいくことができない。中にある面白い領域に届かない。」 (If you do not confront the work directly, you cannot go deeper into it or reach the interesting areas within it).
default.q.n2-40-q60-60.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not mention income or money while the person is unable to decide on a job.
default.q.n2-40-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Constantly worrying about whether you are meeting everyone’s expectations will not produce good results.
default.q.n2-40-q61-61.explanation:
Main point: As a jockey, the author receives great expectations from fans and those around him. However, there is no point in worrying about each expectation individually; what matters most is focusing completely on competing with all one's strength and performing at one's best.

Question translation: Which explanation best fits 「その一つ一つを数えても仕方がない」(There is no point in counting them one by one)?
Answer choices:
1. Counting whether the number of fans is increasing or decreasing is meaningless.
2. It is impossible to count how many horse-racing tickets have been sold, one by one.
3. Looking back to see how many expectations one has fulfilled so far is meaningless.
4. Thinking about whether one has fulfilled the expectations or not will not produce good results.
default.q.n2-40-q61-61.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because 'counting each one individually' here refers to worrying about each person's expectations, not counting the number of fans.
default.q.n2-40-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because it is a mechanical, literal interpretation of counting each betting ticket, which does not fit the metaphorical meaning of pressure from expectations in context.
default.q.n2-40-q61-61.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not discuss looking back at the past to see how many expectations were fulfilled.
default.q.n2-40-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the author points out that although they know expectations are very high, there is no point in worrying about each one individually. Instead, they should focus entirely on competing and perform to the best of their ability:「でも、その一つ一つを数えても仕方がない。私はこの体を使って、㤿と一つになって走ることだけを考えるのです。私のベストを引き出せるのは、私しかいないから。」
default.q.n2-40-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The mental strength and valuable experience gained through committing oneself to work and enduring hardships.
default.q.n2-40-q62-62.explanation:
Main point: The author asserts that the things one has done and the hardships one has experienced belong uniquely to oneself; taking action and becoming directly involved in real situations helps build this valuable store of inner strength and experience.

Question translation: What does 「そういう財産」(such an asset) refer to?
Translation of the choices:
1. Praise received from others.
2. Expectations placed on one by people around them.
3. Money earned from work.
4. Inner strength gained through work.
default.q.n2-40-q62-62.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author says that no matter what words others may give them, external praise is not an inner asset that one has accumulated oneself.
default.q.n2-40-q62-62.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because expectations from people around you are an external influence, not an asset acquired through work experience.
default.q.n2-40-q62-62.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention money or material wealth at all.
default.q.n2-40-q62-62.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because the preceding sentence states: 「やってきた仕事は自分のもの、苦しんだ経験も自分だけのもの。動いていけ消、そういう財産が 蓄 えられていくのです。」 The work one has done and the painful experiences one has endured belong to oneself; by taking action and moving forward, such personal assets and experiences gradually accumulate.
default.q.n2-40-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 4: because the human eye has a large amount of visible white area.
default.q.n2-40-q63-63.explanation:
- Main point: The passage points out that, unlike other primates, human eyes contain a large amount of visible white. It is thanks to this structural feature (そのおかげ) that humans can move their eyes flexibly, direct their gaze, and engage in the human form of face-to-face communication.
- Question translation: The passage uses the phrase “thanks to that” (そのおかげ). What does it refer to?
- Answer choices:
  1. Facing each other and talking.
  2. Directing one’s gaze.
  3. Moving the eyeballs flexibly.
  4. Having a large amount of visible white in the eyes.
default.q.n2-40-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Facing each other while talking (向き合って話をする) is a communication behavior made possible by the characteristics of the eyes. It is the result, not the cause referred to by the demonstrative 「その」.
default.q.n2-40-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Directing one's gaze (視線の方向を定める) is one of the actions that takes place during communication, not the cause indicated by 「そのおかげ」.
default.q.n2-40-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Moving the eyeballs actively (眼球を盛んに動かす) is an accompanying action, not the fundamental cause stated in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n2-40-q63-63.why.3: (d) Correct. The preceding sentence states: 「人間の目はほかの霊長類 と違って白目の部分が多い。║球を盛んに動かし、視線の方向を定めて、相手と向き合って話をするという人間らしい師田画ニケーシ自ンができるのは そのおかげ である。」 The demonstrative 「その」 directly replaces the information that human eyes have more white than the eyes of other primates.
default.q.n2-40-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 2: When you want to know what the other person is thinking or feeling.
default.q.n2-40-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point: The author explains why the ability to recognize another person's gaze evolved: a person's eyes provide valuable clues about their inner state, such as their interest or goodwill. Looking into someone's eyes is a way of reading and understanding what that person is thinking and feeling.
- Translation of the question: According to the passage, when can looking deeply into the other person's eyes be considered appropriate?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. When you want the other person to see your face clearly.
  2. When you want to know what the other person is thinking.
  3. When you want to look at the same thing the other person is looking at.
  4. When you want to tell the other person what you are thinking.
default.q.n2-40-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not mention at all that looking into the other person’s eyes is intended to let them see one’s face clearly.
default.q.n2-40-q64-64.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「相手の視線が、相手の心の中の状態、例えば自分への関心や好意などについて有力な手がかりを与えてくれるであろう」 and 「目を見て相手の心を読んだりする」. Looking into the other person's eyes helps one grasp their mood, thoughts, and feelings.
default.q.n2-40-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The article discusses reading the other person's emotions and thoughts through their eyes, not looking at the object the other person is looking at.
default.q.n2-40-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage says that signaling with one's eyes (目くばせ) is for conveying a message, whereas looking into the other person's eyes (目を見る / のぞきこむ) is for reading their innermost thoughts (相手の心を読んだりする).
default.q.n2-40-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Women are more capable than men of seeing through the other person's true feelings or lies.
default.q.n2-40-q65-65.explanation:
- Main idea: The passage states that women have a larger area of visible sclera than men, which enables richer facial expressions and makes it easier to detect the direction of another person's eye movements and receive subtle signals. Therefore, women are particularly good at reading another person's thoughts from their eyes.
- Question translation: What can be inferred from this passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. Women's eyes are generally larger than men's eyes.
  2. People avoid eye contact when they feel hostile toward the other person.
  3. Women are better than men at seeing through another person's lies.
  4. Feeling a sense of mutual understanding when one's eyes meet another person's is strange.
default.q.n2-40-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage only states that 「白目の面積は男より女のほうが大きい」 (the area of the whites of the eyes is larger in women than in men); it does not say that women’s eyes are larger overall.
default.q.n2-40-q65-65.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The article states that among wild animals and monkeys, making direct eye contact is a sign of intimidation or hostility (目を合わせることは威嚇 や敵意の表現). It does not say that people who avoid eye contact are hostile.
default.q.n2-40-q65-65.why.2: (c) Correct. The text states: 「白目の面積は男より女のほうが大きい。...相手の目の動く方向を読み取ることで、相手から多彩な信号を受けることができる。女性が...目を見て相手の心を読んだりするのが得意なのは、なるほどと思われる。」 Because women have more visible sclera, they can receive signals from the eyes more effectively and are better at reading the other person's mind, so they are more capable of seeing through the truth or lies.
default.q.n2-40-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The opening paragraph states that among humans, communicating through eye contact increases intimacy and mutual understanding (「目で語り合う」ことで親密度を増す...ヒトという種に独特のものだ), so this is completely natural rather than strange.
default.q.n2-40-q66-66.verdict: The provided answer is 1 (私); however, based on the grammar and context of the passage, the correct answer should be 4 (男の先生).
default.q.n2-40-q66-66.explanation:
- Main idea: A junior high school in a newly developed urban area has a warm, original school song. The principal wrote the lyrics, the music teacher composed the music, and the principal cleverly incorporated the name of a male teacher named "Kaoru" into the lyrics.
- Question translation: Who was the person whose name was "incorporated"?
- Answer choices:
  1. Me
  2. The principal
  3. The music teacher
  4. The male teacher named Kaoru
default.q.n2-40-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect, although it is one of the choices provided: In the passage, “I” (私) is simply a resident or student at the school, not the person whose name is incorporated into the school song lyrics.
default.q.n2-40-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect: The principal (校長先生) is the person who wrote the song lyrics (作詞), meaning the person who performed the action of incorporating the name (織り込んだ人), not the person who had their name incorporated (織り込んでもらった人).
default.q.n2-40-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect: A music teacher (音楽の先生) composes music (作曲); they are not someone whose name is inserted into the lyrics of a song.
default.q.n2-40-q66-66.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「名前が『 薫 』という男の先生は、歌詞の中にさりげなく自分の名前を織り込んでもらった。」 In the structure 「〜てもらった」, the subject before the particle 「は」 is the male teacher named "Kaoru" (男の先生), who had his name skillfully woven into the song lyrics by the principal.
default.q.n2-40-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 廃校を目前にした日 (the day before the school was about to close).
default.q.n2-40-q67-67.explanation:
- Main point: When the junior high school decided to close after nearly 20 years of operation, former students and teachers gathered at the school to sing the school song together one last time. That emotional mass choral performance before the school closed remains vivid in the author's memory.
- Question translation: What day does “that day” (あの日) refer to?
- Answer choices:
  1. The day the school song was composed
  2. The day before the school closed (when the school was about to end its history)
  3. Graduation day
  4. Entrance ceremony day
default.q.n2-40-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The day the school song was composed (校歌ができた日) was when the school had just been founded, not the day of the large chorus performance (大合唱) that the author remembers at the end.
default.q.n2-40-q67-67.why.1: (b) Correct. The passage states: 「廃校が決まった時、有志の呼びかけで、たった 20 年足らずの歴史を閉じようとしている母校に、卒業生や、かつての先生方が集まり、校歌を合唱した。...あの日 の大合唱は今でも私の耳に残っている。」 The phrase “that day” (あの日) refers to the day when graduates and former teachers gathered to sing the school song as the school was about to close (廃校を目前にした日).
default.q.n2-40-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Graduation day (卒業式の日) is mentioned only as a general association with the graduation season in March (3 月は卒業の季節); it is not the date of a special event at the author’s school.
default.q.n2-40-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect: The entrance ceremony day (入学式の日) is not mentioned anywhere in the passage.
default.q.n2-40-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 3. はじめに移り住んだ人たちの子供たちはほとんどいない (There are almost no children of the people who originally moved there).
default.q.n2-40-q68-68.explanation:
- Main idea: After the economic bubble burst, land prices fell and no new residents moved into the new town. In particular, the children of the original residents—the second generation—gradually moved elsewhere after starting their own families, causing the number of students to fall sharply. The school had already closed six years earlier.
- Translation of the question: What is the new town like now?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. The population is increasing, and the schools are getting larger.
  2. No one lives there at all anymore, and the schools have also disappeared.
  3. There are almost no children of the people who originally moved there living there anymore.
  4. Thanks to appeals from dedicated people, former residents are returning.
default.q.n2-40-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect: The situation of “the population increasing and schools growing larger” occurred during the past economic bubble period (中学校の生徒数も増え続け...), not in the present.
default.q.n2-40-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The problem lies in the phrase “there are no residents left at all” (住む人が全くいなくなり). The passage only says that no one moves in and that the children of the residents leave; it does not say that nobody remains.
default.q.n2-40-q68-68.why.2: (c) Correct: The supporting sentence is 「住人の 2 代目は新しい家庭を持って、次々とニュータウンから出て行ったのである。中学校の生徒数も減っていき、ついに 6 年前に廃校になってしまった。」 The second generation—the children of the first residents—started families and left the new town one after another.
default.q.n2-40-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The appeal by the enthusiastic volunteers (有志の呼びかけ) was intended to bring former students and teachers together to sing the school song once when the school closed, not to move back and live there again.
default.q.n2-40-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Both A and B agree that in state-owned enterprises, services may not be valued or carefully improved.
default.q.n2-40-q69-69.explanation:
- Translation of the question: What do A and B have in common in their opinions?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. If an organization is state-owned, its services may not be valued.
  2. A competitive mindset generates profits.
  3. If an organization is state-owned, a great deal of wasteful, unprofitable activity will arise.
  4. State-owned and private organizations serve different groups of people.
- Main point and analysis: Passage A argues that because state-owned organizations lack competition, they are unlikely to develop an awareness of the need to improve service quality (国営では競争がないため、サービスを向上させようという意識が生まれにくい). Although passage B warns about the disadvantages of privatization, it also acknowledges that a drawback of state ownership is that citizens have no choice but to put up with poor service (国営だとサービスが悪くても国民は我慢せざるを得ないという難点もある). Therefore, both authors recognize that state-owned businesses can lead to service quality being neglected.
default.q.n2-40-q69-69.why.0: (a) Correct. Passage A states: 「国営では競争がないため、サービスを向上注せようという意識が生まれにくい」 (Because there is no competition in state-run services, it is difficult for an awareness of improving service to develop). Passage B also agrees with this limitation: 「ただ、国営だとサービスが悪くても国民は我慢せざるを得ないという難点もある」 (However, a drawback of state-run services is that even when the service is poor, citizens have no choice but to put up with it). Both recognize that state-run services may not receive sufficient attention.
default.q.n2-40-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Only A mentions creating services that attract many users in order to generate profit (「より多くの人に利用してもらうようなサービスを考え、利益をあげる」). B does not regard this as a shared point; rather, B is concerned that pursuing profit may cause essential services to be neglected.
default.q.n2-40-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Only Author A mentions that privatization would eliminate waste that produces no profit (「また、利益にならない無駄代いもなくなるはずだ」); Author B never mentions waste caused by state-owned enterprises.
default.q.n2-40-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Neither passage mentions or distinguishes the users served by public-sector and private-sector organizations.
default.q.n2-40-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Author A fully supports privatization, while Author B points out its problems and negative aspects.
default.q.n2-40-q70-70.explanation:
- Question translation: What positions do A and B take on privatization?
- Answer choices:
  1. A is completely in favor, while B is completely opposed.
  2. A is completely opposed, while B is in favor.
  3. A is completely in favor, while B points out the problems involved.
  4. A points out the problems involved, while B is completely in favor.
- Main point and analysis: Author A fully supports privatizing public services (民間でできるものは民営化するべきだと思う), emphasizing competitive incentives, service improvements, and reinvestment in redevelopment, citing JR and telecommunications as examples. In contrast, author B argues that there is no need to privatize indiscriminately (むやみに民営化する必要はない), because privatization can lead to unprofitable services being eliminated, such as rural post offices and local railway lines, causing hardship for many people. Although B acknowledges that services may improve after privatization, B's main focus is on its disadvantages and unresolved problems, and on the need to consider those who are negatively affected.
default.q.n2-40-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The statement about A is correct, but the statement about B is wrong because B is not "completely opposed" to privatization: B says 「民営化が必ずしも悪いというわけではない」—privatization is not necessarily bad—and acknowledges improvements in JR and NTT services.
default.q.n2-40-q70-70.why.1: (b) Completely incorrect. The position is reversed and differs from the actual views of the two authors.
default.q.n2-40-q70-70.why.2: (c) Correct. Author A fully supports privatization: 「民間でできるものは民営化するべきだと思う」 (I think anything that the private sector can do should be privatized) and points out a range of benefits. Author B, meanwhile, identifies problems with privatization: 「利益にならないことは行なわれなくなるので、困る人も出てくる」 (Things that are not profitable will no longer be carried out, leaving some people in difficulty), citing the closure of village post offices and reductions in local train services as examples (「採算のとれないローカル線は、次々に廃止しており、犠牲を強いられている人もたくさんいるはずだ」).
default.q.n2-40-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice reverses the roles of the two authors: A is the one who fully agrees, while B points out the issue.
default.q.n2-40-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「最近読んだ本の内容はよく覚えている」 does not belong to Hebb’s learning mechanism, in which neural pathways are reinforced through repeated activity.
default.q.n2-40-q71-71.explanation:
• Main point: Hebb's rule explains the human learning mechanism through the transmission of signals between neurons across synapses. When something is repeated many times (or when there is an extremely strong stimulus), the signaling pathway is strengthened and becomes more efficient, enabling the body to respond immediately or retain memories for a long time (for example, salivating at the sight of salted plums, recognizing faces, or typing). By contrast, simply remembering a book read recently is only short-term or temporary memory and does not reflect the establishment of neural pathways according to Hebb's rule.

• Translation of the question: Which is NOT consistent with the human learning mechanism identified by Donald Hebb?
• Translation of the choices:
1. Someone who is accustomed to eating salted plums salivates as soon as they see one.
2. Remembering very clearly the contents of a book read recently.
3. Knowing immediately who someone is just by looking at their face.
4. Being able to type accurately without looking at the keyboard.
default.q.n2-40-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this is an example that correctly illustrates the Hebbian rule quoted in the passage: 「例えば、私たち日本人は梅干しを食べ慣れているので、見たり想像したりしただけで口の中に唾...が出てきます」 Repeatedly eating pickled plums has formed a reflex pathway that triggers salivation.
default.q.n2-40-q71-71.why.1: (b) Correct because remembering something temporarily simply because it was read recently is short-term memory, not the result of repeated practice or extremely strong stimulation establishing a durable neural pathway (as the passage states: 「一夜漬けのように詰め込んだものは忘れてしまいがちです」).
default.q.n2-40-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this is an example that fits the Hebbian rule described in the passage: 「人間は繰り返し繰り返し、この作業を行っているため、効率的に区分することができます」 (people can recognize faces quickly because they repeatedly perform this process).
default.q.n2-40-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because touch-typing is developed through repeated practice, which perfectly matches the mechanism of transmitting signals through synapses repeatedly to optimize reaction speed.
default.q.n2-40-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Learning and memory can remain highly effective without repetition when learning is linked to a shocking event that provides strong stimulation and leaves a deep impression.
default.q.n2-40-q72-72.explanation:
• Main idea: According to Hebb's rule, synapses undergo long-term changes and become more efficient at transmitting signals in two cases: (1) a signal is transmitted repeatedly along the same pathway, OR (2) even if it occurs only once, it involves extremely strong stimulation or arousal (a shocking experience or an unforgettable impression).

• Question translation: In which case can learning still be highly effective even without repetition?
• Answer choices:
1. A case in which the person practiced very slowly and carefully, even if only once.
2. A case in which the person had to learn quickly because there was not enough time.
3. A case in which learning was accompanied by a shocking, unforgettable event that left a strong impression on memory.
4. A case in which the person studied under the guidance of someone and in an atmosphere of trust.
default.q.n2-40-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage never mentions that practicing 「ゆっくりていねいに練習」 once would produce changes in synaptic function.
default.q.n2-40-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that material crammed in a short time when there is no time available, such as 「一夜漬け」, is easily forgotten: 「一夜漬けのように詰め込んだものは忘れてしまいがちです」.
default.q.n2-40-q72-72.why.2: (c) Correct because the passage states: 「あるいはたった 1 回であっても強力な興奮が伝達されたりした場合、そのシナプスに長期的な変化が起こり、ニ...ーロン同士の信号の伝達効率がよくなると考えたのです」 (Even if strong stimulation is transmitted only once, a long-term change occurs in the synapse, improving the efficiency of signal transmission between neurons.) This corresponds to learning accompanied by a powerful, unforgettable experience.
default.q.n2-40-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention a tutor or trust during the learning process.
default.q.n2-40-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 1: When something happens repeatedly, the brain establishes efficient neural pathways, enabling people to respond more quickly.
default.q.n2-40-q73-73.explanation:
• Main point: Donald Hebb explains the brain's mechanism: when the same stimulus is received repeatedly, the synapses connecting neurons form an efficient transmission route (効率的な伝達ルート), enabling the body to respond quickly and making predictions and judgments more easily.

• Question translation: How did Donald Hebb explain the mechanism of the human brain?
• Answer choices:
1. When similar events occur repeatedly, people respond to them more quickly.
2. The human brain treats every object and event as a new experience.
3. People are born with a processing program like a computer.
4. The human brain contains a mechanism that prevents people from ever forgetting anything, even if they experience it only once.
default.q.n2-40-q73-73.why.0: (a) Correct because the reading clearly states: 「すなわち、よく受ける刺激に対する反応は頭の中に効率的な伝達ルートが確立するため、すぐに身体が反応したり、予想や判断がしやすくなったりするのです」 (Frequently received stimuli establish efficient transmission routes in the brain, allowing the body to respond immediately and making prediction and judgment easier.)
default.q.n2-40-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the brain does not treat everything as a new experience; repeated stimuli already follow previously established neural pathways.
default.q.n2-40-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the article says that humans differ from computers in their ability to process things flexibly through repeated practice («人間は繰り返し繰り返し、この作業を行っているため...»), not that they are born with a fixed processing program like a computer.
default.q.n2-40-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the human brain does not retain everything permanently after a single ordinary experience. In reality, things crammed in over a short period are easily forgotten («一夜漬けのように詰め込んだものは忘れてしまいがちです»).
default.q.n2-40-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 3: カフェスタッフ（C店） (café staff / Event C) is the job that best fits the conditions of short-term work and flexible hours.
default.q.n2-40-q74-74.explanation:
- Main point: The information summarizes six part-time job listings (A through F), each with specific requirements concerning applicants' age, education, and experience, as well as the workplace, working hours, pay, and application method. Job C is a short-term event/café position with flexible scheduling—you can work for just one day—and is suitable for students who want to work in their free time.
