  1. Bookstore employee (Store A)
  2. Convenience-store employee (Store B)
  3. Café/event staff (Store C)
  4. Tutor (Company D)
default.q.n2-40-q74-74.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because job A requires a fixed schedule—“those able to work 2–3 days per week” (週 2 日～ 3 日勤務可能な方)—and shift ③ does not allow minors (未成年不可), so it does not meet the requirements for flexibility or personal circumstances.
default.q.n2-40-q74-74.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because Job B (焼肉 ジュージュー亭) requires night shifts from evening until early morning, 「午後 5 時～午前 2 時」, requires applicants who can work 「週 3 日～ 5 日勤務可能な方」, and does not accept high school students for late-night shifts, 「高校生不可」.
default.q.n2-40-q74-74.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct. Passage C clearly states: 「短期 イベント会場運営＆設営スタッフ募集！！」「高校生以上☆学生・フリーターさんなど！！」「未経験 OK 好きなときに働きたい方歓迎！！」「勤務日・勤務時間： 不定期 ★ 1 日でも OK ！」, which fully matches the requirements for short-term work with flexible hours.
default.q.n2-40-q74-74.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the E/D job (家庭教師) recruits only university students 「大学生・家庭教師募集」, sets the hourly wage according to teaching experience 「指導経験に応じて時給が決まります」, and requires applicants to send a résumé with a photo 「履歴書（写真付き）送付」.
default.q.n2-40-q75-75.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Choice 4 (taking advantage of extra shifts on days off/Sundays) is the key factor that allows Yamamoto to maximize the number of shifts and earn the highest weekly income.
default.q.n2-40-q75-75.explanation:
- Summary of the passage: The reading provides job postings with different working conditions:
  + A: Some shifts do not allow minors (③ は未成年不可).
  + B: A yakiniku restaurant, evening shifts from 5:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m.; high school students are not allowed to work the night shift (高校生不可).
  + C: Short-term event work with no fixed schedule (even one day is acceptable), for high school students and above, paying 3,800 to 15,500 yen per day.
  + D: Applicants must be at least 18 years old (18歳以上).
  + E: University students are being recruited as tutors.
  + F: Sorting goods in a warehouse near Mitani Station (bicycles and motorcycles allowed), working 5–8 hours per day, with Saturdays and Sundays off.
  Yamamoto is a 17-year-old high school student who has cram school on Tuesdays and Thursdays. He wants to work after 5:00 p.m. on weekdays and work all day on days off to earn as much as possible.
- Translation of the question: Which part-time job would allow Yamamoto to earn the highest income in one week? Yamamoto’s conditions are as follows.
- Translation of the choices:
  1. A 12th-grade male student (17 years old). He lives near Mitani Station.
  2. He can commute by bicycle.
  3. On weekdays, he wants to work part-time after 5:00 p.m., but he attends cram school on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
  4. He wants to work on days off, including Sundays.
default.q.n2-40-q75-75.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because this is a condition concerning age and residence. Yamamoto is a 12th-grade student (17 years old, under 18) and lives near Mitani Station, so they are excluded from jobs that do not accept high-school students or anyone under 18, such as B (焼肉 - 「高校生不可」), shift ③ at A (「③ は未成年不可」), and D (「18 歳以上」).
default.q.n2-40-q75-75.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is incorrect because this is a condition concerning transportation (being able to commute by bicycle); it is merely a condition that meets job F’s requirements (「自転車・バイク通勤 OK」), not the factor determining the highest income.
default.q.n2-40-q75-75.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this condition limits work on weekdays: the person can work only after 5 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday because of supplementary classes on Tuesday and Thursday. Thus, relying only on weekdays restricts the total number of working hours per week.
default.q.n2-40-q75-75.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct. Working on holidays, including Sundays, allows Yamamoto to maximize working time. Combined with jobs suitable for high school students, such as C (「不定期 ★ 1 日でも OK ！」「日給 3,800 円～ 15,500 円」) or F (「1 日 5h ～ 8h 勤務」「週 2 日以上できる方歓迎」), working on holidays would produce the highest total weekly income.
default.q.n2-40-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 上がった (combined to form the intransitive verb 仕上がる, meaning to be completed or finished being sewn).
default.q.n2-40-q11-11.explanation:
Meaning: "The clothes I ordered have been completed."
- Kanji and vocabulary: 仕上がる (しあがる: to be completed, finished - intransitive verb), 仕上げる (しあげる: to complete or finish something - transitive verb).
- Example: クリーニングに出していたスーツが綺麗に仕上がった。(The suit I had sent to the cleaners was finished beautifully.)
default.q.n2-40-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「仕終山った」: The kanji is incorrect (終山), and this combination does not exist. If the intended form is 「し終わる」, it describes a person finishing an action and does not take 「が」 to mark a completed object.
default.q.n2-40-q11-11.why.1: (b) 「し終えた」: 「～終える」is a transitive verb indicating that a person completes an action (e.g., 宿題をし終えた), so it does not combine with the inanimate subject 「洋服が」.
default.q.n2-40-q11-11.why.2: (c) 「上がった」 combines with 「し（仕）」 to form the intransitive verb 「仕上がる」（しあがる）, meaning that clothing, a product, or a work has been completed or finished. It fits the subject 「洋服が」 perfectly.
default.q.n2-40-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「上げた」 combines to form the transitive verb 「仕上げる」 (しあげる: to complete or finish something), which requires an object marked by 「を」, as in 洋服を仕上げた, not 「洋服が」.
default.q.n2-40-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 力 (forming the adjective 力強い: strong, vigorous, full of vitality).
default.q.n2-40-q12-12.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: "His paintings use powerful lines and bold colors."
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 力強い（ちからづよい - POWERFUL: strong, vigorous, assertive), 手強い（てごわい - FORMIDABLE: difficult, tough to beat), 心強い（こころづよい - REASSURING: reassuring, giving confidence).
- Example: 彼の力強いスピーチを聞いて、勇気が湧いてきた。(After hearing his powerful speech, I felt courage welling up inside me.)
default.q.n2-40-q12-12.why.0: (a) 「体」: The compound 「体強い」 does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n2-40-q12-12.why.1: (b) 「手」 forms the adjective 「手強い」(てごわい), meaning “formidable, tough, challenging,” commonly used for an opponent or difficult problem. It is not used to describe artistic lines or colors.
default.q.n2-40-q12-12.why.2: (c) 「力」: Combined with 「強い」, it forms the adjective 「力強い」（ちからづよい）, meaning "powerful, vigorous, assertive, full of vitality." It naturally modifies 「線と色」 (lines and colors).
default.q.n2-40-q12-12.why.3: (d) 「心」 forms the adjective 「心強い」（こころづよい）, meaning “reassuring” or “giving peace of mind” when one has support or something to rely on. It is not suitable for describing lines in a painting.
default.q.n2-40-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 非 (a prefix that forms 非常識: lacking common sense, improper, or ill-mannered).
default.q.n2-40-q13-13.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "That person lacks common sense and manners, so everyone finds them troublesome."
- Distinguishing Sino-Japanese prefixes:
  + 非（ひ - HI: contrary to standards or rules）: 非常識 (lacking common sense), 非公式 (unofficial), 非公開 (private, not open to the public).
  + 不（ふ - FU: not）: 不真面目 (not serious), 不安 (anxiety, unease).
  + 無（む - MU: without, lacking）: 無責任 (irresponsible), 無関心 (indifferent, unconcerned).
  + 未（み - MI: not yet）: 未成年 (minor), 未定 (undecided).
- Example: 夜中に大音量で音楽を流すのは非常識だ。(Playing music at high volume in the middle of the night is really inconsiderate.)
default.q.n2-40-q13-13.why.0: (a) 「不」is a negative prefix meaning “not” or “un-” (e.g., 不可能, 不親切, 不都合); it does not combine with 常識, as 不常識 is not a Japanese word.
default.q.n2-40-q13-13.why.1: (b) 「未」: a prefix meaning "not yet" or "incomplete" (as in 未成年, 未完成, 未経験); it does not combine with 常識.
default.q.n2-40-q13-13.why.2: (c) 「無」: a prefix meaning “without, lacking” (as in 無責任, 無関心, 無意味...); it does not combine with 常識, so 無常識 is not used.
default.q.n2-40-q13-13.why.3: (d) 「非」 is a prefix meaning "anti-" or "contrary to." Combined with 「常識」, it forms the noun/na-adjective 「非常識」（ひじょうしき）, referring to behavior or a person lacking awareness of ordinary norms and manners.
default.q.n2-40-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 通り (forms the noun 人通り, meaning pedestrian traffic or the flow of people along a street).
default.q.n2-40-q14-14.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “At night, there are few people walking along this street.”
- Vocabulary and kanji readings: 人通り（ひとどおり - people passing along a street; 人通りが多い: many people passing by / 人通りが少ない: few people passing by).
- Related terms: 人出（ひとで - crowds of people going out for entertainment or sightseeing), 交通量（こうつうりょう - traffic volume).
- Example: この商店街は夜遅くまで人通りが絶えない。(People continue passing through this shopping district until late at night.)
default.q.n2-40-q14-14.why.0: (a) 「集まり」: There is no compound 「人集まり」; to refer to a gathering of people, use 「人の集まり」 or 「集まり」.
default.q.n2-40-q14-14.why.1: (b) 「通り」: Combined with 「人」, it forms the noun 「人通り」（ひとどおり）, meaning “pedestrian traffic, the number of people passing by,” and is used with 「多い/少ない」to indicate whether a street is busy or quiet.
default.q.n2-40-q14-14.why.2: (c) 「帰り」: the compound 「人帰り」 does not exist; to express people returning from work, use 「仕事帰りの人」.
default.q.n2-40-q14-14.why.3: (d) 「行き」: it does not form the noun 「人行き」; to refer to people coming and going, use a phrase such as 「行き交う人々」.
default.q.n2-40-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 切れ (forms the verb 売り切れる: to sell out completely, be sold out).
default.q.n2-40-q15-15.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: “That magazine just sold out a little while ago.” (Note: 「注っき」 in the question is a typographical error for 「さっき」, meaning “a little while ago.”)
- Vocabulary: 売り切れる（うりきれる）: to sell out completely, to be sold out (intransitive verb); 売り切る: to sell out all the stock (transitive verb); 売り切れ: sold-out condition / sold out.
- Related words: 売り出す（うりだす: to put on sale, launch on the market), 売れ行き（うれゆき: sales performance, consumer demand).
- Example: その限定版の雑誌は、発売当日に全て売り切れてしまった。(That limited-edition magazine sold out completely on the day it was released.)
default.q.n2-40-q15-15.why.0: (a) 「止め」 combines to form 「売り止める」（うりとめる: stop selling / suspend sales）, and is not used to express that goods have just completely sold out.
default.q.n2-40-q15-15.why.1: (b) 「返し」: It forms 「売り返す」(うりかえす: to sell back to someone), which does not fit the context of the magazine having sold out.
default.q.n2-40-q15-15.why.2: (c) 「切れ」: Combined with 「売り」, it forms the intransitive verb 「売り切れる」 (うりきれる → 売り切れました), meaning "to sell out completely" or "be sold out," which correctly describes the magazine having just sold out.
default.q.n2-40-q15-15.why.3: (d) 「消し」: The compound verb 「売り消す」does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n2-40-q16-16.explanation:
Overall meaning: “To maintain product quality, various preservation technologies are being researched.”
- Kanji note: 維持 (maintenance, preservation).
- Example: 健康を維持するために、毎日運動しています。(I exercise every day to maintain my health.)
default.q.n2-40-q16-16.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 連続 (れんぞく) means occurring continuously without interruption, as in 連続勝利 (consecutive victories), and does not combine with 質を... to mean maintaining quality.
default.q.n2-40-q16-16.why.1: (b) Correct. 維持 (いじ) means maintaining an existing state or good quality, and naturally combines in 「商品の質を維持する」(maintain product quality).
default.q.n2-40-q16-16.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 普及 (ふきゅう) means spreading widely among people, as in スマートフォンの普及; it does not fit the meaning of preserving quality.
default.q.n2-40-q16-16.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 催促 (さいそく) means urging or pressing someone to do something (e.g., 借金の返済を催促する - urge someone to repay a debt), so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-40-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (感じられる).
default.q.n2-40-q17-17.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “What you say seems rather selfish / unreasonable to me.” (Note: 「山がまま」 in the question is an OCR error for 「わがまま」, meaning selfish or self-centered.)
- Kanji: 感じられる (to feel, be perceived).
- Example: 彼の態度は少し冷たいと感じられる。(His attitude seems somewhat cold.)
default.q.n2-40-q17-17.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 生じられる is the passive/potential form of 生じる (しょうじる, to arise or occur), and it cannot be used with 「〜だと...」 to express a subjective impression.
default.q.n2-40-q17-17.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 報じられる is the passive form of 報じる (ほうじる - to report or announce through the media or press), so it is not used for a personal impression.
default.q.n2-40-q17-17.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 信じられる is the potential form of 信じる (しんじる: to believe), usually expressing whether something can be believed. It is unnatural with 「私には〜だと...」 when stating an impression or evaluation of someone's character or words.
default.q.n2-40-q17-17.why.3: (d) Correct. 感じられる is the spontaneous/potential form of 感じる (かんじる, “to feel”), forming the pattern 「私には〜だと感じられる」 (“to me, it feels as though...” / “I feel that...” ).
default.q.n2-40-q18-18.explanation:
Meaning of the whole sentence: “My older brother has belonged to the personnel department ever since he joined the company.” (Note: 「人中課」 in the question is an OCR error for 「人事課」 - the personnel department.)
- Kanji meaning: 属する (belong to, be affiliated with).
- Example: 私はマーケティング部に属しています。(I belong to the marketing department.)
default.q.n2-40-q18-18.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 対して comes from 対する (たいする: toward, directed at, in comparison with), and the structure 「〜に対して」 is not used to indicate belonging to a department.
default.q.n2-40-q18-18.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 面して comes from 面する (めんする - to face, to face toward a direction; e.g., 海に面している - facing the sea), and is not used for organizations or departments.
default.q.n2-40-q18-18.why.2: (c) Correct. 属して comes from 属する (ぞくする - to belong to, be affiliated with), and with the particle に forms 「〜課に属している」(belonging to or being affiliated with a particular department).
default.q.n2-40-q18-18.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 彙して is a nonexistent compound; 彙 is the kanji found in 語彙 (vocabulary), and there is no verb 彙する in this context.
default.q.n2-40-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning: “My child had a fever, the refrigerator broke down, and last week I really went through a terrible time.” (Note: 「あ流 た」is an OCR error for 「あった」in the expression 「目にあった」.)
- Fixed expression: ひどい目にあう (to have a terrible experience, go through hardship).
- Example: 旅行中、財布を盗まれてひどい目にあった。(While traveling, my wallet was stolen and I went through a terrible ordeal.)
default.q.n2-40-q19-19.why.0: (a) Incorrect. おしい (惜しい - regrettable, a shame) is used when something good was nearly achieved or something was wasted; it is not used with 「〜目にあう」.
default.q.n2-40-q19-19.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Although まずい can mean “bad” or “dangerous,” the standard Japanese idiom for having a bad experience is 「ひどい目に遭う」, not 「まずい目に遭う」.
default.q.n2-40-q19-19.why.2: (c) Incorrect. のろい (鈍い - slow) refers to speed or slowness and is completely unsuitable for the context.
default.q.n2-40-q19-19.why.3: (d) Correct. ひどい combines with 目にあう to form the fixed idiom 「ひどい目にあう / ひどい目に遭う」, meaning to experience something terrible, suffer greatly, or have bad luck.
default.q.n2-40-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (い流せいに - いっせいに / 一斉に).
default.q.n2-40-q20-20.explanation:
Meaning of the entire sentence: 'The traffic light turned green, and the cars that had been stopped all set off at once.' (Note: In the test, OCR errors changed the small 「っ」 in the adverb and changed 「緑/青」 to 「採」; the original answer was 一斉に - いっせいに: all at once.)
- Kanji etymology: 一斉 (all together, simultaneously).
- Example: 鳥たちが一斉に空へ飛び立った。(The birds all flew into the sky at once.)
default.q.n2-40-q20-20.why.0: (a) Incorrect. いっそうに, from 一層 (いっそう), means "even more" or "to a greater degree," indicating an increase in degree, as in 寒さが一層厳しくなる. It does not indicate multiple subjects acting simultaneously.
default.q.n2-40-q20-20.why.1: (b) Incorrect. いっぱんに, from 一般に, means “generally, ordinarily, in general” (e.g., 一般に言われている, “commonly said”). It does not fit the context of vehicles departing.
default.q.n2-40-q20-20.why.2: (c) Correct. い流せいに (the original is 一斉に - いっせいに) means “all at once” or “simultaneously,” describing the cars starting to move together when the signal changes.
default.q.n2-40-q20-20.why.3: (d) Incorrect. いったん (一旦 - 一旦) means temporarily, for a while, or once something has happened... (e.g., いったん休憩しよう), so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-40-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (まごまご).
default.q.n2-40-q21-21.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “When I was confused and bewildered after getting off at the station for the first time, a stranger kindly showed me the way.”
- Mimetic word: まごまご (to be confused, flustered, or unsure what to do).
- Example: 案内図を見ても行き先が分からず、まごまごしてしまった。(Even after looking at the map, I did not know where to go and became completely confused.)
default.q.n2-40-q21-21.why.0: (a) Incorrect. ぶつぶつ is an onomatopoeic word describing muttering or grumbling under one’s breath, or small pimples (e.g., ぶつぶつ文句を言う); it does not fit a situation involving asking for directions.
default.q.n2-40-q21-21.why.1: (b) Correct. まごまご is an onomatopoeic expression describing a confused, bewildered state in which someone does not know the way or how to deal with a situation in an unfamiliar place (まごまごする: to be confused, bewildered).
default.q.n2-40-q21-21.why.2: (c) Incorrect. はきはき describes speaking or behaving clearly, briskly, and energetically (e.g., はきはき答える, “answer clearly and confidently”), which is contrary to the context of someone giving directions.
default.q.n2-40-q21-21.why.3: (d) Incorrect. もともと (元々) is an adverb meaning “originally, from the beginning,” not a word describing an accompanying action with「〜していたら」.
default.q.n2-40-q22-22.explanation:
Overall meaning: 'This law is interpreted differently by different scholars.' (Note: 「ぐ律」 in the question is an OCR error for 「法律」 - law.)
Sino-Japanese reading: 解釈 (interpretation, understanding).
Example: 文脈によってその言葉の解釈が異なる。(The interpretation of the word differs depending on the context.)
default.q.n2-40-q22-22.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 解散 (かいさん) means to dissolve a group, meeting, or parliament (e.g., 国会を解散する); it has nothing to do with understanding or interpreting laws.
default.q.n2-40-q22-22.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 解決 (かいけつ — resolution) means solving a problem or conflict (e.g., 問題を解決する); it is not used to mean interpreting or defining a law.
default.q.n2-40-q22-22.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 解放 (かいほう – liberation) means to release someone from restraints or set them free (e.g., 束縛から解放される), so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-40-q22-22.why.3: (d) Correct. 解釈 (かいしゃく) means interpreting or understanding the meaning of a text or law. 「法律の解釈がちがう」 is a standard expression referring to a difference in the interpretation of a law.
default.q.n2-40-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 4. ただ (merely, simply).
default.q.n2-40-q23-23.explanation:

default.q.n2-40-q23-23.why.2: (c) 「簡単に」 means “simply” or “easily,” referring to the degree of complexity or ease of an action. It is not equivalent to 「単に」, meaning “merely” or “just.”
default.q.n2-40-q23-23.why.3: (d) 「ただ」 means "only / merely" and is a perfect synonym of 「単に」; both combine with 「〜だけ」 to form the pattern 単に／ただ〜だけ: "it is merely...".

default.q.n2-40-q28-28.explanation:
「高尚」（こうしょう）is a na-adjective used to describe thoughts, education, art, or hobbies that are sophisticated, refined, and elevated, focusing on intellectual or spiritual values rather than trivial matters. Common expressions include: 高尚な趣味 (a refined hobby), 高尚な思想 (an elevated philosophy), 高尚な話題 (an intellectually elevated topic).

default.q.n2-40-q28-28.why.2: Incorrect because 「高尚」is not used for places or neighborhoods; an upscale, elegant residential area should be described as 「高級（な）」or「閑静（な）」.
default.q.n2-40-q28-28.why.3: Incorrect because 「高尚」is not used to describe objects or merchandise; an expensive or high-end watch should be described as 「高価（な）」or「高級（な）」.
default.q.n2-40-q29-29.explanation:
「相応」（そうおう）is a noun or na-adjective meaning appropriate or proportionate to one's ability, contribution, status, position, or circumstances. Common uses: 相応の＋N (相応の待遇, appropriate treatment; 相応の報酬, appropriate compensation), 年相応 (appropriate for one's age), 身分相応 (appropriate to one's status).
Example: 彼の努力に見合った相応の評価を受けるべきだ。(He deserves an evaluation commensurate with his efforts.)
default.q.n2-40-q29-29.why.0: Incorrect because when something corresponds to a specific ratio or number, such as one-sixth of Earth's gravity, the verb 「相当する」must be used, not 「相応する」.
default.q.n2-40-q29-29.why.1: This is incorrect because when something matches or satisfies a specific standard or condition, use 「該当する」(がいとうする) or 「当てはまる」.
default.q.n2-40-q29-29.why.2: Incorrect because the appropriate amount of seasoning in cooking is expressed with 「適量」（てきりょう）or 「見合った量」, not 「相応」.
default.q.n2-40-q29-29.why.3: Correct because 「相応の待遇」 (“待遇 appropriate or proportionate to one’s contribution or ability”) is a natural and accurate use of 「相応」.
default.q.n2-40-q30-30.explanation:
「にじむ」（滲む） is an intransitive verb used when a liquid (water, ink, blood, sweat, or tears) spreads across a surface, causing an image or writing to become blurred, or when light or emotion gradually shows through. Common expressions: 字がにじむ (the writing becomes blurred), 涙がにじむ (tears well up), 血がにじむ (blood oozes).
Example: 雨でぬれて、手紙の文字がにじんで読めなくなった。(The letter got wet in the rain, and the writing became blurred and unreadable.)
default.q.n2-40-q30-30.why.0: Correct because「にじむ」is appropriate when water causes writing or ink to bleed and become blurred.
default.q.n2-40-q30-30.why.1: Incorrect because a runny nose caused by a cold is expressed with 「鼻水が出る」, while nasal congestion uses 「鼻がつまる」; 「にじむ」 is not used for the nose.
default.q.n2-40-q30-30.why.2: Because speaking too much causes the voice to become hoarse or disappear, use 「声がかすれる」 or 「声が枯れる」（かれる）, not 「にじむ」.
default.q.n2-40-q30-30.why.3: This is incorrect because when food absorbs seasoning deeply, use 「味が染みる」(しみる) or 「味が染み込む」(しみこむ), not 「にじむ」.
default.q.n2-40-q31-31.explanation:
「欠如」（けつじょ）is a noun and a する verb meaning a lack or absence of abstract qualities that should be present, such as awareness, responsibility, morality, trust, or concreteness. Common expressions: 自覚の欠如 (lack of self-awareness), 責任感の欠如 (lack of a sense of responsibility), 道徳心の欠如 (lack of moral sense).
Example: 彼の計画は具体性に欠如している。(His plan lacks concreteness.)
default.q.n2-40-q31-31.why.0: It is incorrect because money is a concrete material thing. When it is lacking or runs out, use 「不足する」,「足りなくなる」, or 「底をつく」, not 「欠如」.
default.q.n2-40-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because lost or missing books and other objects are expressed with「なくなる」or「紛失する」; if a book is missing pages, use「落丁する」, not「欠如」.
default.q.n2-40-q31-31.why.2: Correct because 「自覚が欠如している」 (lacking awareness or self-discipline) is an accurate standard combination for expressing the absence of an abstract quality or awareness that one should have.
default.q.n2-40-q31-31.why.3: Incorrect because when someone is absent from a sports match, 「欠場する」 (けつじょうする) or 「欠席する」 should be used; 「欠如」 is not used for people.
default.q.n2-40-q32-32.explanation:
「案の定」（あんのじょう - just as expected, as predicted）is an adverb placed before a predicate or clause to indicate that something happened exactly as previously expected or feared. It often accompanies a bad or undesirable result, or something serving as a warning.
Example: 危ないと思っていたら、案の定事故が起きてしまった。(I thought it was dangerous, and sure enough, an accident occurred.)
default.q.n2-40-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because 「案の定」 is an adverb that modifies a verb or predicate; it cannot be used as a noun predicate with 「だ」. 「予想通りだ」 should be used here.
default.q.n2-40-q32-32.why.1: Correct because 「案の定」 is an adverb meaning “as expected” or “sure enough.” It comes before a verb to describe a negative development occurring as predicted: the sky was cloudy, and it did indeed rain.
default.q.n2-40-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because expressing “turning a dream into reality” requires 「夢が現実になる」 or 「夢が叶う」; 「案の定」 cannot modify a positive change of state such as a dream coming true.

default.q.n2-5-q49-49.verdict: Correct order: 2 → 1 → 3 → 4 (the ★ position is answer choice 3: つまり).
default.q.n2-5-q49-49.explanation: このプロジェクトのテーマは「エコ」、すなわちエコロジー、つまり環境を考えるということです。(The theme of this project is 「エコ」, namely ecology—in other words, thinking about the environment.)
default.q.n2-5-q49-49.why.0: (a) 「すなわちエコロジー、」 follows 「テーマは「エコ」、」 to explain that the abbreviation “Eco” means ecology.
default.q.n2-5-q49-49.why.1: (b) 「テーマは「エコ」、」 combines with the possessive phrase 「このプロジェクトの」at the beginning of the sentence to form the main subject.
default.q.n2-5-q49-49.why.2: (c) 「つまり」is a conjunction used to explain or summarize (“in other words/to sum up”); it stands at ★ to introduce the definition of the nature of the action that follows.
default.q.n2-5-q49-49.why.3: (d) 「環境を考える」 is a predicate phrase (“to think about the environment”) and combines directly with the concluding pattern 「ということです」.
default.q.n2-5-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 1. にあったては (the correct form is にあたっては): It indicates the time of or occasion for an important event.
default.q.n2-5-q50-50.explanation: This is a thank-you letter and work update sent to a teacher who provided assistance and introduced the writer to a job. The letter opens by expressing gratitude for the milestone of seeking employment: 「就職にあたっては、大変お世話になりました」(Thank you very much for all your help when I was looking for a job). The N2 grammar pattern 「N + にあたって（は）」is commonly used in formal contexts to refer to the beginning of a major event or an important turning point in one's life.
default.q.n2-5-q50-50.why.0: (a) Reasonable: The grammar 「N + にあたって（は）」 means "on the occasion of" or "when beginning a major event," such as starting a job, entering school, or getting married. Here, 「就職にあたっては、大変お世話になりました」 expresses deep gratitude for the help received when starting a job search. Although choice 1 contains a minor typographical error (にあったては), it is still the only grammatically correct answer.
default.q.n2-5-q50-50.why.1: (b) Illogical: 「～に沿って / にそっては」means "in accordance with / along" a policy, plan, or expectation. It cannot follow 「就職」to introduce a thank-you message marking an event.
default.q.n2-5-q50-50.why.2: (c) Inappropriate: 「にはたっては」 is not an existing Japanese grammar pattern; it is a misspelling.
default.q.n2-5-q50-50.why.3: (d) Illogical: 「～に応えて / にこたえては」 means “in response to” or “to meet” expectations, requests, cheers, and so on. It does not combine with 「就職」 to begin a thank-you statement.
default.q.n2-5-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 次第では means that the result or possibility may change depending on...
default.q.n2-5-q51-51.explanation: This passage describes the writer's current work situation: although they are currently in charge of accounting, they may still have a chance to transfer to the sales department they originally hoped to join if they make the necessary effort (「努力次第では希望していた営業部へ移ることも可能だ」). The N2 grammar pattern 「N + 次第では」 is commonly used with nouns such as 努力 (effort), 成績 (performance), and 天気 (weather) to express that something may happen depending on that factor.
default.q.n2-5-q51-51.why.0: (a) Not reasonable: 「N + 向け」means "intended for/aimed at" a particular group (e.g., books for children, products for women). It is not used to express a condition dependent on the noun 「努力」.
default.q.n2-5-q51-51.why.1: (b) Inappropriate: 「～に先立ち / に先立って」 means “before starting” or “prior to an event,” and does not combine naturally with 「努力」.
default.q.n2-5-q51-51.why.2: (c) Reasonable. The grammar 「N + 次第だ / 次第では」 means “depending on N” or “the result is determined by N.” 「努力次第では...可能だ」 means that depending on one's efforts, transferring to the sales department is entirely possible, which is grammatically and contextually accurate.
default.q.n2-5-q51-51.why.3: (d) This is inappropriate: 「～に対し / に対する」means “toward / in contrast to” and does not express a condition that determines the result.
default.q.n2-5-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 見習いつつ: It describes two actions taking place simultaneously (learning by observing one's senior while remembering the work).
default.q.n2-5-q52-52.explanation: The blank requires a conjunction expressing the simultaneous performance of two actions while learning a job: learning by observing a senior colleague’s methods (先輩のやり方を見習う) while also learning the work itself (仕事を覚える). The grammar pattern 「V-masu + つつ」is a formal written expression equivalent to 「ながら」, making it suitable for a polite letter to a teacher or superior.
default.q.n2-5-q52-52.why.0: (a) Unreasonable: 「V-masu + 次第」means that something will be done immediately after V is completed. It is generally used with a completed action, followed by a future volitional action, so it does not go with the ongoing expression 「覚えているところです」.
default.q.n2-5-q52-52.why.1: (b) Not appropriate: 「V + くせに」 means “and yet,” and is used for negative criticism or sarcasm, which is completely contrary to the writer's humble attitude toward learning.
default.q.n2-5-q52-52.why.2: (c) The interpretation is unreasonable: 「V-ru + 上で」 means “in the process of doing V / when doing V, it is important or necessary to...”. The following clause is normally advice or a necessary condition, not a description of two simultaneous actions.
default.q.n2-5-q52-52.why.3: (d) Reasonable: The grammar 「V-masu + つつ」 means “while doing...” and is a formal expression equivalent to ながら. The sentence means: “At present, I am learning by following the methods of my predecessors while gradually memorizing the work.”
default.q.n2-5-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 2.使わざるを得ない: It expresses being forced by circumstances to do something, even if one is not good at it or does not want to do it.
default.q.n2-5-q53-53.explanation: The author presents the practical circumstances of the job: the company operates globally and involves frequent business trips, so the author is in a situation where they have no choice but to use even foreign languages they are not good at (苦手な外国語も使わざるを得ない状況). The pattern 「V-ざるを得ない」 expresses being forced by circumstances to do something despite not feeling confident or wanting to do it.
default.q.n2-5-q53-53.why.0: (a) Unreasonable: 「～にすぎない」 means “nothing more than” or “only,” which does not create a logical contrast with the following clause 「やりがいがあります」 (“the work is rewarding/meaningful”).
default.q.n2-5-q53-53.why.1: (b) Reasonable: The grammar 「V-nai (remove ない) + ざるを得ない」means "have no choice but to / be forced to do..." due to circumstances. Combined with 「苦手な外国語も」(although the foreign language is still difficult, one has no choice but to use it because the company operates globally), it forms a logical contrast with 「～状況ですが、やりがいがあります」.
default.q.n2-5-q53-53.why.2: (c) This is illogical: 「～べきではない」means “should not” or “must not,” which is completely contrary to the actual job requirement of using a foreign language.
default.q.n2-5-q53-53.why.3: (d) Inappropriate: 「使われつつある」 is a passive form combined with つつある (“is gradually coming to be used”), so it does not fit when the subject performing the action is the writer himself or herself.
default.q.n2-5-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 4. にこたえる: it combines with the noun 期待 to form the fixed expression 期待に応える, meaning “to meet or respond to expectations.”
default.q.n2-5-q54-54.explanation: At the end of the letter, the writer expresses determination and deep gratitude toward the teacher who introduced the job. In Japanese, the standard set expression for living up to someone’s expectations is 「～の期待に応える（こたえる）」. Combined with the purpose pattern 「～ことができるよう」 (“so that one can...” ), this is the most natural, accurate, and polite phrasing.
default.q.n2-5-q54-54.why.0: (a) Illogical: 「～にあたる」(～に当たる) means “correspond to” or “coincide with,” and does not combine with 期待 in a structure followed by ことができるよう.
default.q.n2-5-q54-54.why.1: (b) Not appropriate: 「～にかかわる」(～に関わる) means "to be related to / affect..." and is not used to express making an effort to live up to someone's expectations.
default.q.n2-5-q54-54.why.2: (c) Illogical: 「～に対する」(N + に対する + N) directly modifies the following noun and cannot be followed directly by 「ことができるよう」.
default.q.n2-5-q54-54.why.3: (d) Reasonable. The fixed expression 「期待に応える（にこたえる）」means “to meet or respond to someone's expectations.” The complete sentence is: 「先生のご期待にこたえることができるよう、これからもがんばります」(I will continue working hard so that I can live up to the expectations of the teacher who introduced me.)
default.q.n2-5-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 3: They value the role of forests in nature and believe that planting as many trees as possible is beneficial.
default.q.n2-5-q55-55.explanation:
**Main point of the passage:**
People often assume that planting trees is always beneficial. However, when trees are planted in arid regions, they may consume the limited water supply, even depleting groundwater and reducing the amount of water in rivers. The widespread belief that places too much emphasis on the role of forests while overlooking the natural water cycle is the “forest-planting myth” (the misconception that planting forests is inherently beneficial).

**Question translation:**
What is 「植林神話」?
(What does the “forest-planting myth” refer to?)

**Answer choices:**
1. To increase groundwater in arid regions, suitable tree species must be planted according to the environment.
2. The belief that the natural water cycle should be considered when choosing where to plant trees.
3. The belief that forests play an important role in nature and that planting as many trees as possible is beneficial.
4. Reconsidering the role of forests in arid regions and thinking about actively planting large numbers of trees.
default.q.n2-5-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Choice 1 proposes planting suitable trees to increase groundwater, whereas the passage states that planting trees in dry regions drains water and depletes groundwater. It does not mention the proposed solution.
default.q.n2-5-q55-55.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This choice expresses a sound idea that takes the natural cycle into account, which is the opposite of the "植林神話," a misconception caused by "forgetting the natural cycle" (自然の循環を忘れた).
default.q.n2-5-q55-55.why.2: (c) Correct. This matches the statements in the passage: 「木を植えることはいいことだ。われわれは無条件にそう考えがちだ。」 and 「森林の役割を重視したあまり、自然の循環を忘れた「植林神話」が世界に広がっているそうだ。」 In other words, people overemphasize the role of forests and assume that planting more trees is always good.
default.q.n2-5-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage warns that in dry regions (乾燥地帯), trees consume the scarce water supply and deplete groundwater; it does not support planting more and more trees (どんどん植える).
default.q.n2-5-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The retail agencies cooperated in distributing survey forms to customers.
default.q.n2-5-q56-56.explanation:
■ Main point:
The text is a business letter from the sales manager of Seito Pharmaceutical Company to distributors and retailers (「販売店各位」). To mark the first anniversary of the launch of “Energy Z,” the company wants to conduct a customer survey about the product’s price and effectiveness. Therefore, it asks the retailers to help distribute survey forms to customers who purchased the product.

■ Question translation:
The word 「ご協力」(cooperation) appears. Who is cooperating with what?

■ Answer choices:
1. The retailers cooperate in further increasing sales of this product.
2. The retailers cooperate by giving out survey forms to customers.
3. People who purchased the product cooperate by recommending it to others.
4. People who purchased the product cooperate by answering the survey.
default.q.n2-5-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the text only states that sales of the product have been growing steadily (「順調に売り上げを伸ばしてまいりました」). The purpose of the letter is not to ask the dealer to cooperate in increasing sales.
default.q.n2-5-q56-56.why.1: (b) Correct because the text is a letter to retail dealers ("販売店各位") requesting: 「本製品をお買い上げのお客様へのアンケート用紙の配布および ご協力の呼びかけをお願いいたします。販売店のみなさまにはご面倒をおかけいたしますが、よろしくお願い申し上げます。」 This clearly identifies the dealers as the people being asked to distribute survey forms to customers.
default.q.n2-5-q56-56.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage contains no information or requirement about the buyer recommending the product to others.
default.q.n2-5-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the people directly addressed and asked to cooperate are the retailers (「販売店各位」), and the main request is assistance with distributing the survey forms (「アンケート用紙の配布」).
default.q.n2-5-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 2: After use, the water is recycled, and all of it is supplied from the recycling equipment.
default.q.n2-5-q57-57.explanation:
- Main point: The passage discusses the International Space Station (ISS) and the extremely high cost of transporting water from Earth into space (300,000–400,000 yen per cup). In 2008, a device for recycling used water was installed to provide drinking water, water for experiments, and oxygen. Once the device operates fully, it will no longer be necessary to transport additional water from Earth.
- Translation of the question: According to the passage, what will happen to the water used on the International Space Station when the regeneration device is operating fully?
- Translation of the answer choices:
1. Water transported from Earth will be used for experiments and producing oxygen.
2. Used water will be recycled, and all water will be supplied by the regeneration device.
3. Water from Earth will be used for drinking, while the rest will be supplied by the regeneration device.
4. Both water transported from Earth and water produced by the regeneration device will be used.
default.q.n2-5-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that recycled water is used for drinking, experiments, and producing oxygen (「再生された水は飲料水や実験のほか、酸素を作り出すのにも使われる」), not that water from Earth is used for experiments and oxygen production.
default.q.n2-5-q57-57.why.1: (b) Correct. Evidence from the passage: 「ステーシ自ンで使用した水をリサイクルする装置が設置された」 and 「いずれ装置が完全に機能すれば、地球から新たに水を運ぶことも不要になる。」 (Once the device is fully operational, transporting additional water from Earth will no longer be necessary → all the water will be supplied by the recycling device).
default.q.n2-5-q57-57.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that recycled water is also used as drinking water (「再生された水は飲料水や...」); it does not say that drinking water must come from the Earth.
default.q.n2-5-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage clearly states that once the equipment is fully operational, it will no longer be necessary to transport new water from Earth (「地球から新たに水を運ぶことも不要になる」). It does not say that both sources will be used in parallel.
default.q.n2-5-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 1: It is an act intended to help the other person develop or improve.
default.q.n2-5-q58-58.explanation:
■ Main idea of the passage:
The passage distinguishes ordinary praise, which is a natural expression of emotion, from praise in “praise education.” In praise education, praise itself is not the original goal; rather, it is a highly intentional act designed to influence the other person’s psychology and behavior, motivate them, give them confidence, help them improve, and guide them in the direction desired by the educator.

■ Translation of the question:
What kind of behavior is praising someone in “praise education”?

■ Translation of the answer choices:
1. It is behavior intended to help the other person develop and improve.
2. It is behavior intended to guide the other person in the direction they themselves wish to take.
3. It is behavior that conveys exactly what one feels to the other person.
4. It is behavior intended to make the other person express their natural emotions.
default.q.n2-5-q58-58.why.0: (a) CORRECT. The passage clearly states: 「本来の目的は、ほめることを通して相手に影響を与えることです。相手の心と行動に影響を与え、やる気を出注せたり、自身をもたせたり、伸びていきようにする -------- 。」 (The true purpose is to influence the other person through praise—to influence their mind and behavior, motivate them, give them confidence, and help them grow and improve.)
default.q.n2-5-q58-58.why.1: (b) INCORRECT. This choice says to guide someone in the direction the other person themselves wants (相手自身が望む), whereas the passage states that the goal is to guide them in the direction desired by the teacher (「こ活らが望んでいるような方向へ向か山せることがねらいなのです」).
default.q.n2-5-q58-58.why.2: (c) INCORRECT. This choice describes the nature of ordinary praise, whereas the passage states that educational praise differs in this respect: it is not a natural expression of emotion but an extremely deliberate act with another purpose (「自然な気持ちのあらわれなどではなく、ほかのねらいをもった...き山めて意図的な行為です」).
default.q.n2-5-q58-58.why.3: (d) INCORRECT. The passage does not mention praising someone to make them express their feelings naturally; the purpose of the praise here is to influence the other person and guide their behavior and progress.
default.q.n2-5-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 1: A capable worker is someone who devotes themselves fully to work suited to their strengths and skillfully avoids work that does not suit them.
default.q.n2-5-q59-59.explanation:
【Main point of the passage】
According to the author, the most important common characteristic of a "capable person" (仕事ができる人) is being good at analyzing their own abilities, clearly identifying their strengths and weaknesses. In reality, a capable person is not someone who can do everything, but someone who actively handles tasks that match their strengths and skillfully avoids tasks that do not.

【Question translation】
What does this author consider to be the characteristic of a "capable person"?

【Answer choices】
1. Give one's utmost effort to work that suits one's abilities and skillfully avoid work that does not.
2. Always strive to improve one's abilities and actively take on every task.
3. Learn how to work from people who can do everything and overcome one's weaknesses.
4. First determine whether a task matches one's abilities...
default.q.n2-5-q59-59.why.0: (a) Correct. The supporting sentence is: 「『得意な仕事』を積極的にこなし、『不得意な仕事』からは上手に逃げている 人が、実は｢仕事ができる人｣と評価されるのだ。」 (In fact, people who actively handle their strong points and skillfully avoid their weak points are evaluated as "people who are capable at work."), which is completely equivalent in meaning to choice 1.
default.q.n2-5-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not say that people should strive to improve their abilities or actively take on every task (何にでも積極的に取り組む). Instead, the author emphasizes knowing when to avoid things one is not good at.
default.q.n2-5-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. “All-mighty” (オールマイテイ) is mentioned only as an example of a small number of exceptionally capable people; the author does not advise readers to imitate them to overcome their weaknesses (不得意なことを克服する).
default.q.n2-5-q59-59.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This choice does not state the author's main point about people who are capable: they understand their own strengths and weaknesses, make use of their strengths, and skillfully avoid tasks that expose their weaknesses.
default.q.n2-5-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The author finds it strange because the child who eats the baked goods is the one receiving the benefit, yet the expression 「〜もらえる」(“get them to eat it for me”) makes the baker sound like the recipient of a favor or benefit.
default.q.n2-5-q60-60.explanation:
- Question translation: Which of the following explanations by the author is the most appropriate?
- Answer choices:
  1. The ones who should benefit were the children eating the cake, but the expression "get the children to eat it" makes the baker seem like the beneficiary.
  2. When children are hungry, they will find something to eat themselves, so spending time making cake to make them happy is a waste of time.
  3. Children today are so overnourished that they need to diet, so making cake for them to eat is merely the parents' self-satisfaction.
  4. Children will like a tasty cake regardless of its shape, so there is no point in taking the trouble to make a soccer-ball-shaped cake.
- Main point: The author finds it paradoxical and disagrees when the mother says, "This way, the children will happily eat it for me" (喜んで食べてもらえる). Eating begins with the eater's need for survival when hungry—the child is the beneficiary—not with the child doing a favor for the person who made the cake.
default.q.n2-5-q60-60.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage says:「『喜んで食べてもらえる』という言葉に強い違和感を覚えた」「子供たちには別に食べてもらわなくてもいい。腹が空けば、彼らは食べる。」 In essence, children eat for their own benefit when they are hungry, but when the mother uses「〜もらえる」, it makes the children's eating the cake sound like a favor or benefit to the person who made it.
default.q.n2-5-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage says that fasting for one day can save parents the effort of cooking for one day; the author never says that painstakingly baking something to make the child happy is a "waste of time" (時間の無駄).
default.q.n2-5-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage only says that fasting helps parents lose weight (ダイエットにもなります); it does not say that children today are overnourished and need to lose weight, or that baking for one’s children is a selfish form of parental gratification.
default.q.n2-5-q60-60.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author does not discuss whether making the sponge cake in the shape of a soccer ball has meaning (サッカーボール型のスポンジケーキにする意味はない). The focus is the strange feeling caused by the phrase 「食べてもらえる」.
default.q.n2-5-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Learning gratitude for food and feeling grateful for being alive.
default.q.n2-5-q61-61.explanation:
- Question translation: The passage says “learn many things.” For example, what did people learn?
- Answer choices:
  1. Rules of conduct in group life and general social knowledge.
  2. The importance of paying school lunch fees.
  3. Ways to save time and methods of losing weight.
  4. A sense of gratitude for being alive.
- Main point: The author emphasizes that meals help people learn and deeply understand gratitude for food, life, and the things that sustain us («食事をすることへの感謝»). Modern society is gradually losing this valuable lesson.
default.q.n2-5-q61-61.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The article does not mention “rules for group living or common social knowledge” (集団生活でのマナーや社会の常識).
default.q.n2-5-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Paying for school lunches (給食費を払う) is an unreasonable justification given by parents for demanding that the phrase 「いただきます」be abolished; it is not something that needs to be learned.
default.q.n2-5-q61-61.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Saving time and losing weight are merely secondary examples in the assumption that the whole family fasts for one day (親たちは食事を作る手間を省けるし、ダイエットにもなります), not the essential lesson learned from eating.
default.q.n2-5-q61-61.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「現代社会は食事をするということから、多くのことを学ぶ機会を失いつつある」「いつの間に多くの日本人は食事をすることへの感謝を忘れてしまったのでしょうか」. Through eating and saying 「いただきます」, people learn to appreciate the source of life and express gratitude for life and food.
default.q.n2-5-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author believes that 「いただきます」 (Itadakimasu) expresses gratitude for the meal, regardless of whether one has paid for it.
default.q.n2-5-q62-62.explanation:
- Question translation: The passage mentions "making a strange request to the school." Why does the author call it strange?
- Answer choices:
  1. Because the author thinks it is only natural for parents to pay for the meals.
  2. Because whether to say "Itadakimasu" should be up to the child.
  3. Because the author believes that "Itadakimasu" is an expression of gratitude for the meal.
  4. Because anyone says "Itadakimasu" before eating.
- Main point: The parents believe that "since they have paid for the meals, there is no need to say thank you (Itadakimasu)." The author finds this request strange because "Itadakimasu" expresses deep gratitude for the food and the meal that sustains people; paying for it cannot replace or erase that gratitude.
default.q.n2-5-q62-62.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author is not discussing whether parents paying for meals is self-evident; rather, the author criticizes using meal payments as an excuse to reject saying thanks before eating.
default.q.n2-5-q62-62.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The author does not believe that whether to say it is a child’s freedom (子供の自由). On the contrary, the author is surprised that there is even a debate about whether children should say thank you.
default.q.n2-5-q62-62.why.2: (c) Correct. The mother asks the school not to make her child say 『いただきます』, reasoning that 「給食費を払っているのだから」. The author responds: 「いつの間に多くの日本人は食事をすることへの感謝を忘れてしまったのでしょうか」, affirming that 『いただきます』 is an expression of gratitude for being given food.
default.q.n2-5-q62-62.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author does not argue simply that “it is something everyone says” as a majority trend, but emphasizes its essential meaning: gratitude for the meal.
default.q.n2-5-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 子供の幼稚園はどこがいいかと言うこと (which kindergarten would be best for one's child).
default.q.n2-5-q63-63.explanation:
- Summary: The author gives an example of a married couple discussing which kindergarten to choose for their child, but during the conversation they turn to personal attacks and stray from the original topic of discussion.
- Question translation: What does the phrase "the original topic" refer to?
- Answer choices:
  1. The responsibility parents must take for their child’s education.
  2. Which circumstances or situations should be discussed.
  3. How the couple should care for their child together.
  4. Which kindergarten would be best for their child.
default.q.n2-5-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not discuss parents’ responsibility for education; it only mentions an example of a married couple debating which preschool to choose for their child.
default.q.n2-5-q63-63.why.1: (b) Incorrect. “Under what circumstances should people discuss this?” is merely an opening question that guides the author’s essay, not the subject of a family discussion.
default.q.n2-5-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Childcare was only something the wife said to attack her husband when the argument began (“あんたなんかあの子の面倒をぜんぜん見てないじゃないの！”); it was not the original topic.
default.q.n2-5-q63-63.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage says: '子供をどの幼稚園に入れるかについて議論しているときに... これでは、① 本来のテーマ を離れ、醜い争いになってしまいます' and '「子供を どこの幼稚園に入れるか」という議論の目的は、どこの幼稚園に入れたら教育上最も望ましいか次を決めることです'. This shows that the original topic was choosing which kindergarten to send the child to.
default.q.n2-5-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 4. よい結論を得るために話し合うという点 (the point of discussing the matter together in order to reach the best conclusion).
default.q.n2-5-q64-64.explanation:
- Summary: The author explains that arguments at work or among friends serve the same purpose as a married couple discussing which school their child should attend: all of them aim to pool their wisdom and reach the best “landing point,” or conclusion.
- Question: Regarding [the content above], what does the author say is the same?
- Answer choices:
  1. They can easily turn into arguments and ugly conflicts.
  2. Everyone believes that only their own opinion is correct.
  3. The discussion continues as long as there is time.
  4. People discuss and exchange ideas together to reach the best conclusion.
default.q.n2-5-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author presents ugly disputes ('醜い争い') as a negative consequence of participants forgetting their original purpose. This is not the similarity the author wishes to emphasize when referring to discussions among friends.
default.q.n2-5-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Although everyone involved believes their own opinion is best, the common point here is that everyone is striving to find the best solution or outcome ('その「着地点」を目指すわけです'), not stubbornly insisting that they are right.
default.q.n2-5-q64-64.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not mention continuing the discussion as long as there is time.
default.q.n2-5-q64-64.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage says: 'どのような方針を打ち出せ消いい結果が出せるのかについて、お互いの頭専を結集し、その「着地点」を目指すわけです。 告 友人同士の議論も同じです', showing that the common feature of discussions is bringing together everyone’s ideas to reach the best conclusion or outcome.
default.q.n2-5-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 参加者が目的を共有していなければ有効な議論にならない (If the participants do not share the same purpose, the discussion will not be effective).
default.q.n2-5-q65-65.explanation:
- Summary: The author points out that the essence of discussion or debate is working together toward a common goal: reaching the best possible result or conclusion. If participants become absorbed in defending their own opinions and forget the purpose of the discussion, it will lead to meaningless arguments.
- Question translation: What does the author think about “debate/discussion”?
- Answer choices:
  1. Every aspect of daily life cannot be maintained without debate.
  2. If the participants do not share a common goal, the debate will not be effective.
  3. We discuss things in many different situations, but very few of them are important.
  4. Debate is for pooling opinions and ideas, while the conclusion is not important.
default.q.n2-5-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author only says that discussions take place in every aspect of daily life ('あらゆる場面で議論が行われます'); the author does not claim that life cannot continue without discussion.
default.q.n2-5-q65-65.why.1: (b) Correct. The author emphasizes that if people forget the purpose of their discussion ('何のために議論をしているのかを忘れてしまう'), it will stray from the topic and turn into an ugly quarrel ('本来のテーマを離れ、醜い争いになってしまいます'). Therefore, participants must share a common purpose and work toward the best possible outcome.
default.q.n2-5-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not say that discussions are rarely important ('重要な場合は少ない').
default.q.n2-5-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author states that discussion brings together collective intelligence in order to reach the best conclusion or point of agreement ('その「着地点」を目指すわけです'). Therefore, the conclusion is important, contrary to the statement that it is unimportant.
default.q.n2-5-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The character gained weight because they continuously ate greasy, high-calorie leftovers, such as snacks and fried chicken, at the pub where they worked part-time.
default.q.n2-5-q66-66.explanation:
- Main point and basis: The narrator says that while studying at an art university, she was poor and had no money, so she worked part-time washing dishes at an izakaya. Because she was extremely hungry, she ate leftover food abandoned by customers, such as snacks and deep-fried chicken—high-calorie, oily foods. This diet of leftovers caused her weight to increase from 38 kg to 55 kg (an increase of 15 kg).
- Translation of the question: The phrase “Cause of weight gain” appears. What cause is being referred to here?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. Because she ate only high-calorie foods such as leftovers from the izakaya.
  2. Although she was poor, she spent enough money specifically on food.
  3. Because she only attended a preparatory school and art school and did not exercise.
  4. Because her body naturally developed during the transition from high school student to art university student.
default.q.n2-5-q66-66.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states:「アルバイトで居酒屋の皿洗いをしてたの... 酔っぱらった客がツマミをたくさん注文して、それが手つかずで洗い場に戻って来やがったの... カラアゲが食道を通り抜けた瞬間... 栄養学的には偏った食生活だったけどとにかく食べるものがあるってのはうれしかった」. Because the character ate large amounts of high-calorie leftover food at the izakaya, they gained 15 kilograms.
default.q.n2-5-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage clearly states that the character was very poor and had no money (「貧乏よ」「お金が無くていつもお腹を空かせて働いてた」), not that he spent a lot of money on food and drink.
default.q.n2-5-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not mention that the character only studied and did not exercise.
default.q.n2-5-q66-66.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author gained 15 kg by eating leftover food from drinking establishments, not through the natural development of the body from high school to university.
default.q.n2-5-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The phrase means that the character abandoned human reason and dignity and acted entirely on the instinct to eat.
default.q.n2-5-q67-67.explanation:
- Main point and evidence: Until then, the character had repeatedly told herself to preserve her human dignity and, no matter how hungry she became, never eat customers' leftovers (「どんなにひもじくても客の残り物だけは食べないようにしよう」「残飯だけは食わねえぞ」). But after tasting the first piece of fried chicken, her appetite erupted, causing her to cast aside reason, pride, and self-control and wolf down the food instinctively like a stray dog.
- Translation of the question: What does the phrase “throw away one's humanity and become a stray dog” mean?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. She did not know what was happening herself, but thought that she might have been like a dog at that moment.
  2. She simply continued eating meat with an intensity unimaginable for a human being.
  3. She ate like an animal, using only her mouth rather than dishes or her hands.
  4. She lost the ability to judge and restrain herself and acted only according to her instincts.
default.q.n2-5-q67-67.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not say that the character fails to realize what is happening and therefore guesses that he is like a dog; it is a metaphor for abandoning one's pride in order to eat.
default.q.n2-5-q67-67.why.1: (b) is incorrect. The sentence uses a psychological metaphor, not simply the act of continuously eating meat at an unusually fast speed.
default.q.n2-5-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not mention avoiding chopsticks or dishes and biting and swallowing food with one's mouth like an animal.
default.q.n2-5-q67-67.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage states: 「その時思ったのは、どんなにひもじくても客の残り物だけは食べないようにしようってこと。残飯だけは食わねえぞってね... ひとくち目は躊躇があったけど、カラアゲが食道を通り抜けた瞬間、あたしゃ 人間を捨てて野犬になりました」. Before that, the character maintained his self-respect and refused to eat leftovers, but after taking the first bite, he lost all self-control and moral judgment and acted solely on his instinct to eat.
default.q.n2-5-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is 1: This sentence shows that the character no longer has to forcefully suppress and painfully endure their appetite as before.
default.q.n2-5-q68-68.explanation:
- Main idea and basis: Before eating leftovers, each time the character sees food left by a customer, they experience intense inner conflict, with their body tensing as they struggle to suppress their gnawing hunger. After taking the first bite and accepting that they will eat the leftovers, they release that painful restraint and feel much more mentally relaxed and at ease.
- Question translation: What does phrase ③ “Before that, my body would tense up every time I saw leftovers, but suddenly I felt completely relieved” mean?
- Answer choices:
  1. No longer having to force oneself to endure or suppress it.
  2. Feeling happy simply because one gets to eat anything at all.
  3. No longer having to work while hungry.
  4. Being able to concentrate on studying with peace of mind.
default.q.n2-5-q68-68.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「それまでは残り物を見るたびに、身体が緊張してたんだけど、一気にラクになっちゃった」 Before that, the author's body became tense whenever they saw leftovers because they had to suppress their hunger. Once they decided to eat, that painful restraint was released and they felt relieved.
default.q.n2-5-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage only says that having food was a source of happiness (「とにかく食べるものがあるってのはうれしかった」), but this is not the direct meaning of “the body became lighter or more comfortable” (ラクになった).
default.q.n2-5-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The character still worked at the pub and was still hungry when starting the shift; it does not mean that they no longer had to work while hungry.
default.q.n2-5-q68-68.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Being able to concentrate on studying art (「これで絵の勉強に専念できる」) is a later result of having food, not a direct explanation of 「ラクになった」.
default.q.n2-5-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 1: All three passages, A, B, and C, share the view that it is unnecessary to overuse or use honorific language excessively.
default.q.n2-5-q69-69.explanation:
Summary of the passage:
- Section A: People who are unfamiliar with honorific language often overuse it (過剰な敬語), for example by combining forms redundantly in 「おみえになられました」, making the expression sound awkward and impolite.
- Section B: Excessive double honorifics are now considered inappropriate, but some familiar expressions are accepted (許容されている) because they convey a moderate sense of politeness. In short, not all double honorifics are bad, but there is no need to deliberately layer them (あえて重ねる必要はない).
- Section C: When interacting with someone of high status, people may become overly tense and misuse honorific language (二重敬語), for example by combining 「おっしゃる」 with 「られる」. Combining more honorific forms is not necessarily better; overuse becomes incorrect usage.
=> The point shared by all three sections, A, B, and C, is: There is no need to overuse or excessively layer honorific language.

Translation of the question and choices:
Question: What common point is stated in all three sections, A ～ C?
1. There is no need to use honorific language excessively.
2. In modern language, honorific expressions are unnecessary.
3. Polite honorific expressions are not to be welcomed.
4. The more polite an honorific expression is, the more accurate it is.
default.q.n2-5-q69-69.why.0: (a) Correct. Passage A states「丁寧に話そうとして、救語をたくさん使ってしまうのかもしれませんが、これでは、かえって聞きにくく失礼になります」; Passage B states「救語は重ねてもよいが、あえて重ねる必要はないのです」; and Passage C concludes「救語は、いくつも重ねれ消よいというものではありません。使いすぎるとかえって 間違った救語使いになってしまうので気をつけましょう」. All three authors agree that honorific language need not be overused.
default.q.n2-5-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect. None of the three passages says that honorific language is unnecessary in modern language; on the contrary, using it appropriately remains important.
default.q.n2-5-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passages do not oppose politeness; they warn against excessive or inappropriate use. Passage B also states that a moderate level of politeness (彙度な丁寧注) is acceptable.
default.q.n2-5-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect. All three passages point out that using too much honorific language in an attempt to appear polite can backfire, making speech difficult to listen to, discourteous, or incorrect (かえって聞きにくく失礼になります, 間違いになります).
default.q.n2-5-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Authors A and C argue that double honorifics should not be used because they are considered incorrect or discourteous, whereas author B takes a more open position, saying that not all such forms are prohibited and that some are acceptable without deliberately overusing them.
default.q.n2-5-q70-70.explanation:
Summary of each author’s position on "double honorifics" (二重敬語 / 過剰な敬語):
- Author A: Condemns excessive or overlapping honorifics, such as 「おみえになられました」, calling them unpleasant and discourteous (失礼), and insists on using the standard form 「おみえになりました」.
- Author B: Takes a more flexible view. Although double honorifics are not encouraged by scholars, some are accepted (許容されている) in society and the media because they convey a moderate sense of politeness. Therefore, not every double honorific is prohibited; it is simply unnecessary to deliberately pile on honorifics (二重救語はすべてだめだというわけではない... あえて重ねる必要はない).
- Author C: Considers combining honorifics, such as 「おっしゃる」 + 「られる」, to be incorrect (間違い) because it results from trying too hard, and advises people to avoid overusing them.
=> Authors A and C consider double honorifics incorrect or unacceptable, whereas Author B believes that not all of them are prohibited and that some cases are accepted, even though there is no need to use them deliberately.

Translation of the question & answer choices:
Question: What is each author’s position on "double honorifics"?
1. None of the authors considers them correct, and because they are discourteous to the other person...
2. Authors A and C believe they should not be used, but Author B believes they do not necessarily need to be prohibited completely / need not be used deliberately.
3. Authors B and C believe this is an honorific expression that should not be used, whereas Author A...
4. Authors A and C believe this is a correct usage, whereas Author B believes it is incorrect...
default.q.n2-5-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Author B does not completely reject double honorifics, but states that some cases are accepted: 「チ容されている（注 2 ）表現だと言えます」「二重救語はすべてだめだというわけではない」. Therefore, saying that all authors regard them as impolite or unusable does not reflect B's position.
default.q.n2-5-q70-70.why.1: (b) Correct. Author A considers excessive or repeated honorifics rude and incorrect: 「かえって聞きにくく失礼になります」「正しい表現方ぐです」. Author C states that combining honorific expressions is incorrect: 「救語表現を重ねているので、間違いになります」. Author B, however, says that some forms are accepted and that not every instance is prohibited: 「二重救語はすべてだめだというわけではない 救語は重ねてもよいが、あえて重ねる必要はないのです」.
default.q.n2-5-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Author B does not completely oppose double honorifics like A and C; rather, B acknowledges that some expressions are still accepted in everyday life and the media.
default.q.n2-5-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Both Authors A and C regard the overlapping use of honorifics, creating a double honorific, as incorrect or impolite (間違い/失礼), not as 正しい用法.
default.q.n2-5-q71-71.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「おじ注ん」 (uncle) here refers to the butcher (肉屋).
default.q.n2-5-q71-71.explanation:
- Main point: The passage describes a 12-year-old girl leaving her violin at a butcher shop as collateral because she had forgotten to bring money. After an old man praised it as a famous Stradivarius and offered 500,000 francs for it, the butcher tried to persuade the girl to sell it to him by saying: 「ねえ、そのバイオリン、 ① おじ注んに売ってくれないかね」 (“Say, would you sell that violin to me?”). Therefore, 「おじ注ん」 (uncle/older man) here refers to the butcher.
- Question: Who is 「おじ注ん」 (the uncle/older man)?
- Answer choices:
  1. The Stradivarius violin
  2. The butcher
  3. The girl’s uncle
  4. The elderly gentleman
default.q.n2-5-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because Stradivarius is the name of a famous type of violin, not a person’s name.
default.q.n2-5-q71-71.why.1: (b) Correct because the butcher refers to himself as 「おじ注ん」 (an uncle/older man) when trying to buy the girl’s violin: 「ねえ、そのバイオリン、 ① おじ注んに売ってくれないかね。」 (Hey, would you sell that violin to your uncle?).
default.q.n2-5-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because in this context, it is a familiar form of address used by an adult toward a little girl, not the girl's biological uncle.
default.q.n2-5-q71-71.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the elderly gentleman (老紳士) is the customer who later comes to buy meat and offers to buy the instrument; he is not the person who calls himself 「おじ注ん」 and buys the instrument from the girl.
default.q.n2-5-q72-72.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The butcher is very greedy and really likes making money (お金を儲けることがとても好きである).
default.q.n2-5-q72-72.explanation:
- Main point: The passage describes the butcher as extremely miserly and greedy, always accumulating wealth. When he sees a chance to buy the violin for 50,000 francs and resell it to the old man for 500,000 francs, making a profit of 450,000 francs, he is overjoyed and does everything he can to buy it. This shows that he is highly profit-seeking and very fond of making money.
- **Question translation:** "What can be learned about the butcher from this passage?"
- **Answer choices:**
  1. He is very fond of making money / highly profit-seeking.
  2. He is very fond of deceiving elderly people.
  3. He is very fond of deceiving children.
  4. He is very fond of buying violins.
default.q.n2-5-q72-72.why.0: (a) Correct because the passage clearly describes the butcher as extremely greedy and stingy, accumulating wealth and becoming overjoyed at the thought of making a profit of 450,000 francs: 「たいへん欲の深い肉屋がいた」、「50万フランで売れれば、45万フランの儲けだ。かれが喜んだのも当然だ」、「一攫千金を夢みる、けちな人、欲の深い人が多い」.
default.q.n2-5-q72-72.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the butcher did not enjoy deceiving elderly people; he merely intended to resell the instrument at the price of 500,000 francs that the old man had voluntarily offered.
default.q.n2-5-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the butcher did not enjoy deceiving children. On the contrary, the text says that his conscience troubled him for deceiving the girl, so he returned the money for the meat: 「彼の良心が、子どもをだますことをよしとしなかったのであろう。」
default.q.n2-5-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because he bought the violin solely to resell it for a huge profit; he did not personally have an interest in buying violins.
default.q.n2-5-q73-73.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author wants to assert that the more deeply greedy a person is, the easier it is for that person to be deceived (欲の深い人ほどだまされやすい).
default.q.n2-5-q73-73.explanation:
- Summary of the main point: The passage tells the story of an organized scam involving a girl and an old man, designed to prey on the greed of a butcher-shop owner. The author concludes that people with bottomless greed who dream of getting rich overnight are more likely to be blinded by their own greed and fall into a scam.
- Question translation: "What is the author mainly trying to say in this passage?"
- Answer choices:
  1. Adults are very easily deceived by children.
  2. It is wrong to deceive children.
  3. The greedier a person is, the easier it is for them to be deceived.
  4. It is wrong to deceive greedy people.
default.q.n2-5-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not say that adults in general are easily deceived by children; people are deceived because the victims' greed is targeted.
default.q.n2-5-q73-73.why.1: (b) Incorrect because deceiving children is merely one detail showing the butcher’s brief pang of remorse, not the central message of the passage.
default.q.n2-5-q73-73.why.2: (c) Correct because the author concludes: 「サギにあう人たちの中には、この肉屋のように、一攫千金を夢みる、けちな人、欲の深い人が多い。子どもをだまして、45万フラン儲けようという ”欲 ” が、物事を冷静に見る目を失わせてしまったのである。」 People who fall victim to scams are often like this butcher: miserly and greedy, dreaming of getting rich quickly. His “greed” to deceive a child and make 450,000 francs caused him to lose the ability to view things calmly.
default.q.n2-5-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author analyzes the psychological reasons why victims fall into the trap, rather than discussing the ethics of deceiving greedy people.
default.q.n2-5-q74-74.verdict: The correct answer is 3: During the entire trip, participants only have to prepare their own breakfast on the 23rd, which is eaten on the bus.
default.q.n2-5-q74-74.explanation:
The notice explains the meals during the training trip: On the morning of the 23rd, breakfast will be eaten on the bus before arriving in Tottori, and participants must prepare it themselves; lunch on the 23rd will be distributed at around 12:00 after leaving the prefectural library; dinner on the 23rd will be served in the lobby of Neo Sakyuso at 18:00; after checking out on the morning of the 24th, participants will disperse on site.

- Question translation: Which of the following statements about meals during the trip is correct?
- Answer choices:
1. All meals during the training trip are included, so nothing needs to be prepared in advance.
2. Apart from lunch on the 23rd, when boxed meals will be distributed, participants must arrange all their other meals themselves.
3. Only breakfast on the bus on the 23rd must be prepared by the participants.
4. Lunch and dinner are provided, but breakfast must be prepared by the participants on both days.
default.q.n2-5-q74-74.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the 《注意》 section clearly states that breakfast on the 23rd must be prepared individually (「朝食の準備は各自でご用意ください」); therefore, not all meals are provided as a complete package.
default.q.n2-5-q74-74.why.1: (b) Incorrect because, in addition to the lunch provided on the 23rd (「お渡しします」), the schedule includes dinner at the inn's large hall on the 23rd (「18:00より広間で夕食」). Participants do not have to arrange all the other meals themselves.
default.q.n2-5-q74-74.why.2: (c) Correct. Evidence quoted from the text: 「23日は鳥取に着くまでに朝食を済ませてください（車内）。朝食の準備は各自でご用意ください。」 (Prepare your own breakfast on the 23rd). Lunch on the 23rd will be provided: 「23日の昼食は県立図書館を出たとき（12時ころ）、お渡しします。」 Dinner on the 23rd is included in the itinerary: 「ネオ砂丘荘（チェックイン、18:00より広間で夕食）」.
default.q.n2-5-q74-74.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the schedule only requires participants to prepare their own breakfast to eat on the bus on the 23rd. It does not say that they must prepare breakfast for both days; on the morning of the 24th, everyone disperses after checking out.
default.q.n2-5-q75-75.verdict: The correct answer is 2: She needs to contact Yamada, the person in charge, and express her wish to participate before April 16.
default.q.n2-5-q75-75.explanation:
The passage clearly explains the participation registration procedure: Because accommodation arrangements must be made, anyone wishing to participate must notify the person in charge, second-year graduate student Yamada, of their intention before April 16. From April 17 onward, only cancellations will be accepted. The trip fee must be paid before the departure date, April 21.

- Question translation: What must you do to participate in the training trip?
- Answer choices:
1. Notify them in advance of your intention to participate and buy your train or bus ticket one day before departure.
2. Contact Yamada, the person in charge, and state your intention to participate before the 16th.
3. Submit the application together with the trip fee before the 21st.
4. Reserve your own accommodation and notify the person in charge of your intention from the 17th onward.
default.q.n2-5-q75-75.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Buying a train or bus ticket, including using a JR student discount, is something an individual prepares for the return trip; it is not a prerequisite procedure for registering to participate in the trip.
