default.q.n2-9-q33-33.why.0: (a) 不安がっている: The ending 「〜がる」 is generally used to describe another person’s emotions or attitude. It sounds unnatural with the subject 「私は」 and does not express a change in behavior after 「〜をきっかけに」.
default.q.n2-9-q33-33.why.1: (b) 自信たっぷりだ means "full of confidence," which does not fit the context after stomach surgery and does not express a change following a turning point.
default.q.n2-9-q33-33.why.2: (c) 困ることがない means “there is nothing difficult or troublesome,” which does not fit the meaning or the structure describing a change in behavior.
default.q.n2-9-q33-33.why.3: (d) 注意するようになった: The pattern 「V-るようになる」expresses a change of state or the development of a new habit, fitting perfectly with 「〜をきっかけに」(as a result of, prompted by...).
default.q.n2-9-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3. に関して.
default.q.n2-9-q34-34.explanation:

• Grammar: 「N + に関して / に関するN」(related to 関連): regarding, concerning... This pattern commonly occurs with words such as 質問, 調査, 意見, and 論文.

default.q.n2-9-q34-34.why.0: (a) にとって means “for” or “from the standpoint of” someone, and is not used to indicate the topic of a question.
default.q.n2-9-q34-34.why.1: (b) によって: This indicates a cause, means, method, or difference depending on the context, so it is not appropriate for modifying the topic of 「質問」.
default.q.n2-9-q34-34.why.2: (c) に関して: This means “concerning” or “regarding” a subject, and is used here to introduce the topic of discussion or questions: computer usage.
default.q.n2-9-q34-34.why.3: (d) に際して: Means "on the occasion of / when carrying out" a special or formal event, so it is not appropriate with the noun "usage."
default.q.n2-9-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ことか.

default.q.n2-9-q35-35.why.0: (a) ことだ is used to give advice about what one should or must do (V-る/V-ない), or to express an evaluative exclamation. It is not used with the adverb 「何度」 to indicate degree or frequency.
default.q.n2-9-q35-35.why.1: (b) ことか: The exclamatory pattern 「何度／どんなに／どれほど〜ことか」 means “how many times / how deeply,” expressing strong emotion or regret about something that happened repeatedly.
default.q.n2-9-q35-35.why.2: (c) ものだ: used for natural laws, reminiscing about the past, or expressing感嘆 about the general nature of things or events; it does not combine with 「何度」.
default.q.n2-9-q35-35.why.3: (d) ものか expresses strong denial (“absolutely not,” “as if...”), so it does not fit the exclamatory structure here.
default.q.n2-9-q36-36.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 知りっこない.
default.q.n2-9-q36-36.explanation:

default.q.n2-9-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. せ流かく (an OCR spelling error for 「せっかく」: having gone to the trouble / taking the trouble...).
default.q.n2-9-q54-54.explanation: A familiar adverbial expression and pattern in JLPT N2: 『せっかく (the small OCR-scanned "っ" was incorrectly recognized as "流" in "せ流かく") ... のだから』means "since you have gone to the trouble of... / since you have this valuable opportunity...". In the passage: "せっかく日本に来たのだから、形通りのサービスではなく、地元の人々との素朴な触れ合いを味わいたいと思うものです" (Since visitors have gone to the trouble of traveling all the way to Japan, they naturally want to experience simple, genuine interaction with local people rather than formulaic services). Therefore, choice 1「せ流かく」(せっかく) is the correct answer.
default.q.n2-9-q54-54.why.0: (a) せ流かく (that is, せっかく): An adverb commonly used with 「～のだから / ～のに」 to emphasize a valuable opportunity obtained through effort (“since you went to the trouble of coming to Japan...” ). It is exactly correct here.
default.q.n2-9-q54-54.why.1: (b) 注流そく (早速 - さっそく): means “immediately” or “without delay,” describing the prompt performance of an action. It does not fit a structure expressing appreciation for an opportunity such as 「～のだから」.
default.q.n2-9-q54-54.why.2: (c) まったく: means "completely" (usually with a negative, as in まったく～ない) or is used for emphasis; it does not fit with 「のだから」 in this context.
default.q.n2-9-q54-54.why.3: (d) す流かり (すっかり): Meaning “completely / entirely / thoroughly,” indicating a complete change in degree; it is not used to express appreciation for a special occasion or opportunity.
default.q.n2-9-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Recognizing that it cannot be said from 「理カ」.
default.q.n2-9-q55-55.explanation:
- Main point: The author's family imposed a ban on using the word 「理カ」. Because of habit, family members occasionally let it slip. One time, after saying 「理」, they suddenly remembered the ban, so the child changed it to 「理ビブベボ」, while the author changed it to 「理ン、理ン、理ン」 to gloss over it (ごまかしました), turning their anger into laughter.
- Question translation: In the sentence 「『理』まで言ってから気がついて」(“After saying 「理」, they realized it”), what did they realize?
- Answer choices:
  1. 「理ビブベボ」 and 「理カ」 have the same meaning.
  2. The word 「理カ」 must not be said.
  3. The author does not use the word 「理カ」.
  4. If they say 「理ン、理ン、理ン」, everyone will be amused.
default.q.n2-9-q55-55.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「理ビブベボ」 is merely the child’s evasive or distorted wording to cover up a slip of the tongue; the passage does not say that these two words have the same meaning.
default.q.n2-9-q55-55.why.1: (b) Correct. The opening sentence says: 「我が家では『理カ』という言葉を使ってはいけないという禁止令を出しました」 When the speaker accidentally begins saying 「理」, they suddenly remember the family’s ban on using the word and quickly switch to another word to cover it up (ごまかしました).
default.q.n2-9-q55-55.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author says that the word often slips out unintentionally (「ついつい使ってしまいます」), and the author also accidentally says 「理」 and then has to correct it to 「理ン、理ン、理ン」.
default.q.n2-9-q55-55.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Saying 「理ン、理ン、理ン」 was merely the author's attempt to cover up the situation after realizing that they had nearly violated the rule; it was not what the author realized immediately upon stopping at 「理」.
default.q.n2-9-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (大きすぎて), because the fourth island occupies as much as 95% of the area, so it is too large and the sense of being surrounded by the sea is weak.
default.q.n2-9-q56-56.explanation:
- Main point: The passage explains why Japanese people often forget in daily life that they live on an island nation: the four main islands (Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku) account for 95% of the country’s land area, so they are too large for people to feel surrounded by the sea; to truly experience island life, one must visit remote smaller islands (outer islands).
- Question translation: Which of the following should be inserted in the blank ( )?
- Answer choices:
  1. 多すぎて: too many
  2. 小さすぎて (小さすぎて): too small
  3. 大きすぎて: too large
  4. 少なすぎて: too few
default.q.n2-9-q56-56.why.0: (a) Choice 1, "多すぎて" (too many), is unsuitable because the context concerns the geographical scale and size of the four main islands, which account for 95% of the country's land area, not an excessive number of islands causing a loss of perspective.
default.q.n2-9-q56-56.why.1: (b) Choice 2, "小注すぎて" (too small), is incorrect because it completely contradicts the context: the four islands account for most of the area (95%), so they are very large, and the next sentence says that one must visit smaller remote islands ("もっと小注な、い山ゆる離島に行ってみなければならない") to experience the islands more fully.
default.q.n2-9-q56-56.why.2: (c) Choice 3, "大きすぎて" (too large), is correct. The passage says: "日本全体の画積の 95 パーセントは本州...四つの島が占めている。この四島では（ ）、周囲を海に囲まれているという実感は薄い。" (The four islands account for 95 percent of Japan's area, so on these islands, because they are too large, one has little sense of being surrounded by the sea).
default.q.n2-9-q56-56.why.3: (d) Choice 4, "少なすぎて" (too few), does not fit because it indicates a small quantity and cannot reasonably explain why the feeling of living surrounded by the sea is weakened when the four islands account for as much as 95% of the area.
default.q.n2-9-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Obtaining a water supply is not easy (水を手に入れるのは簡単なことではないということ).
default.q.n2-9-q57-57.explanation:
- Question translation:
The passage says, "This situation has basically remained unchanged even today." What does "this situation" (この事情) refer to?

- Answer choice translations:
1. Disputes frequently occurring over access to water.
2. Japan being a rainy country with abundant water resources.
3. The fact that obtaining water is not easy.
4. The inability to grow rice and other crops because of water shortages.

- Main point and explanation:
The demonstrative expression 「この事情」 (this situation) replaces the content stated immediately before it: Although Japan receives a great deal of rain, its fast-flowing rivers are difficult to use and its groundwater is limited, so obtaining water required considerable effort (「水を得るには大変な苦労が必要であった」). The author goes on to show that this difficult situation still exists today by explaining that towns without major rivers must pay to buy water from nearby areas, resulting in differences in water prices. Therefore, the essence of "this situation" is that obtaining water is far from simple (corresponding to answer choice 3).
default.q.n2-9-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage only mentions disputes over water as something that has occurred in the past (“古くから争ってきた”). It says that places lacking water now have to pay to buy it, but does not state that disputes or conflicts commonly occur today.
default.q.n2-9-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Although the passage says「日本は比較的雨が多い国なので」, it immediately uses「しかし」to point out that making use of the water is difficult. This does not mean that water is always abundant and readily available.
default.q.n2-9-q57-57.why.2: (c) Correct because the preceding sentence clearly gives the reason: "日本の川は...利用が難しく、地下水が出るところも限られているため、水を得るには大変な苦労が必要であった" (Japanese rivers were difficult to use and groundwater was available only in limited places, so obtaining water required considerable effort). This is equivalent to saying "水を手に入れるのは簡単なことではない".
default.q.n2-9-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the inability to grow rice and other crops ("米は...作物さえもほとんど作れない地方もあった") was only a localized consequence in some areas in the past, not the core of the “circumstances” that have continued to the present.
default.q.n2-9-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3. The author mistakenly believed that butterflies could recognize colors but could not distinguish between paper and grass.
default.q.n2-9-q58-58.explanation:
* Main point of the passage:
The author once scattered pieces of brightly colored paper in a cage containing white butterflies and observed that the butterflies preferred flying over green paper. From this, the author assumed that, as far as the butterflies were concerned, any green surface would do—even paper—and that they could recognize color but could not distinguish paper from grass. However, this was a misunderstanding: when real pots of grass were placed in the cage, the butterflies flew only around the real grass and completely ignored the green paper.

* Question:
The passage says, “However, this was an extremely rude misunderstanding of the butterflies.” What exactly did the author misunderstand?

* Answer choices:
1. The author thought that butterflies could distinguish neither colors nor paper from plants.
2. The author thought that butterflies could distinguish shapes but could not distinguish colors at all.
3. The author thought that butterflies could distinguish colors but could not distinguish paper from grass.
4. The author thought that butterflies could distinguish not only colors but also shapes.
default.q.n2-9-q58-58.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author observed that the butterflies preferred flying over green paper, showing that they could distinguish colors. The author did not think that butterflies were unable to tell colors apart.
default.q.n2-9-q58-58.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author knew that butterflies could distinguish colors after observing them choose green paper. The passage never says that the author believed butterflies could distinguish shapes but not colors.
default.q.n2-9-q58-58.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct. Before the question, the author writes: 「なるほど、チ自ウは緑色であれば紙でもいいのだな、とぼくは思った。」 (I see—the butterfly just needs something green, so even paper will do, I thought). This shows that the author believes the butterfly can recognize the color green but cannot distinguish paper from grass.
default.q.n2-9-q58-58.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because this is not the author’s initial mistaken assumption in the experiment involving colored sheets of paper.
default.q.n2-9-q59-59.explanation:
* Main point:
The author begins receiving questions such as "How would you like young people to live?" At first, the author feels bewildered, as if being indirectly told that they are no longer young. However, what the author ultimately realizes is that, all along, they have been far from wanting or imposing any particular way of living on others, including young people and their own children.

* Translation of the question:
When the author says, "I realized," what did the author realize?

* Translation of the answer choices:
1. The author had once thought they did not want to be asked a question such as "How would you like young people to live?"
2. The author had reached the age at which they could talk about how people should live, as in "How would you like young people to live?"
3. The author had once thought that, even if they were no longer young, no young people would listen if they talked about life.
4. Until then, the author had hardly ever wanted or imposed a particular way of living on young people, including their own children.
default.q.n2-9-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author does not say that they did not want to receive the question, only that they felt flustered when unexpectedly asked it at first.
default.q.n2-9-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because feeling old is only the initial reaction (「お前はもう若くないんだ...」), and the author states 「いまはそんなことをいいたいのではない」 (that is not what I want to say now). Therefore, this is not what the author realized.
default.q.n2-9-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The detail 「いうことをきく人がいるものかと」(wondering whether anyone would listen) is merely an additional thought explaining the author's view when looking back on his youth. It is not the central thing he “realized” (「気がついた」).
default.q.n2-9-q59-59.why.3: (d) Correct. The evidence is found in: «そういう質問をされて、自分が長いあいだ、人に｢どう生きて欲しい｣ などと願流たりすることから遠いところにいたんだな次ということに気がついたのです» together with «多少は影響をあたえうるかもしれない自分の子どもにたいしても、ほとんどそういうことは願山ずに生きてきました». The author realizes that for a long time, they had hardly ever wished for or imposed a particular way of living on young people, including their own children.
default.q.n2-9-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author has struggled with shoes for 40 years because they could not find a well-fitting pair and had to endure the pain in their feet.
default.q.n2-9-q60-60.explanation:
Main point: From childhood, the author’s feet were unusually large. For 40 years, the author could not find shoes that fit and always had to force their feet into tight shoes, enduring deformed toes and repeatedly losing toenails.

Translation of the question: Why has the author 「 靴に四十年も悩まされてきた 」 (been troubled by shoes for 40 years)?
Translation of the choices:
1. Because from the eighth grade onward, the author has always had to wear shoes larger than the older brother’s.
2. Because since buying shoes with the first month’s salary, the author has never been able to wear a cute pair of shoes.
3. Because there were no shoes of the right size, and the author had to endure pain in the feet.
4. Because there was no one around willing to listen to stories about the author’s feet.
default.q.n2-9-q60-60.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect: the passage only says that from eighth grade onward, the author became taller than their older brother and their feet grew larger. The reason they suffered for 40 years was not "always wearing shoes larger than their brother's."
default.q.n2-9-q60-60.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect: The author only mentions that the custom-made shoes bought with her first month's salary were not as cute as she had expected, not that she had never worn cute shoes since then. Nor was this the main reason she suffered for 40 years.
default.q.n2-9-q60-60.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct. Evidence from the text: 「足に靴を合わせるのではなく、無理をすれば履けそうな靴に、足を合わせてきた。縮めていた指は、変形し、つめは何度生え変わったことか。痛くならない靴などないのだと、あきらめていた。」 (The author could not find shoes that fit and had to force their feet into tight shoes, causing the toes to deform, the toenails to grow back repeatedly, and constant pain to be endured.)
default.q.n2-9-q60-60.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect: the passage does not mention that “there was no one nearby willing to listen about one’s feet.”
default.q.n2-9-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The difficult part was that the author had to force their feet to fit the shoes for a long time.
default.q.n2-9-q61-61.explanation:
Main point: When the author took off their shoes to show the shoemaker, the shoemaker saw that their feet had become deformed from years of forcing them to fit their shoes. He understood and sympathized with the author, exclaiming that they must have endured great hardship and pain.

Question translation: In the sentence 告 「これは大変でしたね。」 (That must have been very difficult), what was difficult or painful?
Answer choices:
1. The effort of traveling all the way to a shoe shop in Tokyo.
2. Having to force their feet to fit their shoes for a long time.
3. Being able to wear only oversized shoes.
4. Growing up by eating a great deal of fish.
default.q.n2-9-q61-61.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is incorrect: The author happened to be going to Tokyo and stopped by the shoe shop (「用中で東京へ行ったついでに、その靴屋に寄ってみた」); the shoemaker did not say it was difficult because the author had traveled a long distance to get there.
default.q.n2-9-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct. The passage states: 「足に靴を合わせるのではなく、無理をすれば履けそうな靴に、足を合わせてきた。縮めていた指は、変形し、つめは何度生え変わったことか。」 After seeing the author's deformed feet, caused by years of forcing them into shoes, the shoemaker understood the author's suffering and said: 「これは大変でしたね。腰まで痛かったでしょう。」
default.q.n2-9-q61-61.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect: The problem is not that one can “only wear oversized shoes,” but that there are no properly fitting shoes, so one must force one’s feet into tight shoes and endure the pain.
default.q.n2-9-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect: “Growing up by eating lots of fish” is merely a lighthearted conversation later between the shoemaker and the author; it is not the reason the shoemaker says “it is hard work.”
default.q.n2-9-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The most appropriate word for the blank is 'あたたかかった' (was warm).
default.q.n2-9-q62-62.explanation:
Main idea: After trying on the first well-fitting pair of shoes in his life and having a friendly conversation, the shoemaker's warm, understanding smile gave the author an indescribably warm feeling—a smile the author had waited 40 years to encounter.

Question translation: Which word is most appropriate to fill in （ ――― ）?
Translation of the choices:
1. I feel sorry / embarrassed.
2. I feel envious / admiring.
3. I feel nostalgic / longing.
4. I feel warmhearted.
default.q.n2-9-q62-62.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect: もうしわけなかった (“felt sorry/guilty”) does not fit because the shoemaker’s smile brought relief and comfort, not remorse or guilt.
default.q.n2-9-q62-62.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect: うらやましかった (“was envious of” or “admired”) does not fit the context, in which the author felt kindness and warmth from the shoemaker’s smile.
default.q.n2-9-q62-62.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「なつかしかった」 (nostalgic or reminiscent of the past) is unsuitable because this was the first time in 40 years that the author had finally met someone who understood their suffering (「ようやく出会えた」).
default.q.n2-9-q62-62.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct. Evidence from the text: 「『三浦海岸に住んでる人も同じ足でしたよ。どうしてなのかねえ・・・』 靴屋注んの笑顔が、 ③ （あたたかかった）。四十年かかって、ようやく出会えた笑顔だった。」 After 40 years of suffering and feeling self-conscious, the shoemaker's warm, empathetic smile gave the author an overwhelmingly comforting feeling.
default.q.n2-9-q63-63.verdict: The provided answer is 4; however, choice 4 accurately describes the characteristics of a Tokyo alley in the passage, while the question asks for the choice that does not apply (あてはまらない), so there is a contradiction or error in the provided answer.
default.q.n2-9-q63-63.explanation:
- Main point: Paragraph 1 describes Tokyo’s back alleys through the experience of a French person living there: entering from a main street, the alleys open up like a maze and can easily make one lose one’s bearings; modern buildings stand beside old temples and shrines, flowerpots spill into the street, and the alleys are filled with the atmosphere of everyday life and an “imbalance” (an awkward but intriguing mixture) that stimulates pedestrians to explore.
- Question translation: Which of the following is NOT appropriate for describing “an alley like this”?
- Answer choices:
  1. An alley where only balanced and harmonious things come into view.
  2. An alley where modern buildings are neatly aligned in a straight row.
  3. A disorderly, confusing alley where it is difficult to find one’s way.
  4. An alley that conveys people’s everyday lives, with unusual and mismatched things coming into view.
default.q.n2-9-q63-63.why.0: (a) Choice 1 describes an alley containing only things that are well-proportioned. This contradicts Tokyo’s alleys, which always contain interesting mismatches such as 「あれ、こんな所にこんなものが・・・・」という不釣合い.
default.q.n2-9-q63-63.why.1: (b) Choice 2 describes modern buildings arranged neatly in straight rows. This is characteristic of European streets being 「整然としていてきれい」, not of Tokyo’s narrow alleys.
default.q.n2-9-q63-63.why.2: (c) Choice 3 describes winding, confusing alleyways that are difficult to navigate, exactly matching the sentence "路地が迷路のように広がり、すぐ方向がわからなくなる... ごちゃごちゃした所".
default.q.n2-9-q63-63.why.3: (d) Correct. The passage says: 「近代的な建物の横に、古いお宮やお寺があったりする。鉢植えの花が道にはみ出しておいてある。人々の生活のにおいがする...「あれ、こんな所にこんなものが・・・・」という不釣合いを発見しながら。」 Choice 4 most accurately reflects the characteristic of Tokyo’s alleys described in the passage, assuming the question asks for the correct idea.
default.q.n2-9-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (A clean, attractive street does not necessarily win people's hearts).
default.q.n2-9-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point: The author emphasizes that although European streets are clean, beautiful, and orderly, they lack the pleasant surprise of “not knowing what will appear next.” For tourists accustomed to order, somewhat messy corners of everyday life can feel refreshingly new. Therefore, attracting tourists is not simply a matter of making the streets clean.
- Question: What does the sentence “Simply making a city clean and beautiful is not necessarily enough” mean?
- Answer choices:
  1. The ability to beautify a city is very important for attracting tourists.
  2. It is unnecessary to clean the streets in order to attract tourists.
  3. Even if a city is beautified, messy places will not disappear.
  4. A beautiful city is not necessarily able to attract or captivate people.
default.q.n2-9-q64-64.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because it misinterprets the idiom “〜だけが能じゃない” (“being able to ... is not the only thing that matters” / “... alone is not enough”) as meaning “one needs the ability to clean,” which is contrary to the author’s point.
default.q.n2-9-q64-64.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage does not claim that cleaning thoroughly is unnecessary; it only says that cleanliness and beauty alone are insufficient to create a unique appeal.
default.q.n2-9-q64-64.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the idea that “even cleaning does not make a messy place disappear” does not convey the sentence’s main message.
default.q.n2-9-q64-64.why.3: (d) The passage states: 「パリの裏道を歩いていると...きれいだが、何が出てくるかわからないというようなおもしろさはない。美しく整った街を見飽きた目には、ごちゃごちゃした所がかえって新鮮にうつるのだ。この話は、海外からの観光客を誘致したいという政府には、いいヒントとなるだろう。街はきれいにするだけが能じゃないのだ。」 Choice 4 accurately expresses the idea that cleanliness and beauty alone do not necessarily attract tourists.
default.q.n2-9-q65-65.verdict: The provided answer is 4; however, based on the passage, the correct answer should be choice 2 (The French person says that walking through Tokyo’s back alleys leads to many interesting discoveries.)
default.q.n2-9-q65-65.explanation:
- Main idea: The French friend, who has lived in Tokyo for many years, says that although European streets are orderly and beautiful, they lack Tokyo's appeal. He enjoys walking through Tokyo's back alleys because he can continually discover unexpected asymmetry and sense the everyday lives of the residents.
- Question translation: Which statement about the Frenchman agrees with the passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. He says that there are many interesting discoveries in Paris's back streets.
  2. He says that there are many interesting discoveries in Tokyo's back streets.
  3. He says that Tokyo's back streets are difficult to navigate and therefore troublesome.
  4. He says that Paris is an orderly, beautiful city and therefore "not interesting."
default.q.n2-9-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because, regarding Paris’s alleys, the passage clearly states "何が出てくるかわからないというようなおもしろさはない" (they do not have the excitement of not knowing what might appear).
default.q.n2-9-q65-65.why.1: (b) The passage states: "彼はこういう路地を歩き回るのが楽しいと言う。「あれ、こんな所にこんなものが・・・・」という不釣合いを発見しながら。" This proves that the Frenchman finds Tokyo's back alleys interesting because they contain many discoveries. This is the most accurate choice according to the passage.
default.q.n2-9-q65-65.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is incorrect. Although the Tokyo alleyways make it easy to lose one’s sense of direction, 「すぐ方向がわからなくなる」, he does not find this troublesome (困る); he actually likes it: 「これがいいのだそうだ。彼はこういう路地を歩き回るのが楽しいと言う」.
default.q.n2-9-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 does not precisely match what the French person said: In the passage, he only says that European streets are 「確かにきれいですけど、東京のような面白さはありませんよ」 (certainly beautiful, but not as interesting as Tokyo); he never directly says that Paris is “not interesting” (おもしろくない). The discussion of Paris's back streets in paragraph 2 is the author's observation and interpretation.
default.q.n2-9-q66-66.verdict: The provided answer is 4; however, based on the logical connection of the passage, the correct answer is 2 (喜びが半減してしまった - the joy was cut in half).
default.q.n2-9-q66-66.explanation:
- Question translation: “Which sentence is most appropriate to fill in the blank ( )?”
- Answer choices:
  1. The joy became greater.
  2. The joy was cut in half.
  3. The desire became greater.
  4. There was nothing left to want.
- Main idea and explanation: In the first paragraph, the author argues that the joy of an experience includes both the time before it happens and the time during it. For example, a trip is half enjoyable before departure and half enjoyable during the trip. Therefore, when the period of eager anticipation disappears, the joy is cut in half (choice 2: 喜びが半減してしまった). The provided answer 4 does not reflect the logic connecting it to the following sentence.
default.q.n2-9-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect. This choice says that the joy increased, which is completely opposite to the author’s point: losing the period of eager anticipation also took away part of the joy.
default.q.n2-9-q66-66.why.1: (b) This is the correct answer in the context of the passage, although the provided answer key selects choice 4. The author writes: 「旅行の楽しさは旅立つ前が半分、旅行しているときが半分とも言える」 (Half the enjoyment of a trip comes before departure, and the other half while traveling.) When the exciting period of anticipation disappears (期待に胸を膨らませて待つという時間がなくなって), the enjoyment is reduced by half (喜びが半減してしまった).
default.q.n2-9-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. “Having greater desires” is not the direct consequence used by the author to explain the loss of joy during a period of waiting, as developed from the beginning of the passage.
default.q.n2-9-q66-66.why.3: (d) According to the provided answer key, choice 4 is selected: the explanation is that because everything is immediately available, people no longer have anything they deeply long for. However, the following sentence says 「次から次へと新しいものが手に入ると思う人が増えてしまった」 (the number of people who think they can obtain new things one after another has increased), so choice 2 fits the flow of the passage better.
default.q.n2-9-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Waiting for one's turn at a hospital is not a period of joyful anticipation filled with high expectations, as described in the passage.
default.q.n2-9-q67-67.explanation:
- Question translation: “Which of the following does NOT correspond to the ‘waiting time’ mentioned here?”
- Answer choices:
  1. The time spent waiting for one’s turn at a hospital.
  2. The time spent waiting for a purchased car to be delivered home.
  3. The time spent traveling back to one’s home country, where one’s parents are waiting.
  4. The time spent waiting to see a close friend whom one has not met for a long time.
- Main idea and explanation: The “waiting time” (待ち時間) praised by the author is the period spent nurturing expectations and looking forward to a pleasant event or happy occasion, such as a date, trip, or shopping. Waiting for one’s turn at a hospital is tiring and anxiety-inducing, unlike the eager anticipation described in the passage.
default.q.n2-9-q67-67.why.0: (a) Correct. The author defines waiting here as 「この期待に胸を膨らませて待つという時間」 (the time spent waiting with one's heart filled with anticipation) and 「何かを実行する前の 待ち時間 をもっと大切にしたい」 (wanting to value more highly the waiting time before doing something). Waiting for a medical examination is compulsory and exhausting because of illness; it contains neither joy nor positive anticipation.
default.q.n2-9-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect (this belongs to 待ち時間 in the passage). Waiting for a newly purchased car to be delivered corresponds to the example of saving money to buy something: 「通帳を見ながら少しずつそれが実現する日が近づいてくる時に味わう喜び」 (the joy of watching in the bankbook as the day when one's wish will be realized gradually draws closer).
default.q.n2-9-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect; this belongs to the 待ち時間 in the passage. The time spent traveling home to the parents who are waiting is an exciting period before a family reunion, similar to the joy before setting off on a trip (「旅立つ前」).
default.q.n2-9-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect (this belongs to 待ち時間 in the passage). Waiting to meet a close friend again after a long time corresponds to the example at the beginning about the time before an appointment (「デートの前の時間」/「だれに会おうと考えている時の喜び」).
default.q.n2-9-q68-68.verdict: The given answer is 2; however, a close analysis of the passage shows that the most accurate answer is 4 (the feeling of anticipation before actually obtaining what one wants is itself a form of joy).
default.q.n2-9-q68-68.explanation:
- Question translation: "Which of the following is consistent with the content of the passage?"
- Answer choices:
  1. It is good to be able to obtain anything immediately.
  2. People need to take time to experience a sense of accomplishment.
  3. The sense of satisfaction from actually obtaining what one wants is very great.
  4. The anticipation before actually obtaining what one wants becomes a source of joy.
- Main point and explanation: The author emphasizes that the joy of waiting and looking forward to something before doing it—such as going on a trip or buying a favorite item—is enormous and is not at all less than, and may even be greater than, the feeling of actually having it in hand. Therefore, choice 4 is the most accurate match for the reading.
default.q.n2-9-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author does not say that getting everything immediately is good. On the contrary, the author regrets losing the time of waiting filled with anticipation: 「この期待に胸を膨らませて待つという時間がなくなって... 何かを実行する前の 待ち時間 をもっと大切にしたいものである。」
default.q.n2-9-q68-68.why.1: (b) According to the provided answer key (choice 2), this choice refers to taking time to savor a sense of achievement. However, the passage does not mention a "sense of achievement" (達成感); its central theme is the joy of eagerly anticipating something before carrying it out (期待感・実行する前の待ち時間).
default.q.n2-9-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author does not praise the satisfaction of obtaining an object, but emphasizes that the joy of waiting is no less than the joy of finally obtaining it: 「通帳を見ながら少しずつそれが実現する日が近づいてくる時に味わう喜びは、実際にそれが手に入った時の喜びと比べて、決して小さいものではないだろう。」
default.q.n2-9-q68-68.why.3: (d) This is the correct answer according to the reading, although the provided answer selects choice 2. The evidence is: 「あそこに行こう、ここでは何をしよう...と考えている時の喜びは、もしかしたら実際に旅をしている時よりも大きいかもしれない」 and 「通帳を見ながら少しずつそれが実現する日が近づいてくる時に味わう喜びは、実際にそれが手に入った時の喜びと比べて、決して小さいものではないだろう」. The anticipation before obtaining something is itself a great source of joy.
default.q.n2-9-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Both authors A and B are skeptical about whether the popularity of fast fashion can continue for much longer.
default.q.n2-9-q69-69.explanation:
• Summary of the main point: Passage A describes the author's experience shopping at an overcrowded fast-fashion store, which made the author feel exhausted and question people's actual needs. The author also expresses nostalgia for traditional department stores and a desire for them to survive. Passage B analyzes why fast fashion is popular during an economic downturn but questions how long the trend will last, since consumer needs are diverse and consumers may soon become bored if brands fail to innovate. The common point is that both passages question the sustainability of fast fashion's popularity.
• Translation of the question: What point do passages A and B have in common?
• Translation of the answer choices:
1. Both department stores and fast-fashion stores have their own advantages.
2. If fast fashion continues to be popular, department stores will disappear.
3. Fast-fashion stores exist in department stores that have survived.
4. Both question whether fast fashion will continue to be popular for much longer.
default.q.n2-9-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because Author A never mentions anything positive about the fast-fashion store; he only felt tired, overwhelmed by the crowds, and puzzled, and then stopped going there ("買いたかったものを一枚手に取るまでに疲れ果たしててしまった。何か変だ... 以来、私はその店に行かなくなった").
default.q.n2-9-q69-69.why.1: (b) Incorrect because this point is mentioned only in section A (“この不況下で 安いファストファッシ自ンブランドに人気が集中し、百貨店は次々と消えている”). Section B does not say that department stores will disappear completely if fast fashion continues to be popular.
default.q.n2-9-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because passage B only states that fast fashion has expanded even into department stores (“今ではデパートの中にまで進出している”), and does not claim that all surviving department stores have fast-fashion shops; passage A does not mention this either.
default.q.n2-9-q69-69.why.3: (d) Correct because both authors question the fast-fashion boom. Author A wonders whether people really need to buy these items: 「何か変だ。この人たちは本当に必要でかっているのだろうか」. Author B also questions how long the boom will last and worries that consumers may soon become tired of it: 「注て、このファストファッシ自ン熱はいつまで続くのだろうか」「そろそろ別の切り口のブランドを考えていかないと消費者に飽きられてしまうのではないだろうか」.
default.q.n2-9-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Both Authors A and B believe that the popularity of fast fashion is related to the economic downturn.
default.q.n2-9-q70-70.explanation:
• Main point: Both authors A and B begin their comments on the growth of fast fashion with the phrase "during this economic recession" (この不況下で), showing that both view the economic recession as a factor behind consumers' acceptance of fast fashion.
• Question translation: Which of the following statements is correct?
• Answer choices:
1. Both A and B believe that the popularity of fast fashion is related to the economic recession.
2. Both A and B believe that fast fashion and department stores have completely opposite values.
3. A writes from the customer's perspective, whereas B writes from the store's perspective.
4. A rejects fast fashion, whereas B is favorable toward it (supports it).
default.q.n2-9-q70-70.why.0: (a) Correct, because both passages directly mention an economic recession as the context for the popularity of fast fashion. Passage A states: 「この不況下で 安いファストファッシ自ンブランドに人気が集中し...」 (During this recession, popularity became concentrated on inexpensive fast-fashion brands...), while Passage B states: 「ファストファッシ自ンがこの不況下で消費者の心をつかんでいる」 (Fast fashion is winning consumers over during this recession).
default.q.n2-9-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because Passage B does not contrast or compare the value of fast fashion with that of department stores; it only analyzes the need for a variety of clothing depending on age and circumstances.
default.q.n2-9-q70-70.why.2: (c) Incorrect because Author B also expresses an opinion based on personal experience as a consumer looking for work clothes (「実際、私が仕事着にしたいと思うような機能やデザイン、品質を合わせ持ち... 服はなかなか見当たらない」), not from the standpoint of a shop owner or businessperson.
default.q.n2-9-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because Author B does not fully support or have an entirely positive view of fast fashion. B also points out its drawbacks, such as difficulty finding suitable work clothes, and warns that consumers may soon become tired of it.
default.q.n2-9-q71-71.explanation:
- Question: What does 「ふしぎなことに」 (“Strangely enough”) refer to?
- Choices:
  1. The number of foreign workers is greater than the number of Japanese workers.
  2. The content of the published newspaper articles is inaccurate.
  3. There are many people in Japan who have neither jobs nor homes.
  4. Despite a labor shortage, the unemployment rate remains high.
- Main point: The author finds it puzzling and unacceptable (納得がいかない) that two contradictory situations appear in the newspapers: Japan is suffering such a serious labor shortage that it must recruit foreign workers, yet the unemployment rate is high, and many Japanese people have neither jobs nor homes while refusing to apply for the jobs that need workers.
default.q.n2-9-q71-71.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the reading only states that Japan lacks workers and therefore needs to seek labor from other Asian countries. It provides no information comparing the number of foreign workers with the number of Japanese workers.
default.q.n2-9-q71-71.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author points out a contradiction between two pieces of information published in the same newspaper to highlight a social paradox, not to claim that the newspaper article is factually false.
default.q.n2-9-q71-71.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the fact that many people have no jobs or housing is only one part of the situation. The strange point is the contradiction between a labor shortage and many unemployed people who are unwilling to work.
default.q.n2-9-q71-71.why.3: (d) Correct because the author cites a strange paradox: there is such a labor shortage that foreign workers are needed, yet the unemployment rate is high and unemployed people do not apply for jobs: 「しかし、①ふしぎなことに、同じ新聞には、日本の失業率が...生活に困っている人がいるといった記事もある。外国人労働者に来てもらわなければならないほど労働力が不足しているというのに、どうしてそういうところにこれらの日本人が就職しないのか。」
default.q.n2-9-q72-72.explanation:
- Translation of the question: Which statement is closest to the young people's idea of "being true to oneself" (自分らしさ) in the passage?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. "Being true to oneself" lies in turning an unappealing job into an appealing one.
  2. "Being true to oneself" appears only when one is able to do the job one wants.
  3. "Being true to oneself" emerges when one devotes oneself fully to doing an ordinary job.
  4. Because there are very few jobs in Japan that are "right for oneself," it is better to work abroad.
- Main point: Paragraphs 2, 3, and 4 indicate that unemployed young people often make excuses that they have not found "the job that is right for them." For them, "being true to oneself" means idealized images created by the media and films (such as working for a glamorous foreign-owned company in Roppongi); they believe that only doing the job they like means being their true selves, and would rather remain unemployed than do an ordinary job.
default.q.n2-9-q72-72.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the young people in the passage quit or refused to work because they found the jobs unattractive (「魅力がないからやめた」). The passage does not say that they tried to transform the jobs into something appealing.
default.q.n2-9-q72-72.why.1: (b) Correct. According to the young people in the passage, they regard only jobs matching their personal preferences, such as working for a foreign company in Roppongi, as truly “like them.” If they cannot obtain such a job, they would rather stay at home: 「彼らの多くが『自分らしい仕事』が見つからないから失業中だという...『六本木あたりの外資系...の仕事』につくのが『自分らしい』のだと答える...そんな職場や仕事につけないから『自分らしく』ない、だから何もしない」.
default.q.n2-9-q72-72.why.2: (c) Incorrect because this is the author's view in the final paragraph—that one's distinctive character naturally emerges through diligently doing the work assigned to them—which is the complete opposite of the young people's view that ordinary work does not suit them.
default.q.n2-9-q72-72.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage only mentions young people wanting to work for a foreign-capital company (外資系) located in Roppongi, Tokyo. It does not mention working abroad.
default.q.n2-9-q73-73.explanation:
- Question translation: What does the author most want to say through this article?
- Answer choices:
  1. Many young people in Japan currently cannot find jobs, so Japan should not accept more foreign workers...
  2. Young people should stop pursuing unrealistic ideals and first support themselves through their own work...
  3. There are very few ideal jobs in the real world, so searching for a job that truly suits one's character...
  4. Young people today are very selfish and inattentive, so they will never be able to attain an ideal job...
- Main point: The author criticizes the tendency of some young people to use the excuse of "searching for their own style" to avoid working while chasing unrealistic fantasies. The author's core message appears at the end: instead of imagining glamorous ideals, people should work hard and support themselves in the real world; only after becoming self-reliant and finding meaning in life can their "true individuality" emerge.
default.q.n2-9-q73-73.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author does not discuss or oppose policies for accepting foreign workers; the focus is on criticizing young people’s pickiness about jobs.
default.q.n2-9-q73-73.why.1: (b) Correct. The author's message at the end is that young people should abandon idealized images and first become self-supporting in the real world: 「もしも『自分らしさ』というものがあるなら、それは与えられた仕事をまじめにして、自分の生活を作ったときに自然と生まれてくるものなのである。『六本木の外資系』などというイメージより、現実の世界で自立すること。」
default.q.n2-9-q73-73.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author does not encourage people to unrealistically search for a "uniquely fitting job". Instead, the author emphasizes working seriously in the real world and becoming independent.
default.q.n2-9-q73-73.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the comment that young people are selfish is merely a critical point in the body of the passage (「はっきりいって、わがままである」), not the main guiding message of the entire article.
default.q.n2-9-q74-74.explanation:
- Question translation: How many activities or clubs can a man who wants to learn cooking join?
- Choice translations:
  1. 1
  2. 2
  3. 3
  4. 4
- Summary and analysis:
  The passage introduces community clubs in Kasumi City. Among them, there are 2 cooking activities that men can join:
  1. 「インドの伝統カレーを作るサークル ナマステ」: An Indian housewife living in the city teaches participants how to make her specialty dishes and curries; participation is open to everyone.
  2. 「地域の伝統食を守ろう かすみ市の台所」: Participants learn traditional local dishes from elderly women, and the announcement explicitly says that men are welcome ("男性も歓迎").
  Therefore, there are 2 suitable activities in total.
default.q.n2-9-q74-74.why.0: (a) Choice 1 (1つ) is incorrect because there are two cooking-related activities that men can participate in, not just one.
default.q.n2-9-q74-74.why.1:
(b) Choice 2 (2つ) is correct because there are 2 cooking activities suitable for men:
1. 「インドの伝統カレーを作るサークル ナマステ」: Teaches Indian curry cooking ("市内在住のインド人主婦が自慢の料理を教えてくれます") and has no gender restriction.
2. 「地域の伝統食を守ろう かすみ市の台所」: Teaches traditional local cuisine ("地域の人々が昔から食べた伝統の料理をおばあちゃんたちから学びましょう") and explicitly welcomes men ("男性も歓迎").
default.q.n2-9-q74-74.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (3つ) is incorrect because, apart from the two cooking classes mentioned above (ナマステ and かすみ市の台所), none of the other clubs in the passage is related to cooking instruction.
default.q.n2-9-q74-74.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (4つ) is incorrect because the passage lists only 2 cooking activities, not 4.
default.q.n2-9-q75-75.explanation:
- Translation of the question: An international student from India wants to learn traditional aspects of Japanese culture. The student has classes every weekday morning but is free at other times. How many activities meet these conditions?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. 2
  2. 3
  3. 4
  4. 5
- Summary & analysis:
  + The international student’s conditions:
    1. Subject of interest: Traditional Japanese culture (日本の伝統的なもの).
    2. Availability: Busy on weekday mornings (平日午前), but free on weekday afternoons/evenings and all day on weekends (Saturday and Sunday).
  + Review of clubs related to traditional Japanese culture:
    * 「折り紙クラブ」: The traditional Japanese art of origami (「日本に古くからある折り紙」). Schedule: Tuesday afternoon, 16:00–18:00 (fits the student’s free time) → SUITABLE.
    * 「うつせみ」: Learning how to wear a traditional Japanese kimono (「日本伝統の着物の着方を覚えましょう」). Schedule: Friday afternoon, 14:00–16:00 (fits the student’s free time) → SUITABLE.
    * 「茶道教室（表千家） わび庵」: Traditional Japanese tea ceremony (「お茶は日本の心です」). Schedule: From 10:00 every Monday morning (「毎週月曜日 朝 10 時～」) → EXCLUDED because it conflicts with weekday morning classes.
    * Other clubs: Indian Curry Club (not traditional Japanese culture), Elegant Dance (Western culture), Braille Point (community service), Midori Club (planting flowers in parks), Hula Aloha Club (Hawaiian culture), and Tsubasa Club (raising and educating young children).
  + Conclusion: Exactly 2 activities meet both the subject and scheduling requirements.
default.q.n2-9-q75-75.why.0:
(a) Choice 1 (2つ) is correct because exactly two activities satisfy both conditions: learning traditional Japanese culture and being available on weekday mornings:
1. 「折り紙クラブ」: Learn traditional Japanese origami (“日本に古くからある折り紙”), meeting on Tuesday afternoons (“毎週火曜日午後 4 時～ 6 時”).
2. 「うつせみ」: Learn how to wear traditional Japanese kimono (“日本伝統の着物の着方を覚えましょう”), meeting on Friday afternoons (“金曜 午後 2 時～ 4 時”).
default.q.n2-9-q75-75.why.1: (b) Choice 2 (3つ) is incorrect because the traditional tea ceremony class 「茶道教室（表千家） わび庵」 is held on Monday mornings ("毎週月曜日 朝 10 時～"), which conflicts with the exchange student's weekday morning classes (平日午前), making it impossible to attend. Therefore, only two activities are suitable.
default.q.n2-9-q75-75.why.2: (c) Choice 3 (4つ) is incorrect because only 2 clubs both teach traditional Japanese culture and fit the international student’s free schedule.
default.q.n2-9-q75-75.why.3: (d) Choice 4 (5つ) is incorrect because there are not five activities that satisfy all the stated conditions.
default.q.n2-9-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 努力.
default.q.n2-9-q11-11.explanation:
- Sentence translation: As a result of our efforts, our activities have been recognized by society.
- Related vocabulary: 努力 (どりょく: effort), 自慢 (じまん: pride, boasting), 目的 (もくてき: purpose), 覚悟 (かくご: readiness, determination).
- Common expressions: 「努力の結果」(the result of one's efforts), 「努力を重ねる」(make continued efforts).
- Example: 長年の努力の結果、ついに国家試験に合格することができた。(As a result of many years of effort, I was finally able to pass the national examination.)
default.q.n2-9-q11-11.why.0: (a) 自慢 means boasting or conceit, which does not fit the meaning of being recognized by society through one’s efforts.
default.q.n2-9-q11-11.why.1: (b) 努力 (effort) combines with 「〜の結果」to form 「努力の結果」(the result of one's efforts), which fits the sentence context perfectly.
default.q.n2-9-q11-11.why.2: (c) 目的 (purpose) is the goal one aims toward, so 「目的の結果」 does not fit this context.
default.q.n2-9-q11-11.why.3: (d) 覚悟 (readiness; resolve to face something) does not fit before 「〜の結果」 when expressing the reason for being recognized by society.
default.q.n2-9-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 1. すなわち.
default.q.n2-9-q12-12.explanation:
- Sentence translation: My mother's mother, that is, my grandmother, is 72 years old now.
- Grammar / conjunction: 「すなわち」 (that is, in other words = 言い換えれば) is used to clarify or restate the noun or clause before it in equivalent terms (mother's mother = grandmother).
- Distinguishing conjunctions:
  + そのうえ: moreover, in addition (adds information).
  + ところが: however, but (introduces an unexpected or contrasting result).
  + なぜなら: the reason is that (explains a cause, usually followed by 〜からだ).
- Example: 日本の首都、すなわち東京には多くの人口が集中している。(Japan's capital, namely Tokyo, has a large population concentrated there.)
default.q.n2-9-q12-12.why.0: (a) すなわち means “that is” or “in other words,” and is used to rephrase or clarify the preceding phrase (mother's mother = maternal grandmother).
default.q.n2-9-q12-12.why.1: (b) そのうえ (moreover, in addition) is used to add information in the same direction, not to explain an equivalent meaning.
default.q.n2-9-q12-12.why.2: (c) ところが (however, but) connects two contrasting clauses or indicates an unexpected development.
default.q.n2-9-q12-12.why.3: (d) なぜなら (because, the reason is that) is used to begin an explanation of a cause or reason.
default.q.n2-9-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 1. キャンパス.
default.q.n2-9-q13-13.explanation:
- Meaning: Because this university campus became too cramped, it was decided that the university would relocate.
- Katakana vocabulary:
  + キャンパス (campus): a university or college campus.
  + キャンプ (camp): camping, training camp.
  + トンネル (tunnel): tunnel.
  + マーケット (market): market, marketplace.
- Example: 来年、新しいキャンパスに移転する予定です。(We plan to move to a new campus next year.)
default.q.n2-9-q13-13.why.0: (a) キャンパス (campus - a university campus) combines naturally with 「大学」and「せまくなった」and fits the context best.
default.q.n2-9-q13-13.why.1: (b) キャンプ (camping) is not used to refer to the grounds or area of a university.
default.q.n2-9-q13-13.why.2: (c) トンネル (tunnel) is unrelated to a university.
default.q.n2-9-q13-13.why.3: (d) マーケット (market) is unsuitable as the subject referring to a crowded school location.
default.q.n2-9-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 4. なつかしくて.
default.q.n2-9-q14-14.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Yesterday, after meeting friends from my hometown, we felt nostalgic and ended up talking until late at night.
- Related vocabulary: 懐かしい (nostalgic, reminiscent), 惜しい (regrettable, a shame), 悔しい (frustrating, bitterly disappointing), 親しい (close, familiar).
- Expression: 「話し込む」 (to become absorbed in conversation and lose track of time).
- Example: 昔のアルバムを見ていたら、高校時代がなつかしく思い出された。(Looking through an old album brought back nostalgic memories of my high school days.)
default.q.n2-9-q14-14.why.0: (a) おしくて (惜しい: regrettable, a shame, precious) is not used to express the excitement or emotion of meeting old friends again.
default.q.n2-9-q14-14.why.1: (b) くやしくて (悔しい: frustrated, bitter, or upset after losing) does not fit the context of meeting close friends.
default.q.n2-9-q14-14.why.2: (c) したしくて (親しい: close, familiar) is an adjective describing a relationship, so its て-form cannot express the emotional cause of becoming absorbed in conversation, as 「なつかしくて」 does.
default.q.n2-9-q14-14.why.3: (d) なつかしくて (懐かしい: nostalgic, full of longing) accurately expresses the feeling of meeting a friend from one’s hometown again after a long separation, causing both of them to become absorbed in conversation until late at night.
default.q.n2-9-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ならって.
default.q.n2-9-q15-15.explanation:
- Translation: My older sister goes to the swimming pool for her health. Following her example, I decided to start swimming too.
- Pattern / expression: 「〜に倣う（ならう）」 (to follow, imitate, or model oneself on someone or something).
  + Note: 倣う (to imitate or follow an example) differs from 習う (to learn knowledge or a skill).
- Example: 先輩のやり方に倣って、作業を進めてください。(Please proceed with the work by following your senior colleague’s method.)
default.q.n2-9-q15-15.why.0: (a) か山って is meaningless due to a display or spelling error (OCR); it does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n2-9-q15-15.why.1: (b) ならって (倣って: follow, model oneself on) is used with the particle に in 「〜に倣って」, meaning “following / modeling oneself on someone,” which is completely appropriate in this sentence.
default.q.n2-9-q15-15.why.2: (c) まざって (混ざって/交ざって: mix, mingle) is used for objects or substances mixing together, or for mingling with a group; it does not express following an individual's actions.
default.q.n2-9-q15-15.why.3: (d) ならんで (並んで: standing in a line, alongside) indicates a spatial position in a line or at the same level; it does not mean learning by copying someone’s actions.
default.q.n2-9-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (いじめて), because bullying his younger brother is the most appropriate reason for being scolded.
default.q.n2-9-q16-16.explanation:
Meaning: When I was little, I was scolded for bullying my younger brother.
- 虐める / 苛める (いじめる): to bully, harass, or tease.
- 叱る (しかる): to scold (passive: 叱られる - to be scolded).
- Example: 弟をいじめて母にひどく叱られた。(I bullied my younger brother and was severely scolded by my mother.)
default.q.n2-9-q16-16.why.0: (a) 「あいして」(愛して — love): expresses affection and is inappropriate in the context of being scolded (しかられました).
default.q.n2-9-q16-16.why.1: (b) 「いじめて」（苛めて/虐めて）: “bullying” or “teasing.” This fits the context because bullying the younger sibling was the reason the adult scolded them.
default.q.n2-9-q16-16.why.2: (c) 「い消って」is a typing error or meaningless string in Japanese and is inappropriate here.
default.q.n2-9-q16-16.why.3: (d) 「か山いがって」(a misspelling of 可愛がって, to love or dote on): Incorrect spelling and contrary to the context of being scolded.
default.q.n2-9-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (じきに), meaning “soon / before long,” used with the future prediction 「やむでしょう」.
default.q.n2-9-q17-17.explanation:
Meaning: The rain will stop soon. Until then, let's have some tea together.
- じきに (直に): shortly, soon, before long.
- 止む (やむ): to stop (rain), to die down (wind).
- Example: じきに父も帰ってくるでしょう。(My father will probably be back before long, too.)
default.q.n2-9-q17-17.why.0: (a) 「じきに」(直に) means "soon" or "before long." It describes something that will happen shortly and fits very well with 「やむでしょう」.
default.q.n2-9-q17-17.why.1: (b) 「すでに」（既に - already）is used for events that have already been completed in the past, not for near-future predictions.
default.q.n2-9-q17-17.why.2: (c) 「ただ活に」 (a misspelling of 直ちに - ただちに: immediately): The kanji is incorrect, and the expression is generally used in commands or instructions for urgent action.
default.q.n2-9-q17-17.why.3: (d) 「ひとりでに」(独りでに) means "naturally" or "on its own." It describes a spontaneous state without an external force, such as a door opening by itself, and does not indicate a point in time.
default.q.n2-9-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (とんでもない), meaning “absurd / unacceptable / unimaginable.”
default.q.n2-9-q18-18.explanation:
Meaning: "To go back to work immediately after having surgery is completely unacceptable / utterly unreasonable."
- 手術 (しゅじゅつ): surgery.
- とんでもない: unreasonable, outrageous, or unacceptable; it is also used to humbly reject praise or thanks.
- Example: この嵐の中で外出するなんて、とんでもない。(Going outside in a storm like this is out of the question.)
default.q.n2-9-q18-18.why.0: (a) 「くだらない」（下らない - trivial, silly, worthless）is commonly used to judge something pointless or a joke without value.
default.q.n2-9-q18-18.why.1: (b) 「だらしない」 means sloppy, untidy, or undisciplined. It is commonly used to describe a person’s conduct, clothing, or careless personality.
default.q.n2-9-q18-18.why.2: (c) 「とんでもない」 (absurd, unbelievable): Expresses strong opposition to an unreasonable or dangerous action, such as going to work immediately after surgery.
default.q.n2-9-q18-18.why.3: (d) 「やむをえない」（止むを得ない - unavoidable, having no choice）: Indicates that there is no alternative, which conflicts with the oppositional tone of the sentence.
default.q.n2-9-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (手ごろな) because it forms the familiar expression 「手ごろな値段」 with 「値段」, meaning “an affordable, reasonable price.”
default.q.n2-9-q19-19.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Mr. Yamamoto is looking for an affordable handbag.
- 手頃 (てごろ): suitable, reasonably priced, affordable.
- Set phrases: 手ごろな値段 / 手ごろな価格 (an affordable, reasonable price).
- Example: 手ごろな値段のホテルを予約しました。(I booked a reasonably priced hotel.)
default.q.n2-9-q19-19.why.0: (a) 「気楽な」（きらくな - relaxed, carefree）describes a mood, lifestyle, or type of work; it does not combine with 「値段」.
default.q.n2-9-q19-19.why.1: (b) 「けんきょな」（謙虚な: humble）is used to describe a person’s attitude or personality.
default.q.n2-9-q19-19.why.2: (c) 「そまつな」（粗末な）means crude, plain, or shabby. It is used for old items or a simple meal, not with 「値段」.
default.q.n2-9-q19-19.why.3: (d) 「手ごろな」(手頃な - reasonably priced, affordable): Correctly combines with the noun 「値段」 to form 「手ごろな値段」 (a reasonable, affordable price).
default.q.n2-9-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (費用) because it is a noun referring to the cost of an activity, such as studying abroad, and naturally collocates with the verb 「かかる」.
default.q.n2-9-q20-20.explanation:
Meaning: I want to study abroad, so please tell me approximately how much it will cost.
- 費用 (ひよう): cost, expense (kanji meaning: “fee + use”).
- Common collocations: 費用がかかる (incur costs), 留学費用 (study-abroad expenses).
- Example: 旅行にかかる費用を計算してください。(Please calculate the expenses for the trip.)
default.q.n2-9-q20-20.why.0: (a) 「価値」（かち, value）refers to the value of an object or its معنingspiritual significance; it is not used with the verb 「かかる」, which means to require or cost.
default.q.n2-9-q20-20.why.1: (b) 「価格」（かかく - listed price）refers to the price of a specific product and is not used for the total cost of studying abroad.
default.q.n2-9-q20-20.why.2: (c) 「費用」(ひよう): the money paid for an undertaking or plan; it correctly combines in the expression 「費用がかかる」.
default.q.n2-9-q20-20.why.3: (d) 「利用」（りよう - use）: It means to use or make use of something, such as a means of transportation or a service, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n2-9-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (気力) because it describes the loss of one's mental energy, willpower, or motivation to work due to very low wages.
default.q.n2-9-q21-21.explanation:
Meaning: With wages this low, even my motivation to work disappears.
- 気力 (きりょく): energy, spirit, willpower, motivation.
- Common expressions: 働く気力 (motivation to work), 気力が湧く (feel one’s energy return), 気力を失う (lose all motivation).
- Example: 疲労のあまり、起き上がる気力もない。(I am so exhausted that I do not even have the energy to get up.)
default.q.n2-9-q21-21.why.0: (a) 「気力」（きりょく）: Mental strength, willpower, and motivation; 「働く気力がなくなる」 means to lose all motivation to work.
default.q.n2-9-q21-21.why.1: (b) 「体力」（たいりょく - physical strength）refers to the body's physical strength and does not directly decrease merely because one's salary is low.
default.q.n2-9-q21-21.why.2: (c) 「協力」（きょうりょく）means cooperation or joint effort among multiple people, so it does not fit the phrase 「働く協力」.
default.q.n2-9-q21-21.why.3: (d) 「手当て」（てあて）: an allowance, subsidy, or medical treatment; it does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-9-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (けしき) because natural geographical features such as slopes, ponds, and lakes create beautiful scenery (けしきがいい).
default.q.n2-9-q22-22.explanation:
Meaning: The suburbs of this town have many slopes, as well as lakes and ponds, so the scenery is very beautiful.
- 景色 (けしき): scenery, landscape.
- 郊外 (こうがい): suburbs.
- 坂 (さか): slope, 湖 (みずうみ): lake, 池 (いけ): pond.
- Example: この部屋の窓からは海の素晴らしい景色が見える。(You can see a magnificent sea view from this room's window.)
default.q.n2-9-q22-22.why.0: (a) 「けしき」（景色 - scenery, landscape）: This is the most appropriate word for describing natural scenery with slopes, ponds, and lakes (けしきがいい: the scenery is beautiful).
default.q.n2-9-q22-22.why.1: (b) 「気分」: mood or physical condition; it is used for a person’s emotions or state of health (e.g., 気分がすぐれない).
default.q.n2-9-q22-22.why.2: (c) 「気持ち」（きもち - feeling, mood）refers to one's thoughts or pleasant feelings; it is not used to describe the beauty of natural scenery.
default.q.n2-9-q22-22.why.3: (d) 「からだ」 (体 - body) does not combine with 「からだがいい」 to describe scenery or the environment.
default.q.n2-9-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 静かに, because 「そっと」means quietly, gently, or without making noise, and is synonymous with 「静かに」in this context.
default.q.n2-9-q23-23.explanation:
Meaning: I leaned close to her ear and whispered: 「I love you」.
Vocabulary & further notes:
- そっと: gently, quietly, softly (doing something carefully and without making noise or attracting attention). Example: 赤ちゃんが寝ているので、ドアをそっと閉めた (The baby was sleeping, so I quietly closed the door).
- 耳元 (ear): by one's ear, close to one's ear.
- 「愛してるよ」: I love you.
default.q.n2-9-q23-23.why.0: (a) Correct. 「静かに」 (quietly, gently, softly) is synonymous with 「そっと」 in the context of leaning close to someone's ear and speaking softly.
default.q.n2-9-q23-23.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「はっきりと」 means clearly, distinctly, or decisively.
default.q.n2-9-q23-23.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「急に」means suddenly or unexpectedly, equivalent to 突然.
default.q.n2-9-q23-23.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「大声で」 means “in a loud voice” or “shouting,” the opposite of leaning over and speaking quietly.
default.q.n2-9-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 気持ちのいい because「さわやかな」means refreshing, fresh, and pleasant, and is synonymous with「気持ちのいい」.
default.q.n2-9-q24-24.explanation:
Meaning: Today is an extremely refreshing and pleasant morning.
Vocabulary and related expressions:
- さわやか (爽やか): refreshing, fresh, bright, pleasant (used for weather, moods, personalities, smiles, and so on).
- Example: 爽やかな笑顔 (a bright, radiant smile), 朝の爽やかな風 (the fresh, refreshing morning breeze).
default.q.n2-9-q24-24.why.0: (a) Correct. 「気持ちのいい」 means pleasant, comfortable, or refreshing, and is synonymous with the adjective 「さわやかな」.
default.q.n2-9-q24-24.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「晴れた」 describes sunny, clear weather and is not synonymous with さわやか.
default.q.n2-9-q24-24.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「涼しい」 refers specifically to a pleasantly cool temperature, which is narrower than the fresh, invigorating meaning of さわやか.
default.q.n2-9-q24-24.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「あたたかい」 means warm, in terms of temperature or feelings.
default.q.n2-9-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 基準 because 「目安」 means a standard or guideline used as a reference, and is synonymous with 「基準」.
default.q.n2-9-q25-25.explanation:
Meaning: Please tell me the standard amount or guideline for using this medicine.
Vocabulary & further explanation:
- 目安 (めやす): a guideline, reference point, approximate standard used as a basis. Common expressions include 目安にする (use as a guideline) and 1回2錠を目安に (use two tablets per dose as a guideline).
- Example: 1日の摂取量の目安は2000キロカロリーです (The guideline for daily energy intake is approximately 2,000 kilocalories).
default.q.n2-9-q25-25.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「目標」 means a goal or target that one strives toward in order to accomplish it.
default.q.n2-9-q25-25.why.1: (b) Correct. 「基準」means a standard or criterion used as a basis for measuring or evaluating, and is synonymous with 「目安」.
default.q.n2-9-q25-25.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「限界」 means a limit or maximum threshold that cannot be exceeded.
default.q.n2-9-q25-25.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「指示」 means direction, guidance, or an instruction to carry something out.
default.q.n2-9-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 2. かつて, because 「以前」 means before or formerly and is synonymous with 「かつて」.
default.q.n2-9-q26-26.explanation:
Meaning: This area used to have a park.
Vocabulary and related expressions:
- 以前: previously, formerly.
- かつて: once, formerly (often referring to something that existed or was true in the past but no longer does).
- Example: かつてここは海だった (This place used to be the sea).
default.q.n2-9-q26-26.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「第一に」means “first of all” or “most importantly” (equivalent to 何よりも).
default.q.n2-9-q26-26.why.1: (b) Correct. 「かつて」 means “formerly, in the past, once,” equivalent to 以前 or 昔.
default.q.n2-9-q26-26.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「先に」 means “first” in sequence or “earlier,” as in お先に失礼します or さっき.
default.q.n2-9-q26-26.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「真っ先に」 means “first of all” or “before everyone else” (equivalent to 一番初めに).
default.q.n2-9-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2. うるさい because「さわがしい」means noisy or boisterous and is synonymous with「うるさい」in this context.
default.q.n2-9-q27-27.explanation:
Meaning: The classroom is very noisy and boisterous.
Vocabulary and related expressions:
- さわがしい (騒がしい): noisy, rowdy, tumultuous (with lots of loud talking and laughter), or socially unsettled (世間が騒がしい).
- うるさい (煩い / 喧しい): noisy, grating, troublesome.
- Example: 外が騒がしいので、何があったのか見に行った (It was noisy outside, so I went to see what had happened.)
default.q.n2-9-q27-27.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「荒っぽい」 means “rough,” “粗ce,” or “reckless,” and describes rough behavior, brusque gestures, or dangerous driving.
default.q.n2-9-q27-27.why.1: (b) Correct. 「うるさい」 (noisy or bothersome) is synonymous with 「さわがしい」 when describing a loud, boisterous setting.
default.q.n2-9-q27-27.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「あわただしい」(慌ただしい) means hectic, hurried, or busy, describing a rush involving work or time.
default.q.n2-9-q27-27.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「おだやか」 (穏やか: calm, gentle, peaceful) is the opposite of さわがしい.
default.q.n2-9-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 3: くれぐれも is used with a request or piece of advice (気をつけてください) to express an earnest, emphatic reminder or warning.
default.q.n2-9-q28-28.explanation:
「くれぐれも」(earnestly, sincerely, by all means): An adverb used when giving heartfelt advice, reminders, requests, or good wishes. It often occurs with structures such as 「〜てください」and「〜よう（に）お伝えください」.
Example: くれぐれもお体に気をつけてお過ごしください。(Please take especially good care of yourself.)
default.q.n2-9-q28-28.why.0: Incorrect because「くれぐれも」does not indicate an increasing degree of emotion or weather; this sentence should use「ますます」or「めっきり」.
default.q.n2-9-q28-28.why.1: Incorrect because 「くれぐれも」does not modify an act of informing or recounting; this sentence should use 「詳しく」or「こと細かに」.
default.q.n2-9-q28-28.why.2: Correct because 「くれぐれも」 naturally combines with the advice or request pattern 「〜てください」 to emphasize a heartfelt warning or request (くれぐれも気をつけてください: please take great care).
default.q.n2-9-q28-28.why.3: Incorrect because 「くれぐれも」 is not used in a hypothetical or regretful sentence to indicate a possible outcome; 「きっと」 or 「絶対に」 should be used instead.
default.q.n2-9-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1: いきいき (full of vitality, lively, enthusiastic) is used to describe a person's positive attitude and energetic approach to work.
default.q.n2-9-q29-29.explanation:
「いきいき（生き生き）」: full of life, lively, energetic, enthusiastic. It commonly describes a person’s expression, eyes, or positive, energetic manner of working or studying (いきいきと働く、いきいきとした目).
Example: 彼女は子供たちと遊んでいる時、いつもいきいきとしている。(She is always full of energy and joy when playing with the children.)
default.q.n2-9-q29-29.why.0: Correct because 「いきいきと〜する」 describes working or acting energetically, enthusiastically, and with vitality.
default.q.n2-9-q29-29.why.1: Incorrect because to describe the freshness and quality of food or sashimi, use 「新鮮（だ）」or 「生きがいい」, not 「いきいき」.
default.q.n2-9-q29-29.why.2: Incorrect because 「いきいき」has a positive nuance of being full of vitality and is not used for disasters or earthquakes. To describe a disaster scene as vivid and starkly realistic, 「生々しい」is appropriate.
default.q.n2-9-q29-29.why.3: Incorrect because, as in sentence 3, a disaster scene described as vivid or realistic should use「生々しい」or「リアルな」.
default.q.n2-9-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 2: あきらかだ (obvious, clear beyond doubt) is used to affirm an evident fact or truth.
default.q.n2-9-q30-30.explanation:
「明らか（あきらか）」: clear, obvious, evident; used when a fact or truth is beyond doubt. It is often used in forms such as 「〜のは明らかだ」, 「明らかな事実」, and 「〜を明らかにする」.
Example: 調査の結果、事故の原因が明らかになった。(The investigation revealed the cause of the accident.)
default.q.n2-9-q30-30.why.0: Incorrect because a cheerful, radiant expression after passing an exam should be described with 「晴れやかな（顔）」 or 「明るい（顔）」, not 「明らか」.
default.q.n2-9-q30-30.why.1: Correct because the pattern 「〜のは明らかだ」 is properly used to assert that something is clear or obvious (it is obvious that he is lying).
default.q.n2-9-q30-30.why.2: Incorrect because when asking someone to write clearly and neatly for easy reading, use 「はっきりと」 or 「きれいに／丁寧に」.
default.q.n2-9-q30-30.why.3: Incorrect because answering a question confidently and clearly calls for an adverb such as 「はっきりと」 or 「堂々と」, not 「明らかに」.
default.q.n2-9-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 該当する means to correspond to or be equivalent to something (the foreign word corresponding to this word).
default.q.n2-9-q31-31.explanation:
「該当（がいとう）」: to correspond to, fall under, or meet a particular condition, standard, or category. It is used with a verb in 「〜に該当する」, or in compound nouns such as 「該当者」(person concerned/eligible person) and 「該当事項」(corresponding item). 
Example: 条件に該当する方は、窓口でお手続きください。(Those who meet the conditions, please complete the procedure at the counter.)
default.q.n2-9-q31-31.why.0: Incorrect because answering vaguely or casually just to get it over with requires 「適当（てきとう）に」 or 「いい加減に」, not 「該当」.
default.q.n2-9-q31-31.why.1: Incorrect because Japanese does not have the compound 「該当的」. To describe a reasonable or feasible plan, use 「現実的」or 「妥当」.
default.q.n2-9-q31-31.why.2: Incorrect because the word 「該当性」 does not exist; to express validity or persuasiveness, use 「妥当性（に欠ける）」 or 「信憑性」.
default.q.n2-9-q31-31.why.3: Correct because 「〜に該当する」 is the standard structure meaning to correspond to or match a particular concept or criterion, as in the corresponding term from a foreign language.
default.q.n2-9-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 中断する means to interrupt or suspend an activity in progress, such as a match being temporarily stopped because of rain.
default.q.n2-9-q32-32.explanation:
「中断（ちゅうだん）」: to interrupt or temporarily suspend something in progress, usually with the intention of resuming it later. Distinguish it from 「中止」, which means to cancel completely or stop for good before or during an event.
Example: 停電のため、作業を一時中断せざるを得なかった。(Due to a power outage, we had no choice but to suspend the work temporarily.)
default.q.n2-9-q32-32.why.0: Incorrect because canceling or postponing an appointment with friends requires 「取り消した／キャンセルした」 or 「延期した」.
default.q.n2-9-q32-32.why.1: Incorrect because when a field trip is canceled due to a typhoon and does not take place, 「中止（になった）」 should be used, not 「中断」.
default.q.n2-9-q32-32.why.2: Incorrect because a tree broken or toppled by lightning should be described with 「折れた」 or 「倒れた」; 「中断」 is used only for an ongoing event or process.
default.q.n2-9-q32-32.why.3: Correct because 「中断（する）」 accurately describes an ongoing process or activity being temporarily interrupted, as in a game being suspended because of rain.
default.q.n2-9-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 1. いはん.
default.q.n2-9-q1-1.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Throwing garbage into the river is against the law.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 違反 (Iهان — violation).
- Example: スピード違反で警察に止められた。(I was stopped by the police for speeding.)
default.q.n2-9-q1-1.why.0: (a) Correct. 違反 consists of 「違」 (on-reading: い) and 「反」 (on-reading: はん), giving the standard reading いはん (violation).
default.q.n2-9-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「違」does not have the long-vowel reading いい in this word.
default.q.n2-9-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect, because 「反」 is read with the sound はん here; it does not become the semi-voiced sound ぱん.
default.q.n2-9-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it both adds an unnecessary long vowel いい and incorrectly uses the semi-voiced sound ぱん.
default.q.n2-9-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1. しゅのう.
default.q.n2-9-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: It was reported that the leaders of the two countries would hold talks soon.
- Sino-Japanese reading: 首脳 (THỦ NÃO — head, head of state, senior leader).
- Example: 首脳会議で気候変動の問題が話し合われた。(The issue of climate change was discussed at the summit.)
default.q.n2-9-q2-2.why.0: (a) Correct. 首脳 consists of the characters 「首」 (on-reading: しゅ) and 「脳」 (on-reading: のう), so the correct reading is しゅのう (head or senior leader).
default.q.n2-9-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「首」 has only the short on-reading しゅ, not the long reading しゅう.
default.q.n2-9-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect. しゅしょう is the reading of 首相 (prime minister); 「脳」 is not read as しょう.
default.q.n2-9-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect because しゅうし is the reading of 終始 (from beginning to end) or 収支 (income and expenses), and is unrelated to 首脳.
default.q.n2-9-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 3. せんそう.
default.q.n2-9-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning: In history class, we discussed war and its responsibility.
- Kanji: 戦争 means war.
- Example: 私たちは戦争のない平和な世界を望んでいる。(We hope for a peaceful world without war.)
default.q.n2-9-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect: 「戦」 has the on-reading せん, not せい. せいそう is 清掃, meaning cleaning.
default.q.n2-9-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「戦」is not read as せい and 「争」does not have the voiced reading ぞう (せいぞう is 製造—manufacturing, production).
default.q.n2-9-q3-3.why.2: (c) Correct. 戦争 consists of 「戦」 (on-reading: せん) and 「争」 (on-reading: そう), and is correctly read せんそう (war).
default.q.n2-9-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「争」 is read with the sound そう, not voiced as ぞう.
default.q.n2-9-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 2. かんづめ.
default.q.n2-9-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: “Eating only canned food and frozen food is not good for your health.”
- Kanji note: 缶詰 (canned food).
- Example: 非常用に缶詰をいくつか買っておいた。(I bought several cans in advance for emergencies.)
default.q.n2-9-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect because when 缶 (かん) combines with 詰 (つめ), the つめ undergoes rendaku and becomes づめ.
default.q.n2-9-q4-4.why.1: (b) Correct. 缶詰 consists of 「缶」(かん) and 「詰」(the original reading つめ becomes voiced as づめ), so the standard reading is かんづめ (canned goods, canned food).
default.q.n2-9-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 缶 is a metal can (pronounced かん), whereas びん (瓶) is a glass bottle; in addition, つめ has not been converted to kanji.
default.q.n2-9-q4-4.why.3: (d) びんづめ is the reading of 瓶詰 (bottled or jarred goods), not 缶詰.
default.q.n2-9-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ばくはつ.
default.q.n2-9-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: “A document about the possibility of a gas explosion during an earthquake was issued.”
- Kanji note: 爆発 (explosion, to explode; also sudden outburst).
- Example: 工場で爆発事故が発生した。(An explosion accident occurred at the factory.)
default.q.n2-9-q5-5.why.0: (a) Correct. 爆発 consists of 「爆」 with the on-reading ばく and 「発」 with the on-reading はつ, giving the standard reading ばくはつ (to explode, explosion).
default.q.n2-9-q5-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the on-reading of 「爆」 is ばく, not ぼく.
default.q.n2-9-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「爆」is not read as ぼく, and 「発」in this word is read as はつ, not ほつ.
default.q.n2-9-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect because neither ぼう nor ほつ is the correct reading of 爆発.
default.q.n2-9-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 駐車場 (ちゅうしゃじょう - parking lot).
default.q.n2-9-q6-6.explanation:
- Meaning: The people who come to the prefectural office are having difficulty because the parking lot is too small.
- Sino-Japanese readings: 駐車 (parking), 駐車場 (parking lot).
- Distinguish easily confused kanji containing the horse radical (馬): 「駐」(stop, park), 「馳」(run quickly, speed along), 「騒」(make noise), 「駅」(station).
- Example: ここは駐車禁止エリアです。(This is a no-parking area.)
default.q.n2-9-q6-6.why.0: (a) 駅車場: incorrect kanji. 「駅」 (station) is not used to form a word meaning “parking lot.”
default.q.n2-9-q6-6.why.1: (b) 駐車場: Correct. 「駐」 (to stop or park) combines with 「車場」 to form 「駐車場」(ちゅうしゃじょう - parking lot).
default.q.n2-9-q6-6.why.2: (c) 馳車場: The kanji is incorrect. 「馳」(to dash or run quickly) has the horse radical (馬) on the left, but a different meaning, and does not form this word.
default.q.n2-9-q6-6.why.3: (d) 騒車場: incorrect kanji. 「騒」(noise, commotion) contains the horse radical (馬) on the left but has a completely different meaning.
default.q.n2-9-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 偶然 (by chance, coincidentally).
default.q.n2-9-q7-7.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: Yesterday, I happened to run into an old friend at the ticket gates.
- Vocabulary: 偶然 (ぐうぜん—by chance, accidentally). Its antonym is 必然 (ひつぜん—inevitable, necessarily).
- Distinction: The kanji 「偶」 differs from 「寓」 and 「隅」.
- Example: 旅先で偶然昔の同級生に出会った。(I happened to run into an old classmate while traveling.)
default.q.n2-9-q7-7.why.0: (a) 寓然: Incorrect kanji. The character 「寓」 (used in words such as 寓話 and 寓居) has the 宀 radical at the top and does not form the word meaning “accidental”.
default.q.n2-9-q7-7.why.1: (b) 偶然: Correct. 「偶然」(ぐうぜん) means by chance or accidentally, formed from 「偶」 and 「然」.
default.q.n2-9-q7-7.why.2: (c) 隅然: Incorrect kanji. 「隅」 means a corner or nook and has the 阝 radical on the left.
default.q.n2-9-q7-7.why.3: (d) 伝然: Incorrect kanji. 「伝」 is not used in this word, and 「伝然」 does not exist.
default.q.n2-9-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 招待 (invitation - invite).
default.q.n2-9-q8-8.explanation:
- Meaning: When I was invited to a celebration party, I was treated to drinks.
- Kanji reading: 招待 (しょうたい: invitation, inviting someone).
- Distinction: Do not confuse 紹介 (しょうかい: introduction) with 招待 (しょうたい: invitation). The character 「招」(invite) has the hand radical (扌), while 「紹」(introduce) has the silk radical (糸).
- Example: 友人の結婚式に招待された。(I was invited to my friend’s wedding.)
default.q.n2-9-q8-8.why.0: (a) 紹待: Incorrect kanji. It mistakenly combines 「紹」 (as in 紹介) with 「待」, and this word does not exist.
default.q.n2-9-q8-8.why.1: (b) 紹介: Incorrect vocabulary. 「紹介」 (しょうかい - introduction) means introducing a person or thing, not “inviting” or “entertaining.”
default.q.n2-9-q8-8.why.2: (c) 招待: Correct. 「招待」(しょうたい - invitation, entertaining a guest) combines 「招」(invite, beckon) and 「待」(receive, entertain).
default.q.n2-9-q8-8.why.3: (d) 招介: Incorrect kanji. It mistakenly combines 「招」 with 「介」; this word does not exist.
default.q.n2-9-q9-9.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: Smoke got into my eyes and made my tears well up.
- Kanji: 煙 (smoke; kun-readings: けむり, けむ・い, けむ・る; on-reading: エン).
- Distinction: All of these kanji contain the fire radical (火): 煙 (smoke), 燃 (burn), 燥 (dry), 灯 (lamp).
- Example: 煙突から黒い煙が立ち上っている。(Black smoke is rising from the chimney.)
