default.q.n2-9-q9-9.why.0: (a) 煙: Correct. The kanji 「煙」has the kun-reading 「けむり」, meaning “smoke.”
default.q.n2-9-q9-9.why.1: (b) 燃: Incorrect kanji. 「燃」means “to burn” and has the kun-readings 「も・える」(to burn) and 「も・やす」(to set fire to); it is not read as けむり.
default.q.n2-9-q9-9.why.2: (c) 燥: Incorrect kanji. 「燥」means dry and has the on-reading 「ソウ」(as in 乾燥 - かんそう: drying/dryness); it is not read as けむり.
default.q.n2-9-q9-9.why.3: (d) 灯: Incorrect kanji. 「灯」means lamp/light and has the kun-reading 「ひ」or the on-reading 「トウ」(as in 電灯 - でんとう); it is not read as けむり.
default.q.n2-9-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 岩 (rock, cliff).
default.q.n2-9-q10-10.explanation:
- Meaning: Flowers are blooming along a shore covered with rocky outcrops.
- Kanji: 岩 (いわ; on-reading ガン): a large rock, cliff.
- Distinction: 「石」(いし: an ordinary stone) differs from 「岩」(いわ: a large rock or rocky cliff). In 岩, the 山 radical appears above 石. 「砂」(すな: sand) consists of the stone radical and 少.
- Example: 大きな岩の陰に隠れる。(Hide behind a large rock.)
default.q.n2-9-q10-10.why.0: (a) Incorrect kanji. 「石」means a small or medium-sized stone and has the kun-reading 「いし」, not いわ.
default.q.n2-9-q10-10.why.1: (b) 岩: Correct. The kanji「岩」(a large rock, boulder) has the kun-reading「いわ」.
default.q.n2-9-q10-10.why.2: (c) Incorrect kanji. The kanji 「砂」means “sand” and has the kun-reading 「すな」, not いわ.
default.q.n2-9-q10-10.why.3: (d) 炭: Incorrect kanji. 「炭」 means charcoal or coal and has the kun-reading 「すみ」; it is not read いわ.
default.q.n2-19-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 読むことは.
default.q.n2-19-q50-50.explanation: In the quoted thought 『ああ、本を＿＿何と素晴らしいことであろうか』, this is the exclamatory pattern 「何と〜（こと）であろうか / なんと〜ことか」, meaning “How wonderful ...!” To make “reading books” the topic/subject of this exclamatory predicate, the action 本を読む must be nominalized as 「本を読むこと」 and used with the particle 「は」. Therefore, 「読むことは」 completes the sentence: 「本を読むことは何と素晴らしいことであろうか」(How wonderful reading books is!).
default.q.n2-19-q50-50.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「読めば」 is the conditional form (“if one reads”) and cannot come before a particle or directly serve as the subject of the exclamatory predicate 「何と素晴らしいことであろうか」.
default.q.n2-19-q50-50.why.1: (b) Correct because nominalizing the verb as 「読むこと」 and combining it with the particle 「は」 makes it the topic of an exclamatory sentence praising the value of reading books.
default.q.n2-19-q50-50.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「読んでいれば」is a progressive conditional form meaning “if someone is reading,” so it is syntactically unsuitable as the subject of the sentence.
default.q.n2-19-q50-50.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「読んでいる人は」 turns the subject into "a person who is reading," which does not fit the predicate praising the nature of the act, 「何と素晴らしいことであろうか」. It does not fit the passage's focus on how wonderful reading is.
default.q.n2-19-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 3. あったからなのです.
default.q.n2-19-q51-51.explanation: The sentence begins with 「最終的に私が出版を決断した理由はただ一つ、……」 (The final reason I decided to publish was just one: ...). In Japanese grammar, when a sentence begins with the reason-introducing structure 「理由は〜」, it must end with the corresponding concluding structure 「〜からだ / 〜からなのです」 (it is precisely because...). Therefore, the position (51) following 「願いが」 must be 「あったからなのです」 to complete the paired structure: 「理由は…願いがあったからなのです」 (The reason I decided to publish was precisely that I had a wish...).
default.q.n2-19-q51-51.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「ありました」 merely ends an ordinary declarative sentence; 「から」 is needed to correspond to the phrase 「理由は」 at the beginning.
default.q.n2-19-q51-51.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「あったというのです」 is used for indirect quotation or to emphasize information heard from someone else or being questioned about. It is not used when the author explains their own reason.
default.q.n2-19-q51-51.why.2: (c) Correct because 「あったからなのです」 combines the reason pattern 「〜から」 with the polite emphatic explanatory form 「〜なのです」, correctly corresponding to 「理由は…」 at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.n2-19-q51-51.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「あったはずなのです」 expresses a logical inference (“there must have been”), which is unsuitable when the author is talking about their own past wish.
default.q.n2-19-q52-52.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 一体.
default.q.n2-19-q52-52.explanation: The sentence contains the interrogative expression 「何の得があって……」 (“what benefit is there...?”) and ends with the question form 「〜のか？」. In Japanese, the adverb 「一体」 is often used with an interrogative to emphasize confusion or a strong desire to know: 「一体＋interrogative＋〜のか」 (“what on earth...?” / “just what...?”). The context describes an alien’s perspective on humans simply sitting still and reading: “What on earth do humans gain by doing something so dull and monotonous?” Therefore, 「一体」 is the only correct choice.
default.q.n2-19-q52-52.why.0: (a) Correct because the adverb 「一体」 combines with the interrogative 「何の」 and the ending 「〜のか」 to form 「一体何の…か」, expressing extreme puzzlement or questioning (“What on earth is the benefit...?”).
default.q.n2-19-q52-52.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「確かに」means “indeed” or “that is true” and is used to acknowledge or affirm a fact; it does not fit a questioning sentence.
default.q.n2-19-q52-52.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「どうやら」 means “it seems” or “apparently” and is usually accompanied by an inferential ending such as 「〜ようだ / 〜らしい」.
default.q.n2-19-q52-52.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「まさか」 means "surely not" or "it cannot be that," and is usually used with a negative sentence or negative supposition to express surprise at something unlikely.
default.q.n2-19-q53-53.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 傾げるのではないでしょうか.
default.q.n2-19-q53-53.explanation: The passage presents an imaginary situation conceived by the author: 「もし他所の星から来た生物が、本を読んでいる人間を見たら……」 (If a creature from another planet saw a human reading a book...). The sentence containing blank (53) begins with the conjectural adverb 「きっと」(surely, probably) and the idiom 「首を傾げる」(to tilt one’s head in puzzlement or doubt). To offer a gentle, persuasive conjecture about how the extraterrestrial creature would react, the speculative/opinion pattern 「〜のではないでしょうか」(wouldn’t they probably...?) fits perfectly with 「きっと」.
default.q.n2-19-q53-53.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「傾げたのです」 is an affirmative past form describing a real event that happened. It does not fit the hypothetical context introduced by 「もし…」.
default.q.n2-19-q53-53.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「傾げるでしょうか」 is a vague, doubtful question addressed to the reader (“I wonder if they would tilt their heads?”), which conflicts with the highly assertive adverb 「きっと」.
default.q.n2-19-q53-53.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「傾げるようです」expresses an inference based on direct visual observation; it is not used for an abstract hypothetical situation.
default.q.n2-19-q53-53.why.3: (d) Correct because the structure 「〜のではないでしょうか」 combined with the adverb 「きっと」 expresses a supposition and presents an appropriately nuanced opinion in line with the author’s hypothetical reasoning.
default.q.n2-19-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 本書です.
default.q.n2-19-q54-54.explanation: Consider the grammar of the sentence: 「……ということを、くどいくらいに繰り返し語っているのが、＿＿。」 This is an emphatic cleft sentence with the structure 「[clause] のは / のが ＋ [noun] です」 (The thing/place that does A is B). The preceding part already contains the nominalized action 「繰り返し語っているのが」 (the thing that repeatedly states this is...), so the element after 「のが」must be a noun referring to the entity containing that message: 「本書です」 (this book). The complete sentence is: "...ということを、くどいくらいに繰り返し語っているのが、本書です。" (...and the book that repeats this point to an almost excessive degree is this book itself).
default.q.n2-19-q54-54.why.0: (a) Correct because 「本書です」 is a complete noun phrase combined with the emphatic pattern 「〜のが、[Noun] です」: the very book in which this is presented is this book.
default.q.n2-19-q54-54.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the noun 「理由」 (reason) is semantically incompatible with the action 「繰り返し語る」 (repeatedly talk about it).
default.q.n2-19-q54-54.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the nominalizing particle 「のが」already appears before the blank. Continuing with the predicate clause 「明らかになります」would create a redundant or duplicated predicate and result in a grammatical error.
default.q.n2-19-q54-54.why.3: (d) Incorrect because filling in 「本書の中で言いたいことです」 would repeat and unnecessarily duplicate the meaning between 「語っているの」 and 「言いたいこと」, making the sentence wordy and unnatural.
